Whisk in the bread crumbs gradually and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until the sauce reaches your preferred thickness.
Add the chicken cube if using and cook for 3 minutes more. Transfer to a bowl and serve with lechon manok.

intro: Ginataang Salmon gently simmers fish steaks in coconut cream, chilies, ginger, garlic, onion, vinegar, and fish sauce.
steps: Arrange the salmon steaks in a single layer in a pan.
Add the long green chilies, red Thai chilies, garlic, ginger, onion, ground black pepper, fish sauce, and water.
Set the pan over medium heat and bring the liquid to a boil.
Pour in the cane vinegar and cook for 2 minutes without aggressive stirring.
Add the coconut cream and stir gently so the salmon stays intact. Cover, bring back to a boil, then simmer for about 20 minutes, or until the sauce reduces by half and the salmon is cooked through.
Transfer carefully to a serving plate and serve hot.

intro: Chicken dinakdakan is a flavorful pulutan or main dish of boiled chicken grilled until smoky, then mixed with vinegar, mayonnaise, chilies, ginger, and onion.
ingredients: 4 cloves garlic, crushed with skin on
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Simmer the thighs and butts with crushed garlic, bay leaves, pepper, and salt under enough water to submerge them; check tenderness after about 20 minutes.
Drain well, then char the chicken over a charcoal grill or under an oven broiler until the edges turn lightly crisp.
Cut the grilled meat into small chunks and transfer it to a bowl.
Toss with ginger, red onion, minced chilies, mayonnaise, cane vinegar, and a little salt until coated.
Scatter sliced green chilies over the platter and serve while warm.

intro: Chicken pastil is rice wrapped in banana leaf with savory turmeric chicken flakes, served with cucumber, tomatoes, and egg for a complete meal.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs, skin-on and bone-in
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Prepare the rice: rinse the white rice and glutinous rice, drain well, add 3 1/4 cups water in a rice cooker, and cook until done.
For the kagikit, heat a little oil in a pan and brown the chicken thighs on all sides.
Add 1 1/2 cups water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low heat for 20–25 minutes, until the chicken shreds easily. Remove the chicken and reserve the cooking liquid.
Shred the chicken. In a clean pan, heat oil and sauté the garlic and shallots until soft.

Add the shredded chicken and turmeric and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the soy sauce and pepper, then cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring continuously and adding a little reserved liquid to keep it moist.
Taste and add salt if needed.
Soften the banana leaf by passing both sides over a flame until glossy.
For each serving, place rice on a banana leaf and shape it into a log. Top with kagikit, wrap and seal the ends, then serve with cucumber, tomatoes, and boiled egg.

intro: Sinigang na panga ng tuna has a savory broth, fresh vegetables, and a sourness that pairs perfectly with hot rice.
ingredients: 2 lbs tuna jaw / panga ng tuna
4 long green chili peppers / siling pansigang
steps: Bring 8 cups water to a boil over high heat in a large pot.
Add the onion and tomatoes. Boil until the tomatoes soften and begin flavoring the broth.
Add the tuna jaw, reduce to a steady simmer, and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in the sinigang mix, siling pansigang, and eggplant, then simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the okra and sitaw and cook for another 3 minutes, until the vegetables are bright and slightly tender.
Add the kangkong and season with patis. Turn off the heat, cover the pot, and let the residual heat cook the kangkong.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

intro: Moche are soft glutinous rice balls filled with red mung bean and baked with a creamy coconut sauce until lightly browned.
ingredients: 1 cup water, more or less as needed
2 tbsp coconut oil or vegetable oil
1 1/2 cups red mung bean in syrup, drained; reserve syrup
steps: Pulse the drained red mung beans in a food processor until smooth. If dry, add a little reserved syrup, then set aside.
In a bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour, 2 tbsp sugar, oil, and salt. Gradually add water while mixing until a manageable dough forms that is neither wet nor crumbly.
Shape the dough into a ball, flatten it slightly, and divide it into 16 equal pieces.
Roll each piece to about 3 inches long, flatten to roughly 1/2 cm thick, place about 1 tbsp red mung bean paste in the center, and seal the edges around the filling.
Bring plenty of water to a boil in a large pot. Drop in the filled dough in 2 to 3 batches to avoid crowding, and lift them out with a slotted spoon once they float.
Arrange the moche in a single layer in a baking dish and bake at 200°C until the tops are lightly browned.
In a small saucepan, first combine the rice flour and 2 tbsp sugar. Whisk in a little coconut milk to prevent lumps, then add the remaining coconut milk and cook over low heat until thickened.
Turn off the heat, stir in the vanilla, pour some sauce over the moche, and return to the oven for 10 minutes. Serve with the remaining sauce.

intro: Inihaw na pusit cooks quickly, so high heat, frequent basting, and a short grilling time keep it tender.
steps: Rub the squid inside and out with sea salt, then set aside while preparing the sauce.
In a saucepan, combine the soy sauce, 1 cup water, ginger, garlic, shallot, and brown sugar. Heat over medium heat until it begins to simmer.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the remaining 1/2 cup water, pour it into the sauce, and simmer gently until thickened.
Make shallow scores on one side of each squid, brush with oil, and grill over hot charcoal.
Baste repeatedly with the sauce while grilling. Cook over high heat for 2–5 minutes per side depending on size, removing immediately once opaque and cooked through so it does not toughen.

intro: This braised pork hock is tender and gelatinous, with shiitake and oyster sauce gravy poured over crisp-tender broccoli.
ingredients: 1 whole pork leg, cut into 1.5-inch sections
1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
1 cup hot water, for soaking mushrooms
2 cups water, plus more as needed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak the dried shiitake in 1 cup hot water for at least 15 minutes. Strain, reserving both the mushrooms and soaking liquid.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the garlic, ginger, and shallots until fragrant.
Add the pork leg pieces and brown evenly on all sides.

Add the bay leaves, oyster sauce, black pepper, rehydrated mushrooms, mushroom soaking liquid, and 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 1–1 1/2 hours until the meat is tender and the fat is jelly-like, adding water if the liquid runs low.
Remove the pork hock and set aside.
Dissolve the cornstarch in 1/4 cup water, add it to the liquid remaining in the pot, and simmer until thickened and slightly reduced. Season with pepper, salt, and more oyster sauce if needed.
In a separate pot, boil water with a pinch of salt. Cook the broccoli for 2 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Arrange the broccoli on a plate, top with the pork hock, and pour over the sauce.

intro: A simple, satisfying ginisang sayote with ground pork, tomatoes, and fish sauce—ideal for a quick home-cooked meal.
ingredients: 3 large sayote / chayote, peeled and sliced
steps: Peel and slice the sayote evenly so it cooks at the same rate.
Heat the oil in a pan or wok over medium heat. Sauté the onion and garlic until softened and fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3–5 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Add the ground pork, breaking up any lumps with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains, then add the fish sauce and cook for about 1 more minute.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer for 3–5 minutes. Taste and add salt as needed.
Add the sayote and stir to coat it in the sauce. Cover and cook for about 5 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Remove from the heat and serve with rice.

intro: Camote delight is a smooth, creamy, buttery dessert cooked until thick and finished with grated cheese.
steps: Steam the sweet potatoes until tender when pierced. Cool slightly, peel, and place in a large bowl.
Mash the sweet potatoes until smooth, with no large pieces remaining.
Melt the butter in a large nonstick pan over low heat.
Add the condensed milk, fresh cream, vanilla, and salt, stirring until evenly combined.
Add the mashed sweet potatoes and cook over low heat, stirring and folding continuously, until smooth, thick, and easily pulling away from the pan, about 25–30 minutes.
Transfer to a greased tray, smooth the surface, let cool, top with grated cheddar cheese, and serve.

intro: Linubihang Munggo is a creamy Bicol-style mung bean stew where coconut milk softens the beans and dilis adds a deep, savory bite.
ingredients: 3 cups water, plus more as needed
steps: Heat a pot over medium heat and saute the onion for about 2 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato and cook until the tomato collapses and becomes soft.

Add the mung beans, dried anchovies, water, and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover partly, and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are very soft and starting to break down; add a little water if the mixture gets too thick before the beans are tender.
Pour in the coconut cream and simmer gently for 5 minutes more, keeping the heat low so the coconut does not scorch.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Filipino Spaghetti is sweet, meaty, and saucy, with hotdogs and grated cheese making it unmistakably party-table comfort food.
ingredients: 1 large bottle sweet-style tomato ketchup or banana ketchup
400 g tomato puree or tomato sauce
Quickmelt cheese or Colby, grated, for topping
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook the spaghetti noodles in salted boiling water according to the package directions, then drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium heat and saute the garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add the minced beef and minced pork, breaking them up as they cook, and continue cooking until the meat turns light brown.
In a bowl, whisk the flour into the beef stock until smooth, then pour it into the pan with the ketchup, tomato puree or sauce, sliced hotdogs, tomato paste, and basil.
Stir well, bring to a simmer, and cook for 20 minutes over medium-low heat, adding a splash of water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Season with black pepper, salt, and enough sugar to make the sauce distinctly sweet, then simmer for 5 minutes more.
Serve the noodles with the sauce spooned over the top and finish with grated cheese.

intro: Pan de Siosa is a soft Filipino pull-apart bread finished with melted butter, sugar, and grated cheese for a sweet-salty bakery treat.
ingredients: 1/4 cup plus 1 teaspoon white sugar, divided
steps: In a bowl, combine the yeast, warm water, and 1 teaspoon white sugar; let stand until foamy.
Transfer the yeast mixture to a stand mixer and add the flour, remaining 1/4 cup sugar, warm milk, egg, softened butter, and salt.

Using the dough hook, knead on the lowest speed for 5 minutes, then increase one speed level and knead for 10 minutes more, until the dough is elastic and stretchy; knead up to 5 minutes longer if needed.
Shape the dough into a ball, place it in a large bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 1/2 to 3 hours depending on room conditions.
Gently deflate the dough and divide it into 21 to 24 portions. Shape each portion into a ball and arrange evenly among three 9-inch round baking pans.
Cover the pans with a damp towel and let the dough rise again until doubled.
Heat the oven to 180C. Brush the tops with beaten egg and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until lightly golden.
Remove from the oven, brush or pour melted butter over the buns, then sprinkle generously with white sugar and grated cheddar cheese.

intro: Pancit Choca is a Cavite-style seafood pancit colored by squid ink and cooked fast so the noodles soak up a briny sauce.
ingredients: 1 dozen medium prawns, shelled and deveined
250 g fresh baby squid, sliced, ink reserved
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak the bihon noodles in water for no more than 10 minutes, then drain so they are softened but not mushy.
Season the pork belly with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat, brown the pork belly, then remove it from the wok and set aside.
In the same wok, saute the garlic, onion, and celery until fragrant.
Add the prawn broth, soy sauce, and reserved squid ink, then bring the mixture to a boil.

Once boiling, add the drained noodles, prawns, baby squid, cabbage, carrot, and browned pork. Stir-fry over very high heat for about 5 minutes, until the seafood is cooked and the noodles absorb the liquid.
Season with fish sauce and more freshly ground black pepper, then serve with lemon or calamansi wedges.

intro: Filipino Tamales are banana-leaf parcels of coconut rice paste layered with annatto-peanut flavor and savory toppings.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon achuete or annatto powder, dissolved in 1 tablespoon water
1/4 cup chicken breast, boiled and shredded
1 hard-boiled egg or salted egg, divided into 4 pieces
steps: Wash and dry the banana leaves, cut them into about 20 cm squares, and pass fresh leaves briefly over direct heat until pliable.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and saute the onion and garlic just until tender and aromatic.
Pour in the coconut milk, season with salt and ground pepper, and cook until the mixture begins to boil.
Add the rice flour while stirring continuously and cook until it forms a thick paste; add a little water only if the paste becomes too dry to spread.
Divide the paste in half. Keep one half plain, then mix the peanut butter and dissolved achuete into the other half until evenly orange.

Place some plain mixture in the center of a banana leaf and spread into a square about 10 cm wide. Add a layer of the orange mixture on top, then garnish with chicken, ham, cashews, and a piece of egg.

Fold the banana leaf around the filling, wrap again with another leaf with the seam side down, and repeat with more leaves until the parcel is well sealed, using about 4 leaves total; tie securely with string.
Steam or boil the parcels for 20 to 30 minutes, until set and heated through.
Serve hot, or let cool and serve at room temperature.

intro: Coconut Shrimp pairs crisp coconut-coated prawns with a quick sweet chili vinegar sauce for a bright, crunchy appetizer or ulam.
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, cleaned and peeled
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Make the sauce first: blend or process the minced garlic, Thai chili, and 3/4 cup water for about 10 seconds.
Bring the rice vinegar to a boil in a saucepan, add the garlic-chili mixture, and cook for 2 minutes while stirring.
Add the sugar and stir until dissolved, then season with salt and stir in the ketchup.
Mix the cornstarch with 1 1/2 tablespoons water to make a slurry, pour it into the saucepan, and cook over medium heat while stirring until the sauce thickens; set aside.
Season the shrimp with salt and ground black pepper and let them stand for 5 minutes.
For the batter, whisk together the egg, 1 cup flour, fresh milk, baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt until smooth.
Combine the bread crumbs and sweetened desiccated coconut in a shallow bowl.
Coat each shrimp in the 1/2 cup flour, dip in batter, let excess drip off, then roll in the coconut-bread crumb mixture until fully covered.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the shrimp in batches, turning as needed, until both sides are golden brown and the shrimp are cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve with the sweet chili sauce.

intro: Beef Kaldereta sa Gata with Peanut Butter is a rich stew where tender beef simmers in tomato, coconut milk, and a nutty sauce.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat.
Saute the onion, garlic, and chopped tomato until the onion and tomato soften.
Add the beef and cook, stirring occasionally, until the pieces turn light brown on the outside.
Pour in the tomato sauce and beef broth, bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat until the sauce reduces by about half.
Add the coconut milk and Thai chili peppers, cover again, and continue simmering until the beef is tender.
Stir in the peanut butter until fully blended into the sauce.
Add the cubed potatoes, cover, and cook for 10 minutes, or until starting to soften.
Add the red and green bell peppers, cover, and cook for 12 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is rich.
Season with salt and ground black pepper, then serve with warm white rice.

intro: Soup Number 5 is a long-simmered Filipino beef offal soup with lemongrass, sibot herbs, ginger, chilies, and a peppery broth.
ingredients: 800 g bull testes and testicles, cleaned and parboiled
2 stalks spring onions, chopped, white and green parts separated
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: In a large pot, combine the parboiled bull testes and testicles, beef tendons, water, beef stock, lemongrass, and sibot herb mix.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer for about 3 1/2 hours, until the offal and tendons are very tender.
Remove the testes, testicles, and tendons from the pot; discard the lemongrass and sibot herbs, and reserve the cooking liquid.
Slice the testes, testicles, and tendons into bite-sized pieces.
In a second pot, heat oil over medium heat and saute the garlic, onions, white parts of the spring onions, and ginger until aromatic and the onions are soft.
Add the sliced testes, testicles, tendons, and chilies, then saute for 2 minutes.
Pour in the reserved liquid and the beef broth, bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer for 30 minutes.
Raise the heat to high briefly to reduce the broth slightly, then season with fish sauce and plenty of freshly ground black pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with the green parts of the spring onions.

intro: Anghang Sarap Laing with Shrimp is a spicy gata dish where dried taro leaves slowly drink up coconut sauce before shrimp is folded back in.
ingredients: 2 ounces (60 g) dried taro leaves, chopped
5 ounces pork shoulder, sliced into thin small pieces
2 packs (33 g each) Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix
steps: Combine the Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix with 4 1/2 cups water, stir until dissolved, and set aside.
Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat, then pan-fry the shrimp for 1 minute per side. Remove the shrimp and set aside.
Pour the prepared gata mixture into the same pot and bring it to a boil.
Add the pork, onions, ginger, garlic, and Thai chilies. Cover and boil over medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the pork is tender.
Stir in the shrimp paste until distributed through the sauce.
Add the dried taro leaves, cover, and cook over low heat for 20 minutes so the leaves absorb the gata.
Stir gently, then continue cooking for 12 to 15 minutes more, until the taro is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Return the pan-fried shrimp to the pot, stir briefly to coat and heat through, then serve immediately with warm rice.

intro: Kangkong and Ground Pork with Oyster Sauce Stir Fry is a quick, savory vegetable dish finished with crisp browned garlic.
ingredients: 3/4 lb water spinach (kangkong), stalks and leaves separated
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pan over low to medium heat, add the crushed garlic after about 20 seconds, and fry slowly while stirring until golden brown.
Strain or scoop out the browned garlic and reserve both the garlic and the garlic oil separately.
Return 3 tablespoons of the garlic oil to the pan and saute the minced onion over medium heat until softened.
Add the ground pork and saute for 3 to 5 minutes, until it turns light brown.
Stir in the oyster sauce and 1/4 cup water, then cook until the liquid evaporates completely.
Add the kangkong stalks and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the kangkong leaves and some of the browned garlic, then cook for 1 minute, just until the leaves wilt; add up to 1/2 cup extra water only if you want a saucier dish.
Season with salt and ground black pepper, transfer to a serving plate, and top with more browned garlic.

intro: A savory-tangy bangus steak with browned fish, lemon-soy sauce, and sweet onion slices that is perfect with hot rice.
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the sliced milkfish belly until medium brown on one side, then turn and brown the other side; remove the fish from the pan.
Pour off excess oil, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan. Lower to medium heat and cook the crushed garlic until light brown.
Add the soy sauce, water, and lemon juice, stirring to combine and loosen the browned bits in the pan.
Return the fried fish to the pan, cover, and cook for 3 minutes so the sauce flavors the fish.
Add the sliced onion, then season with salt and pepper. Stir gently, cover again, and cook for 2 to 5 minutes, adding a splash of water only if the sauce gets too reduced.
Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

intro: Juicy grilled pork chops get a bright Filipino-style lift from a fresh mango, singkamas, chili, and lime salsa.
ingredients: 3 pork chops, about 6 to 8 ounces each
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: In a bowl, combine the mango, red onion, red bell pepper, jicama, jalapeno, cilantro, and lime juice. Season with salt and ground black pepper, mix gently, and refrigerate while the pork rests.
In a separate small bowl, stir together the garlic powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper.
Rub the seasoning mixture evenly over the pork chops and let them stand for 15 to 30 minutes.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium heat. Grill the pork chops for 6 to 8 minutes per side, until browned outside and fully cooked through without drying them out.
Plate the pork chops and serve with the chilled mango salsa on the side.

intro: These pork siomai are plump steamed dumplings packed with pork, shrimp, vegetables, sesame oil, and savory pork seasoning.
ingredients: 2 sachets Knorr SavorRich Pork Seasoning, 44 g each
steps: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork and minced shrimp until evenly mixed.
Add the jicama, carrots, onion, scallions, egg, ground black pepper, and sesame oil; mix until the filling is well blended.
Pour in the Knorr SavorRich Pork Seasoning and mix again until fully incorporated.
Place about 1 1/2 tablespoons of filling in each wonton wrapper and shape into siomai, repeating until all filling is used.
Arrange the dumplings in a steamer with space between them, set over boiling water, and steam for 15 to 20 minutes, until the pork filling is cooked through.
Transfer to a plate and serve hot with soy sauce-calamansi dip and chili garlic paste if desired.

intro: Bangus Bicol Express turns crisp-fried milkfish belly into a rich coconut dish with bagoong, ginger, and chilies.
steps: Slice the bangus into serving pieces, sprinkle all over with the salt, and let stand for 3 minutes.
Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat. While it heats, dredge the fish pieces lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Fry the bangus for 3 minutes per side, until lightly crisp and browned, then remove and set aside.
Pour off the oil, leaving about 3 tablespoons in the pan. Saute the onion for up to 1 minute, then add garlic for 30 seconds and stir in the ginger; cook until the onion softens.
Add the shrimp paste and cook for 30 seconds, stirring so it flavors the aromatics.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the Thai chilies and long green peppers, then season with ground black pepper.
Return the fried bangus to the pan and cook gently for no more than 2 1/2 minutes, just until heated through and coated with sauce. Serve with rice.

intro: This kakaibang chicken adobo is richer than usual, with yogurt-marinated chicken, lemon-lime soda, liver, eggs, and a thick savory sauce.
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 cup water, plus 1/4 cup for slurry
steps: In a large bowl, combine the plain yogurt and 1/2 Knorr Chicken Cube for the marinade. Add the chicken pieces, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the chicken liver on both sides until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same oil, fry the marinated chicken pieces for 1 minute per side, just to lightly sear them, then remove from the pan.
Melt the butter into the remaining oil. Add the crushed garlic and cook until it begins to brown.
Return the chicken to the pan. Add the soy sauce, vinegar, lemon-lime soda, and 1 cup water, then bring to a boil.
Add the remaining 1/2 Knorr Chicken Cube, cracked peppercorns, and bay leaves. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Add the fried chicken livers back to the pan and stir gently.
Mix the cornstarch with 1/4 cup water to make a smooth slurry. Pour it into the pan while stirring, then add the boiled eggs if using and cook until the sauce thickens.
Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with chopped green onions.

intro: Ginataang pusit is a quick coconut-milk squid dish with ginger, chilies, and fish sauce for a creamy, gently spicy meal.
ingredients: 800 g medium-sized squid, cleaned and sliced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat, then saute the garlic, onion, and ginger for 2 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the white sugar. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Season with fish sauce, add the green chili peppers, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the coconut milk has thickened.
Add the sliced squid and cook for 5 minutes, just until tender and opaque.
Season with freshly ground black pepper, turn off the heat, and serve hot.

intro: Tender pork belly and quail eggs simmer into a glossy, sweet-savory oyster sauce braise with string beans for crunch.
ingredients: 1 bunch string beans, sliced into 2-inch sections
1 1/2 tablespoons Sichuan Doubanjiang or broad bean paste
steps: Put the diced pork belly in boiling water and blanch for a few minutes, skimming off foam as it rises. Drain the pork and set aside.
Set a clay pot or heavy Dutch oven over medium-low heat. Add 2 teaspoons oil and the white sugar, stirring until the sugar melts and caramelizes.
Add the blanched pork belly, Chinese cooking wine, ginger slices, spring onions, and garlic, stirring to coat the meat in the caramel.
Stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce, Sichuan Doubanjiang, and five-spice powder. Pour in 2 1/2 cups water, lower the heat, and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours, until the pork is tender.
Add the peeled quail eggs and let them heat in the braising liquid.

Remove the scallions and ginger, then mash the softened garlic into the sauce. Turn the heat to high, add the string beans, and stir constantly for about 5 minutes until the beans are crisp-tender and the sauce is thick and glossy.
Serve with steamed white rice.

intro: Adobong labong combines bamboo shoots, pork, and shrimp in a simple vinegar-broth sauce with garlic and onion.
ingredients: 2 to 2 1/2 cups bamboo shoots, cut into 1- to 2-inch lengths
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a wok or wide pan over medium heat.
Saute the minced garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add the thinly sliced pork and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the pork or beef broth and bring to a boil. Cover, lower the heat, and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Add the shrimp, bamboo shoots, 2 teaspoons salt, and ground black pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes, until the shrimp turn pink and the bamboo shoots are heated through.
Pour in the vinegar and let it come back to a boil without covering. Simmer uncovered for 3 to 5 minutes so the vinegar sharpness mellows.
Taste and adjust with more salt and pepper if needed, then transfer to a serving plate.

intro: Monghe is a steamed pork, egg, cheese, milk, and Spam loaf sliced, dipped in egg, and pan-fried until golden.
ingredients: 1 can Spam, chopped into small pieces
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the ground pork, 4 eggs, grated processed cheese, powdered milk, chopped Spam, salt, and black pepper until evenly incorporated.
Lightly grease a sheet of aluminum foil with oil. Spread the meat mixture onto the foil, leaving about 1 inch of space on each side.
Roll the foil tightly into a log, tucking and twisting the ends closed to seal it.
Place the wrapped log in a steamer over boiling water and steam for 45 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Remove the log from the steamer and let it cool to room temperature before unwrapping.
Slice the cooled loaf into 1/2-inch-thick pieces, then dip each slice in the beaten eggs to coat.
Heat the vegetable oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Fry the coated slices until golden brown on both sides, then serve with your preferred dipping sauce.

intro: A loaded pulutan-style nacho platter gets Filipino character from crisp sisig, fresh salsa, chilies, and a generous cheese sauce drizzle.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: In a bowl, toss together the chopped tomato, coriander, white onion, bird's eye chilies, a pinch of salt, and freshly ground black pepper; taste and adjust the seasoning.
Spread half of the nacho chips on a serving platter, then spoon over part of the tomato mixture so the chips are lightly covered.
Add the remaining nacho chips and scatter the rest of the tomato mixture over the top.
Pile the crispy sisig over the nachos, drizzle with cheese sauce, and serve right away while the chips are still crisp.

intro: This fish sinigang gets its clean, bright sourness from kamias simmered with tomatoes, onion, green pepper, and mustard greens.
ingredients: 2 lbs fish steaks or 2 whole medium fish, cleaned
12 fresh or fresh frozen kamias, also called bilimbi
steps: Bring 6 cups water to a boil in a large pot over high heat.
When boiling, add the tomatoes, kamias, and onion. Cover and boil for 8 minutes to build the sour broth.
Add the fish and long green peppers. Cover again, lower to medium heat, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Add the mustard greens, then season with salt and pepper and stir gently.
Turn off the heat, cover the pot, and let the residual heat wilt the greens for 5 minutes.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve with white rice.

intro: This grilled litson baka uses an overnight lemongrass-soy marinade, a hot sear, and indirect charcoal heat for tender slices with a savory-sweet dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kilograms prime rib roast, divided into two 750-gram sections
steps: Make the serving sauce by mixing the cane vinegar and sweet chili sauce in a small bowl; set aside.
Blend the lemongrass, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, soy sauce, Knorr liquid seasoning, calamansi or lemon juice, oil, water, and black pepper until smooth, then season the marinade with salt to taste.
Place the beef sections in a resealable bag, pour in the marinade, coat the meat completely, seal, and refrigerate overnight.
Take the beef out of the refrigerator 1 hour before cooking; drain it on a rack, reserve the marinade for basting, and pat the meat dry with paper towels.

Prepare a hooded charcoal grill for indirect cooking by placing the coals on one side; while it heats, set a heavy pan over very high heat and sear the beef on all sides until browned and crusty, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Move the beef to the side of the grill without coals, cover, and keep the grill around 190C; cook for 45 to 50 minutes, brushing with reserved marinade every 15 minutes for a total of 3 bastes.
Remove the beef from the heat and rest it for 15 minutes, then slice thinly and serve with the vinegar-sweet chili sauce.

intro: These sweet, spicy, crunchy dilis make a quick snack or rice topping with just a few pantry ingredients.
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium-high heat until hot enough for frying.
Add the dried anchovies and deep-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring as needed, until they turn light brown; turn off the heat, lift them out, and drain.
In a bowl, combine the fried dilis with banana ketchup and hot chili sauce, then mix until evenly coated.
Sprinkle in the brown sugar and toss until the anchovies are covered all over.
Reheat the oil over medium heat and fry the coated anchovies for about 2 minutes, just until crunchy and glossy; remove before the sugar darkens or burns.
Drain briefly, transfer to a serving plate, and serve once cool enough to crisp fully.

intro: Butter, garlic, calamansi, and rich taba ng talangka coat shrimp in a fast, deeply savory Filipino seafood dish.
ingredients: 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper or cracked peppercorn
steps: Melt the butter or margarine in a pan over medium heat.
Add the cleaned shrimp and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the shells turn orange and the shrimp are nearly cooked through.
Stir in the chopped garlic and cook for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Season with salt and ground black pepper or cracked peppercorn, then add the taba ng talangka and stir to coat the shrimp.
Cook for 2 minutes, then squeeze in the calamansi and pour in the vinegar.
Stir and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce is hot and slightly blended into the butter, then transfer to a serving plate.

intro: Smoky grilled dried squid slowly softens in coconut cream with ginger, onion, chilies, and spinach for a rich ginataan-style dish.
steps: Heat a grill over high heat until hot, then grill one side of the dried squid for 3 minutes; when it curls, straighten it as much as possible and grill the other side for 1 to 2 minutes.
Place the grilled squid in a slow cooker with the coconut cream, sliced green chilies, minced garlic, ginger, onion, fish sauce, and ground black pepper.
Cover and cook on high for 8 hours, until the squid has softened and the coconut sauce is infused with its flavor.
Add the fresh spinach, cover again, and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, just until the leaves wilt.
Transfer the squid and coconut sauce to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

intro: This Quiapo-style sotanghon soup builds a porky annatto broth with jowl, bones, cabbage, and silky bean thread noodles.
ingredients: 500 grams pork jowl, sliced into large chunks
steps: Season the pork jowl generously with salt and let it sit while you prepare the pot.
Heat oil in a large pot over high heat until very hot, then add the pork jowl and brown it well on all sides; remove and set aside.
Lower the heat, add more oil if the pot is dry, and saute the garlic and red onion for about 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the annatto powder and cook until the oil turns a vivid red-orange.
Return the pork jowl to the pot, add the pork back bones and 2 liters water, and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 1 hour and 15 minutes, until the broth is flavorful and the pork is tender.
Add the bean thread noodles and cook for 10 minutes, adding a little water if the soup becomes too thick.
Stir in the chopped cabbage and cook for 3 minutes, just until tender-crisp.
Turn off the heat, season with fish sauce and white ground pepper, garnish with spring onions, and serve with boiled egg.

intro: This chicken liver adobo keeps the livers tender by briefly simmering them first, then finishing them with reduced adobo sauce, aromatics, chilies, and crisp garlic.
ingredients: 6 to 8 cloves garlic, cut into thin slivers
steps: Soak the chicken livers in cold water for several minutes, then drain, rinse with cold water, and set aside.
In a pot, combine the soy sauce, vinegar, water, bay leaves, and peppercorns; bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook for 3 to 5 minutes to mellow the vinegar.
Lower the heat, add the chicken livers one by one, and cook for about 5 minutes, just until firm, opaque, and no longer pink; lift the livers out and keep simmering the sauce until reduced.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the garlic slivers, and stir as the oil heats; lower the heat and fry until golden and crisp, then remove the garlic and reserve it for topping.
In the same oil, cook the ginger for several seconds until lightly browned, then add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the chicken livers and brown the sides gently, then pour in the reduced sauce and simmer until the sauce thickens or nearly cooks down, depending on how saucy you like it.
Stir in the chopped green chilies, turn off the heat, transfer to a serving dish, and top with the crisp garlic.

intro: Pan-seared bangus belly gets finished in the oven with mayonnaise, three cheeses, tomato, peppers, and garlic for a rich baked seafood dish.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 small tomato, peeled, seeded, and chopped
steps: Season the bangus belly with lemon juice, salt, and freshly ground black pepper.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium-high heat, add a small amount of oil, and place the fish skin-side down; cook until the skin turns golden brown.
Flip the bangus and cook the other side until lightly browned, then remove it from the pan.
In a bowl, mix the quick melt cheese, mozzarella, parmesan, chopped tomato, red capsicum, green capsicum, and minced garlic.
Place the bangus on a lightly greased baking tray, spread mayonnaise over the top, and cover with the cheese mixture.
Bake in a preheated 180C oven for 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and lightly golden, then serve hot.

intro: This comforting tinola adds sotanghon noodles to gingered chicken broth with green papaya and malunggay.
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat, then saute the garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant and the onion softens.
Add the chicken breast and cook until the outside turns light brown.
Pour in the rice wash and bring to a boil; add the Knorr Chicken Cube, cover, and simmer over low to medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add the sliced green papaya and sotanghon noodles, then cook for 5 minutes, until the noodles soften and the papaya is tender-crisp.
Stir in the malunggay leaves just until wilted.
Season with patis and ground black pepper, then transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

intro: Leftover lean pork adobo turns into crisp, tangy flakes that are perfect with garlic rice and eggs.
ingredients: 500 grams cooked pork adobo, preferably non-fatty pork
steps: Shred the cooked pork adobo along the grain into small, thin strands.
Heat enough cooking oil for pan-frying in a wok over medium-high heat until very hot and just starting to smoke.
Add the pork strands and cook while stirring constantly so they crisp evenly instead of clumping.
Once the pork is crisp, add the vinegar, toss well, and cook a little longer until the sharp smell fades and the flakes stay crunchy.
Remove the pork from the wok and drain in a colander or on a rack before serving.

intro: Sprite gives this pork adobo a mellow sweetness that balances the soy, vinegar, garlic, and slow-cooked pork belly richness.
ingredients: 1 can Sprite or similar lemon-lime soda
steps: In a large bowl, combine the pork belly, soy sauce, and Sprite; cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours to marinate.
Drain the pork through a sieve, reserving the soy-Sprite marinade separately.
Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic until lightly browned, then add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the drained pork and cook, stirring, until the pieces are lightly browned on the outside.
Pour in the reserved marinade, cover, and bring to a boil. Add the peppercorns and bay leaves, then cook covered over medium heat for 30 minutes.
Add the vinegar and let the sauce return to a boil before stirring. Cover and cook for 25 to 30 minutes more, adding the water only if the sauce reduces too much before the pork is tender.
Serve hot with steamed rice once the pork is tender and the sauce is savory, tangy, and slightly reduced.

intro: This pork lomi is a thick, hearty noodle soup with tender pork belly, chorizo, vegetables, and an egg-swirled broth.
steps: Bring 5 cups water to a boil in a pot. Add the pork belly, cover, and boil over low to medium heat for 30 minutes, then remove the pork, slice it thinly, and reserve the stock.
In a clean pot, heat a little oil over medium heat and saute the garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add the Chorizo de Bilbao and cook for 2 minutes, then add the sliced boiled pork and saute for 1 minute.
Pour in the reserved pork stock plus 1 to 2 cups water as needed, bring to a boil, then stir in the pork cube. Cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the carrots, cabbage, and fresh noodles. Stir, cover, and cook for 8 minutes, or until the noodles are tender.
Mix the cornstarch with 1/2 cup water until smooth, pour it into the soup, and stir until the broth thickens.
Crack in the egg and stir until it disperses through the hot soup. Season with salt and ground black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Pinapaitan is a bold Ilocano-style beef offal soup with tamarind sourness, chile heat, and a clean bitterness drawn from ampalaya.
ingredients: 600 g ox tripe, cleaned, cooked, and sliced into small pieces
250 g beef heart, sliced into small pieces
250 g beef liver, sliced into small pieces
250 g beef brisket, sliced into small pieces
3 medium bitter gourds, seeded and sliced into large chunks
1 large packet sinigang mix or tamarind mix
1 thumb-size piece ginger, crushed and finely sliced
6 green finger chilies or siling haba, left whole
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place the sliced beef liver in the cane vinegar and marinate for 30 minutes while preparing the aromatics and other meats.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic, ginger, and red onion until aromatic and softened.
Add the ox tripe, beef heart, and beef brisket, keeping the liver aside. Stir-fry for about 1 minute, just until the meat surfaces brown lightly.
Pour in the beef stock, then add the bitter gourd chunks and whole green chilies. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer, and cook for 45 minutes.

Drain the vinegar from the liver and discard the vinegar. Remove the bitter gourd chunks from the pot, blend them until smooth, then strain the puree through a fine sieve or muslin cloth back into the pot, rinsing with hot stock to extract the bitterness while keeping the broth clear.
Stir in the sinigang mix gradually, tasting so the sourness stays balanced. Add the marinated liver and simmer for 10 minutes, or until the liver is just cooked through.
Season with fish sauce, salt if needed, cayenne pepper, and freshly ground black pepper. Serve hot while the broth is sharp, bitter, and savory.

intro: Masuki mami is a deeply simmered chicken noodle soup finished with roast pork, chopped chicken, spring onions, and hoisin on the side.
ingredients: 500 g fresh yaka mien noodles or fat Chinese white egg noodles
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add the chicken frames and boneless chicken thighs and blanch for about 5 minutes, until the chicken turns white.
Drain the chicken, then rinse each piece under cold running water to remove scum and impurities.
Place the cleaned chicken frames and thighs in a large pot with 12 cups cold water, the spring onions, ginger, Chinese cooking wine, white peppercorns, and sugar.
Set the pot over low-medium heat and keep it at a gentle simmer without letting it boil hard. After 1 hour, remove the boneless thighs and set them aside.
Continue simmering the chicken frames for 3 more hours, adding water as needed so the chicken stays covered.
Strain the broth through cheesecloth into another pot for a clear stock, season with salt, and keep it barely simmering over very low heat.
Cook the fresh yaka mien noodles in a separate pot of boiling salted water according to package directions until al dente, then drain.
Chop the reserved chicken thighs into small pieces and slice the cooked roast pork.
Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle over the hot broth, and top with chopped chicken, roast pork, and chopped spring onions. Serve with hoisin sauce on the side.

intro: Lumpiang pabasa is a saucy vegetable and tofu filling colored with annatto and made rich with peanut butter and cheese.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons annatto powder or atsuete, dissolved in 1/2 cup boiling water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Saute the garlic and onion until softened and fragrant.
Add the dried shrimps and cook until their aroma becomes pronounced.
Add the jicama and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the carrots and stir-fry for another 2 minutes.
Add the deep-fried tofu and stir-fry for 1 minute, then add the sweet potatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and green beans, if using, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the annatto mixture, vegetable stock, and soy sauce. Bring to a boil, then stir in the peanut butter until evenly blended.
Simmer for about 2 minutes, or until the vegetables are cooked but still hold their shape.
Mix in the grated cheese, then season with fish sauce and freshly ground black pepper. Turn off the heat and serve.

intro: Seafood aligue pasta coats linguine in a creamy crab-fat sauce with tomatoes, spinach, mixed seafood, and cheeses.
ingredients: 1 lb seafood mix, such as shrimp, squid, and mussels
1/2 cup crab fat or taba ng talangka
steps: Bring 1 quart water to a boil in a pot. Add 1 teaspoon salt and cook the linguine according to package directions until tender but still firm, then drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Saute the onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add the crab fat and cook for about 30 seconds, stirring until fragrant.
Add the halved grape tomatoes and cook for 1 minute, then add the seafood mix and saute for another 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste and baby spinach, pour in the chicken stock, and bring the sauce to a boil.
Add the Carnation Everyday Creamer, ricotta, and parmesan, stirring until the cheeses melt into a creamy sauce.
Season with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, add the cooked linguine, and toss until every strand is coated.
Add the chopped parsley, toss once more, and serve warm.

intro: Pininyahang manok turns chicken, pineapple, cream, and simple vegetables into a gently sweet and savory ulam for rice.
ingredients: 1 pound chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 medium red or green bell pepper, sliced
6.7 fluid ounces all-purpose cream or whipping cream
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the carrot and potato for several minutes, turning as needed, until the edges are lightly browned, then remove and set aside.
Using the same oil, saute the onion and garlic over medium heat until softened and fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, until the pieces are lightly browned.
Lower the heat, add the fish sauce and pineapple chunks, stir, then cover and simmer until the chicken is tender and has released its juices.
Return the browned carrot and potato to the pan, add the bell pepper, then pour in the cream and stir gently.
Season with ground black pepper and simmer for about 5 minutes, or until the sauce slightly thickens and the vegetables are tender. Serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: This pork baby back ribs nilaga is a clear, comforting soup with tender ribs, potatoes, cabbage, and baby bok choy.
steps: Pour 8 to 10 cups water into a soup pot and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Add the chopped onion, celery, ground black pepper, and garlic powder. Cover and boil over medium heat for 5 minutes.

Add the sliced baby back ribs, cover, and simmer for 60 to 90 minutes, adding more water as needed, until the meat is tender. For a faster version, boil about 45 minutes, though a longer simmer gives a softer texture.
Add the potatoes and cabbage, stir, cover, and boil for 5 minutes, or until the potatoes are just tender.
Add the baby bok choy and fish sauce, stir, and cook for 1 minute, just until the greens wilt but stay bright.
Taste the broth and adjust with more fish sauce if needed, then serve hot.

intro: Filipino-style chicken noodle soup is a quick, golden broth with short noodles, shredded chicken, vegetables, and a light cornstarch body.
ingredients: 1 cup short noodles, such as vermicelli or angel hair pasta, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Saute the onion and garlic for about 4 minutes, until soft and fragrant.
Stir in the carrot and celery, then add the turmeric, salt, and freshly ground black pepper. Cook for 3 minutes to begin softening the vegetables.
Pour in the chicken stock and add the chicken stock cube. Bring the broth to a gentle boil.
Add the short noodles and cook for about 6 minutes, or until just tender.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer for 4 minutes to heat it through.
Add the cornstarch slurry and stir well until the broth slightly thickens.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper, then remove from heat, ladle into bowls, and garnish with chopped parsley.

intro: Pork adobo with tofu adds fried tofu cubes to a soy-vinegar pork stew enriched with oyster sauce and a touch of sugar.
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the crushed garlic until it turns light brown.
Add the cubed pork and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned.
Pour in the soy sauce, oyster sauce, and water. Add the bay leaves, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for about 45 minutes, or until the pork is tender.
Add the vinegar and let the liquid boil again before stirring so the sharpness cooks off cleanly.
Stir in the sugar and deep-fried tofu, then cook for 3 minutes so the tofu absorbs some of the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, turn off the heat, and transfer to a serving bowl.

intro: Bignay wine is best served simply chilled so its deep red color, sweet fruitiness, and aroma stay front and center.
ingredients: Small fruit slices, optional for garnish
steps: Chill the bignay wine until cold, ideally at least 2 hours before serving.
Set out small wine glasses; add a few ice cubes only if a lighter, colder drink is preferred.
Pour the wine gently, garnish with calamansi or fruit if using, and serve immediately.

intro: Nilagang Okra at Inihaw na Talong is a simple home-style dish, especially with bagoong monamon brightened by lemon.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to a boil over high heat, then cook the okra until tender but not mushy, about 4–6 minutes depending on size.
Drain the okra well and arrange it on a serving plate.
Heat a charcoal grill until hot. Grill the eggplants, turning as needed, until the skins are charred and the flesh is soft throughout.
Transfer the grilled eggplants to the plate with the okra. Peel them if desired, or leave them charred for smoky flavor.
In a small saucer, mix the bagoong monamon and lemon juice, then serve alongside the vegetables as a dipping sauce.

intro: Sinigang na Bangus sa Bayabas is a gently sour, fragrant soup enriched with ripe guavas and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 1 medium bangus, cleaned, scaled, and sliced into steaks
steps: Bring 4 to 5 cups water to a boil in a large pot over high heat.

Add the guavas, tomatoes, onion, and ground black pepper. Cover, reduce slightly to a steady boil, and cook for about 15 minutes, until the guavas and vegetables are very soft; add a little more water if the level becomes too low.
Carefully mash the softened guavas and vegetables in the pot to release their flavor into the broth, then stir in the fish sauce.
Add the bangus steaks and cook over medium heat for 5–10 minutes, just until opaque and cooked through.
Add the okra and jalapeno peppers and simmer for 5 minutes, until the okra is tender but intact.
Add the baby spinach, cover the pot, turn off the heat, and let stand for 5 minutes so the greens gently wilt before serving hot.

intro: This ginataang galunggong combines fried fish, eggplant, bok choy, and malunggay in savory coconut milk with ginger and vinegar.
steps: Rub the galunggong all over with Maggi Magic Sarap and let it season for 10 minutes.
Brush the sliced eggplants with a little cooking oil, heat a pan over medium heat, and cook for about 2 minutes per side until lightly browned and softened. Set aside.
Heat the remaining cooking oil in a wok or deep pan over medium-high heat, then fry the fish until both sides are golden and crisp. Remove and set aside.
Leave about 3 tablespoons of frying oil in the wok. Sauté the ginger, garlic, and onion over medium heat until fragrant and the onion softens.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil. Add the white vinegar and simmer uncovered for 3 minutes without stirring too much.
Season the sauce with fish sauce and ground black pepper, then add the long green pepper and fried fish. Cover and simmer for 3 minutes so the fish absorbs the sauce.
Add the bok choy, fried eggplant, and malunggay leaves. Cook for about 2 minutes, just until the greens wilt, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Chicken Skin Chicharon is made by simmering seasoned skin until its own oil renders out, then frying it in that oil until crisp.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken skin, cut into roughly 3 x 3 inch pieces
Water, enough to barely cover the chicken skin
steps: Place the chicken skin, salt, vinegar, and black pepper in a nonstick pot, then add just enough water to cover the skin.
Bring to a rapid boil over high heat, keeping the pot uncovered, and cook until the liquid evaporates.
Once the pot is nearly dry, reduce the heat to medium and let the chicken skin render its fat, stirring gently from time to time so the pieces do not stick.
Continue cooking the chicken skin in its own oil until the pieces turn golden, bubbly, and crisp.
Lift out the chicharon, drain well, let it cool slightly so it crisps further, and serve.

intro: Flan de Manzanas is a creamy apple custard with caramelized brown sugar, baked in llaneras until softly set.
ingredients: 5 tart apples such as Granny Smith, peeled, cored, and cubed
steps: Preheat the oven to 170 C. In a saucepan, combine the cubed apples and water, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the apples are soft.
Mash the softened apples with a fork and let them cool until no longer hot.
In a bowl, mix the cooled mashed apples with the condensed milk and beaten eggs until evenly combined.
Put 2 tablespoons brown sugar in each llanera. Set each mold over low stovetop heat until the sugar melts, then carefully tilt to coat the bottom with caramel.
Divide the apple custard mixture among the 3 llaneras. Cover each tightly with aluminum foil and place them in a water bath.
Bake for 45 minutes, or until the flan is set with a slight jiggle in the center.
Remove from the oven, cool completely, then chill in the refrigerator before unmolding onto plates and serving.

intro: Masarsang Menudo is a rich tomato-based pork stew with liver, hotdog, vegetables, peas, and cheese for a hearty Filipino ulam.
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute half of the onion and half of the garlic until the onion softens, then add the pork liver and cook for about 1 1/2 minutes while stirring. Remove the liver mixture and set aside.
In the same pot with the remaining oil, saute the rest of the garlic and onion until fragrant, then add the pork and cook until the outside turns light brown.
Pour in the soy sauce and tomato sauce and stir to coat the pork. Add the Knorr Pork Cube and water, then bring the mixture to a boil.
Add the laurel leaves, cover the pot, lower the heat, and simmer for 30 minutes, or until the pork is starting to become tender.
Return the cooked liver mixture to the pot, then add the hotdogs, potatoes, and carrots. Stir and cook for 10 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Add the bell pepper and green peas and cook for 5 minutes more.
Season with salt, ground black pepper, and sugar if using, then stir in the grated cheese until it melts into the sauce. Serve warm with rice.

intro: This Filipino fried pork chop pairs salty-citrusy marinated meat with a bold tomato, salted egg, and bagoong side.
steps: In a bowl, combine the pork chops, calamansi juice, soy sauce, and ground black pepper. Coat the meat well, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours, or overnight for deeper flavor.
For the side dish, halve the tomatoes, remove the seeds if desired, then cut the flesh into cubes and place in a bowl.
Halve the salted eggs, scoop them from the shells, and break them into smaller pieces over the tomatoes. Add the spicy bagoong alamang and gently toss until combined.
Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. When hot, fry the marinated pork chops in batches for about 5 minutes on the first side.
Turn the pork chops and fry the other side for about 4 minutes, or until browned and cooked through; repeat with the remaining pieces.
Transfer the pork chops to a serving plate and serve with the tomato-salted egg mixture and warm rice.

intro: Tinolang Bangus is a clean, gingery fish soup with chayote, malunggay, and hot pepper leaves in a light patis-seasoned broth.
ingredients: 1 large bangus, scaled, cleaned, and sliced
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat, then saute the onion and ginger until fragrant and the onion begins to soften.
Add the ground black pepper, pour in the water, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the sliced bangus. Let the broth return to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, until the fish is cooked and the broth is flavorful.
Stir in the fish sauce and add the chayote. Cook for 8 minutes, or until the chayote is tender but still holds its shape.
Add the malunggay and hot pepper leaves, stir gently, and cook for 2 minutes just until wilted.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

intro: Tinolang Tahong is a quick mussel soup with ginger, garlic, onion, and leafy greens in a light savory broth.
ingredients: 1 bunch chili leaves, or substitute moringa leaves or spinach
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little cooking oil in a pot over medium heat, then saute the garlic, ginger, and onion until aromatic and the onion softens.
Add the cleaned mussels and pour in 3 to 4 cups water. Increase the heat and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot, lower to a simmer, and cook until the mussel shells open. Discard any mussels that stay closed.
Add the chili leaves and simmer for 2 more minutes, just until the leaves wilt.
Season with fish sauce and freshly ground black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Pork Menudo with Ham is a compact, saucy version of the Filipino favorite with tomato sauce, raisins, potatoes, carrots, and bell peppers.
ingredients: 6 ounces pork, cut into small cubes
1 1/2 cups beef broth, or 1 1/2 cups water with 1 beef cube
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic and onion until fragrant and the onion softens.
Add the pork cubes and cook, stirring occasionally, until the outside turns light brown.
Add the ham and cook for 2 minutes to lightly render and flavor the oil.
Pour in the tomato sauce and beef broth, stir, and bring to a boil.
Add the raisins, cover the pot, and cook over low to medium heat until the pork is tender.
Add the potato, carrot, and red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, until the vegetables are tender but not falling apart.
Season with salt and ground black pepper, stir, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more before serving with rice.

intro: This Pinoy-style carbonara is creamy, meaty, and party-ready, with bacon, ground beef, mushrooms, cream, egg yolks, and Parmesan.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
steps: Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente; drain and set aside.
In a pot over medium heat, cook bacon until crisp and fat renders; remove bacon and discard all but a little fat.
Brown ground beef in the bacon fat, then add onion and garlic and cook until the onion softens.
Pour in beef broth and simmer until almost dry; add mushrooms and butter, stirring until the butter melts.
Add 2 1/4 cups cream, bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, then stir in Parmesan, salt, and pepper.
Beat egg yolks with remaining 1/4 cup cream; stir into the sauce continuously until thick and smooth.
Toss sauce with spaghetti and serve topped with crisp bacon and extra Parmesan.

intro: Bibingka muffins bring the holiday rice-cake flavor into soft individual portions topped with cheese and salted duck egg.
ingredients: 6 tablespoons margarine, melted, plus more for topping
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and line a muffin pan with paper cups.
Whisk sweet rice flour, baking powder, and salt in one bowl.
Beat eggs, gradually add sugar, then mix in vanilla, melted margarine, and coconut milk until smooth.
Stir wet mixture into the flour mixture until no dry pockets remain, then fill muffin cups.
Bake for 28 minutes, until set and lightly golden.
Brush tops with margarine, add cheese and salted egg, then bake 3 to 5 minutes more until toppings warm through.
Cool briefly before serving.

intro: Kalderetang manok is a rich tomato chicken stew with potatoes, carrots, chilies, liver spread, and a cheesy finish.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste
1 kg chicken legs and thighs, cubed
2 tablespoons liver spread, liver pate, or beef liver puree
steps: Combine soy sauce, vinegar, 6 minced garlic cloves, and 1 teaspoon pepper; marinate chicken for 1 hour.
Heat oil over medium heat, fry remaining garlic until golden, then remove and reserve.
In the same pot, saute onion until soft; add chicken and brown all sides.
Add stock and bay leaves, bring to a boil, then stir in tomato puree and carrots.
Simmer covered over very low heat for 30 minutes, adding water if needed, until chicken is tender.
Add liver spread and potatoes; simmer 15 minutes, then add tomato paste, chilies, and capsicum for 15 minutes more.
Season with salt and pepper, then top with fried garlic and grated cheese.

intro: Paksiw na baboy is a sweet-sour pork belly stew simmered with vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, and banana blossoms.
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into cubes
steps: Sear pork belly in a pot over medium heat until browned and enough fat renders.
Add garlic and saute for 1 minute.
Pour in soy sauce and water; bring to a boil.
Add bay leaves and peppercorns, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add vinegar, return to a boil without rushing the stir, then mix well.
Add banana blossoms, lower heat to the gentlest simmer, and cook 30 minutes more until pork is tender.
Stir in brown sugar and Maggi Magic Sarap, then serve hot.

intro: Beef misono is a quick, garlicky beef stir-fry cooked hot and fast with soy sauce and butter.
ingredients: 500 g thinly sliced chuck steak or sukiyaki-cut beef
Freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: Season beef lightly with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Heat a heavy wok or pan over high heat; add a little oil until nearly smoking.
Stir-fry beef and garlic in batches if needed for about 5 minutes, keeping the pan hot.
Pour in soy sauce and stir-fry 2 minutes more.
Lower heat, add butter, and stir for 1 minute until glossy; serve immediately.

intro: Malunggay pandesal is a soft, lightly sweet Filipino bread roll enriched with moringa leaves and coated in fine breadcrumbs.
ingredients: 1 cup malunggay leaves, washed and stems removed
3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for kneading
1 medium egg, beaten and at room temperature
steps: Pat malunggay leaves dry and chop coarsely.
Mix flour, sugar, salt, and malunggay in a large bowl; make a well in the center.
Add egg, oil, lukewarm water, and yeast; mix into a dough, then knead on a floured surface until smooth and elastic.
Shape into a ball, lightly oil it, cover, and let rise 30 to 60 minutes until doubled.
Punch down, divide into 16 pieces, shape into balls, and roll each in breadcrumbs.
Arrange on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise 20 to 30 minutes until doubled.
Bake at 365°F for about 15 minutes, until the sides are golden brown.

intro: Cheesy pork caldereta is a hearty tomato-based rib stew finished with liver spread, vegetables, seasoning, and melted cheddar.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper to taste
steps: Season potatoes and carrots lightly with salt; air-fry at 350°F for 12 minutes and set aside.
Boil ribs in 2 cups water for 3 minutes, drain, and discard the water.
Heat oil in a clean pot; saute garlic until lightly brown, add onion until soft, then brown the ribs.
Add soy sauce and cook 1 minute; pour in tomato sauce and remaining 2 cups water, then bring to a boil.
Add pork cube, cover, and simmer 45 to 60 minutes until ribs are tender.
Stir in liver spread and tomato paste; add bell peppers, carrots, potatoes, and peas and cook 2 minutes.
Add cheese and liquid seasoning, cook 2 minutes more, then season with salt and pepper.

intro: Shrimp laing is a coconut-rich taro leaf dish made savory with shrimp paste, pork fat, chilies, ginger, and fresh shrimp.
steps: Prepare shrimp by trimming antennae and deveining; set aside.
Cook pork fat in a pot over medium heat until it renders enough oil.
Saute onion, garlic, and ginger in the rendered fat until the onion softens.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add chilies, shrimp paste, and dried taro leaves; cover and cook 5 minutes.
Press leaves under the coconut milk, cover, and simmer 30 minutes, then stir and cook on low-medium 45 to 60 minutes until very soft.
Season with white pepper, add shrimp, and cook 3 minutes until the shrimp turn opaque.

intro: Pork adobo paksiw turns cooked pork adobo into a saucy, sweet-savory dish with lechon sauce and a short simmer.
steps: Place pork adobo in a pot and warm it over medium heat.
Add lechon sauce, sugar, and water, then stir to coat the pork evenly.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and adding water if the sauce gets too thick.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

intro: Hotsilog is a classic Filipino breakfast plate of red hotdogs, garlic fried rice, fried eggs, and fresh tomato.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a small pot; add hotdogs and 2 tablespoons oil.
Cook until water evaporates, then roll hotdogs in the remaining oil for 1 to 2 minutes until lightly fried; set aside.
Heat 4 tablespoons oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry eggs one at a time, spooning hot oil over each until the edges crisp and the yolk gets a pale film.
Plate garlic fried rice with hotdogs, eggs, and tomato slices.
Serve right away with ketchup.

intro: Linagpang na bangus is a smoky grilled milkfish soup brightened with tomatoes, red onion, spring onion, fish sauce, and pepper.
ingredients: 2 large bangus, char-grilled, whole or sliced into sections
4 stalks spring onions, whites and greens separated, chopped
Freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: In a pot, combine boiling water, spring onion whites, tomatoes, and red onions.
Bring back to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes until the vegetables soften slightly.
Add grilled bangus and simmer over very low heat for 10 minutes so the broth turns smoky.
Season with fish sauce and freshly ground black pepper.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with spring onion greens.

intro: Molo soup is a comforting Iloilo-style dumpling soup with pork-filled wontons, chicken broth, shrimp, annatto, and toasted garlic.
ingredients: 1 cup shrimp, sliced, chopped, or minced
1/2 cup annatto seeds, soaked in 3/4 cup water
1/2 cup minced green onions, plus more for garnish
steps: Boil chicken in 8 cups water for 40 to 60 minutes until tender; remove chicken and reserve the stock.
Mix ground pork, water chestnuts, green onions, 3/4 cup onions, egg, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Put a spoonful of filling on each wonton wrapper, moisten edges, fold, and seal into dumplings.
Shred or chop cooled chicken meat, discarding bones.
Heat oil in a casserole; saute garlic and remaining onion, then add chicken and cook 3 to 5 minutes.
Add fish sauce, strained annatto water, chicken stock, and remaining 4 cups water; bring to a boil.
Add shrimp and cook 1 minute, then add dumplings and simmer over low heat 12 to 18 minutes until cooked through.
Serve hot with green onions and toasted garlic.

intro: Kalamay gabi is a sticky taro and coconut milk dessert chilled in molds and finished with latik or cheese.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon butter or margarine, plus more for greasing
Latik or grated cheese, for topping
steps: Scrub unpeeled gabi, place in a pot, cover with water, and boil covered 15 to 20 minutes until tender.
Drain, cool under running water, peel, and coarsely grate the gabi.
In a wide pot, combine coconut milk, evaporated milk, and sugar; stir until sugar dissolves.
Add grated gabi and cook over medium-low heat, stirring often, until very thick and heavy.
Stir in butter and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until the mixture pulls from the pan sides.
Grease 2 to 3 llanera molds with butter, divide mixture among them, cool, then chill at least 2 hours.
Top with latik or grated cheese before serving.

intro: Espasol is a chewy Laguna rice cake made with toasted glutinous rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, young coconut, and pandan.
ingredients: 1 stalk pandan, tied into a knot
steps: Toast glutinous rice flour in a large wok over medium heat, stirring constantly, until light brown; reserve 1/2 cup for dusting.
In another large wok, combine coconut milk, sugar, young coconut, and pandan; bring to a boil, then lower to medium.
Remove pandan, then gradually add toasted rice flour while stirring.
Cook over low heat about 30 minutes, folding constantly, until thick, doughy, and evenly cooked.
Transfer to a greased surface, flatten, and let cool.
Cut into strips or roll into cylinders, then coat each piece in reserved toasted flour.
For a firmer texture, let the espasol rest until the next day before serving.

intro: Binabad is marinated pork shoulder simmered until the liquid dries, then pan-fried until caramelized at the edges.
ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder chops, sliced into bite-sized pieces
steps: Mix annatto powder, soy sauce, lemon juice, salt, baking soda, black pepper, and garlic in a bowl.
Coat pork with the marinade in a sealed bag or covered bowl, then refrigerate overnight.
Transfer pork and marinade to a wok, add 1 cup water, cover, and cook over medium heat 30 to 40 minutes until liquid evaporates.
Add a little oil, raise heat to medium-high, and pan-fry about 5 minutes until the pork edges caramelize.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot.

intro: Pork menudo sa gata is a creamy coconut-tomato version of menudo with pork shoulder, liver, potatoes, carrots, and bay leaves.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into cubes
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; saute garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add pork and saute until the outside turns light brown.
Stir in soy sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in tomato sauce and coconut milk; bring to a boil.
Add pork cube and bay leaves, cover, and cook on low until pork is tender, adding water if the sauce dries out.
Add pork liver and cook 8 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrot; cook 10 minutes until tender, then season with salt and pepper.

intro: Chicken afritada sa gata is a creamy tomato chicken stew with hotdogs, potatoes, carrots, bell peppers, peas, and coconut seasoning.
ingredients: 4 lbs chicken, sliced into serving pieces
40 grams Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add chicken and saute until lightly browned.
Stir in tomato sauce, hotdogs, and 2 cups water; bring to a boil.
Dissolve ginataang gulay mix in remaining 2 cups water, pour into the pan, cover, and cook on low for 45 minutes.
Add chicken cube, potatoes, and carrots; cook 8 minutes until vegetables begin to tenderize.
Add green peas and bell peppers; cook 3 minutes more.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve with rice.

intro: Chicken pochero is a tomato-based Filipino stew with chorizo, saba bananas, chickpeas, potatoes, and leafy vegetables.
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pot and pan-fry chicken for 2 minutes per side; remove and set aside.
In the same oil, saute onion and garlic, then add chorizo and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until onion and tomatoes soften.
Return chicken to the pot, add tomato sauce and water, and bring to a boil.
Add chicken cube, cover, and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add potatoes, saba bananas, and chickpeas; cover and cook 12 minutes.
Add long beans and cabbage for 3 minutes, then bok choy for 2 minutes; season with fish sauce and crushed peppercorns.

intro: A rich, mildly spicy beef kaldereta thickened with peanut butter.
ingredients: 1 kg beef ribs, stewing beef, or mutton, cubed
Ground black pepper and salt, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and fry the garlic until golden. Strain and reserve as a topping.
Sauté the onion until soft, then add the meat and brown it on all sides.
Pour in the beef stock and add the bay leaves. Bring to a boil, add the tomato puree and carrots, then lower the heat.
Simmer for 1 1/2 hours, adding water as needed, until the meat is fork-tender.
Stir in the peanut butter and cook for 15 minutes until thick.
Add the tomato paste, chilies, capsicum, and fried potatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes, season, and sprinkle with the fried garlic.

intro: Quick-cooking squid with calamansi, garlic, and gentle heat.
ingredients: 600 g baby squid, gutted and cleaned
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: In a pan over low heat, add olive oil and sauté the pounded garlic until light brown and fragrant.
Increase to medium heat. Add the squid, bay leaves, paprika, and cayenne, then cook for 3 minutes, turning once.
Season with salt, soy sauce, and pepper; cook only until the squid is opaque and just done.
Stir in the calamansi juice 1 tablespoon at a time, until the desired tartness is reached.
Turn off the heat, transfer to a plate, and sprinkle with toasted garlic.

intro: A sour, savory pata soup filled with vegetables.
ingredients: 40 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Recipe Mix
1 bunch kangkong, stems and leaves separated
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil the pata in 8 cups water over high heat for 15 minutes. Discard the water and rinse the pata thoroughly.
Pressure-cook the pata with 6 cups fresh water and salt for 12 minutes, then transfer it along with the broth to a large pot.
Add the remaining 2 cups water, onion, and gabi. Cover and boil over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, pork cube, and sinigang mix. Cook for 5 minutes until the seasoning dissolves.
Add the long green peppers, eggplant, okra, snake beans, and kangkong stems. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Add the kangkong leaves, turn off the heat, cover, and let soften before serving.

intro: Paella rice with smoky pork sisig, chorizo, and a creamy seasoning drizzle.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and sauté the onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add the chorizo, pork belly, and pork cube. Sauté for 1 minute, then stir in the paella rice and smoked paprika.
Pour in the water, 3 tsp liquid seasoning, and bell pepper. Stir, cover, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender.
Sprinkle with green onions, crack the quail eggs over the top, and add the long green peppers. Cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise with the remaining liquid seasoning, drizzle over the top, and serve with lemon wedges.

intro: Crisp fried camote fritters that make a delicious snack.
ingredients: 2 large yellow sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into thick matchsticks
steps: Combine the flour, baking powder, milk, eggs, and salt until the batter is smooth.
Add the camote and toss until evenly coated.
Heat oil in a pan. Add a cluster of camote, flatten it slightly with a spatula, and do not overcrowd the pan.
Lower the heat and fry until golden brown and crisp on both sides.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with sugar, and serve hot.

intro: A soupy noodle dish with clam broth, pork, hibe, miki, and bihon.
ingredients: 350 g miki or flat egg noodles
Fish sauce, salt, and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil the chicken frames with enough water and salt. Simmer for 30 minutes, then add the clams and cook until they open.
Strain the broth. Shred any chicken meat and remove the clam meat from the shells; set the meat aside.
In another pot, brown the pork in oil, then sauté the garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add the annatto and hibe. Cook for 3 minutes, pour in the broth, add the meat, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the clam meat, season with fish sauce and pepper, and turn off the heat.
Cook and drain the miki and bihon separately according to the package directions. Place in bowls, ladle over the broth, and garnish with spring onions.

intro: Crispy fishballs served with thick, sweet-savory Manong dipping sauce.
steps: Combine the water, soy sauce, cornstarch, flour, brown sugar, shallot, garlic, and salt in a saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until the sauce slowly boils and thickens.
Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the fishballs in batches until crisp and evenly browned.
Drain the fishballs and serve immediately with the warm sauce.

intro: A hearty chop suey with squid balls, chicken liver, and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add the chicken liver and cook for 3–5 minutes, until no longer pink in the center.
Stir in the oyster sauce and chicken broth. Bring to a boil, add the squid balls, cover, and simmer gently for 10–12 minutes.
Increase to medium heat, season with pepper, and add the carrots and cauliflower. Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the snow peas and bell peppers, then add the cabbage. Cover and steam for 3–5 minutes.
Stir gently, add the quail eggs, season with salt, and serve.

intro: Glossy glazed hamon made with prepared cured pork belly for easy serving.
ingredients: 1 kg prepared cured pork belly slab, skin-on
3/4 cup brown sugar, plus more for topping
steps: Place the cured pork belly, pineapple juice, beer, brown sugar, and star anise in a large pot; cover and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and cook for 1 1/2 hours, turning once, until the meat is fork-tender.
Raise the heat to medium and boil the liquid until it becomes a thick glaze; remove the pork and reserve the sauce.
Cool the pork slightly until the surface dries, then sprinkle with brown sugar.
Caramelize the sugar with a blowtorch or under the hottest oven grill until browned. Slice and serve with the glaze and garnishes.

intro: Spicy, tangy sautéed pig's heart with annatto and vegetables.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb pig's heart, boiled until tender and diced
1/2 cup annatto-seed water, made with 1/4 cup water
steps: Heat the oil and sauté the garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the diced pig's heart and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
