Stir in the crushed red pepper and annatto water, then add the bay leaves and 2 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour in the vinegar and let it return to a boil before stirring.
Add the carrots and bell pepper, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 3 minutes before serving.

intro: Sweet-savory fried pindang made with prepared cured pork strips.
ingredients: 1 kg prepared cured pork scotch, cut into 1/4-inch thick strips
steps: Take the prepared cured pork out of the refrigerator about 2 hours before cooking so the center is not cold.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan over very low heat.
Fry the pork for 3 minutes per side so the sugar does not burn too quickly.
Raise the heat to medium and fry for another 2 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Drain briefly and serve with hot rice and freshly chopped tomatoes.

intro: Soft braided loaf filled with creamy adzuki bean and coconut filling.
ingredients: 2 packed cups cooked adzuki beans, drained and mashed
steps: Melt the butter over low heat, add the condensed milk and brown sugar, then mix in the mashed adzuki beans; stir until thick.
Lower the heat and stir for 20-25 minutes; add the coconut cream and cook for 5 more minutes until spreadable, then cool.
Combine the flour, potato flakes, yeast, salt, milk, cream, lightly beaten egg, and sugar; knead for 20 minutes and let rise for 1 hour until 1 1/2 times its size.
Divide the dough in two, flatten each portion, add half the filling, fold, cut into three strips still joined at one end, and braid.
Place in two greased loaf pans and let rise until nearly doubled, about 1 hour.
Brush with egg wash made from the remaining egg and water; bake at 170°C for 40-45 minutes until golden and cooked through.

intro: Crispy pork shank with creamy peanut sauce and kare-kare vegetables.
ingredients: 1 tbsp salt, or more to taste
1/2 cup peanut sauce or unsweetened peanut butter
1 bundle string beans, cut into 3-inch lengths
steps: Boil the pork shanks with the sliced onion, crushed garlic, peppercorns, salt, and water for 1-2 hours until tender; strain and reserve the broth.
Dry the shanks and deep-fry in hot oil until the skin is blistered and crisp.
In 4-5 tablespoons oil, fry the eggplant until lightly browned and cook the string beans until tender-crisp; set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion and minced garlic until soft, then pour in the pork broth and annatto.
Stir in the peanut sauce and glutinous rice flour; simmer until the sauce is thick and smooth.
Serve the crispy shanks with the sauce, eggplant, string beans, and bagoong on the side.

intro: Simple but flavorful monggo enriched with hibi and spinach.
steps: Boil the mung beans in 4 cups water until the water is absorbed and the beans are tender.
In a separate pot, heat the oil and sauté the garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the hibi and cooked mung beans; mix well.
Pour in the remaining 1 1/2 cups water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook for 3 minutes, then season with patis and pepper; cook for 2 more minutes.

intro: Yellow coconut rice dish filled with chicken, chorizo, and toppings.
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thigh meat, cubed
1/2 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
Fish sauce and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat; cook the chorizo for 2 minutes and set aside.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, cook for 3 minutes per side, and set aside.
Add oil if needed; sauté the garlic and onion until translucent.
Mix in both rices and turmeric, stirring over medium heat for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and broth. Arrange the chicken, chorizo, bell pepper, peas, and raisins on top; season and cover.
Cook for 15-20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is cooked. Remove from the heat, top with eggs, and serve.

intro: Crispy mahi-mahi topped with savory tomato-egg sarciado.
steps: Rub the mahi-mahi with 1 tsp garlic salt and let rest for 10 minutes.
Heat the cooking oil; coat the fish in flour, shake off the excess, and fry over medium heat for 8-12 minutes until crisp and medium brown.
Drain the fish and place it on a serving plate.
For the sauce, heat the olive oil and sauté the onion, tomato, and bell pepper; cover and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add the broth, beaten egg, and remaining garlic salt; stir until the egg curdles, then pour over the fish.

intro: Quick sautéed sitaw with ground pork and fresh tomatoes.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the oil over medium heat and sauté the garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add the ground pork and cook until medium brown and no longer pink.
Mix in the tomatoes and cook for 1 minute until they begin to soften.
Add the sitaw and sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in a little water, bring to a boil, and cook until the sitaw is tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve.

intro: Golden croquettes with creamy mashed potato and savory pork giniling filling.
steps: Combine the mashed potato, pork giniling, one egg, flour, salt, and pepper until evenly mixed.
Beat the remaining 2 eggs in one bowl and place the panko in a separate bowl.
Scoop about 2 tablespoons of the mixture and shape into a ball; dip in egg and coat well with panko.
Heat the oil and fry the croquettes over medium heat, turning them, until golden brown on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

intro: Tangy, savory labanos cooked with ground pork and pork liver.
ingredients: Salt and ground pepper, to taste
steps: Sprinkle the labanos with 2 tbsp salt, rub it in, and let rest for 15 minutes. Squeeze, rinse until no longer salty, and squeeze again.
Combine the labanos, pork, liver, sugar, onion, and vinegar. Mix well and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the garlic until golden brown.
Add the marinated mixture and bring to a boil. Cover, lower to low-medium heat, and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper; serve hot with rice.

intro: Quick-sautéed prepared uok in a classic adobo-style seasoning.
ingredients: 250 g prepared cleaned uok, beetle larvae
steps: Rinse and dry the prepared cleaned uok before cooking.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the uok and sauté for 3-4 minutes until heated through and lightly browned.
Mix in the soy sauce, vinegar, and pepper; let boil without stirring for 1 minute.
Stir and cook for another 1-2 minutes until the sauce is slightly thickened, then serve hot.

intro: Serve prepared basi chilled to enjoy its sweet or robust character.
steps: Chill the bottle of prepared basi thoroughly before serving.
Open and pour into small glasses; add ice if desired.
Serve calamansi wedges on the side and drink responsibly.

intro: Savory banana blossom with pork, vinegar, and mild heat.
steps: Soak the banana blossom in water with 3 tbsp salt for 15 minutes. Drain and squeeze out excess water.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the pork belly until lightly browned.
Add the garlic and onion, then sauté until fragrant and the onion is soft.
Stir in the banana blossom and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock and vinegar; bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and cook until tender for 15 minutes.
Add the green chillies, fish sauce, and pepper. Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, then serve.

intro: Tangy bangus belly soup enriched with miso and fresh vegetables.
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot over high heat.
Add the tomatoes and onion; cover and boil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the miso, cover, and cook for 3-5 minutes until fully dissolved.
Carefully add the bangus belly and cook over low-medium heat for 5-7 minutes.
Add the labanos, okra, and siling pansigang. Cover and cook for 5-8 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the sinigang powder and patis, then add the mustasa. Cover and cook for 4 minutes before serving.

intro: Soft sponge cake with thick yema frosting, cheese, and lengua de gato.
ingredients: 2 tsp vanilla extract, for the cake
1 tsp vanilla extract, for the frosting
steps: Melt the cream cheese, 50 g butter, milk, and vanilla in a double boiler; stir until smooth, then let cool.
Sift together the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt. Mix into the cream cheese mixture on low speed, then add the egg yolks and lemon juice.
Beat the egg whites and cream of tartar on high speed until foamy. Gradually add the sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Gently fold the meringue into the batter. Divide between two parchment-lined 8-inch pans and bake in a water bath at 180°C for 1 hour, until a tester comes out clean.
For the frosting, cook the condensed milk, 6 egg yolks, and vanilla over low heat until very thick; stir in the butter.
Cool the cakes, spread warm frosting between and around them, chill, then decorate with lengua de gato and cheddar. Serve cold.

intro: A cold, smooth mango shake sweetened naturally by ripe mangoes.
ingredients: 3 large Filipino mangoes, peeled, frozen, and cubed
steps: Put the frozen mango, ice, water, sugar, and lemon juice, if using, into a blender.
Blend on high until completely smooth, with no large ice pieces remaining.
Taste, pour into two glasses, and serve immediately while very cold.

intro: Sticky, flavorful chicken wings cooked in a sweet-tangy adobo glaze.
steps: In a large pan, sauté the garlic in oil over low heat until golden brown.
Add the chicken wings and fry until lightly browned.
Pour in 1/2 cup water, vinegar, soy sauce, bay leaves, and brown sugar. Bring to a boil.
Simmer over medium-high heat for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is nearly dry.
Continue cooking over medium heat, browning both sides; add a little oil if needed. Season with pepper and serve hot.

intro: Crispy pork belly in a thick, lightly tangy dinuguan sauce with chicharon.
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, in one whole piece
1 can lemonade soda, such as 7-Up or Sprite
steps: Rub the pork belly generously with sea salt, wrap it, and refrigerate for at least one day. Rinse thoroughly.
Pressure-cook the pork with the crushed garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, soy sauce, soda, and enough water to cover for 20–30 minutes after it whistles.
Dry the tender pork and chill for at least 12 hours. Deep-fry while cold, skin-side down, until golden and crisp, then slice.
Using a little frying oil, sauté the chopped garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add the chillies, sinigang mix, vinegar, and pork stock; bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the blood and simmer for 20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, add the crispy pork, and top with chicharon before serving.

intro: Light, sour salmon belly sinigang filled with okra and leafy tops.
ingredients: 1 kg salmon belly, collar, and fins
steps: Place the onion, tomatoes, and water in a pot; bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, add the salmon, okra, Asian eggplants, and tamarind mix.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the salmon is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the spinach and green chillies, then simmer for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Season with fish sauce and freshly ground pepper, then serve immediately.

intro: Chewy fried rice balls coated in sticky caramel syrup.
ingredients: 1/2 cup water, plus more if needed
steps: Combine the glutinous rice flour and 1/2 cup water until a soft but shapeable dough forms.
Scoop out 1 tablespoon portions of dough, roll into balls, and poke a small hole in each.
Heat oil over medium heat. Fry the balls in batches, turning them, until pale golden and doubled in size.
Drain the carioca on paper towels.
In a saucepan, dissolve the sugar in 1/4 cup water and cook over medium-low heat until bubbling.
Turn off the heat, toss in the carioca until coated in syrup, thread onto bamboo sticks, and serve.

intro: Traditional bibingkang galapong that is creamy, buttery, and topped with cheddar.
steps: Soak the malagkit and Jasmine rice overnight in 1 1/2 cups water.
Preheat the oven to 188°C. Drain the rice and process with the coconut cream until very smooth.
Add the eggs, salt, sugar, baking powder, and 4 tbsp melted butter; process for 1–2 minutes until combined.
Line a 9-inch round pan with fresh banana leaves, pour in the batter, and bake for 35 minutes.
Cool slightly, transfer to a plate, and brush with the remaining butter. Sprinkle with cheddar before serving.

intro: Spicy Tuyo Pasta combines salty dried herring, bright lemon, sun-dried tomatoes, and creamy Kesong Puti.
ingredients: 75 g goat's milk feta or Kesong Puti, crumbled
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook pasta according to package directions; reserve some cooking water and drain.
Pan-fry tuyo for 1 minute per side. Cool, remove scales and bones, then flake.
Heat olive oil and sauté garlic. Add sun-dried tomatoes, cayenne, tuyo, and pasta; toss for 1 minute.
Add 3 tablespoons pasta water, lemon juice, and Parmesan; season with salt and pepper, then toss off heat.
Plate pasta and scatter crumbled feta or Kesong Puti over the top.

intro: Creamy ginataang labong with pork belly and gentle chilli heat.
steps: If the bamboo shoots are not fresh, boil them in water for 30 minutes until tender. Drain, cool, and squeeze dry.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the garlic, ginger, chillies, and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in the bamboo shoots and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes until the liquid has reduced.
Add the coconut cream, fish sauce, and pepper. Simmer gently for 5 minutes and serve with rice.

intro: Thick, savory pininyahang manok with liver spread and colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 red bell pepper, cut into squares
1 green bell pepper, cut into squares
Salt and crushed pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the oil and pan-fry the chicken until light brown; remove and set aside.
In the remaining oil, sauté the onion and garlic until the onion softens. Return the chicken to the pan.
Pour in the soy sauce and scrape up the browned bits from the pan. Add the pineapple and water, then bring to a boil.
Stir in the Chicken Cube, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 25 minutes.
Add the liver spread and carrot; cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the bell peppers and season.
Dissolve the cornstarch in 3 tbsp water, pour it into the pan, and stir until thickened. Add the sugar, cook for 1 minute, and serve.

intro: Whole bangus stuffed with sautéed fish flesh, vegetables, and raisins.
ingredients: 1 tbsp soy sauce, for the filling
1 tbsp soy sauce, for the marinade
steps: Clean and scale the bangus without cutting open the body. Make an opening beneath the gills, remove the innards and flesh, and keep the skin intact.
Rinse the skin and marinate it in 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp juice, and 1 tbsp oil. Cut up the fish flesh, steam until cooked, then flake it and remove the bones.
Sauté the garlic and shallots in oil. Add the carrot and potato and cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, then add the capsicum for 2 minutes.
Mix in the flaked fish, raisins, pickle relish, soy sauce, and tomato paste; cook for 2 minutes. Season, cool slightly, then stir in the flour and egg.
Fill the skin with the stuffing, place on baking paper, and brush with oil. Bake at 180°C for 12–15 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Cool for 5 minutes, slice, and serve.

intro: Hot salabat with bright lemon and gentle honey sweetness.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized piece young fresh ginger, thinly sliced
steps: Put the water and sliced ginger in a small pot or kettle and bring to a boil.
Reduce to low heat and simmer gently for 2 minutes to draw out the ginger flavor.
Strain or pour into a teapot, then stir in the honey and lemon juice until the honey dissolves.
Pour into cups and serve hot.

intro: Hearty pochero with fried tilapia, saba bananas, chickpeas, and a savory tomato broth.
steps: Rub the tilapia with salt, including the cavity, and rest for 5 minutes. Fry over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes per side until golden; set aside.
In a clean pan, cook the pork fat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until rendered and crisp.
Sauté the garlic and onion for 2 minutes, then add the Chinese sausage for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and water, bring to a boil, then add the potato. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the saba bananas and chickpeas; cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the sitaw, fish sauce, and pepper.
Carefully return the fish and simmer for 2 minutes. Place the pechay on top, cover for 1 minute, and serve.

intro: Rich soy-lemon beef with a sesame aroma and tender onions.
ingredients: 1 medium white onion, sliced into rings
1 tbsp cornstarch, dissolved in 2 tbsp cold water
steps: Combine the soy sauce, sugar, and lemon juice. Marinate the steak in it for 30 minutes.
Remove the steak from the marinade and reserve the marinade. Heat the oil and sear the steak for 3 minutes.
Pour in the reserved marinade, water, and sesame oil. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes; add water if needed.
When the liquid has reduced by half, stir in the cornstarch slurry until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper, add the onion, cover, and cook for 2 minutes.
Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

intro: Creamy sweet-savory macaroni salad with chicken, ham, pineapple, and cheese.
ingredients: 8 oz chicken breast, boiled and shredded
Salt and crushed pepper, to taste
steps: Boil the elbow macaroni according to the package timing until al dente, then drain and cool.
In a large bowl, combine the mayonnaise, ham, chicken, pineapple, carrot, celery, pickle relish, onion, cheese, sugar, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Add the cooled macaroni and toss until evenly coated with the dressing.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Toss again before serving cold.

intro: A simple but savory sautéed upo dish with crisp pork belly and tomatoes.
ingredients: 250 g pork belly, cut into small pieces
1 large upo, about 15 inches long, sliced 1 cm thick and 5 cm wide
steps: Heat oil in a pan and fry the pork belly until crisp.
Add the garlic and onion; sauté until the onion is nearly translucent.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, until they begin to soften.
Add the upo and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock, season with salt and sugar, and simmer for 8 minutes, until the upo is tender but still intact.
Season with pepper and serve hot.

intro: Kalderobo is a rich pork adobo braise finished with creamy coconut, peanut butter, and liver spread.
steps: Combine soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, peppercorns, and 6 cloves garlic; coat pork and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Heat oil over medium-high heat and brown the drained pork on all sides; set aside.
Sauté remaining garlic and onion in the pot until fragrant, then cook both capsicums briefly until slightly softened.
Return pork, add marinade, coconut milk, stock, peanut butter, liver spread, and chilies; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for about 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until pork is tender.
Add potatoes and carrot; simmer until tender, then adjust seasoning and serve.

intro: Flavorful grilled liempo with a barbecue-calamansi marinade.
steps: Mix the barbecue sauce, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, calamansi juice, canola oil, and pepper until combined.
Add the pork belly and coat it thoroughly in the marinade. Cover and marinate for at least 3 hours.
Heat the grill over medium heat. Grill one side for 2 minutes, brushing it with the remaining marinade.
Turn the pork over, brush the other side, and continue turning and brushing until the pork is cooked through with a nice char.
Transfer to a plate and serve hot with rice.

intro: Almondigas is a light, comforting misua soup with meatballs and tender patola.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add meatballs and chicken stock; bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Add patola and simmer for 5 minutes until tender.
Add misua and simmer for 2 minutes until softened.
Season with fish sauce, salt if needed, and black pepper; serve immediately.

intro: Crisp turon filled with sweet saba bananas and langka.
ingredients: 1 cup langka, cut into long strips
steps: Separate the wrappers and cover them with a damp paper towel to keep them from drying out.
Peel the saba bananas and halve them lengthwise. Coat each piece well in brown sugar.
Place one sugared banana piece and a few strips of langka near the edge of a wrapper. Fold in the sides, roll it up, and moisten the end with water to seal.
Heat the oil over low heat. Fry the turon in batches for 3–5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

intro: Crisp breaded chicken is topped with a silky, vegetable-studded ala King sauce and sweet corn.
ingredients: 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, plus 3 tbsp for sauce
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pound chicken evenly; season with 1/8 teaspoon each salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Coat chicken in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs; rest 5 minutes.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown and cooked through; drain and plate.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter, sauté corn for 2 minutes, season with 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Melt remaining butter; sauté garlic, onion, and carrot for 2 minutes. Stir in flour, then gradually add milk until thick.
Season sauce with chicken powder, remaining garlic powder, salt, and pepper; stir in cream, pimiento, and parsley for 30 seconds. Spoon over chicken with corn.

intro: Filipino Cocido is a hearty mixed-meat broth with chorizo, vegetables, chickpeas, and saba bananas.
ingredients: 8 cups water, plus more as needed
steps: Heat oil in a large soup pot and brown beef shanks, pork ribs, and pork hock; remove.
Sauté garlic and onions in the same pot, then add peppercorns and return the meats.
Add water to cover; boil, then simmer on low for 1 hour.
Add chorizo and simmer 1 hour longer, adding water if needed to keep meats covered.
Add saba and cook 15 minutes. Add chickpeas, cabbage, and green beans; cook 5 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve the meats, vegetables, and broth together.

intro: Morisqueta Tostada is smoky, savory fried rice with Chinese sausage, ham, shrimp, and egg.
ingredients: 1/3 cup chopped Chinese ham or other ham
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
3 spring onions, chopped, whites and greens separated
steps: Heat peanut oil over medium heat; sauté garlic and spring onion whites for 30 seconds.
Raise heat to high, add Chinese sausage, and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add rice and ham, breaking up clumps; stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes.
Push rice aside, scramble eggs in the empty space, then mix through the rice and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and soy sauce; season with salt and pepper, then stir-fry 1 minute.
Toss in spring onion greens and serve hot.

intro: Sushi Bake layers seasoned rice with spicy salmon and creamy kani for an easy shareable sushi-style meal.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Sriracha, plus more for serving
2 tbsp Kewpie mayonnaise, plus more for serving
steps: Bake salmon at 220°C for 10 minutes; flake it and mix with 2 tablespoons Sriracha.
Mix kani with 2 tablespoons Kewpie mayonnaise and roasted sesame dressing.
Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook with cold water, covered, then rest 10 minutes.
Fold vinegar through rice and press lightly into a 12-by-8-inch casserole dish.
Arrange alternating strips of cream cheese with spicy salmon and kani mixture; bake at 200°C for 10–15 minutes.
Top kani sections with avocado, furikake, mayonnaise, and Sriracha; serve with nori and gari.

intro: Gayabon is a creamy taro-leaf dish enriched with crisp pork belly, bagoong, and coconut.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pork with salt and pepper. Boil with 1 cup water until dry, then fry in its rendered fat until browned and crisp.
Leave 3 tablespoons fat in the wok; sauté garlic, ginger, and onion for 1 minute.
Add 3 cups coconut milk; boil, then simmer over medium-high heat for 20–30 minutes until thick and oily.
Add remaining coconut milk, bagoong, and taro leaves. Gently submerge leaves without overmixing.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, adding a little water only if needed; stir gently to prevent sticking.
Add coconut cream, simmer 10 minutes, season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve.

intro: Brazo de Mercedes is a tender baked meringue roll filled with a lemony cashew custard.
steps: For the filling, combine condensed milk, 10 yolks, 1 tablespoon vanilla, 1/4 cup cashews, and zest of 1 lemon over low heat.
Stir until a thick paste forms, then cool completely. Alternatively, reduce full-cream milk with 1 cup sugar to 2 cups before making the same filling.
Heat oven to 200°C. Beat egg whites and cream of tartar to stiff peaks; gradually beat in 3/4 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Spread meringue over butter-greased baking paper on a large tray. Bake about 10 minutes until browned.
Invert onto another greased, paper-lined tray with the browned side down; cool 15 minutes.
Spread with filling, roll into a log, and dust with icing sugar.

intro: Pork Adobo with Sitaw pairs tender soy-vinegar pork belly with crisp-tender snake beans.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb pork belly, cut into serving pieces
2 cups beef broth, plus more if needed
steps: Mix pork with soy sauce, garlic, and pepper; marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat oil and sauté onion until soft. Add pork with its marinade and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add beef broth, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 45 minutes or until pork is tender.
Add vinegar and allow the liquid to return to a boil before stirring.
Add sitaw and cook 3 minutes. Stir in brown sugar and cook 5–8 minutes until beans are tender.
Serve hot with the adobo sauce.

intro: Ginataang Talong is a velvety coconut stew of eggplant, pork belly, and mild green chilies.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pork with salt and rest 10 minutes. Brown in oil on all sides, then set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion in the same wok. Return pork, add water and half the coconut milk, and bring to a boil.
Simmer on low for 15 minutes until pork is tender.
Add remaining coconut milk, bring to a boil, then add eggplant and chilies. Simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes until eggplant is tender.
Add coconut cream and simmer on low for 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: Beef Pares sa Kanto serves deeply braised, star-anise beef alongside fragrant garlic fried rice.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons oil, sauté beef fat if available for 2 minutes, then sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until onion softens.
Add beef and cook about 5 minutes until medium brown. Add water, star anise, and Beef Cube.
Cover and simmer on low for 2–2 1/2 hours until beef is very tender.
Season with soy sauce, brown sugar, onion powder, pepper, and salt. Stir in cornstarch slurry and simmer until lightly thickened.
For garlic rice, sauté crushed garlic in 3 tablespoons oil until golden; add rice, salt, and cook 3–5 minutes.
Serve beef pares and garlic rice in separate bowls, each topped with green onions.

intro: Adobong Sitaw with Lechon Kawali crowns tangy braised snake beans with crackly fried pork belly.
steps: Boil pork belly in 4 cups water, covered over medium heat, for 30 minutes. Cool pork and reserve 1 cup cooking liquid.
Season pork with salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Fry in hot oil until light brown and crisp; drain.
Heat 3 tablespoons frying oil and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add sitaw and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add soy sauce and reserved pork liquid; cook 5–8 minutes.
Add vinegar and bring back to a boil. Stir in onion powder and remaining pepper.
Transfer sitaw to a bowl and top with crispy lechon kawali.

intro: Siopao Asado features fluffy steamed buns wrapped around sweet-savory, slow-braised pork filling.
ingredients: 3 cups dumpling flour, plus 1/2 cup for dusting
2 tbsp cornstarch, dissolved in 1/3 cup water
1 cup water, plus more as needed
1 tbsp vinegar per litre of steaming water
steps: Sauté garlic in oil, add pork, and stir-fry 3 minutes. Add water, soy sauce, brown sugar, and five-spice; simmer on low about 2 hours until shreddable.
Stir in hoisin and cornstarch slurry; simmer until thick, season with salt, and cool.
Mix yeast, 2 teaspoons sugar, and lukewarm water; leave warm for 30 minutes until foamy.
Mix remaining dough ingredients except baking powder; knead smooth and elastic. Rise in an oiled bowl for 2 hours until doubled.
Deflate dough, knead in baking powder for 5 minutes, divide into 8–10 rounds, fill with pork, seal, and proof 30 minutes.
Steam over water with vinegar for 20–25 minutes until buns are puffy and cooked through.

intro: Spabok is a seafood spaghetti dish coated in a vivid crab-fat and annatto sauce with crunchy toppings.
steps: Cook spaghetti in boiling water according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Boil shrimp in 3 cups water until cooked. Reserve liquid, shell shrimp, and crush shells to extract flavor through a fine sieve.
Blend crab meat, crab fat, shrimp broth, annatto powder, and fish sauce until smooth.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil. Add crab mixture and smoked fish, then bring to a boil.
Stir cornstarch with a little water, add it, and simmer until thick; loosen with water if necessary.
Spoon sauce over spaghetti and garnish with shrimp, chicharon, spring onions, egg, fried garlic, and lemon.

intro: Chicken Castanets is a Spanish-inspired chicken braise with chorizo, mushrooms, and burst cherry tomatoes.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate chicken in soy sauce and Worcestershire sauce overnight.
Sear chicken in olive oil over high heat until golden on both sides; remove.
Over low heat, sauté garlic until lightly browned, then add onion and cook until soft.
Raise heat to medium, stir-fry chorizo 1 minute, then add carrot and mushrooms for 2 minutes.
Add stock, scraping browned bits from the pan. Return chicken with thyme, cover, and simmer 20 minutes.
Add tomatoes, cook over high heat 5 minutes to reduce sauce, season, and serve.

intro: Ginisang Sigarilyas is a quick pork and winged-bean sauté with tomato and fish sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until softened.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
Add water, cover, and cook until the liquid evaporates and pork is tender.
Add sigarilyas and sauté for 3 minutes until bright and crisp-tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper; serve hot with rice.

intro: Mango and Cheese Swirl Ice Cream layers bright mango custard with creamy cheddar-studded cheese ice cream.
ingredients: 1 large ripe mango, yielding 1/2 cup purée and 1/4 cup cubes
Red and yellow food coloring, optional
steps: Make separate bases: heat one half of cream, milk, sugar, cream cheese, and vanilla; heat remaining cream, milk, and sugar in another pan to a gentle simmer.
Whisk 2 yolks in each bowl. Slowly temper each with its matching hot base, then return both custards to their pans.
Cook over low-medium heat, stirring constantly, 5–10 minutes until each coats a spoon. Cool, cover surface, and chill at least 6 hours.
Mix mango purée with lemon juice and optional coloring; reserve mango cubes. Churn both custards separately according to the machine instructions.
Add cheddar near the end of churning the cheese ice cream and mango cubes near the end of churning the mango ice cream.
Layer softened churned ice creams in a loaf pan, swirl lightly, and freeze until firm.

intro: A light, gingery fish soup that lets fresh talakitok shine.
ingredients: 1 large talakitok (trevally), about 1 kg, cut into sections
1 bunch sweet potato tops or pechay, trimmed
steps: Bring the water, tomato, ginger, onion, lemongrass, and chillies to a boil in a pot.
Add talakitok, reduce to medium heat, and cook for 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Add sweet potato tops or pechay and spring onions; season with fish sauce and pepper.
Simmer for 2 minutes, then serve hot.

intro: Hinanggup is a light, smoky bangus soup brightened with tomatoes and lemon.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season the bangus with salt and black pepper. Arrange skin-side up on a greased grill pan with 1 cup water underneath.
Grill on high for 8–10 minutes, until the skin has charred spots. Reserve the pan liquid.
Bring the remaining 4 cups water and reserved liquid to a boil in a soup pot.
Add tomatoes, red onion, and spring onions; cook over medium heat for 1 minute.
Flake the fish into large pieces, add it to the broth, and simmer on low for 2 minutes.
Season with salt, squeeze in lemon juice, and serve hot.

intro: Bok Choy Guisado is a simple pork-and-shrimp stir-fry simmered briefly with tender baby bok choy.
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add pork and cook about 10 minutes until medium brown.
Add shrimp and cook 3 minutes until opaque.
Add bok choy and stir-fry 3–5 minutes until beginning to wilt.
Add chicken stock, fish sauce, and pepper; bring to a boil and cook 5 minutes.
Serve warm with white rice.

intro: Monggo with Tuyo is a savory mung bean stew brightened with malunggay, tomato, and salty dried fish.
ingredients: 6 bottled tuyo or fried tuyo, heads removed
6 cups water, plus more as needed
steps: Bring 5 cups water to a boil. Add monggo, cover, and cook over low-medium heat until soft and most liquid is absorbed.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion, tomato, and garlic until onion softens.
Add tuyo and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in cooked monggo, malunggay, fish sauce, and remaining 1 cup water.
Cook uncovered 3–7 minutes, adding water if desired for a looser stew.
Season with black pepper and serve hot.

intro: A creamy, sweet-savory Filipino macaroni salad packed with chicken, ham, fruit, and vegetables.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring the water and 1 tsp salt to a boil. Add chicken, cover, and simmer over medium heat for 16–18 minutes; cool and dice.
Cook elbow macaroni in the chicken cooking liquid according to package directions. Drain well and place in a large bowl.
Whisk mayonnaise, optional all-purpose cream, onion powder, sugar, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Toss macaroni with chicken, ham, onion, celery, peas, bell peppers, relish, pineapple, and carrots. Fold in dressing until evenly coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Serve chilled.

intro: Sarciadong Pechay is a quick, savory pechay dish finished with tender ribbons of egg.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until fragrant and softened.
Add pechay and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Pour in water and bring it to a boil.
Drizzle beaten egg around the pan and gently stir until the egg sets.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Serve immediately with rice.

intro: Tender goat skin is chilled in a sharp, spicy vinegar dressing.
steps: Boil goat skin with water and crushed ginger for 1 hour, or until tender; drain and cool.
Chop the cooled skin into small pieces.
Whisk vinegar and sugar until dissolved, then stir in fish sauce, minced ginger, onion, chillies, and black pepper.
Mix in goat skin, onion powder, and chili liquid seasoning until evenly coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

intro: This hearty pancit canton-style noodle dish features tender chicken offal and crisp vegetables in a savory sauce.
steps: Heat a wok until very hot, add peanut oil, and stir-fry pork, chicken hearts, and gizzards until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Reduce to medium-high heat. Stir-fry garlic, ginger, and shallot; add garlic sprouts for 30 seconds, then carrot for 30 seconds. Set aside.
Whisk cornstarch with chicken stock, hoisin sauce, soy sauce, and Chinese cooking wine. Pour into the wok and bring to a boil.
Add noodles and toss until coated with sauce. Return meat and vegetables, add bean sprouts, and stir-fry for 1 minute before serving.

intro: A festive Filipino chicken macaroni salad with pineapple, cheese, raisins, and a creamy mayonnaise dressing.
steps: Bring 1 quart water and 1 tsp salt to a boil. Add chicken, cover, and simmer over medium heat for 22 minutes; cool and shred.
Boil macaroni in 3 quarts water with 1 tsp salt for about 9 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until al dente. Drain.
Toss macaroni and shredded chicken in a large bowl. Add pineapple, pimiento, bell pepper, raisins, carrots, relish, and cheese.
Fold in mayonnaise and garlic powder. Season with remaining salt and black pepper, then serve or chill until cold.

intro: Puto Ube is a soft steamed rice cake with earthy ube and a cheesy finish.
steps: Sift rice flour, all-purpose flour, cornstarch, sugar, baking powder, and salt into a bowl.
Add grated ube, coconut milk, evaporated milk, ube flavoring, melted butter, and food gel; stir only until combined.
Fill greased puto molds or silicone muffin cups three-quarters full.
Cover the steamer lid with cloth, then steam for 20 minutes, until a tester comes out clean.
Cool slightly, unmold, top with grated cheese, and serve.

intro: Creamy monggo and salty dilis make a deeply satisfying everyday stew.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until the onion softens.
Add dilis and cook for 1 minute, then sauté soaked mung beans for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add water, bring to a boil, then cook on low until the beans are soft and mushy; add water if needed.
Stir in patis and black pepper, then add spinach.
Cook for 3 minutes until spinach wilts, then serve.

intro: Lechon Sauce is a sweet-tangy, liver-based Filipino condiment for roasted meats.
steps: Season pork liver with salt and pepper; rest for 5 minutes, then grill until fully cooked. Cool and chop.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onions until softened.
Add liver and cook for 1 minute. Pour in vinegar and bring to a boil.
Stir in brown sugar and water; bring back to a boil, then add breadcrumbs and simmer for 2 minutes.
Blend the mixture until smooth, return it to the wok, and bring it just to a boil.
Season with onion powder, salt, and pepper. Cool slightly and serve as a condiment.

intro: Pancit Cabagan is a saucy egg noodle dish crowned with crisp pork chicharon and quail eggs.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook fresh egg noodles according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Season pork belly with salt. Fry in a hot oiled wok until browned and crisp; remove. Sauté garlic and onion in the same wok.
Stir-fry pork liver for 1 minute. Add carrot, French beans, and cabbage; cook 2 minutes, then remove vegetables.
Whisk cornstarch with 1 cup stock. Boil remaining stock with soy sauce, hoisin, and oyster sauce; add slurry and simmer until thickened. Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Fold noodles and half the vegetables into sauce off heat. Plate and top with remaining vegetables, pork belly, chicharon, and quail eggs; serve with lemon or calamansi.

intro: Cooked meatballs become a quick, glossy adobo main dish.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and fry garlic until light brown, watching closely so it does not burn.
Add meatballs, peppercorns, and bay leaves; toss briefly.
Add soy sauce, beef broth, and sugar; stir and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, adding vinegar and a little water if the sauce dries out.
Taste, season with salt if needed, and serve.

intro: Creamy Sipo Egg with Chicken Gizzard combines tender gizzards, vegetables, and quail eggs in a rich sauce.
ingredients: 62 g Knorr Cream of Mushroom Soup
steps: Boil quail eggs for 2 minutes, cool, peel, and set aside.
Boil gizzards in 5 cups water, covered over low heat, for 45 minutes or until tender; drain.
Melt butter with oil in a pan. Sauté garlic and onion until softened and lightly browned.
Add gizzards and sauté for 2 minutes. Dissolve mushroom soup in 3 cups water, add, and bring to a boil.
Add carrot, corn, jicama, and peas; cook uncovered over low-medium heat for 2 minutes.
Stir in cream and quail eggs. Season with salt and pepper, then serve warm with rice.

intro: Braised pata and silky bihon are brought together with rich, sweet-savory gravy.
ingredients: 2 small pork legs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 tablespoon cornstarch, dissolved in 1/2 cup water
400 g bihon, soaked 15 minutes and drained
steps: Brown minced whole garlic in peanut oil; brown pork legs, add pork stock and shiitake, cover with water, then simmer gently for 2 hours.
Reserve 2 cups cooking stock. Add soy sauce, hoisin, oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar, cornstarch slurry, star anise, bay leaves, peppercorns, and sesame oil.
Simmer pata over medium heat for 30 minutes until the sauce is reduced to thick gravy.
Sauté garlic and shallots in oil until soft. Over very high heat, stir-fry bihon, cabbage, carrot, and beans.
Add reserved stock 1/2 cup at a time plus about 1 cup pata gravy; stir-fry about 5 minutes until noodles are tender.
Pile bihon onto a platter and top with pata, mushrooms, and remaining gravy.

intro: Adobong Itlog turns boiled eggs into a rich, tangy adobo-style dish for warm rice.
steps: Cover eggs with water in a pot, boil for 10 minutes, then drain, peel, and set aside.
Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté garlic until lightly browned, then cook onion until soft.
Add oyster sauce, soy sauce, and vinegar. Bring to a boil without stirring immediately.
Add water, bay leaves, and peppercorns; simmer 10 minutes. Gently turn in eggs.
Add sugar and Maggi Magic Sarap. Cook until sauce reduces slightly, then garnish with green onions and serve with rice.

intro: Pinatuyong Pork Hamonado is pork belly slowly glazed with pineapple, soy sauce, and brown sugar.
ingredients: 1 can (20 oz) pineapple chunks, juice reserved
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat and fry pork belly until light brown on both sides.
Add onion and garlic; sauté until the onion softens. Stir in soy sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Add pineapple juice, water, and Knorr Pork Cube. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low until pork is tender.
Stir in brown sugar and half the pineapple chunks. Cook until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and pepper, then continue cooking until the sauce has evaporated.
Fold in remaining pineapple chunks and serve.

intro: This clean chicken soup gains sweetness from vegetables and rice-wash water.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and brown chicken on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add more oil if needed, then sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Return chicken, add rice-wash water and peppercorns, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrot; simmer for 15 minutes until nearly tender.
Add Chinese cabbage and asparagus, simmer 5 minutes, season with fish sauce, and serve.

intro: Maruya is a crisp-edged saba banana fritter dusted with sugar.
ingredients: 4 saba bananas, each sliced lengthwise into 3 pieces
steps: Whisk flour, baking powder, milk, egg, and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Fold the sliced saba bananas into the batter until coated.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Add banana slices individually, allowing space between them.
Lower heat and fry until golden brown and cooked through, turning as needed.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with sugar, and serve warm.

intro: Ginisang Pechay is a simple pork and bok choy sauté with a light fish sauce broth.
ingredients: 1 lb baby bok choy or pechay, chopped
steps: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until softened.
Add pork and cook for 5 minutes, stirring until lightly browned.
Stir in fish sauce and black pepper. Add water, cover, and simmer 10–15 minutes until pork is tender.
Add pechay and cook only a few seconds. Turn off heat, rest 5 minutes, and serve hot.

intro: Dinuguan Laman-Loob is a deeply savory pork offal stew with a tangy, peppery pork-blood sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb pig's small intestine, cleaned, boiled until tender, and sliced
1 tbsp powdered tamarind soup base mix (sinigang sa sampaloc mix)
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add heart, liver, and prepared intestine; cook for 5 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add cooking wine, fish sauce, black pepper, and water. Cover and simmer 30–35 minutes.
Add tamarind mix, chilies, and vinegar; bring back to a boil. Slowly pour in pork blood while stirring continuously.
Cook over low-medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is cooked through. Serve hot with buttered puto.

intro: Eggplant is folded into a savory meat-and-egg omelet patty.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil eggplants in salted water for 5 minutes. Cool, peel, and flatten each intact eggplant with a fork.
Sauté garlic and onion in a little oil. Add beef and pork and cook until lightly browned; stir-fry capsicum for 30 seconds, then cool.
Beat eggs with the cooked meat mixture; season with salt and pepper.
Over low heat, oil a 7- to 9-inch nonstick pan. Add enough egg mixture to coat it, place an eggplant on top, and cover with more egg.
Cover and cook 4 to 6 minutes until set underneath. Flip carefully and cook 3 minutes more.
Repeat with remaining ingredients and serve with ketchup.

intro: Tinapa Fried Rice is a smoky, turmeric-tinted breakfast rice with crisp smoked fish and egg.
ingredients: 150 g flaked tinapang galunggong or other smoked fish
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Break up cold rice with clean hands until no clumps remain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic until fragrant, then add smoked fish and cook until golden with crisp edges.
Add turmeric and rice. Raise heat to high and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Push rice aside and add beaten eggs. Let set before scrambling and mixing through the rice.
Add spring onions and stir-fry 2 minutes. Season with Maggi Savor, pepper, and salt to taste.

intro: Beef Sinigang sa Kamias is a deeply savory beef soup with the sharp fruitiness of kamias.
steps: Bring 5 cups water and beef broth to a boil. Add tomatoes, onion, and kamias; cook for 5–8 minutes.
Add beef and simmer over low-medium heat for 45 minutes.
Add gabi and simmer for 45 minutes more, until beef is tender.
Bring remaining 4 cups water to a boil. Blanch okra, eggplant, and beans for 3 minutes; blanch spinach for 45 seconds, then drain.
Season the beef broth with fish sauce, adding water if needed.
Divide beef, gabi, and broth among bowls, top with blanched vegetables, and serve warm.

intro: Pineapple-marinated pork adobo cooks down until its own fat glistens.
steps: Mix pork and pineapple juice; marinate for at least 3 hours. Separate pork from marinade and reserve the liquid.
Heat oil and sauté garlic until beginning to brown. Add pork and cook until lightly browned outside.
Add soy sauce, bay leaves, and peppercorns; stir for 2 minutes.
Add vinegar and reserved marinade, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low until pork is tender.
Uncover, stir in fish sauce, and cook over medium heat until the sauce evaporates and pork renders fat. Serve with rice.

intro: Kusahos is crisp fried, vinegar-soy cured beef traditionally dried before cooking.
ingredients: 1 kg beef rump steak, thinly sliced
steps: Mix cane vinegar, soy sauce, crushed garlic, and black pepper in a nonreactive bowl.
Massage the beef with the marinade. Refrigerate uncovered overnight to cure and dry the surface.
Arrange beef on a rack over a tray and dry in direct sun beneath a mesh cover for one day, repeating if still moist.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry dried beef until cooked through and crisp at the edges.
Drain briefly and serve warm with rice.

intro: These Filipino barbecue skewers pair sweet banana ketchup marinade with charred pork and juicy chicken.
steps: Mix Knorr Liquid Seasoning, soy sauce, banana ketchup, calamansi juice, garlic, sugar, and pepper into a marinade.
Place pork and chicken in separate resealable bags. Divide half the marinade between them, seal, and refrigerate at least 6 hours.
Thread pork onto soaked bamboo skewers. Combine the reserved marinade with cooking oil for basting.
Grill pork over medium heat, turning and basting every few minutes, until fully cooked and lightly charred.
Grill chicken the same way until browned and its thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C). Serve with rice and spicy vinegar.

intro: Pork and garden vegetables simmer gently in a spicy bagoong coconut sauce.
ingredients: 2 large Asian eggplants, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 squash or buttercup, cut into 1-inch pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and brown pork belly; push it to one side.
Add garlic and onion and sauté until fragrant and soft.
Add squash and okra, stir-fry 2 minutes, then cover on low heat for 5 minutes.
Add string beans and eggplant; stir-fry 2 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk, water, bagoong, and chillies. Cover and simmer over medium heat for 5 to 8 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with black pepper and fish sauce, then serve with rice.

intro: Bihongke is a comforting chicken bihon soup brightened with quail eggs, wood ear fungus, and fried garlic.
ingredients: 1 cup rehydrated wood ear fungus, sliced
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock, add wood ear fungus, and bring to a boil.
Add flaked chicken and bihon. Cook for 6 minutes, adding stock if the noodles absorb too much liquid.
Add carrots and quail eggs, then turn off heat. Season with fish sauce and white pepper; garnish with spring onions and fried garlic.

intro: Steamed Cassava Cake is a rich, chewy cassava dessert topped with melted-style cheese.
ingredients: 1/2 cup shredded quick-melt cheese or sharp cheddar
steps: Bring the steaming water to a steady boil.
Whisk grated cassava, coconut milk, condensed milk, eggs, and melted butter in a large bowl until evenly mixed.
Pour into individual molds and arrange in a steamer.
Steam for 45 minutes, until firm throughout and no longer wet in the center.
Cool the molds, unmold the cakes, top with shredded cheese, and serve.

intro: Sinigang na Bangus sa Miso is a tamarind-sour fish soup enriched with mellow miso.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine onion, tomatoes, and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add bangus, miso, and tamarind mix. Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, until the fish is cooked.
Add mustard greens and green finger chilies; simmer for 2 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Delicate misua turns a simple beef and zucchini broth into a quick meal.
ingredients: 1 beef bouillon cube or 2 to 3 teaspoons beef powder
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add ground beef and cook until light brown.
Add bouillon and water, stir, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add zucchini and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Add misua, fish sauce, and black pepper; cook 3 to 5 minutes until noodles are tender.
Add quail eggs and green onions, then serve.

intro: Canned sardines make this upo and misua soup fast, comforting, and flavorful.
ingredients: 400 g canned sardines in tomato sauce
1/2 small upo (bottle gourd), peeled and sliced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot and sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add sardines with their tomato sauce and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water and upo, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 8 minutes.
Add misua and simmer for 2 minutes until tender.
Season with fish sauce, salt if needed, and black pepper; turn off heat and serve.

intro: Juicy mixed-meat patties are finished with a mushroom-rich brown gravy.
ingredients: 4 cups beef stock, or 2 Filipino Knorr beef cubes dissolved in 4 cups water
Finely ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix beef, pork, onion powder, pepper, and salt. Shape into 1 1/2-cm-thick patties.
Heat oil over high until smoking, reduce to medium-high, and fry patties 2 1/2 minutes per side. Cover on a platter with foil.
In another pan, melt butter with 1/4 cup patty oil over low heat.
Whisk in flour and cook until light brown. Gradually add beef stock while stirring smooth.
Season, bring to a gentle boil, then simmer on low until thick. Add mushrooms and simmer 1 minute.
Spoon gravy over patties and serve with rice.

intro: Liver Steak pairs quickly fried liver with a bright lemon-soy onion gravy.
ingredients: 700 g pork or beef liver, thinly sliced
2 large white onions, sliced into rings
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate liver in 1/2 cup soy sauce, juice of 2 lemons, salt, and pepper for 3 hours.
Drain thoroughly and bring liver to room temperature; pat dry if needed.
Pan-fry liver in hot oil for 3 minutes per side, until cooked through. Set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion rings briefly, keeping them slightly crisp.
Whisk cornstarch with beef stock and remaining soy sauce. Add to the pan and boil until lightly thickened.
Stir in juice of the remaining lemon, salt, and pepper. Pour sauce and onions over liver.

intro: A classic Filipino omelet layers tender eggs with sautéed tomato and red onion.
steps: Beat eggs with sea salt and black pepper in a medium bowl.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Pour in eggs and tilt the pan to spread them evenly. Cook 3–4 minutes until the underside is set.
Flip with a wide spatula and cook 3 minutes more, until set through. Transfer to a plate and serve with pandesal or garlic rice.

intro: Bagoong Guisado is a sweet-savory cooked shrimp paste condiment enriched with pork and tomato.
steps: Heat a pan over medium heat and sear pork until it renders its fat.
Add garlic, onion, and tomato. Sauté for 3 minutes.
Stir in shrimp paste, sugar, and vinegar.
Cover and cook on low for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and fragrant.
Transfer to a bowl and serve as a condiment.

intro: Binondo Style Crab Foo Yong is a seafood-packed omelette served under glossy savory sauce.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh crab meat or drained canned crab meat
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
steps: Whisk seafood stock and 2 tablespoons cornstarch until smooth, then beat in eggs.
Mix in crab, surimi, bean sprouts, spring onions, onion, garlic, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Cook half the mixture, covered, for 4 minutes until golden underneath.
Flip carefully, cover, and cook 4 minutes more. Repeat with remaining mixture.
Simmer broth, oyster sauce, remaining soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil in a saucepan.
Stir in cornstarch slurry until thick. Pour over omelettes and serve hot with rice.

intro: Tokwa at Baboy Humba braises pork belly in pineapple, soy, and salted black beans before adding crisp tofu.
steps: Heat oil in a wok and deep-fry tofu until golden and crisp. Remove and set aside.
Transfer 3 tbsp frying oil to a clean pan. Sauté garlic until browning, add onion, then cook pork until lightly browned.
Add soy sauce and cook until reduced by half. Add pineapple juice and vinegar, cover, and bring to a boil.
Stir in salted black beans. Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 35 minutes.
Add water and brown sugar; cover and simmer over low heat about 40 minutes until pork is very tender. Add star anise for 5 minutes, then discard it.
Season with pepper, fold in fried tofu, and cook 2 minutes before serving.

intro: This festive steamed pork roll is studded with egg and sausage.
ingredients: 8 Vienna sausages, chipolata, or cocktail hotdogs, sliced
4 hard-boiled eggs, halved, or 16 boiled quail eggs
steps: Mix pork, mashed bananas, flour, pickles, carrot, onion, raisins, peas, beaten eggs, salt, and pepper thoroughly.
Divide mixture between foil sheets. Arrange hard-boiled eggs and sliced sausages down each center.
Shape into tight cylinders and wrap securely in foil.
Steam for 1 hour until firm and cooked through.
Cool for 15 minutes, slice while still wrapped, unwrap each slice, and serve plain or shallow-fried with ketchup.

intro: Creamy pork pastel combines tender pork, chorizo, and vegetables in a thick sauce.
ingredients: 1/4 cup flour dissolved in 1/2 cup water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil over high heat and brown pork lightly on all sides; remove.
Melt butter in the pot and sauté garlic and onion. Add chorizo and cook for 2 minutes.
Add stock and return pork. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Add potato, carrot, and mushrooms; simmer 10 minutes until pork is tender.
Add cream, flour slurry, and capsicums. Simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Lechon Lomi is a thick, comforting miki noodle soup that gives leftover roasted pork a second life.
ingredients: 1 beef cube or 3 tsp beef powder
3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
steps: Heat oil in a wide pot and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add lechon and beef cube or powder. Cook for 5 minutes, then add water and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer 30 minutes. Stir in soy sauce and fish sauce.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry, then slowly add beaten egg while stirring continuously until incorporated.
Add miki noodles and black pepper. Cook over low-medium heat for 5–8 minutes, until noodles are tender and broth thick. Serve hot.

intro: Inihaw na Tuna Belly combines citrus-soy marinated tuna with a glossy garlic basting sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg tuna belly, cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine 1 cup soy sauce, juice of 2 lemons, and black pepper. Marinate tuna belly in the mixture for at least 3 hours.
For basting sauce, sauté garlic in oil over low heat. Whisk remaining soy sauce, water, brown sugar, lemon juice, and cornstarch until smooth.
Pour sauce mixture into the pan, bring to a boil, and simmer about 2 minutes until thickened.
Drain tuna and grill over charcoal for 10–15 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Baste continuously during the final 5 minutes.
Remove when cooked through and lightly charred, then serve immediately.

intro: Kesong Puti is a mild, fresh carabao-milk cheese set with cane vinegar and traditionally molded in banana leaves.
steps: Form banana leaves into 2-inch-high, 2-inch-wide cylinders and tie with twine. Set the molds on a tray.
Bring carabao milk to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Simmer 30 minutes, stirring regularly to prevent scorching.
Strain hot milk through cheesecloth into a large bowl and let it cool slightly.
Stir in cane vinegar and rest 15–20 minutes until curds form. Whisk in salt to break curds into finer pieces.
Pack curds into banana-leaf molds and refrigerate 30 minutes until set.

intro: Buto Butong Sotanghon is a soothing pork-back-bone soup with bean thread noodles and vegetables.
steps: Sauté garlic and onion in oil over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add pork back bones and water or stock. Bring to a boil, skim any scum, cover, and simmer over medium-low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add vermicelli and cook 10 minutes, adding more liquid if needed.
Add cabbage and carrot; cook 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and white pepper. Garnish with spring onions and fried garlic, then serve hot.

intro: Talong Bola Bola are crisp pork-and-eggplant fritters with a creamy banana ketchup dip.
steps: Boil eggplants in 4 cups water, covered, for 6 minutes or until tender. Cool, peel, and chop finely.
Mix eggplant with pork, onion, salt, pepper, garlic powder, egg, and flour until uniform.
Heat oil over low heat. Shape or scoop portions, coat each in breadcrumbs, and fry for 8 minutes until deeply golden.
Drain fritters on a wire rack.
Mix mayonnaise and banana ketchup for the dip. Serve alongside the Talong Bola Bola.

intro: Biko Kalabasa is creamy coconut sticky rice folded through sweet mashed squash and topped with latik.
ingredients: 2 cups glutinous rice, washed and drained
steps: Cook coconut cream over medium heat, stirring until oil separates and golden latik curds form; set aside.
Grease an 8-inch square pan or banana-leaf-lined bilao.
Simmer rice, 1 cup coconut milk, water, and pandan. Cover on low until liquid is absorbed and rice is nearly cooked.
Cook squash in 2 cups coconut milk until fork-tender. Mash, add brown sugar, and stir until thick.
Remove pandan, fold rice into squash mixture, and cook while stirring occasionally until fully cooked and absorbed.
Press into the pan, cool slightly, cut, top with latik, and serve.

intro: Pata is twice-cooked until tender in a full-bodied adobo sauce.
ingredients: 3 lb ham hock (pata), sliced into servings
steps: Boil pata in 8 cups water for 60 minutes. Drain, discard the water, and set pata aside.
Heat oil in a large pot. Brown garlic, then add peppercorns and bay leaves for 30 seconds.
Add pata and 6 cups water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add stock cube and soy sauce; cook on low for 40 minutes, adding water if needed.
Add onion powder, vinegar, and sugar. Bring to a boil, stir, cover, and simmer 20 minutes, keeping enough sauce.
Add salt only if needed, then serve.

intro: Beef Ribs Sinigang is a robust tamarind soup filled with tender beef and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 40 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix Original
steps: Pressure-cook beef ribs and water for 25–30 minutes, until tender.
Add onion and tomatoes; cook for 3 minutes. Stir in Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix.
Add labanos, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add green peppers, okra, sitaw, eggplant, and kangkong stalks. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with patis and black pepper. Add kangkong leaves, turn off heat, cover, and rest 5 minutes.
Serve hot in a large bowl.

intro: Leftover lechon becomes crisp, fresh wraps with hoisin and cucumber.
ingredients: 750 g leftover lechon, meat and skin separated
1 teaspoon warm water or sesame oil, optional
6 spring onions, cut into thin 2-inch strips
steps: Heat oven or air fryer to 190°C. Crisp lechon skin on a rack for 7 to 10 minutes in the oven or 3 to 5 minutes in the air fryer.
Rest skin briefly, then slice into thin strips.
Sauté lechon meat in a lightly oiled pan for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and lightly caramelized.
Steam wrappers for 2 to 3 minutes until pliable; keep them covered with a clean towel.
Loosen hoisin with warm water or sesame oil if desired. Spread on wrappers, add meat, skin, cucumber, and spring onions, then roll and serve.

intro: Kale and Tuna Laing is a slow-cooked coconut dish with spicy bagoong and tender dried kale.
steps: Combine coconut milk, tuna with its liquid, chilies, garlic, and ginger in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes. Add dried kale without stirring, cover, and cook 15 minutes over low-medium heat.
Uncover and stir so kale absorbs the coconut milk. Cover and cook 15 minutes more, adding coconut milk if needed.
Stir in coconut cream and bagoong. Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 45–60 minutes, adding coconut milk or water if necessary.
Serve with rice once kale is tender and the sauce is rich.

intro: Fresh guyabano makes a creamy-tart tropical drink brightened with calamansi.
ingredients: 2 cups fresh guyabano (soursop) pulp, seeds removed
steps: Remove all seeds from the fresh guyabano pulp and place the pulp in a blender.
Add water, sugar, and calamansi juice; blend briefly until the pulp is broken down.
Taste and adjust sugar or calamansi juice as desired.
Strain if a smoother drink is preferred, then serve over ice.

intro: Steamed crawfish simmer in a creamy, savory coconut sauce with spinach and long green chilies.
ingredients: 1/8 tsp ground black or white pepper
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion and garlic until onion is translucent.
Add shrimp paste and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, then cover and cook over medium heat until reduced by half.
Add chilies and crawfish. Cook 5 minutes, stirring every minute.
Add spinach and pepper; cook 2 minutes just until spinach wilts. Serve with warm rice.

intro: Beef with Corn and Mushroom is a creamy, savory skillet dish with tender beef and sweet corn.
ingredients: 750 g beef rump steak, thinly sliced
1 can (400 g) whole corn kernels, drained
1 can (400 g) condensed cream of mushroom soup
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over very high heat. Stir-fry beef for 1 minute per side, then remove.
Lower heat, melt butter, and sauté garlic and onion for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the pan with Worcestershire sauce and water. Boil, then simmer on low for 15 minutes or until tender.
Add condensed mushroom soup, corn, and mushrooms. Simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, stir in cream, and turn off heat.
Garnish with parsley and serve.

intro: Seafood, coconut, and malunggay create a lush Dumaguete-style stew.
ingredients: 350 g small squid, cleaned and sliced
1 cup young coconut meat, cut into strips
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Over medium-high heat, pan-fry prawns and squid in batches for about 1 minute per batch; remove.
Add oil if needed, then sauté shallots and ginger until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and coconut water, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 5 minutes.
Add fish, malunggay, young coconut, and tomatoes; cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.
Return squid and prawns, add chillies, season with fish sauce, and simmer 2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper; top with chopped lechon kawali and serve.

intro: Tinutong na Manok sa Gata is a smoky coconut chicken stew with papaya, capsicum, and malunggay.
ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken thighs and legs
4 cups desiccated coconut or dried coconut strips
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
steps: Combine desiccated coconut with 2 cups coconut milk. Rest until rehydrated, then toast at 180°C for 20 minutes until golden and aromatic.
Mix toasted coconut with remaining coconut milk and rest for 2 hours. Strain, then squeeze solids through cloth to extract coconut milk.
Heat oil in a heavy pot. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until onion softens.
Add chicken and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes, browning all sides.
Add stock and all but 1 cup extracted coconut milk. Simmer on low for 45 minutes, until chicken is tender.
Add papaya and capsicum; simmer 15 minutes. Add reserved coconut milk, slowly boil, then add malunggay and cover for 2 minutes. Season and serve.

intro: Ginataang Halo Halo is a creamy coconut dessert of root vegetables, saba bananas, sago, and chewy rice balls.
ingredients: Sugar or preferred sweetener, to taste
steps: Gradually mix water into glutinous rice flour until a firm, shapeable dough forms. Roll into 1.5 cm balls.
Bring coconut milk to a boil in a pot, then lower heat. Add taro and simmer 5 minutes for small taro or 10 minutes for larger pieces.
Add jackfruit and sweet potatoes; simmer 5 minutes.
Add bananas, rice balls, and tapioca pearls. Gently stir and simmer 5 minutes to prevent sticking.
Stir in sugar and salt to taste. Serve warm or chilled.

intro: Longanisa Fried Rice and Ginisang Corned Beef with Kalabasa makes a complete, comforting Filipino breakfast plate.
steps: Mix leftover rice with salt. Beat eggs, cook in a lightly oiled pan until set, and cut into small pieces.
Remove longanisa casings. Cook the meat in oil, breaking it into small pieces as it browns.
Add salted rice and stir-fry for 3–5 minutes. Add egg, carrot, peas, and pepper; cook 3–5 minutes more.
In a clean pan, sauté garlic and onions in oil until onions soften. Add corned beef and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add kalabasa and water. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until squash is tender.
Serve the ginisang corned beef alongside longanisa fried rice.

intro: A bright, brothy canned-fish meal that comes together quickly with pantry staples.
ingredients: 1 can (425 g) mackerel in tomato sauce
1 can (400 g) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook garlic, shallots, and lemon slices slowly until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add the mackerel with its tomato sauce, breaking it gently into large pieces; simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in cannellini beans and water. Simmer about 5 minutes, adding enough water for a light broth.
Stir in lemon juice, then season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with parsley, rice, or crusty bread.

intro: This rich Pinakbet Manyaman balances pork, shrimp, and garden vegetables in a savory bagoong sauce.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon annatto powder dissolved in 1/4 cup hot water
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil over medium heat until fragrant; add pork and brown evenly.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft and saucy.
Add squash and okra; pan-fry 2 minutes, cover, and cook on low for 5 minutes.
Add bitter melon and eggplant; pan-fry 2 minutes.
Add shrimp, bagoong alamang, beer, soda, and dissolved annatto; cover and simmer over medium heat 5–8 minutes, until vegetables are tender.
Season with black pepper and fish sauce to taste, then serve.

intro: Turmeric and coconut give this chicken dish its sunny color and gentle heat.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken thighs, cut into serving pieces
1 packet (20 g) Knorr Ginataang Gulay mix
1 cup hot pepper leaves (dahon ng sili)
steps: Heat oil and sauté garlic, onion, and turmeric until the onion softens.
Add chicken and cook until all sides are light to medium brown.
Add 1 1/2 cups water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over medium heat for 30 minutes.
Dissolve Ginataang Gulay mix in 1 cup water and add it to the pan; bring to a boil.
Add peppercorns and optional Thai chillies. Cover and cook until sauce reduces by half.
Stir in dahon ng sili and fish sauce; cook uncovered for 5 minutes, then serve with rice.

intro: A rich pork-and-offal stew finished with chives and a silky pig’s brain or spinal-cord garnish.
ingredients: 500 g pork belly, cut into small cubes
150 g pork liver, cut into small cubes
1/2 pig’s brain or 1 cup pig spinal cord
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil the pig’s brain or spinal cord in 1 cup water until cooked; drain, cool, cube, and set aside.
Heat pork lard in a pot over medium heat. Fry garlic until golden, then sauté shallots until fragrant.
Add pork belly and brown lightly on all sides. Add pork liver and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in pork stock, cover, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 20 minutes, until pork is tender.
Stir in chives and the cooked brain or spinal cord. Cover and cook for 1 minute; season with fish sauce and pepper.

intro: Ginisang Sardinas with Ampalaya is a quick, savory skillet dish balancing tomatoey sardines with bitter melon.
ingredients: 1 large can sardines in tomato sauce
1 medium ampalaya (bitter melon), cored and thinly sliced
steps: Heat oil in a cooking pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until garlic is lightly browned.
Add ampalaya and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the sardines and their tomato sauce, stirring gently to keep the fish mostly intact.
Add black pepper and fish sauce. Cover and cook over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until ampalaya is tender-crisp.
Transfer to a plate and top with optional scallions and toasted garlic.

intro: Shrimp cooks quickly in soda, butter, and parsley for a glossy, savory finish.
steps: Heat a pan and add shrimp, stirring to start cooking them evenly.
Pour in lemon-lime soda and bring to a boil, stirring the shrimp gently now and then.
Cook until the liquid reduces by half and shrimp are pink and opaque.
Add salt and butter; cook 1 to 2 minutes until butter melts and coats the shrimp.
Stir in parsley and serve warm.

intro: This homemade tinapa uses a garlicky brine and gentle barbecue smoke for deeply savory mackerel.
ingredients: 1 kg mackerel, cleaned, scaled, and gutted
3 handfuls wood chips, soaked in water
steps: Combine water, sea salt, sugar, garlic, pepper, and vinegar in a large bowl. Submerge mackerel and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Drain fish for 1 hour, then pat dry thoroughly.
Put soaked wood chips in a roasting pan over a gas barbecue grill. Heat until they begin smoking.
Set a foil-lined rack above the chips and arrange fish in a single layer. Cover the grill and cook over medium heat.
When smoke stops, turn off the grill and leave fish covered for 10 minutes. Serve once the fish is cooked through and smoked.

intro: Tender coconut rice cakes wrapped in buri leaves are especially good with ripe mango.
ingredients: Buri leaves, formed into small cylindrical containers
steps: Soak the rinsed glutinous rice in the water until absorbed, then gently stir in coconut milk and sea salt; rest 10 minutes.
Fill and securely seal buri leaf cylinders with the rice mixture.
Arrange packets in a large pot, add about 1 quart water, and bring to a boil.
Lower to low-medium heat and steam-boil for 60 minutes, until the rice is tender; cool slightly.
Serve warm or at room temperature with ripe mangoes.

intro: Crisp fried danggit, garlic fried rice, and basted sunny-side eggs make a classic breakfast plate.
steps: Heat the oil in a medium frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the eggs one at a time, spooning hot oil over the whites and yolks until the tops turn yellowish-white; set aside.
Keep the oil hot and quickly fry danggit in batches over medium heat until crisp on both sides.
Drain danggit on paper towels. Plate 1 cup garlic fried rice with 1 egg and 4 danggit pieces per serving.
Serve immediately with spicy vinegar.

intro: This creamy chicken macaroni soup is a comforting, kid-friendly bowl for sharing.
ingredients: 2 ounces ham, cut into small squares
62 g Knorr Cream of Mushroom Soup
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until soft, then cook chicken until lightly browned.
Add ham and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in 3 cups water and bring to a boil.
Add the Knorr Chicken Cube and macaroni. Cover, return to a boil, then cook over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Whisk Knorr Cream of Mushroom Soup with the remaining 2 cups water. Pour into the pot with carrots and corn.
Cover and cook for 8 minutes, until macaroni and carrots are tender. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Adobo de Campesino is browned pork and crisp-tender beans in a deeply savory vinegar sauce.
ingredients: 1/3 cup water, plus a little more if needed
250 g green beans (bitsuelas), sitaw, or sigarilyas, trimmed
steps: Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove and reserve.
Stir-fry annatto powder briefly in the oil until it colors the oil red.
Raise heat to high, add pork, and fry until browned on all sides.
Add water, vinegar, fish sauce, bay leaves, and peppercorns; boil, then simmer on low for 45 minutes.
Cook over medium heat until the liquid nearly dries and pork begins frying again; add beans and stir-fry 5 minutes.
Add a little water and simmer 5 minutes, until beans are tender; top with reserved garlic and serve.

intro: Fish Sinigang is a tangy salmon-head soup with tender vegetables and a miso-rich broth.
ingredients: 23 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc with Miso
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add salmon heads and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then stir in Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc with Miso and daikon.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes. Add okra, green peppers, and tomatoes; cook 5 minutes more.
Season with black pepper and fish sauce. Add mustard leaves and cook for 2 minutes, just until wilted; serve hot.

intro: Kinamatisang Manok is a light, tomato-forward chicken soup with ginger, bok choy, and green chilies.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic until lightly browned, then cook onion and ginger until softened.
Add chicken and cook for 1 minute per side. Stir in half the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water, bring to a boil, then add Knorr Chicken Cube and 2 teaspoons fish sauce.
Cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes, until chicken is cooked through.
Add remaining tomatoes, green chilies, and bok choy. Cover and cook for 3 minutes; season with fish sauce and pepper.

intro: Pork-tail sinigang is a tangy, hearty soup with gabi and tender vegetables.
steps: Boil pig tails in 3 cups water for 10 minutes; drain and discard the water.
Add the remaining 5 cups water, tomatoes, and onion; boil, then cook over medium heat for 40 minutes, adding water if necessary.
Add gabi and simmer 20 minutes, until nearly tender.
Stir in sinigang mix, peppers, sitaw, and eggplant; cover and cook 12 minutes.
Adjust broth and season with patis. Top with spinach, turn off heat, cover 5 minutes, then stir and serve.

intro: Ginisang Pechay at Giniling is an easy savory pork and leafy-vegetable dish for rice.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add ground pork and cook, stirring, until lightly browned and no pink remains.
Add oyster sauce and water. Simmer uncovered over medium heat until the liquid reduces by half.
Add pechay, cover, and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and pepper, then serve with rice.

intro: Bulcachong is a deeply savory Mindanao-style beef stew with tender shank, oxtail, and tendons.
ingredients: 4 stalks spring onions, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tablespoons liver spread or liver pâté
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the tendons, shanks, and oxtails in batches, then set aside.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in the same pot. Return the meat, add stock, lemongrass, spring onions, and enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 1½ hours, adding water if needed to keep the meat covered.
Mix hot broth with liver spread, flour, turmeric, annatto, and paprika until smooth. Stir into the pot and season with pepper and fish sauce.
Simmer 30 minutes. Remove tender meat if necessary; cook tendons up to 1 hour longer until soft, return meat, and simmer 5 minutes.

intro: Sweet-savory Pinoy Barbecue is marinated pork grilled in glossy banana-catsup basting sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder chops, deboned and excess fat removed
1/2 cup banana catsup or sweet-style tomato catsup
2 tbsp banana catsup or sweet-style tomato catsup, for basting
Bamboo skewers, soaked in water for at least 6 hours
steps: Cut pork into roughly 2-by-1-inch pieces. Mix soy sauce, catsup, calamansi juice, baking soda, garlic, onion, pepper, and brown sugar.
Coat pork in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 24 hours. Mix in 4 tablespoons oil before skewering.
Thread 3 pork pieces onto each soaked skewer. Mix the leftover marinade with basting soy sauce, catsup, oil, and sugar.
Grill over medium heat until lightly charred on one side, then turn and baste.
Continue turning and basting until browned, lightly charred, and cooked through.

intro: Tortang Patatas is a simple golden potato omelet for a quick meal or merienda.
ingredients: 2 large potatoes, cut into small cubes
steps: Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Fry potatoes until golden in spots and crisp at the edges.
Season eggs with salt and pour over the potatoes, coating them evenly.
