Cook until the eggs are fully set and firm, then slide onto a plate.
Serve warm, with ketchup if desired.

intro: Pancit Miki Guisado brings fresh miki noodles, chicken, pork belly, and vegetables together in one quick wok meal.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat; cook chicken for 3 minutes.
Add grilled pork belly and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add sherry and onion; cook until the onion softens.
Stir in soy sauce, oyster sauce, salt, and pepper; cook 6–8 minutes, adding a little water if needed.
Add cabbage and carrots; cook until tender.
Add miki noodles and toss for 3 minutes, until heated through; transfer to a platter.

intro: Batso nga Tabungao is a light, shrimp-stock soup brightened with annatto and tender upo.
ingredients: Shells and heads from 250 g small shrimp
1 teaspoon annatto powder diluted in 2 tablespoons water
steps: Toast shrimp shells and heads in oil in a deep pan; add water, boil, and simmer 5 minutes. Cool, pulse briefly, then strain the stock.
In the same pan, sauté garlic and onion in oil over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Raise heat to high; stir-fry upo 1 minute, then add shrimp stock and diluted annatto. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes.
Add peeled shrimp and cook 2 minutes, until opaque.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Sinamak is a sharp, spicy Filipino vinegar condiment that becomes more potent as it rests.
ingredients: 2 to 3 cups white, cane, or coconut vinegar
1 cup bird’s eye or Thai chilies, fresh or dried
steps: Place chilies, ginger, garlic, peppercorns, and onion in a clean, dry bottle or jar.
Shake the container to distribute the aromatics evenly.
Pour in enough vinegar to cover the ingredients, then seal tightly.
Shake lightly and store for at least 3 days before serving; steep longer for a hotter sinamak.
Serve as a condiment with fried or grilled foods.

intro: Sapin-Sapin is a colorful steamed rice cake with ube, langka, and macapuno layers.
ingredients: ½ packed cup fresh ripe jackfruit flesh
⅓ cup macapuno, drained and finely chopped
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, condensed milk, coconut milk, and coconut cream until smooth. Divide evenly among three bowls.
Blend grated ube with ube flavocol into one portion; blend jackfruit and yellow coloring into another; blend macapuno into the last.
Pour the ube mixture into a greased, cling-wrap-lined pan. Steam 15–20 minutes until set, then steam the jackfruit layer for another 15–20 minutes.
Add the macapuno layer and steam 30 minutes, until fully set. Cool completely before slicing.
Toast desiccated coconut in a dry pan over low heat until golden. Sprinkle over the Sapin-Sapin before serving.

intro: Chilled Mango Sago Pudding layers sweet coconut cream, chewy sago, and ripe Philippine mangoes.
ingredients: 4 ripe Philippine mangoes, cut into small cubes
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add tapioca pearls and cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until translucent.
Drain the sago, rinse well under cold running water, and set aside.
Combine coconut milk, coconut cream, sugar, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the sugar dissolves completely.
Chill the coconut mixture. Divide sago among glasses, pour over the chilled mixture, and top with mango cubes. Serve cold.

intro: Fiesta Float is a no-bake fruit-and-cream dessert that becomes sliceable after an overnight chill.
ingredients: 200 g Graham crackers or malt biscuits, plus extra for garnish
2 cans (425 g each) fruit cocktail, drained
steps: Gently fold whipped cream and condensed milk together until evenly combined.
Line the base of an 8-inch square dish, or similar container, with Graham crackers or malt biscuits.
Spread over half the cream mixture and top with one can of drained fruit cocktail.
Repeat the biscuit, cream, and fruit layers. Garnish with crushed crackers and candied cherries.
Cover tightly and refrigerate overnight before cutting and serving cold.

intro: This fiery Pork Adobo na Tuyo reduces tender pork belly into an intensely spicy, oil-rendered adobo.
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into serving pieces
steps: Combine pork, soy sauce, peppercorns, and garlic. Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat and cook the pork with its marinade until browned.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil. Add ghost pepper and Thai chilies, cover, and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add bay leaves and vinegar. Boil, cover, and simmer for 40 to 60 minutes until pork is tender, adding broth or water if needed.
Uncover and cook until liquid evaporates. Continue over low-medium heat until pork renders oil, then serve with rice.

intro: Soft steamed siopao buns hold juicy bola-bola pork, shrimp, salted egg, and Chinese sausage.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon garlic powder or 1–2 cloves garlic, minced
steps: Mix flour, sugar, yeast, baking powder, milk, and water; work in shortening. Knead 10–12 minutes until smooth, then let rise 20–30 minutes.
Mix pork, onion, shrimp, egg, sesame oil, oyster sauce, garlic, flour, pepper, and salt. Cut salted eggs into portions and slice Chinese sausage.
Divide dough into 10 pieces. Roll each into a 4–5-inch round with a thicker center.
Add filling, salted egg, and sausage; gather, pinch, and twist dough closed. Rest buns 5–10 minutes.
Set each bun on paper in a spaced steamer and steam over low heat for 15 minutes, until puffed and cooked through.

intro: Freshly baked Pandesal has a soft, lightly sweet crumb beneath its signature breadcrumb coating.
ingredients: 3 cups high-grade flour, plus more for dusting
steps: Combine flour, sugar, and salt. Stir in milk, egg, and butter, then fold in yeast until a sticky dough forms.
Knead on a floured surface about 15 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Cover dough and let rise in a warm place for 30–60 minutes, until doubled.
Punch down, divide into two logs, and cut each log into 10 pieces. Roll each piece in breadcrumbs.
Place pieces 1 inch apart on a baking sheet; let rise again until doubled.
Bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, until lightly browned; serve hot.

intro: Ginataang Papaya pairs green papaya and fried daing in a creamy coconut-milk sauce.
ingredients: 1 small green papaya, cut into wedges
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and ginger, then add onion and cook until soft.
Add fried daing and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk, stir, and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add green papaya, cover, and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes until tender; add water if needed.
Stir in malunggay, fish sauce, pepper, and optional chilies. Cook for 2 minutes before serving.

intro: Chicken Embutido is a tender steamed meatloaf studded with vegetables, raisins, and cheddar.
ingredients: 750 g boneless, skinless chicken breast, ground or finely minced
steps: Combine chicken, capsicum, carrot, raisins, cheese, bread crumbs, relish, egg, ketchup, pepper, salt, onion, and garlic until evenly mixed.
Divide mixture into 4 portions. Shape each into a log on aluminum foil and seal the ends tightly.
Steam the wrapped logs for 45 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked and firm.
Rest for 5 minutes, unwrap, slice, and serve warm.

intro: Ginataang Langka with Dilis is a creamy coconut stew of unripe jackfruit and crisp dried anchovies.
ingredients: 20 oz canned unripe jackfruit, squeezed and chopped
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and pan-fry dilis for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and bring it to a boil.
Add garlic and onion, then cook for 4 minutes until aromatic.
Add jackfruit and dried chilies. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in fish sauce and continue simmering until the sauce reduces and thickens.

intro: Tortang Tuna with Spinach is a filling Filipino omelet with tender tuna and greens.
ingredients: 1 can (5 ounces) chunk tuna in water, drained
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion until soft, add tuna, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add spinach and cook for 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper, then transfer the mixture to a bowl to cool.
Beat eggs until fully blended, then stir in the cooled tuna and spinach mixture.
Heat the remaining oil in an omelet pan over low-medium heat. Add the egg mixture and cook about 2 minutes, nudging set egg inward.
When the underside is set, turn the omelet and cook the other side until fully set. Serve warm.

intro: This home-style Pinikpikan uses smoked grilled chicken and etag in a fragrant vegetable broth.
ingredients: 200 g speck, etag, or fatty cured smoked pork
1 large bunch bok choy or Shanghai greens
steps: Set up a hooded charcoal grill with coals on one side only. Salt the halved chicken and smoke it, skin-side up away from direct heat, for 15 minutes.
Heat coals until very hot and grill chicken on both sides until charred. Cool, then chop into pieces.
Sauté celery, ginger, onions, and garlic in oil.
Add chicken, tapuy, and etag; add enough water to cover. Boil, then simmer over medium-low heat about 30 minutes, until chicken is nearly tender.
Add chayote and simmer 8 minutes; add bok choy and simmer 2 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot.

intro: Hong Ma is a glossy, slow-braised pork belly dish scented with star anise and shiitake.
ingredients: 1 kg boneless pork belly, whole slab
5 dried shiitake mushrooms, hydrated and sliced
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with ¼ cup water
steps: Mix crushed garlic, grated ginger, soy sauce, cooking wine, sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Marinate pork belly overnight; reserve the liquid.
Drain and pat the pork dry. Sear skin-side down in smoking-hot peanut oil until golden, then remove.
Lower heat and sauté minced garlic, shallots, and mushrooms until caramelized. Return pork skin-side up with marinade, water, star anise, and sugar.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer very gently for 1½–2 hours until very tender, adding water if the liquid gets low.
Cool and slice pork 1 cm thick. Strain braising liquid, simmer it with mushrooms, and thicken with cornstarch slurry.
Adjust sauce with soy sauce and sugar if needed. Spoon sauce over pork and garnish with spring onions.

intro: Sizzling Tofu combines crunchy fried tofu with creamy savory sauce and fresh chilies on a hot plate.
ingredients: 2 blocks extra-firm tofu, about 500 g, cut into small cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Whisk mayonnaise, oyster sauce, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, and water into a smooth sauce; set aside.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C. Fry tofu until light golden brown, then drain well.
In a large pan, quickly sauté onion, bird’s eye chili, and long green chili so the onion stays crisp.
Add fried tofu, sweet red and yellow chilies, and sauce. Toss continuously over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Heat a sizzling plate, melt butter on it, then transfer the tofu mixture and serve immediately.

intro: Pinais na Hipon gently steams shrimp and pork in banana-leaf parcels with a creamy coconut sauce.
ingredients: 250 g skinless pork belly, thinly sliced and chopped
steps: Pound shrimp shells and heads with water, then strain through a fine sieve to collect shrimp juice.
Combine shrimp, pork belly, young coconut, garlic, chilies, shallot, shrimp juice, salt, and pepper.
Spoon 3 tablespoons filling onto each prepared banana leaf; fold into secure packets.
Arrange packets in one layer in a wide pan. Add coconut cream and coconut milk, cover, and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Lift packets onto a platter and serve with the reserved coconut cooking sauce.

intro: Golden cheese sticks are crisp spring-roll parcels with a simple pink mayo-catsup dip.
ingredients: Quickmelt or Colby cheese, sliced into long strips
steps: Wrap each cheese strip tightly in spring roll pastry, sealing every edge to prevent leakage.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a wok over medium-high heat.
Fry the wrapped cheese in batches until the pastry is golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels. Mix equal parts mayonnaise and sweet-style tomato ketchup for dipping.
Serve cheese sticks hot with the dip.

intro: Rufo’s-Style Saucy Tapa is tender seared beef in a glossy sweet-savory garlic sauce.
ingredients: 500 g beef rump steak, thinly sliced
steps: Toss beef with vinegar, baking soda, and salt; marinate 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sear beef in batches until browned with lightly charred edges; set aside.
Lower heat and sauté garlic in the same wok until golden and fragrant.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, banana ketchup, brown sugar, beef stock, and black pepper; bring to a boil.
Return beef, cover, and simmer on low for 30 minutes, until tender and sauce is reduced.
Stir in cornstarch mixed with water; simmer 2–3 minutes until glossy and thick.

intro: Air Fryer Bangus Salpicao gives marinated milkfish a garlicky finish without deep-frying.
steps: Cut the boneless bangus into serving pieces.
Mix half the garlic with black pepper, salt, olive oil, and Worcestershire sauce. Coat the fish in the marinade and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry remaining garlic until golden, then drain and reserve the toasted garlic.
Arrange fish in the air fryer basket and air-fry at 350°F for 8 minutes, until cooked through and lightly browned.
Transfer to a plate and top with toasted garlic. Serve immediately.

intro: Grilled Filipino Sweet Sausage pairs juicy Pampanga longganisa with sharp spicy vinegar.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a medium pot.
Add longganisa, cover, and boil for about 20 minutes, until the water has evaporated.
Preheat a grill to medium heat. Grill the sausages for 15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until browned and fully cooked.
Serve hot with spicy vinegar; fried eggs make a traditional breakfast accompaniment.

intro: Chicken Liver and Gizzard Adobo layers tender gizzards and rich liver in a thickened soy-vinegar sauce.
steps: Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove and reserve.
Fry chicken liver until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
Fry gizzards until browned, then add 1/2 cup water, vinegar, soy sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar.
Bring to a boil and simmer 30–35 minutes, until gizzards are tender.
Mix cornstarch with 4 tablespoons water; add with liver and half the fried garlic. Simmer 10 minutes, reducing sauce if needed.
Serve topped with remaining fried garlic.

intro: Beef Bicol Express is a rich coconut braise made spicy and deeply savory with bagoong alamang.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until the onion softens.
Stir in bagoong alamang, then add beef and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until medium brown.
Pour in coconut milk and add some Serrano pepper, if desired. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for about 40 minutes until beef is tender, adding water as needed.
Season with salt and pepper, then cook for 3 more minutes before serving.

intro: Pork Kilawin tosses grilled, marinated pork belly with a sweet-tangy vinegar dressing and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, for dressing
1/4 tsp ground black pepper, for marinade
steps: Mix marinade soy sauce, banana ketchup, garlic, lemon juice, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Coat pork and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Grill pork belly until fully cooked, then slice into bite-size serving pieces.
Whisk vinegar, dressing soy sauce, sugar, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Add pork, cucumber, optional tomato, red onion, and chilies. Toss until evenly coated.
Serve promptly as a pulutan or with rice.

intro: Bibingkoy pairs baked glutinous rice balls with red bean filling and a warm jackfruit-coconut topping.
ingredients: 1/2 cup ripe jackfruit, cut into strips
steps: Gradually mix water into glutinous flour until a workable dough forms; knead 5 minutes.
Flatten small pieces of dough, enclose 1 tablespoon red bean paste, and shape into balls smaller than golf balls.
Arrange on a greased banana-leaf-lined baking pan. Bake at 180°C for 10 minutes, then broil at 180°C for 10 minutes.
Boil coconut milk, jackfruit, and sugar; simmer on low 10 minutes, until the topping turns golden.
Add tapioca pearls and cook 3 minutes. Spoon topping over bibingkoy and serve.

intro: Pineapple Chicken Afritada balances savory tomato sauce with sweet pineapple and colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces
8 ounces canned pineapple chunks, juice reserved
1 red bell pepper, cut into squares
1 green bell pepper, cut into squares
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook garlic until golden, then sauté onion until soft.
Add chicken and cook for 1 minute per side, until lightly browned.
Add tomato sauce, reserved pineapple juice, and water. Bring to a boil, then add Knorr Chicken Cube and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer on low for 18 minutes. Turn chicken pieces and cook for 12 minutes more.
Add pineapple chunks, potato, and carrot; cook 10 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add both bell peppers and cook 3–5 minutes, until crisp-tender. Serve hot.

intro: Bahalina is a lightly bitter coconut red wine that is especially refreshing served with soda.
steps: Fill two wine glasses with ice cubes.
Pour ½ cup chilled bahalina into each glass.
Top each glass with ½ cup soda water and stir gently. Serve immediately.

intro: Pata Pochero is a tomato-based pork-leg stew with chorizo, saba, vegetables, and garbanzos.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lbs pork pata, parboiled for 15 minutes
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté onion for 30 seconds, garlic for 20 seconds, then tomato until onion softens.
Add Chorizo de Bilbao and cook for 2 minutes.
Add pata, fish sauce, tomato sauce, and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low-medium for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add saba, potatoes, and garbanzos; cook for 5 to 8 minutes. Add water if necessary.
Season with pepper, then add cabbage and long beans. Cover and cook for 3 to 5 minutes before serving with rice.

intro: Kinalas is a Bicol noodle soup layered with slow-simmered beef, tendon, rich broth, and shrimp-thickened gravy.
ingredients: 500 g medium-thick fresh yellow noodles (Shanghai noodles)
2 kg beef leg bones with meat
steps: Cover beef bones and tendons with water, boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse away scum.
Return meat to the pot with peppercorns, sea salt, onions, and water. Simmer covered on low for 2 hours, topping up water as needed.
Strain broth. Remove beef from bones and chop; simmer bones and tendons in broth 1 hour more, then chop tendons and combine with beef.
For gravy, sauté garlic and shallot in oil over low heat until soft. Add powdered hibe and cook for 2 minutes.
Whisk shrimp stock, fish sauce, cornstarch, soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame oil; add to pan and simmer until thick.
Cook noodles according to package directions. Bowl with beef and tendon, hot broth, gravy, spring onions, and optional calamansi or chilies.

intro: Fish in Coconut Milk with Pineapple combines crisp fried fish with a creamy, ginger-scented sauce.
steps: Rub the fish all over with salt and let stand for 10 minutes.
Heat oil to 350°F in a pan. Fry fish on both sides until golden and cooked through; drain on a rack or paper towels.
Heat 3 tablespoons frying oil in a clean pan. Sauté garlic until browning, then add onion and ginger until the onion softens.
Whisk Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix with water. Add to the pan and bring to a boil.
Reduce to medium heat, add pineapple and fried fish, cover, and cook for 3 minutes.
Add bell peppers and baby bok choy; cook uncovered for 3 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Spicy Crispy Fried Calamares delivers tender squid rings in a boldly seasoned, crunchy coating.
ingredients: 1 lb frozen squid rings, thawed, washed, and drained
steps: Soak squid rings in milk for at least 1 hour, then stir in lemon or calamansi juice.
Mix flour, cornstarch, baking powder, cayenne, paprika, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat enough oil in a deep pan over medium heat to fully submerge the squid.
Dredge squid in the flour mixture until fully coated.
Fry in uncrowded batches for 2–3 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Drain with a slotted spoon on paper towels and serve immediately.

intro: Crispy Shrimp Adobo combines a tangy adobo marinade with a shatteringly crisp fried coating.
ingredients: Adobo dipping sauce: 2 parts vinegar, 1 part soy sauce, minced garlic, and whole peppercorns
steps: Mix vinegar, garlic, sherry or rum, soy sauce, and black pepper. Add shrimp and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Combine cornstarch and flour in a separate bowl.
Heat oil in a deep pot; add bay leaves and peppercorns.
Remove shrimp from marinade and coat each piece in the flour mixture.
Deep-fry shrimp for 5–7 minutes, until crisp and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve with adobo dipping sauce.

intro: Cathedral Jelly is a colorful chilled dessert of jewel-like gelatin cubes in a creamy set filling.
ingredients: 1 can reduced cream or thickened cream
steps: Prepare each flavored jelly according to its package directions and chill until firm.
Cut set jellies into small cubes and place them in a mould.
Dissolve unflavoured gelatine and caster sugar completely in boiling water.
Whisk in evaporated milk and cream until smooth.
Pour mixture over jelly cubes, gently stir to separate cubes, and refrigerate until fully set.

intro: This hearty breakfast plate turns leftover Beef Morcon into a complete meal with garlic rice and eggs.
steps: Slice the leftover Beef Morcon and reheat it gently in a covered pan over low heat until hot throughout.
Warm the prepared garlic fried rice in a skillet over medium heat, stirring until evenly heated.
Fry 6 eggs to your preferred doneness, such as sunny-side-up.
Divide garlic fried rice among three plates. Arrange sliced morcon and two fried eggs beside each portion, then serve hot.

intro: Imbaw is a clean, aromatic clam soup flavored simply with ginger, tomatoes, and lemongrass.
ingredients: 1 kg imbaw or other large clams, thoroughly cleaned
1 thumb-sized piece ginger, peeled and julienned
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large pot.
Add tomatoes, ginger, onion, spring onion, and lemongrass. Cover and simmer for 3 minutes to infuse the broth.
Add clams gently and season with sea salt. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1 minute, until clams open. Discard any unopened clams and serve the soup immediately.

intro: Kinamatisang Isda gently poaches red snapper in a bright broth of softened tomatoes and onion.
ingredients: 2 lbs red snapper, scaled and gutted
4 medium plum tomatoes, cut into wedges
steps: Bring water to a boil in a cooking pot.
Add tomatoes and onion, cover, and cook over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes until very soft.
Uncover and mash the tomatoes and onion into the broth.
Add red snapper, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 15 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Stir in fish sauce and cook for 3 minutes, reducing the broth to your preferred level.

intro: Pasig Style Nilagang Pata is a golden pork-hock soup with sweet potatoes, saba, cabbage, and string beans.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg pork hock, cut into sections
3 saba bananas, sliced on an angle
1 tbsp annatto powder, diluted in 1/4 cup water
1 bunch string beans, cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Season pork hock generously with salt. Add it and brown lightly on all sides until no longer pink.
Add chicken stock, diluted annatto, and one sweet potato. Add water to cover, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, pan-fry saba in a little oil until lightly browned; set aside.
Add remaining sweet potatoes and simmer 5 minutes. Add string beans and fried saba; simmer 5 minutes.
Add cabbage and simmer 3 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Annatto Oil is a quick golden-red cooking oil for adding color to Filipino dishes.
steps: Combine annatto seeds and olive oil in a small saucepan.
Warm over medium heat until small bubbles form around the seeds.
Turn off the heat and steep seeds 1–2 minutes; do not overcook them or the oil may turn bitter.
Strain out the seeds into a clean container and use the colored oil as needed.

intro: Paotsin Green Hainanese Rice and Chicken pairs pandan-tinted rice with crisp fried chicken and tart tamarind sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken legs and thighs, cut into small sections
steps: In a rice cooker, sauté garlic, ginger, and shallot in duck fat for 1 minute. Stir in rice and stock; add pandan and food colour, then cook until done.
Mix eggs, sugar, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, and Chinese wine. Add chicken, prick with a fork, cover, and marinate 2 hours.
Combine cornstarch, flour, black pepper, white pepper, and garlic powder. Coat chicken pieces one at a time.
Deep-fry chicken at 180°C for 8–12 minutes, until golden and cooked through; drain on paper towels.
Blend ginger, garlic, salt, lime juice, chicken stock, water, tamarind, calamansi juice, soy sauce, remaining fish sauce, and chilli oil. Simmer gently, strain, and serve with chicken and rice.

intro: Iced Salabat is a cooling fresh-ginger tea with plenty of ice and a lively ginger kick.
steps: Bring water and sliced fresh ginger to a boil in a small saucepan.
Lower the heat and simmer until the tea tastes strongly of ginger, about 10 minutes.
Strain out the ginger and sweeten the tea to taste while warm.
Cool completely, pour over plenty of ice, and serve chilled.

intro: Garlicky Longganisa Tuguegarao uses coarsely ground pork, vinegar, and annatto, then browns the links in their own fat.
ingredients: 1 kg coarsely minced pork, about 35% fat
3 tbsp sukang Iloko or cane vinegar
Hog casing, cleaned and ready to fill
steps: Mix the coarsely minced pork with pepper, garlic, salt, vinegar, and annatto oil until just combined; keep the coarse texture.
Fill prepared hog casings with the pork mixture using a sausage stuffer, then twist or tie into individual links.
Set the links uncovered on a rack in the refrigerator for 2 to 3 hours to dry the surfaces.
Arrange the links in a wide pan with 1 cup water. Simmer until the water evaporates and the pork fat begins to render.
Turn the links in their rendered fat until browned on all sides and cooked through; serve hot.

intro: Sinigang na Salmon sa Miso is a sour, savory salmon-head soup with tender okra and mustard leaves.
ingredients: 2 packs Knorr Sinigang na May Miso Recipe Mix (25 g each)
1 bunch mustard leaves, washed and trimmed
2 medium yellow onions, cut into wedges
steps: Bring 6–8 cups water to a boil in a large pot. Add onion and tomatoes, then return the broth to a boil.
Add salmon heads and stir gently. When boiling again, stir in Knorr Sinigang na May Miso Recipe Mix.
Add long green peppers, cover, and cook over medium heat for 12 minutes.
Add okra, black pepper, and fish sauce. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Add mustard leaves and cook 3–5 minutes until tender. Serve hot.

intro: Bagoong Fried Rice turns leftover rice into a savory skillet dish finished with pork, egg, and sweet mango.
ingredients: 2 cups pork belly, cut into small cubes
steps: Season pork with salt, pepper, and sesame oil; marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a hot wok and fry pork until golden; remove.
Fry garlic in the wok until golden.
Add rice and bagoong; stir-fry 3 minutes until evenly coated. Push rice aside, scramble eggs, then mix through.
Add pork and spring onions; stir-fry 1 minute and season with salt and pepper.
Plate and top with sliced mangoes.

intro: Ginisang Ampalaya at Itlog is a savory pork, egg, and bitter melon stir-fry with a milder finish.
steps: Toss bitter melon generously with salt and leave for 30 minutes. Rinse under warm running water, drain, and pat dry.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant, then add pork and cook for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened. Add bitter melon and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in beaten eggs and let them begin to set. Toss gently and cook 2 minutes more; season with salt and black pepper before serving.

intro: A creamy chilled gulaman dessert brightened with pineapple and chewy raisins.
ingredients: 2 red gulaman bars, torn into small pieces, or 24 g Mr Gulaman jelly powder
400 g canned pineapple, cubed, with liquid reserved
steps: Combine gulaman, water, reserved pineapple liquid, and sugar in a large saucepan; boil, then simmer until the gulaman is fully dissolved.
Remove from the heat and stir in evaporated milk and vanilla. Pour into a jelly mould or container and cool for 5 minutes.
Gently stir in pineapple and raisins once the mixture begins to thicken. Refrigerate until fully set, unmould if desired, and serve chilled.

intro: Seafood Sinigang is a tangy miso-based soup with fish, shrimp, and quick-cooked vegetables.
ingredients: 2 packets Knorr Sinigang na May Miso Recipe Mix, 25 g each
2 banana peppers or long green chilies
steps: Bring rice wash to a boil in a soup pot.
Add tomatoes and onion, then cook for 5 minutes.
Add fish steaks and shrimp, then stir in Knorr Sinigang na May Miso Recipe Mix.
Add snake beans, okra, and banana peppers. Cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until vegetables are tender and seafood is cooked.
Stir in fish sauce and mustard leaves. Cook for 2 minutes, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Char-grilled chicken is gently braised in a creamy corn and mushroom sauce.
steps: Marinate the chicken in soy sauce while preparing the remaining ingredients.
Grill over hot amber charcoal until both sides are charred. Transfer chicken to a plate.
Heat oil in a wok over low heat; sauté garlic and onions until the onions are soft. Stir-fry mushrooms for 1 minute.
Add chicken, stock, and creamed corn. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in cream and cook 1 minute. Season with salt and black pepper before serving.

intro: Silky yellow noodles are tossed in rich beef pares sauce and crowned with tender braised brisket.
ingredients: 700 g beef brisket, cut into strips or cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot; sauté red onion and 8 cloves garlic until fragrant. Brown the beef, then add stock, soy sauce, sugar, star anise, bay leaves, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, reduce to low, and simmer about 2 hours until the beef is very tender. Stir in cornstarch mixed with 4 tablespoons water; thicken and season with fish sauce.
Briefly soak noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain. In a hot oiled wok, sauté shallots and remaining garlic; stir-fry carrot for 1 minute and cabbage for 1 minute.
Add noodles and toss for 2 minutes. Add 1/2 cup water and about 1/2 cup pares sauce; toss until absorbed, seasoning with pepper and fish sauce.
Plate the noodles, spoon beef and extra sauce over them, garnish with fried garlic, and serve immediately.

intro: This rich Pork Adobo finishes with crisp garlic chips and a deeply reduced savory sauce.
steps: Heat the oil over low heat; fry garlic, stirring occasionally, until golden and crisp. Drain, reserving the garlic-infused oil.
Heat 3 tablespoons reserved oil in the pan over medium-low heat. Cook onion until caramelized, then brown pork on all sides.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, soda, oyster sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves, and half the garlic chips. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour, until pork is tender. Uncover and cook until the sauce has evaporated.
Serve with rice and scatter the remaining garlic chips over the Pork Adobo.

intro: Etag is a smoky Cordilleran cured pork best enjoyed simply sautéed with rice.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rinse the prepared etag briefly if very salty, then pat it dry and slice thinly.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat; sauté garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add etag and stir-fry for 5 to 7 minutes, until heated through and lightly crisp at the edges.
Add water and pepper; cook until the water evaporates, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Maki Soup is a silky, hearty pork soup with shiitake and delicate egg ribbons.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pound pork lightly, then marinate it with light soy sauce, wine, garlic, baking soda, salt, and pepper for 30 minutes.
Dust both sides of the pork with cornstarch. Soak mushrooms in hot water until soft, then chop them.
Bring mushroom soaking liquid, beef stock, mushrooms, and soy sauce to a boil; add pork pieces separately.
Mix tapioca starch with 1/2 cup water and stir it in gradually until the soup thickens; reduce heat to low.
Stir in egg yolks gently to make ribbons, season if needed, and garnish with spring onions.

intro: Crispy fried pompano softens in a bright, tamarind-sour Sinigang broth.
steps: Heat a little oil from frying the fish in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add water and bring to a boil. Add fried pompano, okra, tomatoes, and tamarind mix.
Lower heat and simmer for 10 minutes. Add bok choy, green finger chilies, and red chilies.
Simmer 2 minutes, until bok choy is just tender. Season with fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: This chilled Ampalaya Salad balances bitter gourd with sharp vinegar, tomato, and onion.
ingredients: 1 medium Roma tomato, diced and seeded
steps: Rub the sliced ampalaya thoroughly with 1 tablespoon salt and leave it for 30 minutes.
Rinse the ampalaya quickly under running water, then drain it very well.
Whisk vinegar, pepper, sugar, and extra salt if needed in a bowl.
Toss in ampalaya, onion, and tomato; cover and refrigerate for 3 hours before serving.

intro: Lumpiang Sariwa wraps tender pork, shrimp, and vegetables in soft crepes with peanut sauce.
ingredients: 12 cloves garlic, 6 minced and 6 left whole with skins
3 tablespoons cornstarch, dissolved in 1/2 cup water
steps: Whisk flour with 1 cup water, salt, eggs, and remaining water. Cook 1/4-cup portions in a lightly oiled low-heat pan, 90–120 seconds, flip, then cook 15 seconds.
Boil bamboo shoots in salted water until tender and drain. Stir-fry pork in oil, then garlic for 1 minute and bamboo shoots for 2 minutes.
Add carrots, cabbage, and shrimp; stir-fry 1 minute. Add stock and cook over high heat until dry, then drain the filling.
Boil whole garlic in water until soft; peel and mash. Sauté minced garlic, then add soy sauce, water, sugar, mashed garlic, and half the peanuts.
Simmer sauce, stir in cornstarch slurry over low heat until thick, then cool slightly.
Place lettuce and filling on each crepe, roll tightly, and top with peanut sauce and remaining crushed peanuts.

intro: This festive Pancit Bihon pairs savory pork noodles with crisp lechon kawali.
ingredients: Lime or calamansi wedges, for serving
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add boiled pork belly and Chinese sausage; cook for 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce and water, bring to a boil, then dissolve in Pork Cubes. Add bihon, cover, and cook until it begins to soften.
Stir in oyster sauce, dried shrimp, cabbage, snap peas, and carrot. Toss well and cook for 7 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Season with black pepper and additional soy sauce if needed. Transfer to a platter, top with lechon kawali and parsley, and serve with lime or calamansi.

intro: Kilayin is a tangy, peppery pork offal stew with a deep vinegar bite.
ingredients: 500 g pork belly, thinly sliced into strips
200 g pork liver, thinly sliced into strips
1/2 tsp cayenne pepper, or more to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate pork belly and heart with 1/2 cup vinegar and salt; separately marinate liver with 1/2 cup vinegar and salt for 30 minutes.
Drain all meats thoroughly, reserving the marinade. Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork belly, heart, and lungs; cook until lightly browned. Add remaining 1/4 cup vinegar, water, and cayenne, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes. Add liver and simmer 10 minutes more, until all meats are cooked; season with fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: Chewy udon is stir-fried with pork, squid balls, and crisp vegetables in a soy-citrus sauce.
ingredients: 1/4 lb pork, thinly sliced and chopped
steps: Boil water in a deep pot. Cook udon for 10 to 12 minutes until tender but not soggy; drain and toss with olive oil.
Heat cooking oil in a wide wok over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add pork and cook 2 minutes. Add squid balls and cook 2 minutes more.
Stir-fry carrot and cabbage for 3 minutes, then add the prepared udon.
Pour in soy sauce and lemon juice. Stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes, season with salt and pepper, and top with scallions.

intro: Pancit Molo is a comforting chicken broth soup filled with tender pork-and-shrimp dumplings.
steps: Mix pork, shrimp, sesame oil, egg, cornstarch, chives, salt, and black pepper. Place filling in wonton wrappers; fold and seal.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion, then briefly stir-fry the flaked chicken.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil. Add the prepared wontons.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until dumplings are cooked. Add leftover wrappers and simmer 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Garnish with spring onions, fried garlic, and a drizzle of sesame oil.

intro: Binarutak is a sour fish-head soup thickened naturally with taro and filled with vegetables.
ingredients: 3 large fish heads, such as snapper, grouper, or salmon
1/2 cup tamarind paste (kinapal), or 1 packet sinigang mix
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: If using kinapal, mash tamarind paste with warm water and strain; set aside. Sauté onion and ginger in a little oil over medium heat until translucent.
Add 6 cups water and boil. Add sweet potatoes and taro; cook about 10 minutes until beginning to soften.
Add okra, radish, fish heads, and tamarind liquid or sinigang mix. Cook over medium heat about 10 minutes, until fish is cooked through.
Mash the taro into the broth. Add loofah, sweet potato tops, and chillies; cook 1 minute, season with fish sauce and pepper, and serve with rice.

intro: Champeni is a richly sauced beef-offal dish balanced with pineapple, tomato, and chilies.
ingredients: 1 kg mixed beef innards and meat, including tripe, intestines, cow skin, tendons, and beef chunks, cleaned and bite-sized
5 cups water, or enough to cover
1/2 cup tomato sauce or banana ketchup
1 tbsp annatto powder, diluted in 1/2 cup water
steps: Place beef innards and meat in a pot with water, peppercorns, and salt. Boil 1 to 2 hours, skimming foam, until tender; drain.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant, add onions until translucent, then stir-fry the boiled beef for 5 to 10 minutes.
Add soy sauce, fish sauce, pepper, bay leaves, pineapple juice, tomato sauce, annatto water, and chilies. Simmer uncovered 10 to 15 minutes until thickened.
Adjust seasoning, garnish with spring onions, and serve with rice or as pulutan.

intro: Graham Balls are quick no-bake treats with a creamy center and colorful coatings.
ingredients: 250 ml sweetened thick creamer, such as Angel Kremdensada or Alaska Crema Asada
steps: Process graham crackers into a fine crumb.
Combine crumbs, optional salt, and sweetened thick creamer until evenly moistened.
Roll level tablespoonfuls into balls, then coat fully in your preferred topping.
Refrigerate on a tray for 1 hour until firm, then serve or place in small paper liners.

intro: Paddle crabs and young jackfruit simmer in a lush, spicy coconut sauce.
ingredients: 2 cans (500 g each) young jackfruit, sliced
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add coconut milk, green chilies, and crabs. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Remove crabs. Add jackfruit and simmer uncovered over high heat for 15 minutes, until the coconut milk reduces and releases oil.
Return crabs to the wok with coconut cream. Simmer 5 minutes, season with fish sauce and black pepper, and serve.

intro: Paksiw na Salmon Belly is a vinegary fish stew that tastes even fuller after resting overnight.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak salmon belly in 3 cups water and 3 tablespoons salt for 30 minutes. Drain well and discard the soaking water.
Layer onion, salmon, garlic, and ginger in a large wok; arrange eggplant around the sides. Pour in cane vinegar and 1 cup water.
Season with fish sauce, salt, ground pepper, peppercorns, and chillies. Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 15 minutes, until fish is opaque and eggplant is soft.
Cool before serving, or refrigerate overnight for deeper flavor; reheat gently and serve warm with rice.

intro: Tender shrimp and creamy avocado make a cool, tangy salad.
steps: Bring water to a boil. Cook shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes, until medium orange, then drain and cool.
Whisk sour cream, lime juice, garlic powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Gently fold in avocado until coated, then fold in the cooked shrimp.
Transfer to a serving bowl, garnish with chives, and chill before serving.

intro: This chicken Chopsuey combines crisp-tender vegetables in a savory, glossy sauce.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon cornstarch, diluted in 3/4 cup water
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat; sauté onion until separated, then add garlic and cook until the onion softens.
Stir-fry chicken until its exterior is lightly browned. Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and water; cover and bring to a boil.
Add the Knorr Chicken Cube and cook over medium heat until sauce is reduced by half.
Add carrots and cook 3 minutes, then stir in the cornstarch mixture.
Add young corn, cauliflower, bell peppers, broccoli, snow peas, and cabbage; toss, cover, and cook 1 1/2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, fold in quail eggs, and serve while vegetables remain crisp-tender.

intro: Pancit Sotanghon combines glossy bean-thread noodles, chicken, shrimp, and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 1 cup rehydrated wood ear mushrooms or thinly sliced shiitake
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak sotanghon in water for no longer than 15 minutes, then drain. Mix annatto powder with 1/4 cup chicken broth.
Cook beaten eggs in an oiled pan as a thin scramble; cool and slice into strips. In a wok, sauté garlic and onion over medium heat until fragrant.
Stir-fry mushrooms for 1 minute, then cabbage and carrot for 1 minute. Remove vegetables and set aside.
Boil remaining broth with shrimp and chicken. Add noodles and annatto broth; stir until liquid evaporates, then stir-fry 2 minutes and season with fish sauce and pepper.
Plate noodles, top with vegetables and egg strips, and serve with lemon wedges.

intro: Chicken Pancit Habhab is a deeply seasoned noodle dish finished with colorful sautéed vegetables.
ingredients: 2 sachets Knorr SavorRich Liquid Seasoning, 16 g each
1/2 lb boneless chicken breast, boiled and shredded
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons oil over medium heat; sauté chayote 2 minutes, carrots 30–40 seconds, snow peas, then bok choy for 1 minute. Season and set aside.
Heat remaining oil in the pot and sauté onion and garlic until softened. Add chicken and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in Knorr SavorRich Liquid Seasoning and cook 1 minute until chicken is coated.
Add stock and soy sauce; bring to a boil. Add half the Habhab noodles, then the rest as they soften.
Cook over low heat, tossing occasionally, until liquid is absorbed and noodles are tender but not mushy.
Season with pepper, return vegetables, toss for 2 minutes, and serve.

intro: Chicken Guisantes is a simple tomato-braised chicken dish with sweet peas and roasted pepper.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken thighs, cut into serving pieces
1 medium roasted red bell pepper, sliced
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion is soft.
Add chicken and cook about 2 minutes per side, until lightly browned.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 30 to 40 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add peas and cook 3 minutes. Add roasted red bell pepper and cook 3 minutes more.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Chicken Hinalang is a fragrant, spicy soup brightened with lemongrass, ginger, and pepper leaves.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 bunch green onion, cut into 3-inch pieces
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix chicken with soy sauce and vinegar; marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant and softened.
Add chicken and sauté for 5 minutes. Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Add Knorr Chicken Cube and lemongrass; cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Discard lemongrass. Add Thai chilies and chayote; cook 7 minutes.
Add bell pepper, hot pepper leaves, and green onions; cook 5 minutes, season, and serve hot with rice.

intro: Pinulpugan combines smoky chopped pork with a sharp, spicy vinegar dressing.
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, cut into thick strips
steps: Grill pork over hot charcoal until cooked through and charred at the edges.
Chop the grilled pork into small pieces and place in a large bowl.
Mix cane vinegar, soy sauce, red chilies, onion, salt, and black pepper.
Toss pork with the vinegar mixture. Rest 10 minutes, toss again, and serve with calamansi.

intro: This Filipino Style Beef Curry is a mellow coconut braise with tender beef and sweet vegetables.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season beef with salt and pepper. Brown it on all sides in oil in a heavy pot, then remove it.
Sauté onions until soft, then garlic and ginger paste for 1 minute. Add curry powder, beef, stock, and coconut milk; bring to a boil.
Simmer on low for 1 hour, adding water if needed. Add carrots and simmer about 45 minutes, until beef is tender.
Add sweet potatoes and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in coconut cream, boil over high heat, then simmer 5 minutes; add sugar and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with jasmine rice.

intro: Kalderetang Kambing is a rich tomato-and-liver-spread goat stew with tender vegetables.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate goat with vinegar, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour; drain and discard the marinade.
Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add goat and cook until lightly browned. Stir in tomato sauce and crushed chilies; cook 2 minutes.
Add water, bring to a boil, then simmer at least 45 minutes until goat is tender.
Stir in liver spread and cook 5 minutes, adding a little water if the sauce becomes too dry.
Add potato and carrot for 8 minutes, then olives and bell pepper for 5 minutes. Season and serve hot.

intro: Beef Goto is a thick, comforting glutinous-rice porridge enriched with slow-cooked brisket.
ingredients: 1 kg beef brisket, cut into 2 cm cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Lemon or calamansi wedges, for serving
steps: Season beef with salt and pepper; brown in batches over medium-high heat. Sauté quartered onion, smashed ginger, and peppercorns in the same pot.
Return beef, add water, boil, then simmer gently for 2 hours until very tender. Strain broth, keeping beef and discarding aromatics.
In a clean pot, sauté garlic until lightly golden; reserve half for topping. Add chopped onion and julienned ginger until soft.
Stir in rice for 2 minutes, season with fish sauce, then add 10 to 12 cups broth and beef. Simmer 40 minutes, stirring frequently, until creamy.
Add broth or water as needed. Serve with reserved fried garlic, spring onions, eggs, and lemon or calamansi.

intro: Tofu Pinakbet is a savory bagoong-seasoned vegetable stew with shrimp and crisp fried tofu.
ingredients: 2 small Asian eggplants, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 squash or buttercup squash, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tablespoons bagoong monamon or bagoong isda
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add squash and okra; stir-fry 2 minutes, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 5 minutes.
Add string beans, bitter melon, and eggplant; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add water, sugar, tofu, shrimp, and bagoong; cover and simmer over medium heat for 5 to 8 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with pepper and fish sauce if needed, then serve.

intro: Mixed seafood cooks quickly in a reduced coconut and shrimp-paste sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a cooking pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add black pepper, dried Thai chilies, and shrimp paste. Stir and simmer until the liquid reduces by half.
Add mixed seafood and cook 3 to 5 minutes, just until opaque and cooked through. Serve immediately.

intro: Ginataang Alimasag with Malunggay is a creamy crab stew enriched with squash and bagoong.
ingredients: 2 lb medium crabs, cleaned and halved
1/4 cup ginger, cut into thick strips
steps: Combine coconut cream, onion, ginger, and garlic in a pot. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir in bagoong, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add squash, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 12 minutes until nearly tender.
Stir in black pepper and malunggay leaves; cook 5 minutes.
Add crabs, stir gently, and cook 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through and sauce thickens. Season with patis if needed.

intro: Pancit Estacion layers crisp togue beneath smoky tinapa sauce and crunchy garnishes.
ingredients: 1/4 cup lemon juice, or kamias juice
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant. Add stock and atsuete seeds; simmer about 10 minutes until orange, then strain out seeds.
Mix cornstarch with water and stir into the sauce. Add tinapa, lemon juice, fish sauce, salt, and pepper; simmer 5 minutes.
Slowly drizzle in beaten egg while stirring to form delicate strands, then remove sauce from heat.
Blanch togue in boiling water for 1 minute until crisp-tender; drain. Arrange on a platter, spoon over sauce, and garnish with peanuts, chicharon, and spring onions.

intro: Seafood Bicol Express brings mussels, squid, and shrimp together in fiery coconut milk.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add Thai chilies and shrimp paste, cover, and cook 3 minutes.
Add squid, mussels, and shrimp. Stir to coat and cook 3 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until seafood is cooked.
Stir in black pepper and serve at once.

intro: Custard Cake layers silky leche flan beneath a light lemon-scented sponge.
steps: Heat a 9-by-13-inch pan over medium heat. Cook 1 cup sugar with water until caramelized; cool until firm.
Whisk 8 egg yolks, condensed milk, 1 cup fresh milk, and 1/4 cup sugar until dissolved. Pour over caramel.
Beat 6 egg yolks with 1/2 cup sugar until pale. Fold in sifted flour and baking powder alternately with 1/2 cup milk; stir in lemon juice.
Beat egg whites until fluffy, add cream of tartar, then gradually beat in remaining sugar to stiff peaks. Fold in yolk batter.
Pour batter over custard without stirring. Set pan in a larger pan half-filled with hot water; bake at 180°C for 1 hour, until firm.
Cool completely, loosen edges, invert onto a platter, and chill before serving.

intro: Hinalang is a peppery, chile-laced beef soup finished with fresh cabbage and capsicum.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg beef, preferably ribs or neck
1 bunch spring onions, sliced, white and green parts separated
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onions, garlic, ginger, bird's-eye chilies, and the white spring onion portions until fragrant.
Add beef and cook until lightly browned. Cover with water, add peppercorns, bring to a boil, then simmer 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add cabbage and capsicum; cook 5 minutes until just tender. Season with fish sauce and ground pepper.
Garnish with green spring onion portions and serve hot.

intro: Ensaladang Mangga is a sharp, salty-sour green mango salad that pairs beautifully with grilled foods.
steps: Place cubed green mangoes, tomatoes, and onion in a large mixing bowl.
Add sautéed bagoong and toss gently until the fruit and vegetables are evenly coated.
Chill briefly to meld the flavors, then serve as a side dish or with rice.

intro: Kalamay Lansong is a soft steamed coconut rice cake finished with golden latik.
steps: Simmer coconut cream in a nonstick pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until oil separates and curds turn light brown. Cool the latik.
Warm banana leaf over low heat until pliable. Line an 8-inch, 2-inch-deep round pan and grease it with latik oil.
Whisk glutinous rice flour, coconut milk, and sugar until smooth; pour into the prepared pan.
Steam over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes with the lid wrapped in a clean towel, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, unmold, top with latik, and cut into squares.

intro: Chicken Molo Soup is a fragrant annatto-tinted broth with delicate chicken-and-shrimp wontons.
ingredients: 1 1/2 tsp annatto powder or 1/2 cup annatto seeds soaked in 1/2 cup warm water
steps: Mix chicken, minced shrimp, half the onion, 1 teaspoon pepper, salt, and sesame oil. Fill and seal wonton wrappers.
Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add remaining onion, shrimp-head juice, annatto powder or strained annatto water, and half the toasted garlic.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes. Add wontons, chicken cube, remaining pepper, and fish sauce.
Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the wonton filling is cooked through.
Ladle into bowls and top with scallions and remaining toasted garlic.

intro: Crispy Pork Belly Chips are thin, deeply crisp pork strips served with spicy vinegar dip.
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, whole and unsliced
steps: Rub pork belly generously with sea salt, wrap, and refrigerate for at least 24 hours. Rinse away salt and pat dry.
Place pork skin-side up in a pressure cooker with seasoning, garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, baking soda, and water.
Cook 20 to 30 minutes after pressure is reached, until tender. Remove and pat completely dry.
Rub vinegar over the skin, cover, and refrigerate at least 12 hours.
Heat oil to 180°C. Slice cold pork thinly, then deep-fry in batches until golden brown and crisp.
Drain well and serve with spicy vinegar dip.

intro: Tuna Macaroni Pasta is an easy Alfredo-style bake with peas and a bubbling cheddar top.
ingredients: 1 can tuna in water, 6.5 oz, drained
steps: Cook macaroni according to package directions until tender; drain. Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix drained tuna, peas, Parmesan, and Alfredo sauce in a large bowl.
Add macaroni and toss until every piece is coated.
Transfer to a baking dish and scatter cheddar evenly over the top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until hot and bubbling, then rest briefly and serve.

intro: Creamy Tuyo Pesto turns salted dried fish and basil into a bold pasta sauce.
steps: Bring water to a boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
Blend garlic and olive oil until finely chopped. Add salt, pepper, basil, and half the Parmesan; blend to a fine pesto.
Heat water and cream in a pot over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons butter and stir until melted.
Stir in tuyo flakes, pesto, and remaining Parmesan. Simmer until thickened, then spoon over spaghetti.
Finish with the remaining butter if desired and serve.

intro: No Bake Macaroni makes a fast, hearty pasta meal from corned beef in pasta sauce.
ingredients: 520 g CDO Home Style Corned Beef in Pasta Sauce
steps: Cook elbow macaroni according to package directions until tender; drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a wide pot. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add CDO Home Style Corned Beef in Pasta Sauce; cook 3 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, and season with salt and pepper as needed.
Add macaroni and toss for 2 minutes until coated and hot. Plate, then finish with cheddar and parsley.

intro: Three Eggs Polunchay pairs tender spinach with a savory stock enriched by three kinds of egg.
steps: Heat oil over low heat in a wok and gently brown garlic on all sides.
Raise heat to high, add dashi or stock, and bring to a boil. Add spinach and cook for 2 minutes.
Lift spinach onto a serving platter. Reduce heat to medium and keep stock gently boiling.
Add century egg and salted duck eggs without stirring. Slowly pour in beaten eggs while swirling the stock.
Season with fish sauce and white pepper, turn off heat, pour over spinach, and drizzle with sesame oil.

intro: Tender pata and shrimp enrich this substantial coconut stew with monggo and langka.
ingredients: 4 to 6 Thai chili peppers or siling labuyo
steps: Pressure-boil pata in 4 quarts water for 15 minutes; drain and discard water. Add fresh water, peppercorns, bay leaves, and pata; pressure-cook 25 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Pan-fry shrimp 1 minute per side; remove and set aside.
Sauté onion for 30 seconds, then garlic until onion softens. Add coconut milk and bring to a boil; stir in Pork Cube.
Add mung beans, cover, and cook 15 to 18 minutes. Add jackfruit, cover, and cook 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in chilies, bagoong alamang, pepper, and pata. Cover and cook 10 minutes; add pepper leaves and shrimp, then cook 3 minutes.

intro: Chicknigang is a chicken sinigang with tender vegetables in a tangy tamarind broth.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 cup daikon radish (labanos), cut into wedges
22 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens. Add chicken and brown each side for 2 minutes.
Pour in water and bring to a boil. Add labanos and Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix; cover and cook over low-medium heat for 35 minutes.
Add tomatoes, long green peppers, okra, and string beans; cook 8 to 12 minutes until tender. Season with pepper and fish sauce.
Add spinach and cook for 1 minute until wilted. Transfer to a bowl and serve hot.

intro: Stuffed inihaw na pusit stays tender with a quick grill and fragrant tomato-ginger filling.
steps: Marinate squid in soy sauce, mirin, and lime juice for 12 minutes.
Mix tomato, onion, ginger, salt, and black pepper. Stuff squid with scallions and the mixture; secure each opening with a toothpick.
Heat a grill to medium-high. Grill one side for 2 minutes, brushing with annatto oil.
Turn, brush with annatto oil, and grill 2 minutes more. Continue flipping every 2 to 3 minutes only until opaque and cooked through.
Serve immediately with a dipping sauce of chopped tomato, onion, soy sauce, and vinegar.

intro: Pinaupong Manok is salt-roasted whole chicken served with a buttery ginger-garlic dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1 whole garlic, pounded with skin on
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub chicken inside and out with salt, pounded garlic, and pepper. Stuff cavity with onions, lemongrass, garlic, and ginger.
Spread rock salt in an earthenware pot and cover with banana leaves. Sit chicken upright without touching the pot sides.
Cook uncovered over a low open flame for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until chicken is tender and juices run clear.
Rest chicken on a rack and collect its drippings.
Simmer butter, lemon juice, chicken drippings, ginger paste, minced garlic, and salt over low heat for 5 minutes.
Carve chicken and serve with the warm dipping sauce.

intro: Perdis is a fragrant chicken stew with Mallorca liqueur, warm spices, and boiled eggs.
ingredients: 1/3 cup Mallorca liqueur, or sweet red wine plus a splash of orange extract
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium-high heat and sear chicken until lightly golden; transfer to a plate.
In the same pot, sauté garlic, onion, ginger, and tomatoes until soft and fragrant.
Add Mallorca liqueur, scrape up browned bits, and cook 1 to 2 minutes so the alcohol evaporates.
Return chicken with soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon, bay leaf, and stock. Cover and simmer about 30 minutes.
Cook until chicken is tender and sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper, add boiled eggs, and serve with rice.

intro: Inihaw na Baboy is smoky grilled pork belly with a lively garlic-chili vinegar dip.
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, sliced 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix lemon juice, whole minced garlic, soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, salt, and pepper. Coat pork evenly, cover, and refrigerate at least 6 hours.
Mix vinegar, 2 minced garlic cloves, red chillies, shallot, 1 tablespoon sugar, salt, and pepper for the dipping sauce; set aside.
Heat charcoal until amber-red. Grill pork 4 to 6 minutes per side, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Rest briefly, then serve hot with the vinegar dip.

intro: Bacalao is a colorful salted-cod sauté with chickpeas, peppers, and golden potatoes.
ingredients: 600 g dried bacalao, dried salted cod
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak bacalao in cold water overnight in the refrigerator. Drain, flake the fish, and remove any bones.
Fry potatoes in oil over medium heat until golden on all sides; remove. Dissolve annatto powder in hot water.
In the same pan, sauté garlic and onion in oil until fragrant. Add bacalao, chickpeas, tomatoes, capsicum, pepper, and annatto water.
Cook over medium heat about 10 minutes until nearly dry. Return potatoes, cook on low 5 minutes with a little water if needed, and serve.

intro: Arroz a la Cubana is a satisfying plate of savory picadillo, rice, egg, and sweet fried saba.
steps: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry saba slices until golden on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Add oil to the pan and sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add pork and beef. Cook for 10 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Add corn, peas, carrot if using, and raisins. Cook 5 minutes, then add soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Plate steamed rice with the minced meat, a sunny-side-up egg, and fried saba.

intro: Embutido Cordon Bleu pairs steamed meat rolls with ham, Swiss cheese, and creamy Dijon sauce.
steps: Mix pork, chicken, mashed Chicken Cube, relish, cheddar, bell pepper, raisins, carrot, onion, egg, salt, pepper, and breadcrumbs.
Spread 3/4 cup mixture on foil. Top with 2 ham slices and 2 Swiss slices, roll tightly, twist ends, and repeat.
Steam rolls for 1 hour. Cool, unwrap, then coat each in flour, beaten egg, and panko.
Heat oil over medium-high heat and deep-fry until golden brown and heated through. Drain on a rack.
For sauce, soften yellow onion in butter. Add cream and Dijon; reduce over low-medium heat by half, season, and serve alongside rolls.

intro: Dinengdeng na Bunga ng Malunggay is a light pork and vegetable stew seasoned with bagoong monamon.
ingredients: 2 cups buttercup squash, cut into chunks
8 bunga ng malunggay (moringa drumsticks), cut into segments
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Warm a pot over medium heat and cook the pork belly until it takes on a light brown color. Add the onion and tomatoes, then cook until softened.
Add the water or light broth and bring the pot to a low simmer. Mix in the bagoong monamon, seasoning sparingly with salt and pepper.
Put in the squash, broad beans, and moringa drumsticks. Simmer until the squash is tender and the other vegetables are cooked.
Fold in the spinach and let it wilt briefly. Taste, adjust the seasoning if necessary, and serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: Guisadong Monggo is a hearty mung bean soup enriched with pork, shrimp, and optional tinapa.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Fry garlic until golden; remove and reserve.
Fry pork belly in the same pot until golden and crisp; remove and reserve.
Add mung beans and stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer 45 to 60 minutes until beans are very soft; add water if needed.
Add shrimp, tinapa if using, and pork. Simmer 10 minutes, until shrimp is cooked through.
Stir in spinach or watercress. Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then garnish with fried garlic.

intro: Pinatisang Manok is a clean, fish-sauce-seasoned chicken soup enriched with rice wash and leafy greens.
ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken thighs and legs
1 litre rice wash, the water used to rinse rice
1 bunch spinach, malunggay leaves, or watercress
1 bunch chilli leaves or capsicum leaves
steps: Marinate chicken in 4 tablespoons fish sauce for 15 minutes. Heat oil in a pot and pan-fry chicken over high heat for 2 minutes per side; remove.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in the pot until onions are soft. Return chicken, add rice wash, bring to a boil, then simmer 1 hour.
Add chilli leaves and spinach, malunggay, or watercress. Cover and simmer 1 minute, until leaves wilt.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: Ginataang Hipon Sitaw at Kalabasa is a creamy coconut shrimp stew with sweet squash and greens.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add shrimp and cook 1 to 2 minutes, just until pink; remove and set aside.
Add bagoong alamang and coconut milk to the pot. Stir and bring to a boil.
Add kalabasa and cook 8 to 12 minutes until tender.
Return shrimp and cook 1 minute. Add sitaw and malunggay, then cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Larang is a rich coconut fish stew brightened with lemon and salty black beans.
ingredients: 1 kg hapuka or grouper, cut into cubes
1/2 cup coconut cream or kakang gata
2 tbsp salted black beans, lightly mashed
steps: Season the fish generously with sea salt. Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry fish until lightly browned on both sides; set aside.
Leave 3 tablespoons oil in the wok. Sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger until fragrant, then cook tomatoes, chillies, and black beans until tomatoes soften.
Add coconut milk and capsicum; bring to a boil over high heat. Return fish and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour in water and coconut cream. Lower heat and simmer 5 minutes, until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Stir in lemon juice, season with fish sauce and black pepper, and garnish with spring onions before serving.

intro: A hearty Visayan beef soup layered with sweet corn, saba bananas, and tender vegetables.
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef shanks, cut into sections
2 ears fresh sweet corn, each cut into 3 sections
1 piece ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil the beef shanks in water for 15 minutes, then drain, rinse, and discard any scum.
Heat oil in a clean pot over medium heat; sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Add beef, corn, bamboo shoots, lemongrass, salt, and enough water to cover. Boil, then simmer 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add saba bananas and cook for 15 minutes. Add cabbage and cook for 5 minutes.
Add bok choy and spring onions; cook 5 minutes until vegetables are tender. Season with fish sauce and pepper.

intro: Ginisang Gulay is a quick vegetable sauté that keeps ampalaya and garden vegetables tender-crisp.
ingredients: 1 medium bitter gourd (ampalaya), cored and sliced
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add tomatoes and cook 2 minutes until they begin to break down.
Add calabaza squash, stir, and cook 2 minutes.
Add eggplant, okra, string beans, and ampalaya; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth, cover, and cook 5 to 7 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Uncover, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

intro: This Chicken Pork Adobo has crisp potatoes, twice-fried meat, and a glossy vinegar-soy sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Philippine soy sauce or Kikkoman soy sauce
steps: Deep-fry potatoes until golden; drain and set aside. Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden, then remove.
Fry pork belly until browned; remove. Fry chicken nibbles until browned; remove.
Return pork to the pot with water, vinegar, soy sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar. Boil, then simmer 25 minutes until tender.
Add chicken and cook 10 minutes. Drain and reserve the cooking liquid.
Fry the drained meat over high heat until browned on the sides. Dissolve cornstarch in the cool reserved liquid and add it with potatoes.
Simmer 5 minutes until the sauce is glossy. Stir in crisp garlic and serve.

intro: This Crispy Pork Belly Chicharon has a crackling skin and tender, peppery interior.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add salt, bay leaves, peppercorns, and pork belly; cover and boil for 60 minutes.
Drain pork and cool. Prick the skin all over with a toothpick, then cut pork in half to make thinner pieces.
Rub salt over the pork and air-dry for 1 hour, preferably in front of an electric fan.
Heat oil over medium-high heat. Carefully deep-fry pork until crisp and golden brown, using a splatter screen if available.
Drain on a wire rack, cool slightly, and serve with spicy vinegar.

intro: Salmon Sinigang is a tangy fish soup filled with tender vegetables and fresh kangkong.
ingredients: 30 g Knorr Sinigang na Isda mix
1 bunch kangkong, leaves separated and stalks cut small
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add tomatoes, onion, and daikon; cover and cook 5 minutes.
Add salmon and cook gently for 2 minutes. Stir in Knorr Sinigang na Isda mix.
Add long green peppers, okra, and snake beans; cover and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add kangkong stalks, patis, and pepper; cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add kangkong leaves, turn off heat, cover, and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

intro: Corn Soup with Mussels and Malunggay is a sweet, briny soup with tender tahong and fresh greens.
steps: Drain canned corn and blend or process until coarse or smooth, as preferred.
Heat oil in a pot. Sauté ginger and onion until fragrant, then add garlic powder, blended corn, and mussels; cook 1 minute.
Add water and chicken broth, bring to a boil, then simmer 8 minutes until mussels are cooked and open.
Add malunggay, salt, and pepper; cook 2 to 3 minutes until leaves are tender. Serve hot.

intro: Beef Sinina is a slow-cooked coconut beef dish with a spicy ginger-and-spring-onion palapa.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pound spring onions, ginger paste, and 2 finely chopped bird's-eye chillies in a mortar until a rough palapa paste forms; set aside.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, sliced ginger, and onion until softened; add tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Add beef and brown all over. Pour in coconut milk and beef stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour.
Stir in soy sauce and 6 chopped chillies. Continue simmering over low heat for 45 minutes, until the brisket is tender.
Raise heat to high, stir in palapa, and reduce the liquid by half until thickened. Season with salt and black pepper before serving.

intro: This rich Special Goto turns tender offal and rice into a deeply comforting porridge.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons beef powder or 1 beef cube
steps: Bring 6 cups water to a boil. Add tripe, intestine, and 1 teaspoon salt; boil 2 to 3 hours until soft, adding water as needed.
Cool the cooked tripe and intestine, then cut into bite-size pieces.
Heat oil in a deep pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, ginger, and garlic until the onion softens.
Add the sliced offal and cook 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in beef powder or cube, turmeric, and garlic powder.
Add 5 cups water and bring to a boil. Add rice, reduce to low-medium, and cook 30 to 45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with egg, green onion, toasted garlic, and crushed chicharon.

intro: Black sesame gives this soft, chewy Kalamay a nutty crunch.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons black sesame seeds, ground or finely crushed
steps: Whisk the ground glutinous rice, coconut milk, sugar, and black sesame in a saucepan until smooth.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick, glossy, and pulling away from the pan.
Transfer to a lightly oiled dish, smooth the surface, and cool until firm enough to slice.
Cut into small portions and serve at room temperature.

intro: Food for the Gods is a rich, chewy date-and-walnut bar with a buttery brown-sugar crumb.
ingredients: 1 cup butter, cubed and at room temperature
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a baking tray or square baking pan.
Beat the butter until fluffy, then gradually beat in the brown sugar; add eggs and mix until smooth.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt; mix into the butter mixture just until combined.
Fold in dates and walnuts on low speed, then spread the batter evenly in the prepared pan.
Bake for 10 minutes at 180°C, reduce heat to 150°C, and bake 35–40 minutes until set and a tester comes out mostly clean.
Cool completely before cutting into bars and serving.

intro: Seafood Lomi is a thick, savory noodle soup finished with delicate egg ribbons and fresh seafood.
ingredients: 500 g lomi or other thick egg noodles
steps: Bring the seafood stock to a boil. Cook mussels until opened; remove them and reserve both mussels and stock.
Cook lomi according to package directions, then drain, rinse, and set aside.
Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté garlic and shallot until fragrant, then fry squid balls until lightly browned.
Add stock and bring to a boil. Add prawns, kani, and squid; simmer for 3 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with water, stir it into the broth, and simmer 2 minutes until thickened. Add noodles, carrot, and cabbage; return to a boil.
Turn off heat and slowly stir in beaten eggs. Season with pepper and fish sauce; top with mussels, spring onions, and fried garlic.

intro: Balut is a warm, ready-to-eat boiled duck embryo traditionally enjoyed straight from the shell.
steps: Place the prepared balut eggs in a saucepan and cover with water.
Bring the water to a gentle boil over medium-high heat, then warm the eggs for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain and serve the eggs hot with salt and vinegar on the side.
Crack the wider end of each shell, sip the broth if present, then peel and eat the egg.

intro: Gourmet Tuyo turns crisp dried herring into a spicy, aromatic oil-packed rice companion.
ingredients: 1 cup olive oil, sunflower oil, or corn oil
1 red labuyo, sliced, or 1 teaspoon chili flakes
steps: Remove the tuyo heads and fry in hot vegetable oil over high heat until scales loosen; drain on paper towels.
Remove scales and soft portions, then debone or flake the fish as desired and pack it into a clean glass jar.
Combine the chosen oil, garlic, chili, bay leaves, peppercorns, and olives in a saucepan over medium-high heat.
Bring to a brief boil, add paprika, and cook until garlic is tender and lightly browned.
Pour the hot oil mixture over the tuyo, cool completely, then refrigerate at least 3 days before serving with hot rice.

intro: Pata Humba braises pork hocks in a sweet-savory pineapple and soy sauce until fall-apart tender.
ingredients: 4 1/2 pounds pork hocks, cut into serving pieces
steps: Boil pork hocks for 10 minutes, rinse under cold water, and pat dry.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat; fry pork for 2 minutes per side until golden, then remove.
Sauté garlic until lightly browned, add onions until soft, then mash in black beans and cook spices for 30 seconds.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, pineapple juice, and water; return pork, cover, and simmer on low 1 1/2–2 hours until falling from the bone.
Stir in brown sugar, banana blossoms if using, and peanuts; cook 10 minutes until the sauce lightly reduces.
Season with Maggi Magic Sarap and serve hot with steamed rice and sauce.

intro: Ginataang Mais is a silky coconut-and-corn rice pudding best enjoyed warm.
steps: Combine coconut milk and glutinous rice in a pot over medium heat and bring to a boil.
Stir well to prevent sticking, reduce heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add corn, sugar, and salt. Cook 5 to 7 minutes until the corn is tender and the rice is cooked.
Turn off the heat and serve hot.

intro: Linutik is a rustic coconut squash stew with pork, shrimp, and leafy malunggay.
ingredients: 700 g butternut squash, peeled and chopped
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium-high heat and brown the pork for 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic; cook 2 minutes until the onion is translucent.
Add squash, shrimp, coconut milk, and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-low heat for 20 minutes until squash is tender.
Roughly mash the squash with a ladle, leaving some chunks. Stir in fish sauce, sugar, and pepper; simmer 5 minutes.
Add malunggay and cook 3 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and serve hot with rice.

intro: Ginataang Mackerel is a quick canned-fish coconut stew with spinach and ginger.
ingredients: 3 thumb-sized pieces ginger, cut into thin strips
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until the onion softens and garlic is lightly browned.
Add coconut milk and chili peppers. Stir, cover, and cook gently for 5 minutes.
Add mackerel with its brine, water, and vinegar. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Add spinach and cook for 1 minute, just until wilted, then serve.

intro: Filipino Chicken Pasta Alfredo pairs fettucine with a creamy sauce and savory chicken flakes.
ingredients: 300 g CDO Chicken Flakes in Oil
steps: Cook fettucine in boiling water according to the package directions; drain and set aside.
Melt butter in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion is soft.
Add CDO Chicken Flakes in Oil and cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in all-purpose cream and bring just to a boil. Reduce to low heat and stir occasionally until the sauce thickens.
Stir in Parmesan, toss in the fettucine until coated, and serve hot.

intro: These crisp Deep Fried Siomai have a juicy pork, shrimp, and vegetable filling.
steps: Mix pork, carrots, jicama, pepper, salt, green onions, sesame oil, onion, shrimp, and egg until evenly combined.
Place a small spoonful of filling in each wonton wrapper and seal into compact siomai parcels.
Heat 3–4 cups oil over medium heat in a deep pot.
Deep-fry in batches for 5–7 minutes until the wrappers are golden brown and filling is cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chili or Asian dipping sauce and rice.

intro: Paksiw na Galunggong is a clean, tangy vinegar-braised fish dish for warm rice.
steps: Rub salt over the fish, including the cavities, and rest for 10 minutes.
Arrange galunggong, ginger, garlic, and green pepper in a pot. Pour in water and vinegar without stirring.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Cover, reduce to low heat, and simmer 30 to 45 minutes until tender.
Add more water if the pot dries out. Adjust salt carefully and serve with warm rice.

intro: Chicken Gizzard Bicol Express brings chewy-tender gizzards into a creamy, spicy coconut sauce.
steps: Boil chicken gizzards until tender, then set aside.
Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté garlic until beginning to brown, then add onion and cook until softened.
Add boiled gizzards and sauté for 2 minutes. Stir in bagoong alamang and Thai chili.
Pour in water and bring to a boil. Mix in Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix until smooth.
Cover, reduce to low heat, and cook 8 to 10 minutes. Add sigarilyas and cook 5 minutes.
Season with black pepper and serve hot.

intro: Pata ala Lauya is a tangy pork-leg soup enriched with tender young jackfruit and batwan.
