ingredients: 2 kilograms pork leg (pata), cut into sections
500 grams young jackfruit, cut into large chunks
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place pata, onion, salt, and enough water to cover in a large pot; boil, then simmer 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add young jackfruit and boil about 30 minutes, until tender.
Add batwan or sinigang mix and simmer until the broth reaches your preferred sourness.
Stir in annatto powder until evenly colored, then add green chilies.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Crab and Pork Shumai combines sweet crab meat and seasoned pork in tender steamed wonton cups.
steps: Mix pork and crab meat, then thoroughly combine with sesame oil, egg, onion, carrots, salt, and pepper.
Place 1–1 1/2 teaspoons filling in each wonton wrapper; gather the sides around filling while leaving the top open.
Lightly oil a bamboo or metal steamer and arrange shumai with space between each piece.
Bring the steaming water to a boil, cover, and steam 20–25 minutes until the pork filling is fully cooked.
Serve hot with ponzu, soy sauce, and lemon dip.

intro: Rellenong Pusit is tender squid stuffed with a savory pork-and-vegetable filling.
ingredients: 2 tbsp flour, plus more for dredging
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season squid with salt, black pepper, and lemon juice; refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, celery, and tomato; add pork and cook until light brown.
Add carrot and cook 10 minutes. Stir in 2 tablespoons flour, salt, and pepper until the filling becomes sticky; cool completely.
Fill squid with the pork mixture and secure with toothpicks. Dip in egg, then dredge lightly in flour.
Shallow-fry in hot oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Rest briefly, slice crosswise, and serve.

intro: Sisig Pasta brings crisp cooked sisig into a silky calamansi cream sauce for angel hair.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook angel hair according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Add cooked sisig and cook until heated through, crisp, and golden. Stir in calamansi juice and chilli flakes.
Whisk cream and egg yolk together. Lower heat, add the mixture, and stir gently until lightly thickened without scrambling.
Toss in pasta, season with salt and pepper, then garnish with spring onions and Parmesan. Serve immediately.

intro: Tonkatsu Sinangag at Itlog is a crisp pork cutlet breakfast served with garlic rice and egg.
ingredients: 1 5-ounce pork tenderloin slice or pork chop
steps: Rub pork with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Rest for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan over low-medium heat.
Coat pork in flour, then beaten egg, then panko, pressing crumbs over every surface.
Fry 7 minutes per side over low-medium heat until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain the cutlet briefly. Serve beside sinangag and fried egg with tonkatsu sauce.

intro: Pancit Bato Guisado is a savory one-pan noodle dish packed with pork, shrimp, and vegetables.
ingredients: 6 ounces medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork and cook for 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, fish sauce, and chicken broth. Cover, simmer 20 minutes, and add water if the pan becomes dry.
Season with pepper. Add shrimp, snap peas, and carrot; cook 1 minute, then add cabbage and cook 2 minutes.
Add Pancit Bato and stir until liquid is absorbed and noodles are soft, adding a little water if needed.
Transfer to a serving platter and serve.

intro: Kalamay Pinipig is a chewy coconut-and-toasted-rice cake topped with latik.
steps: Soak pinipig in 400 ml coconut milk for 30 minutes.
Line a 6 1/2-inch round pan with banana leaves brushed with coconut oil.
Combine remaining 400 ml coconut milk and brown sugar in a large nonstick pan. Bring to a slow boil over medium heat.
Stir in soaked pinipig. Once thickening begins, lower heat and stir continuously for about 40 minutes until it forms one solid mass.
Transfer immediately to the lined pan, flatten with an oiled spatula, top with latik, and cool before slicing.

intro: Pancit Malabon coats thick rice noodles in an intensely savory crab-and-seafood sauce.
steps: Cook rice noodles according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Boil shrimp, mussels, and squid in 2 cups water until cooked. Reserve the liquid; shell shrimp and mussels, and reserve seafood.
Pound shrimp shells, strain their juices with the seafood cooking liquid, then blend with crab meat, crab fat, annatto, and fish sauce.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil. Add the crab mixture and smoked fish.
Stir cornstarch with a little water, add to the pan, and simmer until thickened, thinning with water if needed.
Toss noodles with sauce. Top with seafood, chicharon, spring onions, eggs, fried garlic, and lemon.

intro: Macapuno Balls are sweet, chewy coconut confections finished in a delicate milk coating.
steps: Drain the macapuno in a fine sieve and rinse with about 2 cups water to reduce the heavy syrup.
Whisk cornstarch and water smooth in a saucepan, then stir in condensed milk and macapuno.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring regularly, until a sticky dough forms and releases from the pan.
Cool completely, oil your hands, and roll tablespoonfuls into balls.
Roll each ball in powdered skimmed milk and wrap or package as desired.

intro: Kangkong Gising Gising is a fiery coconut-milk pork dish with crisp-tender kangkong stems.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic and shallots in a little oil over medium heat until fragrant.
Add pork and stir-fry about 5 minutes until beginning to brown.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered 15 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in bagoong alamang and kangkong stems; cook about 2 minutes until stems soften but remain crisp.
Add coconut cream and chilies, simmer 2 minutes, season with black pepper, and serve hot with rice.

intro: Spicy Ginisang Okra with Tinapa is a quick smoky stir-fry with tender-crisp okra.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Sauté garlic, shallots, and dried chilies until fragrant.
Add flaked tinapa and cook for 2 minutes.
Add okra and stir-fry over high heat for 5 minutes.
Add water, reduce heat to medium, and simmer 5 minutes until the okra is tender but still slightly crisp.
Season with salt and pepper, cook 2 minutes more, and serve hot with rice.

intro: Buko Salad Drink is a chilled pink coconut beverage loaded with gulaman and tapioca pearls.
steps: For each jelly color, dissolve 1 tablespoon jelly powder and 2 tablespoons sugar in 2 cups water, following package ratios if they differ.
Bring each mixture to a low boil, pour into separate molds, refrigerate until firm, then cut into small cubes.
Boil 4 cups water, cook tapioca pearls 10 minutes until translucent, then drain.
Mix evaporated milk, condensed milk, and coconut juice until smooth; stir in coconut strips, pearls, and jelly cubes.
Add red food coloring until evenly pink, then chill in a pitcher or serve over plenty of ice.

intro: Picadillo de Chayote is a lightly sweet, herb-scented beef and chayote skillet meal.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté onion, garlic, and tomatoes in olive oil over medium heat until the tomatoes soften.
Add minced beef and cook, breaking it apart, until light brown.
Add chayote and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in corn, sugar, basil, and oregano; bring to a boil, then simmer 10–15 minutes until chayote is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve warm.

intro: Tapa and Egg Fried Rice combines soy-cured horse meat with a colorful leftover-rice stir-fry.
ingredients: 1/4 cup green onion, chopped and divided
steps: Mix garlic, 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1 teaspoon salt, pepper, and sugar. Coat horse meat, cover, and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Place meat, water, and 2 tablespoons oil in a pan. Bring to a boil, add lemon-lime soda, and cook uncovered until liquid evaporates.
Fry tapa in the remaining oil for 2 minutes until browned; set aside.
Cook beaten eggs in the same pan and break into pieces. Add onion, half the green onion, and bell pepper; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add rice, remaining soy sauce, and sesame oil. Stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes, season with remaining salt if needed, and serve with tapa and green onion.

intro: Beef Mami is a fragrant brisket noodle soup enriched with star anise and tender pechay Baguio.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add beef brisket and cook until lightly browned on the outside.
Add beef cube and star anise, then pour in water and bring to a boil.
Simmer until brisket is tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Place cooked egg noodles and pechay Baguio in bowls. Ladle in beef and hot broth, then garnish with egg and green onions.

intro: Calandracas is a hearty beef, chorizo, chickpea, and macaroni soup.
ingredients: 400 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season beef with salt and black pepper. Heat a little oil in a soup pot until very hot and brown beef on all sides.
Add chorizo, onions, and beef stock. Add enough water to cover the meat, bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 hour.
Add potatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add macaroni and chickpeas; simmer 5 minutes, then add cabbage and cook 5 minutes more until tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Pinoy Style Fried Chicken is simply seasoned, flour-coated chicken with a crisp pan-fried finish.
ingredients: 3 to 4 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Combine sea salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder. Rub the mixture evenly over chicken, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 5 hours.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Shake 2 to 3 chicken pieces at a time in flour until evenly coated.
Fry chicken for 5 minutes per side, then turn again and fry both sides for 4 more minutes.
Drain on a rack or paper towels. Serve hot when the coating is crisp and chicken is cooked through.

intro: Bulalo Kare-kare pairs tender beef shank with peanut-thickened annatto sauce and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
steps: Heat oil in a pot, sauté garlic until fragrant, then sear beef shank for 30 seconds per side.
Add water, boil 10 minutes while skimming, then cover and simmer on low until beef is tender.
Boil annatto seeds in 1 cup water for 1 minute; strain, and blend roasted peanuts into a smooth paste.
Stir peanut paste and annatto water into tender beef; cover 5 minutes, then add Beef Cube and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry until thickened, season with pepper, then cook eggplant and sitaw covered for 5 minutes.
Add bok choy, cover 3 minutes, and serve with bagoong alamang.

intro: Maxs Style Fried Chicken with Kamote Fries features poached, air-dried chicken fried until crisp.
steps: Bring water, onion, peppercorns, and Knorr chicken cube to a boil. Stuff chicken with green onion and lemongrass.
Add chicken and poach over low-medium heat for 35 minutes. Turn and cook 15 minutes more, then cool.
Boil kamote slices in the poaching stock for 3 minutes. Drain and dry. Remove chicken aromatics, rub chicken with Knorr Liquid Seasoning, and air-dry 3 hours.
Halve chicken. Heat oil to 360°F; deep-fry each half skin-side down 5 minutes, turn, and fry 3 minutes.
Refry each half skin-side down for 3 minutes until crisp. Deep-fry kamote until golden and crisp; season with salt and serve together.

intro: This chilled avocado snack is creamy, lightly sweet, and ready in minutes.
steps: Place avocado flesh, powdered milk, and sugar in a bowl.
Gently mash and mix until creamy with some avocado chunks remaining.
Fold in ice cubes and serve immediately.

intro: Honey Calamansi Iced Tea balances bright citrus with honey in a refreshing chilled drink.
steps: Bring 500 ml water to a boil, remove from heat, and steep tea bags for 15 minutes.
Remove tea bags and stir in sugar, honey, and calamansi juice until the sugar dissolves.
Add chilled water, pour over plenty of ice, and serve immediately.

intro: This filling Pinoy breakfast pairs bacon garlic fried rice with a tomato, onion, and cheese omelet.
ingredients: 8 strips bacon, cut into small pieces
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook bacon in a pan until crisp and its fat renders. Reserve about 3 tablespoons bacon fat and remove excess.
Add garlic to the bacon fat and cook until beginning to brown. Stir-fry rice for 3 minutes.
Add 2 teaspoons Knorr Liquid Seasoning, salt, pepper, and 1/4 cup green onions; toss 2 minutes and set aside.
Heat cooking oil, sauté onion until tender, and remove. Arrange tomato in the pan, add butter, and cook 1 minute.
Add 1/2 cup green onions and the sautéed onion. Beat eggs with 1 1/2 teaspoons Knorr Liquid Seasoning and pour over vegetables; add cheese.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat until eggs are set and cheese melts. Serve with bacon garlic fried rice.

intro: Sotanghon Guisado is a savory vermicelli stir-fry with pork, vegetables, and fragrant annatto oil.
steps: Soak sotanghon in water for 10 to 12 minutes. Heat oil, fry garlic until brown, then remove and reserve it.
Add annatto seeds to the garlic oil for about 10 seconds until orange; remove and discard seeds. Brown pork in the oil.
Pour off excess oil, leaving about 3 tablespoons. Sauté onion until soft, add carrot for 1 minute, then add soy sauce and 1/2 cup water.
Add Shrimp Cube, cabbage, snow peas, and bell pepper; cook 2 minutes. Toss in drained sotanghon until evenly mixed.
Add remaining water, cover, and cook over low heat for 3 minutes. Add green onion, season, and top with reserved toasted garlic.

intro: Tasty Pork Afritada is a tomato-braised pork stew with hotdogs, potatoes, and green peas.
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add pork and cook 3–5 minutes until lightly browned.
Add tomato sauce and beef broth, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 45–60 minutes until pork is tender.
Add hotdogs and potatoes; cook 8 minutes until potatoes are nearly tender.
Stir in peas, sugar, salt, and pepper; cook 3 minutes and serve hot.

intro: This shortcut Dinuguan balances rich pork blood with the bright sourness of Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix.
ingredients: 22 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix, Original
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add pork and sauté until lightly browned. Stir in Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix, pork cube, and bay leaves.
Add soy sauce and water, cover, and bring to a boil. Cook over low-medium heat for 35 minutes until pork is tender.
Add long green peppers and pork blood. Stir continuously and cook 5 to 8 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season with sugar and black pepper; add salt only if needed. Serve warm.

intro: Misua and Meatball Soup is a comforting tomato broth with browned pork meatballs and tender patola.
steps: Mix pork, egg, bread crumbs, salt, and pepper; shape the mixture into tablespoon-sized meatballs.
Heat 4 tablespoons oil over low-medium heat and fry meatballs until medium brown; drain and set aside.
Heat remaining oil in a pot, sauté onion and garlic until soft, then add meatballs and water.
Bring to a boil, add beef cube and tomato sauce, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add fish sauce, patola, and spring onions; cook 3 minutes, then add misua and cook 2 minutes.
Serve immediately, adding water if needed as the noodles absorb broth.

intro: Mahi-Mahi Paksiw combines briefly grilled fish with a sharp coconut-vinegar braise.
steps: Rub salt evenly over the mahi-mahi fillet. Preheat a grill over medium-high heat.
Grill the fish for 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
Combine water, coconut vinegar, peppercorns, garlic, and sugar in a pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat.
Add grilled mahi-mahi and green chillies. Cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes until fish flakes easily, adding water if needed.
Transfer the fish and broth to a serving plate and serve hot.

intro: Saucy Pancit Canton is a glossy prawn-enriched noodle dish with pork, kani, and shiitake.
ingredients: 3 cups prawn juice, made from pounded prawn heads and shells with water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Lemon wedges or calamansi, for serving
steps: Soak fresh yellow noodles in boiling water for 1 minute. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry pork for 2 minutes, then remove.
Add oil if needed. Sauté shallots and garlic, then stir-fry carrot and spring onions for 1 minute.
Whisk cornstarch, prawn juice, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and hoisin sauce. Add to the wok and boil until thickened.
Add noodles and prawns; cook over high heat for 2 minutes until prawns are done and noodles absorb sauce. Return pork, season, and serve with citrus.

intro: Biscocho with Condensed Milk transforms homemade yeast bread into a buttery, crunchy sweet toast.
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Combine milk, sugar, salt, and 3 tablespoons butter; warm until lukewarm. Beat in egg.
Mix flour and yeast, add milk mixture, and knead 7 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Let rise, covered, until doubled.
Divide dough into 4 logs, about 6 inches each. Rise 10 to 15 minutes, then bake at 185°C for 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Cool, cut each loaf lengthwise into 4 pieces, and dry at room temperature for 1 to 2 days.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush cut sides with softened butter and condensed milk, then bake at 150°C for 20 to 30 minutes until crisp and lightly golden.

intro: Pork Chao Fan is a quick wok-fried rice dish with savory pork, vegetables, and egg.
steps: Break up clumps in the cold rice so it will fry evenly.
Heat a wok over medium-high, add 2 tablespoons oil, scramble eggs until just set, and remove.
Add remaining oil, sauté onion until soft, then stir-fry pork until browned and cooked through.
Stir in hoisin, soy sauce, and sesame oil, then add carrots and rice; stir-fry on high for 2 minutes.
Add peas and green onions; fry 1 minute, return eggs, season with optional garlic powder, salt, and white pepper, and serve.

intro: Chicken Pandan wraps seasoned chicken in fragrant pandan leaves before deep-frying.
ingredients: 6 chicken wings, small drumsticks, or sliced boneless chicken breasts
6 to 8 fresh or frozen pandan leaves
steps: Mix soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, pepper, garlic, ginger, and lemon or calamansi juice in a bowl.
Add chicken, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Wrap each chicken piece securely in a pandan leaf and tie the leaf ends to hold it closed.
Heat oil in a deep pot over medium heat. Deep-fry wrapped chicken until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain briefly and serve hot, removing the pandan wrapping as you eat.

intro: Kinunot is a tangy coconut fish dish with wilted malunggay and a gentle chile heat.
ingredients: 500 g pagi (stingray) or lemon fish (shark), cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil fish with ginger and salt for 10 minutes until it flakes easily. Drain, cool, and flake.
Toss flaked fish with vinegar and pepper. Marinate 1 hour, then drain well.
Sauté garlic and onion in a little oil. Add coconut milk and bird's-eye chilies; boil and simmer 5 to 10 minutes until shiny and reduced.
Add flaked fish and malunggay; cook over medium heat 5 to 10 minutes until almost dry.
Stir in coconut cream, green chilies, and fish sauce. Simmer over low heat for 5 minutes, then serve.

intro: Chicken Binagoongan braises browned chicken with bagoong alamang, tomatoes, chilies, and sigarilyas.
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil over medium heat; sauté onion 25 seconds, garlic 30 seconds, then cook tomatoes until softened.
Add chicken and sauté until the exterior is medium brown.
Stir in bagoong alamang and cook for 1 minute, then add vinegar and let it come to a boil.
Add water, cover, and boil 5 minutes.
Add sigarilyas, cover, and cook over low-medium heat 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Season with sugar, additional bagoong if needed, black pepper, Thai chilies, and Serrano; cook 3 minutes and serve with rice.

intro: Asado de Carajay is a slow-simmered beef and chorizo stew with smoky paprika and tender vegetables.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg beef brisket, 20% fat, in one block or large strips
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season brisket with salt and pepper. Grill over charcoal 5 to 10 minutes per side until lightly charred, then cool and cube, reserving juices.
Heat olive oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté onions and garlic, then add chorizo and carrots; cook 2 minutes.
Add beef, reserved juices, paprika, tomatoes, stock, and bay leaves. Cover and simmer on low heat for 2 hours, adding water if needed.
Meanwhile, fry potatoes until cooked and lightly browned.
Add tomato paste, potatoes, and capsicum to the beef. Simmer 30 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in lemon juice, adjust salt and pepper, and serve.

intro: Menudo with Raisins and Green Peas is a tomato-braised pork stew with liver, hotdogs, and sweet accents.
steps: Mix pork with soy sauce and half the garlic; marinate 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil. Sauté hotdogs for 1 minute and set aside; soften half the onion, sauté liver for 2 minutes, then set liver aside.
Heat remaining oil in a pot. Brown remaining garlic, soften remaining onion, then cook marinated pork for 3 minutes.
Add tomato sauce and water, cover, and bring to a boil. Add bay leaves and raisins; simmer until pork is tender.
Return liver and hotdogs. Add carrots and potatoes, cover and cook 8 minutes; add peas and Maggi Magic Sarap for 3 minutes, then season and serve.

intro: Creamy Lengua in White Sauce with Mushroom is tender ox tongue in a rich, savory cream sauce.
ingredients: 2 1/2 pounds ox tongue, boiled and sliced
steps: Boil ox tongue 1–1 1/2 hours until tender, cool slightly, peel off the skin, and slice thinly.
Melt butter in a pan over medium heat and sauté onion until soft.
Add sliced lengua and sauté 3 minutes, then add water and bring to a boil.
Add Beef Cube and boil until liquid reduces by half; add mushrooms and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in cream and garlic powder; cook over low-medium heat 3–5 minutes, then stir in mayonnaise until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper, cook until thickened, and serve hot.

intro: Laswa is a light shrimp and vegetable soup with squash, saluyot, and a shell-infused broth.
ingredients: Sea salt or fish sauce, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Peel shrimp and reserve both shrimp and shells. Briefly pulse shells with 2 cups water, then strain the liquid through a fine sieve.
Heat a little oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add squash and string beans, then pour in stock and strained shrimp-shell liquid. Bring to a boil.
Add okra and eggplant; simmer over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until vegetables are tender.
Add shrimp and saluyot, simmer 2 minutes until shrimp turn opaque, then season with fish sauce or salt and black pepper.

intro: Adobong Sili with Pork and Tinapa combines crisp pork, smoky fish, and green chilies in adobo sauce.
ingredients: 600 grams pork belly, cut into bite-sized pieces
200 grams boneless tinapa, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Sauté garlic in oil until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
Fry pork belly until browned; add enough water, vinegar, soy sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar.
Simmer about 45 minutes until pork is tender, then drain and reserve the cooking liquid.
Heat fresh oil in a wok and fry pork until crisp at the edges; add green chilies and cook 5 minutes.
Add tinapa, mix gently, then stir cornstarch into reserved liquid and pour it into the wok.
Simmer 5 minutes until the sauce thickens, top with fried garlic, and serve hot.

intro: Tinola Chicken Mami combines ginger chicken broth, Miki noodles, papaya, and malunggay in one warming bowl.
ingredients: 1/2 small green papaya, sliced into strips
steps: Blanch Miki noodles in boiling water for 20 to 30 seconds. Drain and divide among serving bowls.
Heat oil with garlic over medium heat, stirring until medium brown. Remove garlic and reserve for topping.
Sauté onion and ginger in the remaining oil with black pepper until the onion softens.
Add water and bring to a boil. Add chicken, cover, and cook over medium heat for 35 minutes.
Remove chicken, cool slightly, and shred. Add chicken cube and papaya to broth; cover and cook 10 minutes.
Add malunggay and fish sauce; cook 3 to 5 minutes. Top noodles with chicken and egg, ladle over broth, and finish with fried garlic.

intro: Piaya is a simple pan-cooked pastry with a warm, molten muscovado sugar center.
ingredients: 1 cup flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Process flour, salt, and cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water and process until dough clumps. Transfer to a floured surface, knead gently, and divide into 6 pieces.
Flatten each portion, place 2 teaspoons muscovado sugar in the center, seal like a dumpling, and roll into a 4-inch circle.
Cook in a lightly oiled pan until golden brown on both sides. Serve whole or sliced.

intro: Igado Ilocano is a richly tangy pork offal stew with vegetables and a reduced vinegar-soy sauce.
steps: Marinate the pork liver in 1/2 cup cane vinegar for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes; drain and reserve the liver.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until the onion softens.
Raise heat to high and brown the pork belly and heart.
Add remaining vinegar, soy sauce, bay leaves, and peppercorns; boil, then simmer uncovered over medium heat for 25 minutes until reduced.
Add capsicum, peas, and liver; simmer for 5 minutes, until the liver is cooked through.
Loosen with water if needed, season with fish sauce, and serve with extra cracked peppercorns.

intro: Nilagang Buto-buto ng Baka is a clear, hearty beef-bone soup with saba, potatoes, and greens.
ingredients: 4 pounds beef neck bones, cut into serving pieces
2 cups Napa cabbage, cut into pieces
steps: Put water, onions, peppercorns, and beef neck bones in a deep soup pot and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 3 hours until meat is tender, adding water as needed.
Add saba and potato, raise heat to medium, and boil 10 minutes until tender.
Add bok choy and Napa cabbage, cover, turn off heat, and let residual heat cook vegetables for 8 minutes.
Stir in patis and serve hot with rice.

intro: Champorado with Tuyo is warm chocolate rice porridge served with crisp salted dried fish.
ingredients: 6 to 12 pieces fried salted dried fish (tuyo)
steps: Bring 4 cups water to a boil in a pot over medium-high heat.
Add sugar and cocoa tablea, stirring until the tablea fully melts into the water.
Add salt and glutinous rice. Stir well and return the mixture to a boil.
Lower heat and cook until rice is soft and porridge-like, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes to prevent sticking. Add remaining water as needed.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with fried tuyo.

intro: A creamy Filipino-style potato salad with chicken, pineapple, and sweet relish.
ingredients: 200 g cooked chicken thigh meat, flaked
steps: Boil the unpeeled potatoes for 15–20 minutes, until tender when pierced; drain and cool completely.
Peel the cooled potatoes, cut into 1-inch cubes, and place in a large bowl.
Add chicken, eggs, carrot, celery, pineapple, and onion to the potatoes.
Whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, relish, pepper, salt, and sugar until smooth.
Gently toss the dressing through the salad, then chill or serve.

intro: A rich tomato-braised pork stew with tender vegetables and bright bell peppers.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until softened and fragrant.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned. Stir in tomato sauce, beef broth, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over medium heat for about 45 minutes, adding broth if needed, until pork is tender.
Add potato and carrots; cook 5 to 8 minutes until beginning to soften.
Stir in bell peppers and cook 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Cheesy Lumpia pairs seasoned pork with molten Mozzarella in a crisp fried wrapper.
steps: Combine pork, onion, carrot, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, cornstarch, egg, and black pepper until evenly mixed.
Lay out a wrapper and spread about 1 1/2 tablespoons filling along one side; place sliced string cheese in the center and cover it with pork.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly, and seal the edge; repeat with the remaining filling and wrappers.
Heat the remaining oil in a wok over medium heat and deep-fry lumpia until golden brown and the pork is fully cooked.
Drain on a rack or paper towels, then serve hot with ketchup if desired.

intro: A deeply savory beef and tendon stew finished with potatoes, mushrooms, and capsicums.
ingredients: 600 g beef tendons and/or kneecaps, bite-sized
600 g beef neck and/or brisket, cubed
Freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sauté onions and garlic until translucent and fragrant.
Brown brisket in batches; remove. Brown tendons or kneecaps, then cook tomato until softened.
Cover the tendons with water, boil, then cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Return brisket and add chorizo; simmer 1 hour, adding water as needed to keep the meat covered.
Add potatoes and bay leaf; simmer about 30 minutes until meat and potatoes are tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Add mushrooms and capsicums; simmer 5 to 10 minutes until tender-crisp, then serve with rice.

intro: Chorizo de Cebu is a sweet, garlicky, lightly spicy pork sausage with a caramelized finish.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp carrageenan, red agar powder, or white agar powder
steps: Mix anise liqueur, puréed pineapple, paprika, and annatto powder in a large bowl.
Add pork, sugar, salt, pepper, garlic, chillies, and carrageenan; mix thoroughly until sticky and uniform.
Stuff the mixture into sausage casings, knot the end, and twist every 1 1/2 inches to form links.
Refrigerate the links for 1 day to firm and marinate; freeze any sausages not cooking immediately.
For cooking, cover sausages with a little water in a pan and cook covered over low heat until water evaporates.
Add a little oil and cook slowly until browned and the sugar begins to caramelize.

intro: This hearty Chopsuey combines tender pork, crisp vegetables, and quail eggs in a savory sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 small cabbage, cut into large pieces
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok or large pan over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned, then stir-fry with oyster sauce for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp cube and 1/2 cup water; boil, cover, and cook until the liquid reduces by half.
Stir in cauliflower and carrot, then add bell peppers and cabbage; stir-fry 3–5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Mix cornstarch with remaining water, stir into the pan until thickened, then fold in quail eggs.

intro: Tender beef lengua is pan-fried and simmered in a tangy, olive-studded tomato sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb cooked beef lengua, tender and sliced
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Dredge lengua in flour, shake off excess, and fry about 1 minute per side; set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic in the same pot until soft. Add tomatoes and wine, then simmer 2 minutes.
Return lengua to the pot. Add soy sauce, water, and bouillon; bring to a boil.
Add bay leaves, cover, and cook over low heat until the sauce reduces by about half.
Add vinegar and bring the sauce back to a boil. Stir in sugar, olives, and mushrooms; cook 5 to 8 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve warm.

intro: Dinailan is a coconut-rich pork stew seasoned with shrimp-paste block and sharp cane vinegar.
ingredients: 750 g pork belly or shoulder, cubed
1 cup Dinailan shrimp-paste block, crumbled, or raw pink bagoong, thoroughly rinsed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat; sauté garlic, onion, and siling labuyo for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add pork and brown lightly on all sides, about 7 minutes.
Add vinegar, bring to a high boil uncovered without stirring, and cook for 2 minutes.
Reduce to medium heat, stir in Dinailan until dissolved, then add coconut milk and water.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Uncover, reduce the sauce slightly, then stir in sugar and season with salt and pepper.

intro: Ginataang Alimasag is a creamy coconut crab dish with sweet kalabasa and tender sitaw.
ingredients: 40 g Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste (optional)
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion is translucent.
Whisk the water and Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix until smooth, pour into the pan, and bring to a boil.
Add steamed crab and kalabasa, cover, and boil for 5 minutes.
Add sitaw and cook for 8 minutes, until the squash is tender and the sauce is creamy.
Season with salt and black pepper if desired, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Canned sardines become a quick, fragrant rice companion with tomato, citrus, and optional siling labuyo.
ingredients: 11 oz sardines in tomato sauce, about 2 small cans
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add tomato and cook for 3 minutes until juicy.
Add sardines with their tomato sauce and the siling labuyo; bring to a gentle boil.
Cook over low to medium heat for 5 minutes, adding a little water only if the pan becomes dry.
Stir in lemon or calamansi juice, pepper, and fish sauce or salt; cook 1 minute.
Transfer to a bowl, garnish with parsley, and serve with steamed rice.

intro: Creamy aligue coats pasta with quickly seared prawns and squid in a luxurious seafood sauce.
ingredients: 2 to 3 long squid, sliced into rings
1/4 cup grated Parmesan, plus more to serve
steps: Cook pasta according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Season prawns and squid with salt and pepper. Sear in very hot olive oil until half-cooked, then remove.
Lower heat to medium and sauté garlic and onion in more oil until lightly browned.
Add wine and scrape up browned bits. When reduced and browned, stir in aligue and shrimp stock; boil, then reduce to low.
Add pasta, seafood, parsley, and cream. Raise heat and toss until the sauce coats everything evenly.
Add lemon juice and Parmesan; adjust salt and pepper. Serve immediately with extra Parmesan.

intro: These Choco Crinkles bake into fudgy chocolate cookies with their classic snowy cracks.
steps: Mix cocoa, sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla in a bowl until evenly combined.
Sift flour, baking powder, and salt together, then stir into the cocoa mixture until a soft dough forms.
Cover and refrigerate overnight. Freeze the dough for 30 minutes before shaping.
Heat the oven to 170°C. Roll heaping tablespoonfuls into balls, coat generously in powdered sugar, and space on a lined baking tray.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, until cracked and set around the edges; cool before serving.

intro: Cola gives this pork adobo a gentle sweetness and glossy, deeply savory sauce.
steps: Heat a wide pan over medium-high heat and sear pork, stirring often, until browned and it renders enough fat.
Push pork aside, sauté garlic in the rendered fat for 30 seconds, then mix and cook for 1 minute.
Add vinegar and soy sauce; bring to a boil, stir, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add peppercorns, bay leaves, and cola. Cover and simmer over low heat until pork is tender, about 35–40 minutes.
Add water as needed to prevent drying, season with salt if desired, and serve with the sauce.

intro: Pandesal and Sardines Pizza is a quick, savory snack with tomato-sauced sardines and melted cheddar.
ingredients: 2 small 155 g cans sardines in tomato sauce
A pinch of Italian seasoning, optional
steps: Heat the oven to 370°F (188°C) and split the pandesal in half.
Separate the sardines from their tomato sauce; mix tomato paste, 2 tablespoons sardine sauce, and Italian seasoning.
Spread the tomato mixture over each pandesal half, then top with 1 to 2 sardine pieces and cheddar.
Bake on a tray for 5 to 8 minutes, until the cheese melts and edges are lightly crisp.
Finish with parsley and red pepper flakes; serve warm.

intro: Sotanghon Soup is a comforting chicken, shrimp, and glass-noodle soup enriched with dual stocks.
ingredients: 1 cup rehydrated wood ear fungus, sliced
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add 4 cups each shrimp stock and chicken stock with wood ear fungus; bring to a boil.
Add chicken and sotanghon; cook for 4 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook 3 minutes more, adding stock if a soupier consistency is needed.
Mix 1/2 cup hot broth with annatto until smooth, then return it to the pot with carrot.
Turn off heat, season with fish sauce and white pepper, and top with fried garlic.

intro: A crisp-edged omelette makes the salty crunch of dried shrimps the star.
steps: Heat enough oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry dried shrimps until crisp.
Remove the shrimps and drain briefly, then mix them into the beaten eggs.
Pour off excess oil, leaving a thin coating in the pan.
Divide the egg mixture into three portions; cook each over low heat until firm and golden underneath.
Turn if desired, cook through, and serve warm.

intro: A cool, creamy fruit salad that is especially welcome after a warm Filipino meal.
steps: Whisk condensed milk and whipped cream together in a large chilled bowl until smooth.
Add apples, pineapple, peaches, nectarines, and grapes; fold gently until evenly coated.
Cover and chill until cold. Spoon into serving bowls and top with cherries.

intro: Buntaa is a rich stuffed-crab dish simmered in fragrant coconut milk.
ingredients: 2 kg large female crabs, cleaned and chilled
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Remove the top shells, discard inedible parts, and scrape crab roe and fat into a bowl; rinse the shells and bodies gently.
Mix roe and fat with coconut meat, spring onions, half the garlic, ginger, onion, and salt.
Fill the shells and bodies, reassemble each crab, tie securely with kitchen string, and reserve any released liquid.
Bring coconut milk, remaining garlic, and chilies to a boil over medium heat; gently add crabs and cook 5–7 minutes until orange.
Add coconut cream and reserved liquid, return to a boil, then simmer briefly on low. Season with fish sauce and pepper; serve with rice.

intro: Creamy Ginataang Langka pairs tender young jackfruit with smoky tinapa flakes and malunggay.
ingredients: 3 lb unripe jackfruit, chopped with seeds removed
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add jackfruit and cook 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in tinapa flakes and cook 1 minute.
Add pepper and chili peppers. Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, then stir in bagoong and vinegar.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until jackfruit is tender.
Add malunggay and cook 5 to 10 minutes more. Salt only if needed, then serve with rice.

intro: Prepared tuyo is gently fried and packed in a tangy, aromatic olive-oil dressing.
ingredients: 1/3 cup white wine vinegar or red wine vinegar
steps: Gently fry tuyo in oil just until the scales loosen easily. Drain and cool completely.
Simmer olive oil, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, and salt gently for 15 minutes.
Add carrot and red chilies to the dressing, then remove from heat and cool fully.
Remove the tuyo heads and scales. Pack fish into a clean, dry bottle and cover completely with cooled oil mixture.
Seal and serve the prepared tuyo with rice or bread.

intro: Chicken and Pork Adobo slowly braises two meats in a balanced soy-vinegar sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb pork belly, cut into serving pieces
1 1/2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook garlic until just beginning to brown.
Add pork and chicken; sauté for 5 minutes.
Add peppercorns, bay leaves, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and water; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes, then remove the chicken and continue cooking pork until tender, adding water if needed.
Return chicken, add vinegar, and bring to a boil before stirring.
Stir in brown sugar and cook until the sauce reduces; add salt only if needed and serve with rice.

intro: Sinabawang Talbos ng Kamote is a bright, lightly sour soup that keeps tender greens at the center.
ingredients: Juice of 6 to 7 calamansi or 2 lemons
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine bagoong monamon, tomatoes, onion, calamansi juice, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes to soften the tomatoes.
Add sweet potato tops and simmer 2 minutes, just until tender and bright green.
Season with freshly ground black pepper and serve immediately.

intro: Light Pacensia-style meringue cookies are crisp, delicate, and gently vanilla-scented.
steps: Heat the oven to 140°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Sift the flour and confectioners' sugar together.
Beat egg whites on high speed until frothy, then add lemon juice, vanilla, and sugar; beat to stiff peaks.
Fold in the sifted dry ingredients just until smooth, then transfer the batter to a piping bag.
Pipe 1-inch mounds at least 1 inch apart and bake for about 30 minutes, until light golden and dry.

intro: Luncheon Meat Caldereta turns crisp luncheon meat into a speedy tomato-and-liver-spread stew.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and fry luncheon meat on all sides until browned; set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion in the remaining oil until the onion softens.
Add liver spread and cook for 30 seconds, then add tomato sauce and water and bring to a boil.
Add potato and carrot, cover, and cook for 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Stir in peas, bell peppers, and luncheon meat; cook 2 minutes, then season and top with cheddar.

intro: Oriental Lomi is a thick, comforting noodle soup packed with pork, Chinese sausage, and vegetables.
ingredients: 3 tbsp all-purpose flour mixed with 1/2 cup water
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until softened without browning the garlic.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned. Add Chinese sausage and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in broth and water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add miki noodles and cook 15–18 minutes. Add carrot for 5 minutes, then cabbage and scallions for 3 minutes.
Stir in flour slurry until lightly thickened. Quickly stir in egg, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

intro: Chicken Bicol Express is a creamy, spicy coconut stew sharpened with bagoong alamang.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add chicken and Thai chilies; stir-cook until chicken is lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add Knorr Chicken Cube and cook over low to medium heat until coconut milk is reduced by half.
Stir in bagoong alamang and long green peppers. Cover and cook 2 minutes, then serve.

intro: Hipon sa Aligue features smoky-seared prawns in a luxurious coconut and crab-fat sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg tiger prawns or large prawns, shell-on, cleaned and thoroughly drained
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok until smoking; sear prawns in batches for about 30 seconds per side until lightly charred, then set aside.
Add more oil if needed and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion over medium heat.
Add tomatoes and chillies; cook until tomatoes soften.
Raise heat, add coconut cream and aligue, and bring the sauce to a boil.
Return prawns, season with fish sauce and pepper, and cook for 1 minute until heated through.
Turn off heat; garnish with coriander, drizzle with lemon juice, and serve hot.

intro: Delicate lapu lapu gently cooks in coconut milk with squash, chilies, and malunggay.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add squash and water; bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes.
Add coconut milk, malunggay, lapu lapu, and chilies. Return to a very slow boil.
Simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, until squash is tender and fish flakes easily.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: This no-churn avocado ice cream is silky, fruity, and dotted with fresh avocado pieces.
steps: Whip chilled cream to stiff peaks, stopping before it turns grainy; keep chilled.
Blend condensed milk and mashed avocado until completely smooth.
Gently fold the avocado mixture and cubed avocado into the whipped cream without deflating it.
Transfer to a freezer-safe container, cover, and freeze for about 6 hours or until firm enough to scoop.
Let stand a few minutes at room temperature before scooping and serving.

intro: Menudong Giniling is a hearty tomato-based minced pork stew with sweet raisins and colorful vegetables.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until soft, then add pork and cook until browned.
Add stock, tomato paste, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, potatoes, carrots, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Simmer 10 minutes, then add peas, raisins, and capsicum.
Simmer 10 minutes more, until vegetables are tender and sauce thickens; season with salt and pepper.

intro: Pinayti is a concentrated coconut-and-shrimp dish cooked until its flavorful oil separates.
ingredients: 350 g fresh or frozen micro shrimps, cleaned
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook micro shrimps with water and a pinch of salt over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until cooked and the water evaporates.
Pound the cooked shrimps in a mortar and pestle until pasty.
Heat oil in the same pan, sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant, then stir in the pounded shrimp for 3 minutes.
Add vinegar and cook 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then stir in coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce heat, simmer 10 minutes, add coconut cream, and simmer about 20 minutes until nearly dry and oil separates.

intro: Pata con Setas is a long-simmered pork leg stew with chorizo, tomatoes, beans, and bok choy.
ingredients: 1 1/2 pork legs, cut into smaller sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 bunch bok choy, trimmed and blanched
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork leg and brown lightly on all sides.
Add chorizo, paprika, and 1 tablespoon tomato paste; stir and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water, chopped tomatoes, and bay leaves; boil, then simmer over low heat for 1 1/2 hours, adding water as needed.
Add cannellini beans and remaining tomato paste; simmer 15 minutes, season, and serve with blanched bok choy.

intro: Crema de Fruta layers sponge cake, silky custard, fruit, and a clear pineapple gel topping.
steps: For custard, whisk milk, egg yolks, confectioners' sugar, and flour in a saucepan. Stir constantly over low heat until thickened; cool.
For gelatin, stir pineapple juice, gelatin, water, sugar, and lemon juice over low heat until fully dissolved; cool slightly.
Place one sponge layer in a serving dish. Spread with custard and arrange some peaches, pineapples, and cherries on top.
Add the second cake layer, spread with remaining custard, and arrange remaining fruit. Pour gelatin evenly over the surface.
Chill until the gelatin is fully set, then slice and serve.

intro: Classic chicken adobo gains extra comfort from hard-boiled eggs simmered in its savory sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken thighs, cut into serving pieces
steps: Combine chicken, soy sauce, peppercorns, and half the garlic. Cover and marinate at least 1 hour.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook remaining garlic until browned.
Add chicken with marinade and cook 3 minutes. Pour in broth and bring to a boil.
Add bay leaves and vinegar; bring back to a boil, cover, and simmer until chicken is tender and sauce reaches your preferred consistency.
Taste for salt, add eggs, and cook 2 minutes more before serving.

intro: Tiniim na Manok braises whole chicken in a sweet-savory pineapple sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add pineapple titbits, pineapple juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, peppercorns, and fish sauce; bring to a boil.
Add chicken, reduce to low heat, cover, and simmer about 45 minutes, turning it halfway through, until fully cooked.
Transfer chicken to a serving dish. Keep the sauce simmering over medium heat.
Mix cornstarch with 1/4 cup water, stir into the sauce until thick, then pour over the chicken and serve hot.

intro: Binagoongan Baboy sa Gata balances rich pork, bagoong, coconut milk, tomatoes, and mild chilies.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat and brown pork on all sides; remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion until soft, then add tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Return pork and add vinegar, half the coconut milk, bay leaves, and water. Simmer 45 minutes, until tender.
Stir in bagoong, remaining coconut milk, sugar, and finger chilies.
Simmer until the sauce reduces and turns rich, then season with black pepper and serve.

intro: Ube Cake is a soft purple celebration cake layered with whipped cream-cheese frosting and toasted cake crumbs.
ingredients: 2 tsp ube extract or food color, plus extra drops
3/4 to 1 cup ube halaya or jam
steps: Whisk lard, oil, and 2 tablespoons flour into a smooth pan grease; coat an 8-inch, 3-inch-deep round pan and heat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Beat butter, oil, and sugar until fluffy, about 2 to 3 minutes; beat in eggs one at a time, then vanilla and ube extract.
Add flour, baking powder, salt, and milk; mix just until combined. Reserve 1/2 cup batter for two lined muffin cups, then mix ube halaya into remaining batter.
Bake cupcakes 20 to 25 minutes and cake 50 to 60 minutes, until a center toothpick is clean; cool cake 10 minutes in pan, then completely on a rack.
Crumble cooled cupcakes, bake crumbs 15 minutes, cool, and pulse finely. Split the cooled cake horizontally if using one pan.
Beat cream cheese and powdered sugar smooth; slowly add cream, then whip to stiff peaks and fold in vanilla. Tint most frosting with ube extract.
Fill cake layers with white frosting, cover with ube frosting, press on crumbs, and pipe rosettes with reserved white frosting.

intro: Sinigang sa Pakwan balances beefy tamarind broth with watermelon, taro, and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 1 large seedless watermelon, peeled and cubed
2 lemongrass stalks, white parts only, pounded
1 (40 g) packet sinigang mix, or 400 g tamarind
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil beef in water for 10 minutes to remove scum, then rinse under running water.
Place watermelon in a pot and top with beef, onion, ginger, and lemongrass. Add enough water to cover and simmer 1 hour.
Add taro and simmer 30 minutes, until beef and taro are tender.
Stir in sinigang mix. If using tamarind, simmer it in muslin, squeeze out the juice, then discard solids and lemongrass.
Add chilies and okra; cook 5 minutes. Add kangkong, cover, and turn off heat.
Season with fish sauce and pepper before serving.

intro: Asadong Pork Giniling is a savory braised pork dish with mushrooms and tender quail eggs.
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add minced pork and cook, breaking it apart, until lightly browned.
Add mushrooms, oyster sauce, soy sauce, star anise, sugar, and chicken stock. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry and quail eggs; simmer until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and pepper, fold in spring onions, and serve with jasmine rice.

intro: This hearty Chop Suey combines chicken, liver, and crisp vegetables in a light savory sauce.
ingredients: 3 tbsp Knorr SavorRich Chicken Liquid Seasoning
1 1/2 tsp cornstarch, dissolved in 1/3 cup water
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add chicken and cook until lightly browned. Add chicken liver and cook 1 minute.
Pour in 1/2 cup water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook 5 minutes.
Add carrot, cauliflower, and snap peas; cook 3 minutes. Add bell peppers, cover, and cook 3 minutes.
Add cabbage and toss for 2 minutes. Stir in cornstarch slurry, seasoning, and pepper until lightly thickened.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot.

intro: Soy Garlic Chicken is deeply marinated chicken with a simple crisp, savory shallow-fried finish.
steps: Combine chicken, soy sauce, garlic, lemon juice, and black pepper; marinate covered in the refrigerator for at least 24 hours.
Remove chicken from the refrigerator and let it stand until close to room temperature.
Heat a shallow layer of oil in a covered pan over medium heat.
Shallow-fry chicken for 8 to 10 minutes, turning as needed, until browned and cooked through.
Drain briefly and serve hot.

intro: Filipino Shrimp Curry is a gently spiced coconut curry with tender shrimp and colorful peppers.
ingredients: 1 lb shrimp, deveined, heads and shells removed
steps: Toss shrimp with lemon or calamansi juice, black pepper, and cayenne; marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot; sauté onion for 30 seconds, then add garlic, ginger, and tomato and cook until onion is tender.
Add coconut milk, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Stir in curry powder and Shrimp Cube; cook 2 minutes.
Add turmeric and bell peppers, cover, and cook 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook 3 to 4 minutes until opaque; season with patis, stir in parsley, and cook 2 minutes.

intro: Sinigang na Isda sa Miso at Sampaloc is a deeply savory, tangy fish soup with miso and tamarind.
ingredients: 1 kg Hapuka fish jaws or equivalent, chopped
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine onion, tomatoes, radish, and water in a pot; bring to a boil.
Add fish jaws, yellow miso, and tamarind mix; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add okra and simmer 5 minutes until tender.
Add mustard greens and simmer 2 minutes, just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and freshly ground black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Minanok is a peppery beef-rib soup with potatoes and mustard leaves.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season beef ribs with salt. Heat oil in a soup pot and lightly brown the ribs; remove them.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in the same pot until fragrant.
Return ribs and add enough water to barely cover them. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until tender.
Season with fish sauce and plenty of black pepper. Add mustard leaves, simmer 2 minutes, then serve.

intro: Adobong Tarlac pairs pork and chicken with pineapple for a tangy, caramelized adobo.
ingredients: 2 cups cubed pineapple, fresh or canned
1/2 cup Philippine soy sauce or Kikkoman soy sauce
steps: Marinate pork and chicken in pineapple juice for 2–6 hours. Drain, reserving the juice.
Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove. Fry pork until browned, remove, then brown chicken and remove.
Return pork to the pot with water, vinegar, soy sauce, reserved juice, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar. Boil, then simmer 25 minutes.
Add chicken and cook 10 minutes more, until both meats are tender. Drain and reserve the liquid.
Fry drained meat over high heat until browned. Stir cornstarch into cool reserved liquid, add with pineapple, simmer 5 minutes, and serve.

intro: Pineapple-marinated ribs simmer into a sweet-savory Hamonado with tender fruit chunks.
ingredients: 2 lb spare ribs, cut into serving pieces
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Drain pineapple chunks, reserving juice. Marinate ribs in the juice at least 1 hour, then remove ribs and reserve the juice.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add ribs and cook until lightly browned. Add reserved pineapple juice, soy sauce, and beef broth; bring to a boil.
Add pineapple chunks, cover, and simmer over low to medium heat for 1 hour until ribs are tender.
Stir in brown sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook until the sauce reduces by half, then serve with rice.

intro: Kinamatisang Baka is a beefy tomato soup brightened with sitaw and sweet potato leaves.
steps: Place beef neck bones and water in a pot, bring to a boil, then simmer until the meat is tender, about 90 minutes.
Remove the beef and reserve the cooking broth.
Heat oil in the pot, sauté onion and garlic, then add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Return beef, add reserved broth and beef cube, bring to a boil, and cook for 2 minutes. Season with patis and pepper.
Add sitaw for 5 minutes, then sweet potato leaves; cover for 2 minutes and serve hot with rice.

intro: Pulled Beef Asado transforms slow-boiled beef into a glossy, savory-sweet shredded filling.
steps: Place beef in a pot and add enough water to fully submerge it with extra water above the meat.
Bring to a rolling boil uncovered over high heat; cover, reduce to low, and cook 3 to 4 hours until very tender.
Remove beef from broth and shred it with two forks.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat; sauté garlic and onion until lightly browned.
Add beef, soy sauce, hoisin sauce, black pepper, and cayenne; stir constantly for several minutes until absorbed and combined.

intro: Tapuy is best served simply as a chilled prepared rice wine for a small celebratory toast.
steps: Chill prepared Tapuy thoroughly before serving.
Place ice and a ginger slice in each small glass, if desired.
Pour Tapuy into glasses and serve immediately as a celebratory drink.

intro: Cansi is a sour, aromatic beef-shank soup brightened with batwan, annatto, langka, and chillies.
ingredients: 6 to 8 cups water, plus more as needed
1 stalk lemongrass, tied in a knot
steps: Cover beef shanks with water and rock salt in a pot; cover and bring to a rolling boil over high heat.
Drain, rinse the beef and pot, then return beef to the pot and add enough fresh water to cover.
Bring to a boil over low heat; add onion, lemongrass, and salt, then cover and simmer until fork-tender.
Add batwan, cover, and cook until soft.
Press annatto seeds in a fine sieve submerged in the broth to release their color.
Add langka and cook until tender; add green and red chillies, simmer 3 minutes, and serve piping hot.

intro: Tender pork bola-bola, silky misua, and sweet patola make a soothing everyday soup.
steps: Combine pork, egg, 1 minced onion, flour, salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Shape into balls using about 1 1/2 tablespoons each.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and pan-fry meatballs until lightly browned outside; remove.
Sauté garlic in the remaining oil until golden, then add the remaining onion and cook until soft.
Add water and bring to a boil. Return meatballs, add Knorr Pork Cube, cover, and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add misua and patola, cover, and cook 5 minutes until patola is tender and misua is soft.
Season with patis and remaining pepper. Stir in scallions and serve.

intro: Soft scrambled eggs get a bold, savory lift from sautéed bagoong and sweet tomato.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Cook tomato until soft and juicy.
Add bagoong and stir-fry until fragrant.
Pour in eggs, season with black pepper, and stir gently until softly set. Serve hot.

intro: Lechon Belly is a crisp-skinned rolled pork roast perfumed with garlic, lemongrass, and chilies.
ingredients: 3.5 lb pork belly, about 1 1/2 inches thick
5–6 green onion stalks, trimmed and bundled
steps: Prick shallow holes across the skin and deeper holes in the meat, without piercing through the skin.
Season the meat with pepper and fish sauce. Rub salt over the skin and refrigerate uncovered for at least 3 hours.
Wipe away salt and moisture. Arrange garlic, green onions, lemongrass, and chilies on the meat, roll tightly, and tie every 2 inches.
Brush skin with lye water and chill 1–2 hours. Brush with vinegar and soy sauce, then air-dry briefly.
Roast on a rack at 180°C for 2 hours. Raise to 200°C and roast 30–60 minutes, until the skin is crisp.

intro: Crispy pork belly is glazed in a spicy-sweet bagoong sauce made for plenty of rice.
ingredients: 500 g pork belly, cut into pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place pork, 1 cup water, and 2 tablespoons oil in a wok. Bring to a boil and cook until the water evaporates.
Continue cooking until pork renders its fat. Add garlic and fry over medium heat until pork is brown and crisp.
Add 2 tablespoons water and vinegar to deglaze the wok.
Stir in bagoong, brown sugar, cayenne, and black pepper; cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately with rice.

intro: Sisig Matua is a sharp, spicy vinegar salad of tender steamed pig's face and ears.
ingredients: 800 g pig's face and ears, thoroughly cleaned
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pig's face and ears with salt.
Bring steamer water to a boil, add the pork to the rack, cover, and steam until very tender, about 1 hour.
Cool until safe to handle, then chop the meat into small pieces.
Toss pork with onion, bird's-eye chilies, green chilies, and ginger.
Pour over vinegar, season with salt and black pepper, and serve.

intro: Gisadong Sayote is a straightforward chayote sauté made satisfying with crisp pork belly and savory stock.
ingredients: Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Warm oil in a wok and cook the pork over medium-high heat until browned and crisp. Lift it out and reserve.
Using the rendered fat in the wok, cook the shallots and garlic until the shallots are soft and aromatic.
Stir in the sliced chayote and toss over the heat for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken stock and return the pork. Bring the liquid up to a boil, then cook at a steady simmer for about 5 minutes, until the chayote is tender.
Taste and finish with fish sauce or salt and black pepper. Serve while hot.

intro: Buttered Puto makes soft, pandan-scented steamed cakes with a buttery crumb and cheese topping.
steps: Whisk flour, sugar, and baking powder in a mixing bowl.
Mix in melted butter, evaporated milk, egg, water, and pandan essence until the batter is smooth.
Pour batter into individual molds; top with cheese now if using non-quick-melt cheese.
Bring 4 cups water to a boil in a steamer, arrange molds inside, and steam for about 20 minutes.
For quick-melt cheese, uncover, top each puto, cover again, and steam 2 to 5 minutes until melted.
Remove from molds and serve hot or cold.

intro: Gallina con Guisantes is a comforting chicken stew with potatoes, carrots, leeks, and peas.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken legs, drumsticks and/or thighs
1 cup green peas, canned or fresh
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Toss with flour, salt, and pepper until lightly coated.
Heat butter and oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Fry chicken in batches until golden; set aside.
Cook carrots, leeks, bay leaf, and oregano briefly in the same pot until aromatic.
Return chicken and add hot stock. Bring to a gentle boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook 20 to 25 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook until potatoes and chicken are tender. Stir in peas for the final few minutes.
Adjust salt, pepper, and optional MSG. Serve hot when the broth is lightly thickened.

intro: Pinakaging na Baka turns tender marinated beef ribs into crisp, deeply seasoned fried beef.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg beef ribs or 1 kg rib fingers
steps: Combine garlic, pepper, star anise, calamansi juice, and salt. Coat beef thoroughly and refrigerate overnight.
Place beef and marinade in a pot with bay leaves. Cover and simmer over very low heat for about 1 1/2 hours, until tender.
Add 1/2 cup water only if the pot becomes dry, then cool the cooked beef.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C. Fry cooled beef in batches until golden brown and crisp outside.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

intro: A rich coconut-based Dinuguan with tender pork belly and mild chayote.
ingredients: 1 large chayote or small green papaya, small cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat; brown the pork belly.
Add garlic, onion, and ginger; cook until the onion is soft.
Add chilies, coconut milk, and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer 35 minutes until coconut oil begins separating.
Add cane vinegar and return to a gentle boil for 5 minutes.
Lower heat; stir in chayote or papaya and pig's blood slowly. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring gently, until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Lumpiang Hubad is a fresh vegetable stir-fry finished with a rich, savory peanut sauce.
ingredients: 100 g shrimp, shelled and finely chopped
8 cloves garlic, divided: 2 minced and 6 skin-on
3 tsp cornstarch dissolved in 1/2 cup water
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat; brown the pork, then stir-fry the 4 minced garlic cloves for 1 minute.
Add sweet potato and cook 1 minute; add cabbage, French beans, and shrimp, then stir-fry 1 minute.
Add chicken stock, simmer 1 minute, season with salt, then drain the filling thoroughly in a colander.
Boil the 6 skin-on garlic cloves in water until soft; peel and mash them.
Heat peanut oil in a saucepan; brown 2 minced garlic cloves, then add soy sauce, water, sugar, crushed peanuts, and mashed garlic.
Boil, then stir in cornstarch slurry over low heat until thick. Plate filling, spoon over sauce, and finish with ground peanuts.

intro: Sinanglaw is a clear, tangy Ilocano beef soup balanced with a distinctive bitter note.
ingredients: 500 g beef brisket or another economical beef cut, cubed
300 g beef tendons, cut into squares
1/4 cup diluted beef bile or 2–3 bitter gourd pieces, roughly chopped
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a deep pot; sauté garlic, onions, and ginger until fragrant. Brown the beef, then add the tendons.
Add enough water to cover. Boil, then simmer gently for 45 minutes; strain the broth and reserve the meat.
Return clear broth and tendons to the pot. Simmer 90–120 minutes, adding water as needed, until tendons are soft.
Add beef, tripe, and chillies. Add bile, or bundle bitter gourd with kamias or tamarind in muslin; simmer 30 minutes.
Press the bundle to release its juices, season with fish sauce or salt, and wilt in spinach if using. Serve hot.

intro: A deeply caramelized coconut cheesecake with the familiar savoriness of bibingka toppings.
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated quickmelt or Kraft Eden cheese
Banana leaf, cut to fit an 8 x 3-inch springform pan
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C. Beat cream cheese at medium speed until completely smooth, then beat in sugar until silky.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix in coconut cream and vanilla, then sift in both flours and mix only until smooth.
Line the 8 x 3-inch springform pan snugly with banana leaf. Pour in batter and arrange salted duck egg slices over it.
Bake for 20 minutes. Scatter cheese over the top and bake 20 minutes more, until darkly caramelized with a gently jiggly center.
Cool completely, remove the pan and banana leaf carefully, then chill before slicing.

intro: A hearty wok noodle dish with chicken, liver, and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 1 packed cup rehydrated wood ear fungus, sliced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak the Pancit bihon in water for up to 10 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion. Stir-fry snow peas and carrot for 2 minutes, then set aside.
Stir-fry chicken livers for 2 minutes, until browned on all sides.
Add chicken stock, soy sauce, wood ear fungus, and shredded chicken; bring to a boil. Add Pancit miki and cook 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add bihon and livers; stir-fry 5 minutes. Return vegetables, cook 2 minutes, season with fish sauce and pepper, and serve with lemon.

intro: This no-churn ice cream balances sweet creaminess with savory salted duck egg yolks.
ingredients: 10 cooked salted duck egg yolks, chilled
2 whole salted duck eggs, sliced, for garnish
steps: Whip the chilled cream to stiff peaks, stopping before it turns grainy; refrigerate.
Blend condensed milk and salted duck egg yolks until completely smooth.
Gently fold the yolk mixture into the whipped cream until evenly combined.
Transfer to a freezer-safe container and freeze until firm.
Scoop into bowls and garnish with sliced salted duck eggs.

intro: Chicken Halang Halang is a warming coconut stew with green papaya, ginger, and lively chilli heat.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add chicken and brown lightly on all sides.
Add stock, lemongrass, green chillies, and cayenne. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk and papaya; cook 10 minutes, until the papaya is tender.
Add chilli leaves and simmer 3 minutes. Season with salt or fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: Soft Pinoy Scrambled Eggs make a quick, savory breakfast with tomatoes and green onions.
ingredients: Sinangag and banana ketchup, for serving
steps: Beat eggs with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder until evenly combined.
Melt butter in a pan over medium heat; cook onion and tomatoes for 3–5 minutes, until tomato liquid evaporates.
Pour in eggs gradually, stirring continuously until softly firm.
Plate, scatter with green onions, and serve with sinangag and banana ketchup.

intro: Camto Soup pairs rich beef-bone broth with sweet-savory tender beef, cabbage, and eggs.
ingredients: 700 g beef flank steak or brisket, cut into small strips or cubes
8 cups water, plus more as needed
2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 4 tablespoons water
steps: Sauté half the garlic and onions in oil; brown the beef and bones on all sides.
Add water and a little salt; boil, then simmer gently for 1½ hours, replenishing water as needed. Remove beef; simmer bones 1 hour longer.
Fry remaining garlic until golden; reserve it. Add 1 cup bone broth, beef, soy sauce, sugar, spices, pepper, and slurry; simmer 30 minutes until very tender.
Add cabbage to the bone broth and cook 5 minutes. Fill bowls with broth, cabbage, sauced beef, eggs, spring onions, and fried garlic; serve with rice or noodles.

intro: Mini turon pairs crisp banana-and-jackfruit lumpia with a light brown-sugar caramel.
ingredients: 1/2 cup ripe jackfruit, sliced into strips
steps: Boil water with 1 cup brown sugar, stirring until dissolved; simmer over low heat until reduced by half, then cool slightly.
Place banana and jackfruit on each wrapper. Add 1–2 teaspoons filling sugar, fold in the sides, roll tightly, and seal with water.
Heat canola oil. Brush or dip each roll in syrup, then fry over low-medium heat for 3 minutes per side.
Fry until golden and crisp, drain, and serve with vanilla ice cream if desired.

intro: This chilled two-layer jelly pudding pairs a cocoa base with a creamy milk topping.
steps: In a small pot, dissolve 1 teaspoon jelly powder in 2 cups room-temperature water and bring it to a boil.
Reduce to low heat; stir in evaporated milk, sugar, and cocoa until smooth and fully dissolved.
Pour the chocolate mixture halfway into 12 molds and let it begin setting.
Dissolve remaining jelly powder in 1 cup water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat.
Stir in cream and condensed milk until blended; pour gently over the chocolate layer.
Cool until set, then chill thoroughly before serving.

intro: A creamy, vividly colored chilled dragon fruit drink.
ingredients: 2 large dragon fruits, peeled and diced
steps: Combine diced dragon fruit, water, evaporated milk, and sugar in a large container.
Stir until the sugar dissolves and the milk is evenly mixed.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours to deepen the color and flavor.
Stir again, fill glasses generously with ice cubes, and pour in the juice.

intro: Pianono is a light Filipino sponge roll coated with sugar and filled simply with margarine.
steps: Heat oven to 180°C. Beat egg whites until fluffy, gradually beat in sugar, and continue until thick and glossy.
Sift flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and baking soda. Beat yolks with vanilla, then mix in dry ingredients on low speed.
Fold yolk mixture gently into whites. Spread evenly in a wax-paper-lined jelly roll pan.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the cake springs back lightly when touched.
Scatter sugar over fresh wax paper. Immediately invert hot cake onto it and peel away the baking paper.
Spread with margarine, roll from the long side, slice, and cool before serving.

intro: Binondo Style Beef Tendon Curry is a fragrant coconut curry with exceptionally tender tendon and crisp-edged potatoes.
ingredients: 1 kg beef tendons, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 Chinese Soup Herb Bag or Herbal Soup Chinese Seasoning Set
6 cups water, plus more as needed
steps: Sauté garlic, ginger, and shallots in oil for 1 minute; add capsicum and cook 1 minute more.
Add water, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, tendon, herb bag, lemongrass, curry powder, and optional MSG. Boil, then simmer low 4–5 hours until very soft.
Maintain the liquid level with water. Fry potatoes at 180°C for 6 minutes, until cooked; drain.
Stir potatoes and coconut milk into tender tendon; simmer 2 minutes. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot with rice.

intro: Bocheng Monggo pairs chewy glutinous rice dough with a textured, sweet mung bean center.
steps: Soak mung beans overnight and drain. Cover with fresh water, boil, then simmer until tender, adding water as needed.
Stir in sugar, condensed milk, and flour. Blend coarsely, cook until thick enough to hold shape, then cool.
Knead glutinous rice flour with water into a workable dough; adjust with flour or water as needed and divide into 8 portions.
Flatten each portion, enclose 2 tablespoons filling, seal, and roll into balls.
Heat oil to 180°C, add brown sugar, and fry the balls one at a time until the sugar melts and coats them. Drain and cool.

intro: Ginataang Manok with Sitaw at Kalabasa is a creamy coconut chicken stew with tender squash and beans.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
340 g kalabasa, calabaza squash, or butternut squash, cubed
1 (40 g) packet Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until softened. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in 2 cups water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over medium heat for 40 minutes, adding water if necessary.
Stir in kalabasa and cook for 5 minutes. Dissolve Ginataang Gulay Mix in 3/4 cup lukewarm water and add it.
Add sitaw, cover, and cook 3–5 minutes until crisp-tender. Stir in patis and pepper; cook 1 minute and serve.

intro: Crisp fried chicken gets its deep savory flavor from a simple patis marinade.
ingredients: 2 lb whole chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Combine chicken, black pepper, and patis in a bowl; marinate for 1 hour.
Mix flour and cornstarch in a shallow container.
Heat oil in a deep pot over medium heat until ready for frying.
Coat each chicken piece thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Fry chicken about 12 minutes on the first side, then 8 to 10 minutes after turning, until golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly and serve hot.

intro: Fresh vegetable-and-shrimp Lumpiang Togue is best fried immediately for a crisp shell.
steps: Combine bean sprouts, cabbage, carrot, green beans, shrimp, sesame oil, oyster sauce, sugar, and salt.
Heat enough oil in a wok for deep-frying.
Place 3 tablespoons filling near one wrapper corner; roll, fold in both sides, and seal the final edge with water.
Fry each lumpia immediately until crisp and golden, then drain on paper towels.
Mix vinegar, red chilies, garlic, pepper, onion, sugar, and salt for the dip.
Serve the hot Lumpiang Togue with the vinegar dip.

intro: Beef Pares Mami combines sweet-savory braised beef with rich beef broth, noodles, and fresh toppings.
ingredients: 1 kg beef brisket, cut into strips or cubes
6 tablespoons brown sugar, adjusted to taste
3 kg beef leg bones, cut into sections
Sea salt and/or fish sauce, to taste
2 large bunches Shanghai bok choy, ends trimmed
steps: Sauté minced garlic and red onion in oil. Brown brisket, then add pares water, soy sauce, sugar, star anise, bay leaves, and ground pepper.
Boil, then simmer about 2 hours until the beef nearly falls apart. Reduce over higher heat until thick; season with fish sauce.
Cover beef bones with water, boil 15 minutes, then drain and rinse. Sauté whole garlic and quartered onions in a clean pot.
Add bones, peppercorns, and water to cover. Boil, then simmer about 3 1/2 hours; season broth with salt or fish sauce.
Blanch bok choy and cook noodles according to package directions. Divide them among bowls, add broth, pares, egg, and spring onions.
Serve with soy sauce and sriracha alongside.

intro: Gokong Halo is a deeply simmered pork and chicken soup scented with ginger and sibut herbs.
ingredients: 1 kg pork hock or leg, chopped into chunks
1 small sea cucumber, soaked and sliced, optional
8 cups water or light bone broth
steps: Boil pork and chicken for 5 minutes to remove impurities; drain and rinse well.
Place pork, onion, garlic, ginger, and water or broth in a clean large pot; bring to a boil.
Add daikon, sibut pack, and optional sea cucumber. Reduce to a gentle, uncovered simmer.
Simmer about 2 hours, skimming as needed, until broth is lightly reduced and golden brown.
Add chicken and simmer 30 minutes more, until pork is tender and chicken is cooked through.
Season with salt and white pepper, discard sibut, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: A rich, creamy Pininyahang Manok with pineapple, vegetables, and melted cheese.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into small pieces
2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch squares
1 can (500 g) pineapple chunks in syrup
steps: Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Sauté garlic until golden, then cook onion until translucent.
Add chicken and sauté for 1 minute. Stir in patis, pepper, and pickles; cover and simmer until the chicken releases juices.
When chicken is half-cooked, add pineapple chunks with their syrup and continue simmering.
Add carrots and potatoes once chicken is cooked; simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in bell pepper and bring to a boil. Add evaporated milk and cheese, stirring until melted, then serve with rice.

intro: Abistsuelas Guisado is a quick pork and green bean sauté brightened with tomato and shrimp stock.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Lower to medium heat, add tomato, and cook until softened.
Add pork and cook for 10 minutes, breaking it up until cooked through.
Add green beans and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in shrimp stock, bring to a high boil, and season with fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: Solita turns lollipop-cut pork chops into a crisp, savory fried centerpiece.
