steps: Cut each chop halfway from the bone and push the meat to one end, forming a lollipop shape.
Mix pepper, bay leaves, garlic, lemon juice, soy sauce, and salt. Massage over pork and marinate for 30 minutes.
Place pork and marinade in a covered pan with stock. Steam over medium heat, reduce to low, and cook 25 minutes until fully cooked.
Uncover and cook over high heat until remaining liquid is absorbed; cool the pork. Whisk flour, water, and egg into a lump-free batter.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C. Coat pork in batter, fry about 5 minutes until crisp, and drain well.

intro: Sinaing na Tulingan slowly braises salted bullet tuna in sour kamias, vinegar, pork fat, and banana leaves.
ingredients: Banana leaves, for lining and wrapping
steps: Clean the fish, removing gills and innards; optionally twist off tails. Soak in water for 20 minutes to remove blood, then drain.
Rub fish with 1/2 cup rock salt and wrap each with banana-leaf strips.
Line a clay pot or large wok with banana leaves. Make a base of pork fat and 1/2 cup dried kamias, then arrange fish on top.
Add remaining kamias and 1 tablespoon salt. Pour in vinegar and enough water to cover; top with banana leaves and cover.
Bring to a boil, reduce to the lowest heat, and simmer 4 hours. Add 1/2 cup water if drying; uncover for the final 30 minutes to reduce.

intro: Carneng Asada is grilled marinated beef served with a light citrus sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg beef nape, sirloin, or top round, thick-cut
1/3 cup dayap juice or lemon juice
steps: Combine olive oil, dayap juice, and parsley. Coat beef, then marinate at least 6 hours or overnight, turning occasionally.
Heat charcoal or a grill until hot. Grill beef to medium-rare or medium, brushing with reserved marinade to keep it moist.
Rest the grilled beef before slicing it against the grain.
Simmer reserved marinade with water or stock. Gradually whisk in rice flour until a smooth, thick sauce forms.
Finish beef with fine salt and serve with sauce and optional fried potatoes.

intro: Sweet Pepper Relyeno features tender peppers stuffed with seasoned pork, crumbed, fried, and baked through.
ingredients: 10 sweet peppers, halved lengthwise and seeded
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix pork, 1 egg, plain breadcrumbs, onion, carrot, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until combined.
Press about 1½ tablespoons filling onto each pepper half.
Heat oil over medium heat. Beat remaining eggs; dip filled peppers in egg, then coat the filling completely with Panko.
Fry filling-side down until crumbs are light to medium brown; turn and cook 2 minutes. Bake on a foil-lined tray at 350°F for 25 minutes.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve with ketchup.

intro: Bicho-bicho/Shakoy are chewy twisted donuts with a crisp sugar-coated exterior.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons melted butter, margarine, or oil
2 to 3 cups corn or canola oil, for frying
steps: Mix flour, sugar, and salt. Add milk, egg, melted butter, and yeast; stir into a sticky dough.
Knead on a floured surface for 7 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and let double, 30 to 60 minutes.
Deflate dough; divide into 16 pieces. Roll each into a 12-inch rope, twist, and pinch the ends together.
Cover twists and let rise until nearly doubled; turn them over and rest 5 to 10 minutes until puffy.
Fry in medium-hot oil in batches for 3 to 5 minutes, turning until evenly golden brown.
Coat warm Shakoy in sugar, mixed with cinnamon if desired, and serve warm.

intro: Inihaw na Panga ng Tuna is smoky grilled tuna jaw with a sweet, spicy soy glaze.
steps: Combine marinade soy sauce, lime or calamansi juice, pepper, chillies, garlic, and brown sugar; stir until sugar dissolves.
Place tuna jaw in a sealed bag with the marinade. Refrigerate overnight, about 3 hours according to the total preparation time.
Mix basting soy sauce and white sugar. Heat a grill and arrange the tuna jaw on the grate.
Baste and grill the first side 3–5 minutes. Turn, baste the top and sides, and grill 5 minutes.
Turn again and grill 5–7 minutes; flip back and grill 5 minutes more, until opaque and cooked through. Serve with soy-citrus-chilli dip.

intro: Kimchinigang gives pork sinigang a spicy, fermented kimchi depth with tender tofu and mustard leaves.
ingredients: 1 packet sinigang tamarind mix or 400 g tamarind
steps: Cover pork and onion with water in a pot. If using whole tamarind, tie it in muslin and add it; boil, then simmer 45 minutes.
Add gochujang and kimchi with its juices. Return to a boil and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in sinigang mix. For whole tamarind, press its muslin bundle through a colander into the pot, then discard solids.
Add tofu and mustard leaves; cook 5 minutes until leaves soften.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Sizzling Pusit combines tender squid and crisp vegetables with a tangy ketchup-based sauce.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt 2 tablespoons margarine over medium-high heat; stir in flour for 1 minute, then blend in the Shrimp Cube.
Add liquid seasoning, ketchup, wine, and water. Bring to a boil, season with garlic and onion powders, and set aside.
Heat oil over medium heat; sauté ginger and onion until onion layers separate.
Add carrot and celery for 1 minute. Add bell pepper and squid; cook 2 minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons margarine on a hot metal plate, add squid and vegetables, and pour sauce over.
Serve immediately while the platter is sizzling.

intro: Ginisang Sayote at Sardinas is a fast, comforting sauté of chayote and sardines in tomato sauce.
ingredients: 10 oz canned sardines in tomato sauce
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic until lightly browned.
Add onions and tomato; sauté 1 minute. Add chayote and cook 2 minutes.
Gently stir in sardines and their tomato sauce; cook 30 seconds.
Add water, bring to a boil, then simmer low until sauce reduces by half. Stir in Maggi Magic Sarap and serve with rice.

intro: Tender beef strips and crisp-bitter ampalaya come together in a glossy savory sauce.
ingredients: 1 large or 2 small bitter gourds, cored and thinly sliced
1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons Chinese cooking wine
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix cornstarch, 2 tablespoons Chinese cooking wine, salt, and baking soda; coat beef and set aside.
Heat peanut oil with a little sesame oil in a wok over high heat. Sauté garlic and shallot.
Stir-fry beef in batches for 3 minutes; remove.
Add bitter gourd and 1/4 cup water. Cover and cook 2 minutes, until water evaporates.
Return beef to the wok. Mix remaining water, tapioca starch, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and remaining wine; add and bring to a boil.
Turn off heat when sauce thickens; season with black pepper and serve.

intro: Sinigang na Tilapia sa Miso is a sour, savory fish soup with mellow yellow miso.
ingredients: 1 large tilapia, about 1 lb or more, scaled and gutted
steps: Season tilapia with salt and rest 10 minutes. Heat oil and pan-fry the fish over medium heat for 5 minutes per side; set aside.
Transfer 2 tablespoons frying oil to a pot. Sauté onion and tomatoes, then add miso, fish sauce, and water; bring to a boil.
Stir in sinigang mix. Return fried tilapia and cook 3 minutes, then add okra and cook 2 minutes.
Turn off heat, add pepper and mustard leaves, cover 5 minutes, and serve.

intro: Ginataang Bitsuelas pairs pork and green beans in a fragrant bagoong alamang coconut sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add Thai chilies, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 15 minutes.
Stir in bagoong alamang and cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add long green beans and cook 3 minutes, then add spinach and cook 1 minute.
Season with black pepper and serve.

intro: Rotisserie Chicken Arroz Caldo turns leftover lechon manok into comforting, ginger-scented rice porridge.
ingredients: 1/2 rotisserie chicken or lechon manok, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion until soft.
Add ginger, garlic powder, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and rice, stirring for 2 minutes. Pour in broth and water, then bring to a boil.
Reduce to low-medium heat, cover, and cook 35 to 44 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes; add water if it becomes too thick.
Stir in saffron or kasubha and season with salt and pepper. Serve with scallions and a lemon slice.

intro: Beef Short Rib Sinigang Na May Pakwan balances tangy broth, rich beef, and mellow watermelon.
ingredients: 50 g Knorr Sinigang na may Gabi Recipe Mix
1 bunch kangkong, cut into serving pieces
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pressure cooker; add tomato and onion and boil 5 minutes.
Add short ribs, cover, and pressure-cook 30 minutes.
Uncover; add watermelon and boil 10–12 minutes. Stir in Knorr Sinigang na may Gabi Recipe Mix and cook 3 minutes.
Add sitaw and cook 5 minutes; season with pepper and fish sauce. Add kangkong, cover, and rest 5–8 minutes before serving.

intro: Kalamay Kapit is a chewy coconut rice cake roll filled with ube halaya and sweet jackfruit.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh jackfruit, washed and sliced
steps: Simmer jackfruit, water, and white sugar over low heat for 30 minutes, until tender and syrupy; cool.
Mix glutinous rice flour and sugar, then whisk in coconut milk until the batter is smooth.
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch square pan, level the surface, and steam over medium heat for 30 minutes.
Turn warm cake onto a large tray, remove parchment, and use an oiled rolling pin to flatten it into a rectangle.
Spread ube halaya down the center, add sweetened jackfruit, and gently roll into a log.
Cool completely, slice, then top with jackfruit, syrup, and latik.

intro: Smoky grilled eggplant is brightened with kamatis and a sharp bagoong dressing.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Grill eggplants until their skins are charred and the flesh is soft.
Cool slightly, then peel away the charred skins while keeping each eggplant intact.
Mix bagoong, cane vinegar, brown sugar, and bird's eye chili in a small bowl.
Arrange eggplants on a plate, cover with tomatoes and onion, then drizzle with dressing.
Season with black pepper, garnish with spring onions, and serve.

intro: This simple Lugaw is a warming ginger rice porridge with classic toppings.
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice twice and drain thoroughly.
Heat oil over medium heat in a pot. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until limp and aromatic.
Add rice, water, fish sauce, white pepper, and optional kasubha. Bring to a boil, stirring regularly.
Reduce heat and cook until rice is expanded and fully tender, adding water as needed for your preferred consistency.
Ladle into bowls and top with hard-boiled egg, green onion, toasted garlic, and ground pepper.

intro: Danggit Fried Rice turns leftover rice into a quick, savory breakfast with crisp dried fish.
ingredients: 3 cups cooked white rice, preferably chilled leftover rice
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry garlic for 10–15 seconds until fragrant.
Add chopped danggit and stir-fry until the garlic is light brown and the fish is cooked.
Add rice and stir-fry 5–8 minutes, breaking up clumps and mixing until evenly heated.
Plate the rice, top with green onion, and serve hot.

intro: Batangas Lomi is a thick, hearty noodle soup packed with pork, offal, kikiam, and crunchy toppings.
ingredients: 500 g lomi or other thick egg noodles
3 tablespoons sweet potato starch mixed with a little water
steps: Cook noodles according to the packet; drain, rinse, and set aside.
Fry pork belly in a little oil until golden; remove. Brown pork heart, add kikiam for 2 minutes, then sauté garlic and shallots 1 minute.
Add liver and cook until light brown. Add stock, boil, then simmer low 10 minutes; return pork belly and simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in starch slurry and simmer 2 minutes. Add noodles, bring to a boil, then remove from heat and stir in beaten eggs.
Season with pepper and fish sauce. Serve topped with chicharon, hard-boiled eggs, and spring onions.

intro: Minatamis na Saging is a warmly caramelized saba dessert with optional sago and milk.
ingredients: 6 medium ripe cardaba or saba bananas, sliced
1 cup cooked black sago pearls, optional
steps: Cook black sago pearls according to the package directions, if using.
Melt 1 tablespoon brown sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until lightly caramelized.
Carefully add water. Bring to a boil, then add remaining sugar, salt, and vanilla; simmer 10 minutes until dissolved.
Add bananas and cook 10 to 15 minutes until tender but still holding their shape.
Stir in sago, if using. Spoon into dessert bowls and finish with evaporated milk, if desired.

intro: Ginataang Monggo with Pork is a rich coconut mung bean stew finished with leafy greens.
ingredients: 7 oz mung beans, soaked overnight in 4 cups water
steps: Heat a pot and sear pork until it renders oil. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add soaked mung beans and sauté for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 4 cups water, coconut milk, and Pork Cube. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 30 to 35 minutes.
Add more water if needed to prevent drying. Add spinach, ampalaya leaves, and optional chillies; cover and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Halo-Halo is a customizable chilled Filipino dessert layered with sweet preserves, frozen milk, ube, and leche flan.
steps: Divide Minatamis na Saging, jackfruit, sweetened beans, coconut, corn, nata de coco, kaong, and pinipig between tall glasses, filling only one-third.
Shred frozen milk by gently pounding its carton inside a towel, or carve the frozen block with a knife for finer shavings.
Pile frozen milk into each glass, nearly to the rim; add sugar only if desired.
Top each serving with leche flan and cooked sweet purple yam; serve immediately.

intro: Guinobatan Longanisa is a sweet, garlicky pork sausage with a caramelized glaze.
steps: Mix soy sauce and annatto powder in a large bowl. Add pork, fat, brown sugar, salt, garlic, and pepper; mix thoroughly by hand.
Load the mixture into a sausage stuffer. Knot the casing onto the nozzle and fill gently, twisting every 2 1/2 inches.
Refrigerate sausages for 1 day to cure, then freeze any portions not being cooked.
Place sausages in a covered pan with a little water and cook over low heat until water evaporates.
Add a little oil and cook slowly until browned and the sugar caramelizes into a glaze. Serve hot.

intro: Chicharon Bituka is boiled, seasoned intestine fried until deeply crisp for a classic bar snack.
ingredients: 2 lb thoroughly cleaned pig or cow intestine
Vinegar and chilli pepper dip, for serving
steps: Bring water to a boil. Add 2 tablespoons salt and vinegar, boil 2 minutes, then add the cleaned intestine.
When the liquid returns to a boil, add bay leaves and peppercorns. Simmer 40 minutes, until the intestine is tender.
Drain well, cut into preferred lengths, and coat evenly with the remaining 1 tablespoon salt.
Heat oil for deep-frying. Fry intestine until crunchy, drain, and serve with vinegar and chilli dip.

intro: Pork Adobo Flakes crisps shredded adobo into a quick, savory topping for garlic fried rice.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb prepared Pork Adobo, sauce removed
1 tbsp soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce
steps: Shred the prepared Pork Adobo into fine threads, removing any remaining sauce.
Heat oil over medium heat. Cook garlic until light brown, then remove it before it darkens.
Add shredded adobo to the garlic oil and toss for 1 minute.
Add soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce and black pepper; stir-fry for 3 minutes until lightly crisp.
Transfer to a bowl, top with fried garlic, and serve with garlic fried rice.

intro: Adobong Pusit sa Gata balances tender squid with a reduced coconut adobo sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and fry garlic until light brown.
Add squid and cook 2 minutes, then transfer it to a plate.
Pour in coconut milk and bring it to a boil. Add soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, and pepper.
Cover and cook until the liquid reduces by half.
Return squid, add 1 teaspoon fish sauce, and cook covered for 3 to 5 minutes. Adjust with more fish sauce if needed.

intro: Pan-cooked Hopia Ube Dice have flaky pastry wrapped around a soft ube jam center.
steps: Pulse flour, sugar, butter, and salt in a food processor until pea-sized. Pulse in egg just until clumpy.
On a floured surface, press dough together, adding ice water 2 tablespoons at a time. Rest 5 minutes.
Roll and fold dough three times, then shape into a long log.
Flatten small dough portions, fill each with 1 tablespoon ube jam, then seal into compact parcels.
Cook in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat, gently pressing into dice shapes, for 2 minutes per side until light brown.
Add butter and cook each side 1 minute more, basting with melted butter.

intro: Pinaso is a creamy cracker custard finished with a crackly caramelized sugar top.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon grated lemon or dayap rind
steps: Combine evaporated milk, eggs, saltine crackers, 1/2 cup sugar, grated rind, and vanilla in a pot.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously, until the mixture thickens.
Transfer the thick custard to a serving dish and smooth the surface.
Sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 cup sugar.
Caramelize the sugar with a culinary torch, or press it with a very hot heavy iron turner until deeply browned.

intro: Bistek Bangus brings pan-fried milkfish together with a bright lemon-soy onion sauce.
ingredients: 2 large white onions, sliced into rings
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season milkfish with salt and black pepper. Heat oil in a pan and fry fish until cooked through; set aside.
Using the same pan, sauté onion rings briefly until just softened, keeping them intact.
Whisk cornstarch, water, and soy sauce until smooth. Add to the pan and boil; add water if the sauce is too salty.
Stir in lemon or calamansi juice, season with salt and pepper, then turn off heat. Spoon sauce and onions over milkfish.

intro: Crab with Misua and Patola is a light, aromatic seafood soup finished with silky noodles.
ingredients: 1 medium patola, peeled and sliced crosswise
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Sauté garlic and ginger, then cook onion until soft.
Add crabs, fish sauce, and water. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
Season with pepper, add patola, return to a boil, and cook 1 minute.
Stir in misua and cook 1 minute. Add green onions and cook 1–2 minutes more before serving.

intro: Riyandang is a fragrant beef braise layered with toasted coconut, roasted rice, turmeric, galangal, and coconut milk.
ingredients: 1 kg stewing beef or beef brisket, cubed
2 lemongrass stalks, white sections only, thinly sliced
4 spring onions, white sections only, thinly sliced
steps: Pound roasted rice coarsely. Pound turmeric, galangal, lemongrass, capsicum, ginger, spring onion, garlic, and chillies into a rough palapa paste.
Mix beef with pounded rice and spice paste; rest 30 minutes.
Toast grated coconut in a dry pan over medium-high heat until golden, then set aside.
Heat a little oil in a wok over medium heat. Add marinated beef and spices, cover, and let it cook in its juices for 15 minutes.
Add bay leaves, coconut milk, soy sauce, toasted coconut, and lime zest. Simmer on low 1 1/2 to 2 hours until tender, adding water if needed.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Raise heat for the last 5 minutes to reduce sauce and release coconut oil; season with salt.

intro: Lechon Pata is a tender pork leg roasted until deeply browned with crackling skin.
ingredients: Water, enough to cover the leg
steps: Place pork leg in a large pot, cover with water, and add bay leaves, peppercorns, lemongrass, onion, garlic, and salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 60 to 90 minutes until the leg is tender.
Remove pork, cool, and air-dry for 30 to 45 minutes. Heat oven to 475°F.
Place leg on a greased baking tray and roast for 45 minutes.
Brush all over with milk and roast 60 to 90 minutes more, until browned and crisp; broil 10 to 15 minutes for extra crackling.
Rest briefly, transfer to a platter, and serve with lechon sauce.

intro: Crisp red snapper becomes a bright centerpiece beneath a sweet-tart mango sauce.
ingredients: 1 large whole red snapper, cleaned, gutted, and scored
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season snapper inside and out with salt and black pepper.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a wok; fry fish until golden outside and cooked through, then drain.
Carefully drain wok, leaving 2 tablespoons oil. Sauté garlic and shallot until fragrant.
Whisk mango jam, lemon juice, sugar, cornstarch, and water; pour into wok and bring to a boil.
Add mango and simmer 1 minute. Pour sauce over fish, garnish with spring onions, and serve.

intro: Fried Tilapia in Coconut Milk, or Ginataang Tilapia, turns crisp fish into a gentle, gingery coconut stew.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add banana pepper and fried tilapia; cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add optional chili peppers and fish sauce, turn fish carefully, cover, and cook 10 minutes.
Add malunggay and cook 5–8 minutes; serve hot.

intro: Slow-braised pork soft bones become tender in an aromatic soybean paste and spice sauce.
ingredients: 2 spring onion stalks, tied in a knot
1 spring onion stalk, chopped, for garnish
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pork soft bones with salt.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking; stir-fry pork until browned around the edges.
Add garlic, ginger, dried chilies, and soybean paste; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add water, soy sauce, star anise, bay leaves, cinnamon, and knotted spring onions. Boil, cover, then simmer 1 hour until tender.
Raise heat during the final 10 minutes to reduce the braising liquid into a glossy sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with chopped spring onion, and serve.

intro: Kangkong with Bagoong pairs crisp blanched greens with a punchy sweet-salty shrimp bagoong topping.
steps: Heat pork lard in a wok and fry garlic and shallot until golden; reserve some fried garlic for topping.
Add raw shrimp bagoong, vinegar, cayenne, and sugar. Stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes until dark red.
Season the sautéed bagoong with black pepper.
Blanch kangkong leaves and stalks briefly in boiling water, then drain thoroughly.
Arrange kangkong on a plate and spoon over sautéed bagoong and fried garlic.

intro: Black Kutsinta is a chewy steamed rice cake with dulce de leche and toasted coconut.
steps: Grease 24 puto or kutsinta molds. Whisk tapioca starch, flour, brown sugar, molasses, lye water, and water smooth.
Fill molds and steam over medium heat for 15 minutes, covering the steamer lid with a clean cloth. Cool completely.
For dulce de leche, keep the condensed-milk can unopened, cover with water, boil, then simmer 1 hour. Cool before opening.
Toast coconut in a dry nonstick pan over medium-low heat, stirring often, until golden. Unmold kutsinta and top with dulce de leche and coconut.

intro: Aloha Pork Chop pairs tender pork with a tangy pineapple and capsicum sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder chops or pork chops
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 can (227 g) pineapple chunks, juice retained
steps: Season pork chops with salt and black pepper. Fry in oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes per side, then remove.
Reduce heat to medium and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion in the same pan, adding oil if needed.
Mix pineapple juice, banana ketchup, brown sugar, fish sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, cornstarch, and reserved pineapple juice.
Pour sauce into the pan. Return pork with pineapple chunks and both capsicums; bring to a boil.
Cover, simmer on low for 15 minutes, adjust salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Garlic Butter Bangus features crisp milkfish belly glazed in a buttery calamansi sauce.
ingredients: 2 tbsp banana ketchup or tomato sauce
1 tbsp calamansi juice or lemon juice
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pat bangus dry and season with salt and pepper. Fry skin-side down in a little oil over medium heat for 4 minutes per side.
Remove fish when golden and crisp. Add 1 tablespoon oil and butter to the same pan.
Sauté minced garlic until lightly golden, then add shallots and cook until translucent.
Stir in oyster sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, calamansi juice, and optional sugar; simmer 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return bangus, spoon sauce over it, and simmer 2 to 3 minutes. Garnish with chillies and crispy garlic; serve with rice.

intro: Sarciadong Isda, Ampalaya at Tausi combines crisp fried mackerel, bitter melon, black beans, and silky egg sauce.
steps: Halve ampalaya, scrape out seeds, salt generously, and set aside. Season mackerel with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil over high heat and fry mackerel until golden on all sides; remove. Rinse, thinly slice, rinse again, and drain ampalaya.
Leave 2 to 3 tablespoons oil in the pan. Sauté garlic and onion, then cook tomato over low heat until soft.
Stir-fry ampalaya for 1 minute. Add water, boil uncovered, and add tausi, mashing some beans.
Return fish and boil on high 3 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper, then gently add beaten eggs and fold once partly set.
Top with spring onions and serve with hot rice.

intro: Binungor is a deeply savory freshwater-snail stew loaded with squash, jackfruit, mushrooms, and chilies.
ingredients: 250 g butternut squash, peeled and bite-size pieces
½ cup rehydrated wood ear fungus
steps: Rinse agurong until clear, soak in salted water 30 minutes, rinse, blanch 2 minutes, and drain; remove shells if preferred.
Sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger in oil over medium heat for about 2 minutes. Stir in bagoong for 1 minute.
Add water, squash, jackfruit, bamboo shoots, and patani; simmer gently 8 minutes.
Add agurong and oyster mushrooms; simmer 6 minutes until snails are cooked and vegetables tender.
Add wood ear fungus and siling labuyo; simmer 2–3 minutes. Adjust bagoong, rest 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

intro: Adobong Sitaw at Kangkong with Chicharon is a quick vegetable adobo enriched by savory pork cracklings.
ingredients: 1 bunch kangkong, leaves separated and stalks cut small
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens and garlic is lightly browned.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, and water; bring to a boil. Add chicharon, cover, and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add sitaw and cook 5 minutes. Add kangkong stalks and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in kangkong leaves and cook 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: This tangy Sinigang na Lapu lapu sa Miso combines delicate grouper with tamarind and miso broth.
ingredients: 2 lb grouper (lapu lapu), cleaned and sliced
steps: Boil tamarind in water, covered, over medium heat for 40 minutes. Cool slightly, then strain into a clean pot.
Bring the tamarind broth to a boil. Add tomatoes, onion, and miso; cover and cook 15 minutes.
Add grouper, daikon if using, okra, and long green peppers. Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce.
Add mustard leaves, cover, and cook 3 to 5 minutes until wilted. Serve immediately.

intro: Inday Inday is a coconut-rich dessert of soft glutinous rice cakes and young coconut.
steps: Combine coconut milk and brown sugar in a pan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes, stirring often.
Add young coconut strips and cook until the sauce reaches your preferred thickness; set aside.
Mix glutinous rice flour and water, then shape into balls and flatten slightly.
Bring water to a boil in a deep pan; lower heat and poach rice cakes in batches.
When cakes float, turn and cook 1 minute more. Drain and arrange on a platter.
Pour the coconut-and-brown-sugar sauce over the cakes and serve.

intro: Batsui is a hearty pork-and-offal misua soup with ginger and a clean, peppery finish.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok and brown pork belly, spleen, pancreas, and kidneys. Remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in the same wok until fragrant. Add water and pork stock, then bring to a boil.
Return the browned meat and offal, then simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Add misua and cook 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper; garnish with spring onions and serve with bird's-eye chillies.

intro: Sizzling Bulalo serves tender beef shank under a buttery mushroom gravy.
ingredients: 10 oz condensed cream of mushroom soup
steps: Melt 1 tablespoon butter, sauté mushrooms for 3 minutes, then add soup, 3/4 cup water, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Simmer 5 minutes.
Place beef shank in a pot with 1 teaspoon salt and 3 cups water. Boil, then simmer until tender, adding water if needed.
Season both sides of tender beef with remaining salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a pan and fry beef for at least 2 minutes per side.
Heat a sizzling plate with remaining butter. Add beef, spoon over gravy, arrange corn alongside, and serve immediately.

intro: Hinalog na Manok is a tart, tomato-rich chicken stew softened by green papaya and chilli leaves.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and brown chicken pieces; transfer them to a plate.
Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion over low heat for 2 minutes. Add tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Return chicken, add sriracha, and pour in enough water to cover. Boil, then simmer 20 minutes.
Add papaya and sinigang mix; simmer 15 minutes until papaya is tender.
Add chilli leaves and simmer 2 minutes. Season with fish sauce and white pepper.

intro: Bam-i combines Chinese egg noodles and sotanghon with pork, chicken, prawns, and a savory shrimp-enriched broth.
ingredients: 15 medium prawns, heads and shells reserved
1 cup rehydrated wood ear fungus, sliced
steps: Soak sotanghon in water for no more than 10 minutes. Pound prawn heads and shells with ½ cup stock, strain, and reserve the liquid.
Brown pork belly in oil over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until soft; add cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes, then remove pork and vegetables.
Boil remaining stock with prawn liquid, soy sauce, wood ear fungus, and chicken. Add sotanghon and cook 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add egg noodles and prawns; cook 5 minutes, adding water if needed. Return pork, cabbage, and spring onions; stir-fry 1 minute.
Season with fish sauce and white pepper, then serve.

intro: Luñis preserves fatty pork belly by slowly frying it in its own rendered fat.
steps: Toss cubed fatty pork belly evenly with rock salt.
Place pork fat-side down in a large wok over medium heat and cook until it begins rendering fat.
Continue frying in the rendered fat, stirring frequently, until pork is cooked, golden brown, and crisp.
Transfer pork and rendered oil to a heatproof bowl and cool completely.
Pack into clean jars and use as needed.

intro: Filipino Spanish Bread is a soft, breadcrumb-coated roll with a buttery sweet crumb filling.
ingredients: 1/8 cup water or milk, plus more if needed
steps: Mix flour, sugar, salt, lukewarm milk, melted butter, egg, and yeast into a slightly sticky dough. Knead on an oiled surface 10 to 12 minutes.
Place dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 30 to 60 minutes.
For filling, cook butter, 1/4 cup crumbs, flour, water or milk, sugar, salt, and remaining filling crumbs over medium-low heat until paste-like.
Divide dough into 16. Roll each into a long triangle, brush with butter, spread filling with a 1 cm border, and roll from wide end.
Brush rolls with milk or water, coat in crumbs, place seam-side down on lined trays, and rise covered 20 to 30 minutes.
Bake at 150°C on the middle rack for 20 minutes, until set and lightly golden. Serve warm.

intro: Dinengdeng is a light vegetable soup enriched with bagoong monamon and fried fish.
ingredients: 1 pack spinach leaves or other leafy vegetables
2 tablespoons bagoong monamon or ground anchovies in oil
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and red onion until aromatic.
Dilute bagoong in rice wash, strain it into the pot, pressing to extract liquid, then bring to a boil.
Add bamboo shoots and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add okra and string beans; cook for 3 minutes. Add spinach and saluyot, season, and simmer 2 minutes.
Transfer vegetables and broth to bowls, top with fried fish, and serve.

intro: Puto Flan layers a tender steamed puto batter over a set condensed-milk custard.
steps: Whisk egg yolks, condensed milk, and lemon juice into a smooth custard. Bring a steamer to a boil.
Lightly grease puto molds and fill each one-third full with custard. Cover the steamer lid with muslin and steam 20 minutes.
Sift flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. Beat egg whites to foamy peaks, then gently fold in dry ingredients while gradually adding water.
Fill molds to the brim with puto batter over the cooked custard. Steam 15 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Cool slightly, then tap molds gently to release the Puto Flan.

intro: Crispy Pata Dinakdakan combines crackling pork and liver in a creamy, spicy dressing.
steps: Boil pata with peppercorns, bay leaves, 6 cups water, and 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, covered over low-medium heat for 80 minutes. Drain, cool, and debone.
Rub pata skin with 2 teaspoons salt. Mix mayonnaise, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, vinegar, and black pepper into a smooth dressing.
Rub liver with 1 teaspoon salt. Fry in hot oil until browned on both sides, then slice.
Deep-fry pata until golden and crisp; cool slightly, then chop into bite-size pieces.
Toss pata, liver, dressing, onions, green onions, and chilies until coated. Transfer to a serving plate.

intro: Arroz Valenciana is a colorful coconut sticky-rice dish with chicken, vegetables, and festive garnishes.
ingredients: 5–6 chicken wings, separated into wingettes and drumettes
2 cups glutinous or sticky rice, washed
1 cup bell pepper, cut into strips
steps: Over medium heat, sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft. Add chicken and cook about 3 minutes until nearly cooked; add fish sauce if using.
Stir in rice and turmeric for 1 minute. Add carrots, bell pepper, bay leaves, salt, pepper, peas, and raisins.
Pour in coconut milk and 1 cup water. Cover and cook 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding water if rice remains firm.
Cook until rice is tender and all liquid is absorbed. Remove bay leaves, then mold in a llanera or serve directly.
For a festive mold, place egg, shrimp, bell pepper, raisins, and peas in the llanera before adding the rice.

intro: Garlic Bihon uses golden fried garlic and annatto chicken stock for deeply savory noodles.
steps: Boil chicken in water for 35 minutes. Remove, cool, shred, and reserve the stock.
Add annatto seeds to the stock, cover, and boil 5 minutes; set aside.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Fry garlic until golden, then reserve half for topping.
Sauté onion and celery in remaining garlic. Add shredded chicken and cook 1 minute.
Strain in annatto stock, bring to a boil, and dissolve in the chicken cube. Add carrot and half the green onion; cook 2 minutes.
Add bihon, cover 2 to 3 minutes, then toss until stock is absorbed. Season, cover over low heat 1 1/2 minutes, and top with reserved garlic and green onion.

intro: Palitaw sa Latik are tender rice cakes served in coconut-brown sugar syrup with toasted coconut curds.
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour and water by hand into a smooth dough. Form small balls and flatten into ¼-inch-thick oval discs.
Boil 400 ml coconut milk with 200 ml coconut cream, then simmer medium, stirring, until oil separates and curds turn brown; reserve latik.
Boil remaining coconut milk with brown sugar and salt. Cook palitaw in batches until each piece floats; remove.
Add remaining coconut cream to the syrup and simmer 10 minutes. Plate palitaw, spoon over syrup, and finish with latik.

intro: Dinakdakan is a smoky Ilocano pork salad folded with mayonnaise, vinegar, aromatics, and chillies.
ingredients: 500 g pork ears, preferably thick ends
4 cloves garlic, crushed with skin on
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cover pork cheeks and ears with water in a large pot; add garlic, bay leaves, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer about 45 minutes until tender. Drain well.
Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat and grill pork until lightly charred and crisp at the edges.
Chop pork into bite-sized pieces and place in a mixing bowl.
Add ginger, red onions, bird's eye chillies, mayonnaise, cane vinegar, salt, and pepper; toss until evenly coated.
Transfer to a platter, garnish with sliced green chillies, and serve.

intro: Buchi are sesame-coated glutinous rice balls with a sweet red bean paste center.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups or more red bean paste
steps: Dissolve sugar in boiling water, then cool for 15 minutes.
Mix in glutinous rice flour and knead gently until a workable dough forms. Divide into 20 to 24 balls.
Flatten each ball, add 1 tablespoon red bean paste, seal into a ball, and roll in sesame seeds.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or wok over medium heat.
Deep-fry Buchi until golden brown and puffed.
Drain with a slotted spoon on paper towels; cool slightly before serving.

intro: Chicken Mami uses a deeply simmered chicken broth with tender noodles and classic toppings.
ingredients: 3 kg chicken bones, including thighs and legs
Freshly ground black pepper, for serving
steps: Split chicken bones to expose marrow. Simmer bones, thighs, carrot, peppercorns, celery, onions, ginger, toasted onions, and toasted garlic in 2 to 3 litres water for 45 minutes.
Remove thighs, flake the meat, and return their bones. Simmer remaining bones 2 hours, until very soft.
Strain broth, chill, remove hardened surface fat, then reboil with up to 2 tablespoons fat. Reduce for richness and season with salt.
Boil fresh egg noodles for 30 seconds, drain and rinse, then pour boiling water over them in the colander.
Divide noodles among bowls with chicken, spring onions, egg, and toasted garlic. Add hot broth; finish with pepper, lemon juice, and fish sauce.

intro: Maskara is a novelty bar dish of boiled whole pig head deep-fried until crisp.
steps: Place the cleaned whole pig head in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer until the head is fully cooked and tender, then drain thoroughly and allow excess moisture to evaporate.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying. Carefully fry the pig head in batches if needed until the skin and exterior are crisp.
Drain well, chop or serve in portions, and serve hot as bar chow, optionally with beer.

intro: A creamy Avocado Shake is a quick chilled treat with condensed milk and fresh milk.
steps: Halve the avocados, remove pits, and scoop the flesh into a blender.
Add ice cubes, condensed milk, and full-cream milk.
Blend until completely smooth and creamy.
Pour into glasses and serve immediately.

intro: Pork Mechado is a tomato-braised pork stew with potatoes, peas, and sweet bell peppers.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix pork with soy sauce and lime or calamansi juice; marinate 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until onion softens. Add pork with marinade and cook until lightly browned.
Add tomato sauce and water, bring to a boil, then stir in Pork Cube.
Cover and cook over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes.
Add potato and peas; cook 10 minutes. Add both bell peppers and cook 5 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.

intro: Ginataang Monggo is a creamy coconut and malagkit dessert with nutty toasted mung beans.
steps: Toast mung beans in a dry pan until browned; cool, then crack them coarsely with an almires or mortar and pestle.
Bring coconut milk to a boil in a pot.
Add malagkit and crushed mung beans. Cook over low heat 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until coconut milk is nearly absorbed.
Stir in sugar, remove from heat, and serve warm or chilled.

intro: Chicken Pastel in a Cup serves a creamy chicken-and-vegetable filling in crisp toasted bread cups.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Flatten bread slices, press into a cupcake pan, and bake 5–6 minutes; cool.
Melt butter in a pan. Sauté mushrooms, chicken, and hotdogs for 5 minutes.
Add potato, carrot, and half the broth. Boil, cover, and cook over medium heat 5–7 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in flour gradually until smooth. Add eggs and remaining broth; cook until thickened, then season with salt and pepper.
Fill bread cups with chicken pastel, top with cheddar, and serve.

intro: Tokwat Baka pairs grilled beef and fried tofu with a warm, sharp soy-vinegar dressing.
ingredients: 4 pieces extra-firm tofu, fried and cubed
steps: Arrange sliced grilled porterhouse steak and fried tofu cubes in a serving bowl.
Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, black pepper, salt, and minced red onion in a separate bowl.
Microwave dressing for 20 to 30 seconds, just until warmed and the sugar dissolves.
Pour warm dressing over beef and tofu, then top with green onions and roasted sesame seeds.
Serve immediately or let stand briefly for the flavors to mingle.

intro: Ensaladang Labanos with Alamang is a crisp, tangy radish salad with savory fermented shrimp.
steps: Toss daikon with 2 tablespoons sea salt and rest for 5 minutes.
Squeeze out liquid, rinse the daikon under running water, and drain very well.
Combine daikon, tomatoes, red onion, bagoong alamang, cane vinegar, and sugar in a bowl.
Toss until the dressing and bagoong coat everything evenly. Serve with grilled or fried meat or seafood.

intro: Ube Halaya is a silky, intensely purple yam dessert finished with buttery latik.
steps: Combine grated ube, evaporated milk, coconut milk, condensed milk, sugar, salt, melted butter, and ube flavoring in a large nonstick pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until boiling.
Lower to medium-low and stir continuously for 35–45 minutes, until thick enough to hold a dough-like shape.
Divide into 3 butter-greased llaneras or 6 individual pie pans. Smooth, cool, and top generously with latik.

intro: Binagoongang Talong brings eggplant and pork belly together in a savory, lightly tangy bagoong sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Fry eggplant slices 1 minute per side; remove.
In the same pot, sauté garlic, shallots, and tomato until shallots soften.
Add pork belly and bird's eye chilies; cook until pork is light brown.
Stir in bagoong alamang and cook 1 minute. Add enough water to cover pork, boil, then simmer on low 40 minutes.
Add eggplant, cane vinegar, brown sugar, and long green chilies; simmer 2 minutes.
Season with black pepper and serve.

intro: Chicken Tocino is sweet, garlicky, and quickly caramelized after curing.
ingredients: 1 kg boneless chicken thighs, sliced 1/4 inch thick
steps: Mix anise wine, annatto powder, salt, brown sugar, soy sauce, garlic, and baking soda in a shallow bowl.
Add chicken and coat every piece evenly with the curing mixture.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 1 hour, then refrigerate for 1 day.
Place chicken in a heavy pan with enough water to reach halfway up the pieces. Bring to a boil and turn once.
When water evaporates, add a little oil and fry quickly until the sugar caramelizes.

intro: Tinapa Spaghetti gives tomato pasta a smoky Filipino twist with salted duck eggs and chicharon.
ingredients: 500 g dried spaghetti, cooked according to packet directions
3 large tinapa or an equivalent amount smoked fish, flaked
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic and onion in olive oil until the onion softens.
Add tomatoes, oregano, basil, and cane vinegar; cook, stirring, until tomatoes break down.
Stir in flaked tinapa and simmer 20 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper; simmer over low heat 10 minutes.
Top cooked spaghetti with sauce, chicharon, salted duck eggs, and parsley.

intro: Sans Rival is a frozen Filipino cashew meringue cake layered with rum buttercream.
steps: Beat egg whites until foamy; add cream of tartar and sugar gradually, beating to stiff peaks. Fold in 1 1/2 cups cashews.
Divide among three parchment-lined 9-inch pans and bake at 160°C for 35 to 40 minutes, until light golden.
Turn off oven and dry meringues inside, door closed, for 30 minutes for chewy layers or 2 hours for crisp layers.
Beat butter until light. Separately beat yolks; boil sugar and water to soft-ball syrup, then stream it into yolks while beating fast.
Beat in butter and rum; chill briefly if buttercream is too soft. Layer meringues with buttercream and 1/4 cup cashews between layers.
Frost cake, cover with remaining cashews, and freeze at least 4 hours before serving.

intro: Christmas Chicken and Ham Macaroni Salad is a creamy, sweet-savory chilled pasta salad for sharing.
steps: Bring water to a boil and cook chicken over medium heat for 15–18 minutes. Cool, shred, and reserve.
Cook elbow macaroni according to package directions, then drain and cool.
Mix mayonnaise, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl. Stir in onion, carrot, raisins, and sweet relish.
Toss in macaroni, ham, and shredded chicken. Fold in eggs, cheddar, and pineapple tidbits.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.

intro: Chocnut Turon wraps saba bananas and chocolatey Chocnut in a crackly caramelized shell.
ingredients: Toasted sesame seeds, optional, for garnish
steps: Peel each saba banana and cut it lengthwise in half.
Lightly coat banana halves in brown sugar.
Place one banana half, one Chocnut, and the remaining banana half on each wrapper. Roll, fold sides, and seal with water.
Add enough vegetable oil for deep-frying to a wok with remaining brown sugar. Heat over medium until sugar melts and rises.
Carefully fry Turon until golden brown and evenly coated with caramelized sugar.
Drain excess oil, garnish with toasted sesame seeds if desired, and serve.

intro: Buko Juice is a simple chilled drink of young coconut water, tender meat, and condensed milk.
ingredients: Young coconut meat from 3 fresh young coconuts
steps: Open the young coconuts through the top and pour their liquid into a large pitcher.
Add condensed milk and stir until fully dissolved.
Halve the coconuts, score the tender meat with a fork, and scrape it into strips with a spoon.
Add coconut meat and ice to the pitcher, stir gently, and serve immediately.

intro: Inihaw na Pusit with Scallion is tender grilled squid basted in a sweet, savory banana ketchup glaze.
steps: Rub squid with salt and tuck scallions into the cavities. Thread squid onto long metal or soaked bamboo skewers.
Mix soy sauce, sugar, garlic powder, black pepper, banana ketchup, and lime juice for the basting sauce.
Heat the grill. Brush squid on both sides, then grill the first side for 3 minutes.
Turn, brush again, and grill 3 minutes. Continue turning and brushing for 2 minutes per side, until cooked to your preference.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve immediately.

intro: Kani and Corn Egg Drop Soup is a light, silky chicken broth with sweet corn and delicate egg ribbons.
ingredients: ½ cup spring onions, sliced, white and green parts separated
steps: Bring chicken bone broth to a boil and season with salt and black pepper.
Add corn and white spring onion parts; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry until slightly thickened, then simmer 5 minutes.
Add kani and green spring onions; simmer 30 seconds.
Turn off heat and slowly pour in eggs while gently stirring. Rest 10 seconds, stir lightly, adjust seasoning, and serve.

intro: Sarciadong Daing coats fried dried fish in a quick savory tomato sauce.
ingredients: 3 to 5 red and green chili peppers, optional
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in optional chilies, black pepper, and fish sauce; cook for 3 minutes.
Add fried daing and cook for 1 minute, just until coated and heated through. Serve immediately.

intro: Copycat Kanin Club’s Vegetarian Delight is a thick, mushroom-rich tofu soup with banana blossoms.
ingredients: 425 g canned straw mushrooms, drained and halved
4 tablespoons oyster sauce or vegetarian oyster sauce
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot and sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant. Add vegetable stock and bring to a boil.
Add dried shiitake mushrooms and banana blossoms. Simmer over low heat for 20 minutes.
Add button mushrooms and straw mushrooms; simmer 5 minutes.
Whisk tapioca starch, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and water until smooth. Stir into the pot, then add tofu.
Simmer over medium-high heat about 5 minutes until thick. Season with salt and white pepper, drizzle with sesame oil, and serve hot.

intro: Pork Adobo in Pineapple Juice with Boiled Egg balances rich pork with sweet pineapple and tangy vinegar.
steps: Mix pork, pineapple juice, and soy sauce; cover and marinate at least 1 hour.
Cover eggs with water, bring to a rapid boil, turn off heat, and leave 10 minutes. Cool in iced water 10 minutes, then peel.
Brown crushed garlic in oil over medium heat. Separate pork from marinade and brown pork lightly.
Add reserved marinade and water; bring to a boil. Add Pork Cube, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer over low-medium heat for 1 hour, until pork is tender.
Stir in vinegar and brown sugar, turn off heat, and add eggs or serve them alongside.

intro: Crispy Palabok contrasts puffed bihon with a rich crab, pork, and smoked-fish sauce.
steps: Boil water; cook shrimp and squid 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. Drain, reserving the cooking liquid.
Blend crab meat, crab fat, reserved liquid, annatto powder, and fish sauce for 1 minute.
Sauté garlic and shallots in oil. Add minced pork and cook 3 minutes, then add crab mixture and smoked fish.
Mix cornstarch with a little water; stir into sauce. Boil and simmer until thickened, adding water if needed.
Heat frying oil to 180°C. Fry vermicelli in 50 g batches for 2 to 3 seconds per side until puffed; drain.
Arrange noodles with seafood, chicharon, spring onions, eggs, and lemon. Pour sauce over just before serving.

intro: Pork Nilaga with Kalabasa is a clean, comforting peppercorn broth with tender pork and sweet squash.
ingredients: 1 beef or pork cube, or 1 tsp beef powder
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add onion and peppercorns, cover, and boil for 10 minutes.
Add pork, stir, cover, and simmer 45 to 60 minutes until tender.
Add cube or beef powder, kalabasa, and potato; cook 7 minutes.
Add cabbage and green onions; cook 5 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in fish sauce and cook 1 to 3 minutes more before serving.

intro: This quick omelet turns leftover pork giniling kaldereta into a satisfying meal.
ingredients: A dash of ground black pepper
steps: Crack eggs into a bowl and whisk until smooth.
Whisk in salt, onion powder, and black pepper, then stir in pork giniling kaldereta until evenly combined.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Pour in half the mixture and cook for 3 minutes.
Flip with a wide spatula and cook 2 to 3 minutes until set. Repeat with remaining mixture.
Transfer to plates and serve with ketchup, toast, or white rice.

intro: Sago Samalamig is a refreshing brown-sugar drink with chewy sago, grass jelly, and plenty of crushed ice.
ingredients: 3 tightly packed cups brown sugar, for syrup
1 tightly packed cup brown sugar, for sago
steps: Cook sago according to package directions; rinse, drain, cover with cold water, and stir in 1 cup brown sugar.
Melt ¼ cup of the syrup sugar in a pot until lightly caramelized, without burning it.
Add water, vanilla, and remaining syrup sugar; boil, then simmer at least 10 minutes until fully dissolved.
Strain syrup through cheesecloth or muslin. Fill glasses with syrup, sago, grass jelly, and crushed ice.

intro: Crispy Buttered Chicken coats crunchy fried chicken in a fragrant, lightly sweet garlic-butter sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken nibbles, legs, or thighs
steps: Whisk eggs and fish sauce. Add chicken, pierce with a fork, cover, and marinate 2–3 hours.
Mix flour, cornstarch, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt. Shake chicken pieces in the mixture until evenly coated.
Heat oil to 180°C. Deep-fry chicken in batches for about 15 minutes, until golden, crisp, and cooked through.
Melt butter over low heat; cook garlic until fragrant but not browned. Stir in sugar just until dissolved, then turn off heat.
Drain chicken thoroughly and toss in garlic butter until coated. Serve immediately.

intro: Pancit Luglug covers thick rice noodles with a richly colored crab and smoked fish sauce.
steps: Cook rice noodles according to packet directions, drain, and set aside.
Boil shrimps, mussels, and squid in 2 cups water; reserve cooking liquid and seafood. Shell shrimp and mussels, then strain liquid through pounded shrimp shells.
Blend crab meat, crab fat, reserved seafood liquid, annatto, and fish sauce for 1 minute on low speed.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil. Add crab mixture and smoked fish.
Mix cornstarch with a little water until smooth; add to sauce, boil, and simmer until thickened, adding water if too thick.
Ladle sauce into bowls, add noodles, and garnish with seafood, chicharon, spring onions, eggs, fried garlic, and lemon.

intro: Fried Fish Adobo gives prepared fish adobo a crisp golden finish for a simple rice meal.
steps: Drain all liquid from the prepared Fish Adobo and pat the fish as dry as possible.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry fish in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp at the edges.
Drain on a paper towel-lined plate and serve hot with warm rice.

intro: Cinniejen’s Puto de Ube is a soft purple yam rice cake that can be finished with salted egg or cheese.
ingredients: Cheese and/or salted egg (pulang itlog), optional topping
steps: Wash rice, soak it in water overnight, then grind it finely. Boil scrubbed ube until soft, cool, peel, and mash.
Combine ground rice and mashed ube, then pass through a strainer to remove lumps.
Mix in sugar, butter, evaporated milk, and baking powder until thoroughly combined.
Fill puto molds two-thirds full. Steam over boiling water, cover, and top each with cheese and/or pulang itlog.
Steam until a toothpick comes out clean. Unmold and serve with grated coconut.

intro: Buridibud is a hearty vegetable-and-prawn soup enriched with bagoong monamon.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Add chicken stock and half the sweet potatoes. Bring to a boil and simmer until very soft.
Add bitter gourd, remaining sweet potatoes, moringa fruit, and eggplants; simmer 7 minutes.
Stir in bagoong monamon, prawns, and pea shoots; cook 3 minutes until prawns are opaque.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: A fresh tomato and onion relish with the bold saltiness of bagoong isda.
steps: Combine tomatoes, onion, and bagoong isda in a serving bowl.
Squeeze in lemon or calamansi juice and add ground black pepper.
Mix thoroughly until the vegetables are evenly seasoned.
Top with scallion and serve with fried fish or bagnet.

intro: Ginataang Langka with Malunggay and Daing is a savory coconut stew with tender jackfruit.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion, chili peppers, and garlic until onion softens.
Add jackfruit and cook 1 minute.
Add flaked daing and cook 30 seconds.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil. Cook over medium, stirring occasionally, until reduced.
Stir in malunggay leaves and fish sauce; cook 3 minutes.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot.

intro: Pesang Isda with Ginisang Miso combines ginger-poached fried fish and vegetables with a savory miso-tofu sauce.
ingredients: ½ cup green onions, cut into 2-inch pieces
Soy sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: For Ginisang Miso, sauté chopped onion 20 seconds and garlic 10 seconds in oil. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add tofu, then miso; sauté 2 minutes. Add soy sauce, pepper, and ½ cup water; cook 1 minute and set aside.
Fry fish in oil until golden on both sides; set aside. In a clean pan, sauté wedged onion and ginger until onion separates, then add garlic for 30 seconds.
Add rice washing and peppercorns; boil 2 minutes. Add fish, cook 3 minutes on one side and 5 minutes on the other.
Season with patis, add Napa cabbage, bok choy, and green onions, and cook 2 minutes. Serve with Ginisang Miso.

intro: Guinumis is a refreshing samalamig drink of gulaman, pinipig, sugar, water, and crushed ice.
ingredients: 1 cup prepared gulaman, cut into small cubes
steps: Stir sugar and water together until the sugar dissolves; chill the sweetened water thoroughly.
Divide prepared gulaman cubes and pinipig among four tall glasses.
Add crushed ice to each glass, then pour in the chilled sweetened water.
Stir gently and serve immediately while cold.

intro: Beef Lauya is a comforting clear beef soup with ginger, leafy vegetables, and crispy fried shallots.
ingredients: 1 1/2–2 kg stewing beef, beef ribs, oxtail, or neck bones
1/2 cup crispy fried shallots, plus more for garnish
steps: Cover beef with water in a pot, bring to a boil, and boil 5 minutes until scum rises.
Drain and rinse beef and pot thoroughly. Return beef to the clean pot with ginger, onion, peppercorns, fried shallots, and fish sauce.
Cover with water, bring to a boil, then simmer 1 1/2–2 hours until the meat is very tender.
Add Chinese cabbage and bok choy, adjust fish sauce, and cook 5 minutes until vegetables are tender but still crisp.
Serve topped with extra crispy fried shallots and spring onions.

intro: Speck and Bratwurst Sopas is a creamy, hearty Filipino-style noodle soup with smoky sausage and eggs.
steps: Sauté speck in a large pot over medium heat until its fat renders and edges crisp. Add bratwurst and brown lightly; reserve half if desired.
Cook onion in the rendered fat until soft, then add garlic and cook until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a gentle boil. Add macaroni and rigatoni, reduce heat, and simmer until just tender.
Add carrots and cook until softened. Stir in cream and simmer gently 2 to 3 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and black pepper; stir in half the spring onions. Serve topped with eggs, reserved meats, and remaining onions.

intro: Oxtail Kare-Kare is a deeply savory peanut stew served with bagoong alamang.
ingredients: 1 small fresh banana blossom (puso ng saging), sliced
3/4 cup annatto water, from 1/2 cup annatto seeds soaked in 3/4 cup water
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until softened. Add oxtail and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in water, bring to a boil, add Knorr Pork Cube, and cover. Simmer over low-medium heat until tender, about 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Stir in peanut butter and ground peanut, then add annatto water and cook for 3 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with 1/2 cup cold water. Stir into the pot until the sauce thickens.
Cook banana blossom 3 to 4 minutes, eggplant and sitaw 5 minutes, then bokchoy 2 minutes. Serve with bagoong alamang.

intro: Adobong Isaw braises tender small intestines in a spicy, reduced soy-vinegar adobo sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb pig or cow small intestine
steps: Bring 4 cups water to a boil with 2 teaspoons salt, rice wine, and 2 bay leaves. Add intestines and simmer until tender.
Drain intestines, let cool enough to handle, and cut into 2-inch lengths.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic and dried Thai chillies until fragrant.
Add intestines and cook 1 minute. Add peppercorns, remaining bay leaves, soy sauce, vinegar, and remaining 1/2 cup water.
Stir in remaining salt and sugar, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until sauce has evaporated and coated the intestines.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot.

intro: Ginataang Langka with Alimasag is a creamy coconut jackfruit stew enriched by sweet blue crab and malunggay.
ingredients: 2 cans (20 oz each) unripe jackfruit, chopped
2 packs (33 g each) Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add jackfruit and sauté 3 minutes. Mix Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix with 1 cup water until smooth.
Add optional chili and the Ginataang Gulay mixture. Bring to a boil; cook over medium heat 10–12 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Add crabs, cover, and cook 10 minutes.
Add malunggay and fish sauce; cook 5 minutes, until liquid evaporates completely. Serve hot.

intro: Pinoy Pork and Chicken Curry is a coconut-rich curry with tender meats and vegetables.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Pan-fry potato for 1 minute per side and set aside; pan-fry chicken 1 to 1 1/2 minutes per side and set aside.
Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in the remaining oil. Add pork belly and cook until its exterior is light brown.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add Knorr Pork Cube, cover, and simmer over low-medium heat until pork is tender, adding water as needed.
Return chicken and cook for 15 to 18 minutes.
Add potato, bell peppers, green peas, and curry powder. Cook 5 minutes, season with patis and pepper, and serve.

intro: Creamy Ginataang Hipon at Kalabasa balances sweet squash, shrimp, and crisp beans.
ingredients: 1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic, onion, and finger chillies until fragrant.
Add butternut squash and string beans; stir-fry until the squash develops light browning.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and fish sauce; simmer for 2 minutes, until shrimp are pink and just cooked.
Finish with black pepper and serve hot.

intro: Soft pandan puto with carrots and sugar-free sweetness makes a cheerful steamed snack.
steps: Combine flour, Splenda, and baking powder in a bowl.
Add evaporated milk, butter, egg, water, carrots, and pandan essence; whisk until thoroughly smooth.
Fill lightly greased puto molds, then top with cheese and sliced salted eggs.
Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes, until set and a tester comes out clean.

intro: A creamy Sipo Egg combines colorful vegetables, shrimp, cashews, and tender quail eggs.
steps: Whisk the cornstarch into the chicken stock until smooth.
Melt butter in a pan over low heat; sauté garlic and onion until the onion is soft.
Add corn, carrots, and peas; cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the stock mixture, cashews, shrimp, and quail eggs. Cook over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring gently.
Season with salt and white pepper, drizzle with sesame oil, and serve.

intro: A creamy, spicy Chicken Gising-gising made with sigarilyas and coconut vegetable sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant and the onion softens.
Add chicken and stir-fry until lightly browned outside. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil.
Dissolve Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix in the remaining 2 cups water; add to the pan, cover, and cook on low-medium for 20 minutes.
Stir in shrimp paste, long green chilies, and sigarilyas. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Add Thai chilies, if using, and cook for 2 minutes. Serve hot with rice.

intro: A rich, broiled pork-and-beans casserole made extra silky by slow-cooked pata.
ingredients: 1 kg pata (pork hock), cut into sections
steps: Lightly fry the bacon in oil without crisping; set aside.
Brown the pata well in the same pot, then remove it.
Sauté garlic and onion in the pot until fragrant and lightly golden.
Return pata, add water to cover, season lightly, and simmer until tender and the broth is gelatinous.
Add chorizo and simmer for 10 minutes, then gently stir in baked beans.
Transfer to a baking dish, top with bacon, and broil until bubbling and lightly caramelized.

intro: Paklay is a rich Visayan offal stew brightened with pineapple, bamboo shoots, and sinigang seasoning.
ingredients: 1/3 kg beef chuck steak or pork shoulder, cut into thin strips
1/3 kg pre-cooked beef tripe, cut into thin strips
1/4 kg beef liver, cut into thin strips
1/4 kg pork heart, cut into thin strips
3 cups bamboo shoots, cut into thin strips
2 thumb-sized pieces ginger, cut into thin strips
3 tsp annatto powder, dissolved in 1/2 cup water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a large wok and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Add beef or pork, pork heart, tripe, and bamboo shoots; cook for 5 minutes.
Add bay leaves, beef stock, and sinigang mix. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 30 minutes.
Add liver, pineapple, chilies, and dissolved annatto. Simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, salt if needed, and black pepper before serving.

intro: Lechon Sisig turns leftover roast pork into a bright, crisp, citrusy sizzling-style dish.
ingredients: 1 kg leftover pork lechon, preferably fatty head cuts with skin, chopped
1/2 cup calamansi or lemon juice, divided
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Put the chopped lechon in a large bowl. Add 1/4 cup of the calamansi or lemon juice, soy sauce, onion, chillies, and salt, then mix thoroughly.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Cook the garlic and ginger until their aroma blooms.
Add the seasoned pork and stir-fry until thoroughly hot, sizzling, and lightly crisp around the edges.
Remove from the heat and plate the sisig. Spoon over the remaining citrus juice, add black pepper, and serve immediately.

intro: A thick, economical monggo stew brightened with kangkong and savory hibi.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté onion, garlic, and tomato until the tomato softens.
Add mung beans and cook for 1 minute, then pour in water and bring to a boil.
Stir in the Knorr Shrimp Cube, cover, and cook until beans are very tender and the soup thickens, about 2 hours.
Add hibi and kangkong stalks; cook for 3 minutes. Season with patis and black pepper.
Add kangkong leaves and cook for 2 minutes. Serve with rice and crushed chicharon, if using.

intro: This hearty Filipino chicken noodle soup combines round miki, bacon, chicken, and vegetables in a savory broth.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken, cut into small serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add chicken; cook 3–5 minutes until lightly browned, then add chicken liver and cook 2 minutes.
Add water and chicken broth; boil, cover, and simmer 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir in bacon, carrot, and cabbage; cook 5–8 minutes, then season with fish sauce.
Add miki and cook 5–7 minutes until tender, loosening with broth or water if needed; stir in green onions and serve.

intro: Crunchy pickled mango balances sweet, tangy, salty, and optional heat.
ingredients: 2 pounds almost-ripe Carabao or Manila mangoes
steps: Boil clean glass jars for 10 minutes; dip lids for 10 seconds, then air-dry upside down.
Boil vinegar, water, sugar, salt, peppercorns, and cloves; simmer 3 minutes until dissolved, then cool.
Peel mangoes, slice the flesh into 1-cm pieces, rinse, drain, and pack into the jars with chili if using.
Cover mangoes completely with cooled brine, seal, and stand in a cool place or refrigerate for 1–2 days before serving.

intro: This savory Longganisa Fried Rice turns leftover rice into a quick, satisfying meal.
steps: Mix rice, salt, and garlic powder, gently breaking up clumps until evenly seasoned.
Heat oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook chopped longganisa for 2 minutes.
Add rice and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally until hot and lightly toasted.
Push rice to one side. Crack eggs into the empty space and scramble them with a spatula until set.
Fold eggs into the rice, add soy sauce, and stir-fry for 1 minute before serving.

intro: Guiso is a hearty tomato-and-pickle pork and chicken stew with hotdogs and liver.
ingredients: 450 g pork belly, skin and fat on, cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and brown pork belly on all sides, about 15 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic in the same pot until the onion softens.
Add chicken and browned pork; cook for 5 minutes, stirring continuously.
Add hotdogs, pickles, bay leaves, tomatoes, and pickle juice. Cover and simmer on medium-low for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in pork liver and cook on medium-low for 15 minutes, until cooked through. Season with salt and black pepper.

intro: Sweet Filipino spaghetti combines a cheesy banana-ketchup sauce with hotdogs and corned beef.
ingredients: 1 medium red bell pepper, finely diced
1 medium green bell pepper, finely diced
1 (165 g) block cheese, such as Eden or Velveeta
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, or to taste
steps: Cook spaghetti according to package directions; drain.
Heat oil and butter over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until tender.
Cook ground beef, breaking it up, for about 3 minutes until no pink remains; add hotdogs for 2 minutes.
Stir in corned beef, carrot, peppers, and mushrooms; cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato sauce, banana ketchup, salt, and pepper; simmer 5–7 minutes until carrot is tender.
Melt in half the grated cheese, toss with spaghetti, and finish with remaining cheese.

intro: Kusido is a clean, tangy tilapia soup with ginger, calamansi, and tender greens.
ingredients: 2 lb tilapia, sliced into serving pieces
steps: Bring water to a boil in a cooking pot.
Add tomatoes, onion, ginger, and long green peppers; simmer for 3 minutes.
Add tilapia and simmer gently for 7 to 10 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Stir in calamansi juice and season with salt.
Add sweet potato leaves and cook for 1 minute, just until wilted. Serve hot.

intro: Seafood Pancit Canton is a saucy noodle platter loaded with tender seafood and vegetables.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 3 tablespoons water
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a wok; stir-fry shrimp, squid, crab meat, and squid balls for 1 minute.
Add mushrooms, carrots, and Napa cabbage; cook 3 minutes. Add oyster sauce, sesame oil, and 3 cups broth; boil and thicken with cornstarch slurry.
In a clean wok, heat remaining oil and sauté onion until soft. Add soy sauce and remaining 2 cups broth; bring to a boil.
Add pancit canton, cover, and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes. Toss in seafood topping and sauce until noodles absorb it.

intro: Dinoydoy pairs crisp pork belly with softened squash and pleasantly bitter ampalaya.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork belly and brown on all sides until crisp.
Add tomato and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock, add squash, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the squash starts breaking down.
Add bitter melon and cook for about 5 minutes until tender. Season with fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: Pork Kaldereta sa Gata is a rich coconut-braised pork stew with tender vegetables.
steps: Heat oil over medium heat; sauté garlic until lightly golden, then cook onion until soft.
Brown pork belly, add tomatoes, and cook until the tomatoes break down.
Pour in 2 cups pork broth and bring to a boil. Add Thai chilies, liver spread, and bay leaves.
Stir in coconut milk, cover, and simmer on low-medium for 45–60 minutes, adding remaining broth as needed, until pork is tender.
Add carrots and potatoes; cook 7 minutes. Add bell peppers and cook 7–8 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper; simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens.

intro: Kalamay sa Latik pairs tender steamed rice cakes with palm-sugar syrup and toasted coconut curds.
ingredients: Coconut oil, for greasing and serving
1 1/2 cups palm sugar or brown sugar
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour, white sugar, and 2 1/2 cups water until smooth; pour into a coconut-oil-greased heatproof container.
Steam for 25 minutes, until set and cooked through; cool slightly and cut into squares using an oiled knife.
Boil 3 cups water with palm sugar for 10 minutes, until dissolved and slightly reduced to a pourable syrup.
Cook coconut cream in a nonstick pan, stirring occasionally, until curds form and oil separates; lower heat until curds turn light brown.
Drain the latik, then serve kalamay squares in syrup topped with toasted curds and a little coconut oil.

intro: Candied white beans are glossy, tender sweets with a delicate powdered-sugar finish.
steps: Soak cannellini beans overnight, then drain and rinse well.
Steam beans over boiling water for 45 minutes, until softened but still holding their shape.
Bring sugar and water to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until dissolved. Add beans, cover, and simmer on very low heat for 1 1/2 hours.
Cool beans in syrup for 15 minutes, drain, and dry in one layer on a paper towel-lined rack until completely dry.
Sift powdered sugar over the dried beans, turning gently to coat evenly.

intro: Pasulbot is a comforting coconut-milk dessert of soft glutinous rice cakes in caramel sauce.
ingredients: 1 cup water, plus more as needed
1/4 cup brown sugar, or to taste
steps: Knead glutinous rice flour with 1 cup water into a smooth dough, adding water or flour as needed. Set aside.
Melt brown sugar in a pot over medium heat until dark brown and caramelized.
Slowly stir in coconut milk and bring the caramel mixture to a gentle boil.
Shape dough into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Add the rice cakes and simmer over low heat for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cooked and the coconut sauce thickens.
Cool slightly in a serving bowl before serving.

intro: Crisp Camaron Rebosado gets its light, spicy crust from a quick beer batter.
ingredients: 1 lb medium or large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Heat oil in a deep pot for frying.
Beat egg with beer, black pepper, garlic powder, cayenne, and salt.
Whisk in flour in two additions until smooth, then stir in baking powder.
Dip shrimp in batter and fry in batches for 2 minutes.
Turn shrimp and fry 1 minute more, until crisp and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with ponzu or sweet-and-sour sauce.

intro: Callos is a deeply savory tomato stew of tripe, pork leg, chorizo, and chickpeas.
ingredients: 500 g precooked ox tripe, cleaned and cut into 1 1/2-by-1/2-inch strips
1 small pork leg, cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until garlic is golden.
Add pork leg and brown it on all sides. Add tomatoes and 4 cups beef stock; boil, then simmer gently for 1 hour.
Remove pork leg, pull meat from bones, slice it into strips, and return meat and bones to the pot.
Add tripe, chorizo, tomato paste, bay leaves, chickpeas, soy sauce, and paprika; simmer on low for 30–45 minutes, adding stock if needed.
Discard bones, add capsicums, season with fish sauce and pepper, then simmer 10 minutes. Serve topped with fried garlic.

intro: Cardillong Isda pairs crisp fried fish with a silky tomato-and-egg sauce.
ingredients: 1 large snapper or other fish, cleaned, gutted, and scored
steps: Season fish inside, in the scores, and outside with salt and pepper; rest 30 minutes.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C. Pat fish dry, fry until golden brown, then drain.
Sauté garlic and onion in a little frying oil until soft. Add tomatoes and cook about 2 minutes, until mashable.
Add water, bring to a boil, add fried fish, and simmer 3 minutes. Slowly stream in beaten eggs while stirring.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, then garnish with parsley before serving.

intro: Sinuglaw pairs tangy vinegar-cured fish with freshly grilled pork belly.
ingredients: 400 g fresh snapper or other white-fleshed fish, cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place fish in a nonreactive bowl with 3/4 cup vinegar and soak for 10 minutes.
Gently press the fish to remove excess liquid, then drain and discard the soaking vinegar.
Combine fish with cucumber, onion, ginger, chilies, salt, and black pepper.
Add lemon juice and remaining vinegar. Chill for 1 hour to cure and develop flavor.
Mix in freshly grilled, chopped pork belly immediately before serving.

intro: Ginarep is a clean, sweet corn and prawn soup enriched by a shell-infused broth.
ingredients: 250 g prawns, shelled and deveined; heads and shells reserved
3 large ears corn, kernels removed; cobs reserved
steps: Heat oil in a pot; fry prawn heads and shells, crushing the heads, until toasted and fragrant.
Add water, chicken stock, and corn cobs; boil, then simmer gently for 15 minutes.
In another pot, sauté garlic and onion in oil; add tomato and cook until soft.
Strain the prawn-corn broth into the tomato pot; add corn kernels, boil, and simmer 15 minutes.
Add prawns for 3 minutes, then malunggay for 1 minute; season with fish sauce and white pepper.

intro: Adobong Tahong coats tender mussels in a sharp, garlicky soy-vinegar sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb mussels, cleaned and shells removed
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook crushed garlic and peppercorns until the garlic is light brown.
Add mussels and stir for 2 minutes.
Add bay leaves, soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon toasted garlic. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 to 7 minutes.
Pour in vinegar, let the sauce return to a boil, then stir and cook for 3 minutes.
Season with salt, transfer to a plate, and top with remaining toasted garlic.

intro: This hearty longanisa fried rice is studded with egg, peas, and carrot.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Beat eggs, then cook as a thin omelet in 3 tablespoons hot oil; flip, cook through, and remove.
Add remaining oil and cook longanisa over medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fully cooked.
Add butter and let it melt, then fold in rice and cook for 3 minutes.
Slice the omelet, add it to the pan, and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add peas and carrot; cook 3–5 minutes until heated through and carrot is tender.
Season with salt and pepper, stir well, and serve.

intro: Soft steamed Puto Cheese is lightly sweet, fluffy, and topped with melted cheese.
steps: Whisk flour, sugar, and baking powder together.
Whisk in milk and egg just until the batter is smooth.
Mix in water, melted butter, and vanilla, then gently fold in grated cheese.
Grease molds and fill each three-quarters full with batter.
Steam over a very low, gentle simmer for 10–12 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Top with cheese strips, steam 1–2 minutes until melted, cool slightly, and unmold.

intro: These tender Cheese Cupcakes have a rich, milky crumb and crisp cheddar top.
ingredients: 1 cup grated cheddar cheese, plus more for topping
steps: Heat oven to 180°C and line a muffin pan with paper cups.
Sift flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Beat butter, sugar, and eggs until combined. Beat in flour mixture and condensed milk on low speed until smooth.
Fold in grated cheddar. Fill cups three-quarters full and scatter extra cheddar over each.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

intro: Chicken Kare Kare has a savory peanut sauce, tender chicken, vegetables, and cooked bagoong alamang on the side.
ingredients: 2 tsp cornstarch, diluted in 1/4 cup water
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add chicken and cook 1 to 1 1/2 minutes per side, then continue sautéing for 2 minutes.
