Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil. Stir in annatto paste until fully dissolved.
Cover and boil over medium heat for 30 to 35 minutes, until chicken is tender.
Stir in peanut butter and enough cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Add eggplant and snake beans; cover and cook 5 minutes. Add bok choy and cook 3 minutes. Serve with bagoong alamang.

intro: This rich Laing with Shrimp slowly cooks gabi leaves in deeply savory coconut milk.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon red chili flakes or 1 tablespoon Sriracha sauce
steps: Combine coconut milk, pork, onion, bagoong, ginger, and garlic in a large pot; bring to a boil.
Stir gently once boiling, cover, and simmer near boiling for 18 minutes.
Add dried taro leaves over low-medium heat without stirring; press them into the coconut milk and cook for 10 to 12 minutes.
When leaves absorb the liquid, stir and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
Add chili flakes or Sriracha and shrimp; cook 8 to 10 minutes, until shrimp are opaque.

intro: Beer Marinated Grilled Chicken Breast Inasal is juicy, lightly tangy chicken with a turmeric-annatto glaze.
ingredients: 1/4 cup white or apple cider vinegar
steps: Pound chicken between cling film until evenly flattened.
Combine vinegar, ginger, 1/4 cup soy sauce, beer, salt, pepper, lime juice, turmeric, and annatto; refrigerate chicken in the marinade at least 3 hours.
Mix remaining marinade with 3 tablespoons soy sauce and margarine; microwave 1 minute for the basting sauce.
Grill over medium heat 3–4 minutes per side, basting after turning and repeating until chicken is cooked through.
Serve hot with papaya atchara and sinamak, if desired.

intro: Bulanglang Kapangpangan is a guava-soured pork rib soup packed with tender vegetables.
ingredients: 1 kg pork ribs, preferably soft-bone sections, cut into pieces
steps: Place pork, guava, onions, and tomatoes in a pot. Add enough water to cover and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add taro and fish sauce; cook for 15 minutes until the taro is tender.
Add okra and eggplant and cook for 5 minutes.
Add kangkong and cook for 2 minutes. Adjust fish sauce, then serve.

intro: Avocado Ice Candy is a sweet, creamy frozen Filipino treat.
steps: Halve, pit, and scoop the avocados into a blender.
Add evaporated milk, condensed milk, sugar, and water; blend until completely smooth and sweet to taste.
Use a funnel to fill ice-candy bags, leaving room to tie each bag securely.
Freeze until firm, then serve straight from the freezer.

intro: Abuos are delicate ant eggs or larvae simply sautéed with garlic for an adventurous Ilocano dish.
steps: Heat a small amount of oil in a pan over low to medium heat.
Sauté minced garlic until fragrant but not browned.
Add the abuos and cook gently, stirring just until heated through.
Season lightly with salt and serve immediately.

intro: Satti features charcoal-grilled beef and chicken skewers with a warmly spiced, thick taro sauce.
ingredients: 500 g rib-eye or other tender beef, cut into small squares
steps: Mix 1/2 cup coconut milk, 10 g annatto, citrus juice, 3 tablespoons water, and 1/2 teaspoon salt; coat beef and chicken and refrigerate at least 12 hours.
Blend bird’s-eye chillies, ginger, shallots, turmeric, oregano, 1/4 cup water, and remaining annatto into a smooth spice paste.
Boil stock and 500 ml water with taro; simmer 10 minutes until soft, mash and blend smooth.
Sauté bagoong and tomato in oil, then spice paste; add taro mixture. Stir in flour, cornstarch, sugar, and 1/2 cup water; simmer 20 minutes until thick, seasoning with salt.
Skewer meat and brush with coconut milk; grill beef 5–7 minutes per side and chicken 10–12 minutes per side over medium-high heat. Serve with warm sauce.

intro: Adobong Dilaw is turmeric-bright chicken adobo with crisp potatoes and a tangy finish.
steps: Season chicken with salt. Deep-fry potatoes until golden, then set aside.
Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove. Cook turmeric for 30 seconds, then brown chicken.
Add water, cane vinegar, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar. Boil, then simmer 25 minutes.
Drain chicken and sauce separately. Fry chicken over high heat until browned on the sides.
Return sauce and potatoes, adding vinegar or liquid if needed; simmer 5 minutes, adjust salt, and top with fried garlic.

intro: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta cooks penne directly in a flavorful chicken stock sauce.
ingredients: 350 g boneless chicken thigh fillets, sliced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season chicken with salt and black pepper. Brown in olive oil in a large pan, then transfer to a plate.
Add more oil if needed; sauté garlic and onion until soft. Add mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock, bring to a boil, then add penne. Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add evaporated milk, quick-melt cheese, Parmesan, basil, and chicken. Return to a boil, then simmer on medium-low for 6 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and extra Parmesan, if desired, and serve.

intro: Chicken Igado is a tangy soy-vinegar sauté of tender chicken heart and liver.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pan-fry chicken liver in 3 tablespoons oil until its liquid evaporates and it turns light brown; avoid overfrying, then set aside.
Wipe out the pan, heat remaining oil, and sauté garlic until browning; add onion and soften.
Add chicken hearts and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce and vinegar, cover, bring to a boil, and cook for 1 minute.
Add bay leaves and water; cover and simmer over low-medium heat for 35 minutes.
Return liver, cook 3 minutes, add vegetables for 2 minutes, then season and serve.

intro: Loslos is tender adobo-braised pork ribs finished in a crisp, seasoned coating.
steps: Combine ribs, water, soy sauce, cane vinegar, peppercorns, bay leaf, and garlic; boil, then simmer over medium-low heat 30 minutes until tender.
Remove ribs and cool slightly.
Mix flour, salt, and pepper; dip each rib in egg, then coat thoroughly in the seasoned flour.
Heat oil to 180°C and fry ribs in batches for 2–3 minutes until golden and crisp; drain and serve hot.

intro: Lawot Lawot is a creamy coconut vegetable stew with pork and bagoong alamang.
ingredients: 1/4 squash or buttercup squash, cut into roughly 1-inch pieces
1 large bunch large-leaf spinach or alugbati
2 bunches kangkong, tender stalks and leaves only
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork and brown evenly, then stir-fry bagoong alamang for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk, add squash, okra, and tomatoes, then bring to a boil and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in coconut cream, kangkong, and spinach or alugbati; cook for 3 minutes until greens wilt.
Season with black pepper and fish sauce or sea salt as needed.

intro: Lechon Sinigang turns crisp roast pork into a deeply savory tamarind soup with fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 2 lbs lechon, cut into serving pieces
22 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Original
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until the onion softens.
Add lechon and sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Stir in sinigang mix, cover, and simmer on the lowest heat for 30 minutes.
Add daikon and cook for 5 minutes. Add peppers, okra, string beans, and eggplant; cook 5 minutes.
Add kangkong and cook 2 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Kinulob na Manok is a banana-leaf-covered chicken pot dish packed with cured meats, potatoes, and calamansi.
ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken, about 1 to 1.3 kg
1 large bunch spring onions, about 6 to 8 stalks
steps: Fry bacon in a little oil until crisp. Cool, crumble, and reserve the rendered oil.
Rub chicken generously with salt, including under the skin and cavity; rinse and pat dry.
Stuff chicken with half the chorizo, bacon, salami, and spring onions. Seal the openings and place in a clay pot or palayok.
Arrange onion, potatoes, tomatoes, peppercorns, and remaining meats and spring onions around the chicken.
Add olive oil, soy sauce, calamansi juice, and water. Cover with three banana-leaf layers and a heavy lid; simmer on low for 1 hour.
Uncover carefully and serve.

intro: Copycat Aristocrats Honey Fried Chicken is brined, steamed, fried crisp, and finished with honey.
steps: Dissolve salt and sugar in warm water. Submerge chicken and refrigerate for 6 hours.
Place water, bay leaves, garlic, and lemongrass in a steamer. Steam chicken for 30 minutes.
Refrigerate steamed chicken for 2 hours until cooled through.
Heat frying oil to 180°C. Deep-fry chicken for about 15 minutes, until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on a wire rack, cut each thigh in half, brush with honey, and serve.

intro: Pork Ginataan slowly braises pork belly in spicy, creamy gata.
steps: Heat oil and sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until onion is soft and translucent.
Add pork and sauté until lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and coconut cream and bring to a boil.
Add Thai chilis, cover, and cook 45–60 minutes until pork is tender.
Add spinach, cover, and cook for 2 minutes.
Season with black pepper and patis, then serve.

intro: Kababayan are soft, brown-sugar Filipino muffins with a buttery, lightly sugared finish.
steps: Heat oven to 180°C and lightly prepare a nonstick muffin pan.
Sift flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together.
Whisk eggs, milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla; gently whisk into the dry mixture just until combined.
Fill muffin wells halfway and bake 15 minutes, until the tops are golden brown.
Brush with melted butter, remove from the pan, sprinkle with sugar, and cool on a rack.

intro: This spicy Calderetang Kambing gets its hearty body from tomato and peanut butter.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, cut into squares
1 green bell pepper, cut into squares
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and chilies for 3 minutes.
Add goat meat and sauté until lightly browned. Stir in tomato paste and tomato sauce.
Pour in beef broth, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 90 minutes or until tender.
Stir in peanut butter, salt, and pepper until smooth. Add peas and bell peppers, cover, and cook 8–10 minutes.

intro: Maki Mi is a thick, silky noodle soup with tenderized pork, shiitake, and egg ribbons.
ingredients: Lamian or ramen noodles, cooked according to packet instructions
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pound pork slices lightly. Mix light soy sauce, cooking wine, garlic, baking soda, salt, and pepper; marinate pork for at least 30 minutes.
Coat both sides of the pork with cornstarch. Soak shiitake in hot water until soft, then chop them.
Bring mushroom soaking liquid, beef stock, mushrooms, and soy sauce to a boil. Add pork pieces one at a time.
Mix tapioca starch with 1/2 cup water and stir it into the soup gradually until thickened; reduce heat to low.
Stir in egg yolks gently to form ribbons, add sesame oil, and adjust salt.
Divide cooked noodles among bowls, ladle over soup, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: Fried Bangus delivers crisp, golden milkfish with a lightly tangy garlic marinade.
ingredients: 1 large boneless bangus (milkfish), scaled, cleaned, and butterflied
steps: Mix vinegar, garlic, peppercorns, and salt in a bowl.
Place bangus flesh-side down in a deep plate, cover with marinade, and refrigerate for 8 to 12 hours.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry bangus about 5 minutes per side until medium brown and crisp.
Cover loosely while frying to control splatter and allow steam to escape. Serve with sinamak.

intro: Dinengdeng with Bilong-bilong is a light Ilocano vegetable soup with fried moonfish.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot.
Add ginger, onion, and tomato; cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in bagoong isda.
Add ampalaya, okra, and sitaw; cover and boil for 5 minutes.
Add malunggay and fried bilong-bilong; cover and cook over medium heat for 5–7 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls.

intro: Golden dory fillets are finished in a silky mushroom cream sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix 1/2 cup flour, cornstarch, salt, and pepper. Season fish with lemon juice, salt, and pepper; rest for 15 minutes.
Dredge fish lightly in the flour mixture and pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides; set aside.
Cook mushrooms in a little oil for 1 minute; remove. Melt butter and sauté garlic and shallots.
Stir in 3 tbsp flour and cook into a roux. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thick.
Add nutmeg and mushrooms; simmer 1 minute. Add fish, simmer 1 minute more, and adjust seasoning.

intro: Ginisang Munggo with Tinapa is a smoky mung-bean stew served beside crisp red snapper.
ingredients: 1 1/2–2 cups water, plus more as needed
steps: Soak mung beans in 4 cups water overnight; drain. Rub snapper with sea salt.
Heat 10 tablespoons oil and fry snapper on both sides until crisp; drain.
Heat remaining oil and sauté onion, garlic, and tomato. Add tinapang isda and cook 1 minute.
Stir-fry mung beans 1–2 minutes, add 1 1/2–2 cups water, and simmer low-medium until very tender and mashable.
Season with fish sauce and pepper; add Malunggay leaves for 2–3 minutes. Serve with fried snapper and rice.

intro: Buko Pandan is a cold, creamy coconut dessert with fragrant pandan gulaman.
steps: Crumble gulaman bars into a pot with coconut juice; soak 30 minutes.
Bring to a boil, reduce to medium, stir in sugar until dissolved, then cook on low for 10 minutes. Stir in 3 drops pandan extract.
Strain into a flat container, cool, refrigerate until firm, then cut into small cubes.
Combine gulaman, young coconut, sago, and nata de coco. Whip cream until thick, then mix in condensed milk and remaining pandan extract.
Fold cream mixture through the coconut mixture and chill before serving.

intro: Tokwa at Baboy combines tender pork and crisp tofu in a sharp vinegar-soy dressing.
ingredients: 600 g pork ears, pork belly, or a mixture of both
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub pork with salt, black pepper, and oil. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Steam pork for 45 minutes or until tender and sticky. Cool slightly, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
Fry tofu in enough oil until golden and crisp. Cool, then cut into cubes.
Mix vinegar, onions, soy sauce, water, brown sugar, and black pepper until sugar dissolves.
Combine pork and tofu in a serving dish, pour over dressing, top with red chilies, and serve immediately.

intro: Chicken Sotanghon Soup is a comforting noodle broth finished with eggs and fried garlic.
steps: Boil chicken in water until cooked; slice it and reserve both chicken and broth.
Brown all but 1 tablespoon garlic in oil; remove and reserve the fried garlic.
Sauté onion and remaining garlic in the oil, then add chicken, fish sauce, and pepper for 2–3 minutes.
Add reserved broth and broth cube; bring to a boil.
Dissolve achuete in 1/2 cup hot broth, add it, then cook carrot 1–2 minutes.
Add sotanghon, then cabbage once softened; cook 1–2 minutes until noodles are done. Serve topped with egg, fried garlic, and green onion.

intro: Adobong Baboy sa Gata combines tender pork belly with reduced, fragrant coconut adobo sauce.
steps: Mix pork, soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic; marinate for 3 hours.
Drain pork, reserving the marinade. Cook pork in a pot over medium heat until browned.
Add oil, if using, and cook for 1 minute until garlic lightly browns.
Add reserved marinade, water, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Cover and boil over medium heat until pork is tender.
Stir in coconut cream, cover, and cook for 10 minutes. Continue boiling until reduced by half, then season with salt.

intro: Ginataang Manok with Papaya is a ginger-scented coconut chicken stew with tender green papaya.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 small green papaya, cut into wedges
steps: Heat oil in a pot; pan-fry chicken 1 1/2 minutes per side, then remove.
Sauté onion, ginger, and garlic in the remaining oil until the onion softens.
Return chicken, cook 1 minute, then add coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add chili peppers, cover, and cook over low to medium heat for 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add papaya for 5 minutes, then spinach for 2 minutes; season with patis and black pepper.

intro: Ginataang Langka, Monggo at Malunggay is a hearty coconut stew with pork, shrimp, and jackfruit.
steps: Heat oil over medium heat, season pork with salt, and brown it on all sides.
Add stock and mung beans; bring to a boil, then simmer until beans are tender but not mushy.
In another pot, heat oil and sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add kalcag for 2 minutes.
Add langka and cook for 5 minutes, then add the pork, monggo, and stock.
Add coconut milk and simmer gently on low for 30 minutes. Add malunggay, cook 5 minutes, and season with fish sauce.

intro: Bulalo Pares pairs fall-apart beef shanks with a sweet, deeply savory soy-anise sauce.
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 4 tbsp water
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add beef shanks and brown all sides.
Add stock, water, soy sauce, brown sugar, star anise, bay leaves, pepper, and cornstarch slurry; bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer about 1 1/2 hours, until beef is nearly falling apart.
Season with fish sauce to taste.
Garnish with fried garlic and spring onions; serve with garlic fried rice and clear beef soup.

intro: Pork Tapsilog pairs sweet-savory pork tapa with garlic rice and a fried egg.
steps: Combine pork, soy sauce, garlic, sugar, salt, and pepper in a resealable bag. Marinate overnight in the refrigerator.
Heat oil in a frying pan over low to medium heat.
Fry marinated pork, turning as needed, until both sides are medium brown and cooked through.
Plate the pork with garlic rice and fried eggs. Serve with spicy vinegar and ketchup, if desired.

intro: Higadillo is a tangy pork and liver stew enriched with lechon sauce and cane vinegar.
ingredients: 800 g pork belly, cut into strips
350 g pork liver, cut into strips
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot, brown the pork strips, then remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion in the same pot until fragrant.
Add pork liver and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return pork, add bay leaves, soy sauce, lechon sauce, and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 30 minutes.
Add vinegar and sugar; simmer 10 minutes, adding water if needed, until pork is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Homemade salted eggs need only fresh eggs, a strong brine, and patient curing.
steps: Boil water and salt until the salt dissolves completely, then cool the brine fully.
Place eggs in a large glass jar and pour in enough cooled brine to submerge them completely.
Weight eggs down with a water-filled plastic bag, seal the jar, and cure at room temperature for 3–4 weeks.
At week 3, boil one test egg, covered over low heat, for 10–12 minutes; cure another week if more saltiness is needed.
Boil remaining eggs if desired, label them, and refrigerate for up to one month.

intro: Serkele is a robust Tausug-style beef innard stew enriched with beef blood.
ingredients: 700 g beef innards, such as tendons, tripe, heart, and intestines, cut into small cubes
300 g beef brisket, cut into small cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: If using tendons, boil them in water for 1 hour until beginning to tender.
Add remaining innards, brisket, beef stock, and vinegar; boil for 45 minutes.
Drain meat, reserving the broth. Heat oil in the wok and sauté garlic on low until lightly browned; add onions until soft.
Return meat and cook for 10 minutes. Add reserved broth and green chilies.
Slowly stir in beef blood continuously, then boil and simmer on low for 30 minutes until meat is tender.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and black pepper. Serve hot with rice or puto.

intro: This creamy Filipino macaroni salad is packed with chicken, ham, pineapple, cheese, and sweet-savory mix-ins.
steps: Boil water with 1 teaspoon salt; cook macaroni about 8 minutes until al dente, then drain.
Boil chicken in fresh water about 12 minutes until fully cooked; cool slightly and dice.
Fold macaroni with mayonnaise, remaining 2 teaspoons salt, and black pepper.
Fold in chicken, ham, pineapple, bell pepper, carrots, onion, raisins, relish, pimiento, onion powder, and garlic powder.
Fold in cream and cheddar, cover, and refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.

intro: Salmon Belly Paksiw sa Gata combines oven-grilled fish with a sharp coconut-vinegar sauce and bok choy.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
2 stalks spring onions, chopped; white and green parts separated
steps: Season salmon belly with salt and pepper; bake on a foil-lined tray at 180°C for 15 minutes until golden and cooked.
Blanch bok choy for 1 minute, drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
Sauté garlic, onion, spring-onion whites, and ginger in oil until fragrant.
Add water, vinegar, and chillies; bring to a gentle boil, add coconut milk, and return to a slow boil.
Season with fish sauce and pepper; add salmon and tray juices, simmer 2 minutes, then serve beside bok choy with spring-onion greens.

intro: Balicasag Island Soup is a creamy seafood soup layered with lemongrass, eggplant, and green chilies.
ingredients: 200 g squid, cleaned and cut into rings
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté tomatoes, onion, garlic, and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add water and bring it to a boil.
Add squid, crabs, prawns, fish, scallops, eggplant, and chilies. Simmer 5 to 7 minutes, until seafood is cooked and vegetables are tender.
Stir in evaporated milk and simmer 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with salt, drizzle in sesame oil, remove lemongrass, and serve hot.

intro: Biyaki is a steamed cassava cake wrapped in banana leaves with corn and coconut cream.
steps: Mix cassava, brown sugar, salt, corn kernels, and coconut cream in a bowl until evenly combined.
Cut banana leaves into 30-by-30-cm squares and lay them flat.
Place 4 tablespoons cassava mixture on each leaf; fold into secure 10-by-6-cm rectangular packets.
Steam packets for 30 minutes, until the Biyaki is firm. Cool slightly before serving.

intro: This Filipino-style roast beef finishes tender slices in a velvety mushroom cream sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chuck roast beef, brisket, or round
5 large champignon mushrooms, sliced, or 1 small can champignon mushrooms
steps: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear roast on all sides until golden, about 8 to 10 minutes total.
Transfer beef to a pot with salt, peppercorns, and enough water to cover. Boil, then cover and cook on lowest heat for at least 2 hours until tender.
Cool slightly and slice beef thinly.
Melt butter in a skillet, sauté garlic until soft, then cook mushrooms until lightly browned.
Add mushroom soup, all-purpose cream, soy sauce, and white pepper; simmer, thinning with beef broth if needed. Add beef and simmer 10 minutes.

intro: Pork Sinigang sa Kamias is a bright, sour pork soup layered with fresh vegetables.
steps: Bring water, tomatoes, onion, and kamias to a boil.
Add pork, return to a boil, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add taro and long green peppers; cover and simmer 30 minutes more, until pork is tender.
Stir in fish sauce.
Add okra, string beans, and eggplant; cook for 5 minutes.
Add kangkong, cover, turn off heat, and let residual heat wilt it before serving.

intro: Pesang Manok is a soothing ginger chicken soup with potatoes and delicate leafy vegetables.
ingredients: 2 thumb-sized pieces ginger, peeled and sliced
steps: Combine chicken, ginger, onion, peppercorns, and rice wash water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
Add Napa cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add bok choy and spring onions; simmer for 2 minutes until just tender.
Season with fish sauce and serve hot.

intro: Longanisa Lumpiang Shanghai combines savory pork rolls with a sharp sweet-and-sour dip.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 7 teaspoons water
steps: Mix pork, longanisa, carrot, onion, singkamas, green onion, garlic powder, salt, pepper, grated Pork Cube, and egg.
Place 1 tablespoon filling on each lumpia wrapper and roll tightly, sealing the edges.
Deep-fry in oil at 320°F over medium heat for about 12 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through.
For sauce, boil sugar, ketchup, soy sauce, and vinegar; stir in cornstarch slurry until thick.
Serve the fried lumpia with the sweet-and-sour sauce.

intro: Melon Juice is a cold, creamy Filipino cantaloupe drink made directly in a pitcher.
steps: Cut the melon in half and remove the seeds.
Scrape the melon flesh into a large pitcher.
Add water and evaporated milk, if using.
Stir in sugar to taste and plenty of ice; serve chilled.

intro: Chewy Peanut Tikoy Rolls hide a creamy peanut butter center under crunchy roasted peanuts.
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, water, and vanilla until lump-free.
Grease an 8-inch square pan with coconut oil, pour in batter, and steam 15–18 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes, then turn the tikoy onto a coconut-oil-greased mat.
Pipe peanut butter near one edge, roll tightly to enclose it, seal, and cut off the roll; repeat with remaining tikoy.
Cut rolls into pieces and coat every side with ground roasted peanuts.

intro: Jumbo Siopao are substantial steamed buns filled with seasoned chicken, char siu, salted egg, and Chinese sausage.
ingredients: 3 cups dumpling flour, plus 1/2 cup for dusting
400 g finely chopped or minced chicken thighs
1 tbsp vinegar per litre of steaming water
steps: Mix chicken, light soy sauce, cornstarch, brown sugar, sesame oil, and salt. Keep char siu, salted egg, and Chinese sausage separate.
Combine yeast, 2 tsp sugar, and lukewarm water; leave somewhere warm for 30 minutes.
Knead flour, remaining sugar, salt, shortening or oil, and warm water until smooth and elastic. Let rise in a greased bowl for 2 hours.
Deflate dough, knead in baking powder for 5 minutes, then divide into 8 pieces and roll thin.
Fill each round with about 50 g chicken filling, char siu, sausage, and egg. Seal, place on greased paper, and proof 30 minutes.
Add vinegar to the steamer water. Steam buns for 30 to 40 minutes, until puffed and cooked through.

intro: Ginataang Bilo-bilo is a creamy coconut dessert with chewy rice balls, fruit, and tapioca.
ingredients: 2 (400 ml) cans coconut milk or cream
2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour with 1 cup water into dough; roll scant half-spoonfuls into balls.
Bring 2 cups water, coconut milk, and sugar to a boil.
Add sweet potato and cook 3 minutes, stirring occasionally; add banana and cook 3 minutes.
Add rice balls and simmer about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they float.
Add jackfruit and cooked tapioca; simmer 3–5 minutes until fruit is tender.
Serve warm or chilled; the dessert thickens as it cools.

intro: Bohol Adobo is a dark, tangy pork adobo with black beans, annatto, and fried potatoes.
ingredients: 1/3 cup Philippine soy sauce or Kikkoman soy sauce
4 tbsp black beans, drained and roughly mashed
2 tbsp annatto powder, dissolved in 4 tbsp boiling water
steps: Deep-fry potatoes in hot oil until golden; drain and set aside.
Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden, then remove and reserve it.
Fry pork belly until browned. Add 1 cup water, vinegar, soy sauce, black beans, annatto, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour until pork is tender; reduce the sauce near the end.
Mix cornstarch with remaining 1/4 cup water. Add slurry and potatoes, then simmer 5 minutes before serving.

intro: Sinigang na Pompano sa Miso balances tamarind tang, mellow miso, and tender fish.
ingredients: 2 whole pompano, about 500 to 600 g each, cleaned, scaled, and cut into serving portions
2 cups fresh tamarind pulp, from boiled and strained tamarind pods
1 daikon radish, peeled and cut into rounds
1 bunch mustard leaves, washed and trimmed
steps: Boil tamarind pods in 3 cups water until soft, mash them, then strain to make tamarind pulp.
Bring 8 cups water to a boil. Add onion, ginger, and tomatoes; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in tamarind pulp and miso until dissolved. Add daikon and simmer about 10 minutes until tender.
Gently add pompano and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until just cooked through.
Add mustard leaves and siling pangsigang for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in patis, adjust salt, and serve.

intro: Estofadong Pata is a rich, slow-braised pork dish with saba bananas and banana blossoms.
ingredients: 1 kg pork leg, cut into sections
1 kg pork trotters, cut into sections
1 tablespoon cornstarch dissolved in 1/2 cup water
steps: Brown garlic in oil in a large pot, then brown pork leg and trotters on all sides.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, brown sugar, cornstarch slurry, fish sauce, peppercorns, and shallots; bring to a boil.
Simmer gently for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the pork is very tender.
Add banana blossoms and simmer 15 minutes; add saba bananas and simmer another 15 minutes.
Raise heat to reduce the liquid until thick, then serve.

intro: Pinangat na Isda is crisp pompano gently simmered in a bright sour tomato broth.
ingredients: 1 large pompano, cleaned, gutted, and scored
4 tablespoons tamarind powder, or 8 bilimbi (kamias), or 1/2 cup lemon or calamansi juice
steps: Season pompano inside and out with salt and pepper. Shallow-fry in hot oil until crisp at the edges; set aside.
Leave 3 tablespoons oil in the wok. Sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger, then cook tomatoes and bilimbi, if using, until soft.
Add water, boil, and cover-simmer 3 minutes; simmer 3 minutes longer when using bilimbi.
Add fish and tamarind powder or citrus juice, if using. Simmer on low 5 minutes, turn fish, and simmer 2 minutes.
Adjust sourness with water and season with fish sauce and pepper. Add spring onions and chilies; simmer 2 minutes.

intro: Everlasting is a festive steamed pork loaf set in individual llaneras.
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated quick-melt cheese or processed cheese
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic and onion in oil. Add pork and chorizo; cook for 10 minutes.
Add capsicum, tomato paste, soy sauce, and pickle relish. Simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Stir in raisins and cheese; season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat and cool completely.
Mix in beaten eggs. Grease four llaneras with margarine and place one boiled-egg half in each.
Fill llaneras with meat mixture, cover tightly with foil, and steam for 1 hour.

intro: Maja Blanca is a chilled coconut-and-corn pudding with a toasted coconut finish.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can whole sweet kernel corn
steps: Bring coconut milk to a boil in a pot.
Stir in sugar, condensed milk, and corn until evenly combined.
Simmer for 8 minutes.
Whisk fresh milk and cornstarch until completely smooth.
Stir the slurry into the pot and cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Spread in a serving tray, cool, refrigerate at least 1 hour, and garnish with toasted coconut.

intro: Filipino Vinegar Dipping Sauce offers three sharp, spicy Sukang Sawsawan variations for grilled and fried dishes.
ingredients: Panlasang Pinoy spicy vinegar: 1 cup coconut vinegar
Panlasang Pinoy spicy vinegar: 1/2 cup Thai chili peppers
Panlasang Pinoy spicy vinegar: 4 thumbs ginger, julienned
Panlasang Pinoy spicy vinegar: 1 garlic head, crushed
steps: For Sinamak, combine its listed ingredients in a clean mason jar. Seal and steep for at least 3 days before using.
For the Tokwat Baboy-style sauce, heat its vinegar with salt and sugar until dissolved, then cool completely.
Transfer cooled Tokwat Baboy-style vinegar to a jar with its chilies, bell pepper, garlic, peppercorns, and ginger. Seal, shake, and refrigerate.
For Panlasang Pinoy spicy vinegar, heat its vinegar with salt until dissolved and let it cool.
Process cooled spicy vinegar with its chilies, ginger, and garlic for 2 minutes. Transfer to a clean jar and use immediately.

intro: Corn and Malunggay Soup is a simple, lightly sweet chicken-broth soup for everyday meals.
steps: Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add shredded corn and stir well.
Pour in chicken broth, bring to a boil, then simmer for 8 to 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper; cook for 2 minutes.
Add malunggay leaves and simmer for 2 minutes until tender. Serve hot.

intro: Turrones de Casoy is a chewy cashew nougat cut into neat wafer-wrapped sweets.
ingredients: 4 sheets wafer paper, each cut into 4 equal 3 x 4-inch pieces
steps: Toast cashews in a pan over low-medium heat until golden, then set aside.
Whip egg white to stiff peaks. Warm honey and sugar over low heat until dissolved.
Fold whipped egg white into the honey mixture continuously over low heat for about 15 minutes, until chewy.
Fold in cashews. Sift powdered sugar with cornstarch and scatter half into a parchment-lined 8-inch square pan.
Spread in hot nougat, add remaining powder, and cool 30 minutes; cut into rectangles and wrap in wafer paper.

intro: Gotong Batangas is a deeply savory vinegar-kissed beef and offal soup.
steps: Soak both tripe types in 1 cup vinegar and salt for 30 minutes; drain, rinse, and drain again.
Season shank, tripe, and heart. Brown them in batches in oil, then marinate with remaining 1/2 cup vinegar.
Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion in the same pot. Fry annatto powder briefly until it colors the oil.
Add tendon, rice wash, and beef stock; boil, then simmer low for 1 hour. Add drained marinated meats and simmer 1 hour more.
Add chilies and liver; simmer 20 minutes. Season, then garnish with spring onions and fried garlic.

intro: Batangas Bulalo is a clean, long-simmered beef shank soup served with a sharp chili-citrus dip.
ingredients: 3–4 lb beef shank with extra bones
1 1/2 tbsp rock salt or coarse sea salt
steps: Bring water to a boil, add beef shank and bones, cover, and boil over low-medium heat for 1 hour.
Skim off floating scum and oil.
Add onions, peppercorns, salt, and 4–5 tablespoons fish sauce; cover and simmer for 3 hours.
Arrange cabbage and bok choy in a large bowl, then place beef and bones over the vegetables.
Ladle over the hot broth.
Serve with chili peppers, remaining fish sauce, and lemon or calamansi for dipping.

intro: Cuapao fills soft lotus leaf buns with long-simmered pork asado, burong mustasa, and roasted peanuts.
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornstarch, dissolved in 1/3 cup water
steps: Heat oil in a pan, sauté garlic, add pork, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add water, soy sauce, brown sugar, and five-spice powder. Bring to a boil and simmer on low for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Stir in hoisin sauce and cornstarch slurry. Simmer until thick, season with salt, and set aside.
Wash mustard greens, drain, and sun-wilt for 2 hours. Cook rice with boiled water over medium heat until soft.
Mash wilted mustard greens with sea salt in a sterilized jar. Strain rice water, cool it, pour it over the greens, and ferment at room temperature for 5 days.
Steam lotus leaf buns as directed. Fill with burong mustasa, 2 tbsp pork asado, and roasted peanuts.

intro: Sinigang na Ulo is a quick, tangy fish-head soup with tender mustard greens.
ingredients: 3 large Hapuka heads or other large fish heads
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine onion, tomatoes, and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add fish heads and tamarind mix; simmer 5–10 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Cook large fish heads individually if necessary, extending the cooking time as needed.
Add mustard greens and simmer for 2 minutes until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Kilawing Isda cures fresh white fish in bright vinegar and citrus with aromatic vegetables.
ingredients: 500 g white fish meat, such as grouper or snapper, cut into small cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix fish with 1/2 cup vinegar and soak for at least 5 minutes.
Drain fish in a colander and lightly squeeze out excess liquid.
Combine remaining vinegar, lemon juice, ginger, onion, garlic, chillies, coconut milk if using, salt, and black pepper.
Mix fish with the dressing, cover, and refrigerate for 4 to 6 hours. Serve chilled.

intro: Suman sa Lihiya is a chewy glutinous-rice cake wrapped in banana leaves and served with palm sugar sauce.
steps: Cut banana leaves into roughly 10-inch squares and quickly pass them over an open flame until pliable, without burning.
Soak glutinous rice in 1 can coconut milk for 1 1/2 hours. Drain, then mix in lihiya until rice turns yellow.
Wrap 3 tablespoons rice in each leaf, fold both ends, and tie securely with cotton string.
Cover suman with water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 2 hours.
Heat remaining coconut milk and palm sugar on low, stirring until melted. Simmer gently for 30 minutes until syrupy.
Unwrap the suman and pour palm sugar sauce over each serving.

intro: Crispy Nilasing na Hipon is wine-marinated shrimp fried with a crunchy, spicy coating.
ingredients: 1 lb shrimp, heads and shells on
steps: Rinse shrimp under running water and drain well. Toss with garlic salt and black pepper.
Add Shaoxing wine, toss thoroughly, and marinate for 10 minutes.
Mix flour, cornstarch, and cayenne pepper in a separate bowl.
Heat oil in a deep pan or wok to 325°F. Dredge shrimp completely in the flour mixture.
Fry shrimp 1–2 minutes per side, until dark orange and crisp. Drain on paper towels and serve with spicy vinegar.

intro: Sweet and Spicy Dilis coats crisp dried anchovies in a glossy ketchup, sugar, and cayenne glaze.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and fry dilis for 1–2 minutes; do not overcook or they may become bitter.
Drain the anchovies and toss them in a bowl with ketchup, brown sugar, and cayenne until coated.
Sauté garlic in a little oil, then add the coated dilis.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously until the sugar melts and forms a coating.
Cool before serving.

intro: Soft, buttery Ensaymada is finished with sweet margarine and a generous cheese topping.
ingredients: 4 1/2 cups high-grade flour, plus more for kneading
1 cup cold butter, cut into small cubes
Grated edam or cheddar cheese, for topping
steps: Mix lukewarm water, 1 teaspoon sugar, and yeast; let bloom. Sift flour, 3/4 cup sugar, and salt, then whisk milk, yolks, and eggs.
Using a dough hook on low speed, mix in yeast mixture and wet ingredients until a dough forms.
Increase speed gradually, adding butter one cube at a time. Knead 20 to 25 minutes until smooth, elastic, and no longer clinging to the bowl.
Cover dough and let double in a warm place; for best flavor, refrigerate covered for at least 12 hours, then deflate.
Divide into 24 pieces, roll into 8-inch ropes, coil on lined trays, and let double again. Bake at 180°C for 12 to 15 minutes until light brown.
Cool, then spread with margarine mixed with sugar; add more sugar and grated edam or cheddar.

intro: Spicy Adobong Tahong turns plump mussels into a buttery vinegar-soy adobo.
steps: Soak mussels in water with rock salt for 20 minutes.
Steam mussels with 1 cup water and ginger over medium heat until shells open. Cool, reserve broth, remove meat, and discard beards.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil over medium heat until lightly browned and fragrant.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, 1/4 cup reserved broth, bay leaves, and peppercorns; simmer unstirred for 5 minutes.
Add mussels, brown sugar, butter, and chili labuyo; cook 5 minutes, until sauce thickens.

intro: Adobong Salagubang is an adventurous adobo-style preparation using prepared edible beetles.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Use only food-grade, properly cleaned salagubang from a reliable supplier.
Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add salagubang and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, water, and black pepper; do not stir until the vinegar boils.
Cover and simmer until the liquid reduces and the beetles are heated through.
Serve hot with rice.

intro: Liempo Estofado is a sweet-sour pork belly stew with saba bananas and carrots.
ingredients: 4 ripe saba bananas, peeled and sliced
1/4 cup red wine vinegar or cane vinegar
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add pork and cook for 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce, water, bay leaves, and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Add vinegar and brown sugar; cook 15 minutes, adding water if the pot becomes dry.
Add saba bananas and carrots. Cook for 10 minutes, until carrots are tender.
Season with salt and serve.

intro: Batutay Longganisa is a spicy cured beef sausage enriched with pork back fat.
steps: Mix beef, pork back fat, garlic, chilies, soy sauce, salt, pepper, paprika, and oregano until evenly combined.
Stuff mixture into sausage casing, tie off the end, and twist into 2 1/2-inch links, packing each link gently.
Hang sausages in direct sunlight for 6 hours, then refrigerate in a tightly covered container for 3–5 days to cure.
To cook, cover sausages with a little water in a pan over low heat until water evaporates; add oil and pan-fry slowly until cooked through.

intro: Baaoeno Tinuktok is a bright, sour fishball soup with papaya and kangkong.
ingredients: 700 g white-fleshed fish fillets, such as snapper, grouper, cod, or monkfish
2 stalks lemongrass, chopped, white parts only
steps: Pulse fish, prawns, cornstarch, shallots, lemongrass, and ginger in a food processor until minced but not pasty.
Shape the mixture into large spoonful-sized fishballs and set aside.
Bring water to a gentle boil. Add onion and young papaya; simmer until papaya is tender.
Gently add fishballs and season with fish sauce. Simmer until the fishballs are cooked through.
Add white pepper, calamansi or lemon juice, kangkong, and optional chilies. Simmer a few minutes, then serve.

intro: Pinoy Carbonara with Ham and Bacon uses a creamy mushroom sauce and crisp bacon over spaghetti.
ingredients: 8 strips bacon, cut into 1/2 cm pieces
68 g Knorr Cream of Mushroom Soup
steps: Cook spaghetti according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Cook bacon in a pan until crisp; remove and set aside.
Melt butter in the same pan; sauté garlic 10 seconds, then stir in mushrooms and flour for 30 seconds.
Whisk soup mix with water, add to the pan, and stir over heat until the sauce thickens.
Stir in Parmesan and pepper, turn off heat, toss with spaghetti, and top with bacon and extra Parmesan.

intro: Adobong Sitaw with Tofu is a quick soy-vinegar braise of crisp beans and golden tofu.
ingredients: 12 to 15 string beans, cut into 2 1/2-inch lengths
3 pieces extra-firm tofu, about 3 oz each, fried until medium brown
steps: Cut the fried tofu into squares.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add tofu, soy sauce, and water. Bring to a boil.
Pour in vinegar and allow the sauce to return to a boil.
Add string beans, stir, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Mango Taho layers warm tofu jelly with mango sauce, arnibal, and sweet boba.
steps: Blend 1 cup mango cubes, white sugar, and lime juice until smooth; set aside.
Cook boba according to its package directions, drain, and toss with an equal amount of sugar.
Combine water and brown sugar at a 1:3 ratio; simmer 5 minutes to make arnibal.
Steam tofu jelly in covered heatproof cups for 15 minutes, keeping condensation out.
Drizzle warm tofu with arnibal and mango sauce, then add mango cubes and sweetened boba.
Serve immediately while warm.

intro: Pancit Lusay is a savory Laoag noodle dish with longganisa, bagoong alamang, and egg.
ingredients: 6 Laoag or Vigan longganisa, roughly sliced
500 g thin fresh yellow noodles (miki or lusay)
steps: Briefly blanch fresh noodles in boiling water, drain well, and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok and cook longganisa while gently breaking it up. When browned, push it to one side.
Add shallot and garlic; sauté for 30 seconds. Add bagoong alamang and cook until fragrant.
Add noodles and spring onions. Stir-fry for 1 minute, distributing the longganisa and bagoong evenly.
Make a well, add beaten eggs, and let them set. Break up the egg, stir-fry for 1 minute, and serve.

intro: Atcharang Labanos is a crisp, sweet-sour daikon pickle for serving beside savory meals.
steps: Slice daikon crosswise as thinly as possible, preferably with a mandoline.
Toss daikon with 3 1/4 tablespoons salt and rest for 30 minutes. Rinse in a colander and drain well.
Mix vinegar, remaining 1/4 tablespoon salt, sugar, and peppercorns; microwave for 30 seconds, then cool slightly.
Pack daikon and onion into a pickling jar, cover with vinegar mixture, and refrigerate for 3 days before serving.

intro: Squid Ball Pancit Canton is a quick, savory noodle dish with seafood balls and tender vegetables.
steps: Heat oil in a wok; sauté garlic, onion, parsley, and black pepper until fragrant.
Add squid balls and optional lobster balls; stir-fry 2–3 minutes.
Add cabbage and carrots; toss and cook 5 minutes until beginning to soften.
Add soy sauce and broth, then bring to a boil. Lay noodles over, cover, and steam 1–2 minutes.
Uncover and gently toss until noodles are tender and liquid is absorbed; finish with lime juice.

intro: Lang Lang is a comforting sotanghon soup with chicken, pork-shrimp meatballs, and crisp snow peas.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup rehydrated wood ear fungus, thinly sliced
steps: Combine chicken, celery, spring onion, peppercorns, and water. Boil for 30 minutes; remove chicken, strain broth, and flake the cooled meat.
Mix minced pork, chopped shrimp, egg, cornstarch, black pepper, and salt; form small meatballs.
Heat oil in a pot, fry garlic until golden and crisp, remove it, then sauté shallots in the remaining oil.
Bring strained broth to a boil. Add meatballs one by one, lower heat, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add chicken and wood ear fungus for 5 minutes, then sotanghon and fish sauce for 5 minutes.
Add snow peas, cover, and let residual heat cook them. Garnish with fried garlic and serve.

intro: Pork Salpicao features seared pork cubes in a buttery Worcestershire and garlic finish.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pork with salt and black pepper; marinate for 15 minutes.
Warm olive oil in a heavy pan over low heat. Fry garlic until golden and crisp, then remove it.
Pour off oil and heat the pan over high heat until smoking. Brown pork in batches on all sides.
Return all pork to the pan with butter, half the fried garlic, Worcestershire sauce, and spring onions; toss over very high heat for 1 minute.
Transfer to a platter, drizzle with Maggi Savor, top with remaining garlic, and serve.

intro: Chicken and Liver Adobo uses mashed liver to make its vinegar sauce especially rich.
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil and pan-fry chicken liver until thoroughly cooked; remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic for 15 seconds in the remaining oil. Fry chicken pieces for 15 seconds per side.
Add vinegar, boil, scrape up browned bits, cover, and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add oyster sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves, water, and Chicken Cube. Boil, cover, and cook 15 minutes.
Mash liver into the pan and cook 15–20 minutes more. Serve with warm rice.

intro: Pork Bistek layers lemon-marinated pork with a soy-beef sauce, soft onions, and crisp potatoes.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
2 large white onions, sliced into rings
steps: Marinate pork with one-third of the lemon juice, salt, and pepper for at least 24 hours.
Deep-fry potato slices until crisp; drain. Drain pork thoroughly and bring it to room temperature.
Pan-fry pork in hot oil until cooked, then remove. Briefly sauté onions in the same pan without overcooking.
Whisk cornstarch, water, beef stock, and soy sauce until smooth; add to the pan and boil until lightly thickened.
Add remaining lemon juice, adjust salt and pepper, then pour sauce over pork and garnish with onions and fried potatoes.

intro: Manuk Kiarehan is a fragrant coconut chicken curry with black beans and curry leaves.
ingredients: 3 tbsp salted black beans, lightly mashed
1 handful coriander, stems finely chopped and leaves separated
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat and brown chicken on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion for 1 minute. Add curry leaves and coriander stems; sauté 1 minute more.
Add coconut milk, carrots, and chicken. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 30 minutes.
Stir in curry powder, chili powder, black beans, and coconut cream. Simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Season with black pepper and fish sauce, then garnish with coriander leaves before serving.

intro: Ginataang Munggo, or Lelut Balatung, is a warm coconut pudding of rice and toasted mung beans.
ingredients: 2 cups water, or more as needed
steps: Rinse glutinous rice. Toast mung beans over medium heat until brown and nutty, then crack them with a rolling pin and sieve away loose skins.
Bring coconut milk and 1 cup water to a simmer. Add rice and mung beans, cover, lower heat, and cook about 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally and add water as needed until rice and beans are expanded, soft, and nearly dry.
Stir in sugar and half the coconut cream; cook 5 minutes. Serve topped with remaining coconut cream, warm or chilled.

intro: Inihaw na Bangus is smoky grilled milkfish filled with a fresh tomato-ginger stuffing.
steps: Wash bangus and pat dry thoroughly.
Open the belly incision and rub salt inside the fish.
Combine tomato, onion, ginger, lemon or calamansi juice, and black pepper.
Stuff the mixture inside the bangus.
Grill over medium heat for 10–12 minutes per side, until cooked through and flaky.
Serve with toyomansi and steamed rice.

intro: Tambo Tambo is a coconut-mango porridge with chewy glutinous rice balls and tapioca.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (75 g) small dried tapioca pearls
1/2 cup (125 ml) water, plus more as needed
2 ripe mangoes, peeled, pitted, and diced
steps: Soak tapioca in 1 cup water for 30 minutes.
Mix rice flour with 1/2 cup water, adding water by tablespoons if needed, until slightly tacky dough forms.
Roll teaspoonfuls into about 20 small balls; cover with a damp towel.
Drain and rinse tapioca, then boil coconut milk, remaining water, salt, and sugar.
Reduce to low, add rice balls, and simmer 3–5 minutes until chewy and expanded.
Bring back to a boil, turn off heat, stir in tapioca until translucent, then stir in mango and serve warm.

intro: Pesa is a light, comforting fish soup enriched with yellow miso, greens, and rice wash.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg white, fleshy fish with bone and head
steps: Season fish with salt and pepper. Lightly fry in very hot oil, then remove and reserve some oil.
Sauté garlic and red onion in reserved oil over medium heat until soft. Add ginger and tomatoes; cook until tomatoes soften.
Add rice wash, yellow miso, and peppercorns; bring to a boil.
Add fish, return gently to a boil, and simmer 4 minutes. Add pak choy, cabbage, leek, and nori; simmer 4 minutes more.
Season with fish sauce to taste and serve hot.

intro: Humba is a sweet-savory Bisaya pork belly braise with banana blossoms and salted black beans.
steps: Sear pork belly in a wok until brown and fat has rendered. Remove pork and set aside.
Use about 3 tbsp rendered oil to sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Return pork, add soy sauce, and sauté for 1 minute. Add vinegar and cook until the liquid evaporates.
Pour in clear soft drink, cover, and bring to a boil. Add peppercorn and simmer on low for 35 minutes.
Add banana blossoms, salted black beans, and the pork cube. Cover and cook until pork is tender, adding water as needed.
Stir in brown sugar and cook 1 minute before serving with warm rice.

intro: Creamy Chopseuy brings colorful stir-fried vegetables and chicken liver together in mushroom sauce.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon cornstarch, dissolved in 1/4 cup water
2 cups mushroom soup, canned or homemade
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil broccoli for 2 minutes, drain, and rinse under cold running water. Season chicken liver with salt and black pepper.
Heat a wok over very high heat, add oil, and brown liver on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add more oil if needed, then sauté garlic and onion. Stir-fry carrot, celery, and mushrooms for 2 minutes.
Return liver and add cabbage and capsicum; stir-fry 2 minutes. Add broccoli and stir-fry 1 minute.
Add mushroom soup, sugar, and quail eggs; bring to a boil and season with salt and pepper. Stir in cornstarch slurry if needed to thicken, then serve.

intro: Ginataang Hipon na may Sitaw at Kalabasa is a lush coconut seafood stew with tender vegetables.
ingredients: 2 thumb-sized pieces ginger, cut into strips
steps: Combine coconut milk, garlic, onion, and ginger in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Add the Knorr Shrimp Cube, cover, and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add kalabasa and long green chili peppers, if using; cook for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and coconut cream, stirring until the liquid returns to a boil.
Add sitaw and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in fish sauce and black pepper, then cook 1 to 2 minutes.

intro: Taochiam Guisado is a savory beef noodle stir-fry with crisp vegetables and a light, glossy sauce.
ingredients: 250 g beef rump steak, thinly sliced
Beef marinade: 1 tbsp Chinese cooking wine
steps: Mix the beef with all marinade ingredients; cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a smoking-hot wok. Sear beef in one layer for about 1 minute per side, until 70–80% cooked; remove.
Boil Taochiam noodles according to the packet directions until al dente; drain well.
Over medium-high heat, stir-fry garlic, shallots, and ginger in oil until fragrant. Add carrot and beef; cook until carrot is lightly tender.
Add noodles, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, salt, and white pepper; toss until evenly seasoned.
Add stock, Chinese cabbage, and sugar snap peas. Stir-fry until vegetables are tender and the liquid reduces; finish with sesame oil.

intro: Pork Adobo with Potato is a deeply savory soy-vinegar braise with tender pork and sauce-soaked potatoes.
ingredients: 1 cup water, plus more as needed
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic about 30 seconds, until lightly browned.
Add pork and peppercorns; cook 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add soy sauce, water, and bay leaves; boil, cover, and simmer on low 40–60 minutes until pork is tender.
Add vinegar and boil 1 minute before stirring. Add potatoes, cover, and simmer 10–12 minutes until tender but intact.
Add salt only if needed; reduce the sauce a few minutes for a thicker adobo, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Corned Beef Sinigang is a tangy tamarind soup with tender beef and gently cooked vegetables.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs corned beef, cut into serving pieces
2 medium taro, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks
Tamarind paste or tamarind powder, to taste
Fish sauce or salt, to taste
steps: Simmer corned beef and water in a covered pot for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until fork-tender. Alternatively, pressure-cook on high for 40 minutes.
Add tomatoes, onion, and taro; cook about 5 minutes.
Add radish and eggplant; cook about 3 minutes, until radish starts to soften. Add okra and green chilies.
Stir in tamarind paste or powder to your preferred sourness. Season with fish sauce or salt.
Turn off the heat once vegetables reach your preferred tenderness, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Crisp, buttery Biscocho is an easy way to turn sponge cake into a sweet toasted snack.
ingredients: 1 store-bought 8 x 8-inch (22 x 22 cm) sponge cake base, cut into 1-inch-thick slices
steps: Heat the oven to 120°C (250°F) and arrange the cake slices in a single layer on baking sheets.
Brush both exposed sides generously with melted butter, then sprinkle the tops evenly with sugar.
Bake for 1 hour, until dry and crisp around the edges.
Cool completely on the trays before serving or storing airtight.

intro: Ginataang Sapsap is butterfish gently cooked in a spicy coconut sauce with spinach.
steps: Dissolve Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix in water and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until onion softens.
Pour in ginataan mixture, add Thai chilies, bring to a boil, and cook for 1 minute.
Add butterfish, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in vinegar and add long green pepper. Cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Add spinach, stir gently, and cook for 1 minute. Serve warm with rice.

intro: These chewy coconut macaroons bake into tender, sweet little dessert bites.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Whisk egg, melted butter, vanilla, and condensed milk until blended.
Fold in desiccated coconut and salt until evenly moistened.
Place mini baking cups in a mini muffin pan and fill each with about 1 tablespoon mixture.
Bake 10–13 minutes until lightly golden.
Cool before transferring to a plate and serving.

intro: A rich coconut chicken kare-kare with vegetables and savory bagoong alamang on the side.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Rub chicken with salt; rest for 5 minutes.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil over medium-high heat. Fry chicken for 2 minutes per side, then remove.
Add remaining oil; sauté garlic and onion until translucent. Stir in coconut milk, paprika, and turmeric; bring to a boil.
Return chicken and add the Knorr Chicken Cube. Cover, reduce to low-medium, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Stir in ground peanuts until smooth. Add eggplant and snake beans; cover and cook 5–8 minutes.
Add bok choy and cook 3 minutes. Season with pepper and serve with bagoong alamang.

intro: A chilled, citrus-cured tuna kilawin enriched with creamy coconut.
steps: Place the cubed tuna in a bowl.
Season with salt, pepper, ginger, onion, Thai chilies, jalapeños, and lime or calamansi juice; mix thoroughly.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to cure the tuna.
Stir in the coconut cream until evenly combined, then serve chilled.

intro: A savory mung bean stew with fish flakes, spinach, and bagoong isda.
ingredients: 1 1/4 cups mung beans, soaked overnight in 1 1/2 cups water
steps: Heat oil over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until the onion is soft.
Add fish flakes and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, then stir in tomatoes and cook for 1 minute.
Add mung beans, bagoong isda, and 1 cup water; cover and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes.
Season with pepper, stir in spinach and remaining water as needed, then boil for 5 minutes. Adjust bagoong isda and serve.

intro: A spicy, tangy Bopis na Manok with tender minced chicken offal and crisp vegetables.
steps: Pressure-cook gizzards in 6 cups water for 15 minutes after pressure is reached; drain and mince. Boil hearts for 15 minutes, then mince.
Warm oil over low heat with annatto seeds until red; strain the seeds. Heat the annatto oil in a pot.
Sauté onions, garlic, ginger, and tomato until soft. Add gizzards, cook 1 to 2 minutes, then add hearts and cook 2 minutes.
Add chilies, bay leaves, soy sauce, and water. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add vinegar and let it return to a boil before stirring; cook 5 minutes. Add carrots, daikon, and bell pepper; cook 3 minutes.
Season with patis and black pepper to taste, then serve hot.

intro: Sweet Saba bananas become a crisp, savory stuffed snack with seasoned pork.
ingredients: 1 bird's eye chili, seeded and finely chopped
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add pork, chili, and soy sauce. Stir-fry for 10 minutes, until the pork is fully cooked; season with salt and pepper.
Drain pork in a colander to remove excess liquid. Cut a lengthwise pocket into each banana and fill with pork.
Whisk flour and water smooth, then spoon the batter over the exposed filling.
Heat 2 inches of oil over medium heat. Fry bananas filling-side up for about 4 minutes, until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels, cool slightly, and serve.

intro: Sinigang na Isda sa Kamias with Miso is a tangy, mellow fish soup brightened by bilimbi and vegetables.
ingredients: 1 lb fish fillet or whole fish with bones
1 bunch kangkong (ongchoy or water spinach), cleaned and chopped
3 tbsp miso paste (shiromiso or yellow miso)
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a pot. Add tomatoes, onion, and kamias; boil for 1 minute.
Stir in miso paste, cover, and boil for 10 minutes.
Gently add the fish and cook over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, until opaque and cooked through.
Add long green peppers, string beans, and okra; cook for 5–7 minutes until tender.
Stir in fish sauce. Add kangkong, cover, turn off the heat, and let stand for 8 minutes before serving.

intro: Galunggong gently braised with tart dried kamias, aromatics, and pork fat.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub the galunggong with salt and let stand for 5 minutes.
Spread pork fat, kamias, onion, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and green peppers in a pot.
Arrange fish on top, season with pepper, add water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and cook for 15 minutes; season if needed, then uncover and reduce the sauce by half. Serve with rice.

intro: Tender Paksiyo Baboy Bisaya balances tangy cane vinegar, brown sugar, and sweet saba bananas.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg pork hock (pata), cut into serving pieces
1/4 cup brown sugar, or to taste
3 ripe saba bananas, sliced and pan-fried
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water, optional
steps: Heat oil in a deep pot over medium-high heat; brown the pata on all sides, then set aside.
Lower heat and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant. Return the pork.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Boil uncovered for 5 minutes without stirring.
Add water or broth until pork is covered. Cover and simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours, until fork-tender.
Add fried saba and simmer 10–15 minutes, until soft but intact. Stir in slurry if a thicker sauce is wanted.
Adjust with soy sauce, sugar, or salt, then serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: Insarabasab is smoky grilled pork brightened with calamansi, vinegar, and fresh aromatics.
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly or pork shoulder, sliced 2 cm thick
3 tablespoons sukang Ilocos or white vinegar
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1/2 cup calamansi juice or lemon juice
steps: Combine calamansi juice, garlic, and salt in a covered container; coat the pork thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Prepare a charcoal grill over medium-high heat and grill the pork until cooked through, allowing occasional flare-ups for smoky flavor.
Rest the grilled pork briefly, then chop it into small pieces.
Toss pork with vinegar, red onions, ginger, red chilies, and black pepper; serve warm.

intro: This rich Calderetang Baboy cooks pork belly in a savory tomato and liver sauce.
ingredients: 1 small red bell pepper, cut into small squares
1 small green bell pepper, cut into small squares
3 medium ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil and pan-fry carrot and potato for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly browned outside; set aside.
Pour off excess oil. Sauté onion, garlic, and tomatoes until soft.
Add pork belly and cook until lightly browned. Stir in tomato sauce and water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low heat for 45 to 60 minutes, until pork is tender.
Stir in liver spread until smooth. Add bell peppers and cook over medium heat until sauce reduces by half.
Season with salt and pepper, fold in carrot and potato, and cook 3 to 4 minutes before serving.

intro: Tender kangkong and squid balls are quickly cooked in a glossy oyster sauce.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add squid balls and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Stir in oyster sauce. Mix chicken broth and cornstarch until smooth, then pour into the pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, until the sauce thickens.
Add kangkong and cook 2–3 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Chicken Galantina is a festive roasted, deboned chicken filled with a rich pork and sausage stuffing.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine soy sauce, fish sauce, lemon juice, and black pepper. Rub inside the deboned chicken and marinate for 30 minutes.
Mix minced pork, Chinese sausages, Vienna sausages, bacon, carrot, capsicum, relish, raisins, flour, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Pack the filling into the chicken cavity, placing hard-boiled eggs through the center. Tie the legs and secure the cavity with kitchen twine.
Rub the chicken generously with softened butter and set it on a roasting rack.
Roast at 180°C for 45–60 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked. Rest briefly, cool slightly, and slice to serve.

intro: This Binondo-style fresh lumpia layers crisp vegetables, savory filling, noodles, peanuts, and sweet sauce.
ingredients: 1/3 cup dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced
1 cup vermicelli noodles, deep-fried, drained, and crumbled
1/2 cup toasted hoti or toasted nori sheets, crumbled
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic. Add pork and shrimp; stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Raise heat, add cabbage, carrot, beans, jicama, mushrooms, onion, and stock. Stir-fry until crisp-tender and nearly dry; drain well.
Combine water, soy sauce, fish sauce, Hoisin, 5 tablespoons sugar, vinegar, cornstarch, and white pepper; simmer on low until thickened.
Mix peanuts with remaining 4 tablespoons sugar. Separately combine vermicelli and toasted hoti or nori.
For each serving, overlap two wrappers, spread with sauce, then add noodle mixture, peanut mixture, and filling. Fold burrito-style and serve.

intro: Simply steamed blue crabs with salt for a clean, sweet seafood meal.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large pot.
Add salt and crabs, cover, and cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve immediately once the crab shells are bright and the meat is cooked through.

intro: Sizzling Tuna Sisig pairs browned tuna with creamy mayonnaise, peppers, and crunchy chicharon.
ingredients: 8 ounces tuna steak, cut into small cubes
steps: Toss tuna with Knorr Liquid Seasoning and let stand for 10 minutes.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a pan over medium-high heat; cook tuna until medium brown.
Add onion and sauté for 2 minutes, then add long green peppers, Thai chilies, and mayonnaise; cook 3 to 5 minutes, stirring.
Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder; cook for 3 minutes until well blended.
Heat a sizzling plate, melt the remaining butter over it, and coat the surface.
Transfer tuna sisig to the plate, stir gently for 1 to 2 minutes, and top with chicharon and extra chili if desired.

intro: Crispy Ulo is slow-cooked pig head broiled until crackling, served with thick homemade lechon sauce.
steps: Boil pig head in water for 10 minutes, covered; discard the water. Add fresh water, lemongrass, medium onion, and 5 bay leaves.
Cover and boil 60 to 90 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender. Cool, score the skin in crosshatches, salt, and air-dry at least 3 hours.
Rub with 2 tablespoons oil and broil in a turbo broiler at 400°F for 1 hour, until the skin is crisp.
For sauce, sauté liver in 3 tablespoons oil for 3 minutes; blend with 1 3/4 cups water until smooth.
Sauté garlic, large onion, remaining bay leaf, and peppercorns for 1 minute. Add liver purée, bring to a boil, then add vinegar and soy sauce.
After it reboils, stir in sugar. Blend for 1 minute, return to the pot, boil, season with salt, and thicken with breadcrumbs. Serve alongside the ulo.

intro: Royal Bibingka is a soft, chewy rice cake with a buttery, browned cheese topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Combine glutinous rice flour, sugar, and powdered coconut milk in a bowl.
Whisk in water, evaporated milk, and eggs until the batter is smooth and even.
Grease a baking pan with margarine, pour in the batter, cover with foil, and bake for 15 minutes.
Remove the foil, scatter cheddar over the top, cover again, and bake for 15 minutes.
Uncover, brush generously with margarine, and bake for 10–15 minutes until set and lightly browned.
Brush with margarine once more, then cool before slicing and serving.

intro: This easy ginisang upo lets spicy sardines enrich tender bottle gourd.
ingredients: 1 medium bottle gourd (upo), peeled and sliced
2 (5.5-ounce) cans spicy sardines in tomato sauce
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until aromatic.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft and saucy.
Add upo and sauté for 3 minutes.
Stir in sardines and their tomato sauce, then add water. Bring to a boil.
Cook 3–5 minutes until the upo is tender. Season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve.

intro: A hearty Beef and Tripe Pochero simmers rich meat with tomato sauce, saba, and vegetables.
ingredients: 1 lb ox tripe, cleaned and cut into squares
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Sauté onion and garlic, then cook tripe for 2 minutes.
Add beef and Chinese sausage; cook 2–3 minutes, until beef turns light brown.
Add broth and tomato sauce; bring to a boil. Cover and simmer 90 minutes, until beef and tripe are tender.
Add chickpeas, saba, and potatoes; cook 10–12 minutes, adding broth or water if needed.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, cook 2 minutes, then add bok choy and cook 3 minutes. Serve hot.

intro: Hototay is a clear, hearty Filipino-Chinese soup loaded with tender meats, vegetables, and egg.
ingredients: 1 cup woodear fungus, thinly sliced, rehydrated if dried
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a large saucepan and brown pork, gizzards, and liver. Add chicken and stock; bring to a boil.
Simmer for 25 minutes, until the chicken is tender. Remove all meats and strain the broth for clarity, if desired.
Flake the chicken and discard any inedible pieces. Sauté garlic and onion in oil in a clean pot.
Return strained broth and all meats to the pot; bring to a boil. Add carrot, cabbage, and woodear fungus; simmer 3 minutes.
Add sugar snap peas and simmer 2 minutes. Stir in sesame oil and season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls, top each serving with a freshly cracked egg and spring onions, and serve piping hot.

intro: Beef Chop Suey combines quickly seared tenderloin with colorful vegetables in a glossy savory sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
3 tsp cornstarch dissolved in 1/4 cup water
steps: Combine beef with baking powder, cooking wine, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, salt, and pepper; marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat a wok until very hot. Sear beef in oil in a single layer for 1 minute per side; work in batches and set aside.
Lower heat to medium and sauté garlic and onion. Raise heat, then stir-fry cabbage, celery, garlic sprouts, and cauliflower for 2 minutes.
Add mushrooms, carrot, and both bell peppers; stir-fry 2 minutes. Return beef and cook 1 minute.
Add beef stock and cornstarch slurry; bring to a rapid boil until thick. Season with sugar, fish sauce, and pepper.

intro: Crispy bangus, garlicky sinangag, and fried eggs make a classic breakfast plate.
steps: Rub bangus with 4 grams Maggi Magic Sarap and rest for 10 minutes.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil; fry garlic until golden, reserve it, then stir-fry rice for 3 minutes.
Season rice with 2 grams Maggi Magic Sarap and three-quarters of the garlic; cook 3 minutes and plate with remaining garlic.
Fry eggs to preferred doneness. Dredge bangus in flour, optionally mixed with cornstarch, then fry in remaining oil until crisp and golden. Serve together.

intro: Suam na Mais is a comforting chicken-and-corn soup finished with tender baby spinach.
ingredients: 500 g bone-in chicken thighs, cut into smaller chunks
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season chicken with salt and rest for 15 minutes. Slice kernels from cobs, reserving kernels and cobs.
Heat oil in a pot; sauté garlic and onion, then brown chicken on all sides.
Add stock, water, and corn cobs. Boil, skim foam, then simmer 25 minutes.
Strain broth into another pot. Flake chicken, then add it with corn kernels to the broth.
Boil and simmer 15 minutes, adding water if needed. Turn off heat, stir in spinach, and season with fish sauce and pepper.

intro: Spicy Laing slowly cooks dried taro leaves in rich coconut milk with pork and daing.
steps: Combine pork, daing, garlic, onion, ginger, coconut milk, and coconut cream in a pot over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, then lay in the dried taro leaves and Thai chilies without stirring.
Simmer gently for 40 to 50 minutes, until the liquid is nearly reduced and the coconut smells deeply fragrant.
Add long green chilies, salt, and pepper; gently stir and cook for 3 more minutes.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot.

intro: Surol is a comforting coconut chicken soup fragrant with lemongrass, ginger, and kalabo.
ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken (about 1.2 to 1.4 kg), cut into serving pieces
2 lemongrass stalks, trimmed and lightly bruised
1/2 green papaya or sayote (chayote), peeled and cut into wedges
1 teaspoon fresh Mexican oregano or kalabo
2 red siling labuyo or 1 long green chili, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine chicken, lemongrass, ginger, and onion in a large pot; add enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, skim off foam, then simmer until chicken is tender, about 1 hour for free-range chicken.
Stir in coconut milk and a little salt; keep at a gentle simmer without hard boiling.
Add tomatoes, papaya or sayote, oregano, and chilies; simmer until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in spring onions until wilted, and serve hot.

intro: Sopas de Upo is a light pork and bottle-gourd soup brightened with bagoong isda and greens.
ingredients: 1 bunch greens, such as kamote tops, spinach, or malunggay
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic, shallots, ginger, and tomatoes until fragrant.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned. Pour in water, bring to a simmer, and cook about 30 minutes until tender.
Stir in bagoong isda. Add upo and simmer for 7 minutes, until tender.
Season with salt and pepper as needed. Add greens just before turning off the heat.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with spring onions.

intro: A clear, comforting chicken soup with Saba bananas, potatoes, and bok choy.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add onion, peppercorns, and chicken broth; cover and return to a boil.
Add chicken gently and boil over medium heat for 30 minutes.
Add Saba bananas and potatoes. Cover and boil for 12 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Season with fish sauce. Add bok choy, cover, and let residual heat wilt it for about 5 minutes.
Serve hot with white rice.

intro: Creamy tofu sisig and cheesy garlic salmon create a generous shared meal.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Knorr Liquid Seasoning, Chili flavor
steps: Air-fry tofu for 15 minutes. Mix 1/2 cup mayonnaise, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, onion powder, pepper, and water for the sisig dressing.
Sauté onion in 2 tablespoons butter until soft; add peppers for 1 minute, then tofu for 30 seconds.
Melt remaining butter on a sizzling plate, add tofu sisig, and spoon over dressing.
Heat oven to 180°C. Salt salmon, spread with remaining mayonnaise mixed with lemon juice, and bake 12 to 15 minutes; top with Parmesan and toasted garlic.

intro: Steamed tikoy is chilled until firm, then egg-coated and pan-fried until golden.
ingredients: 4 packed cups glutinous rice, for rice method
1 cup water, plus extra for soaking
4 packed cups glutinous rice flour, for flour method
1/2 cake tikoy or nian gao, sliced 1 cm thick
steps: For the rice method, soak glutinous rice in water for 24 hours, drain well, then blend with sugar and 1 cup water until pancake-batter smooth.
For the flour method, whisk glutinous rice flour, sugar, and warm water until lump-free.
Pour either batter into a plastic-wrap-lined container and steam for 1 hour. Cool, then refrigerate overnight until firm.
Remove chilled tikoy from its mold and slice it, or use the prepared 1/2 cake tikoy slices.
Heat a little oil over medium-low heat. Dip each slice in beaten egg and fry, turning once, until both sides are golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

intro: Sweet Pusit Adobo is a quick squid adobo balanced by vinegar, soy sauce, tomatoes, and sugar.
steps: Heat a little cooking oil in a pan. Sauté garlic, sibuyas, and tomatoes for 3 minutes.
Add water, dahon ng laurel, and toyo; bring to a boil.
Add squid and cook for 1 minute.
Add sugar and sukang puti, then bring the sauce back to a boil.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately with rice.

intro: Pininyahang Baboy sa Gata combines tender pork, pineapple, coconut milk, and colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 20 oz canned pineapple chunks with juice
Salt and fish sauce, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add pork and sauté until light brown.
Add pineapple juice, half the pineapple chunks, and coconut milk. Cover and simmer on low until pork is tender, adding water if needed.
Add carrot and remaining pineapple; cook 7 minutes. Add bell peppers and cook 5 minutes.
Season with salt and fish sauce, then serve warm with rice.

intro: Cebu-style steamed rice layers egg fried rice with a glossy pork and prawn topping.
ingredients: 3/4 cup green peas, fresh or frozen
steps: Tenderize pork, season with salt and baking powder, and marinate 15 minutes; coat lightly in corn flour and deep-fry over medium heat for 2 minutes until golden.
Sauté shallots and both garlic additions in oil. Add wine, soy sauce, and stock; boil, add pork, and cook 5 minutes.
Stir water with tapioca starch; add prawns, peas, and slurry, then boil 3 minutes until thick. Finish with sesame oil and salt.
Stir-fry rice and salt in hot oil for 1 minute; scramble eggs in a center well and mix through. Pack into bowls, top with sauce, and steam on high 7 to 10 minutes.

intro: Inutak is a layered coconut and ube rice cake with a golden coconut-cream top.
ingredients: Vanilla or ube ice cream, for serving
steps: Whisk glutinous rice flour, sugar, salt, vanilla, and coconut milk until lump-free; divide evenly between two bowls.
Mix purple yam powder and enough food coloring into one portion for a deep purple mixture.
Cook each mixture separately in nonstick pans over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until thick, smooth, and slightly oily.
Line a 7-inch baking pan with banana leaf. Press in the purple layer, then the white layer, smoothing each evenly.
Pour coconut cream over the top. Bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, then broil at 230°C until golden brown.
Cool before slicing and serve with vanilla or ube ice cream.

intro: Chicken and Ham Sopas is a creamy, hearty noodle soup made for a filling family meal.
ingredients: 1/2 pound wide egg noodles or elbow macaroni
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a deep pot over medium heat; sauté onion for 2 minutes, then celery for 1 minute.
Add ground chicken and break it apart while cooking 3 to 5 minutes; add ham and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in broth and water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes.
Add potato and carrots; cook 5 minutes, then add noodles and cook until almost tender.
