Stir in evaporated milk and thyme; gently simmer 5 to 7 minutes without boiling hard.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve warm.

intro: Lobo Lobo makes small silver fish into crisp, savory pan-fried omelette cakes.
steps: Mix eggs, rice flour, cornstarch, garlic, shallot, salt, and white pepper in a bowl.
Fold in the lobo-lobo until evenly coated.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon in individual portions and fry for about 3 minutes, until golden and crisp underneath.
Turn carefully and cook 2 minutes more until both sides are golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

intro: A rich turmeric coconut beef stew brightened with palapa and fresh chillies.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg meaty beef neck bones or beef ribs
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté shallots until fragrant; add palapa and cook until aromatic.
Add beef and cook until no longer pink and its released liquid has mostly evaporated; stir in turmeric.
Add water, boil, then simmer gently for about 2 hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Stir in coconut milk and capsicum; cook 10 minutes. Season, then fold in spring onions and chillies before serving hot with rice.

intro: Binagoongang Okra with Chicharon Bits keeps tender-crisp okra in a savory tomato bagoong sauce.
ingredients: 1 cup crushed chicharon, plus more for garnish
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté shallots until softened.
Add garlic and tomatoes; cook 1 minute, crushing the tomatoes gently to release their juices.
Stir in sautéed bagoong and crushed chicharon. Add a little water only if the mixture needs moisture.
Bring the sauce to a boil and adjust seasoning if needed. Add okra and sauté 4 to 5 minutes, until cooked but still crisp.
Remove from heat and top with extra chicharon before serving.

intro: Grilled Liempo Sisig turns smoky pork belly and creamy chicken liver into a sizzling, rich dish.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season chicken liver with 1/2 tsp garlic powder, salt, and pepper; rest for 10 minutes.
Melt 1 tbsp margarine in a pan. Fry liver over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side; set aside.
Process grilled liempo until minced. Mince the onion separately, then process fried liver with mayonnaise until soft.
Melt the remaining margarine; sauté onion until soft. Add liempo and cook for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the liver mixture; cook 8–12 minutes until nearly dry. Season with remaining garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat a sizzling plate with 1/2 tbsp margarine, add sisig, and top with egg and green onion. Serve with rice.

intro: Sigarilyas gising-gising is a creamy, mildly spicy pork and coconut milk dish.
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion begins to soften.
Add ground pork and sauté for 5 minutes, until browned.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil. Stir in sigarilyas and long green peppers.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and cook 30–35 minutes, until liquid reduces by half.
Stir in fish sauce and pepper. Cook uncovered a few minutes until creamy but still saucy, then serve.

intro: Flaky hopia pastries can be filled with smooth munggo paste or prepared Ube Halaya.
ingredients: 1 cup red or yellow mung beans, boiled
1 tbsp sugar dissolved in 1/4 cup water
1 egg, beaten and diluted with 1/4 cup water
steps: For munggo filling, cook soaked beans until soft. Add sugar, blend smooth, then cook with condensed milk and 1/4 cup flour until thick; cool.
For Dough 1, mix 1 cup flour, sugar water, 1/4 cup shortening or lard, and salt just until combined. Form a ball and cover.
Mix 1/2 cup flour and 1/4 cup shortening into smooth Dough 2. Roll Dough 1 into a rectangle and Dough 2 to two-thirds its size.
Place Dough 2 over two-thirds of Dough 1; letter-fold, roll, and repeat twice. Rest 5–10 minutes, roll, halve lengthwise, roll into cylinders, and cut 24 pieces.
Roll each piece thin, fill with munggo or Ube Halaya, seal, and shape. Bake pinched-side up at 350°F for 15–20 minutes.
Turn pastries seam-side down, flatten lightly, brush with egg wash, and bake 5–10 minutes until lightly browned. Cool on a rack.

intro: Chicken liver, gizzards, quail eggs, and vegetables simmer in a creamy sauce.
ingredients: 500 g chicken gizzards, cut into bite-size pieces
300 g chicken livers, cut into bite-size pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring water and gizzards to a boil, then simmer 45 minutes until tender. Drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion. Add gizzards and liver, browning all sides.
Add chicken stock, carrot, and peas. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add quail eggs and cream; simmer 5 minutes until heated through.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Hardinera is a colorful Lucban-style steamed pork loaf studded with fruit, sausage, and decorative toppings.
ingredients: 1 large green or red bell pepper, diced
1 cup Vienna sausage, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1 small green bell pepper, cut into rings
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in oil over medium heat. Add pork and chorizo; cook until opaque and lightly browned.
Add tomato paste, water, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer over low heat for 30–40 minutes, until pork is tender.
Uncover and reduce to a thick sauce. Add diced carrot, bell pepper, pineapple tidbits, relish, raisins, cheese, and Vienna sausage; cook until dry.
Cool the mixture completely, then mix in breadcrumbs and beaten eggs.
Oil a llanera, line with banana leaf or wax paper, arrange pineapple, carrot flowers, eggs, bell pepper rings, and raisins, then pack in filling.
Cover with foil and steam for 30 minutes until set. Cool briefly, invert onto a plate, and lift away the mold.

intro: Wok-fried Chao Fan combines pork belly, squid balls, eggs, and seasoned day-old rice.
ingredients: 3 spring onions, white and green parts separated and chopped
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Season pork with salt and pepper, then stir-fry until golden.
Add squid balls, garlic, and spring onion whites; stir-fry 1 minute.
Fluff rice, add it with corn, and stir-fry 4 minutes. Push rice aside, scramble eggs, chop them up, and combine.
Add peas and spring onion greens; add Maggi Savor, soy sauce, fish sauce, Sriracha, curry powder, and sesame oil. Stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes and season if needed.

intro: Ginisang Labong is a savory bamboo-shoot sauté with pork, prawns, and fish sauce.
ingredients: 3 cups bamboo shoots (labong), cut into strips
steps: Heat oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat; sauté garlic and onion until aromatic and softened.
Add ground pork and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up as it browns.
Add prawns and cook until pink on all sides.
Stir in labong and fish sauce; season with salt and pepper, then cook until bamboo shoots are tender.
Add green onion just before turning off the heat and transfer to a serving dish.

intro: Sarciadong Itlog turns hard-boiled eggs into a quick, savory tomato and egg sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, tomatoes, and bell peppers for 3–5 minutes.
Pour in broth and bring to a boil. Stir in fish sauce and black pepper.
Slowly add beaten egg while stirring to distribute it through the sauce; cook 3 minutes.
Add scallions and hard-boiled eggs; cook 2 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and top with parsley.

intro: Ginataang Manok is a creamy coconut chicken stew with green papaya, bok choy, and chilies.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant. Add chicken and brown on all sides.
Add chicken stock and 1 cup coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for 25 minutes.
Add remaining coconut milk, green finger chilies, and papaya; simmer 10 minutes until papaya begins to soften.
Add bok choy and coconut cream; simmer 5 minutes until chicken is cooked through and greens wilt.
Season with fish sauce or salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Atchara is a crisp, sweet-sour green papaya pickle that improves after a few days in the refrigerator.
steps: Toss shredded green papaya with 1/4 cup salt and let stand for 1 hour.
Rinse the papaya thoroughly in a colander, then wrap it in muslin and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix papaya with carrot, capsicum, ginger, and raisins in a bowl or clean containers.
Bring cane vinegar, water, sugar, and 1 tsp salt to a boil. Simmer 5 minutes without stirring.
Pour the hot brine over the vegetables, seal tightly, and refrigerate. Marinate for at least 2 days before serving.

intro: A bright talbos ng kamote salad balances tangy dressing, salted egg, and crisp dilis.
ingredients: 1 large bunch kamote leaves (sweet potato leaves)
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pick leaves from stems, rinse under cold water, and drain well.
Steam leaves for about 2 minutes until wilted, or blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds.
Plunge leaves into iced water for 30–40 seconds, then drain thoroughly.
Combine leaves, duck egg, tomatoes, and red onion in a bowl.
Whisk vinegar, fish sauce, olive oil, sugar, salt, and pepper. Toss with the salad, top with dilis, and serve.

intro: Nasing Marangle brings crispy pork belly, dried pinakbet, and bagoong fried rice onto one platter.
ingredients: 1 can lemonade soda, such as 7-Up or Sprite
1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 squash or buttercup, cut into 1-inch pieces
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Salt pork generously and refrigerate at least 1 day. Rinse, then pressure-cook with crushed garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, soy sauce, soda, and enough water to cover for 20 to 30 minutes.
Dry the tender pork, chill at least 12 hours, then deep-fry skin-side down in hot oil until golden and crisp. Cube it.
Sauté minced garlic, onion, and tomatoes; add squash, okra, beans, shrimp stock, sugar, and 2 tablespoons bagoong. Cover and cook on low 15 minutes; season.
Fry minced garlic in 2 tablespoons oil until golden, add rice and 4 tablespoons bagoong, and stir-fry 5 minutes. Gently mix in vegetables for 3 minutes, then top with pork.

intro: Kinamatisang Salmon pairs crisp-seared salmon with a chunky, basil-scented tomato sauce.
ingredients: 3 large salmon steaks, 200 to 250 g each
2 cans Italian-style chopped tomatoes, 400 g each
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season salmon with salt and pepper. Sear in a heavy pan over high heat with near-smoking oil until golden and crisp on both sides; set aside.
Add more olive oil if needed, then sauté garlic and onion until soft. Add fresh tomatoes, sugar, and basil; cook until softened.
Stir in canned tomatoes and oregano. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add red wine vinegar and season with salt and pepper. Place salmon in an ovenproof dish and cover with sauce.
Bake at 230°C for 10 minutes, until salmon is cooked through, then serve immediately.

intro: Sardines with Misua and Patola is a fast, comforting soup made from pantry sardines and tender gourd.
ingredients: 400 g canned sardines in tomato sauce
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot and sauté garlic and red onion until fragrant.
Add sardines with their tomato sauce and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water and patola. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add misua and simmer for 2 minutes, until the noodles are tender.
Season with fish sauce, salt if needed, and black pepper. Turn off the heat and serve.

intro: Ginisang Papaya is a light shrimp sauté with unripe papaya and malunggay leaves.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add parsley and papaya; sauté 3 minutes. Cover and cook 3–5 minutes over medium heat.
Uncover, add shrimp, and cook 1–2 minutes until just opaque.
Add malunggay and cook 3 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Bok Choy Adobo is a quick vegetable dish with tangy adobo sauce and crisp fried garlic.
steps: Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat; fry garlic and bay leaves until garlic is light to medium brown.
Remove and reserve half the garlic, leaving the remainder in the pan.
Add bok choy and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce and vinegar, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in sugar, pepper, and salt if needed; cook 1 minute, then top with reserved fried garlic.

intro: Menudo Sulipena is a slow-braised oxtail stew enriched with chorizo, chickpeas, and tomatoes.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season oxtails with salt and pepper. Brown them on all sides in olive oil in a deep heavy pot; remove.
Add more oil if needed and sauté garlic and onion. Add bacon scraps and chorizo; cook 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook 30 seconds. Return oxtails with chopped tomatoes, paprika, and chili flakes.
Add enough water to cover the meat. Bring to a boil, lower heat, cover, and simmer 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add bell pepper, carrot, chickpeas, and remaining tomato paste; simmer 30 minutes more, until oxtails are fork-tender.
Season to taste, stir in brandy, and serve.

intro: This sweet, meaty Filipino-style spaghetti is finished with a generous layer of cheese.
ingredients: 500 g UFC Sweet Filipino Style Spaghetti Sauce or Del Monte Filipino Style Spaghetti Sauce
1 1/2 cups Jufran Banana Ketchup or UFC Banana Ketchup
Cooked spaghetti pasta, cooked 2 minutes beyond package directions
Grated quick-melt cheese, such as Eden Cheese, for garnish
steps: Heat oil in a large saucepan over low heat. Sauté onion until soft, then add garlic and cook fragrant without browning.
Add beef and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in spaghetti sauce, banana ketchup, and condensed milk until combined.
Add liver spread and hotdogs. Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes, then turn off heat.
Place pasta on a platter, spoon over sauce, and garnish generously with grated cheese.

intro: Tinola sa Miso is a deeply savory chicken soup enriched with yellow miso and leafy greens.
ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken thighs and legs
1 bunch finger chilli leaves or capsicum leaves
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add chicken and brown all sides over high heat for 2 minutes.
Add stock, bring to a boil, and simmer 45 minutes for free-range chicken, or about 20 minutes for regular chicken.
Stir in miso and simmer 15 minutes. Add chilli leaves and spinach, cover for 1 minute, then season with fish sauce and pepper.

intro: Ginataang Tulingan is an oily fish stew simmered in coconut milk, vinegar, eggplant, and fresh chilies.
ingredients: 1 kg skipjack tuna or another oily fish, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a large nonstick wok. Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Add fish and vinegar. Simmer over high heat for up to 5 minutes, until vinegar reduces by about half.
Add coconut milk, coconut cream, siling labuyo, and eggplant; bring to a boil.
Lower to medium heat and simmer 12–15 minutes, until eggplant is tender and sauce thickens.
Season with black pepper and fish sauce, then serve.

intro: Chicken Sotanghon Soup with Patola is a clear, golden noodle soup with tender chicken and squash.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat annatto oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic until lightly golden, then cook onion until soft.
Add chicken and stir until lightly browned on all sides.
Add water and chicken powder. Bring to a boil, skim foam, then simmer 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add sotanghon and cook about 3 minutes, stirring gently to prevent clumping.
Add patola and cook 2 minutes until tender. Season with fish sauce and pepper; garnish with roasted garlic and green onions.

intro: Pinakbet sa Gata combines tender vegetables and squid in a savory coconut and bagoong sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until the onion softens.
Add squid and sauté for 2 minutes, then remove it and set aside.
Add squash and sauté for 3 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add okra, sitaw, bitter melon, and eggplant; stir and cook for 8 minutes.
Return squid to the pot with bagoong and pepper; cook 5 minutes, then serve.

intro: Pandan and lemongrass perfume this simple, deeply aromatic roasted chicken.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Rub salt all over the chicken, including the cavity.
Mix garlic, onion, bay leaves, and peppercorns; stuff into the cavity, followed by pandan leaves and knotted lemongrass.
Place chicken on a roasting rack or in a roasting pan.
Roast for 90 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Rest 10 minutes.
Discard cavity aromatics, carve, and serve.

intro: Fresh calamansi juice is a bright, sweet-tart iced drink for warm days.
steps: Wash calamansi thoroughly and halve them crosswise.
Set a strainer over a pitcher and squeeze the juice from 20–24 calamansi through it.
Add sugar and half the water; stir until sugar dissolves completely.
Stir in remaining water, then add the remaining calamansi halves and lightly crushed mint, if using.
Fill each glass with 1/2 cup ice and pour in the calamansi juice.

intro: Chao Pat Chin is a colorful seafood-and-chicken stir-fry finished with cashews and glossy sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Blanch broccoli in rapidly boiling water for 90 seconds; drain and plunge into ice water.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Increase to high heat; stir-fry carrot and baby corn for 2 minutes.
Add prawns and squid; cook 1 minute, then add capsicum and chicken and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Mix oyster sauce, soy sauce, stock, sugar, and cornstarch; add to the wok and bring to a boil.
Add broccoli, simmer over high heat for 1 minute, season with fish sauce and pepper, then toss in cashews.

intro: Tuna jaw simmers in a bright tamarind broth with tender vegetables.
ingredients: 2 cups string beans (sitaw), cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Bring water to a boil; add onion and tomatoes and cook until tender.
Add tuna jaw and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in sinigang mix, chillies, and eggplant; simmer 3 minutes. Add okra and sitaw and cook 3 minutes.
Fold in kangkong and fish sauce, turn off heat, cover, and let residual heat wilt the greens. Serve hot.

intro: Dynamite Lumpia is a crunchy, cheesy finger-chili snack served with a creamy ketchup dip.
ingredients: 12 large finger chilies, halved and seeded
12 strips soft cheddar cheese, such as Kraft Eden or Colby
steps: Mix mayonnaise and ketchup in a small bowl; set aside as the dip.
Place one cheese strip between each halved finger chili. Wrap securely in a spring roll wrapper and seal tightly.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C.
Fry the Dynamite Lumpia until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels, cool briefly, and serve with the mayonnaise-ketchup dip.

intro: Dinaldalem is a tangy pork and liver stew with chickpeas and bright red capsicum.
steps: Marinate pork liver in 1/2 cup cane vinegar for 1 hour, mixing every 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until the onion softens.
Add pork belly and stir-fry over high heat until no longer pink.
Add chickpeas, remaining vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Boil, then simmer uncovered over medium heat for 25 minutes.
Drain liver, then add it with capsicum. Simmer 5 minutes, adjust with water and fish sauce, and serve with cracked pepper.

intro: Taisan is a light Filipino chiffon loaf with a tender crumb and buttery finish.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (320°F) and grease two 9 x 5-inch loaf pans.
Sift flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Beat egg whites with cream of tartar on high speed; gradually add sugar and beat to medium peaks.
Whisk yolks, vanilla, evaporated milk, oil, and water; gently mix into the dry ingredients until smooth.
Fold the meringue into the batter, divide between pans, and bake 25 to 30 minutes until a tester comes out clean.
Cool the loaves, then brush their tops with melted butter before serving.

intro: Ginisang Monggo with Vegetables is a hearty mung bean stew with pork, shrimp paste, and garden vegetables.
ingredients: 1 Chinese eggplant, sliced into serving pieces
3 cups water, plus more as needed
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak mung beans overnight, then drain. Sauté half the garlic, onion, and tomatoes in 2 tablespoons oil until soft; add beans and sauté 2 minutes.
Add 3 cups water and the Pork Cube. Cover and simmer over low-medium heat 45 minutes, adding water as needed, until beans are tender.
In another pot, sauté remaining garlic, onion, tomatoes, and ginger in remaining oil. Add pork and cook about 5 minutes until light brown.
Add 3/4 cup water, cover, and simmer until pork is tender and liquid nearly evaporates. Stir in shrimp paste and cook 1 minute.
Add calabaza for 2 minutes, then eggplant, bitter melon, okra, and string beans for 2 minutes. Add 1/2 cup water and bring to a boil.
Stir in cooked mung beans and simmer 3 minutes. Season cautiously with pepper and salt, then serve with rice.

intro: Fresh dulong is gently cured in citrus with ginger and siling labuyo.
ingredients: 1–2 teaspoons bird's eye chili (siling labuyo), minced
steps: Gently combine dulong with salt and black pepper.
Mix in ginger and siling labuyo until evenly distributed.
Squeeze in lemon or calamansi juice and gently stir.
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes, until the citrus has cured the fish.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve chilled.

intro: Paksiw na Pata is a tender pork leg braise with soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, and dried banana blossoms.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg pork leg, cut into 1 1/2- to 2-inch sections
steps: Heat oil in a wok and brown pork leg on both sides; remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic in the wok until golden and fragrant.
Return pork. Add water, soy sauce, half the vinegar, peppercorns, and bay leaves; boil, then simmer over low heat for 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add remaining vinegar, brown sugar, and dried banana blossoms. Simmer 15–20 minutes more.
Season with salt and serve hot.

intro: Tortang Dulong is a crisp-edged silverfish omelet that cooks quickly in a skillet.
ingredients: 250 g dulong or silverfish, washed and drained
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Whisk eggs, flour, and cornstarch together in a bowl.
Fold in dulong and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Spoon in portions of mixture.
Pan-fry until cooked through and crisp around the edges. Serve with rice and sweet chili sauce or ketchup.

intro: Crispy liempo tops tangy sinigang rice with a side of light vegetable tempura.
ingredients: 22 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Original Mix
1 cup cake flour, plus more for dredging
steps: Boil pork in 3 cups water, covered, over low-medium heat for 30 minutes. Add sinigang mix and boil 15 minutes; remove and cool pork.
Wash rice, then cook it in strained sinigang broth until tender. Marinate pork in fish sauce 15 minutes, coat with cornstarch, and fry until golden and crisp.
Sauté onion 30 seconds in 3 tablespoons oil; cook beans 1 1/2 minutes. Add green pepper and cooked rice, stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes, then season with pepper and paprika.
Heat 2 cups oil to 360°F. Mix yolk, cold water, ice, and cake flour briefly until lumpy; flour and batter vegetables, frying 2 to 3 minutes, or spinach under 1 minute. Plate rice, pork, and tempura.

intro: Gambas is a quick, spicy garlic shrimp dish in a lightly winey tomato sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Toss shrimp with lemon juice in a non-reactive bowl and marinate 15 minutes.
Heat oil over high heat; sauté garlic and shallot, then add bell pepper, shrimp, and cayenne. Stir-fry 2 minutes.
Mix wine and tomato purée, add to the pan, and boil while stirring for 4 to 5 minutes until shrimp are cooked.
Season with salt and pepper; garnish with parsley and crispy fried garlic.

intro: Pinakbet Tagalog brings lechon kawali and mixed vegetables together in a savory bagoong broth.
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Sauté onion and garlic with ginger, if using, until onion softens.
Add half the lechon kawali and sauté 1 minute. Pour in water, bring to a boil, then add the Shrimp Cube.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes. Add tomatoes and bagoong alamang, cover, and cook 3 minutes.
Add kalabasa and optional kamote; cook 7 minutes. Add sitaw, okra, ampalaya, and eggplant; cover and cook 5 minutes.
Season with black pepper, add remaining lechon kawali, heat through, and serve.

intro: Pancit Macao is a rich wok noodle dish loaded with meats, prawns, greens, and savory sauce.
steps: Soak fresh yellow noodles in boiling water for 1 minute; drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat; stir-fry beef for 2 minutes, then remove.
Add more oil if needed; sauté shallots and garlic, then stir-fry Chorizo de Macau, cabbage, and spring onions for 1 minute.
Mix cornstarch, stock, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and hoisin; pour into the wok and boil until thickened.
Add noodles, beef, char siu, and prawns; stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes until noodles absorb the sauce.
Season with white pepper and serve hot.

intro: Creamy chicken macaroni sopas is a comforting, hearty Filipino soup.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups fresh milk or 1 (14-ounce) can evaporated milk
steps: Bring water to a boil. Add chicken and cook over low-medium heat for 45 minutes, until tender.
Remove chicken, reserve the cooking water, cool chicken, then shred the meat and discard bones.
Melt butter in a clean pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, carrot, and celery for 3 minutes; add chicken and ham for 2 minutes.
Add chicken broth and reserved cooking water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add macaroni and cook 15 minutes, adding water if needed. Stir in milk and cabbage, if using, and bring to a boil.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Ginisang Repolyo with Giniling is a quick cabbage sauté with savory pork and sweet peppers.
ingredients: 1 small red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 small green bell pepper, cut into strips
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic until light brown. Add onion and tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add ground pork and sauté until light brown and no longer pink.
Pour in chicken broth, bring to a boil, cover, and cook 15 minutes.
Add both bell peppers and cabbage. Cover and cook 5 to 8 minutes, until cabbage is tender but not mushy.
Stir in fish sauce and black pepper; cook 2 minutes and serve.

intro: Pancit is a substantial noodle dish layered with pork, Chinese sausage, fried savory sides, and colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 green bell pepper, sliced into strips
steps: Sear pork belly until medium brown. Add 1 1/2 cups water, boil, then simmer until tender and much of the fat has rendered; remove pork.
Fry squid balls and kikiam in rendered fat for 2–2 1/2 minutes until browned; remove. Sauté bell peppers, carrots, and cabbage for 2 minutes; remove.
In a clean pan, sauté Chinese sausage in 3 tbsp oil for 30 seconds. Add onion and garlic; cook until onion softens.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and 6 cups water; boil, then lower heat. Stir in Maggi Magic Chicken Cubes.
Add egg noodles and cook 2 minutes, tossing occasionally. Season with black pepper.
Mix cornstarch with 1/4 cup water and stir into the pan. Toss in pork, sausage, squid balls, kikiam, and vegetables; serve.

intro: Scallop Chop Suey pairs quickly seared scallops with crisp vegetables in a light savory sauce.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, cut into wide strips
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until onion begins to soften.
Sear scallops for 1 1/2–2 minutes per side; remove and set aside.
Cook carrot and cauliflower for 3 minutes. Add snow peas, cabbage, and bell pepper; cook 3–5 minutes.
Add broth and bring to a boil, then add quail eggs and cornstarch mixture. Stir until thickened.
Return scallops, toss gently for 30 seconds, season with salt and pepper, and serve warm.

intro: Ginisang pechay with pork and shrimp is a fast, savory weeknight stir-fry.
ingredients: 2 packs bok choy, about 500 g or 6 stalks
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until soft.
Add pork and cook until browned and it has rendered some fat.
Add tomato and cook until softened.
Add shrimp and bok choy; stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes.
Add shrimp stock, bring to a boil, and simmer over high heat for 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Turn off heat and serve.

intro: Palitaw are soft rice cakes coated in coconut, toasted sesame, and sugar.
ingredients: 1 cup water, plus more for boiling
steps: Toast sesame seeds in a dry nonstick pan, stirring until golden. Soak desiccated coconut in coconut milk until hydrated, then place coconut, sesame, and sugar on separate plates.
Bring about 2 litres water to a boil. Mix glutinous rice flour and 1 cup water into a soft, workable dough.
Flatten tablespoon portions of dough and boil about 6 at a time until they float.
Lift out with a slotted spoon; coat first in coconut, then sesame seeds, and finally sugar. Serve warm.

intro: Ginataang Sitaw at Kalabasa with Fried Tilapia combines creamy vegetables with crisp salted fish.
steps: Wash tilapia thoroughly, pat dry, and rub salt over the fish and inside the cavities.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat; fry tilapia until each side is golden brown and crisp, then set aside.
In another pan, sauté garlic and onion until fragrant; add kalabasa and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add string beans and cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 minutes.
Dissolve Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix in water, pour into the pan, cover, and bring to a boil.
Cook 5 to 7 minutes until vegetables are tender, then serve with fried tilapia.

intro: Kakaibang Tokwat Baboy combines grilled pork belly and crisp tofu in a lively calamansi-soy-vinegar dressing.
steps: Steam pork belly for 45 minutes, then cool. Mix calamansi juice with 3/4 cup soy sauce and marinate pork in a resealable bag for 1 hour.
Cut tofu into smaller pieces, rub with oil, and air-fry at 400°F for 17 minutes. Cool and cut into cubes.
Grill marinated pork belly until fully cooked. Let cool slightly, then slice into serving pieces.
Combine red onion, chilies, 1/4 cup soy sauce, vinegar, lemon-lime soda, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Add tofu and grilled pork; toss gently until coated. Serve as an appetizer or main dish.

intro: Nido Soup is a delicate Filipino-Chinese chicken broth enriched with bird's nest, egg white, ham, and corn.
ingredients: 100 g dried bird's nest, or 1 bundle bean threads plus 1 tsp honey for a mock version
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak dried bird's nest in water for 12 hours, then drain and rinse clean. For the mock version, soak bean threads for 30 minutes.
Flake cooked chicken very finely. Sauté onions in a little oil until translucent.
Add chicken stock, boil, and simmer 5 minutes. Strain through a fine sieve into another pot.
Bring stock to a boil. Add bird's nest, or bean threads and honey, plus corn and ham; simmer 30 minutes.
Stir in chicken, Chinese cooking wine, and dissolved cornstarch. Fold in lightly beaten egg whites and simmer 3 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Golden baked pork empanadas have a flaky crust and a sweet-savory filling.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil and brown pork. Add onion and cook soft; add raisins, Worcestershire sauce, and broth, then cover and cook over medium heat 10–12 minutes.
Add peas, carrot, and potato; cover and cook 5–8 minutes. Stir in brown sugar, salt, and pepper; cook 1 minute and cool.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Pulse flour and salt with butter until crumbly; pulse in egg and milk gradually until dough forms.
Divide dough into two disks, chill at least 20 minutes, then roll out and cut circles.
Fill each circle with 1–2 tablespoons pork mixture, fold, seal, and crimp with a fork. Arrange on a parchment-lined tray.
Bake 15 minutes. Brush with egg white mixed with 2 tablespoons milk; bake 5–7 minutes more until medium brown. Cool slightly and serve.

intro: Menudong Nagcarlan turns tender tripe and vegetables into a creamy peanut-rich stew.
ingredients: 600 g beef tripe, cleaned, pre-cooked, and cubed
150 g green beans, cut into short pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add tripe and brown on all sides. Add stock and bay leaves, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 25 minutes.
Add potato, carrot, chayote, and peanut butter; simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add green beans and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in cream, season with fish sauce and pepper, and serve.

intro: Kulambo is a chewy coconut rice cake topped with fragrant latik on banana leaves.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon anise seeds or fennel seeds
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour, coconut milk, coconut cream, sugar, and anise or fennel seeds until smooth.
Cook in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat, stirring continuously, until the mixture becomes sticky.
Stir in coconut oil and continue cooking for about 15 minutes until a cohesive dough forms.
Line a 10-inch flat bowl or bilao with banana leaves and press in the rice cake evenly.
Top with latik, cool until set, and slice to serve.

intro: Special Nilupak is a rustic cassava mash served with ube, cheese, coconut, and condensed milk.
ingredients: 1 kg cassava, peeled and cut into short lengths
Ube flavoring, to taste and desired color
1 cup shredded processed cheese, such as Eden or Cheezee, or mild cheddar
steps: Grease a baking dish with butter or margarine. Steam cassava 35 to 40 minutes until very tender; drain and cool.
Remove and discard the tough stringy cores. Pound cassava in batches with a mortar and pestle until mashed.
Mix cassava with condensed milk, butter, and salt until creamy. Divide in half and mix ube flavoring into one portion.
Pound each portion again briefly for a coarse, rustic texture. Press plain and ube mixtures into opposite halves of the prepared dish.
Smooth the top, portion, and serve with cheese, coconut, margarine, and extra condensed milk.

intro: Pinaputok na Tilapia bakes mango-and-tomato-stuffed fish until juicy, then broils it golden.
steps: Cut 2–3 deep slits on each side of each tilapia. Rub each side with about 1 teaspoon salt and rest 15 minutes.
Mix mango, tomato, onion, ginger, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Stuff the fish cavities with the mixture.
Wrap each fish completely in foil. Bake at 370°F for 20 minutes.
Open the foil, brush fish with oil, and broil at about 510°F for 15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Serve with toyomansi.

intro: Comida Tsina is a fragrant rice-cooker meal topped with marinated chicken, sausage, and mushrooms.
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
6 shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced
400 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
2 spring onions, white parts only, thinly sliced
steps: Mix brown sugar, cornstarch, marinade oyster sauce, soy sauce, rice wine, sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Add chicken and marinate 1 hour.
Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic, ginger paste, and spring onion whites for 30 seconds.
Stir-fry chicken over high heat for 1 minute. Add mushrooms and Chinese sausage; stir-fry 1 minute, then remove from heat.
Place rice and chicken stock in a rice cooker. When it begins boiling, spread chicken mixture on top, cover, and complete the cook cycle.
Rest on warm for 10 minutes. Boil sauce oyster sauce, water, and sugar; serve over rice with crispy fried garlic.

intro: Kalabasang Ukoy makes crisp vegetable fritters from sweet squash, carrots, and scallions.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fish sauce, or sea salt for a vegetarian option
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Whisk flour, cornstarch, eggs, cold water, fish sauce or sea salt, garlic, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Fold in buttercup squash, carrots, spring onions, and red onion until fully coated.
Heat enough oil for shallow-frying in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1/2 cup batter and flatten it with a spatula.
Fry until light golden and crisp underneath, flip, and fry the second side until equally crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

intro: Fork-tender beef cheeks are chilled, sliced, and quickly stir-fried with ginger and spring onions.
ingredients: 1 bunch spring onions, sliced with white and green parts separated
2 tablespoons soy sauce, or to taste
Optional: 1 teaspoon oyster sauce or a splash of rice wine
steps: Cover beef cheeks with water in a pot. Add salt, pepper, ginger slices, and crushed garlic; gently simmer 2–3 hours, skimming impurities, until fork-tender.
Refrigerate cooked beef overnight until firm, then slice thinly.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry minced garlic and julienned ginger until fragrant; add spring onion whites briefly.
Add sliced beef and stir-fry 2–3 minutes. Add soy sauce, pepper, and optional oyster sauce or rice wine; toss to coat.
Add spring onion greens, toss quickly, and serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: Deremen is a dense, chewy coconut rice cake perfumed with pandan and finished with tender young coconut strips.
steps: Soak deremen in 1 1/2 cups water for 1 hour, then drain.
Combine coconut milk, sugar, pandan leaves, and salt in a nonstick wok over medium heat. Bring slowly to a boil, stirring constantly.
Add drained deremen and young coconut strips. Remove pandan leaves.
Lower heat to medium-low and stir continuously as the mixture thickens and dries.
Once the coconut cream is absorbed, keep stirring and cooking for 35–40 minutes until very sticky and dry.
Turn off the heat. Press into a banana-leaf-lined platter about 1 1/2 inches thick, then refrigerate before serving.

intro: Crispy Pancit Canton Noodles are topped with a thick crab-and-corn sauce, chicken, seafood, and vegetables.
ingredients: 37 g Knorr Crab and Corn Soup
steps: Blanch carrot, bok choy, and shrimp separately, beginning with carrot for 1 minute; cool each in ice water for 2 minutes and drain.
Heat oil in a wok and deep-fry pancit canton for 30–45 seconds, tossing gently until crisp. Drain and arrange on a platter.
Sauté garlic and white green onion, then cook chicken for 2 minutes. Add shrimp and carrot; stir-fry 30 seconds.
Mix Crab and Corn Soup with water, add to the pan, and cook while stirring until thickened.
Add quail eggs, oyster sauce, and sesame oil. Arrange bok choy around noodles, spoon sauce over, and serve warm.

intro: Avocado Float is a chilled graham dessert layered with fluffy avocado cream and fresh avocado slices.
ingredients: 2 packs all-purpose cream, 500 ml each, chilled
steps: Chill all-purpose cream overnight or freeze 30 minutes. Line an 8-inch or 6-inch square dish with baking paper, if desired.
Heat sugar and water over medium heat just until dissolved and bubbling; remove from heat and cool.
Cube one avocado and blend smooth with half the condensed milk. Thinly slice the remaining avocado and keep slices in cold water.
Whip chilled cream until doubled in volume. Beat in remaining condensed milk, then beat in avocado purée until smooth.
Layer Graham crackers, syrup, one-quarter of the cream, and avocado slices; repeat for 3 layers, ending with cream. Brush exposed avocado with syrup.
Cover and refrigerate 3 to 5 hours, until crackers are soft and the float is set; garnish with crushed Graham or avocado before serving.

intro: Tender kangkong is coated in a glossy oyster sauce with toasted garlic.
ingredients: 1 bunch kangkong (ongchoy or water spinach), cleaned
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Separate kangkong leaves from stalks and cut stalks into 2-inch pieces.
Whisk beef broth, oyster sauce, and cornstarch until smooth.
Heat oil over medium-high heat; cook stalks for 2 minutes. Add sauce mixture and toasted garlic, stirring for about 1 minute until thickened.
Add leaves and optional red pepper flakes; cook 1 to 2 minutes until wilted. Season and finish with optional sesame seeds.

intro: Inihaw na Liempo at Pusit brings together pineapple-tenderized pork belly and stuffed grilled squid.
steps: Combine pork belly and crushed pineapple in a resealable bag; refrigerate overnight, then discard the pineapple.
Mix 1 tablespoon Knorr Liquid Seasoning, soy sauce, juice of 1/2 lemon, banana ketchup, and garlic; reserve one-quarter for basting and marinate pork in the rest for 3 hours.
Peel squid, then coat with sugar, baking soda, and juice of 1/2 lemon; rest 1 hour and rinse well.
Mix tomatoes, onion, pepper, and 2 teaspoons Knorr Liquid Seasoning; stuff squid and secure with toothpicks.
Grill pork over medium-high heat, turning and basting each time, until cooked through and lightly charred.
Grill stuffed squid just until opaque and cooked through; avoid overcooking, then serve with the pork.

intro: Spicy Chicken in Coconut Milk (Ginataang Manok) is a turmeric-tinted chicken stew with chilies and malunggay.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Heat coconut cream in a cooking pot. Add ginger, garlic, and red onion; stir and bring to a boil.
Add chicken and the chicken cube, then let the coconut cream return to a boil.
Add red chilies, green peppers, and turmeric. Cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until chicken is tender.
Stir in malunggay leaves and cook for 5 minutes.
Add fish sauce and cook for 2–3 minutes. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.

intro: Binignit is a creamy coconut dessert stew of root vegetables, fruit, landang, and bilo-bilo.
steps: Rinse landang until the water runs clear, then boil in water, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Add sweet potatoes and taro with coconut milk; bring to a gentle simmer until tubers are tender.
Mix glutinous rice flour with enough water to form small bilo-bilo, then drop them into the simmering pot.
Add saba bananas and jackfruit; cook until the bananas soften.
Stir in coconut cream and sugar; simmer until thickened to your preferred consistency.
Fold in cooked sago just before serving.

intro: This airy steamed puto cake is topped with salty egg and melted cheese.
ingredients: 2/3 cup fresh milk, plus more as needed
steps: Line an 8- or 9-inch removable-bottom pan with parchment. Sift flour, baking powder, and 1/4 cup sugar together.
Beat egg whites until bubbly; add cream of tartar if using, gradually beat in remaining sugar, then beat to medium-firm peaks.
Mix milk into dry ingredients to a pancake-like batter. Whisk in one-quarter of meringue, then gently fold in the rest in batches.
Pour into pan, add half the cheese, and steam over a very gentle simmer on very low heat for 10 minutes. Add remaining cheese and salted egg; steam 5 to 10 minutes until a toothpick is clean.

intro: This classic tocino breakfast plate pairs caramelized pork with salted egg and fresh tomato.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pan or pot.
Add oil and pork tocino. Cook over medium heat until the water completely evaporates.
Fry tocino in the remaining oil until browned, turning to cook both sides evenly.
Plate with salted egg and chopped tomato. Serve with rice and spicy vinegar dip.

intro: La Paz Batchoy layers noodles and pork offal in a robust three-stock broth.
ingredients: 300 g pork belly, cut into small pieces
150 g pork liver, cut into small pieces
2 pork hearts, cut into small pieces
steps: Boil pork belly and hearts for 5 minutes; drain and rinse cold. Separately boil liver 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat oil in a clean pot. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion is translucent.
Add pork, beef, and shrimp stocks, pork belly, hearts, pepper, sugar, soy sauce, and shrimp paste. Boil, then simmer 30–40 minutes until tender.
Add liver, season with fish sauce, and simmer 10 minutes.
Cook noodles according to package directions and divide among bowls.
Ladle boiling broth and meat over noodles. Top with chicharon, fried garlic, spring onion, and a fresh egg; serve immediately.

intro: Pork Giniling with Quail Eggs is a comforting tomato-braised pork dish with peas, carrots, and raisins.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion until soft. Add ground pork and cook until light brown.
Stir in garlic powder and raisins. Add tomato sauce and beef broth.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes.
Add carrot and green peas, cover, and cook 7 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Add quail eggs, stir gently, cook 1 minute, and serve.

intro: Tibok Tibok is a smooth carabao's milk pudding finished with fragrant latik.
ingredients: 2 cups fresh carabao's milk, or fresh cow's milk
Latik (toasted coconut milk curd), for topping
steps: Mix sugar and cornstarch, then whisk in 1/4 cup milk until smooth and dissolved.
Warm remaining milk over low heat until simmering.
Strain in the cornstarch mixture and stir constantly until thick and the first bubble breaks the surface.
Immediately pour into a greased container, tap to release air, and cool until set. Chill if desired, cut diagonally, and top with latik.

intro: Ginataang Kamoteng Kahoy is tender cassava simmered in a lightly sweet coconut sauce.
ingredients: 500 g yucca, peeled, cleaned, and cut into 2-inch sections
steps: Place cassava in a small pot and add enough water to barely cover. Bring to a boil and cook over medium heat about 10 minutes, until slightly tender.
Add coconut milk, palm sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil over high heat and cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Avoid overcooking so the cassava holds its shape. Remove cassava carefully and set aside.
Reduce the coconut liquid further if a thicker sauce is preferred, then spoon it over the cassava to serve.

intro: Cheesy Baked Macaroni combines beefy tomato pasta with a creamy cheese topping.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain. Meanwhile, sauté garlic, onion, and bell peppers in oil for 3–5 minutes.
Add beef and cook until browned. Stir in bouillon, tomato sauce, salt, and pepper; boil, then cook 5 minutes.
Melt butter over medium-low heat. Stir in flour, then whisk in milk until smooth and thick; melt in quick-melt cheese.
Toss macaroni with meat sauce, a few tablespoons white sauce, and some cheddar. Transfer to a baking pan and cover with remaining white sauce.
Bake at 375°F for 15–18 minutes until golden. Rest a few minutes before serving.

intro: Imbaliktad is a fiery, fast-cooked beef dish sharpened with cane vinegar, ginger, and chilies.
ingredients: 500 g beef rump steak, cut into very thin strips
1 thumb-sized ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a wok over very high heat until hot. Add oil and heat until smoking.
Add beef, garlic, onion, ginger, chilies, and spring onion. Stir-fry continuously for 2 minutes.
Add cane vinegar and let it come to a boil while keeping the heat high.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve immediately.

intro: Sotanghon Overload is a festive vermicelli platter piled with chicken, pork, chorizo, and quail eggs.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil pork belly in 1 quart water for 40 minutes; cool, slice, and reserve 1 1/2 cups pork stock.
Soak vermicelli in 1 quart water for 8 minutes, then drain.
Slowly fry garlic in the oil until golden; strain, reserving both toasted garlic and garlic-infused oil.
Heat 3 1/2 tablespoons garlic oil in a wok; sauté onion and scallion whites, then chicken for 40 seconds.
Add chorizo and pork; cook 2 minutes, then add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and reserved stock and bring to a boil.
Remove meats; add annatto, carrot, bell peppers, cabbage, and vermicelli. Cover and cook on low for 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper; toss with half the scallions, quail eggs, and half the meats. Plate, then top with remaining meats, scallions, and toasted garlic.

intro: These adobo pork chops are first browned, then braised in soy, vinegar, garlic, and spices.
steps: Heat oil in a wide deep pan over medium-high heat. Fry pork chops 3–5 minutes per side, until light to medium brown.
Add garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves; cook 2–3 minutes until garlic is lightly browned.
Add water and soy sauce, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 40–50 minutes until liquid reduces by half, adding water if necessary.
Add vinegar, bring to a boil, stir, and cook uncovered 10 minutes.
Adjust salt if needed and serve with steamed white rice.

intro: Ginisang Upo at Kalabasa is a simple pork sauté with tender squash and fresh upo.
ingredients: 2 cups kalabasa or butternut squash, cubed
steps: Heat a pot and sear pork belly until it releases its fat.
Add onion, garlic, and tomato; sauté until onion softens.
Add water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low to medium heat until pork is tender and liquid evaporates; add water if needed.
Add kalabasa and sauté over high heat for 3–5 minutes. Add upo and sauté 2 minutes.
Season with patis and pepper. Add up to 1/2 cup water for a saucier dish, then serve.

intro: Tender lengua is simmered with corn in a silky mushroom-cream sauce.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pressure-cook ox tongue in water for 45 minutes until tender. Cool, peel away the outer layer, and slice into serving pieces.
Melt butter over low-medium heat; cook garlic until beginning to brown, then add onion and cook until tender.
Add sliced lengua and sauté 2 minutes. Add water and Beef Cube, bring to a boil, then add corn and cover for 20 minutes.
Stir in cream of mushroom and all-purpose cream; cook 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper before serving.

intro: Manga at Bagoong is a simple sweet-tart mango snack with salty fermented shrimp paste.
steps: Wash and peel the semi-ripe mangoes.
Slice the mango flesh into wedges or thin pieces.
Spoon bagoong alamang into a small dipping bowl.
Serve the mango immediately and dip each piece into bagoong alamang.

intro: Baby squid is briefly cooked in a buttery, spicy garlic sauce with a thick glossy finish.
steps: Bring water to a boil. Blanch scored baby squid for 1 minute, then immediately remove and reserve 1/3 cup blanching water.
Melt butter in a wok over medium heat. Sauté crushed garlic until fragrant and golden.
Add oyster sauce, banana ketchup, brown sugar, and red chilies; cook briefly to combine.
Whisk cornstarch into reserved blanching water. Add to wok, bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes until thickened.
Add squid and cook 1–2 minutes, just until tender and cooked through.
Garnish with spring onion and crunchy garlic; serve with chili garlic oil.

intro: Paella Negra (Arroz Negre) is a striking squid-ink rice dish topped with shrimp, squid, and lemon.
ingredients: 5 medium squid, cleaned and sliced crosswise
1 1/2 cups white wine, such as Chardonnay or Pinot Grigio
2 1/2 cups fish broth or clam juice
4 Roma tomatoes, peeled and finely diced
steps: Heat olive oil in a paellera or wide pan over medium heat. Fry shrimp 1 minute per side; remove. Stir-fry squid 1 to 2 minutes; remove.
Sauté garlic and onion for 30 seconds. Add tomatoes and cook until onion is soft and translucent.
Add half the bell peppers and rice; stir for 1 minute. Pour in wine, fish broth, and tinta de calamar, then bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, adding water if needed, until rice is nearly tender.
Top with shrimp, squid, lemon wedges, and remaining bell peppers. Cover and cook 5 minutes, until rice is perfectly cooked.

intro: Adobong Talong is tender fried eggplant finished in a balanced soy-vinegar adobo sauce.
steps: Trim eggplant stems. Cut each eggplant into 3-inch pieces, then halve each piece lengthwise.
Heat 4 tbsp oil over medium heat. Fry eggplant in batches for 2–3 minutes per side until lightly browned and tender; remove.
Heat remaining oil in the same pan. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds.
Add soy sauce, water, cracked black pepper, and bay leaves; bring to a boil. Add cane vinegar and boil 1 minute without stirring.
Stir in brown sugar and simmer 2 minutes. Return eggplant, toss gently to coat, and simmer 2 minutes until it absorbs sauce.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with warm rice.

intro: Fried bangus and string beans simmer in a spicy, savory coconut sauce.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season bangus with Maggi Magic Sarap, coat evenly with flour, then fry in hot oil until light to medium brown on both sides. Set aside.
Using 2 tablespoons frying oil, stir-fry beans for about 90 seconds; remove. Add 2 tablespoons oil and sauté garlic until browning, then onion and ginger until soft.
Add shrimp paste and Thai chillies; sauté 30 seconds. Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Return bangus and beans, lower heat, and simmer 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve with rice.

intro: Sinanglay na Tilapia gently cooks stuffed fish in coconut milk, pechay, lemongrass, and chilies.
ingredients: 2 large or 3 medium whole tilapia, cleaned and trimmed
steps: Cut a long incision along each tilapia back through the stomach cavity to create a pocket.
Combine onion, tomato, ginger, garlic, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Stuff the mixture into each fish.
Wrap each fish in 2–3 pechay leaves and tie securely with lemongrass.
Arrange fish in one layer in a wok or deep skillet. Add coconut milk and chilies, season with remaining salt, cover, and cook over medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
Uncover and cook 5 minutes to reduce the liquid, then serve with hot rice.

intro: Arroz Caldo with Tokwa is thick ginger chicken congee topped with crisp tofu and green onions.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat; cook ginger, garlic, and onion for 3 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until medium brown.
Stir in patis, rice, water, and chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Simmer for about 45 minutes, stirring occasionally so the rice does not stick, until thick and porridge-like.
Top with cubed fried tofu and green onions; season at the table with pepper, extra patis, and chili flakes if desired.

intro: Aligue Rice is a richly savory fried rice that makes excellent use of chilled jasmine rice.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a wok over medium-high heat and melt the butter.
Add garlic and sauté until golden and fragrant.
Stir in aligue and cook for 1 minute.
Add rice, breaking apart clumps and tossing until the aligue coats every grain.
Add spring onions and stir-fry for 5 minutes; season with salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Kamaro is a Pampanga dish of edible mole crickets simmered with garlic, then pan-fried with tomato and onion.
ingredients: 1 cup cleaned food-grade mole crickets (kamaro), legs and wings removed
steps: Rinse the prepared kamaro and drain well.
Bring the water or broth and crushed garlic to a simmer; add the crickets and cook for 5 minutes.
Drain the crickets. Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and soften the onion and tomato for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the crickets and pan-fry, stirring, until browned and crisp and cooked through, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Season lightly with salt and serve hot.

intro: This early-style adobo slowly braises pork in cane vinegar, garlic, and peppercorns.
ingredients: 1½ kg pork belly or shoulder, cut into thick chunks
½ cup cane vinegar, preferably sukang Iloko or sukang tuba
steps: Rub pork with salt and rest for at least 1 hour; refrigerate overnight for a deeper cure.
Line an earthenware or heavy pot with lard, then layer pork, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Pour in vinegar without stirring. Bring to a boil uncovered over low heat.
Cover and simmer undisturbed for 2 hours, until the pork is fork-tender. Serve hot with rice or boiled root crops.

intro: A comforting beef soup with tender kalabasa and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 1/2 medium butternut squash or calabaza squash, cubed
2 medium yellow onions, cut into wedges
steps: Bring the water and beef broth to a boil in a covered pot.
Add beef, onions, and peppercorns; simmer over low-medium heat for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until beef is tender.
Add kalabasa and cook for 5 minutes.
Add long beans and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in pechay and patis; cook for 1 minute, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Rellenong Manok is a festive roast chicken filled with savory pork stuffing and whole eggs.
steps: Season the chicken inside and out with salt and pepper; leave at room temperature for 2 hours.
Combine the pork, carrot, peas, chorizo, breadcrumbs, onion, spring onions, relish, and beaten eggs.
Fill the chicken, placing the hard-boiled eggs down the center; pull the skin over the opening and secure it.
Roast on a rack at 180°C for 1 hour 35 minutes, basting every 20 minutes with melted butter mixed with lemon juice.
Rest for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

intro: Tangy salmon-head sinigang gets a bright, fruity note from pineapple.
ingredients: 1 small can (227 g) pineapple chunks in juice, not syrup
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine onion, tomatoes, green chilies, water, and pineapple juice in a pot; bring to a boil.
Add salmon heads, pineapple chunks, and sinigang mix; simmer 5 to 10 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Add spinach and simmer for 2 minutes until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve immediately.

intro: A creamy, crunchy Bangus Sisig that turns flaked milkfish into a lively sizzling-style dish.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon labuyo or Thai chili, chopped
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat; cook the onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the ginger, if using, and cook over low-medium heat for 2 minutes.
Stir in the flaked bangus, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and soy sauce; cook for 5 minutes.
Add chicharon, scallions, and chili; stir for 3 minutes until heated through.
Fold in mayonnaise, transfer to a serving plate, and serve immediately.

intro: Afripaya is a tomato-rich beef rib stew brightened with young papaya and capsicum.
ingredients: 1 kg water buffalo or beef ribs, cut into sections
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add ribs and brown them on every side.
Stir in tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, and basil; cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add carrot and simmer 10 minutes, then add papaya and tomato paste; simmer 15 minutes.
Add capsicum, season with fish sauce or salt and pepper, and cook just until heated through.

intro: Creamy matcha sago is chilled with strawberries, nata de coco, and soft almond jelly.
ingredients: 1 cup green nata de coco, drained
½ cup small sago or tapioca pearls
¼ cup condensed milk, adjusted to taste
steps: Boil the sago for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally; cover off heat for 5 minutes, then rinse cold and drain.
Whisk matcha with a small splash of warm water until smooth.
Whisk cream, milk, condensed milk, and matcha until lightly frothy; stir in the cooked sago.
Fold in strawberries, almond jelly, and nata de coco. Chill at least 30 minutes, then serve cold.

intro: A savory Ilocano vegetable stew enriched with crisp bagnet and bagoong isda.
ingredients: ½ bundle string beans, cut into 2-inch lengths
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pan, then stir in the bagoong isda and return it to a boil.
Add kamote, followed by okra, ampalaya, eggplant, string beans, tomato, and onion; simmer 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Add bagnet and simmer 5 minutes until heated through. Serve hot.

intro: Manila Clam and Mussel Tinola is a light ginger broth filled with sweet shellfish and greens.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté ginger, fennel, and onion until the onion turns translucent.
Add water, bring to a boil, cover, and boil over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add mussels and Manila clams; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in spinach, red pepper flakes, and salt; cook for 1 minute until spinach wilts.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

intro: This Salmon Sisig combines broiled salmon, creamy mayonnaise, fresh aromatics, and crisp chicharon.
steps: Coat the salmon with cooking oil and broil at 390°F for 12 minutes; cool slightly, then flake.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a pan with the oil over medium heat. Stir-fry salmon for 30 seconds.
Add half the onion, green onion, and chili; stir for 2 minutes. Add garlic powder and Knorr Liquid Seasoning; cook 1 minute.
Stir in mayonnaise for 30 seconds, then mix in chicharon. Transfer to a bowl and let cool slightly.
Toss with remaining onion and green onion; season with black pepper. Melt remaining butter on a hot metal plate, add sisig, and top with chicharon and chili.

intro: Saucy bihon noodles are topped with a sunny-side egg and banana ketchup.
ingredients: 1 small carrot, peeled and thinly sliced
Lemon or lime wedges, for garnish
steps: Poach chicken in the stock until cooked through; shred it and reserve the stock.
Heat 1 to 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over medium-high heat; sauté garlic until fragrant and golden.
Stir-fry onion, carrot, and Chinese cabbage for 3 minutes; add fish sauce and soy sauce, then set aside with chicken.
Bring reserved stock to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook bihon for about 8 minutes until soft.
Return chicken and vegetables; toss over medium-high heat until hot and lightly saucy, adding water if needed.
Serve topped with sunny-side-up eggs, banana ketchup, spring onions, and lemon or lime wedges.

intro: Slow-grilled St. Louis ribs make a smoky centerpiece with ensaladang talong and bagoong guisado.
steps: Mix the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt, lemon pepper, and brown sugar into an even rub.
Coat the ribs thoroughly with the rub and let them stand for 10 minutes.
Heat the grill to 250°F over low heat; grill the first side for 1 1/2 hours.
Turn the ribs and grill for 1 hour more, until tender and deeply browned.
Rest for 15 minutes, slice, and serve with ensaladang talong, bagoong guisado, and rice.

intro: Sizzling Tofu Sisig delivers crisp tofu in a creamy, tangy sisig-style dressing.
steps: Press tofu dry, freeze it overnight in a resealable bag, thaw, and press again to remove remaining moisture.
Heat oil over medium-high heat and fry tofu on both sides until golden and crisp; cool, then chop finely.
Mix mayonnaise, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, onion powder, lemon juice, and green onion for the dressing.
Sauté red onion until softened; add tofu and liver spread, then cook for 1 minute.
Add bell pepper and dressing, stirring until coated. Serve on a heated sizzling plate.

intro: Nilat-an na Tiil ng Baboy is tender pork leg slowly braised with saba and ube.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg pork leg, cut into sections
steps: Mix the annatto powder, pepper, garlic, soy sauce, cane vinegar, sugar, salt, and bay leaves for the marinade.
Coat the pork leg evenly with the marinade, cover, and marinate for 2 hours.
Bring the pork to a slow boil over medium heat, then reduce to the lowest heat.
Simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until tender, adding the water if the cooking liquid dries out.
Add ube and simmer 15 minutes; add saba and simmer another 15 minutes before serving.

intro: This chilled crema de fruta layers ladyfingers, fruit cocktail, vanilla custard, and a clear fruit gel.
ingredients: 1 large can fruit cocktail, drained with juice reserved
steps: Warm the milk until hot but not boiling. Whisk ⅓ cup sugar, cornstarch, and yolks smooth, then gradually whisk in milk.
Cook over low heat, whisking constantly, for 10–12 minutes until the custard coats a spoon; stir in vanilla and cool.
Stir gelatin and 1 tbsp sugar into water; boil over medium heat until dissolved. Remove from heat, stir in reserved juice, and cool.
Line a 6-by-8-inch or 7-by-7-inch pan with ladyfingers. Spread over half the custard and fruit cocktail.
Repeat the ladyfinger, custard, and fruit layer; add cherries if using. Gently pour gel over the fruit and chill at least 1 hour.

intro: Creamy pancit combines bihon, miki, chicken, liver, and chicharon.
ingredients: 250 g pancit miki or thick yellow noodles
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil chicken breast in stock until tender; chop it and reserve the broth.
Season liver with salt and pepper; pan-fry in oil until browned, then slice and set aside.
Sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant; add chicken and stir-fry with 1 tablespoon soy sauce.
Add broth, remaining soy sauce, bihon, and miki; simmer for 3 minutes.
Add sayote, if using, and carrot; simmer 3 minutes. Add cabbage and evaporated milk; simmer 2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper; garnish with liver, chicharon, and spring onions.

intro: Soft steamed Siopao-Asado buns hold a savory prepared Chicken Asado Filling.
steps: Combine warm water, 1 tablespoon sugar, and yeast; stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, and baking powder. Add yeast mixture and shortening; mix into dough.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 5 minutes until smooth. Oil the dough, cover, and rise 1 hour or until doubled.
Deflate dough, divide into 8 to 10 portions, and flatten each into a 4- to 5-inch round with a thicker center.
Add 1 tablespoon Chicken Asado Filling to each round, gather and twist the edges closed, then rest 5 to 10 minutes.
Set each bun on paper, space apart in a steamer, and steam for 15 minutes. Keep covered off heat for 5 minutes before uncovering; cool slightly.

intro: This Cebu-style dessert pairs gingered puto maya with sikwate and a creamy peanut topping.
steps: Rinse and drain rice, then bring it and 1 cup water to a boil. Reduce to a simmer.
Add ½ cup coconut cream and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until absorbed; the rice should remain undercooked.
Steam the rice in a mound. Whisk remaining coconut cream with sugar, salt, and ginger; pour about ½ cup over rice every 5 minutes, three times total.
Boil 1 cup water, whisk in tablea until smooth, then add milk and sugar; heat gently without a rolling boil.
Simmer peanut butter with evaporated milk until smooth. Serve puto maya with sikwate, peanut sauce, and condensed milk.

intro: Tinumtuman is a creamy coconut stew of bamboo shoots and clams with a gentle chile warmth.
ingredients: 1 cup shelled clams, steamed in 1 cup water, liquid reserved
steps: If using non-fresh bamboo shoots, boil them in water for 30 minutes until tender; drain, cool, and squeeze dry.
Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic, ginger, chiles, and onion until fragrant.
Add bamboo shoots, coconut milk, and reserved clam liquid; boil, then simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes until reduced.
Stir in coconut cream and clams, season with fish sauce and pepper, and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: This hearty beef batchoy pairs tender meats with fresh miki noodles and crisp toppings.
ingredients: 1 lb bung (pork large intestine), cleaned and boiled until tender
½ lb pork liver, cut into strips
steps: Slice the prepared bung into serving pieces. Heat oil in a large pot and sauté garlic, onion, and celery until the onion softens.
Stir in pepper, beef tendon, and shank; cook 1 minute. Add bung and water, boil, then cover and simmer 2–3 hours.
Bring to a medium boil, add liver, and cook 10–15 minutes until cooked through. Stir in fish sauce and add water if needed.
Blanch miki noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Divide noodles among bowls; add meats and hot broth. Top with toasted garlic, scallions, and chicharon.

intro: Papaitan is a deeply savory beef offal soup balanced by ginger, chilies, citrus, and bitter bile.
ingredients: 1/2 pound beef, thinly sliced and chopped
steps: Bring 4 cups water and 1 tablespoon salt to a boil; add tripe and small intestine, then simmer 35–50 minutes until tender.
Remove and slice the tripe and intestine; discard their cooking water.
Heat oil in a clean pot. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger, then add beef, heart, tripe, and intestine; cook 3–4 minutes.
Add remaining salt and black pepper; stir for 1 minute. Add remaining water, boil, then simmer 40 minutes.
Stir in bile and simmer 5 minutes. Add finger chilies and lemon or calamansi juice; simmer 3 minutes and serve hot.

intro: Sinangag is a straightforward Filipino garlic fried rice with crisp golden garlic throughout.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Use clean hands to separate the cold rice into loose grains.
Heat a large wok over high heat and add enough oil to lightly coat its surface.
When the wok begins to smoke, lower the heat and fry garlic until golden brown.
Add rice and stir-fry continuously for 10–15 minutes until hot and evenly seasoned with garlic.
Season with sea salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Creamy Ginisang Munggo gets deep smoky flavor from tinapa, hibe, and chicharon.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rinse mung beans, combine with broth in a pot, and simmer 30 to 35 minutes until soft and creamy.
Heat oil over medium heat; sauté garlic until lightly golden, then cook onion until softened.
Add hibe and cook briefly until fragrant. Stir in tinapa and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sautéed mixture to the mung beans and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in chicharon, reserving some for topping if desired. Add spinach and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Betamax is a simple street-food style skewer of grilled cubes of congealed chicken or pork blood.
ingredients: 500 g prepared congealed chicken or pork blood, cut into cubes
steps: Cut prepared congealed blood into bite-size, even cubes.
Thread the cubes onto soaked bamboo skewers, leaving a little space between pieces.
Heat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers, turning gently, for 8 to 10 minutes until hot throughout and lightly charred at the edges.
Serve immediately while warm.

intro: Juicy prawns and lychees are tossed in a glossy sweet-and-sour sauce with crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 500 g large prawns, peeled and deveined
½ of a 500 g can lychees, drained and halved
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
¼ cup ketchup or banana ketchup
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Season prawns with salt and pepper, then coat lightly with 2 tablespoons cornstarch. Fry in hot oil until pink and lightly crisp; set aside.
Mix ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and water. Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion in the same pan until fragrant.
Add capsicums and carrot; cook 2 minutes until slightly tender but crisp. Pour in sauce and bring to a simmer.
Stir in cornstarch slurry until glossy and thick. Toss in prawns and lychees, simmer 2 minutes, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: Rich coconut pork and long beans make this fiery Bicol Express Gising-gising satisfying with rice.
steps: Heat oil in a wok or pan and sear pork belly until it releases enough fat.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, and chili peppers; cook until the onion softens. Sauté bagoong alamang for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk, cover, and bring to a boil. Stir in the Knorr Pork Cube.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat until pork is tender. Add long green beans and cook 5 minutes.
Season with black pepper and serve hot.

intro: This richly savory pinapaitan uses ampalaya, tender offal, and sour kamias.
ingredients: 2 bitter melons (ampalaya), seeded and finely chopped
10 oz beef tripe, boiled and chopped
10 oz beef heart, boiled and chopped
12 oz beef small intestine, boiled and chopped
steps: Boil chopped ampalaya in water for 3 minutes; drain and reserve the cooking water.
Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until softened.
Add tripe, heart, and intestine; cook for 5 to 7 minutes. Add liver and cook for 1 minute.
Add vinegar and bring to a boil. Pour in the strained ampalaya water, cover, and simmer on low until tender.
Add kamias and chilies; cook for 15 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Lightly coated crablets fry into a crunchy, chile-tossed snack.
steps: Mix cornstarch, flour, baking soda, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Toss crablets in the coating, drizzle with lime juice, and mix gently again.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C. Fry fresh crablets for 4 to 5 minutes, or frozen crablets for 7 to 8 minutes.
Drain well, toss with chopped green chilies, and serve.
For extra crispness, cool first, then refry at 180°C for 1 to 2 minutes until golden.

intro: Buko ice candy is a creamy frozen coconut treat made for hot afternoons.
steps: Stir coconut water, fresh milk, condensed milk, and vanilla in a large bowl or pitcher until smooth.
Mix in the shredded young coconut; finely chop it first if a smoother texture is preferred.
Use a funnel to fill ice-candy bags, press out excess air, and tie each bag securely.
Freeze overnight until solid, then serve straight from the freezer.

intro: Sotanghon with Sayote and Giniling is a light, colorful noodle soup with pork and chayote.
steps: Warm the oil with annatto seeds, stirring until orange and shimmering; turn off the heat, steep briefly, then strain out the seeds.
Use the annatto oil to brown the garlic, then sauté the onion and lower portions of the green onions until softened.
Add ground pork and cook until browned; stir in 2 tsp fish sauce.
Add 2 cups water, cover, boil, then cook over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining water, bring to a boil, then add chayote and sotanghon; cook 8 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, garnish with chopped green onion, and serve hot.

intro: Ginisang Monggo with Inihaw na Liempo pairs tender mung beans with citrusy grilled pork belly.
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups mung beans, soaked in 2 cups water
6 ounces pork, sliced into small pieces
steps: Combine pork belly, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, and lime or calamansi juice; marinate at least 1 hour.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a pot; sauté garlic, onion, and tomato. Add sliced pork and cook 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Add soaked mung beans, soaking water, 2 cups water, and pork cube. Cover and cook over medium heat 30–40 minutes until beans are soft.
Stir in malunggay, black pepper, and fish sauce; cook 5 minutes. Transfer monggo to a serving bowl.
Grill liempo for 3 minutes per side, basting with Knorr Liquid Seasoning, lime juice, and 2 tablespoons oil until cooked through. Serve with monggo.

intro: This golden grilled cheese gives steamed pork embutido a fresh basil and tomato finish.
ingredients: 3 slices pork embutido, steamed Filipino meatloaf
steps: Layer cheese, embutido, basil, and tomatoes on one bread slice, then close with the second slice.
Melt half the butter in a medium pan over medium heat and add the sandwich.
Cook 60–90 seconds, pressing gently, until the underside is golden brown.
Add remaining butter, turn the sandwich, and cook until the second side is golden. Halve and serve.

intro: Chicken Wings Inasal pairs a tangy, turmeric-scented marinade with glossy annatto margarine basting.
steps: Mix black pepper, cayenne, ginger, garlic, brown sugar, vinegar, 7-Up, turmeric, and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Add the wings, cover, and marinate for 5 to 8 hours.
Thread the wings onto bamboo skewers.
Mix margarine, annatto powder, salt, and 1 tbsp lemon juice for the basting mixture.
Grill the wings while basting, cooking 6 to 8 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Transfer to a plate and serve.

intro: This rich Copycat KC Turon layers saba, ube halaya, macapuno, and sweetened red beans in crisp wrappers.
steps: Place one banana half on each spring roll wrapper.
Top each with 1 heaping tablespoon ube halaya, 1 tablespoon macapuno, 1 tablespoon sweetened red beans, and 1 teaspoon brown sugar.
Roll each wrapper tightly around the filling and seal the edge securely.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying over medium heat. Fry turon gently until evenly golden brown.
Drain on a wire rack, cool briefly, and serve warm.

intro: Pigar-pigar is a quick, intensely hot-fried beef and liver dish with onions.
steps: Marinate beef and liver in soy sauce, salt, and black pepper for at least 1 hour.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a wok until nearly smoking.
Fry beef and liver in batches until the edges are crisp, then lift out with a slotted spoon.
Drain on a metal sieve and immediately toss with sliced onion, letting the residual heat soften it.

intro: Rodic’s-Style Chopped Beef Tapa is tender shredded brisket cooked down into sweet-savory crisp-edged morsels.
steps: Place beef, brown sugar, soy sauce, garlic, black pepper, and water in a pressure cooker.
Pressure-cook for 1 1/2 hours, then slowly release pressure and safely open the cooker.
Transfer beef to a plate, leaving the liquid behind; shred the meat with forks.
Return shredded beef to the pot and cook over medium heat until the liquid has evaporated.
Add oil and cook 2 minutes, until some flakes crisp at the edges. Garnish with fried garlic.

intro: Ginisang okra with galunggong flakes is a quick, savory rice-friendly skillet dish.
steps: Remove bones from the fried galunggong and shred the fish into flakes.
Heat oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add tomato and fish flakes; cook 2 minutes. Stir in okra and cook 5–10 minutes over high heat until tender.
Add patis and black pepper; cook 2 minutes more. Serve with rice.

intro: Chargrilled Dried Squid is a quick smoky snack served with a sharp chile-vinegar dip.
steps: Prepare a hot grill and place the dried squid directly over the heat.
Grill for no more than 30 seconds per side, just until lightly charred; longer cooking can make it bitter.
Mix vinegar, water, green chiles, garlic, sugar, and black pepper for the dipping sauce.
Skewer or cut the grilled dried squid as desired and serve immediately with the dip.

intro: Chicken Lininggil is a turmeric-and-palapa coconut chicken braise finished with tender string beans.
ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken, cut into sections
¼ cup liver spread or mashed chicken liver
steps: Pound or process garlic, shallots, ginger, and turmeric into a paste. Heat oil in a wok and brown chicken on all sides; remove.
Lower heat, add oil if needed, and sauté palapa until fragrant. Add tomato and cook until soft.
Pour in coconut milk; return chicken and add liver spread or mashed liver and chilies. Bring to a medium boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes. Add string beans, raise heat, and cook about 5 minutes until tender and sauce nearly dries.
Season with salt as needed and serve.

intro: Chicken feet adobo is fried first, then simmered in a savory, tangy sauce until tender.
steps: Heat 16 tbsp oil in a pot and fry chicken feet until light brown; transfer them to a plate.
Heat remaining 2 tbsp oil in a clean pot. Sauté garlic and dried chilies until fragrant.
Add chicken feet, soy sauce, and water; bring to a boil. Add bay leaves, peppercorns, oyster sauce, and sugar.
Simmer until tender, adding water if needed. Stir in vinegar and cook 5 minutes more.
Taste, season with salt as needed, and serve hot.

intro: Balut and Penoy are warming Filipino duck-egg street snacks best enjoyed simply with salt.
steps: Place balut in a steamer over boiling water and steam for 25 minutes.
