For penoy, place eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil, and cook 15 minutes for hard-boiled eggs.
Keep cooked eggs warm in a basket lined with a warm cloth, if desired.
For balut, crack the top, make a small opening, and sip the broth before eating the contents with salt.
Crack and peel penoy like a regular hard-boiled egg; season with a pinch of salt.

intro: Beef Teriyaki Tapa makes a quick, satisfying breakfast plate with garlic fried rice and eggs.
steps: Mix beef with teriyaki sauce in a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add beef and all marinade.
Stir-fry for 5 to 10 minutes, until the beef is cooked and the sauce has evaporated.
Cook the eggs to your preferred doneness.
Divide garlic fried rice between two plates, then add an egg and half the beef to each plate.

intro: Lomisua is a comforting thick soup with misua, crisp pork belly, squid balls, and vegetables.
steps: Heat a little oil in a pot and fry pork belly until golden; remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic and shallot for 1 minute, then fry the squid balls briefly.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a boil; return pork and simmer 2 minutes.
Stir cornstarch with a little water, add it to the pot, and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add patola, carrot, and Chinese cabbage; return to a boil and simmer 2 minutes, adding water if needed.
Add misua and cook 2 minutes, turn off heat, then stir in eggs; season and garnish with spring onions.

intro: Inaslum is a simple pork-enriched vegetable stew that keeps upo, okra, sitaw, and greens tender-crisp.
steps: Heat a little oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook pork until its fat renders and the meat browns.
Add garlic and onion; sauté until fragrant.
Add sitaw, okra, and upo. Pour in enough water to cover vegetables, bring to a boil, and simmer 5 minutes.
Add spinach or kangkong and season with fish sauce. Cover, turn off heat, and let residual heat wilt the greens before serving.

intro: Chilled tuna kinilaw is cured in vinegar, citrus, ginger, and chile.
ingredients: 2 lb tuna, skinned, deboned, and cubed
steps: Place tuna in a large bowl and pour over 3/4 cup vinegar.
Stand for 2 minutes, then gently press the tuna with a spoon and drain.
Rinse the tuna gently with vinegar and drain completely.
Mix tuna with remaining vinegar, lemon or calamansi juice, ginger, salt, pepper, and chilies.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Top with red onion before serving.

intro: Bas-Uy is a warming pork, liver, and chayote soup scented with ginger and lemongrass.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and brown pork liver; remove and set aside.
Add more oil if necessary, then sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until softened.
Add pork and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 5 minutes. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Pour in pork stock, add tied lemongrass, bring to a boil, and simmer 30 minutes.
Return liver and add chayote; cook 8 minutes. Add spring onions for 2 minutes, season, and serve.

intro: This Batangas-style paksiw slowly braises pata with vinegar, garlic, and peppercorns.
ingredients: 1.5 kg pork leg (pata), cut into sections
steps: Cover pata with water in a pot, bring to a boil, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Drain, rinse the pork to remove scum, and clean the pot if needed.
Return pork with garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, and water barely covering the meat; simmer on low for 45 minutes.
Add chilies, vinegar, onions, and fish sauce; simmer 30 minutes more until very tender, adding water if needed.
Serve hot with rice.

intro: Malibog is a coconut-pandan dessert filled with bilo-bilo, corn, sago, boba, nata de coco, and sesame.
ingredients: ¾–1 cup water, for rice dough
Fresh corn kernels from 2 ears corn
½ cup sugar, adjusted to taste
3 pandan leaves, tied in a knot
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour with ¾ cup water, adding only enough extra water to form a firm, shapeable dough. Roll into 1.5-cm balls.
Cook mini sago in boiling water according to package directions until translucent; drain. Boil boba until floating, then simmer 40 minutes and drain.
Bring coconut milk, 1 cup water, and pandan to a gentle medium boil; lower heat. Add corn and simmer 10 minutes.
Add bilo-bilo and simmer 5 minutes until floating. Stir in sago, boba, and nata de coco; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in sugar and salt, simmer 2 minutes, remove pandan, and add sesame seeds. Serve warm or chilled.

intro: Spring Onion Stuffed Squid combines crisp fried squid, tender spring onions, and a glossy sweet-savory sauce.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon corn flour, dissolved in 1/2 cup water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season squid inside and out with salt and black pepper. Stuff each cavity with spring onions and secure the openings with toothpicks.
Dredge squid lightly in corn flour. Deep-fry at medium-high heat for 3 minutes, just until crisp; avoid overcooking.
Meanwhile, combine teriyaki sauce, hoisin sauce, and dissolved corn flour in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer until thick.
Drain squid, remove toothpicks, and cut several openings in each. Spoon sauce over and garnish with fried garlic.

intro: Inihaw na Panga is juicy grilled fish jaw brushed with a sweet-tangy garlic basting sauce.
ingredients: 2 kg large fish jaw, such as tuna, hapuka, or grouper
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine 1/2 cup soy sauce, juice of 1 lemon, salt, and pepper. Marinate fish jaw for at least 2 hours.
For basting sauce, sauté garlic in oil over low heat until fragrant.
Whisk remaining soy sauce, water, brown sugar, lemon juice, and cornstarch until smooth; add to garlic and bring to a boil.
Simmer the sauce for 2 minutes until thickened. Drain the fish jaw.
Grill over charcoal or medium-high heat for 10 to 15 minutes per side, brushing continuously with sauce during the final 5 minutes.

intro: Ginisang Upo and Spinach is a quick prawn and vegetable sauté in a light savory broth.
ingredients: 1 large upo, about 15 inches long, sliced 1 cm thick and 5 cm wide
steps: Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add tomato and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add prawns and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add upo and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock, fish sauce, and sugar; simmer 8 minutes until the upo is tender.
Stir in spinach, simmer 2 minutes, season with black pepper, and serve.

intro: Adobong mani is a crisp garlic peanut snack seasoned simply with salt.
steps: Peel away the loose outer garlic skin, separate the cloves with inner skins intact, and lightly pound them.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; fry garlic until golden and crisp, then remove.
Lower the heat and fry peanuts for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their skins turn brown but not dark brown.
Drain peanuts in a colander, season with fine salt, and toss with the fried garlic before serving.

intro: Chicken adobo fried rice topped with crisp-edged tortang corned beef makes a hearty leftover meal.
ingredients: 1 cup chicken adobo, shredded and chopped
steps: Mix sautéed corned beef, egg, and pepper. Heat 4 tbsp oil and fry the mixture in four flattened portions, 1–2 minutes per side, until cooked.
Mix leftover rice with salt, gently separating the grains.
Heat 3 tbsp oil over medium heat and cook garlic until light brown.
Stir-fry chicken adobo for 1 minute, then add rice and toss for 3–5 minutes until hot.
Plate the fried rice, top with tortang corned beef, and serve with a preferred condiment.

intro: Crispy Tahong turns steamed mussels into a quick, garlicky, lightly spicy fried snack.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place mussels and 1/4 cup water in a covered pot; cook until shells open, then keep covered.
Combine flour, cornstarch, cayenne, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Remove mussel meat from shells and toss with garlic. Dredge each piece in the flour mixture.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Deep-fry mussels for 2 minutes until golden brown.
Drain well and serve immediately.

intro: Pinugot is a shrimp-shell broth soup brightened with tamarind and loaded with vegetables and sotanghon.
ingredients: 1 bunch kangkong or talbos ng kamote
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Peel shrimp and reserve the meat. Roast shells on a foil-lined tray until red-orange and lightly charred.
Pulse shells with 1 cup water, add remaining water, then strain well, pressing out the liquid to make broth.
Bring broth, onions, tomato, and taro to a boil. Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes until taro begins to soften.
Add daikon, sitaw, and okra; return to a boil and simmer 5 minutes.
Add shrimp, kangkong or talbos ng kamote, sotanghon, and sinigang mix. Boil, then simmer 2 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper; add water if needed and serve hot.

intro: Double-fried tofu is tossed in a creamy, tangy sisig dressing and served sizzling.
ingredients: 2 medium bell peppers, cut into squares
2 long green chili peppers, halved and sliced crosswise
steps: Mix Maggi Savor Hot Chili, mayonnaise, soy sauce, calamansi juice, pepper, and optional liver spread into a smooth dressing.
Deep-fry tofu over medium-high heat until golden. Drain on paper towels for 5 minutes, then fry again 2 minutes until very crisp.
Leave 1 tablespoon oil in the wok and melt 1 tablespoon butter. Cook half the onions, bell peppers, and chilies until slightly softened.
Toss in tofu for 30 seconds. Transfer to a bowl, add dressing and remaining raw onions, and toss well.
For a sizzling plate, heat it over medium, melt remaining butter, add tofu sisig, and serve immediately with rice.

intro: Tender sayote, minced beef, and prawns come together in this light, savory ginisa.
ingredients: Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add minced beef and cook until browned. Stir-fry sayote for 1 minute.
Add chicken stock, bring to a boil, then simmer about 5 minutes until sayote is tender.
Add prawns and cook 2 minutes until pink and opaque. Season with fish sauce or sea salt and black pepper.

intro: Pata Tim is a glossy, slow-braised pork leg dish with saba bananas and tender banana blossoms.
ingredients: 2 small pork legs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 tablespoon cornstarch, dissolved in 1/2 cup water
steps: Heat peanut oil in a pot over medium heat and brown garlic.
Add pork leg and brown all sides.
Add soy sauce, hoisin sauce, pork stock, brown sugar, cornstarch slurry, fish sauce, star anise, bay leaves, and peppercorns; bring to a boil.
Lower heat and gently simmer 1 1/2–2 hours, until pork is very tender.
Add banana blossoms and simmer 15 minutes, then add saba bananas and simmer 15 minutes more.

intro: Estofadong baboy braises marinated pork with saba banana in a sweet-sour soy sauce.
steps: Mix pork with peppercorns, garlic, soy sauce, and vinegar; marinate at least 3 hours.
Heat oil and pan-fry saba slices for 45 seconds per side; set aside.
Pan-fry marinated pork about 1–1½ minutes per side. Add the marinade garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add remaining marinade and broth, bring to a boil, then cover and cook over medium heat 50–60 minutes until tender.
Stir in brown sugar and cook 15 minutes. Fold in fried saba, then transfer to a serving plate.

intro: Adobong Okra with Pork brings tender pork belly and okra together in a soy-vinegar braise.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and cook garlic until medium brown.
Add pork belly and cook for 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce and water, cover, and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes or until pork is tender.
Add more water if needed, then pour in vinegar and let the liquid return to a boil.
Add okra, stir, cover, and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Stir in sugar, salt, and pepper, then serve.

intro: Filipino Polvoron is a buttery, melt-in-the-mouth shortbread enriched with toasted pinipig.
steps: Toast flour in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until lightly colored and fragrant.
Remove from heat while the flour is still hot.
Mix in powdered milk, caster sugar, ground pinipig, and melted butter until evenly combined.
Pack the mixture firmly into polvoron molds or small medicine cups, then tap out the cakes gently.
Chill until firm, then serve or wrap individually.

intro: Chocolate cupcakes are finished with silky yema and crunchy macadamias.
ingredients: 3/4 cup crumbled macadamias, plus more for topping
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Sift flour, cocoa, coffee, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and both sugars together.
Whisk eggs, oil, 2 teaspoons vanilla, and buttermilk. Stir into dry ingredients just until combined; do not overmix.
Fill lined muffin cups three-quarters full and bake 20 minutes, until a tester comes out clean. Cool completely.
For yema, cook yolks and condensed milk over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened but still spreadable.
Stir in butter and salt until glossy; remove from heat, mix in 1/2 teaspoon vanilla, and cool.
Dip cupcake tops in yema, then immediately coat with crumbled macadamias.

intro: Pineapple gives this sweet-sour paksiw na pata a bright, mellow finish.
ingredients: 3 lb pork or ham hock (pata), sliced crosswise
1 pack (1 oz) dried banana blossoms, washed and soaked in water
steps: Bring 6 cups water to a boil, add pata, and boil for 30 minutes. Drain and set the pork aside.
Heat oil in a clean pot and sauté garlic until light brown.
Add pork, soy sauce, pineapple chunks with juice, and remaining 2 cups water; bring to a boil.
Add bay leaves, peppercorns, and vinegar; boil, then cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in beef cube, if using, and brown sugar or panutsa. Add banana blossoms and simmer until pork is tender.
Season with salt and serve. Add water if needed while tenderizing the pork.

intro: Adobo steak simmers tenderloin in soy, vinegar, and honey before a quick pepper-and-onion finish.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a pot and cook beef for 1–2 minutes.
Add soy sauce and water, bring to a boil, and simmer 15–20 minutes; add water if the pan dries out.
Stir in honey and vinegar, bring back to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes. Set beef aside.
Heat remaining oil in a wok and sauté bell pepper and onion for 3 minutes.
Add beef, season with salt and pepper, stir-fry 1 minute, and serve.

intro: Panlasang Pinoy Omelet is a tender vegetable omelet finished with melted cheddar cheese.
steps: Beat eggs with a pinch to 1/4 tsp salt until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Sauté onion and tomato until soft, then add bell pepper and scallions; cook 1 minute.
Pour in eggs and spread evenly; cook 2 to 3 minutes until the bottom is set.
Flip carefully and cook the second side until set.
Move to a plate, top with cheddar, and serve.

intro: Barbara’s Pinoy Barbecue delivers sweet, tangy, garlic-marinated pork with smoky grilled edges.
ingredients: 1 kg pork chops, cut into medium square pieces
3 tablespoons olive oil or vegetable oil
steps: Combine soy sauce, banana ketchup, lemon juice, garlic, onion, pepper, brown sugar, salt, and oil in a bowl.
Coat pork thoroughly in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 10 hours or overnight.
Thread 5 to 9 pork pieces onto each skewer, allowing for shrinkage during grilling.
Heat a grill or grill pan until hot. Grill skewers, turning each side 2 to 3 times, until evenly browned and lightly charred.
Brush with marinade while grilling and cook until pork is fully done; serve hot.

intro: Nilagang Litid ng Baka is a clean, peppery beef-tendon soup with potatoes and cabbage.
ingredients: 2 lbs beef shoulder bones with tendons
½ small cabbage, cored and quartered
steps: Bring water and optional beef broth to a boil in a soup pot. Add peppercorns and onion; boil 5 minutes.
Add beef shoulder bones with tendons, cover, return to a boil, then cook over low-medium heat for 60–120 minutes until tendons are tender.
Add potatoes and cabbage; cook 5 minutes until beginning to soften.
Stir in fish sauce, adjusting to taste, and cook 5 minutes more. Serve hot with rice and spicy fish sauce with lemon if desired.

intro: Sinigang na sardinas is a quick, miso-enriched mackerel soup packed with tender vegetables.
ingredients: 75 g Maggi Magic Sinigang with Gabi
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Strain the mackerel, reserving its oil. Heat cooking oil and sauté onions, ginger, garlic, and tomatoes until softened.
Add reserved mackerel oil, 1 tbsp fish sauce, pepper, miso, and 1½ qt water. Bring to a boil.
Add daikon and cook over medium heat 5 minutes. Stir in sinigang mix, then boil eggplant for 2 minutes.
Add okra, long green peppers, and string beans. Add remaining water, cover, reboil, and cook 2 minutes.
Gently add mackerel and kangkong; cook 2–3 minutes. Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

intro: Cheesy Baked Macaroni Pinoy Style layers beefy Filipino spaghetti sauce with creamy cheese sauce.
steps: Cook macaroni according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Brown beef in a wok; add onion and garlic, then sauté until onion softens. Add bell pepper and cook 1 minute.
Add Filipino-style spaghetti sauce and water; stir and cook 12 to 15 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
For white sauce, melt butter, cook flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in milk and half the cheese until thick.
Combine macaroni, meat sauce, and white sauce; transfer to a baking pan and top with remaining cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes, until hot and melted, then serve.

intro: Pork Giniling is a rich tomato-based ground pork stew finished with vegetables, cheese, peas, and eggs.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon calamansi juice or lime juice
steps: Sauté garlic and onion in oil over medium heat until soft. Add tomato sauce and paste; cook until oil separates from the sauce.
Add ground pork and cook until lightly browned. Add water and simmer 10 minutes.
Add soy sauce, calamansi juice, salt, and pepper; cook 10 minutes. Add butter, cover, and simmer 5 minutes.
Add carrot, potato, and bell pepper. Cover and simmer 5 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Stir in cheese until melted, add green peas for 1 minute, then fold in hard-boiled eggs. Serve with rice.

intro: Betute is a Pampanga specialty of farm-raised rice field frogs stuffed with seasoned minced pork and deep-fried.
ingredients: 4 large cleaned farm-raised rice field frogs (tugak)
250 g minced pork or seasoned ground meat
steps: Pat the cleaned frogs dry. Season minced pork with salt and black pepper, then divide it among the frog cavities.
Secure each stuffed frog closed as needed and pat the exterior dry before frying.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying to 175°C. Fry frogs in batches until deeply golden and the pork filling reaches 71°C.
Drain on a rack or paper towels for several minutes. Serve hot.

intro: Law-uy is a vegetable-rich soup with fried pork, taro, and saluyot.
ingredients: 4 medium Asian taro, cut into 1/2-inch sections
1 thumb-size piece ginger, thinly sliced and pounded
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season the pork well with salt and pepper. Fry it in oil in a wok until golden, then remove it from the pan.
In the same wok, cook the garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the water, taro, and pounded lemongrass. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the eggplant, squash, okra, and fried pork, then continue simmering for 5 minutes.
Add the patola and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in the saluyot for the final minute, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve.

intro: Mango Ice Cream is an easy no-churn frozen dessert packed with chewy dried mango.
steps: Mix lime juice and boiling water in a small bowl, add dried mangoes, and soak for 15 minutes.
Whip chilled cream to stiff peaks, taking care not to overwhip it.
Drain excess liquid from the soaked mangoes.
Gently fold condensed milk and dried mangoes into the whipped cream until evenly combined.
Transfer to a container, smooth the surface, and freeze for 6 to 8 hours or overnight.
Scoop and serve frozen.

intro: Pork guisantes is a tomato-braised pork dish with green peas and sweet capsicum.
ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder, sliced into long strips
1 small yellow capsicum, sliced into strips
1 small red capsicum, sliced into strips
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork and brown all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add tomato purée, stock, basil, and oregano. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat 35–40 minutes.
Add both capsicums and green peas; cook 2–3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve with steamed rice.

intro: Kalcag Rice is a savory fried-rice dish with crisp kalcag, toasted garlic, and fresh spring onions.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Break up the leftover rice with clean hands until the grains are separated.
Heat a large wok over high heat and add enough oil to lightly coat its surface.
When the wok begins to smoke, lower heat slightly and fry garlic until golden brown.
Add kalcag and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until brown and crisp.
Add rice and stir-fry continuously for 10 minutes until hot and evenly seasoned.
Mix in spring onions, then season with sea salt and black pepper before serving.

intro: Chicken Giniling with Green Peas is a comforting tomato-braised ground chicken meal with tender vegetables.
ingredients: 1 large potato, cut into small cubes
1 large carrot, cut into small cubes
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add ground chicken and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add tomato sauce and chicken broth; bring to a boil. Add bay leaves, cover, and simmer 35 minutes, adding broth if needed.
Add carrot and potato; stir and cook 8–10 minutes until tender.
Add green peas and cook 3–5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Pichi-pichi is a chewy cassava sweet rolled in fresh or coconut-milk-softened coconut.
ingredients: 3 pandan leaves, tied in a knot
steps: Boil water with pandan leaves, then simmer 15 minutes. Cool, discard leaves, and measure 2 cups liquid, adding water if necessary.
Mix cassava, sugar, lye water, pandan liquid, and food coloring, if using, until evenly combined.
Pour into molds and steam for 1 hour, until translucent. Cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
If using desiccated coconut, heat coconut milk until hot but not boiling and mix it with the coconut.
Unmold, cut large portions into bite-size pieces, and roll each in fresh grated coconut or the softened desiccated coconut.

intro: Pata Paksiw slowly braises pork hock in soy, vinegar, sugar, and aromatic spices.
ingredients: 100 g dried banana blossoms, soaked in water
steps: Boil pork hock in 6 cups water for 15 minutes. Discard the water and rinse pork thoroughly under running water.
Bring 2 cups water to a boil with peppercorns and bay leaves. Add soy sauce and garlic.
Add pork hock and simmer 1–1½ hours until tender, or pressure-cook 30 minutes.
Add vinegar and simmer 10 minutes. Add soaked banana blossoms and simmer 5–7 minutes.
Stir in brown sugar and salt, simmer 2 minutes, and serve hot.

intro: Binatog is warm, burst hominy topped simply with coconut, butter, sugar, and salt.
steps: Drain the hominy and rinse it well under running water.
Place hominy in a pot and add enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat 20 minutes until kernels burst open.
Divide warm hominy among bowls and top with grated coconut, butter, sugar, and salt to taste.

intro: Lechon sa Hurno is oven-roasted pork neck with crackling skin and fragrant aromatic drippings.
steps: Submerge pork neck and rock salt in enough water to cover; refrigerate for 24 hours.
Remove pork from refrigeration 1 hour before roasting and drain thoroughly.
Set a rack over a shallow water-filled baking dish; line the rack with baking paper and cover with lemongrass, spring onions, onion, and garlic.
Season pork all over with fish sauce and place it over the aromatics.
Roast at 170°C for 2 1/2 hours, basting the skin with tray drippings every 30 minutes.
Raise heat to 180°C and roast 30 minutes more until the skin crackles at the edges; rest 15 minutes before serving.

intro: Sardines with Sotanghon and Pechay is a fast pantry noodle soup with tender greens.
ingredients: 1 can (5.5 ounces) sardines in tomato sauce
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Crush and chop garlic, then sauté until beginning to brown.
Add chopped onion and cook until softened.
Add sardines with their tomato sauce and cook for 1 minute. Add pechay and sauté 30 seconds.
Add water and bring to a boil. Stir in sotanghon and cook until softened.
Season with patis and black pepper. Top with green onion and serve hot.

intro: Inasal na Liempo is charcoal-grilled pork belly with a bright vinegar marinade and buttery lemon basting sauce.
ingredients: 1 kilogram pork belly, cut 3/4 inch thick
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Process ginger, garlic, lemongrass, coconut vinegar, 1/2 cup lemon juice, fish sauce, brown sugar, and black pepper into a marinade.
Massage pork belly with marinade and baking soda in an airtight container. Cover and marinate at least 6 hours.
Combine annatto powder, butter, juice of 2 lemons, and salt in a saucepan; simmer over low heat for 2 minutes.
Grill pork belly over charcoal, basting occasionally with butter sauce, until cooked through and charred at the edges.

intro: Tortang talong with sardinas combines smoky grilled eggplant with a savory tomato-sardine omelet topping.
ingredients: 1 (5.5 oz) can sardines in tomato sauce
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat some oil and sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until soft. Add sardines and one-quarter of their sauce; cook 2 minutes.
Season the sardines, add lemon or calamansi juice and some green onion, then set aside. Whisk eggs until smooth.
Grill eggplants, turning regularly, until soft and steam escapes through cracked skin. Cool, peel, and flatten each with a fork.
Heat remaining oil. Dip eggplant in egg, fry flat, top with sardines and green onion, then spoon egg over it.
Cook until golden underneath, carefully flip, and cook through. Serve with rice, sardine side upward.

intro: Boneless Bangus wrapped in pandan leaves steams its tomato-ginger filling as it cooks.
steps: Wash the boneless bangus and season lightly with salt and ground black pepper.
Combine tomatoes, onion, and ginger; season the mixture with salt and pepper.
Stuff the fish with the tomato mixture.
Wrap pandan leaves around the fish, tucking each end securely to keep the filling enclosed.
Grill in a nonstick pan for 10 to 15 minutes per side, or bake for 20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Remove pandan leaves and serve warm.

intro: Bacon Cuchifrito pairs crisp bacon with smoky tinapa fried rice, salted duck egg salad, and cucumber.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, for salad
steps: Heat oil in a frying pan. Lightly coat bacon with flour and fry until golden and crisp; set aside.
Combine tomatoes, onion, and salted duck eggs in a bowl. Squeeze over calamansi and add black pepper.
In another pan, sauté garlic and tinapa until fragrant.
Add leftover rice, season with salt and black pepper, and stir-fry until hot and evenly mixed.
Serve fried rice with bacon, salted duck egg salad, and sliced cucumber.

intro: This Pinoy fried chicken is marinated, steamed, air-dried, then fried golden.
ingredients: 32 g Knorr SavorRich Chicken Liquid Seasoning
steps: Mix chicken with onion powder, nutmeg, cooking wine or rum, patis, and Knorr SavorRich until coated.
Seal in a resealable bag and marinate overnight in the refrigerator.
Steam chicken over boiling water for 45 minutes, then place on a wire rack to air-dry for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or pot and fry until golden brown. Serve with banana ketchup.

intro: Lengua a la vinagreta is tender chilled ox tongue dressed in a sharp egg-and-herb vinaigrette.
steps: Bring water to a boil, add ox tongue and 3 tbsp salt, and simmer about 1 hour until tender.
Cool the tongue, peel away its skin with a paring knife, and slice it thinly.
Combine garlic, onion, parsley, bell pepper, olive oil, vinegar, chopped eggs, salt, and pepper.
Toss sliced tongue with the vinaigrette, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Serve cold as an appetizer, with or without the dressing.

intro: Killer Pork Sinigang is a full-bodied tamarind pork soup loaded with classic vegetables.
ingredients: 66 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix with Gabi
steps: Heat oil in a pot; sauté onion until separated, then sauté half the tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add pork and sauté until browned, adding about 1 tbsp fish sauce.
Pour in water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Stir in Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix with Gabi; cover and simmer over low-medium heat for 30 minutes until pork starts becoming tender.
Add labanos, cover, and cook 30 minutes more until pork is tender.
Add talong, string beans, and okra for 5 minutes; add kangkong stalks, remaining tomatoes, and shishito peppers for 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: These pork-and-prawn kikiam rolls are steamed first, then fried until their beancurd wrappers turn crisp.
steps: Process half the pork into a paste, then mix with remaining pork, prawns, onion, garlic, carrot, cornstarch, five-spice, sugar, and salt.
Place filling on beancurd sheets and roll tightly like spring rolls.
Steam the rolls for 15 minutes, then cool; refrigerate or freeze any not being fried immediately.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying. Fry thawed rolls over medium heat about 3 minutes, until crisp, then drain.
Slice and serve with sweet chili sauce.

intro: Nilagang Pata is a comforting pork-hock soup filled with corn, potatoes, and fresh vegetables.
steps: Clean pork hocks thoroughly. Bring 8 cups water to a boil in a large pot, add pork, cover, and cook 10 minutes.
Skim off scum. Add Knorr Pork Cube, onions, and peppercorns; cover and simmer on low 60–90 minutes until pork is completely tender.
Raise heat to low-medium, add corn and potatoes, and cook 10 minutes.
Add long green beans, bok choy, and cabbage; boil 3–5 minutes until just tender. Season with fish sauce and serve hot with rice.

intro: This loaded pancit canton brings together seafood, meats, noodles, and crisp vegetables.
steps: Boil salted water and cook pancit canton for 2 minutes; drain and set aside.
Blanch bell peppers, cabbage, carrots, and snow peas for 1 to 2 minutes; chill in ice water for 30 seconds and drain.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until softened. Add chicken, squid balls, and Chinese sausage for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook 1 minute. Stir in soy sauce, oyster sauce, and 1 cup water; bring to a boil.
Add shrimp cube, noodles, and parsley. Cover and cook over low-medium heat 2 to 3 minutes until done but not soggy.
Toss in vegetables, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

intro: Puchero Bulalo is a hearty beef shank pochero with chorizo, saba, vegetables, and tomato broth.
steps: Heat a pressure cooker or pot until hot. Sear beef shank for 2 minutes per side, then remove.
Add oil and sauté onion, garlic, and tomato. Add Chinese sausage and sauté 2 minutes.
Return beef. Add tomato sauce and broth, bring to a boil, cover, and pressure-cook 20–30 minutes.
Release pressure safely. Add saba, garbanzos, and potato; cook 5–8 minutes.
Add beans, bok choy, and cabbage; cook 3–5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Longganisang Hubad is sweet, garlicky, loose pork longganisa cooked until richly browned.
steps: Mix soy sauce, cane vinegar, and annatto powder in a large bowl.
Add pork, brown sugar, salt, garlic, and black pepper; mix thoroughly until evenly seasoned.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the longganisa mixture and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring constantly, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot.

intro: Tinadtad na Baka is a hearty, tamarind-soured beef soup filled with crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 750 g beef brisket, cut into very small cubes
1 cup lima beans, edamame, or broad beans
1 packet sinigang mix or 12 bilimbi, trimmed
steps: Heat oil in a deep pot and brown beef. Remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant, then cook tomatoes until soft. Return beef to the pot.
Add enough water to cover meat and add bilimbi, if using. Bring to a boil and simmer 40 minutes.
Add lima beans and daikon; simmer 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Add string beans, wing beans if using, and okra; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in sinigang mix, if using, and season with fish sauce. Add kangkong, cover off heat for 2 minutes, then serve.

intro: Mamon is a light Filipino sponge cake finished with melted butter and grated cheddar.
ingredients: 1/3 cup butter, melted, plus more for brushing
steps: Beat egg yolks, 1/2 cup sugar, and water at high speed until well combined.
Beat in baking powder, salt, flour, melted butter, orange extract, and lemon extract on low speed; set aside.
Beat egg whites with cream of tartar at high speed, gradually adding remaining sugar until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the yolk mixture into the egg whites without deflating the batter.
Fill lined muffin cups three-quarters full and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, until springy and cooked through.
Brush warm mamon generously with melted butter and finish with grated cheddar.

intro: Crispy Dinakdakan pairs twice-fried pork with a creamy, sharp chile dressing.
steps: Bring water to a boil with pork belly, pork ears, white onions, peppercorns, salt, bay leaves, and garlic; cover and simmer 60 minutes until tender.
Drain, salt the meat, and cool for a few hours or refrigerate uncovered overnight.
Heat oil to 180°C. Fry pork for 8 minutes, rest 10 minutes, then fry again 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Chop pork bite-size and toss with red onion, spring onions, and bird's-eye chilies.
Whisk mayonnaise, soy sauce, lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and pepper until smooth; toss with pork and serve immediately.

intro: Kutsinta is a soft, chewy steamed rice cake with a caramel color and fresh coconut topping.
steps: Sift rice flour, flour, and brown sugar into a bowl.
Gradually whisk in water until the batter is smooth and lump-free.
Dissolve annatto powder in hot water, then mix it into the batter with lye water until evenly colored.
Pour into lightly greased individual molds and steam for 45 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Unmold and serve topped with freshly grated coconut.

intro: Special Pancit Canton is a festive noodle platter loaded with pork, liver, seafood, vegetables, and quail eggs.
ingredients: 21 oz pancit canton noodles (flour stick noodles), pre-boiled
¼ lb pork liver, thinly sliced
½ lb shrimp, peeled, with heads and shells reserved
1 cup long green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 medium red bell pepper, sliced into strips
steps: Soak liver in milk at least 1 hour; drain, rinse, and pat dry. Boil pork belly in water with salt 45–60 minutes until fork-tender; slice and reserve stock.
Simmer shrimp shells and heads in pork stock 2–3 minutes; strain. Stir cornstarch into the warm stock until dissolved.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil over medium-high heat. Add pork, kikiam, and Chinese sausage for 2 minutes; add liver and cook 1½ minutes until no longer pink.
Stir in oyster sauce, cabbage, beans, carrot, bell pepper, shrimp, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Add stock, boil, then dissolve in Shrimp Cube.
Cook about 3 minutes until shrimp are pink and curled. Toss in noodles until most sauce is absorbed; season and top with quail eggs.

intro: Ube halaya is a rich purple yam jam cooked until glossy, thick, and spoonable.
ingredients: 1 lb purple yam, fresh or frozen, peeled and cubed
1 (10 fl oz) can sweetened condensed milk
steps: Melt butter in a wide, deep pan over medium heat. Add ube and coconut milk, bring to a boil, and cook 15 minutes.
Blend the cooked ube mixture until very smooth, using a blender or immersion blender.
Return it to the pan with condensed milk, evaporated milk, and sugar. Simmer over medium-low heat, stirring regularly, 20–30 minutes.
Cook until very thick, heavy, and pulling away from the pan sides when stirred.
Butter 2–3 llanera, fill them, cool, then chill at least 2 hours. Top with latik or grated cheese.

intro: Special Tokwat Baboy is a tangy vinegar-dressed mix of grilled pork belly, crisp tofu, and fresh onions.
ingredients: 1 pound pork belly, grilled and sliced
steps: Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Pat tofu dry and fry on both sides until golden brown. Cool slightly, then cut into small cubes.
Mix vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, salt, and black pepper; microwave for 20 seconds.
Combine grilled pork belly, tofu, red onion, and green onions in a large bowl.
Pour over the warm vinegar mixture, toss well, and serve.

intro: Camaron Rellenado features prawns wrapped in seasoned pork and crab filling, then fried in a crisp panko crust.
ingredients: 1/2 cup crab meat or minced prawns
2 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and finely chopped
12 large prawns, shelled and deveined with tails on
steps: Mix pork, crab meat or minced prawns, shiitake, egg, spring onion, cornstarch, white pepper, and 1 teaspoon salt.
Dredge each prawn in flour. Enclose it in a thin layer of filling, leaving the tail exposed.
Season beaten eggs with salt. Dip each wrapped prawn in egg, then coat with panko.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C. Fry prawns 8–10 minutes until cooked through and golden brown.
Drain excess oil and serve hot.

intro: Igado is a tangy Ilocano pork and offal stew accented with raisins and green capsicum.
steps: Marinate pork liver in ½ cup cane vinegar for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes; drain and reserve.
Heat oil and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until the onion softens.
Add pork belly and heart; stir-fry over high heat until no longer pink.
Add remaining vinegar, soy sauce, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Boil, then simmer uncovered over medium heat 25 minutes to reduce.
Add liver, raisins, and capsicum; simmer 5 minutes. Add water if needed, season with fish sauce, and serve.

intro: This plated meal combines prepared Pork Adobo Paksiw, crispy fried jeprox, shrimp fried rice, egg, and spicy vinegar.
steps: Prepare or reheat the Pork Adobo Paksiw, crispy fried jeprox, and shrimp fried rice until hot.
Divide the shrimp fried rice among four individual plates, using about 1 cup per plate.
Arrange portions of Pork Adobo Paksiw and crispy fried jeprox beside the rice.
Halve or leave the hard-boiled eggs whole and add one to each plate. Serve with spicy vinegar.

intro: A creamy macaroni salad with cheddar, eggs, peas, and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 1/2 cup red bell pepper, finely chopped
steps: Cook macaroni in salted boiling water until tender but not mushy; add peas during the final minute.
Drain, rinse under cold water until cool, and drain thoroughly.
Mix mayonnaise, Dijon, pickle relish, pickle juice, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Gently toss in macaroni, peas, celery, bell pepper, red onion, cheddar, eggs, and parsley until coated.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour. Stir gently, adjust seasoning, and serve cold.

intro: Kandingga is a rich, spicy coconut stew of pork offal with vinegar and lemongrass.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place pork heart, lungs, pork neck, lemongrass, 1 cup vinegar, 1 tablespoon salt, and enough water to cover in a pot.
Bring to a boil and cook 30 to 40 minutes until tender but not fully cooked. Cool, then finely dice the meat.
Heat oil in a heavy pan; sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add diced meat, chilies, and bay leaves. Stir-fry for 10 minutes.
Add capsicum, remaining vinegar, and coconut milk; boil, then simmer over high heat until thickened.
Stir in coconut cream, season with fish sauce and black pepper, simmer 2 minutes, and serve.

intro: Ginataang Kangkong with prawns is a creamy coconut vegetable dish brightened by red chilies.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add coconut milk, bring to a boil, and simmer over medium heat 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add kangkong, chilies, prawns, and coconut cream. Simmer 5 minutes until prawns are pink and cooked through.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Pork tausi braises browned pork belly in a savory salted-black-bean sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok and brown pork slices around the edges.
Push pork aside, then sauté garlic, ginger, onion, and chilies until fragrant; stir together.
Mash salted black beans with a spoon and combine with dark soy sauce, sugar, and water.
Pour in the sauce over high heat and bring to a boil while stir-frying.
Cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes. Raise heat during the last minutes to thicken, then season and serve.

intro: Misua soup with pan-fried meatballs and watercress is a light, fast-cooking comfort meal.
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add meatballs and chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add watercress and simmer 5 minutes.
Add misua and simmer 2 minutes, until the noodles are tender.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and pepper. Garnish generously with fried garlic and serve immediately.

intro: Pork Giniling Hardinera turns prepared pork giniling into a colorful steamed fiesta loaf.
steps: Halve the boiled eggs lengthwise and set aside.
Mix prepared pork giniling, green peas, breadcrumbs, raw eggs, pineapple, cheese, pickle relish, raisins, and roasted red bell pepper.
Arrange the mixture and boiled egg halves in oval llanera molds, then cover each mold with foil.
Bring 8 cups water to a boil in a steamer and steam the covered molds for 30 minutes.
Cool for 1 to 2 hours before serving, or chill for 3 hours and serve cold.

intro: Pilipit is a twisted fried pastry glazed with a thin, sweet sugar coating.
steps: Sift flour, salt, and baking powder into a bowl. Mix evaporated milk with the beaten egg separately.
Pour milk mixture into dry ingredients and knead until smooth. Cover with a damp cloth and rest 15 minutes.
Divide dough in half. Flatten each piece, cut into 1/2-inch strips, roll thinner, join ends, and twist; rest 20 to 30 minutes.
Heat oil to 180°C and deep-fry twists until golden brown. Drain on a wire rack.
Cook powdered sugar and water over medium heat until fully dissolved. Dip pastries in glaze and return to the rack until dry.

intro: Oven Baked Pork Chop Silog with Atchara makes a complete plate of crisp pork, sinangag, eggs, and pickled papaya.
steps: Rub pork chops with salt and black pepper; rest 10–15 minutes. Heat oven to 350°F.
Beat raw egg in one bowl and place flour in another. Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Coat each pork chop in flour, egg, then flour again. Fry 1 minute per side and place on a baking tray.
Bake 35 minutes, until pork is cooked through.
Serve each pork chop with 1 cup sinangag, 2 fried eggs, and papaya atchara.

intro: Sinigang na Sinangag combines crispy pork, tangy fried rice, and airy vegetable tempura.
ingredients: 2 tbsp sinigang mix, or to taste
steps: The day before, blanch pork in boiling water for 5 minutes; drain, rinse pork and pot, then cover pork with fresh water, onion, chile, tomato, and sinigang mix.
Bring to a boil, simmer 1 hour until tender, season, reserve broth, cool pork, and refrigerate it at least 6 hours.
Cook rice with 3 cups reserved broth; fluff, cool, and refrigerate uncovered overnight.
Deep-fry chilled pork at 180°C until crisp. Sauté garlic in oil, stir-fry rice 5 minutes, add 2 tbsp sinigang mix, and fry 3 minutes.
Set a bowl over ice; lightly mix flour, cornstarch, ice-cold water, baking powder, and salt without overmixing.
At 180°C, dip vegetables in batter and fry up to three at once for under 1 minute until light brown; drain.
Serve sinigang fried rice topped with crispy pork and tempura vegetables, garnished with tomatoes.

intro: Chao Long is a fragrant Vietnamese-Filipino beef noodle soup with lemongrass, five-spice, and calamansi.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized ginger, thickly sliced and pounded
400 g round or flat rice noodles, cooked according to package directions
Calamansi or lemon wedges, for serving
steps: Mix 6 cloves minced garlic, ginger, fish sauce, five-spice, and brown sugar. Coat brisket and marinate 30 minutes.
Cover bones with water, boil 10 minutes, drain, and rinse. Simmer bones with 2 litres water, lemongrass, and 1 tablespoon salt, covered, for 2 hours.
Brown marinated brisket in oil; deglaze with ½ cup water and add this liquid to the bone stock.
Sauté whole-head garlic and red onions in the same pan. Cook tomato paste 1 minute, then soy sauce and banana ketchup 1 minute; toss in beef.
Add pan contents and carrots to stock. Boil, then simmer low 1–1½ hours until brisket is tender; season with salt and white pepper.
Place cooked noodles in bowls, add beef, carrots, and broth, then garnish with bean sprouts, coriander, white onion, and calamansi.

intro: Pinasingawang Gulay is a gentle steamed vegetable platter served with salty bagoong monamon and calamansi.
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato, cut into chunks
1 bunch kangkong or talbos ng kamote
3 tablespoons bagoong monamon, to serve (soy sauce for a vegan option)
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot fitted with a steamer basket or bamboo steamer.
Layer sweet potato first, then eggplant, okra, and kangkong or talbos ng kamote. Place tomato on top if using.
Cover and steam 10–15 minutes, until vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Transfer vegetables to a serving plate. Serve warm with bagoong monamon or soy sauce and calamansi halves.

intro: Kilawing Labanos at Baboy is a bright vinegar-braised pork dish with crisp-tender daikon.
ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder chops, thinly sliced
steps: Marinate pork in 1/2 cup cane vinegar, salt, and pepper for 30 minutes.
Salt the daikon generously for 15 minutes, rinse under cold water, then soak it in 1/2 cup vinegar.
Drain the daikon and discard its vinegar; drain pork and reserve its marinade.
Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic with half the onions. Add pork and stir-fry over high heat until lightly browned.
Add reserved pork vinegar, remaining 1/2 cup vinegar, water, and bay leaves; boil, then simmer 20 minutes.
Add daikon and cook uncovered for 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper, garnish with remaining onion, and serve.

intro: Roasted pork neck is chopped and finished sizzling with calamansi, aromatics, and egg.
ingredients: 1 kg whole pork neck, skin on
1/2 cup calamansi or lemon juice, divided
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub the baking soda over the pork skin; season the pork generously with salt and black pepper.
Roast on a rack over a drip tray at 160°C for 2 hours. Raise to 180°C and roast 45–60 minutes until crisp and golden.
Cool until safe to handle, then chop the pork finely. Toss with 1/4 cup calamansi juice, soy sauce, onion, chillies, and salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sauté garlic and ginger, add pork, and toss until sizzling.
Drizzle with remaining calamansi juice, add black pepper, and crack the eggs over the hot sisig before serving.

intro: Pesang Baboy at Manok is a gentle ginger broth with pork, chicken, potatoes, and pechay Baguio.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
2 medium potatoes, cut into large cubes
1 large banana pepper or 2 siling pansigang
steps: Combine pork, chicken, ginger, peppercorns, and 8 cups water in a pot; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 1 hour.
Add remaining 2 cups water, or more as needed, and return to a boil.
Add potatoes and banana pepper or siling pansigang; cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add pechay Baguio and fish sauce; stir and cook 3 minutes. Serve with rice.

intro: Chicken gizzard ginataan cooks tender gizzards in reduced coconut milk with kangkong.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring water to a boil with bay leaves. Add gizzards and boil over medium heat 35–45 minutes, until tender; remove them.
Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until the onion softens.
Add boiled gizzards and sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, and simmer until reduced by half.
Add bell pepper and cook 2 minutes. Add kangkong, season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve with rice.

intro: Kapampangan Pulutok Bopis is a deeply savory minced pork-lung dish finished until it pops on a hot plate.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons annatto powder or annatto seeds
2 green finger chilies, thinly sliced diagonally
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and dissolve annatto powder until the oil is orange; if using seeds, remove them once colored.
Sauté garlic and onion in annatto oil until soft and aromatic.
Add pork lungs and cook for 5 minutes, until browned.
Pour in vinegar and simmer untouched for 2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, cover, and simmer until tender; add water 1/2 cup at a time only if needed.
Uncover, add carrots and green chili, and cook while stirring until most liquid evaporates.
For Pulutok, cook a portion on a very hot skillet or sizzling plate until it begins popping, then serve.

intro: Fried Pork Belly Liempo is boiled until seasoned, dredged, crisp-fried, and served with a spicy garlic-onion dip.
ingredients: ¾ tsp ground black pepper, divided
steps: Season pork belly with Maggi Magic Sarap and ½ teaspoon black pepper. Add 5 cloves garlic and water; boil 10 minutes.
Turn pork over and continue boiling until all liquid evaporates. Remove pork and let cool.
Mix flour and cornstarch. Dredge pork, shaking off excess. Heat oil and fry until browned and crisp on both sides; drain.
Mix remaining garlic, onion, Thai chilies, green onion, sugar, remaining pepper, and salt for the dipping sauce. Serve with liempo and steamed rice.

intro: Pork Hamonado is a sweet-savory pineapple-braised pork belly dish best served with hot rice.
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, sliced into serving pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat; fry pork belly for 2 minutes per side.
Add soy sauce, pineapple juice, half the pineapple chunks, garlic, and peppercorns; cover and bring to a boil.
Lower to a gentle simmer and cook about 60 minutes, adding water as needed, until the pork is tender.
Stir in remaining pineapple and brown sugar; season with salt and cook 2 minutes.
Serve warm with rice.

intro: Baked Relyenong Tahong pairs juicy mussels with a savory pork, bacon, and cheese filling.
steps: Heat the oven to 370°F (188°C) and line a baking tray.
Mix pork, seasonings, bacon, parsley, cheese, egg, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Spoon 1–1 1/2 tablespoons filling into each mussel half-shell and arrange them on the tray.
Bake for 30–40 minutes, until the pork is cooked through and lightly browned.
Serve hot with banana ketchup.

intro: Inangit is a coconut-rich sticky rice cake with a lightly browned banana-leaf crust.
ingredients: 2 cups glutinous rice, washed and drained
1 cup water, plus more as needed
Banana leaves, for lining and covering
steps: Simmer the coconut milk, 200 ml coconut cream, 1 cup water, salt, and sugar over medium heat.
Stir in the rice and cook until expanded and most liquid is absorbed, stirring often to prevent sticking.
Line a covered skillet with banana leaves; spread in the rice and cover with more leaves. Cook over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes.
Invert the rice onto a plate, return it to the skillet, and cook the second side for 15 to 20 minutes, until browned in spots.
Whisk rice flour with 1/4 cup water. Simmer remaining coconut cream with brown sugar over medium-low heat; stir in slurry until thick.
Cut the Inangit into portions and serve warm with the coconut sauce.

intro: Bulanghang is a rich coconut-braised beef dish with tender brisket, tendons, and green chillies.
steps: Season the brisket generously with salt. Simmer tendons in 4 cups water over low heat for 1 1/2 hours.
Heat oil in another pot and brown brisket on all sides. Add garlic, shallots, and annatto; sauté until fragrant.
Add the tendons and their broth, plus enough water to cover. Simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Raise heat and reduce the broth until thick but not dry. Add coconut milk, chillies, and sugar; simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in evaporated milk and simmer on low for 5 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Camaron Rebosado is crisp battered shrimp with a bright lemon seasoning.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season the shrimp with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper; set aside while preparing the batter.
Whisk 1 cup flour, baking powder, fish sauce, cold water, and egg until smooth.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Coat each shrimp in the remaining flour, dip into batter, then fry until deeply golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with sweet chilli sauce, if desired.

intro: Rellenong Ampalaya pairs tender bitter gourd with a savory baked pork filling.
ingredients: 2 large bitter gourds (ampalaya), cored and cut into 2-inch sections
steps: Salt the inner surfaces of the ampalaya generously and rest for 2 hours; rinse well and drain.
Mix pork, carrot, egg, breadcrumbs, onion, garlic, chilli flakes, salt, and black pepper until evenly combined.
Pack the pork mixture firmly into the ampalaya sections and arrange them on a parchment-lined baking tray.
Bake at 180°C for 25 minutes, until the filling is cooked through, then serve hot.

intro: A savory tomato penne tossed with sweet-salty Skinless Longganisa and cheddar.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until the onion is soft.
Add tomato sauce and bring it to a boil. Stir in Italian seasoning and red pepper flakes.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, then toss in the cooked penne; cook for 1 minute.
Halve the longganisa, add it to the pasta, and toss until evenly coated.
Season with salt and pepper, fold in cheddar, and serve warm.

intro: Bangus Filipino Paksiw is a tangy vinegar-poached milkfish layered with vegetables and aromatics.
ingredients: 3 1/2 lb milkfish, cleaned and sliced crosswise into serving pieces
steps: Heat a wide pan over medium heat and render the pork fat until it releases enough oil.
Turn off the heat; layer garlic, ginger, onions, and peppercorns in the pan.
Arrange milkfish, long green peppers, eggplant, and bitter melon over the aromatics.
Pour in vinegar, cover, bring to a boil, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water, return to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes until the fish and vegetables are cooked.
Season with fish sauce and serve with rice.

intro: This rich Cheese Ice Cream blends cream cheese and sharp cheddar into a familiar Filipino-style frozen dessert.
ingredients: 1 packet cream cheese, cut into small cubes
Yellow food colouring, a few drops
steps: Warm cream, cream cheese, milk, and sugar in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth and nearly boiling; do not let it boil.
Whisk about 1 cup hot cream mixture gradually into the yolks, then return the yolk mixture to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the custard coats the back of a spoon; remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla and yellow food colouring. Cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Churn with the shredded cheddar according to the ice-cream maker instructions, about 30–35 minutes. Serve soft or freeze at least 6 hours for firm scoops.

intro: Hi-Bol is a hearty Ilocano-style noodle soup loaded with beef cuts, pinapaitan mix, and warming aromatics.
ingredients: 350 g cooked ox tripe, sliced small
500 g lusay or fresh cooked yellow noodles
1 thumb-sized piece ginger, crushed and finely sliced
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, ginger, and onions until aromatic.
Add tripe, heart, tendon, and brisket. Stir-fry over very high heat for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Add beef stock, whole siling haba, and cayenne pepper. Boil, then simmer 45 to 60 minutes until the meats are tender.
Stir in pinapaitan mix and sukang Iloco; simmer 10 minutes. Season with fish sauce, salt if needed, and black pepper.
Divide noodles among six bowls. Ladle over hot soup and meat, then top each with spring onions and two egg halves.

intro: This creamy macaroni salad is loaded with bacon, egg, green peas, and crisp vegetables.
steps: Bring water to a boil, add 1 teaspoon salt and macaroni, and cook for 7 minutes; drain and cool.
Whisk mayonnaise with remaining salt, sugar, and pepper in a large bowl.
Stir in onion, celery, and green peas until coated.
Gently fold in macaroni, then fold in eggs and bacon without breaking them up.
Taste, adjust seasoning if needed, and serve chilled or at room temperature.

intro: Chicken Chop Suey is a colorful wok dish of vegetables, offal, shrimp, and quail eggs in a light savory sauce.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, cut into squares
1 qt ice water, for shocking vegetables
steps: Boil the blanching water. Cook carrot 30 seconds; add snow peas, corn, pepper, and cauliflower for 1 minute, then cabbage for 1 minute.
Shock vegetables in ice water for 2 minutes, then drain. Blanch shrimp in the same water until orange; set aside.
Boil gizzards until tender, then drain. Heat oil in a wok; sauté garlic until light brown and onion until soft.
Add liver and cook 3 minutes until lightly browned. Add gizzards, oyster sauce, vegetables, and Maggi Magic Sarap; stir-fry 1 minute.
Add quail eggs, shrimp, and mushrooms; cook gently for 2 minutes. Stir cornstarch with 3 tbsp water, add, and cook until coating thickens.

intro: This rich Chicken Sisig combines grilled chicken, liver, mayonnaise, and a sizzling egg topping.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs grilled chicken breast, finely chopped
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté onion until soft.
Add chicken liver and cook until browned.
Stir in chopped grilled chicken and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add garlic powder, soy sauce, salt, pepper, and mayonnaise; stir immediately until creamy and combined.
Heat a sizzling plate or cast-iron pan, melt butter in it, then add the sisig.
Crack the egg over the sisig, arrange serrano peppers on top, and serve immediately.

intro: Ensaladang Lato is a crisp sea-grape salad with a sharp cane-vinegar and bagoong dressing.
steps: Place the rinsed lato, tomatoes, onion, and bagoong in a serving bowl.
Stir the sugar into the cane vinegar until dissolved.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad and gently toss.
Let stand for at least 15 minutes before serving.

intro: This Binagoongan combines crackly pork belly, savory bagoong, charred eggplant, and fresh mango.
ingredients: 1 can lemonade soda, such as 7-Up or Sprite
steps: Salt the pork belly heavily, wrap, and refrigerate overnight. Rinse off the salt before cooking.
Pressure-cook pork with whole garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, soy sauce, soda, and enough water to cover for 20 to 30 minutes after pressure builds.
Dry the tender pork, chill at least 12 hours, then deep-fry cold pork in hot oil until golden and crisp. Drain, cool, and cube.
Sauté minced garlic and shallot in pork lard until golden. Stir in bagoong, vinegar, sugar, cayenne, and black pepper; cook 3 to 5 minutes until dark red.
Toss pork cubes in the bagoong sauce. Top with eggplant, mangoes, tomatoes, white onion, and spring onions.

intro: Crisp bangus belly and prawns are finished in a bright sweet-and-sour escabeche sauce.
steps: Pan-fry bangus belly in hot oil for about 4 minutes per side, adjusting for thickness; set aside.
Leave 3 tablespoons oil in the pan and sauté garlic, red onion, and ginger until aromatic.
Add capsicum, carrot, and prawns; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Whisk vinegar, cornstarch, water, sugar, salt, pepper, and tomato purée, then pour into the pan.
Add pineapple and tomato; bring to a boil and simmer for 2 minutes.
Return bangus to the sauce, add spring onions, simmer 30 seconds, then serve.

intro: Copycat Palabok d’e Tisoy layers bihon with smoky prawn sauce and generous toppings.
ingredients: 500 g thin rice noodles or bihon
steps: Cook bihon according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Grill prawn shells until red-orange and lightly charred. Blend with 3 cups water, press through a fine sieve, and reserve the prawn broth.
Dissolve annatto in 1/4 cup hot water, then combine it with prawn broth and fish sauce.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil; cook pork for 3 minutes. Add broth mixture and smoked fish.
Whisk cornstarch with a little water, add it to the sauce, and simmer until thickened; thin with water if necessary.
Pour sauce over noodles and top with lechon kawali, calamares, chicharon, spring onions, eggs, and fried garlic. Serve with calamansi.

intro: Chicken Nilaga with Kalabasa is a clear, comforting soup with tender chicken and sweet squash.
ingredients: 2 lbs skinless chicken thighs, cut into serving pieces
1 small butternut squash or kalabasa, peeled and cubed
steps: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add onion, peppercorns, and chicken; cover and boil over medium heat for 30 minutes, adding broth or water if needed.
Add kalabasa and cabbage, then cook for 5–8 minutes until the squash is tender.
Stir in baby bok choy and patis, then cook for 1 minute until the greens wilt.
Ladle into bowls and serve with rice.

intro: Chicken Binakol is a light coconut-water chicken soup scented with ginger and lemongrass.
ingredients: Sea salt or fish sauce, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season chicken with salt and pepper; collect coconut water and scrape the coconut meat from both coconuts.
Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat; brown chicken on all sides, then transfer to a plate.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in the same pot until fragrant.
Add coconut water, lemongrass, chicken, and firm coconut meat; boil, then simmer on low for 25 minutes until tender.
Add chili leaves and soft coconut meat, if using; simmer 2 minutes.
Season with salt or fish sauce and serve in bowls or coconut shells.

intro: Crispy Tadyang ng Baka combines tender braised beef riblets with a bright, spicy vinegar dip.
ingredients: 1 kg beef spareribs, cut into riblets
steps: Cover ribs with water, boil until scum rises, then drain and rinse the beef.
Return ribs to the pot with soy sauce, crushed garlic, star anise, bay leaves, 1 tablespoon sugar, peppercorns, and water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 2 hours until fork-tender; drain and cool.
Pat ribs dry, refrigerate on paper towels for at least 4 hours, then deep-fry in hot oil until crisp.
Drain on paper towels; mix vinegar, chillies, shallot, minced garlic, remaining sugar, and pepper, then serve alongside.

intro: Cold rice, pork belly, soy sauce, and fried garlic make a hearty Filipino breakfast rice.
ingredients: 4 to 5 cups cooked white rice, preferably cold
steps: Toss pork with soy sauce and marinate for 30 minutes. Mix the cold rice gently with salt.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Fry garlic until medium brown, then remove and set aside.
Cook pork with its marinade over low to medium heat for 5 minutes.
Increase to medium-high heat and stir-fry rice for 5–7 minutes, stirring almost continuously until hot and separated.
Stir in half the fried garlic for 1 minute. Plate and top with the remaining garlic.

intro: Aristocrat Style Chicken Barbecue is sweet, tangy, charcoal-grilled chicken finished with a glossy sauce.
steps: Mix tomato catsup, soda, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, lemon juice, and black pepper for the marinade.
Prick chicken all over, coat with marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 24 hours.
Bring chicken to room temperature. Drain well and reserve the marinade.
Whisk water and cornstarch until smooth, then combine with reserved marinade and oil. Simmer until thickened.
Grill chicken over charcoal without basting until nearly cooked through. Brush with sauce and grill 1 minute per side before serving.

intro: Pancit Habhab is a saucy Lucban-style noodle dish served on banana leaf with a bright citrus finish.
ingredients: 500 g Lukban miki noodles or Shanghai noodles
4 to 6 cups pork or chicken stock
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Calamansi, lime, or vinegar, for serving
Cleaned banana leaves, passed over an open flame
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat; stir-fry pork until browned.
Add onion and garlic; stir-fry 2 minutes, then add carrot, sayote, and liver for 1 minute.
Remove the meat and vegetables. Add 3 cups stock and soy sauce to the wok and bring to a boil.
Add noodles and cook 5 minutes, adding stock as needed until tender and saucy.
Return meat and vegetables; season with fish sauce and black pepper, then toss well.
Serve on banana leaves with calamansi, lime, or vinegar.

intro: A sweet, peppery Filipino fishball sauce with a gentle chili heat.
steps: Whisk flour, water, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, salt, and pepper in a saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously, until the sauce reaches a simmer.
Add labuyo and keep stirring for 3 to 5 minutes, until thickened.
Cool slightly before serving as a dip for fishballs.

intro: Tupig is a lightly sweet, coconut-studded glutinous rice cake grilled in banana leaves.
steps: Soak glutinous rice in enough water to cover overnight at room temperature.
Drain thoroughly, then press the rice in cheesecloth to remove excess moisture.
Process rice into a fine paste, blending in coconut milk and brown sugar until smooth.
Fold in young coconut strips.
Spoon 2 tablespoons onto each banana leaf, roll tightly, and fold the ends closed.
Grill over charcoal, turning often, until every side of the leaf is charred; cool briefly before serving.

intro: Donya Aurora Eggs are hard-boiled egg halves rebuilt with savory pork relleno and fried golden.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mash the cooked yolks with pork, raisins, capsicum, shallots, garlic, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Press filling into each egg-white cavity, shaping it into a complete egg with an egg-white base and packed pork half.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C.
Dip each filled egg in beaten egg and fry until golden brown and the pork filling is cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet chilli sauce.

intro: Ginisang Puso ng Saging pairs tender banana heart with pork and sotanghon in a savory sauté.
steps: Thinly slice the banana heart. Soak in vinegar, 1 cup water, and salt for 10–20 minutes; drain and squeeze out the liquid.
Soak sotanghon in 2 cups water for 12 minutes, then drain.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil until soft. Add pork and cook until browned.
Add 1 cup water, cover, and cook over low-medium heat until the liquid evaporates.
Sauté banana heart for 2 minutes. Add sotanghon, remaining 1 cup water, and the pork cube; cover and simmer until reduced by half and tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper; add a little water if needed to soften the banana heart, then serve with rice.

intro: Low-Carb Breaded Pinatisang Baboy is crisp pork flavored with patis and lime.
steps: Season pork with black pepper, lime juice, and patis; marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat oil for deep-frying over medium heat.
Coat each pork slice in almond flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat again in almond flour.
Fry for 4 to 6 minutes, until golden brown, crisp, and cooked through. Drain and serve.

intro: Beef Kare-Kare pairs tender beef with a nutty, annatto-tinted sauce and crisp blanched vegetables.
ingredients: 1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch lengths
steps: Heat oil and sauté onion until soft, then add garlic. Season with black pepper and brown the beef lightly.
Stir in ground peanuts and cook for 2 minutes. Add beef broth, boil, cover, and simmer 60 to 90 minutes until tender.
Blanch string beans for 2 minutes, then chill in ice water. Blanch eggplant and bok choy in batches the same way.
Mix annatto powder, water, and glutinous rice powder. Add to tender beef with fish sauce and cook over medium 3 to 5 minutes until thick.
Transfer to a bowl and arrange vegetables alongside. Serve with warm rice and bagoong alamang, if desired.

intro: Ginisang Talong with Bagoong is a rich pork and eggplant sauté balanced by cane vinegar and bagoong alamang.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add minced pork and cook, stirring often, until light brown.
Add tomato and cook until soft and saucy.
Add eggplant, water, vinegar, sugar, and bagoong alamang; boil, then simmer on low for 5 minutes.
Season with black pepper, mix well, and cook 3 minutes more until eggplant is tender.
Serve hot.

intro: Lelot Paro is a prawn-shell broth porridge enriched with century egg and fried garlic.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Roast prawn shells on a foil-lined tray until red-orange and lightly charred. Blend with 1 cup water, add remaining water, strain, and press out the broth.
Devein prawns and season with salt and black pepper. Stir-fry in oil over medium heat for about 2 minutes; remove.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in the pot until fragrant. Stir-fry glutinous rice for 1 minute.
Add prawn broth, bring to a boil while stirring, then simmer on low for about 40 minutes until porridge-soft; add water if too thick.
Return prawns, season with fish sauce and pepper, then bowl up with century egg, spring onions, fried garlic, and lemon.

intro: Tuslob Buwa is a thick, bubbling Cebu-style pork brain dip served with puso.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat and add the prepared pork brain.
Mash and stir the brain continuously until it breaks down into a smooth mixture.
Add soy sauce, shrimp paste, salt, and pepper; stir well.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, until reduced, thick, and visibly bubbly.
Serve hot with puso for dipping.

intro: Sinarsahang Manok is a rich tomato-braised chicken dish with colorful vegetables and a subtly sweet sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a pan and flash-cook the capsicum, sugar snap peas, and green peas for 45 seconds. Set them aside.
Add more oil to a large pot. Brown the chicken over medium-high heat for roughly 3 minutes on each side, then transfer it out.
Cook the garlic and onion in the same pot until fragrant and the onion turns translucent.
Add the soy sauce, tomato sauce, and soda. Once gently bubbling, put the chicken back in, cover, and simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Mix in the tomato paste and liver spread, if using. Leave uncovered and simmer until the sauce becomes thick and full-bodied.
Fold in the reserved vegetables and cook for 2 minutes to warm through. Season with salt and black pepper, then serve with rice.

intro: Ube Ice Cream is a creamy churned custard with the earthy sweetness of cooked purple yam.
steps: Warm cream, milk, and sugar in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves and the mixture is nearly boiling.
Whisk about 1 cup hot cream mixture gradually into egg yolks, then return the yolks to the saucepan.
Cook while stirring until the custard coats the back of a spoon; do not boil.
Transfer to a heatproof container; tint with red and blue food coloring, then stir in vanilla.
Cool completely and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Churn the custard with mashed ube according to the ice-cream maker directions, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Serve soft, or freeze at least 6 hours for a firmer scoop.

intro: Bagoong Rice is a quick, savory fried rice topped with pork belly, green mango, and scallions.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons bagoong guisado or bottled shrimp paste, divided
steps: Heat a dry frying pan and sear pork belly for 2 to 5 minutes, until it releases its fat.
Stir 1 tablespoon bagoong into the pork, cook 1 minute, then remove pork from the pan.
Heat cooking oil in the same pan. Cook garlic for 15 seconds, then fry remaining bagoong over medium heat for 30 seconds.
Add rice and gently toss for 10 minutes, scraping the pan bottom occasionally until evenly seasoned.
Serve rice topped with pork, green mango, and scallions.

intro: Masi are chewy black-and-white glutinous rice balls with a sweet roasted peanut filling.
ingredients: 1/2 cup black glutinous rice flour (pirurutong or tapol)
Banana leaves or parchment paper squares, optional
steps: Combine crushed peanuts and brown sugar or muscovado for the filling.
Mix white and black glutinous rice flours with salt. Gradually add water until a smooth, pliable dough forms.
Flatten 2 to 3 tbsp dough into a disc. Add 1 tsp filling, seal the edges, and roll into a smooth ball.
Boil water, add the balls gently, and stir lightly to prevent sticking. Cook until floating for 1 to 2 minutes.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve warm, plain or wrapped in banana leaves or parchment.

intro: A chilled tamilok kinilaw dressed with coconut vinegar, calamansi, onion, and chili; this traditional preparation uses no heat.
ingredients: 250 g prepared, cleaned tamilok, kept chilled
steps: Keep the prepared tamilok chilled and drain any excess liquid.
Mix the vinegar and calamansi juice with the sliced onion, chili, and a pinch of salt.
Toss the chilled tamilok with the dressing in a clean bowl and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Serve immediately while cold, with the dressing spooned over.

intro: These homemade Fish Balls have a springy fish paste center and a crisp fried finish.
ingredients: 500 g cold or slightly frozen fish fillet, cut into pieces
1/2 cup potato starch, tapioca starch, or cornstarch
steps: Process fish with onion powder, garlic powder, salt, sugar, pepper, oil, flour, starch, baking powder, and egg white.
Gradually add ice water while processing for 2 to 3 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and homogeneous.
Oil one hand and squeeze small balls through a thumb-and-finger opening; use a spoon to drop them into 40°C lukewarm water.
Transfer balls to gently simmering water, never a rolling boil, and cook 20 minutes. Drain in a colander.
Cool before freezing, or deep-fry until crisp and serve with fish ball sauce.

intro: Beef Sopas is a creamy, hearty macaroni soup enriched with tender beef cheeks and corned beef.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a pot and sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add beef cheeks and brown them on all sides.
Add beef stock, carrot, and corned beef; boil, then simmer 40 minutes until beef is tender, adding water if needed.
Stir in macaroni, basil, and thyme; simmer 15 minutes until pasta is tender.
Add evaporated milk, bring just to a boil, immediately turn off the heat, and season with salt and pepper.

intro: Chicken Hamonado is a sweet-savory pineapple braise with browned drumettes and a sticky sauce.
steps: Marinate drumettes with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a wok and brown chicken on all sides. Remove the chicken and set aside.
Add more oil if needed; sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add soy sauce, pineapple juice, and sugar. Bring to a boil, return chicken, and simmer on low for 20 minutes.
Add pineapple chunks with their juice. Simmer on high 15 minutes until thickened; season with fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: A slow-simmered beef broth and tender brisket make this Manong-style Beef Mami deeply comforting.
ingredients: 2 whole beef leg bones, each cut into 3 to 4 pieces
steps: Cover bones and brisket with water, boil, then simmer for 15 minutes. Drain and rinse both thoroughly.
Sauté garlic in oil over medium heat, then sweat onions for a few minutes.
Add bones, peppercorns, and enough water to cover; boil, then simmer gently for 2 1/2 hours.
Cool broth, remove bones, strain, chill, and lift off the hardened fat.
Return broth, bones, and brisket to a pot; boil, then simmer for 1 hour. Season with salt or fish sauce and pepper.
Cook noodles according to package directions. Divide into bowls, add brisket and broth, garnish with spring onions, and serve with soy sauce and sriracha.

intro: Pan-fried pork chops simmer briefly in a smooth beef-stock cream sauce with mushrooms.
ingredients: 5 large pork shoulder chops, about 1-inch thick, halved
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pork with salt and pepper. Pan-fry in oil over medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side until cooked through; set aside.
Cook mushrooms in the same pan for 2 minutes, then set aside.
Melt butter over low heat and sauté garlic and onion until the onion is soft. Stir in flour to make a roux.
Whisk in beef stock gradually, then add cream and cook until a smooth sauce forms.
Return pork and mushrooms, simmer on low for 5 minutes, season, garnish with parsley, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

intro: Puto Pao is a fluffy steamed rice-cake-style bun filled with sweet-savory pork and topped with salted duck egg.
ingredients: 2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Sift flour, baking powder, and 1/2 cup sugar; stir in water and milk until lump-free.
Whip egg whites with cream of tartar to soft peaks; gradually add 1/3 cup sugar to stiff peaks, then fold into batter.
Sauté garlic in oil, brown pork, then simmer with soy sauce, brown sugar, and water for 45–60 minutes until tender.
Stir in cornstarch slurry over high heat, shred pork as liquid thickens, then cool the filling.
Boil steamer water with vinegar; grease molds, fill halfway with batter, add 2 teaspoons filling, cover with batter, and top with duck egg.
Steam 15 minutes with a cloth under the lid; cool slightly, unmold, and serve.

intro: Kinamunggayang Manok is a gingered chicken soup with banana blossom and malunggay.
ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken thighs and legs
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak shredded banana blossom in 3 cups water and salt for 2 hours, then drain.
Heat oil in a pot; sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add chicken and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes, browning all sides.
Add chicken stock, bring to a boil, then simmer 45 minutes for free-range chicken, or about 20 minutes for regular chicken.
Add banana blossom and simmer 10 minutes. Add malunggay, cover, simmer 5 minutes, then season with fish sauce and pepper.

intro: Ginisang Munggo is a hearty puréed mung bean soup with pork, tinapa, greens, and chicharon.
ingredients: 2 cups mung beans (monggo), washed and drained
3 tbsp fish sauce or 1 tbsp salt
2 cups spinach or bitter gourd leaves
steps: Boil mung beans in 5 cups water over medium heat; cover, lower heat, and simmer about 30 minutes until tender.
Purée the cooked beans with their liquid using an immersion blender or blender.
Heat oil in the pot; brown pork belly until fat renders, then sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until tender.
Add fish sauce and cook 1 minute, then stir in the mung bean purée.
Add 1 to 2 cups water if needed; simmer with ampalaya, celery, and tinapa for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in chicharon and spinach; season with salt if needed, turn off heat, and serve with rice.

intro: Pancit Chami is a thick, savory stir-fried noodle dish packed with chicken, prawns, and vegetables.
ingredients: 500 g miki noodles or thick yellow noodles
500 g boiled chicken thighs, sliced into strips
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak fresh miki or thick yellow noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes; drain.
Heat a wok over high heat with oil; stir-fry chicken and prawns 1 minute, then remove.
Add oil if needed; sauté shallots and garlic, then stir-fry carrot for 1 minute.
