Add cabbage and chilies; stir-fry 1 minute, then add noodles and sugar snap peas.
Add stock, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and brown sugar; stir-fry 2 minutes, return chicken and prawns, and cook until thick.
Season with fish sauce and pepper; serve with lemon or calamansi.

intro: Chicken Soup with Misua and Patola is a light, soothing noodle soup with tender vegetables.
steps: Boil chicken in 5 cups water over medium heat for 15 to 18 minutes. Remove, cool, shred, and reserve the stock.
Sauté garlic in oil until light brown, then cook onion until tender. Add shredded chicken and sauté 2 minutes.
Add reserved stock, remaining water, and chicken cube. Cover and simmer over medium heat for 12 minutes.
Add patola and hot pepper leaves; cook 5 minutes. Add miswa and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in scallions, fish sauce, and pepper; cook 2 minutes and serve.

intro: Crispy Lechon Belly with Bacon is a tightly rolled pork roast with crackling skin and savory bacon filling.
steps: Prick the pork skin thoroughly. Combine garlic powder, black pepper, and onion powder.
Season the meat side with Knorr Liquid Seasoning and the dry seasoning mixture, rubbing it in evenly.
Layer bacon and spring onions over the meat. Roll tightly, secure with kitchen twine, then brush skin with vinegar and sprinkle with salt.
Air-fry or turbo-broil at 325°F for 90 minutes. Dab excess skin oil, raise heat to 400°F, and cook until crisp.
Rest briefly, slice, and serve with lechon sauce or spiced vinegar.

intro: Tinolang Isda is a ginger-scented fish soup finished with bok choy and spring onions.
ingredients: 1 kg fish, scaled, gutted, and cut into sections
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
steps: Season fish generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a pot and fry fish until browned on both sides; remove carefully.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in the same pot until onion softens.
Return fish, add stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 12 minutes.
Add bok choy and spring onions, cover, and simmer 3 minutes; season with fish sauce and pepper.

intro: Tuna-filled Relyenong Talong turns eggplant rings into crisp, savory skillet patties.
steps: Cut eggplants into 1/2-inch rounds, remove the centers to make rings, and chop the removed eggplant.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil; sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add tuna and chopped eggplant and cook 3 to 5 minutes.
Season with Knorr Liquid Seasoning, cool, then mix with eggs, half the carrot, green onion, and bell pepper.
Heat remaining oil and fry eggplant rings for 1 minute on one side.
Turn rings, add remaining vegetables and tuna filling, then cook over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Top with remaining vegetables, turn carefully, and cook 2 to 3 minutes more before serving.

intro: Creamy Mango Jelly Salad combines tropical jelly, nata de coco, tapioca, and mangoes.
ingredients: 2 jars nata de coco, 340 g each, drained
1 can mango condensed milk, 410 ml, adjusted to taste
steps: Whisk water, mango purée, gelatine, and sugar in a saucepan until dissolved.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, then pour into a flat container and let set.
Cut the firm mango jelly into cubes or strips.
Whip chilled all-purpose cream to stiff peaks.
Fold jelly, tapioca pearls, nata de coco, whipped cream, and mango condensed milk together, adding condensed milk gradually to taste.
Chill for 1 to 2 hours, then gently fold in mango cubes just before serving.

intro: Daing Silog is a classic breakfast plate of fried daing na bangus, sinangag, egg, and atchara.
steps: Have the prepared daing na bangus and sinangag ready for serving.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the eggs to your preferred doneness.
Arrange daing na bangus, garlic fried rice, and one egg on each plate.
Add papaya atchara if using, scatter with scallions, and serve.

intro: Monggo Guisado with Dilis and Malunggay is a comforting mung bean stew with savory dried anchovies.
ingredients: 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, or to taste
steps: Boil mung beans in 5 cups water for 35 to 40 minutes until soft and expanded, adding water as needed.
Heat oil in another pot. Sauté garlic and onion, add tomato, and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in dilis, then add cooked mung beans and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add 1 to 2 cups water, bring to a boil, and simmer over low-medium heat for 5 to 8 minutes.
Add malunggay, fish sauce, and black pepper. Cook 1 to 2 minutes more, then serve hot.

intro: Humba is a thick, sweet-salty pork braise enriched with salted black beans, banana blossoms, and eggs.
ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder or belly, cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic until golden, then remove and reserve.
Brown pork on all sides in the same pot.
Add water, vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, star anise, reserved garlic, and bay leaves; boil, then simmer 30 minutes.
Add banana blossoms and salted black beans; simmer 30 minutes more until pork is tender and sauce is thick, adding water if needed.
Add hard-boiled eggs and black pepper; simmer 5 minutes, then season with salt if needed.

intro: Apan Apan is a tangy, savory kangkong dish enriched with tulapho and bagoong alamang.
ingredients: 2 bunches kangkong, leaves and tender stems only
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion is soft.
Stir in bagoong alamang, add vinegar, and bring to a boil.
Add kangkong and tulapho, then toss with soy sauce for 2 minutes, until the greens wilt.
Season with salt if needed and black pepper, then serve immediately.

intro: Thin seared beef is folded into a creamy mushroom sauce with onions and lemon.
ingredients: 1 kg chuck or rump steak, thinly sliced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Tenderize beef, season with salt and pepper, then drain thoroughly and bring to room temperature.
Sear beef in hot oil over very high heat for 2 minutes per side; remove before it overcooks.
Sauté onion rings briefly in the same pan and remove. Cook mushrooms, adding oil if needed, then remove.
Cook butter and flour over low heat. Gradually whisk in beef stock, add cream, and simmer gently until smooth.
Return beef, mushrooms, and onions; simmer 2 minutes, season, turn off heat, drizzle with lemon juice, and serve.

intro: Pork Tinola is a warming ginger broth with tender pork, chayote, spinach, and rice washing.
steps: Heat oil in a deep pot and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until the onion is soft.
Add pork and cook about 5 minutes until browned. Stir in black pepper.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil. Add 1 cup rice washing, cover, and simmer 45–60 minutes until pork is tender.
Add remaining rice washing and return to a boil. Add chayote and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, add spinach, cover, turn off the heat, and let residual heat wilt the leaves before serving.

intro: Fried Galunggong is a simple, crisp fish dish that is especially good with rice.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season galunggong generously inside and out with salt and black pepper.
Heat enough oil in a wok or skillet for frying over medium-high heat.
Fry fish in batches without crowding until golden brown on both sides and cooked through.
Drain briefly and serve hot.

intro: Inihaw na Isda with Aligue Sauce combines smoky grilled fish with a rich, sharp crab-fat sauce.
ingredients: 1 large snapper or tilapia, cleaned and gutted
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/4 cup cane vinegar or lemon juice
steps: Prepare a charcoal grill. Season fish with salt and pepper, then fill the cavity with lemon slices.
Wrap fish in banana leaves if using. Grill 10 to 15 minutes per side, until opaque and flakes easily.
Meanwhile, heat oil over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic for 2 to 3 minutes until softened.
Add aligue and stir constantly over low heat for 5 minutes. Add chillies, vinegar or lemon juice, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Cook 5 to 10 minutes until sauce thickens. Serve alongside or spooned over the grilled fish.

intro: Kulawong Talong is smoky grilled eggplant in a deeply coconutty sauce with ginger and chilies.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Prick eggplants with a fork, season with salt, and grill whole until charred and fully soft; cool and peel.
Mix coconut threads with half the coconut milk; bake at 200°C until browned.
Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat; sauté garlic, ginger, and shallots until fragrant.
Add remaining coconut milk, coconut cream, vinegar, and browned coconut threads; boil, then simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Strain the liquid into another pan; add eggplants, mash lightly, and simmer 2 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, top with chilies, and serve.

intro: Isaw brings grilled pork intestine and chicken gizzard skewers together with a sweet-savory baste and spicy vinegar dip.
ingredients: 1 kg mixed pork intestine and chicken gizzard
steps: Mix 1 cup vinegar, onion, minced garlic, chillies, 1/4 cup sugar, pepper, and 1 teaspoon salt for the dipping sauce.
Boil intestines and gizzards with 1 1/2 cups vinegar, 1 1/2 liters water, peppercorns, 1/4 cup salt, whole garlic, and bay leaves.
Cook intestines about 30 minutes and gizzards about 45 minutes; drain and cool.
Slice intestines into 1.5 cm pieces, halve gizzards, and thread four pieces onto each skewer.
Mix soy sauce, 1/2 cup water, oil, and 1 tablespoon sugar for basting; grill over hot charcoal, basting, for 3–5 minutes until lightly charred.
Serve immediately with the chilli vinegar dip.

intro: Buttery cashew Polvoron is a crumbly Filipino milk candy wrapped for sharing.
steps: Toast flour in a large dry skillet over medium heat, stirring constantly, for about 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Remove from heat and thoroughly mix in powdered milk, sugar, and ground cashews.
Pour in melted butter and stir until the mixture is evenly moistened.
Pack into a polvoron mold, release each piece, and wrap in Japanese paper, tissue paper, or cellophane.

intro: Lapu-Lapu de la Reyna is chilled steamed fish dressed in mayonnaise and bright pickled vegetable garnishes.
ingredients: 1 whole grouper (lapu-lapu) or snapper (maya-maya), scaled, cleaned, and gutted
4 hard-boiled eggs, yolks and whites separated and finely chopped
steps: Season fish with salt, pepper, and lemon juice; stand 15 minutes. Stuff its cavity with squeezed lemon skins and spring onions.
Steam for 25 minutes or until the flesh flakes easily. Remove stuffing and cool fish to room temperature or colder.
Boil water, sugar, and vinegar. Blanch carrot in a sieve for 30 seconds, drain, and cool; repeat with capsicum.
Place fish on a platter and coat with mayonnaise. Decorate with capsicum, carrot, yolks, relish, red onion, and egg whites.
Serve chilled or at cool room temperature.

intro: Ginisang Patola is a light pork-and-mushroom sauté with tender sponge gourd.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add tomato and cook until softened.
Add minced pork and cook for 1 minute, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add mushrooms and cook for another minute.
Pour in chicken stock, raise heat to high, and bring to a boil.
Add patola and cook on high for about 5 minutes, until tender and liquid has reduced. Season with fish sauce and white pepper.

intro: Special Pork Kaldereta is a hearty tomato-braised pork stew finished with liver spread and cheese.
ingredients: 1 small red bell pepper, cut into squares
1 small green bell pepper, cut into squares
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until the onion turns translucent. Brown the pork lightly.
Add tomato sauce, water, and pork cube. Cover and cook over low-medium heat until pork is tender.
Add carrot and olives; cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in potato and bell peppers. Add liver spread, cover, and cook 5 to 7 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a platter and top with Cheddar.

intro: Baked Tahong tops steamed green mussels with garlicky crumbs and melted cheese.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Colby or other quick-melting cheese, grated
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cover mussels in a pan with 1/4 cup water and cook over medium heat until all shells open. Drain, cool, and discard top shells.
Melt butter over medium heat. Sauté garlic over low heat until golden, add breadcrumbs, and stir until crisp.
Stir parsley into the crumb mixture for 1 minute. Combine Colby and Parmesan.
Place 1 teaspoon crumbs and 1 teaspoon cheese mixture on each mussel.
Grill at 180°C for about 10 minutes, until cheese melts. Season with black pepper and serve.

intro: Grilled Pork Ala Pobre pairs charred pork belly steaks with a savory gravy and crisp fried garlic.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pork belly steaks with salt and pepper; let stand at room temperature while preparing the sauce.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until the onion is soft.
Stir in flour until evenly combined.
Whisk in beef stock, roast drippings, and liquid seasoning; simmer on low 30 minutes until smooth and thickened.
Grill pork steaks to your preferred doneness.
Plate pork, spoon over gravy, and finish generously with fried garlic.

intro: Copycat Ribchon Baby Back Baboy uses a fragrant lemongrass marinade and slow charcoal grilling for tender, smoky ribs.
ingredients: 2 kg baby back ribs, cut into large slabs
steps: Purée lemongrass, spring onions, onion, garlic, peppercorns, brown sugar, salt, soy sauce, and oil until smooth.
Coat ribs thoroughly, seal with remaining marinade, and refrigerate 12–18 hours.
Remove ribs from refrigeration 1 hour before grilling.
Set a covered charcoal grill for indirect heat at 180°C (356°F); loosely wrap ribs in foil and grill 2–2 1/2 hours until tender, misting with water if dry.
Increase to direct high heat and grill ribs 3 minutes per side until browned; rest 10 minutes before serving.

intro: Tofu Green Bean Stir Fry is a fast savory-sweet dish with crisp beans and crunchy fried tofu.
ingredients: 250 g green beans, trimmed and sliced
steps: Deep-fry tofu in 180°C oil until golden and crisp. Drain well.
Heat a little oil in a wok and sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add green beans and chilli; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, peanut butter, lime juice, and maple syrup. Stir-fry until evenly coated, adding a little water if needed.
Add tofu and sesame oil, then stir-fry 1 minute. Serve hot.

intro: Sopas ala Pobre is a deeply simmered beef-bone soup finished with misua and malunggay.
ingredients: 2 kg meaty beef leg bones, cut into small sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onions, and optional turmeric until fragrant.
Add beef bones and salt. Pour in beef stock, then add enough water to cover the bones.
Bring to a boil, reduce to low heat, and simmer about 2 1/2 hours until the broth is rich.
Add misua and malunggay, season with fish sauce and pepper, and simmer 10 minutes until noodles are tender.
Serve hot.

intro: Ice Buko with Monggo is a creamy coconut-and-red-mung-bean frozen treat.
steps: Mix condensed milk, all-purpose cream, and coconut strings in a large bowl until combined.
Add coconut juice and sugar, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Spoon 1 1/2 tablespoons red mung beans into each mold, then fill with coconut mixture just below the rim.
Cover molds with foil, pierce the center, insert popsicle sticks, and freeze for at least 4 hours or overnight.

intro: This Copycat Chicken Joy pairs crisp seasoned chicken legs with a creamy chicken gravy.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups chicken drippings from roasted chicken
steps: Whisk 1 1/2 cups milk and egg in a large bowl. Set aside.
Combine garlic, warm water, 2 tablespoons salt, and 1 teaspoon MSG; brine chicken for no longer than 30 minutes, then discard brine.
Transfer chicken to the milk-egg mixture. Heat shortening to 180°C.
Mix cornstarch, flour, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, garlic powder, onion powder, five-spice powder, and remaining MSG.
Coat chicken in small batches by shaking it in the covered coating container, then deep-fry in batches for 10 minutes.
Whisk leftover coating mix, stock, drippings, 1/4 cup milk, and cream; simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until thick. Serve with chicken.

intro: Copycat Savory Chicken is soy-marinated roast chicken with crisp skin and a lightly spiced peanut gravy.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pulse roughly chopped lemongrass, spring onions, garlic, soy sauce, water, fish sauce, white pepper, and five-spice; rest 30 minutes, then strain.
Marinate chicken with strained mixture, pounded lemongrass, and bay leaves overnight in the refrigerator.
Bring chicken to room temperature for 1 hour; drain, then combine reserved marinade with sesame oil for basting.
Roast at 220°C for 1 1/2 hours, basting every 15 minutes, until juices run clear between leg and thigh.
For gravy, cook peanut oil and flour over low heat until light brown; whisk in stock, peanut butter, five-spice, salt, and pepper until thick.
Heat peanut oil to 180°C; carefully pour over roasted chicken skin, then serve chicken hot with gravy.

intro: Piyalam Istah is golden fried fish simmered briefly in an aromatic turmeric, ginger, and lemongrass sauce.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized fresh turmeric, peeled and pounded
steps: Rub fish inside and out with turmeric powder. Rest 5 minutes, rinse, drain well, and season with salt.
Shallow-fry fish in oil over medium heat for 7 minutes per side, until golden with crisp edges; set aside.
Leave 3 tablespoons oil in the wok. Sauté garlic, onion, ginger, and fresh turmeric until fragrant.
Cook tomatoes until soft, then add lemongrass, chillies, fish, and water. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and serve.

intro: Baka Tula-sog is a bold beef stew balancing pineapple, bagoong alamang, curry, turmeric, and tablea.
ingredients: 1 kg stewing beef or brisket, cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season beef with salt and pepper, then brown in hot oil; set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion in the same pot, then add chillies and bagoong alamang for 1 minute.
Return beef and add turmeric, stock, vinegar, pineapple juice, tablea, curry powder, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours until beef is tender.
Raise heat to reduce sauce until thick, adjust seasoning, fold in pineapple chunks, and serve.

intro: Pata and Beans is a slow-simmered pork hock and navy bean stew with a sweet, tangy tomato sauce.
ingredients: 500 g white or navy beans, soaked overnight
1 kg pork hock (pata), cut into sections
steps: Heat oil in a pot and brown pork hock on all sides. Transfer to a plate.
Sauté garlic and onion in the same pot until fragrant.
Return pork hock and add drained beans, ketchup, tomato paste, tomato puree, beef stock, sugar, vinegar, mustard, pepper, and cinnamon.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for about 2 hours until pork and beans are tender.
Check liquid occasionally and add water if needed. Serve when the sauce is thick and glossy.

intro: Porbidang Kangkong braises leafy kangkong in a spicy, rich coconut sauce.
ingredients: 1 large bunch kangkong leaves, rinsed and cleaned
steps: Separate kangkong leaves from stems and cut the stems into smaller pieces.
Sauté garlic and shallots in oil over medium heat, then stir-fry chilies for 30 seconds.
Add coconut milk and pork stock cube. Bring to a high boil until slightly thickened and coconut oil begins to render.
Add kangkong stems and simmer uncovered for 90 seconds.
Add leaves and simmer 1 minute.
Stir in coconut cream, simmer 1 minute, season with fish sauce, and garnish generously with fried garlic.

intro: Kamatis Bagoong at Lasona is a bright, salty tomato side dish for grilled or fried food.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine tomatoes, shallot, and bagoong isda in a bowl.
Mix in lemon juice and black pepper until evenly seasoned.
Top with sliced spring onions and serve immediately alongside grilled or fried meats.

intro: Tortang Okra makes tender sliced okra into crisp-edged, savory egg fritters.
ingredients: 2 spring onions, chopped, white and green parts separated
steps: Whisk eggs, cornstarch, water, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic with the white spring onion parts.
Add okra and stir-fry over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Mix the cooked okra and green spring onion parts into the egg mixture.
Heat oil in a clean pan. Add about 2/3 cup mixture per fritter and flatten gently.
Cook over low heat for 3 minutes per side, until set and golden.

intro: Carne Frita is a high-heat seared beef dish with calamansi-soy flavor, quick onions, and sesame oil.
steps: Mix calamansi or lemon juice, soy sauce, black pepper, and garlic. Coat beef and marinate overnight.
Remove beef from the refrigerator 1 hour before cooking. Drain and squeeze dry, reserving the marinade.
Heat a lightly oiled wok over very high heat until smoking. Sear beef in batches without moving until browned, then turn and brown briefly.
Add 1/2 cup water to the wok to loosen browned bits. Boil, add reserved marinade and sugar, and reduce until thickened.
Add onions for 30 seconds, return beef, and toss with sesame oil. Remove from heat and serve.

intro: Caldereta Nueva braises beef in coconut, peanut butter, and tomato paste until richly tender.
ingredients: 1 kg beef ribs or stewing beef, cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and fry garlic until crisp and golden; remove for garnish. Sauté onion until soft.
Add beef and brown all over. Add beef stock, coconut milk, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Add carrots and simmer over very low heat about 1 1/2 hours, adding water if needed, until beef is tender.
Stir in peanut butter and tomato paste; simmer 15 minutes.
Add coconut cream, chillies, peas, and capsicum; simmer 15 minutes. Add potatoes, season with fish sauce and pepper, then top with fried garlic.

intro: Crispy Air Fried Liempo Pinakbet with Ube combines crackling pork belly with a hearty bagoong vegetable stew.
steps: Boil liempo in 5 cups water for 35 minutes; remove, cool, and reserve the pork stock.
Rub pork with salt and rest 10 minutes. Air-fry at 370°F for 18 minutes per side until crisp; slice.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and tomato until softened.
Add ube and kalabasa; sauté 2 minutes, then add 1 1/4 cups pork stock and bring to a boil.
Stir in Pork Cube and bagoong alamang; cover and cook 5 minutes.
Add talong and ampalaya for 2 minutes, then okra and sitaw for 7 to 10 minutes until tender.
Season with pepper, top with crispy liempo, and serve.

intro: Adobong Kambing is tender goat meat finished in a reduced soy-vinegar adobo sauce.
steps: Bring 3 cups water, ginger, onion, and salt to a boil. Add goat and simmer until tender; drain and discard the aromatics.
Heat oil in a wok and fry garlic until light brown. Pan-fry goat until lightly browned outside.
Add soy sauce, 1 cup water, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add vinegar, bring to a boil, and simmer 5 to 7 minutes. Add dried chilies if using.
Continue simmering until the sauce thickens, then transfer to a serving plate.

intro: Chicken with Ampalaya in Oyster Sauce is a quick savory stir-braise with tender chicken and pleasantly bitter gourd.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken breast, thinly sliced
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add chicken and cook 2–3 minutes, until lightly browned.
Stir in oyster sauce and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water or broth, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 10–12 minutes, adding liquid if needed.
Add ampalaya and cook over medium heat for 3–5 minutes until just tender; season and serve with rice.

intro: Adobong Atay and Puso ng Manok is a reduced soy-vinegar braise of chicken liver, hearts, and gizzards.
steps: Heat oil over low heat; sauté garlic until golden, then remove and reserve.
Brown chicken liver on all sides; remove, then brown chicken hearts and remove.
Brown chicken gizzards, then add 1/2 cup water, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, 2 tbsp peppercorns, and 4 bay leaves.
Bring to a boil and simmer 30 minutes, or until gizzards are tender.
Return liver and hearts; simmer over medium heat 20 minutes until the sauce reduces, then serve.

intro: Tikoy Turon wraps sweet rice cake in a crisp caramelized lumpia shell.
ingredients: 12 tikoy slices, each about 4 x 3/4 inch thick
steps: Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a wok to 180°C.
Place one tikoy slice in the center of each wrapper and sprinkle with 1 tablespoon brown sugar.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly, moisten the edge with water, and seal. Repeat with remaining tikoy.
Deep-fry gently until the wrappers are golden brown, then drain and serve warm.

intro: Kamote Cue is a classic street snack of caramel-coated fried sweet potato on skewers.
ingredients: 4 large sweet potatoes or kumara, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a wok over medium heat.
Add sweet potato and brown sugar, frying until the potatoes are tender and the sugar melts into caramel.
Add salt and toss carefully until every piece is coated in caramel.
Lift out with a slotted spoon, thread onto skewers, and cool on a wire rack before serving.

intro: Tokneneng coats hard-boiled eggs in a vivid annatto batter and serves them with tangy vinegar dip.
ingredients: 1 red chilli, finely chopped with seeds
steps: Whisk flour, cornstarch, baking powder, water, annatto powder, salt, and black pepper. Rest batter for at least 30 minutes.
Combine cane vinegar, water, sugar, shallot, garlic, chilli, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and black pepper for the dip.
Coat each hard-boiled egg evenly in batter.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry battered eggs one at a time until crisp and golden.
Drain well and serve immediately with the vinegar dip.

intro: 7-Up Marinated Pork Scotch delivers juicy, caramelized pork with a lightly sweet lemon-lime glaze.
ingredients: 1 kg pork scotch, cut into thick slices
1 cup 7-Up or other clear lemon-lime soda
1 tsp garlic and spiced salt powder
steps: Combine soda, scallions, ginger, cooking wine, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and garlic and spiced salt powder.
Add pork, coat well, cover, and marinate at least 2 hours or overnight.
Toss pork with starch until lightly coated.
Heat a thin layer of oil over medium-high heat and fry pork in batches until deeply caramelized and crisp at the edges.
Optionally simmer leftover marinade in the pan until sticky, glaze the pork, then rest briefly before serving.

intro: A complete rice plate with warmed meatball adobo, shrimp fried rice, and freshly fried eggs.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cooking oil, for frying eggs
steps: Warm the prepared meatball adobo in a covered pan over medium-low heat until steaming.
Reheat the shrimp fried rice in a separate wide pan, stirring until hot throughout.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan and fry the eggs to your preferred doneness.
Divide the hot fried rice among six plates and add a portion of meatball adobo to each.
Top each plate with a fried egg and serve immediately.

intro: Pork Chop Sinigang is a bright, sour soup with tender pork and a generous mix of vegetables.
ingredients: 1 medium yellow or white onion, wedged
steps: Bring 6 cups water to a boil. Add tomatoes and onion and boil for 3 minutes.
Add pork chops, cover, and cook over medium heat for 30 to 40 minutes until tender.
Stir in sinigang mix until dissolved.
Add okra, eggplant, siling pansigang, and snake beans. Cover and cook 10 to 12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add fish sauce and spinach. Cover, turn off heat, and let stand 5 minutes before serving with rice.

intro: Ginataang Mais at Malagkit is a sweet, creamy coconut porridge with chewy rice and tender corn.
steps: Combine coconut milk and coconut cream in a pot and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Add glutinous rice and stir continuously for 10 minutes to prevent sticking.
Stir in sugar until dissolved.
Add sweet corn, lower heat, and cook 8 minutes, or longer for softer corn and rice.
Stir in vanilla and salt, then transfer to serving bowls.

intro: Ginataang Tilapia gently cooks whole fish in spicy, fragrant coconut milk.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon fresh turmeric, cut into strips, optional
2 to 3 medium tilapia, scaled, gutted, and cleaned
1 to 2 siling labuyo, cut into pieces
1 cup malunggay leaves or pak choi
steps: Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in oil over medium-low heat until aromatic. Add turmeric, if using, and cook 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk and fish sauce, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add tilapia and siling labuyo. Cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes, until fish flakes easily.
Add malunggay or pak choi 1 minute before removing from the heat, then serve.

intro: Guisadong Pechay is a quick bok choy and pork stir-fry in a lightly thickened bagoong sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic and red onion until fragrant.
Add pork belly and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add bok choy and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Mix cornstarch, chicken stock, and bagoong until smooth. Pour into the wok, bring to a boil, and simmer 2 minutes.
Finish with black pepper and serve immediately.

intro: Creamy Chicken Liver Pasta with Mushrooms is a rich fettuccine dish with crisp guanciale and tender livers.
steps: Cook fettuccine in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Cook guanciale over medium heat until crisp. Remove it, leaving the rendered fat in the pan.
Over medium-high heat, sear chicken livers 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned but slightly pink inside; remove.
Add olive oil if needed, brown mushrooms, then cook garlic for 30 seconds.
Return guanciale and livers; add cream and Parmesan. Stir until melted, loosening with pasta water if needed.
Toss in fettuccine, season with salt and pepper, and serve with parsley if desired.

intro: Sinuglaw sa Gata brings together vinegar-cured fish, freshly grilled pork belly, coconut milk, and chilli.
ingredients: 400 g fresh snapper or other white-fleshed fish, cubed
steps: Place fish in a non-reactive bowl with 3/4 of the vinegar and cure for 10 minutes.
Gently press fish to remove excess liquid, then discard the vinegar.
Combine fish with cucumber, onion, ginger, chillies, salt, and black pepper.
Add lemon juice, coconut milk, and remaining vinegar. Cover and chill for 1 hour.
Immediately after grilling, chop pork belly and fold it into the chilled fish mixture. Serve at once.

intro: Beef Pares serves tender sweet-savory braised beef with its clear, aromatic beef broth.
ingredients: 2 lb beef brisket, cubes, or shank
2 tbsp toasted garlic, plus more for garnish
1/2 cup spring onions, chopped, plus more for garnish
1 tbsp cornstarch dissolved in 1/2 cup water
steps: Soak beef in water for 10–15 minutes, discard water, and rinse. Boil 8–10 cups fresh water with beef, quartered onion, peppercorns, and fish sauce.
Cover and simmer on low 30–40 minutes until fork-tender, adding water if needed. Remove meat, cube it, and return shank bones to broth if using.
Season broth with salt and add toasted garlic and chopped spring onions; keep hot for serving.
Sauté finely chopped onion, garlic, and ginger in oil over medium heat until tender. Add beef and brown the edges.
Add soy sauce, star anise, five-spice, bay leaves, sugar, pepper, 2 cups broth, and cornstarch slurry. Cover and simmer 15–20 minutes until tender and glossy.
Serve beef with toasted garlic and spring onions, accompanied by the seasoned broth and fried garlic rice.

intro: Adobong Baboy with Boiled Eggs is a glossy soy-vinegar pork stew enriched with tender eggs.
steps: Toss pork with 4 tablespoons soy sauce and marinate for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a wide pot. Cook garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves until garlic is light golden brown.
Add pork, its marinade, and sherry; cook for about 5 minutes.
Add remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 40 minutes.
Add vinegar and allow the stew to return to a boil before stirring in sugar.
Add peeled boiled eggs and cook 2 to 3 minutes. Serve with warm rice.

intro: Longsilog is a classic Filipino breakfast plate of longaniza, sinangag, sunny-side-up eggs, and atchara.
steps: Cook longaniza in a skillet over medium heat until browned and fully cooked, adding a little water first if needed.
Fry eggs sunny-side up until the whites are set and yolks remain soft.
Warm sinangag in a skillet until hot and lightly crisp.
Arrange sinangag, longaniza, eggs, and atchara on a plate; serve immediately.

intro: Pochero with Pork and Beans is a comforting pork stew with saba, vegetables, chorizo, and a rich tomato-bean broth.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté onion, garlic, and tomato until softened.
Add pork and sauté until light brown, then stir in Pork Cube and chorizo; cook 1 minute.
Add water, boil, cover, and cook over low-medium heat 45 to 60 minutes until pork is tender, adding water if needed.
Add potato and saba; cover and boil 5 minutes.
Add pork and beans and cook 3 minutes.
Add long beans, cabbage, and pechay; cook 2 to 3 minutes until just tender.
Season with patis and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Taghilaw is a robust pork offal stew simmered in a sharp vinegar and pork-stock broth.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season pork neck, intestines, heart, liver, and pig's brain with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add intestines, pork neck, and heart; cook until lightly browned at the edges.
Add vinegar and pork stock, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Add liver, pig's brain, and chillies; cook 15 minutes more, adjust seasoning, and serve.

intro: Tortang Noodles at Sardinas turns instant noodles and sardines into crisp, saucy mini omelets.
ingredients: 5 oz sardines in tomato sauce, fish and sauce separated
steps: Boil water, cook noodles until soft, then drain thoroughly.
Mash sardines, mix with eggs, salt, and pepper, then stir in noodles, flour, and half the green onion.
Heat oil and fry 1/2-cup portions for 1 1/2 minutes per side, scattering green onion on top before flipping.
Sauté onion in remaining oil until soft, add reserved tomato sauce, and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in remaining green onion, spoon sauce over the noodle omelets, and serve.

intro: Bagoong Fried Chicken is lemony, garlic-scented chicken marinated in sautéed shrimp paste and pan-fried until crisp.
steps: Mix sautéed bagoong, lemon juice, black pepper, and garlic until combined.
Coat chicken thoroughly in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Heat enough oil in a pan over medium heat.
Pan-fry chicken for about 5 minutes per side, adjusting heat as needed until browned and cooked through.
Drain briefly and serve hot.

intro: Kapeng Barako is a bold Batangas coffee with a naturally anise-like fragrance.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a small saucepan or kettle.
Add ground kapeng barako, lower the heat, and simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes.
Remove from heat and let the grounds settle for 2 minutes.
Strain into cups and sweeten with sugar if desired.

intro: This excursion-style adobo braises chicken and pork belly until tender, then reduces the vinegar sauce.
ingredients: 3 lb pork belly, cut into large cubes
2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 beef cube or beef bouillon cube
steps: Mix soy sauce, garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Add pork and chicken, toss well, cover, and refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Add meat with its marinade and cook 10–12 minutes until browned.
Add water, bring to a boil, stir in beef cube, cover, and simmer on low about 60 minutes until very tender.
Add coconut vinegar, bring back to a boil, and cook until the liquid nearly evaporates.
Taste, adjust salt and pepper if needed, and serve.

intro: Sotanghon with Upo Soup is a comforting chicken-broth noodle soup with pork, shrimp, and toasted garlic.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion and garlic until onion softens. Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in chicken broth, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add shrimp and return the broth to a boil. Stir in sotanghon.
Add upo, cover, and cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, adding broth if needed.
Season with pepper and patis. Add deep-fried garlic, cook 1 to 2 minutes, and serve.

intro: Crisp pork meatballs are finished in a pineapple sweet-and-sour sauce with colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix pork, flour, eggs, shallots, 4 cloves garlic, five-spice, fish sauce, white pepper, chilli, and salt. Shape with wet hands.
Deep-fry meatballs in hot oil for 5–7 minutes, depending on size, until cooked through; drain.
Sauté remaining garlic and ginger in oil. Add bell peppers, carrots, and red onion; stir-fry 1 minute.
Add chicken stock, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, pineapple juice, ketchup, and cornstarch slurry. Boil, then simmer 2 minutes; season with salt and black pepper.
Add pineapple pieces and meatballs, then simmer 2 minutes until coated and hot.

intro: Tuna Pie is a crisp, shallow-fried bread pocket filled with creamy tuna and melted processed cheese.
ingredients: 4 processed cheese slices, cut in half
182 g canned tuna in oil, drained
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix tuna, carrot, onion, mayonnaise, pickle relish, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place beaten eggs in a shallow bowl and panko on a wide plate.
Flatten each bread slice with a rolling pin.
Place filling on one half of each slice, top with half a cheese slice, fold, and firmly crimp edges with a fork.
Dip each pie in egg, then coat evenly in panko.
Shallow-fry over medium heat until both sides are crisp and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

intro: Sarciadong Manok is tender chicken braised in a tomato-rich sauce with peas.
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté onion, garlic, and tomato until softened.
Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in tomato paste, if using, and chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Add bay leaves and parsley, cover, and simmer over low to medium heat for 35 to 40 minutes.
Add more broth if needed, then stir in green peas and season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Serve hot once the chicken is tender and cooked through.

intro: Crispy Shrimps Binondo Style features whole fried shrimp tossed in a fragrant salt-and-pepper finish.
ingredients: 500 g whole small shrimp, sharp parts trimmed
steps: Pat shrimp completely dry, then toss with garlic powder and cornstarch until coated.
Heat deep-frying oil in a wok to 180°C (356°F).
Fry shrimp in batches for about 1 minute, until golden and crisp; drain in a colander.
Dry-roast sea salt and peppercorns over low heat for 10 minutes, cool, then roughly grind.
Toss fried shrimp with the salt-and-pepper mixture over medium heat for about 1 minute and serve.

intro: Pakdol is a clear, nourishing beef or carabao shank soup with corn, saba bananas, and greens.
ingredients: 2 kg beef or carabao shank with marrow bones
1 tbsp salt, plus more to taste
steps: Cover shank and marrow bones with water, bring to a boil, discard the water, and rinse the meat.
Return meat to the pot with fresh water, onion, peppercorns, and salt. Simmer gently 2 1/2 hours until tender.
Add corn and cook 10 minutes.
Add saba bananas and cook 10 to 12 minutes until just tender.
Add cabbage and pechay or mustasa; simmer 5 minutes. Adjust salt, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: Sweet potato Ensaymada is a soft, buttery Filipino bread finished with sugar and Edam cheese.
steps: Warm milk, cream, water, and shortening in a saucepan until very warm but not hot.
Mix 1/2 cup flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Gradually add the warm liquid, then beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Beat in mashed sweet potato, egg, and 1/2 cup flour at high speed for 2 minutes. Gradually beat in remaining flour.
Cover and refrigerate dough for 2 hours. Beat in egg yolks on low, cover, and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Shape chilled dough into ropes, coil in greased pans, brush with melted butter, and let rise in a warm place until doubled, 1 to 2 hours.
Bake at 180°C for 15 minutes. Cool on a rack, brush with butter, then top with sugar and Edam cheese.

intro: Grilled Liver Bistek combines smoky pork liver with a reduced soy-lemon onion sauce.
ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion, sliced into rings
steps: Grill liver for 4 minutes per side, then slice it into strips.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add grilled liver and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in salt, pepper, soy sauce, lemon juice, and water.
Bring to a boil, add sugar, and cook over medium heat until the sauce reduces by half. Serve with warm rice.

intro: Cheese Pimiento is a smooth, tangy Filipino cheese spread flecked with tender red capsicum.
ingredients: 250 g sharp cheddar cheese, finely grated
1/2 large red capsicum or bell pepper
steps: Cook capsicum with a small amount of water and a pinch of salt, covered over medium heat, for about 5 minutes until tender but not soft.
Drain, cool, and finely chop the capsicum.
Mix cheddar, butter, cream cheese, and evaporated milk on low speed until combined.
Warm the mixture in a microwave-safe dish in 10-second bursts until spreadable, without fully melting it.
Stir in capsicum and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cover and chill before serving.

intro: Pata Hamonado slowly braises pork leg in pineapple juice and soy sauce until tender and glossy.
ingredients: 2 kg pork legs, whole or cut into sections
1 cup water, plus more if needed
steps: Sauté garlic in oil until golden brown in a large pot.
Add pork leg and brown on all sides.
Add soy sauce, pineapple juice, water, fish sauce, peppercorns, and pineapple chunks, keeping the pork submerged with extra water if needed.
Bring to a boil, reduce to a slow simmer, and cook 2 hours until tender.
Raise heat to high, stir in optional brown sugar and pineapple chunks, then boil 15 minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens. Serve hot.

intro: Cheesy Fried Wedges are fluffy potato wedges with rugged crisp edges, cheese powder, and cool sour cream.
ingredients: 2 large potatoes, thick-cut with skin on
steps: Heat oil in a deep fryer to 120°C and add potato wedges.
Allow the oil to rise to 180°C over 5 to 6 minutes. Lift and shake the fryer basket once each minute to roughen the edges.
Continue frying 6 to 8 minutes at 180°C until wedges are crisp outside and golden brown.
Drain on a cooling rack until crisp, then generously dust with Cheesemiss cheese powder.
Serve in bowls topped with sour cream.

intro: Munggo Ice Candy freezes creamy blended red beans with sweet whole-bean bites.
steps: Simmer red beans in 4 cups water over medium heat for about 1 1/2 hours, until tender; cool.
Reserve one-third of the cooked beans.
Blend evaporated milk, condensed milk, sugar, remaining beans, and 2 cups bean-cooking liquid, leaving a little texture.
Using a funnel, place 1 teaspoon reserved beans into each ice candy bag, then fill with the blended mixture.
Tie bags tightly and freeze until solid before serving.

intro: Burong Mustasa is a gently fermented mustard-green pickle with a salty rice-water brine.
steps: Wash mustard greens, pat dry, and leave in the sun for about 1 hour until wilted.
Cook rice and water in a covered pot over medium heat until the rice is soft.
Toss wilted mustard greens with coarse sea salt, gently mash, and pack into a resealable jar.
Set a mesh strainer over the jar and strain in the rice cooking water, leaving the soft rice behind.
Cover and ferment at room temperature for 4 to 6 days.
Serve as an appetizer or use with fish and egg dishes; refrigerate around 50 to 55°F for further flavor development.

intro: Ginisang Kalabasa at Sitaw with Daing is a savory everyday sauté of squash, beans, and salty dried fish.
ingredients: 1 lb calabaza squash or kalabasa, cubed
8 string beans or sitaw, cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until the onion begins to soften.
Add daing and stir briefly until fragrant.
Add kalabasa and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook 5–6 minutes until water has mostly evaporated and squash softens.
Add sitaw, fish sauce, and pepper; cook over medium heat 3–5 minutes until beans are tender-crisp.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot.

intro: A light, gingery mussel soup brightened with malunggay.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot.
Add onion, ginger, and lemongrass; cook over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add mussels and boil for 6 minutes.
Gently add malunggay leaves and cook for 6–8 minutes, until wilted.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Crisp bread pockets hold a warmly spiced mango and peach filling.
steps: Mix mangoes, peaches, brown sugar, cornstarch, and cinnamon powder in a bowl.
Roll each bread slice thin, cut in half, then fold each half into a pocket; moisten and press the edges, leaving one side open.
Fill each pocket with the fruit mixture and seal the remaining edge firmly.
Heat oil over medium heat. Coat each nugget in beaten egg, press into Panko, and fry both sides until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm as dessert.

intro: A rich Filipino-style spaghetti with beef, mushrooms, and a creamy tomato sauce.
ingredients: 500 g spaghetti noodles, cooked according to package directions
1/2 cup beef stock, plus more if needed
2 tbsp liver spread or spicy liver pâté
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until the onion is soft.
Add minced beef and cook, breaking it apart, until lightly browned.
Pour in beef stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in tomato puree, tomato paste, cream of mushroom soup, and basil; simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Add mushrooms and liver spread; cook 5 minutes, loosening with extra stock if the sauce becomes too thick.
Season with sugar, salt, and black pepper. Spoon sauce over cooked spaghetti and finish with Parmesan.

intro: A light, gingery Tinolang Halaan broth highlights sweet clams and tender spinach.
ingredients: 1 bunch fresh spinach, washed and drained
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a stockpot.
Add ginger and onion; cover and boil over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add clams and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, until the shells open.
Add spinach, cover, and cook for 1 minute until just wilted.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve immediately in bowls.

intro: Calderetang Manok is a rich tomato-braised chicken stew with vegetables, liver spread, and cheese.
ingredients: 3 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate chicken with soy sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, and lime juice for at least 1 hour.
Heat oil over medium heat; fry potato and carrots until lightly browned, then drain and set aside.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a pot. Sauté onion and 4 cloves garlic until the onion softens.
Add chicken and sauté until medium brown. Add tomato sauce and water; boil, cover, then simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in liver spread, bell peppers, potato, and carrots. Season with fish sauce and pepper, then cook until vegetables are tender.
Stir in grated cheese until melted, then serve hot with rice.

intro: A tomato-braised Chicken Mechado with tender chicken, potatoes, and bright bell pepper.
ingredients: 2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat; fry potatoes for 3 minutes per side, then remove.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add chicken and cook 3 to 4 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in soy sauce for 1 minute, then add tomato sauce and water; bring to a boil.
Add Knorr Chicken Cube and laurel leaves. Cover and simmer on very low heat for 40 minutes.
Stir in lemon zest and bell pepper for 3 minutes, then add sugar and potatoes for 2 minutes. Season and serve with rice.

intro: Crisp fried bangus meets a tangy, savory miso-sampaloc broth.
ingredients: 1 large fresh bangus (milkfish), scaled and gutted
3 tbsp white or yellow miso paste
1 sachet sinigang sa sampaloc mix, for 2 liters
steps: Rinse and thoroughly pat dry the bangus; cut diagonally into 1 1/4-inch pieces, rub with sea salt, and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat oil over medium-high heat and fry bangus, covered against splatter, for 3–4 minutes per side; set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons frying oil in a pot. Sauté garlic, onions, and tomatoes until the tomatoes soften.
Stir in pepper and miso, add water, and bring to a boil. Add sinigang mix and fried bangus; simmer 15–18 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and spinach. Cover, turn off heat, and let stand 8 minutes before serving.

intro: This rich Batangas Kaldereta combines tender beef with a savory, lightly spicy cheese-thickened sauce.
ingredients: 3 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
steps: Mix beef with soy sauce and marinate for 30 minutes.
Melt margarine in a pot, stir in annatto powder, then sauté garlic until lightly browned and onions until soft.
Add beef and sauté, stirring often, until lightly browned all over; add Worcestershire sauce and pickle relish, then cook 2 minutes.
Add water and beef powder, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until the beef is tender, about 60 minutes.
Stir in liver spread, optional peanut butter, cheddar, and chilies until smooth; cook over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in breadcrumbs, season with salt and pepper, and serve once the sauce has thickened.

intro: Tender beef slices are baked beneath a rich mushroom, carrot, and cream gravy.
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Season beef, coat lightly with 1/4 cup flour, then brown all over in oil and 1/4 cup butter in a Dutch oven; set aside.
Sauté garlic and onions until soft. Return beef, add stock and enough water to reach two-thirds up the roast, then cover.
Bake at 180°C for 1 1/2 hours, until fork-tender. Rest the beef, slice it 1.5 cm thick, and reserve 3 cups strained cooking liquid.
Boil carrots until tender and drain. Over low heat, cook 1/3 cup butter and 1/3 cup flour into a roux.
Whisk in reserved liquid gradually, add cream, mushrooms, and carrots, then simmer 5 minutes; season with salt and pepper.
Layer sauce and beef in a baking dish, cover with remaining sauce, bake at 180°C for 25 minutes, and garnish with parsley.

intro: This savory-sweet Beef Asado pairs tender beef with olives, potatoes, and peppers.
ingredients: 1 jar pitted Manzanilla olives (5 oz), with juice
steps: Season beef with salt and pepper. Sauté diced onion and garlic in oil over medium heat for about 5 minutes; transfer to a 6-quart pot.
Brown beef pieces on all sides, then add them to the pot with tomatoes, peppercorns, olives and juice, quartered onion, bay leaves, and bouillon.
Bring to a boil, stir in ketchup, reduce to medium-low, and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove beef, add bell pepper to the sauce, and simmer 30 minutes. Meanwhile, fry potatoes until golden and add them to the pot.
Slice beef against the grain, return it to the sauce, and cook 5 minutes. Thicken with corn flour mixed with water if needed.

intro: Sinangkutsang Manok is golden pan-browned chicken finished in a gingery annatto sauce.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, cut into matchsticks
2 tsp annatto powder, dissolved in 1/4 cup water
steps: Season chicken generously with salt and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Brown chicken undisturbed for a few minutes per side, then transfer to a plate.
Over medium heat, add more oil if needed and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until soft and fragrant.
Return chicken to the wok. Add water and annatto mixture, bring to a rapid boil, cover, and cook over high heat for 15 minutes.
Uncover and toss until the reduced sauce coats the chicken. Season with black pepper, stir in lemon juice, and serve hot with rice.

intro: Tender pork monggo is served alongside salty, crisp fried galunggong.
ingredients: 4 oz pork, cut into small pieces
5 cups water, plus more as needed
steps: Bring 4 cups water to a boil, add mung beans, cover, and cook over low heat until soft.
Rub galunggong, including the cavities, with salt. Heat 1 cup oil and fry until crisp; drain and set aside.
Heat 3 tablespoons of the fish-frying oil. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until the onion softens.
Add pork and cook until beginning to brown. Add 1 cup water, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in softened mung beans and additional water as needed; cook for 5 minutes.
Add hot pepper leaves, fish sauce, and black pepper. Serve with warm rice and crispy galunggong.

intro: Paksiw na Isda is a tangy vinegar-braised fish dish with eggplant and green chillies.
ingredients: 800 g fish, such as milkfish, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces if large
1/2 thumb-size piece ginger, thinly sliced and pounded
steps: Combine vinegar, water, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, and peppercorns in a pot; bring to a boil.
Add fish, eggplant, finger chillies, bay leaves, and onion.
Cover, reduce to medium heat, and simmer for 15 minutes until the fish is cooked through and eggplant is tender.
Serve hot with rice.

intro: Soft, lightly sweet puto with coconut milk and optional anise.
ingredients: 1 tsp anise seeds, plus extra for topping (optional)
steps: Whisk rice flour, salt, sugar, baking powder, and yeast in a large bowl.
Combine coconut milk and hot water until lukewarm; whisk into the dry ingredients with oil and optional anise seeds.
Rest batter for 10 minutes, stir gently, then divide into greased molds and rest 20 minutes.
Bring steamer water to a boil 5 minutes before steaming; use medium heat for cracked tops or low heat for smooth tops.
Cover the steamer lid with cloth and steam 15–20 minutes, until a toothpick emerges clean. Cool slightly, then unmold.

intro: Ginisang Sitaw with Bell Pepper is a savory pork-and-bean sauté with a subtly sweet Coca-Cola braise.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a wok over medium heat; cook pork belly until its fat renders and the meat begins browning.
Add garlic and sauté for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, 3/4 cup water, and Coca-Cola; cover and simmer until pork is tender.
Uncover and cook until the liquid evaporates. Stir in onion and tomatoes until softened.
Add string beans and sauté 1 minute. Add oyster sauce and remaining 1/4 cup water; cover and cook 3 minutes.
Add bell pepper and cook 2 minutes. Season with sugar, salt, and pepper; serve with steamed rice.

intro: Thin chicken skewers get the bright, smoky character of Chicken Inasal BBQ with annatto basting.
ingredients: 2 lb boneless chicken breast, thinly sliced
steps: Toss chicken with ginger, lemongrass, 5 tablespoons annatto oil, brown sugar, coconut vinegar, peppercorn, and 1 teaspoon salt; refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Thread the chicken onto bamboo skewers.
Heat a grill to medium-high heat. Melt margarine with 4 tablespoons annatto oil and 1/2 teaspoon salt for the basting sauce.
Grill chicken for 2 to 4 minutes per side, brushing with basting sauce as it cooks.
Continue turning and basting until the chicken is fully cooked, then serve hot.

intro: This richer Chicken Adobo gets extra savoriness from oyster sauce, butter, and crisp fried garlic.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Mix chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, and half the garlic; marinate for at least 1 hour.
Fry remaining garlic in oil until golden; reserve the garlic and its flavored oil.
Heat butter with garlic oil; sauté onion, then add chicken and cook until light brown.
Add oyster sauce, remaining marinade, and water; bring to a boil. Add cube, sugar, bay leaves, fried garlic, and peppercorns.
Cover and simmer 35 to 45 minutes. Garnish with green onions and serve.

intro: Panara is a crisp fried wonton snack filled with savory shrimp and tender-crisp upo.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic and onion in a little oil until fragrant.
Add shrimp and upo; stir-fry for 3 minutes, keeping the upo crisp. Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then cool.
Place 1 tablespoon filling in each wrapper. Brush edges with beaten egg, fold into triangles, and press firmly to seal.
Heat deep-frying oil to 170°C (340°F). Fry the wontons in batches until golden brown.
Drain on a rack or paper towels and serve warm.

intro: Lambanog is a potent Filipino coconut spirit traditionally served simply and well chilled.
ingredients: Prepared lambanog, aged from tuba for at least 48 hours
steps: Chill the prepared lambanog thoroughly before serving.
If using raisins, steep them in the lambanog until their flavor develops to your preference.
Pour into small serving glasses, add ice if desired, and serve responsibly.

intro: Gotong Batangas Bulalo is a deep, beefy soup enriched with rice wash and annatto.
ingredients: 2 1/2 kg meaty beef leg bones or shanks, cut into sections
300 g beef tendon, cut into small cubes
1 thumb-size piece ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate beef bones or shanks in cane vinegar for 1 hour; drain and season generously with salt and pepper.
Brown the beef in batches in oil over medium-high heat, removing each batch before adding the next.
Add oil if needed, then sauté garlic, ginger, and onions in the same pot until fragrant.
Fry annatto powder briefly in the aromatics until it dissolves into the oil.
Return beef and add tendon and rice wash. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 3 hours.
Add chillies, adjust salt and pepper, and simmer 15 minutes more. Garnish bowls with spring onions and fried garlic.

intro: Sweet-salty Filipino-Chinese Pork Asado with tender sliced pork and glossy sauce.
ingredients: 2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Marinate pork with soy sauce, five-spice, garlic, onion, Chinese cooking wine, and salt for at least 1 hour.
Place pork, marinade, water, peppercorns, bay leaves, and dark soy sauce in a pot; bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer 1 hour, turning the pork once, until tender.
Rest pork for 10 minutes. Strain the braising liquid, then simmer it with cornstarch slurry until thickened.
Thinly slice the pork and spoon the thickened sauce over it.

intro: A loaded Chopsuey with seafood, chicken liver, tofu, and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 6 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Deep-fry tofu until golden. Soak shiitake in warm water for 20 minutes, then slice.
Heat oil over medium-high heat; cook chicken liver through, then remove. Cook lap cheong until lightly crisp, then cook shrimp until pink; remove.
Add oil if needed and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant. Stir-fry carrot, broccoli, and baby corn for 3 minutes.
Add cabbage, snap peas, and bell peppers; cook 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Return liver, lap cheong, shrimp, tofu, and shiitake.
Add stock, cornstarch slurry, XO sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, fish sauce, and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes, until lightly thickened.

intro: Crisp dilis brighten a fresh calamansi-dressed tomato and onion salad.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and stir-fry dried anchovies until lightly browned.
Transfer anchovies immediately to a plate and let them cool until crisp.
Squeeze calamansi into a bowl; mix with fish sauce, black pepper, and optional sugar.
Toss tomatoes and purple onion gently with the dressing.
Fold in the cooled anchovies and serve immediately.

intro: Tinumis is a tangy pork and pork-blood stew enriched with Sinigang na Sampaloc Mix.
ingredients: 1 lb pork, cut into small cubes
1 packet (20 g) Knorr Sinigang na Sampaloc Mix
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic until medium brown, then cook onion and tomato until soft.
Add pork and cook over low-medium heat, stirring constantly, for 5 to 7 minutes until lightly browned. Stir in Sinigang na Sampaloc Mix.
Add pork blood and cook, stirring, for 10 to 15 minutes. Pour in water and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the Knorr Pork Cube, cover, and simmer on low for 15 to 25 minutes, adding water if the stew becomes too thick.
Season with salt and pepper, add long green peppers, and cook for 3 minutes before serving.

intro: Mamon Tostado is a twice-baked Filipino sponge cake with a golden, toasted exterior.
steps: Mix 1 tablespoon flour with 2 tablespoons oil and lightly grease molds. Preheat oven to 350°F (170°C).
Sift cake flour, powdered sugar, baking powder, and salt. Beat whites foamy, add cream of tartar, then sugar gradually until stiff peaks form.
Whisk yolks, vegetable oil, milk, and vanilla until frothy. Fold in the sifted mixture in 3 to 4 additions.
Gently fold meringue into batter in batches, stopping when no white streaks remain. Fill molds over halfway and tap out bubbles.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until golden; cool and unmold. Invert cakes overnight, then bake again 20 to 25 minutes until their bodies are golden.

intro: Homemade Chicharon becomes airy and crackly after drying and a brief hot fry.
steps: Season pork rind with salt and pepper, then arrange pieces in a single layer on a wire rack.
Fan-bake at 170°C for 1 hour until dried.
Cool completely, then refrigerate overnight.
Deep-fry in very hot oil for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until puffed and crisp.
Drain well and serve with vinegar dip.

intro: Pulot is a rich coconut-and-muscovado sauce finished with toasted pili nuts.
ingredients: 1 cup diluted coconut milk or water
steps: Toast pili nuts in a dry pan over low heat until lightly golden and fragrant; set aside.
Combine kakang gata, diluted coconut milk or water, muscovado sugar, pandan, and salt in a saucepan.
Cook over low heat at a gentle simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally; avoid a vigorous boil so the coconut milk stays smooth.
Stop earlier for a pourable sauce, or cook longer for a thicker, taffy-like consistency.
Discard pandan, stir in most pili nuts, and garnish with the remainder before serving.

intro: Beef Salpicao is a quick, sizzling garlic beef dish with a buttery Worcestershire glaze.
ingredients: 800 g beef sirloin or tenderloin, cubed
steps: Season beef with salt, pepper, and minced garlic; rest for 5 minutes, then toss with olive oil.
Heat a heavy cast-iron pan over high heat until very hot. Sear beef in batches without crowding until browned on each side.
Add butter and Worcestershire sauce, then toss just until the beef is evenly coated.
Transfer to a warm platter or sizzling plate and generously garnish with fried crispy garlic.

intro: Bagnet uses a double-fry method for remarkably crisp pork belly with a tender interior.
steps: Put pork belly in a pot and add enough water to cover. Add garlic, pepper, salt, bay leaves, and baking powder.
Bring to a boil, skim off foam, then simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes. Cool completely.
Chill pork until cold, then cut into 2- to 3-inch-thick portions.
Heat deep-frying oil until near smoking, lower the heat, and fry pork for 10 minutes. Cool, then chill again until cold.
Fry the pork a second time for 5 minutes until deeply crisp. Serve with bagoong monamon and lemon wedges.

intro: Crispy tokwa, kangkong, and golden garlic make a deeply savory rice-ready dish.
steps: Cook garlic in 1/2 cup oil over medium heat; when bubbling, reduce to low and stir until golden. Strain, reserving garlic and oil.
Heat the remaining 1 cup oil with all but 3 tablespoons of garlic oil. Fry tofu until golden, cool slightly, then dice.
Whisk oyster sauce, Knorr Liquid Seasoning, soy sauce, cornstarch, and water until smooth.
Heat reserved garlic oil in a clean pan; sauté onion until soft. Add tofu and cook 30 seconds.
Add kangkong and sauté 1 minute. Add sauce and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Fold in half the browned garlic, then plate and top with remaining garlic.

intro: This quick Seafood Salpicao pairs mixed seafood with crisp vegetables and buttery garlic.
ingredients: 1 cup young corn, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 medium red bell pepper, cut into squares
steps: Heat oil over low heat. Fry all but 1 tablespoon garlic until golden; remove and reserve.
Sauté remaining garlic over medium heat until aromatic, then add shiitake and young corn for several seconds.
Add seafood, oyster sauce, and soy sauce; toss well.
Add broccoli, snow peas, bell pepper, and chilli flakes; stir briefly.
Mix water, cornstarch, and brown sugar. Add to the pan and cook under 5 minutes, until seafood and vegetables are half-cooked.
Stir in butter and ground pepper. Transfer to a dish and top with reserved garlic.

intro: Ube Pandesal makes soft purple bread rolls with a lightly crisp breadcrumb coating.
ingredients: 3 1/2 cups high-grade flour, plus more for dusting
1/2 tightly packed cup mashed steamed ube
Several drops ube flavocol, adjusted to desired color
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm water and set aside until bubbly. Mix in milk, egg, sugar, softened butter, and ube flavocol.
Combine flour and salt on a work surface. Make a well, add the yeast mixture and mashed ube, and mix into a dough.
Knead for 15 minutes until soft and clay-like, dusting lightly with flour only as needed. Cover and let rise warmly for 1 hour.
Deflate dough, divide into 1-inch-thick rolls, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces, shape into buns, and arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Let buns rise in a warm place for 1 hour. Top with breadcrumbs and bake at 200°C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.

intro: Lengua Kare Kare pairs tender beef tongue with a nutty sauce and simply steamed vegetables.
steps: Pressure-cook beef tongue in water for 45 minutes. Cool, peel away skin, and slice into serving pieces.
Steam eggplant and string beans for 10 minutes; steam bok choy for 5 minutes.
Dry-roast peanuts and almonds until lightly browned, then process into a paste.
Heat annatto oil in a wok; sauté garlic and onion until soft. Add lengua and sauté 2 minutes.
Add beef broth, cover, and boil gently on low for 10 minutes. Stir in nut paste, cook uncovered 7 minutes, season, and serve with vegetables and bagoong alamang.

intro: Dilisilog pairs garlicky sinangag, crisp dilis, eggs, and cool cucumber for a classic breakfast plate.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
200 g boneless dilis or regular dilis
steps: Fry garlic in oil over medium heat until golden. Add rice and stir-fry for about 10 minutes until evenly coated; season with salt and pepper.
For boneless dilis, deep-fry at 180°C (355°F) for about 1 minute until crisp and golden.
For regular dilis, pan-fry over medium heat for about 1 minute per side until crisp but not darkly toasted.
Drain dilis on paper towels and cook eggs to your preference.
Serve each plate with sinangag, dilis, two eggs, and sliced cucumber.

intro: Pork Menudo is a tomato-based celebration stew with liver, hotdogs, and colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, cut into squares
1 green bell pepper, cut into squares
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate pork in soy sauce for 10 minutes. Fry carrots and potatoes over medium-high heat until beginning to brown; drain, reserving 2 tablespoons oil.
Sauté hotdogs for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes; set aside. Sauté half the onion with liver until lightly browned; set aside.
Sauté garlic until starting to brown, add remaining onion until soft, then sauté marinated pork until light to medium brown.
Add tomato sauce, water, bay leaves, and beef powder. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until pork is tender.
Return hotdogs and liver; cook 3 minutes. Add bell peppers, carrots, and potatoes, then cook 1 minute.
Stir in sugar, season with fish sauce and pepper, and serve with rice.

intro: Chicken Lomi is a hearty, thickened noodle soup with chicken and vegetables.
ingredients: 10 oz boneless chicken breast, thinly sliced
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and carrots until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in water, bring to a boil, add the chicken cube, then cover and simmer over low-medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add cabbage and miki noodles; cook 8 to 10 minutes until noodles are tender.
Stir in scallions and beaten egg. Mix cornstarch with 1/4 cup water, then stir it into the soup until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper; cook 2 minutes and serve warm.

intro: Chocolate Biko is a chewy coconut-rice dessert enriched with melted cacao tablea.
steps: Bring coconut milk to a boil in a pot over medium heat.
Add cacao tablea and stir until completely dissolved.
Add glutinous rice, brown sugar, and salt. Cover and cook over low-medium heat until rice absorbs about half the liquid.
Stir often, scraping the bottom, until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed; add coconut milk or water if needed before rice is done.
Transfer to a greased baking dish, cool, then serve.

intro: A quick vegetable Chopsuey in a creamy Crab and Corn Soup sauce.
ingredients: 37 g Knorr Crab and Corn Soup
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add carrot, cauliflower, and broccoli; cook for 2 minutes. Toss in cabbage, bell peppers, and snow peas.
Add soy sauce and oyster sauce, then cook for 2 minutes.
Whisk water with Knorr Crab and Corn Soup, pour into the wok, and bring to a boil.
Add fried tofu and quail eggs. Cook until the sauce reduces and thickens, then season and serve.

intro: Ginataang Puso ng Saging combines banana blossom and pork in a reduced coconut sauce.
ingredients: 1 banana flower bud (puso ng saging), outer 2 to 3 layers discarded and thinly sliced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak sliced puso ng saging in salted water for 15 minutes. Drain, rinse, and squeeze out its liquid.
Heat oil in a wok; sauté onion, ginger, and garlic until aromatic.
Add pork and brown on all sides. Add banana blossom and cook for 2 minutes.
Add 1 cup water, 1 cup coconut milk, vinegar, and chillies. Cover, boil, then simmer medium-low for 15 to 20 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Add remaining coconut milk and simmer over medium heat until thick and oily.
Turn off the heat and serve with steamed rice.

intro: Pritong Talong is a simple crisp-edged eggplant dish made for rice and bagoong alamang.
steps: Halve the eggplant lengthwise, then cut it into 3-inch pieces.
Dredge all eggplant pieces lightly in flour.
Heat 4 tablespoons oil over medium heat. Pan-fry until dark brown on one side, turn, and cook until tender throughout; add remaining oil as needed.
Serve hot with bagoong alamang.

intro: Tortang Talong with Giniling is a smoky eggplant omelet layered with savory ground beef.
steps: Grill eggplants until their skins blacken. Cool, peel, and flatten each eggplant gently with a fork without tearing it.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until soft; add ground beef and cook through, stirring occasionally.
Beat eggs with salt. Heat remaining oil in a pan sized for an eggplant over medium heat.
For each omelet, add one-quarter of the egg, lay in an eggplant, spread over beef filling, and pour egg over the top.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes, carefully flip, and fry 2 to 3 minutes more until the egg is set. Serve hot.

intro: Kilawing Isda at Baboy combines chilled vinegar-cured fish with crisp pork belly.
ingredients: 250 g white fish meat, such as grouper or snapper, cubed
250 g pork belly with fat, cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak fish in 1/2 cup vinegar for at least 5 minutes. Drain in a colander and gently squeeze dry.
Combine remaining vinegar, lemon juice, ginger, onion, garlic, chillies, salt, and pepper. Cover with fish and refrigerate 4 to 6 hours.
Simmer pork with salt, pepper, and water over medium heat for 15 minutes. Drain, then chill in the freezer for 30 minutes.
Heat deep-frying oil over high heat. Fry chilled pork for under 2 minutes until crisp; drain.
Fold crispy pork into the chilled fish mixture and serve immediately.

intro: Sweet-style spaghetti sauce gets a savory boost from canned corned beef and liver spread.
ingredients: 1 large bottle sweet-style tomato ketchup or banana ketchup
1 can chopped tomatoes or tomato purée
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook spaghetti according to the package directions; drain.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add corned beef and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up as it heats.
Stir in ketchup, tomatoes or purée, tomato paste, liver spread, and beef stock; simmer 20 minutes, adding water if needed.
Season with pepper, salt, and sugar. Simmer 5 minutes more, then serve sauce over spaghetti.

intro: Pork Monggo is a comforting mung-bean stew finished with leafy greens and crunchy chicharon.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add pork and cook until light brown. Pour in water, bring to a boil, and stir in Knorr Pork Cube.
Add mung beans; cover and simmer over low-medium heat until tender, adding water if needed.
Add malunggay leaves and spinach; cook 2 minutes. Season with pepper and patis, then cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve topped with crumbled chicharon.

intro: Tangy Pork Tapa is served as a hearty breakfast plate with crisp saba and salted egg.
steps: Mix vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper, and garlic. Coat pork in the mixture and marinate at least 3 hours.
Drain pork and air-dry it on a plate for 1 to 2 hours, covered to protect it.
Heat half the oil over medium heat. Coat saba bananas in cornstarch and fry 1 to 2 minutes per side; drain on paper towels.
Add oil as needed and fry pork until medium brown and cooked through.
Serve pork with rice, salted egg, fried saba, and spicy vinegar dip.

intro: Ginataang Salmon is a quick, creamy coconut fish stew with spinach and fresh chilies.
ingredients: 1 packet (45 g) Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Whisk Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix with water until smooth. Add to the pot and bring to a boil.
Add salmon pieces, long green chilies, and optional Thai chilies. Cover and cook over medium heat for 5 to 8 minutes.
Add spinach and black pepper; add salt if desired. Cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes until spinach wilts.
Serve hot with rice.

intro: Beef Morcon is a festive stuffed beef roll braised until fork-tender in tomato sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb beef brisket, sliced thinly to about 1/3 inch
2 cups water, plus more if needed
2 medium carrots, cut into 1 cm batons
2 to 3 whole pickles, cut into 1 cm strips
3 hard-boiled eggs, each cut lengthwise into 4
80 g cheese, cut into 1 cm strips
steps: Pound beef thin, then marinate in soy sauce and lemon or calamansi juice for at least 1 hour.
Drain and reserve marinade. Fill each beef slice with carrot, hotdog, pickle, egg, and cheese; roll tightly.
Tie rolls at 1-inch intervals, coat in flour, then sear in hot oil until browned all over.
Leave 2 tablespoons oil; sauté onion and garlic over medium heat. Add tomatoes, reserved marinade, and water; bring to a boil.
Add rolls in one layer, cover, and simmer on low for 1 to 2 hours, turning occasionally, until fork-tender; add water if needed.
Remove rolls and reduce sauce until thick. Remove twine, slice, and serve with sauce.

intro: Latik is a fragrant topping of golden coconut curds made from slowly rendered coconut cream.
steps: Pour coconut cream into a pot and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Continue cooking until the cream separates and releases clear oil.
Lower the heat and stir constantly while the curds gently fry until golden brown.
Strain the mixture, reserving the golden curds as latik and the rendered coconut oil separately.

intro: Golden Chicken Empanada with a savory-sweet chicken, vegetable, pea, and raisin filling.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic and onion in oil. Stir-fry chicken over high heat until lightly browned.
Lower to medium heat; add potato, carrot, soy sauce, stock, salt, and pepper. Cook 5 minutes, then add raisins, peas, and sugar until dry; cool.
For homemade pastry, combine flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, butter, and cold water into a dough; chill rolled portions. Alternatively, use the shortcrust pastry sheets.
Roll or cut pastry rounds. Fill each with a heaping tablespoon of cooled filling, fold into half-moons, crimp, and place on a greased tray.
Mix milk and egg, brush over empanadas, and bake at 200°C for 20–25 minutes until golden. Cool briefly on a rack.

intro: Tuna in Can Sarciado is a fast, saucy canned-tuna dish with tomato, egg, and scallions.
ingredients: 1 can (12 oz) chunk light tuna in water
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until soft.
Add tuna with its canning liquid and cook for 3 minutes. Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Beat the egg, pour it into the pan, and stir gently as it sets for a few minutes.
Add pepper and scallions; cook for 2 minutes. Stir in fish sauce, adding more water if you prefer a thinner sauce.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot.

intro: Crispy Tenga turns tender, seasoned pig ears into a crunchy pulutan-style snack.
steps: Cover pig ears with 5 cups water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes; discard the water.
Cover ears with fresh water, add garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, and 1 teaspoon salt, then bring to a boil.
Add soy sauce and vinegar. Cover and boil over medium heat for 60 minutes, or until tender.
Cool ears, slice into small pieces, and rub with the remaining salt.
Heat oil in a deep pot and fry ears until crisp. Drain thoroughly and serve with spicy vinegar.

intro: Ginisang Monggo with Pork Pata is a deeply comforting mung bean soup with tender pork leg.
ingredients: 1 kg pork leg, cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic until golden, then remove and reserve it for garnish.
Add pork leg and fry until golden on all sides.
Add mung beans and stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 1/2 hours until beans are very soft and pork is very tender.
Add water if needed for your preferred consistency. Stir in spinach, if using, and season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Serve hot, topped with the reserved fried garlic.

intro: A crisp bacon and avocado sandwich makes a fast, satisfying Filipino-style merienda.
steps: Mix Dijon mustard and mayonnaise until smooth.
Toast bread to your preferred level.
Spread the mustard mayonnaise evenly over one side of each bread slice.
Layer lettuce, tomato, bacon, and avocado on one slice, then close with the second slice, spread-side down.
Serve immediately with a favorite drink.

intro: Tender blanched okra and eggplant make an easy rice meal with bagoong isda dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1 cup bagoong isda with tomato and onion
steps: Bring 6 cups water to a boil in a large pot.
Boil okra 3 to 5 minutes. Transfer to ice-cold water for 2 minutes, then drain and arrange on a plate.
Boil eggplants for 5 minutes, then chill in the ice water for 2 to 3 minutes and drain.
Arrange eggplants beside the okra. Serve with bagoong isda with tomato and onion and warm rice.
