intro: Chicken Pancit combines bihon and sotanghon with vegetables in a fragrant chicken broth.
steps: Boil chicken in 6 cups water for 30 minutes. Remove, cool, shred the meat, discard bones, and reserve the broth.
Soak bihon and sotanghon in water for 10 minutes. Stir-fry cabbage and carrots in oil for 3–5 minutes; set aside.
Sauté onion, celery, and garlic in the same pan. Add pepper and chicken; cook 3–5 minutes.
Add soy sauce and 1 cup reserved broth; boil 2 minutes. Toss in drained noodles until liquid absorbs, adding broth if dry.
Toss in vegetables and parsley, then serve.

intro: Delicate misua and patola turn baked pork meatballs into a comforting, light soup.
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Roll 1 tablespoon pork burger patty mixture into each meatball and arrange on a greased tray.
Bake for 25 minutes, until cooked through.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens. Add baked meatballs.
Add chicken broth and water; bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low-medium, and cook 12 minutes.
Add patola and cook 5 to 8 minutes until tender. Stir in misua and green onion; cook 3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately.

intro: Skinless Longganisa delivers garlicky, sweet-savory pork in easy paper-wrapped portions.
steps: Mix soy sauce, vinegar, and annatto powder in a large bowl.
Add pork, brown sugar, salt, garlic, and black pepper; mix thoroughly until evenly seasoned.
Cut wax paper into 4-inch squares. Place 2 tablespoons pork mixture on each square and roll into compact logs.
Unwrap the longganisa and pan-fry in a small amount of oil over low heat until browned and cooked through.

intro: Binallay is a steamed glutinous rice cake served with palm-sugar coconut sauce and latik.
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour with enough water to form a bread-like dough, then knead for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into ping-pong-size balls and flatten each into a rectangle.
Brush banana leaves with coconut oil, wrap each dough rectangle securely, and steam for 25 minutes.
Bring coconut milk and coconut cream to a boil in a saucepan until beginning to thicken.
Add palm sugar and boil until the sauce is brown and thick.
Unwrap binallay, place over the sauce, and sprinkle with latik.

intro: Binagoongan is tender pork belly simmered in a savory, tangy bagoong sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and brown pork on all sides; remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion until soft, then stir-fry tomatoes until softened.
Return pork to the pot. Add vinegar, bay leaves, and water; simmer 45 minutes or until tender.
Stir in bagoong, sugar, and finger chillies. Cook until the sauce reduces.
Season with freshly ground pepper and serve.

intro: Snails with Spinach in Coconut Milk is a creamy, spicy ginataang seafood dish.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Stir in shrimp paste, fish sauce, black pepper, and crushed red pepper.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add sea snails, raise heat to medium, cover, and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring gently every 3 minutes.
Add spinach and cook for 3 minutes until wilted, then serve.

intro: Pocherong Tinomas combines tender beef with sweet plantain, vegetables, and Mang Tomas sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg stewing beef or 1 1/2 kg beef short ribs
1/2 cup bacon scraps or cubed jamon
2 medium sweet potatoes, cubed and pan-fried
steps: Season beef with black pepper, then brown it in batches in oil; set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion in the same pot, add bacon scraps or jamon, and cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef, add beef stock, and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Stir in tomato paste and Mang Tomas Sauce; simmer 15 minutes.
Add French beans, fried sweet potatoes, and fried saba; simmer 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, add bok choy, turn off heat, cover 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

intro: Fresh Lumpiang Ubod pairs savory hearts-of-palm filling with soft wrappers, peanut-topped sauce, and lettuce.
ingredients: 3 tbsp cooking oil, plus oil or cooking spray for wrappers
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté onion and 4 garlic cloves in 3 tablespoons oil. Brown pork, add 1 1/2 cups water and Shrimp Cube, then simmer until nearly dry.
Add ubod for 5 minutes, carrot for 3 minutes, and shrimp until orange. Stir in parsley, fish sauce, and pepper; cool.
Boil 1 1/2 cups water with brown sugar, soy sauce, and remaining garlic for 20 seconds. Stir in cornstarch mixed with 3 tablespoons water until thickened.
Whisk eggs, canola oil, 1 cup water, and flour smooth. Cook thin layers in a lightly greased nonstick pan over medium heat until they release easily.
Place lettuce and filling on each wrapper, roll, then spoon over sauce and scatter with crushed peanuts.

intro: Kutsinta Extreme Overload tops chewy brown rice cakes with yema, coconut, and cheese.
steps: Melt white sugar in a pan, then stir in butter, condensed milk, egg yolk, and fresh cream; set yema spread aside.
Whisk flour, tapioca flour, dark brown sugar, and water smooth. Mix in annatto powder and lye water.
Grease moulds with melted butter and fill each about three-quarters full.
Steam for 45 minutes until kutsinta is set. Cool before gently unmoulding.
Top with grated coconut, yema spread, and grated processed cheese.

intro: Pancit Grade One is a rich noodle dish with pork jowl, shrimp, kamias, and achuete color.
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cubed and deep-fried
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Soak achuete seeds in water for at least 30 minutes, then strain to make an achuete extract.
Heat oil in a wok; sauté onion and garlic until aromatic. Add pork jowl and cook until browned.
Add shrimp and cook 2–3 minutes. Pour in pork broth and bring to a boil.
Add kamias and achuete extract; season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add noodles, carrot, and Chinese celery. Cook until noodles absorb most liquid but remain moist; top with fried tofu.

intro: Sinigang na Salmon Belly at Hipon is a quick, tangy seafood soup with tender vegetables.
ingredients: 1 large packet Tamarind Mix (Sinigang Mix) or 1/2 cup tamarind pulp
steps: If using tamarind pulp, boil it with 2 cups water until soft, strain the liquid, and reserve it.
Put onion, chillies, tomatoes, and radish in a pot. Add remaining water, or all 800 ml when using Sinigang Mix, and bring to a boil.
Add prawns, salmon belly, and Sinigang Mix if using. Simmer for 5 minutes until seafood is just cooked.
Add spinach and simmer 2 minutes until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then ladle into bowls.

intro: Stuffed Ampalaya bakes savory pork filling inside tender bitter melon rings.
ingredients: 2 ampalaya, about 10 to 12 inches each, cored and cut into 2-inch slices
steps: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix pork, onion, carrots, shredded bread, garlic powder, salt, pepper, paprika, and egg until evenly combined.
Pack the pork mixture into the hollow ampalaya slices.
Grease a baking pan and arrange the stuffed ampalaya in a single layer.
Bake for 22 to 26 minutes, until the pork is fully cooked, then serve.

intro: Tofu Sarciado combines fried tofu with a fresh tomato-and-egg sauce.
ingredients: 3 pieces extra-firm tofu, each sliced in half and fried until brown
steps: Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic, tomato, and onion until the onion is soft.
Add water and fish sauce, stir, and bring to a boil.
Pour in beaten egg, stir quickly, then cook for 2 minutes while stirring gradually until softly set.
Add fried tofu and black pepper. Stir gently and cook for 1 minute more.
Transfer to a plate, sprinkle with dried parsley, and serve hot.

intro: Tulapho slowly cooks pork belly before crisping it in its own rendered fat.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large wok.
Add pork, sea salt, and black pepper. Cover and boil over medium heat until pork is tender, adding water if needed.
Raise heat to high and cook until the liquid evaporates and the pork begins rendering fat.
Fry the pork in its rendered fat, turning as needed, until golden brown on all sides.
Drain on a paper towel-lined plate and serve.

intro: Kalabasa Soup with Ampalaya Leaves is a light, naturally sweet broth with a pleasantly bitter green finish.
ingredients: 1/2 medium butternut squash, seeded and cubed
steps: Combine chicken broth and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add onion and butternut squash; boil for 20 minutes until squash is tender.
Stir in garlic powder, then add ampalaya leaves and cook 5 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot.

intro: Seafood Pancit Bihon Guisado is a stock-soaked noodle stir-fry loaded with prawns and vegetables.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion. Add fish balls and cook 2 minutes.
Add 2 cups stock and pancit bihon, stirring continuously until noodles soften.
Add squid, prawns, carrot, and celery; stir 5 minutes while gradually adding remaining stock and soy sauce.
Add bok choy and spring onions; stir 3 minutes until noodles are cooked and liquid is absorbed.
Season with fish sauce and white pepper. Serve with lemon or calamansi.

intro: 7up Chicken Asado braises a whole chicken in a sweet, aromatic soda sauce.
steps: Rub chicken with soy sauce and crushed peppercorn. Put minced onion and lemongrass in the cavity; rest for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté sliced onion and garlic until soft. Add chicken and cook 3 minutes per side over medium heat.
Add remaining marinade and 7-Up; bring to a boil. Add star anise, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 30 minutes.
Turn chicken and cook 12 minutes more, until cooked through. Remove, halve, and arrange on a platter.
Reduce the sauce by half, stir in garlic and onion powders, strain, season with salt if needed, and pour over chicken.

intro: Instant Pancit Canton with Vegetables is a quick noodle bowl with crisp-tender colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 2 individual packages instant pancit canton, any flavor
3/4 cup chopped purple or green cabbage
Seasoning packets from the instant pancit canton
steps: Bring water to a boil in a deep pot and add salt.
Add noodles, carrots, broccoli stem, and cabbage. Boil for 2 to 3 minutes until noodles are soft but not soggy.
Drain through a fine colander, then run cold water over the noodles and vegetables to stop cooking and retain texture.
Drain thoroughly and transfer to a bowl. Mix olive oil, sesame oil, and both package seasonings, then toss through the noodles.
Serve immediately, optionally with garlic bread or chopped green onions.

intro: Ciento Quince is a luxurious coconut stew of jackfruit, pork, shellfish, and fiery chillies.
ingredients: 2 cans young jackfruit (565 g each), sliced
steps: Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic, onion, finger chillies, and ginger until fragrant.
Add pork and stir-fry until browned on all sides.
Pour in 600 ml coconut milk, bring to a boil, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add jackfruit and simmer for 30 minutes, until the liquid is nearly dry.
Add crabs, shrimps, mussels, bird's eye chillies, and remaining coconut milk; bring back to a boil and simmer 15 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Ginisang Pusit is a fast, savory squid sauté with tomato and onion.
ingredients: 2 lb medium squid, cleaned and sliced
steps: Heat oil in a wok or sauté pan over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, and tomatoes until the onion softens.
Add squid and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and water; cook 3–5 minutes, just until the squid is tender.
Season with black pepper and additional fish sauce if needed, then serve.

intro: Sinigang Mix Inasal na Manok gives grilled chicken a tangy tamarind marinade and orange annatto glaze.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into serving pieces
2 1/2 tbsp Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Recipe Mix (Original)
steps: Pound garlic, ginger, and lemongrass. Mix with Sinigang sa Sampaloc Recipe Mix, lemon-lime soda, salt, and pepper.
Put chicken in a resealable bag, add marinade, remove the air, seal, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Melt margarine in a saucepan over low heat. Add annatto seeds and cook until orange; strain out and discard seeds, then season the oil.
Heat a grill to medium heat. Grill chicken, turning every 5 minutes and brushing with annatto margarine.
Cook until the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C), then serve with warm rice.

intro: Inaloban a Isda features grilled fish gently simmered in a spicy palapa coconut sauce.
ingredients: 2 medium fish, such as tilapia or snapper
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pound spring onions, ginger paste, and bird's-eye chillies in a mortar until a paste-like palapa forms.
Grill fish over high charcoal heat for 4 minutes per side.
Heat oil in a wok; sauté shallots for 2 minutes. Add palapa and turmeric, then stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add coconut milk and capsicum, bring to a boil, and simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Add grilled fish, pechay, and coconut cream; simmer 5 minutes until pechay is tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Lomi is a thick, soothing noodle soup with pork, prawns, squid balls, and ribbons of egg.
ingredients: 500 g lomi or thick egg noodles
steps: Cook noodles according to package directions; drain, rinse, and set aside.
Fry pork belly in a little oil until golden; remove. Sauté garlic and shallot for 1 minute, then fry squid balls.
Add chicken stock and bring to a boil. Add prawns and pork; simmer 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with a little water, add to pot, and simmer 2 minutes until thickened.
Add noodles, carrot, and cabbage; bring back to a boil. Turn off heat, stir in eggs continuously, season with pepper and fish sauce, and serve.

intro: Adobo sa Patis features browned chicken and pearl potatoes in a glossy fish sauce-vinegar glaze.
ingredients: 1 tsp cornstarch, diluted in 3 tbsp water
steps: Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove and set aside.
Fry chicken and potatoes until browned on all sides.
Add water, vinegar, fish sauce, sugar, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil and simmer for 25 minutes.
Drain and reserve the cooking liquid. Cook chicken and potatoes until dry, then let them refry in their own oil for 5 minutes.
Mix cornstarch slurry into reserved liquid, return it to the wok, and simmer 5 minutes until lightly thickened.

intro: Adobong Hipon sa Gata balances shell-on shrimp with a tangy adobo sauce and creamy coconut milk.
ingredients: 1 lb shrimp, shell-on and head-on, cleaned
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add garlic and peppercorns, cooking until garlic is medium brown.
Add shrimp and cook for about 3 minutes, until orangey.
Add soy sauce and water, stir, bring to a boil, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add bay leaves and vinegar. Cover, bring to a boil, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add coconut milk, bring to a boil, and cook for 2 minutes. Season with salt, then remove shrimp to a serving bowl.
Simmer the remaining sauce until thick, pour it over shrimp, and serve.

intro: Chorizo Fried Rice turns leftover rice into a smoky, colourful one-pan meal.
ingredients: 3 chorizos, about 250 g total, roughly chopped
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and sauté chorizo until cooked.
Add garlic, bell pepper, and chilli powder; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add leftover rice and soy sauce, breaking up clumps and tossing until evenly seasoned.
Add frozen corn and paprika; stir-fry for 5 minutes until the rice is hot throughout.
Serve immediately.

intro: Linapwahan is a deeply savory shrimp soup packed with dried fish and garden vegetables.
ingredients: 6 bunch drumsticks (bunga ng malunggay), trimmed and sliced
steps: Shell shrimps and reserve meat. Briefly pulse shells with 2 cups water, strain through a fine sieve, and reserve the liquid.
Sauté garlic and onion in a little oil until soft, then add flaked daing na bisugo.
Add remaining water, shrimp-shell liquid, and tomatoes. Bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add squash, papaya, and drumsticks; simmer 5 minutes. Add okra and ampalaya; simmer 3 minutes.
Add shrimps, saluyot, and malunggay; simmer 2 minutes until shrimp is cooked. Season with bagoong monamon and pepper.

intro: Tender squid and malunggay simmer in a thick, spicy coconut sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb small to medium squid, cleaned
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until softened.
Add squid and cook for 1 minute, then remove it to a plate.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add fish sauce and green chilies.
Simmer uncovered for 12–18 minutes, until the coconut milk is thickened.
Return squid, add malunggay, and cook 5 minutes. Stir in pepper and serve with rice.

intro: Poqui-Poqui is a rustic Ilocano eggplant-and-egg scramble with sweet tomatoes.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Char eggplants over charcoal or a stovetop until skins blacken. Cool, peel, roughly chop, and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add eggplant and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper, then pour in eggs. Cook about 2 minutes until set but still moist.
Serve hot.

intro: Pork Belly Sinigang sa Sampaloc is a tangy tamarind soup balanced by gabi and fresh kangkong.
steps: Bring water, onion, tomatoes, and tamarind to a boil in a casserole; boil for 20 minutes.
Remove the tamarind from the broth.
Add pork belly and cook for 45 minutes, until tender.
Add gabi and long green pepper; cook for 10 minutes until the gabi is tender.
Add kangkong and patis, cook 2 minutes, and serve with rice.

intro: Ginisang Monggo with Kalabasa is a thick, shrimp-scented mung-bean stew with squash and greens.
steps: Soak mung beans overnight in 1/2 quart water.
Heat oil in a deep pot. Sauté garlic until browning, then add onion and tomatoes until soft.
Add hibe and soaked mung beans. Add fish sauce and 1 quart water; cover and simmer until beans are soft and broth is thick.
Add calabaza squash, cover, and cook until tender; add water as necessary.
Add malunggay leaves and spinach for 1 minute. Season with pepper and Maggi Magic Sarap, then top with chicharon.

intro: Adidas are Filipino street-food chicken feet, typically skewered and grilled until hot and charred.
steps: Thread prepared chicken feet securely onto bamboo skewers.
Preheat a grill to medium-high heat and arrange the skewers in a single layer.
Grill, turning often, until thoroughly hot with lightly charred edges, then serve immediately.

intro: Crisp lechon kawali becomes tender in creamy Ginataang Gulay sauce with kalabasa and beans.
ingredients: 1 45 g pack Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix
1/2 small butternut squash or kalabasa, cubed
23 long green beans (Baguio beans), cut into 2-inch lengths
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Sauté onion for 20–30 seconds, add garlic, and cook until onion softens.
Add lechon kawali and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix with 1 1/2 cups water and add to the pot. Cover and cook over medium heat for 45 minutes, adding water if needed.
Add kalabasa, cover, and cook 5 minutes. Add green beans and cook covered for 2–3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Dinardaraan is an Ilocano pork and blood stew with a bold vinegar finish and gentle chili heat.
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
1/4 cup white or apple cider vinegar
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until soft.
Add pork and black pepper; sauté until the pork turns medium brown.
Add broth or water, bring to a boil, reduce to low, and simmer covered for 25 to 30 minutes until tender.
Add vinegar and bring to a boil. Stir in green chilies and pork blood.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens; season with salt and serve.

intro: Asadong Baboy is tender pork in a lightly sweet, aromatic soy-anisado sauce.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornstarch, dissolved in 2 tbsp water
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork, soy sauce, anisado wine, and beef broth. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 30 to 35 minutes until tender.
Stir in brown sugar and season with salt and ground black pepper.
Add the cornstarch slurry and stir until the sauce reaches your desired thickness.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot.

intro: Tulingan Bistek is fried bullet tuna gently braised in calamansi-soy sauce and onions.
ingredients: 2 lb tulingan, cut into serving pieces
steps: Marinate tulingan with calamansi juice, soy sauce, and 3 cloves garlic for 30 minutes.
Heat oil and fry fish until golden brown; remove.
Leave about 3 tablespoons oil. Sauté remaining garlic until golden, then add ginger and onion until slightly soft.
Add remaining marinade and water; bring to a boil. Return fish, lower heat, and simmer 30 minutes, adding water if needed.
Season with sugar, pepper, and Maggi Magic Sarap. Add onion rings and green onion; cook 5 minutes and serve with rice.

intro: Sinampalukang Kambing is a sour tamarind goat soup with ginger, leeks, and green chilies.
ingredients: 1/2 cup leeks or green onion, chopped
steps: Soak goat meat in buttermilk overnight. Rinse thoroughly under running water and drain.
Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add goat, tamarind, onion, and ginger.
Simmer 60–90 minutes, skimming foam and adding water as needed, until goat is tender.
Remove tamarind and ginger. Add leeks and green chilies; cook 5 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, cook 2 minutes more, and serve hot.

intro: Ginataang Galunggong gently cooks round scad in a fragrant reduced coconut sauce.
ingredients: 4 medium round scad (galunggong), cleaned and salted
steps: Bring coconut milk to a boil in a wide pot.
Add garlic, ginger, onion, fish sauce, and black pepper. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Arrange galunggong and Serrano peppers in the pot. Cover and cook over medium heat for 30 minutes.
Uncover and reduce the sauce to about 1/2 to 3/4 cup.
Transfer carefully to a serving plate and serve with warm rice.

intro: Lechon Paksiw turns leftover lechon into a sweet, tangy, richly sauced pork dish.
ingredients: 2 kg leftover lechon leg, chopped into manageable pieces
2 cups water, plus more as needed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat, then cook the garlic and onion for about 1 minute, until aromatic.
Add the lechon along with the water, vinegar, Mang Tomas sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring the pot to a boil. Lower the heat and cook gently for 45 to 60 minutes, until the pork yields easily to a fork and the sauce has reduced and thickened; add water if it begins to dry out.
Adjust the seasoning with fish sauce, salt, and black pepper. Serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: Bistek Silog is a complete breakfast plate of bistek Tagalog, sinangag na kanin, and eggs.
steps: Prepare or reheat the bistek Tagalog until hot.
Prepare or reheat the sinangag na kanin until hot.
Place 1 cup sinangag on each of three plates.
Add one serving bistek Tagalog and two fried eggs to each plate.
Serve immediately with a preferred egg condiment, such as ketchup.

intro: Nilupak is a soft, sticky cassava treat enriched with condensed milk, coconut, and butter.
ingredients: 500 g grated cassava, frozen is fine
steps: Soak desiccated coconut in coconut milk until rehydrated.
Mix grated cassava, condensed milk, melted butter, and 1/2 cup soaked coconut in a bowl.
Cook in a wok over low heat for about 30 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and sticky.
Spread on a banana-leaf-lined tray, score with a fork, and top with remaining coconut and margarine before serving.

intro: Ginisang Mustasa is a quick mustard-green sauté enriched with salted duck egg and softly set egg.
ingredients: 2 large bunches mustard greens, trimmed, cleaned, and cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add mustard greens and salted duck egg; stir-fry until the greens begin to wilt.
Pour in stock and gently spread beaten eggs over the vegetables without stirring. Cover and cook on high for 1 minute, until eggs set.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Spicy Daing na Bangus is overnight-marinated milkfish pan-fried until deeply golden.
steps: Lay bangus open, belly-side up. Rub with Knorr Liquid Seasoning and rest 5 minutes.
Rub in peppercorns, chillies, and garlic. Pour over vinegar, turn fish belly-side down, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Heat oil in a wide pan until hot. Pan-fry fish until golden brown, using a splatter screen if needed.
Turn carefully with a wide spatula and fry the second side until golden. Drain and serve with garlic fried rice.

intro: Pata Estofado is a sweet-tangy braised pork hock finished with carrot and fried banana.
ingredients: 2 lb pork pata, boiled for 15 minutes
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and fry banana slices until browned; remove and set aside.
Pan-fry the pre-boiled pork pata for 3 minutes per side.
Add garlic and brown sugar; stir until the sugar melts.
Pour in soy sauce, vinegar, and water. Cover and bring to a boil, then add Pork Cube, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer over low heat for about 40 minutes until tender, turn pata, then cover and cook 30 to 40 minutes more.
Add carrot and fried banana, cover, cook 5 minutes, and serve.

intro: Gambas con Kabute brings prawns, mushrooms, and capsicum together in a spicy, shell-stock sauce.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with 3 tbsp water
1 tsp cayenne pepper, or to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Remove prawn heads and shells. Roast them until brownish red and crisp, then simmer with water for 10 minutes, mash, reduce to 1 cup, and strain.
Marinate peeled prawns in lemon juice for 15 minutes.
Sauté mushrooms in oil for 2 minutes; remove. Sear prawns over high heat; remove.
Sauté garlic and shallot over high heat. Add capsicum and cayenne for 1 minute, then tomato paste for 1 minute.
Return prawns and mushrooms. Add prawn stock and cornstarch slurry; boil, stirring continuously, for 4 to 5 minutes until thick.
Season with salt and pepper. Garnish with parsley and crispy fried garlic before serving.

intro: Bulanglang na Gulay is a clean, vegetable-forward Batangas soup brightened with ginger.
ingredients: 1/2 small unripe papaya, cut into wedges
steps: Bring water to a boil in a cooking pot.
Add garlic, ginger, and onion. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, unripe papaya, and kalabasa; cover and cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add eggplant, okra, and patola; cook 3 to 5 minutes until nearly tender.
Stir in the Knorr Fish Cube and cook 2 minutes.
Add malunggay and spinach. Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Spanish Style Sardines uses milkfish slowly pressure-cooked in olive oil, wine, and pickled vegetables.
ingredients: 3/4 cup white wine, plus more if needed
steps: Cover milkfish generously with salt and let stand for at least 1 hour. Rinse under running water.
Place a rack in the bottom of a pressure cooker to prevent sticking. Pack in fish, chili, bay leaves, carrot, cocktail onions, and gherkins.
Add white wine, fish sauce, olive oil, and black pepper; ensure the liquid covers the fish, adding more wine if necessary.
Heat until nearly boiling, reduce heat, seal the cooker, and pressure-cook for 45 minutes.

intro: Creamy Mais Maja Blanca is a chilled coconut-and-corn pudding topped with crisp latik.
steps: Whisk fresh milk, table cream, and cornstarch until smooth.
Bring coconut milk to a boil in a pot over medium heat.
Add sugar, condensed milk, and cream-style corn. Stir in cornstarch mixture and cook, stirring, until thick and paste-like.
Pour into a mold, cool, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Top with latik, slice, and serve chilled.

intro: Pork and Chicken Sinigang layers tender meats and vegetables in a sour tamarind broth.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
44 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix (Original)
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté pork until much of its fat renders. Add chicken and sauté until lightly browned.
Add onion, taro, daikon, and half the tomatoes; cook 5 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add water and bring to a boil. Stir in Sinigang Mix, cover, and simmer over low heat for about 1 hour, until pork is tender.
Return chicken and cook 15 minutes. Add long green peppers, string beans, okra, and eggplant; cook 8 minutes.
Add remaining tomatoes and season with fish sauce and pepper. Add kangkong, cover, turn off heat, and rest 2 minutes.
Serve hot with rice.

intro: Stuffed, crisp squid is coated in a sticky honey-soy glaze.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season squid inside and out with salt and pepper. Stuff each with chives and secure the openings with toothpicks.
Coat squid in 1/2 cup cornstarch and deep-fry for 3 minutes; do not overcook. Drain.
Meanwhile, sauté garlic and ginger in 2 tablespoons oil over low heat.
Whisk soy sauce, water, honey, oyster sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, and 2 teaspoons cornstarch until smooth.
Add sauce mixture to the pan, boil, then simmer over medium heat until thick. Remove toothpicks, score squid, and coat with glaze.

intro: Ube Buko Pie layers creamy young coconut filling over ube jam in flaky pastry.
steps: Open coconuts, reserve 1/2 cup coconut water, and scrape out the young coconut meat.
Heat evaporated milk and sugar over low heat, stirring until dissolved. Add coconut meat and cook 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with coconut water, stir into the pan, and cook until thick. Cool completely.
Line a 9-inch pie pan with one pastry sheet. Fill with pie weights and blind-bake at 220°C (425°F) for 15 minutes; cool.
Spread ube jam over the crust, add coconut filling, top with remaining pastry, seal edges, and vent the top.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for about 50 minutes, until light golden brown. Serve warm.

intro: Mango Bango is a chilled Filipino fruit-and-cream dessert with nata de coco and kaong.
ingredients: 6 ripe Filipino mangoes, flesh scooped out, cubed, and chilled
340 g nata de coco, drained and chilled
steps: Purée the flesh from 1 mango in a blender or food processor.
Whip chilled fresh cream to stiff peaks. Gradually beat in condensed milk and mango purée until evenly combined.
Combine remaining mango cubes, nata de coco, and kaong in a large bowl. Fold in mango cream until evenly distributed.
Chill until cold and serve.

intro: This baked whole-wheat penne is a simple, cheesy casserole using Filipino spaghetti meat sauce.
steps: Cook penne according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Mix spaghetti meat sauce, pimiento, and garlic powder in a large bowl.
Place pasta in a deep baking dish. Add three-quarters of the sauce mixture and toss thoroughly.
Spread remaining sauce over the pasta and top evenly with quick-melt cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 20 to 25 minutes, then broil for 7 minutes until the top is browned.
Rest briefly and serve hot.

intro: Bagnet Pancit Canton combines saucy egg noodles, shrimp, crisp vegetables, and rich bagnet.
steps: Boil 6 cups water with Knorr Pork Cube. Add egg noodles and cook until soft but not mushy; drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a clean pot; sauté onion and garlic until onion softens.
Add mushrooms, carrot, cabbage, snow peas, bell peppers, and parsley; cook 30 seconds. Add shrimp and cook until orange.
Add Napa cabbage, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and 1/4 cup water; toss for 1 minute.
Return noodles, toss thoroughly, season with pepper, and top with bagnet before serving warm.

intro: Ginisang Bagoong is a sweet, spicy sautéed shrimp paste condiment with a rich caramelized finish.
steps: Quickly rinse bagoong alamang in a fine sieve under cold water, drain well, and set aside.
Heat about 3 tablespoons oil over medium heat and sauté garlic until golden.
Add shallot and cook over low heat for 1 minute.
Add brown sugar and cook until caramelized.
Stir in bagoong alamang, vinegar, bird's eye chillies, and long green chilli; stir-fry over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add a little water if needed, cook until thick, season with black pepper, and cool before serving.

intro: Salted Egg Boneless Bangus coats crisp milkfish in a creamy, glossy salted-yolk sauce.
ingredients: 750 g boneless bangus belly, cut into serving pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season bangus with salt and pepper. Lightly coat with flour and shake off excess.
Fry in oil over medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides; remove and set aside.
Melt butter over low heat and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add mashed salted egg yolks and stir into a paste. Whisk in coconut milk until smooth.
Add sugar, paprika, and chili; simmer until thick and glossy.
Return bangus to the pan or spoon sauce over it. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

intro: Fresh mango juice is a simple, chilled Filipino fruit drink.
ingredients: 2 ripe fresh mangoes, peeled and sliced
steps: Place mango, sugar, and cold water in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth, adding more water if a lighter drink is preferred.
Taste and adjust the sugar, then chill or pour over ice before serving.

intro: Baguio Beans Guisado is a fast pork and French bean stir-fry with a lightly sweet soy finish.
ingredients: 300 g French beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
300 g pork belly, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork belly and stir-fry until cooked, browned, and crisp at the edges.
Add French beans and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce and brown sugar; stir-fry 1 minute, season with black pepper, and serve.

intro: Chicken Pastel is a creamy chicken-and-vegetable stew enriched with bacon, sausage, and evaporated milk.
ingredients: 800 g chicken thighs, deboned and diced
3 large pork sausages, cooked and sliced
steps: Fry bacon in butter until browned; remove. Sauté garlic and onion for 1 minute, then remove.
Quickly fry chicken in the same pot until browned all over; remove.
Stir flour into the pot to make a roux. Whisk in chicken stock until smooth.
Return chicken, sausage, potatoes, carrots, mushrooms, bacon, garlic, onion, and celery; boil, then simmer 15 minutes.
Add evaporated milk, return to a boil, and simmer 5 minutes. Season with salt and white pepper; garnish with parsley.

intro: Paksing Demonyu is a fiery vinegar-braised vegetable dish with sweet, sharp, and bitter notes.
ingredients: 1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 Scotch bonnet or bird's-eye chilies, finely chopped
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Generously salt ampalaya and rest 15 minutes. Rinse under cold water and drain well.
Sauté garlic, onion, ginger, and chilies in a wok until fragrant.
Combine vinegar, water, and brown sugar; bring to a boil, then add ampalaya, eggplant, string beans, and tomato.
Simmer 12–15 minutes, until vegetables are cooked. Season with fish sauce and black pepper before serving.

intro: Palapa is a fragrant Maranao condiment of aromatics, chilies, and toasted coconut.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh coconut, grated and toasted
steps: Finely chop scallions and chilies, pound ginger, and grate turmeric.
Toast grated coconut in a dry pan for about 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden.
Combine scallions, ginger, turmeric, chilies, and toasted coconut in a large bowl.
Cook the mixture in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring constantly, until dry and fragrant.
Stir in salt, cool completely, and refrigerate in a sterilized glass jar for up to 1 month.

intro: Pork Monggo with Kangkong is a hearty mung bean stew topped with lechon kawali and chicharon.
ingredients: Patis and ground white pepper, to taste
steps: Soak mung beans in 3 cups water overnight, then drain.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, and tomato until soft; add lechon kawali and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add soaked mung beans and sauté for 2 minutes. Add water, bring to a boil, then stir in Knorr Pork Cube.
Cover and simmer over low-medium heat for about 30 minutes until beans are soft, adding water if needed.
Add chicharon and kangkong; cook for 2 minutes. Season with patis and ground white pepper, then serve.

intro: Pininyahang Manok braises browned chicken in creamy coconut milk with pineapple and red capsicum.
ingredients: 2 tsp cornstarch, dissolved in 1/4 cup water
steps: Marinate chicken in 1/2 cup pineapple juice and black pepper for at least 12 hours. Drain and pat dry.
Heat oil in a wok and brown chicken evenly; remove and set aside.
Sauté ginger, garlic, and onion until fragrant. Return chicken and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add chicken stock, coconut milk, and remaining pineapple juice. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch mixture, pineapple chunks, and capsicum. Simmer 5 minutes, then season with fish sauce and black pepper.

intro: Abra Miki is a robust noodle soup with slow-simmered meat broth, bagnet, and quail eggs.
ingredients: 500 g flat egg noodles (miki), cooked according to package instructions
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion, then brown pork bones and chicken frames lightly on both sides.
Add water and bagoong monamon, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours.
Strain stock into a clean pot. Remove meat from bones and return meat to the broth.
Mix annatto powder with 1 cup stock, stir into the soup, and keep at a very low simmer. Season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Divide cooked miki among bowls. Add six quail eggs each, ladle over soup and meat, then top with bagnet and spring onions.
Serve hot with chilies and vinegar.

intro: Crisp Beef Lumpia makes a satisfying party snack with sweet chilli sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Thoroughly combine beef, carrot, garlic, spring onions, sesame oil, cornstarch, water, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Place a heaping spoonful near one corner of a wrapper set like a diamond; roll over filling, fold sides inward, then roll tightly.
Moisten the final corner with water to seal. Freeze the rolls until firm for the best frying results.
Deep-fry frozen lumpia for 8–10 minutes, until crisp, deeply golden, and the beef is cooked through.
Drain briefly and serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.

intro: Patotin is a sweet-savory braised duck finished with steamed vegetables and glossy sauce.
steps: Rub duck all over with salt and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pan and fry duck for 3 minutes per side; remove.
Sauté onion in the remaining oil until soft. Add soy sauce, pineapple juice, and lemon-lime soda; cover and bring to a boil.
Stir in Knorr Chicken Cube, bay leaves, and cracked pepper. Return duck to the pan.
Cover and boil duck for 35 minutes per side, until cooked through and tender.
Add brown sugar and banana ketchup; cook until sauce reaches your preferred thickness. Steam vegetables for 5 minutes and serve beside duck with sauce.

intro: Smoky burnt coconut and turmeric give Piyanggang Manok its distinctive deep flavor.
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, lower white parts only, trimmed and sliced
1-inch knob ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
1-inch piece fresh turmeric, peeled and roughly chopped
1/2 small red onion, peeled and quartered
steps: Grill the coconut shells over charcoal until their interiors are completely black; cool, scrape off the charred meat, and pound it into a fine powder.
Blend 1/4 cup burnt coconut, spring onions, lemongrass, ginger, turmeric, red onion, garlic, chilies, 1/4 cup oil, and salt into a smooth paste.
Coat chicken with the paste, reserve any excess, and marinate covered overnight for best flavor.
Indirect-grill the chicken in a covered charcoal grill for 45 minutes, keeping it away from direct coals.
Sauté the reserved paste until fragrant; stir in coconut milk and 1 teaspoon burnt coconut, simmer gently, and season with salt.
Move chicken over coals, baste, and turn every 10 minutes for 25–30 minutes, until charred and cooked through; serve warm.

intro: Tangy Fish Steak pairs crisp fried tanigue with savory soy-citrus sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb mackerel or tuna steak cuts
2 tablespoons lemon juice or kalamansi juice
steps: Mix soy sauce, lemon or kalamansi juice, and pepper; coat the fish and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat oil over medium-high heat and fry fish until golden brown and cooked through; arrange on a serving plate.
In the same pan, stir-fry onion rings until lightly browned at the edges but still crisp; place over the fish.
Simmer the remaining marinade for 1 minute, then spoon it over the fish and onions before serving.

intro: No-Bake Filipino Style Lasagna layers pork-hotdog tomato sauce, cheesy white sauce, and tender pasta.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add pork and cook until light brown; add hotdogs for 1 minute.
Add tomato sauce and water. Cover and cook over low-medium heat 40 minutes; season with sugar, salt, and pepper.
Boil lasagna sheets in salted water according to package directions, about 10 minutes if specified; drain.
Melt butter and stir in flour. Gradually whisk in milk until thick; stir in 1/2 cup cheddar until melted.
Layer meat sauce, pasta, white sauce, and cheese in an 8-inch square pan three times. Cover and broil at 400°F for 35 minutes, then uncovered at 350°F for 12 minutes; slice and serve.

intro: A crisp, salty daing na bisugo breakfast is especially good with warm sinangag and sharp spiced vinegar.
steps: Heat the cooking oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry all the daing for 1 minute per side, turning promptly so the first side does not scorch.
Drain the fish on a paper towel-lined plate.
Serve the daing with sinangag and sinamak or pinakurat.

intro: Crispy lechon kawali and tofu are coated in a glossy, savory Chinese-style sauce.
steps: Cut tofu into 3/4-inch slabs; deep-fry in hot oil until golden, drain, then cut into cubes.
Leave 2 tablespoons oil in the wok and sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger until fragrant.
Whisk fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, cooking wine, sugar, pork stock, and cornstarch; add to the wok and boil until thickened.
Add lechon kawali and tofu; toss over very high heat for 2 minutes, seasoning with white pepper.
Drizzle with sesame oil, transfer to a platter, garnish with spring onions, and serve.

intro: Crisp snapper is gently simmered with ampalaya in a light, aromatic broth.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
steps: Season snapper generously with salt and black pepper. Deep-fry in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain.
Heat a little oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant and translucent.
Add tomato and cook until softened. Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Add bitter gourd and simmer about 5 minutes, until it begins to soften.
Nestle in the fried snapper, season with fish sauce and pepper, and simmer 5–7 minutes. Serve hot with rice.

intro: A savory shrimp Pancit Bihon with tender noodles and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 8–12 fresh shrimp, shelled and heads removed
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Pan-fry shrimp for 1 minute per side; transfer to a plate.
In the same pot, sauté garlic, onion, and celery until fragrant. Stir in parsley and black pepper.
Add soy sauce, water, and Knorr Shrimp Cube. Bring to a boil, then cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add carrots, cabbage, snow peas, and pansit bihon. Toss gently until noodles absorb the liquid, adding water only if needed.
Return shrimp to the pot and cook for 3 minutes. Serve hot.

intro: A bright, comforting salmon-head sinigang with tender vegetables and tamarind broth.
ingredients: 1 medium white radish, thinly sliced diagonally
5 yardlong beans, trimmed and cut into 3-inch pieces
1 salmon head, gills removed, cleaned, and halved
1 medium eggplant, cut diagonally into 1-inch pieces
1 packet tamarind soup mix for 1 liter
1 bunch water spinach (kangkong), tough stalk ends trimmed
steps: Bring the water to a boil over high heat.
Add tomatoes, onion, ginger, radish, and yardlong beans. Cover, reduce to medium heat, and simmer 5 minutes, until radish is halfway tender.
Add salmon head, eggplant, okra, chilies, tamarind soup mix, and fish sauce. Stir gently and simmer 5 minutes, until fish is cooked.
Add kangkong and cook just a few seconds. Remove from heat and serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: Kiniing Bukel is a comforting smoked-meat soup with beans and tender bok choy.
ingredients: 400 g canned red or white beans, drained
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot over medium heat; sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger until fragrant and the shallots soften.
Add the kiniing and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in pork stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Add beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add bok choy and cook for 1 minute, until just tender; taste and season with salt before serving.

intro: Smoky grilled chicken becomes a hearty meal under creamy, savory chorizo gravy.
steps: Season chicken with paprika, garlic, salt, and olive oil; marinate for 30 minutes.
Grill chicken over medium-high heat for about 8 minutes per side, until fully cooked. Transfer to a platter.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a saucepan and brown chorizo, breaking it up slightly. Remove and reserve.
Melt butter in the same pan over low heat, stir in flour, then gradually whisk in milk until thickened.
Stir in tomato paste and reserved chorizo. Simmer 30 seconds, season with salt and pepper, then spoon over chicken.

intro: This comforting baked macaroni combines corned beef tomato sauce with a generous trio of cheeses.
ingredients: 1 cup shredded cheddar or quick-melt cheese
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add corned beef and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, breaking it apart.
Stir in tomato sauce and beef broth; cover, simmer over low-medium heat for 20 minutes, then add tomato paste, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook 5 minutes.
Boil 10 cups water with 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cook macaroni for 7 minutes, then drain.
Mix macaroni with the sauce and all cheeses. Transfer to a baking dish.
Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes, until hot and lightly browned.

intro: Pork Giniling with Oyster Sauce is a savory, potato-studded everyday meal for rice.
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; fry potatoes until lightly browned outside, then remove and set aside.
Using the remaining oil, sauté onion, garlic, and tomatoes until the onion softens.
Add pork and stir continuously for 2 minutes, breaking it into small pieces.
Add soy sauce and water; reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered until the liquid is reduced by half.
Stir in oyster sauce and cook 5 minutes. Return potatoes, cook 2–3 minutes, then season with black pepper.

intro: Garlicky Pechay & Tofu balances crisp tofu with lightly wilted greens.
ingredients: 2 blocks firm tofu (about 500 g), cut into small cubes
400 g pechay or baby pak choy, chopped
3 tbsp light soy sauce, or to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil for deep-frying and fry tofu until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
In another wok, sauté garlic in a little oil over low heat until light brown.
Add shallots and ginger; cook until the shallots soften.
Raise heat to high, add pechay, and stir-fry 30 seconds. Add stock and soy sauce, then cook 1 minute until slightly wilted but still crisp.
Add tofu, sugar, and sesame oil; toss to coat, season with black pepper, and adjust seasoning if needed.

intro: Suman Moron layers vanilla and chocolate rice dough inside steamed banana-leaf parcels.
steps: Whisk the first rice flour, glutinous rice flour, and white sugar; stir in one coconut milk can and vanilla.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, until a very thick sticky white dough forms; transfer to a bowl.
Whisk remaining flours, cocoa, and brown sugar; add remaining coconut milk and vanilla, then cook over low heat until slightly thickened.
Stir in peanuts, if using, and continue cooking until very thick and sticky; cool both doughs slightly.
Warm banana leaves until pliable. Spread white dough into 6-by-4-inch rectangles, layer chocolate dough inside, roll, wrap, and tie.
Steam over low heat for 30 minutes; cool slightly before serving.

intro: Bagis is a bright, fiery minced-beef dish sharpened with calamansi.
ingredients: 1/2 cup calamansi juice or lemon juice
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add bird's-eye chillies and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add beef and stir-fry until lightly browned. Add stock and a little fish sauce; bring to a boil.
Reduce to medium heat and simmer 15–20 minutes, until beef is tender and liquid is reduced.
Stir in calamansi juice and simmer 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper, garnish with red chillies, and serve.

intro: Sweet pineapple and raisins balance these slow-braised, savory pork ribs.
ingredients: 400 g canned pineapple pieces or tidbits
steps: Heat oil for deep-frying and fry potato until golden and crisp; drain.
Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant. Add ribs and brown lightly.
Add pineapple juice, chicken stock, and soy sauce. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 1 hour, adding water if needed.
Add raisins and pineapple; simmer 15 minutes. Add fried potato, season with fish sauce and pepper, and simmer 5 minutes.

intro: Bacon, eggs, and a sweet-savory adobo braise turn chicken into a rich family-style meal.
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Combine chicken, garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, and peppercorns. Cover and marinate at least 3 hours.
Cook bacon in a pan over medium heat until crisp and its fat renders; remove bacon.
Pan-fry chicken and marinade garlic in the bacon fat over medium heat for 3 minutes per side.
Add remaining marinade, water, and bacon. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low-medium heat for 30 minutes.
Stir in brown sugar, add boiled eggs, and cook 2 minutes. Season with salt if needed.

intro: Mais Con Yelo is a quick, creamy corn dessert topped with vanilla ice cream.
steps: Put 1 tablespoon sugar and enough cooked corn to fill one-third of a tall glass.
Fill the glass with shaved frozen milk.
Top with vanilla ice cream and an extra scatter of corn kernels; serve immediately.

intro: Linat-an is a clear pork-rib soup enriched with taro, greens, and fragrant lemongrass.
ingredients: 1 large taro root, cubed, or 8 Asian taro
1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 bunch spring onions, cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Cover ribs with boiling water and boil 5 minutes to release scum. Drain, rinse ribs with cold water, and rinse the pot.
Return ribs to the pot with lemongrass, onions, rice washing, pork stock, and salt. Add large taro, if using, plus water as needed.
Bring to a boil and simmer 50 minutes. Add Asian taro, if using, and simmer 10 minutes.
Add string beans and bell pepper; simmer 3–5 minutes. Add kangkong and spring onions; simmer 2 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve.

intro: Liempo Sinangag Itlog pairs juicy grilled pork belly with garlicky rice and fried eggs.
ingredients: 2–3 cups cooked white rice, preferably cold leftover rice
steps: Mix soy sauce, lemon or calamansi juice, pepper, and garlic powder; coat pork belly and marinate for at least 3 hours.
Grill pork over medium-high heat for about 3 minutes per side, basting with the marinade mixed with 1 tablespoon oil, until fully cooked; slice bite-size.
Heat remaining oil over medium heat and fry crushed garlic until light brown.
Increase heat to high, add rice and salt, then fold and break apart the rice for 5 minutes until hot and evenly garlicky.
Divide garlic fried rice among plates, top with sliced liempo and one fried egg each, and serve immediately.

intro: Fish Lumpia turns cooked flaky fish into light, crunchy spring rolls.
ingredients: 1 cup cooked fish meat, flaked, such as milkfish or mackerel
steps: Mix flaked fish, onion, carrot, cornstarch, water, sesame oil, egg, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Spoon filling along one edge of each spring roll wrapper and roll into tight cigar-shaped parcels.
Dampen the wrapper edge with water to seal, then freeze the rolls in a container until firm.
Deep-fry over low heat for 2–3 minutes, until the wrappers are crisp and golden.

intro: Puto Biñan is served with buttery, sweet, salty toppings for an easy merienda.
ingredients: salted egg, finely grated or crumbled
steps: Arrange warm prepared Puto Biñan on a serving plate.
Brush each piece lightly with melted butter while still warm.
Drizzle condensed milk over the puto, then finish with grated cheese and salted egg.
Serve immediately as a sweet-savory merienda.

intro: Chicken and miswa soup is a light, soothing bowl with annatto-tinted broth and tender noodles.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring the water to a boil, add chicken, and cook 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken, cool slightly, then shred; reserve the cooking liquid.
Heat oil in a clean pot. Sauté onion and garlic until soft, then cook shredded chicken for 2 minutes.
Stir in atsuete powder, reserved cooking liquid, and chicken broth. Boil, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
Add miswa and cook 2 minutes until tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in green onions and serve hot.

intro: Ice Scramble is a quick pink banana-flavored frozen snack with a creamy finish.
steps: Pulse ice with about one-quarter of the milk in a blender until the bottom ice is finely crushed.
Gradually add remaining milk, pulsing and loosening ice with a spoon as needed, until evenly fine and slushy.
Add milk powder, brown sugar, banana essence, and food coloring; pulse until blended and the sugar dissolves.
Spoon into four glasses and serve immediately.

intro: Grilled liempo and crisp tofu are tossed in a lively spiced vinegar dressing.
ingredients: A dash of ground black pepper
steps: Combine vinegar, chili peppers, red onion, sugar, soy sauce, and black pepper in a bowl; stir until blended.
Place chopped grilled liempo and fried tofu in a large bowl.
Pour over the spiced vinegar and toss until everything is evenly coated.
Transfer to a serving bowl, scatter with green onions, and serve.

intro: Adobong pulang sitaw is a quick soy-seasoned bean dish that can be made with or without chicken.
ingredients: 1/4 pound chicken, optional, cut into bite-size cubes
1 pound long red Asian beans, washed, trimmed, and cut into 2-inch lengths
2 tablespoons soy sauce or tamari, plus more to taste
2 teaspoons chopped garlic chives or green onions, optional
steps: Heat oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat; cook garlic for 20 to 30 seconds until fragrant.
If using chicken, add it, season with soy sauce and white pepper, and cook about 3 minutes until browned; remove.
Add long red Asian beans and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes until just tender.
Season with soy sauce and white pepper. Return chicken, if using, and toss until coated.
Garnish with garlic chives or green onions and serve with rice.

intro: Sinam-it is a glossy sweet-savory pork dish brightened with pineapple juice and banana ketchup.
ingredients: 500 grams fatty skin-on pork belly, cut into bite-size pieces
1/2 cup water, plus more as needed
steps: Heat oil in a pot or large skillet over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork, soy sauce, brown sugar, pineapple juice, banana ketchup, and 1/2 cup water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer about 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Raise heat to high and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce becomes a sticky glaze.
Taste, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: Tender talong, crisp tofu, and malunggay simmer in a quick coconut sauce.
ingredients: 40 g Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix
8 oz extra-firm tofu, air-fried for 10 minutes
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Stir Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix into water until smooth, pour into the pan, cover, and bring to a boil.
Add eggplant, cover, and cook for 8 minutes until tender.
Add air-fried tofu and cook for 3 minutes, stirring gently.
Stir in malunggay for 1 minute; season with pepper and salt, then serve hot.

intro: Kwek-Kwek are crunchy orange-battered quail eggs served with a sweet, spicy vinegar dip.
ingredients: 1 red chilli, finely chopped with seeds
Freshly ground black pepper, for the dip
steps: Whisk flour, cornstarch, baking powder, cold water, annatto powder, salt, and pepper until smooth. Rest batter for at least 30 minutes.
Mix vinegar, water, sugar, shallot, garlic, chilli, salt, and pepper for the dip; set aside.
Coat each peeled quail egg thoroughly in batter.
Deep-fry eggs in hot oil, adding them one at a time, until the coating is crisp and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with the vinegar dip.

intro: Ginisang Bunga ng Malunggay is a hearty pork and vegetable sauté with tender moringa pulp.
ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato, cut into thin strips
300 g pork belly, cut into small cubes
steps: Split each malunggay fruit lengthwise and quarter it. Scrape out the pulp in strips, then cut into 2-inch pieces.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add pork belly and brown on all sides for 5 minutes. Add tomato and cook for 1 minute.
Add pork stock, malunggay pulp, patani, and sweet potato. Bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Misua with Patola and Shrimp is a light tomato-based noodle soup finished with toasted garlic.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a deep pot over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Stir in fish sauce, tomato sauce, and black pepper, then add shrimp and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Add misua, shrimp bouillon, and patola; simmer for 3–6 minutes until noodles are tender and patola is soft.
Adjust with salt and pepper, transfer to a bowl, and top with toasted garlic.

intro: Tuba is best enjoyed simply as a chilled, ready-to-drink fermented palm-sap beverage.
steps: Keep prepared tuba refrigerated until thoroughly chilled.
Gently turn the closed bottle once or twice to redistribute any natural sediment; do not shake vigorously.
Pour tuba into small chilled glasses over ice, if desired.
Serve immediately as an alcoholic beverage.

intro: Coca Cola Beef Tapa becomes deeply savory and caramelized as its braising liquid cooks away.
steps: Mix beef with soy sauce, crushed garlic, and pepper; marinate in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours.
Place beef and its marinade in a pot with Coke and oil; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over medium heat until all liquid has evaporated completely.
Fry the beef in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until browned and caramelized; serve hot.

intro: Air Fryer Longganisa Frittata makes individual egg cups with a savory sausage topping.
steps: Halve the cooked longganisa and set aside.
Beat eggs with salt in a large bowl, then stir in bell pepper, peas, and cheddar.
Divide the egg mixture among silicone air-fryer cups and top each portion with two longganisa halves.
Air-fry at 190°C for 15 minutes, until the eggs are completely set. Unmold and serve warm.

intro: Sinigang na Sugpo is a bright tamarind broth showcasing sweet tiger prawns and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 1 40 g packet Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix, Original
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot, then add onions and tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix, then add labanos and siling pansigang; cook for 2 minutes.
Add sugpo and gently stir; cook for 5 minutes, until the prawns are opaque.
Add okra and sitaw and cook for 2 1/2–3 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Season with patis and black pepper, then transfer the hot soup to a serving bowl.

intro: Lechon belly makes a rich, peppery pork adobo with a reduced savory sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant, soft, and lightly browned.
Add lechon belly and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, beef broth, peppercorns, and bay leaves; cover and simmer over low heat for 45 to 50 minutes.
Pour in vinegar and bring to a boil, then stir in sugar.
Cook uncovered until only a little sauce remains; keep it saucy rather than dry, then serve with rice.

intro: Miki ti Batac is a rich Ilocano noodle soup colored with annatto and finished with crunchy toppings.
ingredients: 500 g dried miki noodles or thick yellow egg noodles
1 tablespoon annatto powder dissolved in 1/4 cup water
steps: Simmer chicken breast in chicken stock for 30 minutes, until cooked through. Remove chicken, shred with two forks, and reserve stock.
Sauté garlic in oil until golden. Add shredded chicken and cook 2 minutes, then add fish sauce and cook 1 minute.
Stir in dissolved annatto and cook 1 minute. Add reserved stock and bring to a boil.
Add miki and cook until tender. Season with salt and pepper, then turn off heat.
Ladle into bowls and top with bagnet or chicharon, egg halves, and spring onions.

intro: Crispy adobo gives tender pork belly a final high-heat fry and a shower of toasted garlic.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Philippine soy sauce or Kikkoman soy sauce
steps: Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove and reserve.
Brown pork belly in the same skillet over medium-high heat.
Add 1/2 cup water, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Boil, then simmer 30 to 35 minutes until tender and nearly dry.
Remove pork, drain excess liquid, and cool briefly.
Heat enough oil to 180°C. Deep-fry pork 3 to 5 minutes until crisp.
Drain on paper towels, toss with crisp garlic, and serve.

intro: Adobo sa Puti is a vinegar-forward pork belly adobo with crisp potatoes.
steps: Season pork belly with salt. Deep-fry potatoes until golden, then drain and set aside.
Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove and reserve.
Fry pork belly in the same pot until browned.
Add ½ cup water, vinegar, 2 tbsp peppercorns, 4 bay leaves, and sugar. Bring to a boil, then simmer 25 minutes.
Drain and reserve the liquid; fry pork over high heat until browned on the edges. Return liquid and potatoes, adding vinegar or water if needed.
Simmer 5 minutes, adjust salt, and serve topped with the reserved garlic.

intro: Halo Halo Ice Cream turns chilled halo-halo mix into an easy no-churn frozen dessert.
ingredients: 1 cup halo-halo mix, drained and chilled
steps: Whip chilled cream with a stand mixer until stiff peaks form, stopping before it becomes grainy.
Gently fold in condensed milk and drained halo-halo mix until evenly distributed.
Transfer to a freezer-safe container and freeze until firm.
Scoop and serve straight from the freezer.

intro: This bright Red Iced Tea blends black tea, pomegranate juice, and fresh lemon.
ingredients: 1/3 cup white sugar, or to taste
steps: Pour boiling water into a heatproof jug, add sugar and tea bags, and steep for 10 minutes.
Remove tea bags and stir until the sugar is fully dissolved.
Combine brewed tea with pomegranate juice and lemon juice; chill until cold.
Fill glasses with ice, pour in Red Iced Tea, and serve.

intro: Longaniza Rolls wrap a garlicky Filipino sausage filling in flaky puff pastry.
ingredients: 200 g raw Vigan longaniza, or another longaniza
steps: Remove longaniza from its casings and combine with pork, onion, and parsley.
Unroll puff pastry, place sausage filling down the middle, roll it tightly around the filling, and seal the edges.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with breadcrumbs, and chill at least 1 hour for cleaner slicing.
Cut into 1-inch pieces and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden brown.

intro: This rich Kare-Kare pairs tender beef tripe with peanut sauce and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups peanuts, processed smooth and creamy
steps: Boil tripe in 4 cups water for 1 hour. Drain, discard the cooking water, and set tripe aside.
Boil annatto seeds in 1 1/2 cups water for 2 minutes; set aside. Heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add tripe and sauté 1 minute. Strain annatto water into the pot and bring to a boil.
Add Beef Cube, peanut paste, and remaining water. Boil 8 minutes, then stir in rice flour mixed with 1/4 cup water until thickened.
Add snake beans and eggplant; cook 5 minutes. Add bok choy for 1 minute, season with pepper, and serve with bagoong alamang.

intro: This lighter ginataang gulay pairs shrimp, fried tofu, and colorful vegetables in a coconut sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a wok. Fry shrimp 1 minute per side, then remove.
Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in the remaining oil. Add carrots and long beans; cook 1 minute.
Add broccoli, bell pepper, and half the fried tofu; cook 2 minutes.
Mix Ginataang Gulay Mix with 1 1/2 cups water and add it with turmeric and shrimp. Cover and cook 5–7 minutes, until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, add remaining tofu, and serve with rice.

intro: This hearty Retiro-style beef pares platter pairs thick sweet-savory beef, garlic rice, and crisp chicharon bulaklak.
ingredients: 4 pounds beef shank, cut into large dice
steps: Rub ruffle fat with 2 tablespoons salt. Boil with 1 quart water and bay leaves until water evaporates, then fry in rendered fat until crisp.
Cook 2 heads minced garlic in 1/2 cup oil from cold over medium heat until golden; separate garlic from oil.
Stir-fry rice in 1/4 cup garlic oil for 4 minutes, adding it in two batches. Toss with 2 tablespoons soy sauce, salt, and 1 tablespoon browned garlic.
Pressure-cook beef shank with 1 quart water for 12 minutes; release pressure and reserve beef with stock.
Sauté ginger in remaining garlic oil for 2 minutes, then garlic for 1 minute. Add beef, stock, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and star anise; cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add brown sugar and beef powder. Stir in cornstarch mixed with 1/2 cup water until thickened; serve with rice, chicharon bulaklak, and browned garlic.

intro: Corned Beef Lomi Batangas Style is a thick noodle soup topped with crisp chicharon and tender meatballs.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix three-quarters of the corned beef, carrot, salt, pepper, 1 raw egg, and flour. Shape into meatballs and fry over low heat 1 1/2 minutes per side.
Using the remaining oil in a pot, sauté garlic until browning, then onion until soft. Add remaining corned beef and sauté 1 minute.
Add water and bring to a boil. Stir in Beef Cube and soy sauce, add noodles, cover, and cook 5 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with 1/2 cup water; stir into soup until thick. Add the remaining raw egg while stirring and cook 1 minute.
Add meatballs, season, and cook 3 minutes. Bowl the lomi and top with boiled eggs, chicharon, and green onions.

intro: Bagbet combines crisp bagnet with a colorful, savory medley of vegetables and bagoong monamon.
ingredients: 2 small Asian eggplants, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 squash or buttercup squash, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup frozen lima beans, edamame, or broad beans
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cover pork with water in a pot; add pounded garlic, pepper, salt, bay leaves, and baking powder, then simmer 1 hour 15 minutes. Cool and chill until cold.
Cut pork into 2–3-inch portions. Fry in hot oil, lowering heat near smoking, for 10 minutes; cool, chill again, then fry 5 minutes more and chop.
Sauté minced garlic, onion, and tomatoes in oil until softened.
Add squash, okra, and beans; pan-fry 2 minutes, then cover on low heat for 5 minutes.
Add string beans, bitter melon, and eggplant; pan-fry for 2 minutes.
Add bagnet, water, sugar, and bagoong monamon; cover and simmer over medium heat 5–8 minutes until vegetables are tender. Season to taste.

intro: Pinoy Shawarma Rice combines kasubha rice, grilled tapa, salad, hummus, and garlic yoghurt sauce.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon safflower (kasubha) or a pinch of saffron
125 g natural yoghurt, Greek or Indian
steps: Whisk yoghurt, 1 minced garlic clove, and salt; chill the Garlic Yoghurt Sauce.
Rinse rice, then cook with water, margarine, kasubha or saffron, and toasted garlic in a rice cooker; fluff when done.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, 4 minced garlic cloves, and pepper; marinate beef overnight, then bring it out 2 hours before grilling.
Grill beef over high heat for about 4 minutes per side, depending on thickness; rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Plate 1 1/2 cups rice per serving with cucumber, tomato, lettuce, grilled tapa, yoghurt sauce, and hummus.

intro: Roasted peppers and lemony mayonnaise give this shrimp macaroni salad a fresh, smoky lift.
ingredients: 1 lemon, or 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish
steps: Cook macaroni according to package directions, drain, and cool.
Roast bell peppers directly over a stovetop flame until softened and charred. Rinse while rubbing away burnt skin, then chop.
Heat oil in a pan and sear shrimp 2–3 minutes, until orange and cooked. Cool slightly and chop.
Mix mayonnaise, onion powder, pepper, salt, and lemon juice or pickle relish in a large bowl.
Fold in macaroni, shrimp, celery, and roasted peppers until coated. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.

intro: Ginisang monggo with pata at sotanghon is a deeply savory, creamy mung bean stew with tender pork hock.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil pork hocks in 4 cups water for 10 minutes. Drain, rinse the pork well, and set aside.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add mung beans and sauté 30 seconds. Add pork hocks and remaining 4 cups water; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 50 to 60 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes and adding water as needed, until pork is tender.
Add sotanghon and cook over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until beans are soft and creamy.
Stir in beef powder, fish sauce, and pepper. Add spinach, turn off heat, cover 1 minute, then gently stir and serve.

intro: Sinuam na Halaan at Mais is a clean clam soup brightened with sweet corn and ginger.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Add corn kernels and sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in 2 cups water, add clams and green chillies, then simmer about 10 minutes until clams open.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Stir in spring onions and simmer 2 minutes before serving.

intro: Puto Calasiao is a lightly sweet, fermented rice cake with a pleasantly chewy crumb.
steps: Combine both rices and water in a container, preferably earthenware. Soak for 2 days.
Drain, reserving the soaking liquid. Blend rice with 1 tbsp sugar, adding reserved liquid gradually until smooth like pancake batter.
Cover the batter with pierced plastic wrap and ferment somewhere warm for 3–4 days, until noticeably thicker.
Fold in 3/4 cup sugar. Fill greased puto molds, let rise 1 hour, then steam 15–20 minutes until puffed and set.
Unmold and serve warm or at room temperature.

intro: Crispy lechon sisig turns spaghetti into a silky, tangy, spicy pasta dinner.
ingredients: 500 g chopped lechon head meat, including cheeks, ears, tongue, and brains
1 teaspoon chili flakes or freshly chopped red chilies
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook spaghetti according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic for 3–4 minutes, until soft and fragrant.
Add lechon and cook until crisp and golden. Stir in calamansi juice and chili.
Whisk cream and egg yolk together. Lower heat, add mixture, and stir continuously until gently thickened without curdling.
Toss in spaghetti, season with salt and pepper, then garnish with spring onions and Parmesan.

intro: Kanto fried chicken has a calamansi-patis marinade and an airy double-fried crust.
ingredients: 15 calamansi, juiced, or 4 to 5 tablespoons lemon juice
1/2 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
steps: Score the meaty parts of each chicken thigh deeply enough for marinade and batter to penetrate.
Combine garlic, calamansi juice, fish sauce, liquid seasoning, and pepper. Marinate chicken at least 1 hour.
Heat deep-frying oil to 185°C.
Whisk cornstarch, flour, baking soda, eggs, salt, and cold water into a thick pancake-like batter.
Dip chicken in batter, dust lightly with extra flour, and fry about 15 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Cool slightly, then fry again for 2 minutes until extra crisp. Serve hot with rice and dipping sauce.

intro: Sinugno gently braises grilled tilapia in fragrant coconut milk with bok choy.
ingredients: 3 bunches baby bok choy or Shanghai bok choy
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat a charcoal grill and grill tilapia until marked and cooked; set aside to cool slightly.
Heat a little oil over medium heat and sauté ginger, garlic, and onion until fragrant.
Add coconut milk, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Carefully add grilled tilapia and simmer until heated through and infused with coconut milk.
Season with fish sauce, add bok choy, and cook for 2 minutes until slightly wilted; serve with rice.

intro: Pata Kare-Kare is a rich peanut stew of tender pork hock and vegetables served with bagoong alamang.
ingredients: 2 cups string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 cup annatto seeds, boiled in 3/4 cup water
2 tablespoons glutinous rice flour, mixed with 4 tablespoons water
steps: Boil pata in 4 cups water for 15 minutes; discard water, cool, rinse the meat, and set aside.
Sauté garlic until browning, add onion until soft, then cook pata in the pot for 2 minutes.
Add remaining 4 cups water and Pork Cube; cover and simmer over low-medium heat for 1 1/2 hours, until tender.
Blend roasted peanuts into a paste, then stir it into the stew with annatto water and diluted glutinous rice flour until thickened.
Add eggplant, banana blossom, and string beans; cook 3 minutes. Season with pepper and 1/2 teaspoon bagoong alamang.
Add pechay, cover, and cook 1 1/2 minutes; serve with rice and additional bagoong alamang.

intro: Milky Cheese Donuts are soft fried doughnuts rolled in a sweet powdered-milk coating.
steps: Combine bread flour, sugar, salt, and yeast. Mix in lukewarm water, buttermilk, and egg until a dough forms.
Knead in melted butter for about 20 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Punch down, divide, and shape into round or long donuts, enclosing processed cheese if desired.
Fry in medium-hot oil for about 3 minutes per side until golden; drain well.
Mix powdered milk and powdered sugar, then roll warm donuts in the coating and serve.

intro: Sinigang na Lechon turns leftover roast pork into a deeply savory tamarind soup.
ingredients: 1 kg leftover lechon ribs and backbones, cut into serving pieces
250 g fresh tamarind pulp or 44 g tamarind mix
steps: If using fresh tamarind, boil it in 1 cup water until soft, mash it, and strain the juice.
Combine lechon, remaining water, onion, and tomatoes in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer 20 minutes.
Add gabi and red chillies. Simmer 15 minutes, until gabi is tender and broth lightly thickens.
Stir in tamarind extract or mix. Season with fish sauce, salt, and pepper.
Add okra and simmer 5 minutes. Serve hot.

intro: A thick beef burger layered with coleslaw, cheddar, and chili con carne for a boldly messy meal.
steps: Season beef with salt and pepper, divide into four portions, and shape into thick patties.
Oil a heavy pan and heat over medium-high. Cook patties 3–4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked to your preferred doneness.
Toast bun halves cut-side down in the pan until lightly browned.
For each burger, layer bottom bun, cheese, 3 tablespoons coleslaw, patty, 3 tablespoons chili con carne, and top bun.

intro: Nilasing na Tilapia is wine-marinated, flour-crusted fish fried until crisp.
ingredients: ¾ cup cooking wine, sherry or shaoxing
steps: Rub tilapia, including its cavity, with sea salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Pour cooking wine over the fish in a deep dish; marinate 15 minutes per side.
Shake cornstarch and flour together in a resealable bag. Add fish and shake until fully coated.
Heat oil and fry over medium heat until one side is golden and crisp; turn and cook the second side the same way.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

intro: Tiyula Itum is a deeply aromatic beef soup colored by charred coconut.
ingredients: 4 lemongrass stalks, white parts only, pounded
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Grill coconut on a foil-lined tray at the oven's highest setting until blackened; cool, then process into a powder.
Season beef with salt and black pepper. Brown in batches in hot oil, then set aside.
Sauté garlic, shallots, ginger, turmeric, chillies, and burnt coconut powder in the same pot.
Return beef with lemongrass and stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for 1½ hours until tender.
Adjust salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Ginisang Labanos is a savory radish sauté with pork and dried shrimp for an everyday rice meal.
ingredients: 1 lb daikon, cut into thick strips
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add tomato and cook for 3 minutes until juicy.
Add pork and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add daikon and carrot; cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in dried shrimp, fish sauce, and pepper; cook 10 minutes more until vegetables are tender, then serve with rice.

intro: Crispy Pinatisang Liempo delivers thin, crackling pork belly seasoned simply with patis.
steps: Combine pork belly, water, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a covered pot; simmer over low-medium heat for about 60 minutes until tender.
Cool pork completely, then freeze about 1 1/2 hours to firm the fat before slicing thinly.
Toss slices evenly with fish sauce and refrigerate uncovered until completely dry.
Heat deep-frying oil to 170°C. Fry pork in batches for 3–4 minutes until golden brown and crisp, then drain.
Serve hot, ideally with spiced vinegar, rice, or drinks.

intro: Sisig pizza brings together creamy Alfredo sauce, savory sisig, onion, and fresh chili heat.
ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion, sliced into rings
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Place pizza dough on a flat baking surface and spread Alfredo sauce evenly over it.
Scatter cooked sisig across the sauce.
Top with onion rings and finger chiles, then sprinkle with chili flakes.
Bake for 20 minutes until the crust is cooked and toppings are hot.
Slice and serve.

intro: Cassava Suman is a coconut-scented steamed cassava cake wrapped in banana leaves.
ingredients: 1/2 cup desiccated coconut or fresh young coconut meat
steps: If using frozen grated cassava, thaw it and drain excess liquid. Finely grate, shred, or chop young coconut if using.
Mix cassava, brown sugar, coconut milk, and coconut until evenly combined.
Wash and dry banana leaves. Briefly pass each leaf over heat until pliable.
Place 2 spoonfuls of filling near one leaf edge, roll into a log, and fold both ends inward to seal.
Arrange seam-side down in a steamer and steam 30–35 minutes. Cool slightly before serving warm or cold.
