intro: Kinamatisang buto buto is a tomato-rich pork bone soup made bright with radish and leafy greens.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kilograms pork bones, such as ribs, neck bones, or tail
2 bunches gailan, choysum, or bok choy
steps: Cover pork bones with boiling water and boil 5 minutes. Drain, rinse away scum, and clean the pot.
Heat oil in the clean pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Return pork bones to the pot with daikon and 1 1/2 liters water. Boil, cover, and simmer over low heat for 1 1/2 hours.
Add gailan, choysum, or bok choy and simmer 2 minutes until tender.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and black pepper to taste; turn off heat and serve.

intro: Ginat-an nga Tambo is a creamy coconut stew of crab, bamboo shoots, corn, and vegetables.
ingredients: 2 cups young bamboo shoots (tambo), thinly sliced diagonally
1 tablespoon Visayan shrimp paste (guinamos) or bagoong
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil bamboo shoots until tender, drain, and squeeze out excess moisture.
Bring water to a boil in a pot; add bamboo shoots and boil for 2 minutes.
Add okra, corn, coconut milk, and pounded garlic; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add crabs and guinamos or bagoong; simmer for 5 minutes until crabs are cooked through.
Add tugabang and cook for 1 minute until wilted; season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Kalamay Hati is a dense, glossy coconut-rice cake finished with fragrant latik.
ingredients: 2 cups dark cane sugar or muscovado sugar
steps: Combine coconut milk, glutinous rice flour, and dark cane or muscovado sugar in a nonstick pan; whisk until lump-free.
Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously, for 50–60 minutes until the mixture is very thick and holds its shape.
Grease a banana leaf with latik oil and use it to line an 8–9-inch shallow round pan.
Spread in the hot mixture, top with latik, and cool before serving warm or cold.

intro: This spicy pork kaldereta gets its robust sauce from tomatoes, liver spread, broth, and Thai chilies.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until lightly browned. Stir in diced tomatoes.
Add Thai chilies, soy sauce, and liver spread; cook 2 minutes while stirring.
Add beef broth, cover, bring to a boil, then simmer 45 minutes.
Add carrot, potatoes, bell pepper, and peas. Cover and cook 5–7 minutes, until vegetables are tender; season with salt and pepper.

intro: Filipino Carbonara is a creamy bacon and mushroom spaghetti made with chicken stock and Parmesan.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook spaghetti according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Cook bacon over medium heat until crisp and rendered; remove bacon, leaving a little fat in the pan.
Add butter and garlic to the pan; sauté until aromatic, then cook mushrooms until tender.
Stir in flour for 1 minute, then gradually stir in chicken stock until smooth and thickened.
Add cream and simmer over very low heat for about 5 minutes, until slightly thick; stir in Parmesan and season.
Toss in spaghetti and bacon, simmer 2 minutes until coated, and serve.

intro: Kiam Pung is a deeply savory sticky-rice meal with pork belly, Chinese sausage, mushrooms, and hibe.
ingredients: 2 cups glutinous rice, soaked for 1 hour
3 cups water or mushroom soaking water
steps: Heat oil in a wok, sauté garlic, then stir-fry pork belly until browned all over.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, and 1 cup water. Bring to a boil and simmer until liquid reduces by half.
Add brown sugar, ginger, Chinese sausage, hibe, pepper, salt, and shiitake; simmer 2 minutes.
Transfer to a rice cooker with soaked glutinous rice and remaining 2 cups water. Mix and start cooking.
When boiling begins, stir in mustard leaves. Cook until the rice cooker switches to warm, then rest 5 minutes before serving.

intro: Stovetop BBQ Chicken has charred chicken pieces finished with a glossy calamansi barbecue sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken leg quarters, about 4 pieces
½ tbsp cornstarch dissolved in ⅛ cup water
steps: Mix chicken with soy sauce, garlic, brown sugar, banana ketchup, calamansi juice, salt, and pepper; marinate 20–30 minutes.
Remove chicken and reserve the marinade. Fry chicken over medium-high heat until browned and lightly charred on both sides.
Strain the reserved marinade into a pan, add water, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Whisk in the cornstarch slurry continuously and simmer until slightly thickened. Spoon sauce over chicken and serve.

intro: Bibingkang Malagkit is a sticky coconut rice cake crowned with a dark caramel-like coconut topping.
steps: Bring glutinous rice and coconut milk to a boil in a nonstick pot, then simmer on low, stirring occasionally, until nearly dry and thick.
Stir in 1 cup brown sugar and 1 teaspoon salt over low heat for 10 minutes, until very sticky.
Line a 9-by-13-inch baking pan with banana leaves and spread in the cooked rice.
Boil coconut cream, packed brown sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt; simmer uncovered over medium heat until reduced but still pourable.
Pour topping over rice and bake at 180°C for 20 minutes, until dark and thick but not burnt. Cool slightly and serve warm.

intro: Guisadong Togue is a quick, crisp stir-fry of bean sprouts, shrimp, and fried tofu.
ingredients: 1 large tofu block, cubed and deep-fried
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add carrot and shrimp; stir-fry 2 minutes, until shrimp are cooked.
Add fried tofu, bean sprouts, sugar, and sesame oil. Toss for 1 minute.
Add chicken stock and simmer over high heat 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately.

intro: Champinones al Ajillo is a fast buttery mushroom appetizer with bright lemon.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook until golden.
Increase heat to high, add mushrooms, and stir-fry for about 2 minutes.
Add lemon juice, season with salt and black pepper, and serve immediately.

intro: Chicharon Bulaklak is boiled until tender, then fried into crisp golden pork ruffles.
steps: Cut pork ruffle fat into roughly 3-inch pieces.
Place in a pot with water and salt; cover, bring to a boil over medium heat, and cook until fork-tender.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain thoroughly.
Heat enough oil to cover the pork in a wide pan; fry in batches, turning as needed, until crisp and golden brown.
Drain on a paper towel-lined wire rack and serve warm.

intro: Ginisang ampalaya with shrimp balances tender bitter gourd with sweet shrimp and softly set egg.
ingredients: 1 ampalaya (bitter gourd), halved lengthwise, seeded, and thinly sliced
Salt, plus 1 tablespoon for salting ampalaya
steps: Toss ampalaya with 1 tablespoon salt and rest 15 minutes. Rinse thoroughly and drain.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic until light brown.
Add onion and tomato; cook until soft.
Add shrimp and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in ampalaya and cook 3 to 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Push ingredients aside, pour in beaten eggs, and scramble until set. Mix through and cook 1 minute before serving.

intro: Kangkong and Tofu Stir Fry is a quick savory vegetable dish with crisp-edged tofu.
ingredients: 1 bunch kangkong (water spinach), cleaned and chopped
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry tofu 4–5 minutes per side until browned; cool, then cube.
Leave about 1 tablespoon oil in the pan. Sauté garlic and onion for about 2 minutes.
Add tofu and cook 2–3 minutes. Stir in oyster sauce and black pepper.
Add kangkong and stir-fry 4–5 minutes until wilted but still bright.
Season with salt, add Thai chillies if using, and serve.

intro: Relyenong Talong turns grilled eggplant into a crisp egg-bound chicken-filled meal.
ingredients: salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons oil; sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until soft. Brown chicken for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add bell pepper and peas for 2 minutes, stir in soy sauce, season, and cook until liquid evaporates.
Grill eggplants until soft inside; cool, peel, and flatten each into a fan shape with a fork.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper. Dip each eggplant for 1 minute, then fry in remaining oil for 1 1/2 minutes.
Spread chicken filling over each eggplant, pour on egg, and spoon hot oil over it until set.
Flip and fry filling-side down over low-medium heat for 2 minutes; drain and serve.

intro: This creamy cassava cake is baked twice for a rich coconut topping and melted quick-melt cheese.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a baking pan.
Whisk eggs, evaporated milk, 14 ounces condensed milk, 3 tablespoons butter, and 2 cups coconut cream until smooth.
Mix in grated cassava and 1/2 cup quick-melt cheese. Pour into the prepared pan.
Bake for 1 hour, until the cassava layer is set.
Mix remaining coconut cream, condensed milk, quick-melt cheese, and butter for the topping.
Pour topping over the cake and bake again at 350°F until thickened and lightly browned. Cool, slice, and serve.

intro: Begucan Babi is tender pork belly simmered in a sweet-savory bagoong alamang sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rinse bagoong alamang in a sieve under running water; drain and set aside.
Melt pork lard in a pot and brown pork on all sides. Remove pork.
Sauté garlic and onion until soft, then cook tomatoes and annatto until tomatoes break down.
Return pork; add vinegar, bagoong, and water. Simmer on low 45 minutes, adding water if necessary, until pork is tender.
Stir in sugar and finger chillies until sauce reduces, then season with black pepper.

intro: Pancit Canton at Bihon balances two noodles with chicken, pork, and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 100 g pancit bihon, soaked in warm water until softened
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Calamansi or lemon wedges, for serving
steps: Drain softened bihon. Heat oil in a wide pan or wok and cook pork belly until lightly browned and some fat renders.
Add onion and garlic; sauté until fragrant. Add chicken, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and pepper, then toss well.
Add carrot and cook briefly, then add cabbage and cook until it starts to soften.
Pour in 1 1/2 cups chicken stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Add bihon and toss until it begins absorbing liquid.
After about 2 minutes, add pancit canton and toss until tender, adding remaining stock as needed.
Turn off heat, drizzle with sesame oil, rest a few minutes, and serve with calamansi or lemon.

intro: Air-fried tilapia gives this Sinigang sa Miso a clean, crisp fish flavor.
ingredients: 40 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Recipe Mix
steps: Score each tilapia, rub with salt inside and out, and brush with oil. Air-fry at 350°F for 10 minutes per side; set aside.
Bring water to a boil. Add onion, tomatoes, daikon, and miso; stir until miso disperses and return to a boil.
Gently add tilapia and boil 2 minutes. Stir in Sinigang sa Sampaloc Recipe Mix until dissolved.
Add okra and long green peppers, cover, and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add mustard leaves, pepper, and fish sauce. Cover and cook 3 minutes, then serve warm.

intro: Goto is a comforting safflower-tinted rice porridge with tripe, crackling, and classic toppings.
ingredients: 300 g cooked ox tripe, sliced into strips
300 g pork crackling, broken into small pieces
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add beef broth, kasubha, and glutinous rice; boil, then simmer for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Add cooked ox tripe and simmer for another 25 minutes until rice is tender and porridge-like.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Ladle into bowls; top with an egg, spring onions, fried garlic, and pork crackling, with lemon alongside.

intro: Ube ensaymada is a soft, buttery filled bun finished with sweet margarine and grated cheese.
ingredients: 4 1/2 cups high-grade flour, plus more for kneading
3/4 cup sugar, plus 1 teaspoon for yeast mixture
1 cup cold butter, cut into small cubes
1 1/2 teaspoons ube flavocol (ube flavor extract), divided
Grated edam or cheddar cheese, as needed
steps: Mix lukewarm water, 1 teaspoon sugar, and yeast; let stand until foamy. Sift flour, 3/4 cup sugar, and salt together.
Whisk milk, egg yolks, and whole eggs. Knead dry ingredients with yeast mixture, then add egg mixture until dough forms.
Knead in cold butter, one cube at a time, for 20 to 25 minutes until smooth, elastic, and no longer sticking to the bowl.
Cover and let dough double in a warm place; for deeper flavor, refrigerate tightly covered for 12 to 48 hours, then bring out.
Deflate dough and fold in ube flavocol for a marbled effect. Divide into 24 pieces, fill each with ube jam, seal, and proof until doubled.
Bake at 180°C for 12 to 15 minutes until light brown. Cool, spread with margarine and sugar, then top with grated cheese.

intro: Pork giniling kaldereta is a thick tomato-and-liver-spread stew that comes together quickly for rice meals.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until onion softens.
Add ground pork and cook, stirring occasionally, until light to medium brown.
Add pork cube and liver spread; stir and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato sauce and water. Cover and simmer 15–20 minutes.
Add red pepper flakes, carrots, and olives; cook 7 minutes. Add bell peppers and cook 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper; cook until excess liquid evaporates, then serve with white rice.

intro: This Pinoy Burger layers sisig beef patties with sharp cheese, mango, atchara, and crackling chicharon.
ingredients: Kesong puti or goat's cheese feta
steps: Mix beef, sisig, eggs, flour, salt, and pepper. Divide into 6 portions and form thick patties.
Pan-fry patties 3–4 minutes per side, until cooked through. Mix minced garlic with mayonnaise.
Pat pork skin dry, refrigerate overnight, salt it, then roast on a rack at 160°C for 1 1/2 hours.
Raise oven to 220°C and roast skin up to 15 minutes until light brown and crisp. Cool, then break into squares.
Spread garlic mayonnaise on split pandesal. Layer patty, cheese, chicharon, mango, atchara, and banana ketchup; serve.

intro: Inampalayahang Manok is a home-style chicken stew softened by tomatoes and balanced with bitter gourd.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg chicken thighs, cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season chicken generously with salt and pepper. Salt the bitter gourd separately and set it aside.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown chicken on all sides; remove it from the pot.
Sauté garlic, onions, and ginger in the same pot, then add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Return chicken and add enough water or stock to cover it. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Rinse bitter gourd thoroughly and add it to the pot; cook 10 minutes until tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Mango Royale is a chilled graham-and-cream dessert layered with ripe Filipino mangoes.
steps: Combine crushed Graham crackers and melted butter in a 9-inch cake pan. Press firmly into an even base and freeze.
Whip chilled cream to stiff peaks. Gradually add condensed milk and mix on low speed just until combined.
Spread half the cream mixture over the frozen crust and cover with whole Graham crackers.
Add the remaining cream mixture and top with cubed mangoes.
Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours. Freeze 2 to 3 hours before serving for a firmer, ice-cream-cake texture.

intro: Dinengdeng na Saluyot with Tinapa is a gentle vegetable soup enriched with smoked fish.
ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion, cut into wedges
steps: Bring water, tomatoes, and onion to a boil in a covered pot; cook 3 minutes.
Add sitaw, okra, and ampalaya; cook 3 minutes.
Add saluyot, tinapang galunggong, and bagoong monamon. Cover and cook over medium heat for 3–5 minutes.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with warm rice.

intro: Pan de Coco is soft yeast bread filled with rich, jammy sweetened coconut.
steps: Mix warm water and yeast. Stir in eggs, brown sugar, and margarine, then add flour and salt without kneading.
Cover and let dough rise about 1 hour, until doubled.
For filling, mix coconut milk, water, dark cane sugar, vanilla, and cornstarch smooth; add coconut and gently simmer until thick like jam. Cool.
Deflate dough, divide into lime-sized pieces, flatten, fill each with 1 tablespoon coconut filling, seal, and place seam-side down on a greased tray.
Let rise 1 hour in a warm place, brush with egg wash, and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes until golden.

intro: Kimchi Beef Sinigang gives classic tamarind soup a spicy, fermented depth.
ingredients: 1 packet sinigang (tamarind) mix or 400 g tamarind
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Put brisket and onion in a large pot. Add tamarind in tied muslin, if using, and enough water to barely cover the meat.
Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for about 1 1/2 hours until beef is tender.
Add gochujang and kimchi with juices; return to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in sinigang mix, or press tamarind through a colander into the pot and discard solids.
Add enoki and cook 5 minutes. Stir in spinach until wilted, season with fish sauce and pepper, then serve.

intro: Pan-fried yellowfin tuna gently simmers in creamy coconut sauce with ginger and ampalaya leaves.
ingredients: 3 yellowfin tuna fillets, pan-fried 1 minute per side
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until onion softens. Add ginger and cook briefly.
Pour in coconut cream, stir, and bring to a boil. Add black pepper and fish sauce; cook 1 minute.
Add fried tuna fillets, spooning sauce over them. Cover and cook on low-medium heat for 12 minutes.
Add ampalaya leaves, cover, and cook 3 minutes. Sprinkle with chili flakes and serve.

intro: Tinanglarang Manok is a fragrant chicken soup brightened by lemongrass, ginger, and lemon.
ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken thighs and legs
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add chicken and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes, browning all sides.
Add stock, lemongrass, and lemon peel. Bring to a boil, then simmer 45 minutes for free-range chicken or 25 minutes otherwise.
Add spinach and lemon juice, cover, and simmer 1 minute.
Season with fish sauce or sea salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Batchoy Tagalog is a smoky pork-and-misua soup enriched with liver, heart, and pork blood.
ingredients: 350 g pork belly, cut into small cubes
100 g pork liver, cut into small cubes
100 g pork heart, cut into small cubes
100 g coagulated pork blood, cut into small cubes
steps: Light charcoal and wood chips in a covered grill. Smoke the pork belly, liver, and heart in a flameproof tray for at least 1 hour.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger paste. Add pork belly and cook until browned and crisp.
Add heart and liver; stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add water, pork stock, and finger chilies. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat 15 minutes.
Add pork blood and misua; cook 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper, garnish with spring onions, and serve.

intro: Pepitoria is a Spanish-influenced chicken stew with a silky liver, egg yolk, bread, and pine nut sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 slice white bread or equivalent breadcrumbs
steps: Season chicken and chicken liver with salt and pepper.
Heat oil over high heat and brown chicken on all sides; remove. Brown liver on all sides and remove.
Add oil if needed. Sauté garlic and onion over low heat until onion is caramelized and soft.
Return chicken, add 1 1/2 cups stock and bay leaves, cover, and gently simmer 25 minutes.
Blend browned liver with remaining 1/2 cup stock, egg yolks, bread, and pine nuts into a gravy.
Pour gravy into the pan with safflower and simmer 10 minutes until thick. Season, stir in lemon juice, and garnish with egg whites.

intro: Ginataang Pritong Tilapia pairs crisp fried fish with a spicy coconut milk sauce.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized ginger, cut into thin strips
1 large bunch baby bok choy, trimmed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cut 2–3 slits on each side of the tilapia and rub generously with salt and black pepper.
Fry at 180°C over medium heat for 5 minutes per side, until golden and crisp; drain.
Leave 3 tablespoons oil in the pan and sauté shallots, garlic, and ginger until shallots soften.
Add coconut milk, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 5 minutes. Add fish, cover, and simmer 12 minutes.
Add both chillies, fish sauce, and black pepper; cook 3 minutes. Add bok choy, cover 1 minute, then adjust seasoning and serve.

intro: Shrimp and Chicken Pancit Canton is a hearty noodle dish layered with sausage, vegetables, and savory broth.
ingredients: 8 oz (227 g) pancit canton flour noodles
steps: Heat oil in a pot and pan-fry shrimp for 40 seconds per side; remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion in the remaining oil, then add Chinese sausage and shredded chicken; cook for 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce, water or broth, and shrimp cube; bring to a boil, cover, and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add parsley, snow peas, carrot, and cabbage; cover and cook for 8 minutes. Stir in pepper.
Lay pancit canton over the liquid, cover without stirring, and cook until softened.
Gently toss noodles with shrimp, cover, and cook 3 minutes; serve with calamansi.

intro: Crispy Pritong Baboy delivers crackling pork belly with a simple vinegar-garlic marinade.
steps: Combine pork, vinegar, salt, pepper, and pounded garlic in a nonreactive bowl. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Drain pork thoroughly, removing excess liquid.
Heat enough oil for frying in a wok over medium heat. Add pork carefully.
Fry at medium-low heat, covering occasionally and turning pieces, for about 30 minutes until brown and crisp.
Drain and serve with spiced vinegar.

intro: Pork Ribs Caldereta is a hearty tomato-liver stew with tender ribs and colorful vegetables.
ingredients: salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate pork ribs in soy sauce for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok; sauté onion and garlic until softened, then brown the ribs lightly.
Add tomato sauce and beef broth, bring to a boil, cover, and cook for about 1 hour until tender.
Stir in liver spread and Thai chili. Add carrot, potato, and water if needed; cover and cook 5 minutes.
Add bell peppers and peas, cook 3 minutes, season with salt and pepper, and serve with warm rice.

intro: Japanese Siomai wraps a juicy pork-and-shrimp filling in nori for a simple steamed snack.
steps: Mix pork, shrimp, carrot, salt, cornstarch, and sesame oil thoroughly.
Place a nori sheet on a bamboo sushi mat and spread a generous, even strip of filling near one edge.
Roll firmly with the mat, pressing into a compact log. Remove the mat.
Moisten a sharp knife and cut the log into 1 1/2-inch pieces, moistening between cuts.
Steam for 20–25 minutes, until the pork and shrimp are fully cooked.

intro: Graham de Leche layers chilled leche flan, cream, and softened graham crackers.
steps: Boil sugar and water in a nonstick pan until caramelized; divide between two bread pans and let set.
Whisk evaporated milk, 400 g condensed milk, egg yolks, and vanilla; divide over the caramel.
Cover pans with foil and steam for 30 to 35 minutes until set; cool, then refrigerate.
Whip chilled fresh cream to peaks and fold in chilled condensed milk.
Top each chilled flan with cream and three layers of graham crackers, using cream between layers and on top.
Chill until crackers soften, preferably overnight, before serving.

intro: These Filipino-inspired mushroom burgers pair hearty patties with double Quickmelt cheddar and fresh sandwich layers.
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups brown or button mushrooms, finely chopped
1/2 cup rehydrated shiitake mushrooms, finely chopped
steps: Mix brown mushrooms, shiitake, beef, pinto beans, flour, eggs, onion, garlic, cumin, parsley, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Form the mixture into 8 patties. Cook in a heavy flat pan over medium heat for 4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Split buns and steam briefly until soft and warm.
Spread sandwich spread on each bottom bun. Layer greens, one patty, cheese, a second patty, another cheese slice, cucumber, tomato, and the top bun.

intro: Pork Ginataan with Squash and String Beans is a rich coconut stew brightened by squash and bagoong.
ingredients: 1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pepper and pork; cook until the pork turns light brown.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil.
Stir in coconut milk, return to a boil, then cover and cook on low-medium heat until pork is tender.
Add squash, cover, and cook for 8–10 minutes. Stir in bagoong.
Add string beans, cover, and cook 3–5 minutes until tender-crisp; add salt only if needed and serve.

intro: Max’s Style Fried Chicken is brined, steamed with aromatics, chilled, then fried until deeply golden.
steps: Dissolve salt and sugar in warm water. Submerge chicken, cover, and refrigerate for 6 hours.
Add about 4 cups water, bay leaves, garlic, and parsley to a steamer. Steam chicken for 45 minutes.
Refrigerate steamed chicken for 2 hours until thoroughly cool.
Deep-fry in enough hot oil for about 10 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack and serve.

intro: Tinolang Shell Fish is a gingery broth of mussels, clams, and tender leafy greens.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion in oil in a pot until fragrant.
Add mussels and clams with 5 cups boiling water; return to a rolling boil, cover, and simmer until shells open.
Add chilli leaves and spinach, then simmer 2 minutes until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and freshly ground black pepper; discard any unopened shells and serve.

intro: Tahong Bicol Express wraps tender mussels in a spicy, reduced coconut and shrimp-paste sauce.
steps: Bring water and crushed ginger to a boil; cook 2 minutes to infuse.
Add mussels and boil 1 minute. Drain, remove meat from shells, and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic until beginning to brown, then add onion and minced ginger until soft.
Stir in shrimp paste and Thai chiles for 30 to 45 seconds.
Add coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil. Add mussels and simmer 1 minute, then remove them.
Reduce sauce by half until thickened. Add long green pepper and mussels; cook 1 minute, season with pepper, and serve with rice.

intro: Sinabawang Isda at Gulay is a clean ginger-tomato fish soup with tender kamote tops.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a cooking pan.
Add tomatoes, ginger, and onion; cover and boil for 5–8 minutes.
Add mahi-mahi, cover, and cook over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Stir in sea salt and add kamote tops; cover and cook 1–2 minutes until wilted.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve with warm white rice.

intro: Puto maya and sikwate is a classic sweet rice and tablea chocolate breakfast served with Filipino mangoes.
steps: Wash sticky rice under cold running water and drain. Heat a steamer lined with muslin.
Bring rice and 1 cup water to a boil, then lower heat. Add 1/2 cup coconut cream and simmer 10 minutes until absorbed.
Pile partially cooked rice in the steamer.
Whisk remaining coconut cream with 4 tablespoons sugar, salt, and ginger. Pour about 1/2 cup over rice every 5 minutes, repeating twice, until sticky and fully cooked.
Boil remaining 1 cup water, whisk in tablea until smooth, then stir in milk and 2 to 3 tablespoons sugar just until hot.
Serve puto maya with sikwate and Philippine mangoes.

intro: Laing Fried Rice turns leftover rice and creamy laing into a fast, flavorful meal.
ingredients: 5 cups cooked white rice, preferably leftover
steps: Gently mix cooked rice with salt until evenly seasoned.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat; fry garlic until light brown.
Add cooked laing and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add rice and stir-fry for 5 to 8 minutes until hot and evenly coated.
Add toasted anchovies and cook 1 minute. Plate, top with chili peppers if using, and serve.

intro: Fish Stew (Paksiw na Isda sa Gata) is a rich coconut-vinegar fish dish with fried eggplant.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub fish steaks with sea salt. Heat ¼ cup oil and fry eggplant 1½ minutes per side; remove.
Add remaining oil and fry fish steaks until browned on both sides; remove.
Leave about 3 tablespoons oil. Sauté onion for 1 minute, then garlic and ginger for 1½ minutes.
Return fish, add coconut milk, long green peppers, Thai chillies, and black pepper. Cover, boil, then simmer 4 minutes.
Add vinegar without stirring, cover, bring to a boil, and simmer until the sauce reduces close to half.
Return eggplant, season with fish sauce and Maggi Magic Sarap, then serve with rice.

intro: Spicy Pork Adobo simmers pork butt in a peppery soy-vinegar sauce with dried chilies.
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and cook garlic until light brown.
Add pork and cook 3–5 minutes, until its edges are lightly browned.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and water; stir and bring to a boil.
Add chilies, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Cover and simmer 40–45 minutes, until pork is tender.
Add vinegar and return to a boil.
Stir in sugar and salt, cook 3 minutes more, and serve.

intro: Copycat Wok Inn Sipa wraps a sweet-savory pork filling in crisp, purse-shaped spring roll parcels.
ingredients: 3 rehydrated dried shiitake mushrooms, finely chopped
steps: Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic. Add pork and shiitake; stir-fry 7–8 minutes until pork is no longer pink.
Add carrot and water chestnuts; stir-fry 1 minute.
Mix fish sauce, oyster sauce, hoisin, sugar, mushroom water, and cornstarch. Add to wok with chives and stir until evenly coated.
Cool filling. Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C, then place 1 heaped tablespoon filling in each wrapper and twist into a sealed purse.
Deep-fry quickly until golden and crisp. Drain and serve hot.

intro: Pork Chop Bicol Express simmers pan-fried chops in a spicy, rich coconut sauce.
ingredients: salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan and fry pork chops for 1 minute per side; remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic and onion in the remaining oil until the onion softens.
Add coconut cream and bring to a boil, then stir in Thai chili and siling pansigang.
Return pork chops, add water, cover, and simmer over low heat for 40 minutes or until tender.
Stir in bagoong alamang and cook covered until sauce is thick and reduced.
Season with salt and pepper if needed, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Cassava and saba bananas cook into a glossy, thick coconut dessert sweetened with palm sugar.
ingredients: 400 g cassava or yucca, peeled, cleaned, and cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Combine coconut milk, cassava, and palm sugar in a pot. Bring to a boil, reduce to medium heat, and cook 10 minutes.
Add saba bananas and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in salt and raise heat to high. Cook 3–4 minutes until sauce reduces, turns glossy, and thickly coats the fruit.
Turn off heat and serve warm.

intro: Pinsec frito are crisp pork-and-prawn wontons made for dipping in sweet chili sauce.
steps: Combine minced pork, prawn meat, salt, pepper, sugar, and sesame oil until evenly mixed.
Place 1 teaspoon filling in the center of each wonton wrapper. Moisten edges, fold into triangles, and seal tightly.
Heat oil to 180°C in a deep fryer or wok.
Fry wontons in batches until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels, cool briefly, and serve with sweet chili sauce.

intro: Sinigang sa Ube brings purple yam's earthy sweetness to a tangy pork tamarind soup.
ingredients: 1 bunch kangkong or other leafy vegetables
1 packet sinigang tamarind mix or 400 g tamarind
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place pork, onion, and tomatoes in a pot; add enough water to barely cover pork. Bring to a boil, then simmer 30 minutes.
If using whole tamarind, tie it in muslin and simmer it with the pork.
Add ube and daikon, then simmer for another 30 minutes until tender.
Stir in sinigang mix, or squeeze juice from the tamarind pouch into the soup and discard the solids.
Add chilies and okra and cook for 5 minutes. Add kangkong, cover, and turn off heat.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper before serving.

intro: Sausage Macaroni Pasta is a simple marinara-coated macaroni finished with Parmesan.
steps: Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain while reserving the cooking water.
Melt butter in a pan over medium heat. Add sausage and cook for 1 minute.
Add marinara sauce and dried basil; stir and cook for 3 minutes, then turn off heat.
For each serving, bring about ¾ cup sauce to a boil, add about 1½ cups macaroni and 2–3 tablespoons reserved water, then cook 2 minutes.
Plate the pasta, top with Parmesan, and serve.

intro: Tortang Talong with Crab Meat is a tender eggplant omelet packed with savory crab.
steps: Heat 3–4 tablespoons oil in a pan. Sauté onion until soft, then stir-fry crabmeat for 2–3 minutes.
Season crab with salt, garlic powder, and pepper; cook 1 minute, then transfer to a bowl.
Peel broiled eggplants and flatten each one on a plate with a fork.
Heat remaining oil. Dip eggplant in egg, fry, spread crab on top, then spoon 2–3 tablespoons egg over it and baste with hot oil.
After 3 minutes, turn carefully and cook 3–5 minutes more until set and golden. Serve hot.

intro: This Filipino-style liver spread is a rustic, bacon-rich pâté with a gentle chili warmth.
ingredients: 1 cup plus 3 tablespoons full-fat fresh milk
steps: Cover liver with 1 cup milk and refrigerate at least 1 day. Drain and pat dry before cooking.
Heat a little oil in a pan and fry bacon until crisp. Remove bacon, leaving rendered fat in the pan.
Fry liver in the same pan until well cooked and browned on all sides. Remove.
Cook garlic and shallot in the pan over low heat for 2 minutes. Turn off heat, add butter and liver, and cool.
Process liver, bacon, rendered fat, butter, pan bits, chili, salt, and pepper to a slightly textured paste.
Blend in remaining milk 1 tablespoon at a time until spreadable.

intro: Adobong Bulalo is a richly braised beef shank adobo with a savory-tangy sauce.
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium heat; fry the garlic until lightly golden.
Add the beef shank and brown each side for about 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, water, peppercorns, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to low heat, and simmer for 60–90 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Stir in vinegar and sugar, boil briefly, then cook 3–5 minutes until the sauce is balanced. Serve with warm rice.

intro: Kalabasa and Corned Beef Nuggets are crisp, savory bites with a tender squash-filled center.
steps: Grate the kalabasa finely, then combine it with the corned beef in a bowl.
Mix in the egg, garlic powder, pepper, salt, and 1 cup breadcrumbs until cohesive; add a little more breadcrumbs only if very sticky.
Heat the oil in a deep pot over medium heat.
Shape 2 tablespoons of mixture into each nugget and coat thoroughly with the remaining breadcrumbs.
Fry in batches until both sides are golden brown, then drain on paper towels and serve with a dipping sauce.

intro: Ube Biko is a sticky purple rice cake finished with a rich custard topping and latik.
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice until the water runs clear, drain, then cook in a rice cooker with water and ube flavouring.
Heat coconut milk, brown sugar, and salt over medium heat until simmering; fold in cooked rice and stir constantly for 15 minutes until very sticky.
Press the rice mixture evenly into a 9-by-13-inch baking pan.
Whisk condensed milk, egg yolks, and vanilla in a saucepan; cook over low heat, stirring continuously, for 10 minutes until thick.
Spread the custard over the rice. Bake at 180°C for 10–15 minutes until lightly golden.
Cool, scatter with latik, then cut into portions and serve.

intro: Chicken Asado is a rich tomato-braised chicken dish with potatoes and a savory liver-spread sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 cup calamansi juice or lemon juice
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate chicken in calamansi juice, soy sauce, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour; reserve the marinade after removing the chicken.
Heat oil over medium heat and brown chicken on all sides; transfer it to a plate.
Sauté onion and garlic in the same pan until soft. Return chicken with potatoes, reserved marinade, tomato puree, stock, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is tender.
Stir in liver spread, cover, and cook 10 minutes more. Adjust salt and pepper, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Briny baby squid and bagoong turn leftover rice into a rich, savory Filipino fried rice.
ingredients: 600 g baby squid, gutted and cleaned
steps: Heat enough oil for deep-frying to 180°C; fry the salted duck eggs until lightly browned outside, then drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté pounded garlic until fragrant and lightly browned.
Raise heat to high; cook squid, bay leaves, and cayenne for 3 minutes, turning once. Season with soy sauce, salt, pepper, and calamansi juice.
Remove squid. Add oil and minced garlic to the wok; fry until golden, then stir-fry rice and bagoong for 5 minutes.
Mix in spring onions, season with salt and pepper, then return squid and cook for 1 minute.
Serve topped with fried salted duck eggs, chopped spring onions, and fried garlic.

intro: Nilauja is a deeply savory braised pork dish brightened with vinegar and fermented black beans.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Raise heat to high and brown the pork on all sides; stir in annatto powder until evenly colored.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, and water. Boil, then simmer over medium-low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes until tender and nearly dry.
Add a little water, stir to loosen the sauce, then add fermented black beans and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Season with black pepper, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: Star Bread, or Putok, is a lightly sweet Filipino roll with a signature split sugar crust.
ingredients: 4 cups bread flour or all-purpose flour
1/4 cup unsalted butter or margarine, softened
steps: Mix flour, milk powder, sugar, and salt; make a well in the center.
Add 3/4 cup lukewarm water and yeast, then mix in softened butter to form a dense dough.
Knead 7–10 minutes until smooth, adding water a tablespoon at a time only if needed.
Cover dough in a greased bowl and leave in a warm place for 1 hour.
Divide into 20 balls, place on a parchment-lined tray, snip crosses on top, and rest 30 minutes.
Whisk egg with milk, brush over rolls, sprinkle sugar, and bake at 180°C/350°F for 18–20 minutes until golden.

intro: Crispy bangus, garlic fried rice, and silky pumpkin soup make a comforting Filipino meal.
ingredients: 70 g Knorr Cream of Pumpkin Soup mix
steps: Rub the bangus with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt; set aside.
Cook garlic in oil over low-medium heat until golden; remove garlic and reserve all but 3 to 4 tablespoons oil.
Stir-fry rice over medium-high heat for 2 minutes; season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and some garlic, then cook 1 minute.
Heat reserved garlic oil to about 350°F. Coat bangus in flour and cornstarch, then fry flesh-side down 5 minutes and skin-side down 3 minutes.
Top fish and rice with parsley and remaining garlic. Boil soup mix with water, stirring until thickened, then serve alongside.

intro: Banana Chips are thin, crunchy banana slices finished with a delicate sweet-salty coating.
steps: Stir 1 tablespoon salt and turmeric into the ice water.
Peel and mandolin-slice the bananas directly into the seasoned water; soak for 10 minutes, then drain and pat very dry.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying over medium-high heat. Stir the remaining 1 tablespoon salt with 1 tablespoon water.
Fry small batches until crisp; near the end, carefully add a little salt water to the oil, standing back from splatter.
Drain chips on paper towels. Boil the remaining water and sugar, then simmer until reduced to about two-thirds.
Dip chips in the syrup, drain on a wire rack, and let dry completely before storing airtight.

intro: Silvanas are chilled cashew meringue sandwiches layered with silky buttercream and crumb coating.
steps: Draw thirty 10 x 7 cm ovals on baking paper, flip ink-side down on trays, and heat oven to 145°C.
Whip egg whites to foam; add cream of tartar, then gradually beat in 1/2 cup sugar until stiff, glossy peaks form. Fold in salted cashews.
Pipe meringue into ovals and smooth tops. Bake 20 minutes until lightly browned; switch off oven and leave cookies inside 10 minutes, then cool.
Whisk yolks, 1/3 cup sugar, vanilla, and salt over simmering water to 68°C. Cool over cold water, whip 8 minutes, then beat in softened butter gradually.
Mix graham crackers and cashews. Sandwich three meringues with buttercream, coat the outside, roll in crumbs, and chill before serving.

intro: This rich Lomi Udon pairs pork, prawns, vegetables, and glossy egg-thickened broth.
ingredients: 600 g fresh or frozen Sanuki udon noodles
3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
2 stalks negi or spring onions, sliced
steps: Cook pork belly in a large pot over medium heat until its fat renders and edges are golden.
Sauté onion and garlic in the rendered fat until soft and fragrant; add dashi and pork stock, then bring to a gentle boil.
Add prawns, carrot, and cabbage; simmer 2 minutes, until prawns are pink.
Add udon; if frozen, cook about 2 minutes until separated and hot.
Stir while adding cornstarch slurry; simmer until the broth becomes glossy and gravy-like.
Turn off heat and slowly stream in eggs while swirling. Serve with sesame oil, negi, and sesame seeds.

intro: This silky Coco Jam is a three-ingredient coconut and palm sugar spread scented with pandan.
steps: Combine palm sugar, coconut milk, and pandan leaves in a saucepan over low heat.
Stir occasionally until the sugar melts completely, then raise heat to medium and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Reduce to medium-low and stir constantly as it simmers, scraping the base so the mixture thickens evenly.
Cook until syrupy like maple syrup; it should coat a spoon but remain slightly loose because it thickens as it cools.
Remove from heat, discard pandan, and cool completely in a clean covered glass container before refrigerating.

intro: Pisatisati turns tinapa and mackerel into crisp, warmly spiced fish croquettes.
ingredients: 2 tbsp rice flour, plus more as needed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place the tinapa, mackerel, capsicum, spring onion, garlic, turmeric, and rice flour in a large bowl.
Season with salt and pepper, then work in the beaten eggs until the fish mixture can be compacted into a shape. Add extra rice flour only if it feels too wet.
Form the mixture into bite-size balls or short croquettes.
Warm frying oil over medium-high heat. Cook the croquettes in small batches, turning as needed, until deeply golden and crisp.
Transfer to paper towels to remove excess oil. Serve while hot with vinegar or palapa.

intro: Adobong Puso ng Saging turns tender banana bud into a tangy pork adobo-style main dish.
ingredients: ¼ cup water, plus more as needed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Peel away the red outer layers of the banana bud, cut into wedges, and boil until tender, about 30 minutes or less.
Drain, cool until handleable, and slice the banana bud into smaller pieces.
Heat oil in a wok and fry pork until browned. Add garlic and cook until golden, then stir-fry shallots for 2 minutes.
Add banana bud and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add soy sauce, vinegar, and water; simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add a little water if needed, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

intro: Sampalok Candy is a tangy tamarind-and-sweet-potato confection rolled in a sweet-salty coating.
ingredients: 2 cups sugar, plus extra for coating
steps: Combine tamarind pulp, boiled sweet potato, 2 cups sugar, water, and optional chilli flakes in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until very thick and cool enough to hold a ball shape.
Let the mixture cool completely. Combine extra sugar with a small pinch of salt on a wide plate.
Shape the mixture into small balls and roll each one in the sugar-salt mixture before serving or storing.

intro: Sugpo sa Gata pairs sweet prawns with a gently spiced coconut sauce.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic, onion, and chillies until fragrant and softened.
Add coconut milk, bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add prawns and fish sauce; simmer for 2 minutes, until the prawns are opaque and just cooked.
Season with black pepper, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: Pork Curry Tinola is a creamy coconut broth with tender pork, papaya, and warming spices.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add pork and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned outside. Stir in chili garlic oil and the Knorr Pork Cube.
Add coconut milk, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 20 minutes.
Add water, return to a boil, then cover and cook over the lowest heat until pork is tender.
Add papaya and cook 7 to 10 minutes. Stir in curry powder and turmeric.
Season with fish sauce, add Thai chilies and spinach, cover, and cook 2 minutes before serving hot.

intro: Shrimp Pancit Canton is a quick, savory noodle stir-fry loaded with crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 1 lb medium or large shrimp, deveined and peeled
1/2 small red bell pepper, cut into strips
1/2 small yellow bell pepper, cut into strips
1/2 small green bell pepper, cut into strips
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season shrimp with garlic powder, salt, and pepper; rest for at least 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry shrimp 1 minute per side; remove.
Add remaining oil and stir-fry onion and bell peppers for 2 minutes; add bok choy and Napa cabbage for 2 minutes, then remove.
Bring chicken broth and oyster sauce to a boil in the wok. Add Pancit Canton, tossing every minute until liquid is absorbed.
Return vegetables and cook 2 minutes. Add shrimp, season to taste, and cook 2 to 3 minutes before serving.

intro: Peach Mango Pie pairs sweet tropical mangoes and peaches under a flaky lattice crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Toss mangoes, peaches, lemon juice, sugar, flour, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Line a pie pan with one pastry sheet and spoon in the fruit filling.
Cut the remaining pastry into strips and arrange them in a lattice over the filling.
Brush the pastry with beaten egg and bake for 45 minutes, until the crust is golden brown.
Cool briefly before slicing and serving.

intro: Copycat Aristocrat South China Chicken pairs crisp fried chicken with a glossy ham, egg, and oyster sauce.
ingredients: 1 bunch choy sum, bok choy, or gailan, blanched
steps: Dissolve 1/3 cup salt and 1 tablespoon sugar in warm water. Brine the chicken in a sealed bag for 12 hours; drain and bring toward room temperature for 1 hour.
Heat deep-frying oil to 180°C. Fry the chicken for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain, cool, and chop.
Whisk chicken stock, soy sauce, oyster sauce, cooking wine, cornstarch, 1 tablespoon sugar, sesame oil, and white pepper.
Sauté garlic, shallot, and ginger paste in a wok. Add the sauce over high heat and bring to a boil.
Add ham and quail eggs; boil until the sauce thickens. Add chicken without stirring, cover, and simmer 2 minutes.
Plate chicken, spoon over sauce, ham, and eggs, and serve with blanched greens.

intro: Siopao Bola Bola are soft steamed buns filled with seasoned pork and shiitake mushrooms.
ingredients: 3 cups dumpling flour, plus 1/2 cup for dusting
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and chopped
1 tbsp vinegar per litre of steaming water
steps: Mix pork, shiitake, soy sauce, cornstarch, brown sugar, sesame oil, and salt; refrigerate while preparing the dough.
Combine yeast, 2 tsp white sugar, and lukewarm water. Leave somewhere warm for 30 minutes until active.
Knead dumpling flour, remaining white sugar, salt, shortening, warm water, and yeast mixture until smooth and elastic. Cover and rise in an oiled bowl for 2 hours.
Deflate dough, knead in baking powder for 5 minutes, then divide into 10 pieces. Roll thin, fill, pleat shut, and rest 30 minutes.
Add water and vinegar to a steamer. Steam buns for 20 to 25 minutes, until puffed and the pork filling is cooked through.

intro: Helmet is a street-food style dish of skewered chicken heads, usually grilled until browned.
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Thread cleaned chicken heads onto sturdy skewers and season with salt and pepper.
Heat a grill to medium-high heat and lightly brush the skewers with oil.
Grill, turning often, until browned and heated through, about 15–20 minutes.
Rest briefly, then serve hot as a grilled snack.

intro: Inun-unan gently braises milkfish and vegetables in a bright cane-vinegar broth.
ingredients: 2 milkfish, scaled and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
steps: Arrange milkfish, eggplants, okra, onion, garlic, ginger, chillies, vinegar, water, peppercorns, and salt in a pot.
Cover and slowly bring to a boil over medium heat.
Lower heat and simmer gently for 15 minutes, until fish is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Turn off heat and serve at room temperature.

intro: Sugpo con Mayonesa is a quick prawn dish in buttery aligue and creamy Kewpie sauce.
ingredients: 12 large tiger prawns or Argentinian prawns
⅓ cup crab fat or aligue
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a pan over low heat and gently brown the garlic.
Add aligue and increase heat to medium. Once bubbling, add the prawns.
Cook prawns for 3 minutes and season with salt and black pepper.
Stir in Kewpie mayonnaise, bring just to a quick boil, then turn off the heat.
Garnish with coriander and serve immediately.

intro: This Pork Adobo finishes tender braised pork with crisp potatoes and a glossy vinegar-soy sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Philippine soy sauce or Kikkoman
steps: Deep-fry potatoes until golden, then drain. Over low heat, fry garlic in oil until golden and set it aside.
Fry pork belly until browned. Add water, vinegar, soy sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar; boil, then simmer 1 hour until tender.
Drain the pork, reserving its braising liquid. Fry pork in clean hot oil over high heat until browned again.
Whisk cornstarch into the cooled reserved liquid, add it with fried potatoes to the pork, and simmer 5 minutes until glossy. Top with fried garlic.

intro: Squash and Eggplant in Coconut Milk is a creamy, gently spiced vegetable dish.
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until tender.
Add squash, eggplant, and fish sauce; sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer about 10 minutes until vegetables are nearly tender.
Add chili, season with pepper and salt if needed, then simmer over medium heat until vegetables are tender and sauce thickens.

intro: Sweet pork tocino gives this colorful fried rice a satisfying breakfast-style richness.
ingredients: 225 g CDO Funtastyk Young Pork Tocino
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons oil over low-medium heat and fry tocino on both sides until browned; remove and slice into serving pieces.
Beat the eggs. Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil in the same pan, cook the egg through, then chop it into small pieces.
Melt butter in the pan, add tocino, and cook for 30 seconds. Add rice and toss for 3 minutes.
Season with soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Add carrot and peas; stir-fry for 2 minutes until hot and tender.
Return the chopped egg, toss for 30 seconds, and serve.

intro: Burger Steak Sardinas turns sardines and banana blossom into hearty patties under a creamy tomato gravy.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub the minced banana blossom with 1 tablespoon salt, rinse well, and squeeze dry.
Separate sardines from their sauce. Mash sardines with banana blossom, egg, garlic powder, 1 teaspoon onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Gradually mix in 1/2 cup flour until firm, then form into patties using about 1/4 cup mixture each.
Melt butter in a saucepan, stir in 5 tablespoons flour, and cook until medium brown and lumpy.
Whisk in sardine sauce and milk gradually until smooth enough to pour; season with onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Fry patties in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat until browned on both sides. Serve topped with gravy.

intro: Java Rice gets its sunny color and fragrant flavor from annatto-infused oil.
ingredients: 4 cups cold cooked rice, hand-mashed to separate grains
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; stir-fry annatto seeds for about 1 minute until the oil turns reddish orange.
Discard the annatto seeds, leaving the colored oil in the wok.
Add garlic and cook until lightly browned, then sauté shallots until soft.
Add rice, salt, and pepper. Raise heat to high and stir-fry 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until evenly colored and heated through.

intro: Ginisang Tuna turns canned albacore into a bright, broth-kissed onion sauté.
ingredients: 1 (12 oz) can solid white albacore tuna in water, drained
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Drain the canned tuna.
Heat a small amount of oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté onion for 1 minute.
Add tuna and sauté 2 to 3 minutes, breaking it into large flakes.
Add chicken broth, cover, and cook 3 to 5 minutes until nearly evaporated.
Stir in parsley, salt, pepper, and lime juice; serve warm.

intro: Seafood Lomi Noodles is a thick, comforting noodle soup loaded with vegetables and seafood favorites.
ingredients: 55 g Knorr Crab and Corn Soup
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until the onion softens.
Add squid balls and soy sauce; sauté for 2 minutes.
Whisk Knorr Crab and Corn Soup with water, add to the pot, and bring to a boil.
Add carrots, kani, beans, and cabbage; cover and cook for 3 minutes.
Add noodles and egg, stirring for 3–5 minutes until noodles are tender; season with salt and pepper.

intro: Pinoy Style Glazed Ham is a festive pineapple-glazed centerpiece with a sweet, tangy crust.
ingredients: 4–5 kg fully cooked bone-in ham, fat on and skin removed
1 litre lemonade soda, such as Sprite or 7-Up
330 ml stout beer, such as Guinness
steps: Combine pineapple juice, soda, stout, 1 cup brown sugar, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, submerge ham, and cook over medium heat for 1 hour.
Cool the ham in its liquid, then refrigerate overnight. Drain, reserving 2 cups liquid, and bring ham to room temperature.
Boil reserved liquid with pineapple chunks, remaining brown sugar, and mustard over medium heat until reduced and thickened.
Score the ham in a crosshatch about 1 cm deep, stud intersections with cloves, and brush generously with glaze.
Roast on a rack at 160°C for 1½ hours, glazing every 30 minutes. Raise heat to 200°C and roast until well browned.
Brush with pan juices, cool slightly, carve, and serve.

intro: Tausug Beef Kulma is a slow-cooked coconut curry enriched with peanut butter, tomato, and lemongrass.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix salt, curry powder, paprika, cinnamon, and lemon juice. Coat beef and marinate for 30 minutes.
Brown beef in hot oil and set aside. Sauté garlic and onions in the same pot until soft.
Return beef with bay leaf, beef stock, and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add tomato paste, peanut butter, lemongrass, and chillies; simmer over low heat for 45 minutes.
Stir in coconut cream and cook 15 minutes more, until beef is tender and sauce is rich. Season with salt and pepper.

intro: Filipino Burger Steak features tender beef patties under a savory mushroom gravy.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Beat egg, then mix with beef, breadcrumbs, onion, and sesame oil; shape into patties.
Shallow-fry patties over medium heat until browned and cooked through; set aside.
Quickly fry mushrooms in the same pan; remove.
Melt butter in the pan, stir in flour, and cook until a smooth roux forms.
Whisk in drippings until lump-free; add onion powder, soy sauce, and mushrooms. Season, then spoon gravy over patties.

intro: Filipino BBQ Pork Skewers are sweet-savory grilled pork with a bright calamansi marinade.
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder or tenderloin, cut into bite-size pieces
1/2 cup lemon soda, such as 7-Up or Sprite
steps: Mix pork with pepper, salt, marinade soy sauce, marinade banana ketchup, lemon soda, garlic, and lemon or calamansi juice for 3 minutes.
Cover and marinate at least 3 hours, or refrigerate overnight.
Thread 5 to 6 pork pieces onto each bamboo skewer, alternating fatty and lean pieces where possible.
Mix oil, brown sugar, basting soy sauce, basting banana ketchup, and leftover marinade for basting.
Grill over medium heat, brushing before and during cooking, until browned on both sides and cooked through.
For a dipping sauce, boil any remaining marinade before serving; serve skewers with spicy vinegar if desired.

intro: This pared-back halo-halo layers creamy macapuno, banana preserves, ice, and leche flan.
ingredients: 9 tbsp minatamis na saging with syrup
steps: Set out 3 large glasses and add 2 tablespoons macapuno to each.
Divide minatamis na saging among the glasses, adding 3 tablespoons banana and 2 tablespoons syrup to each.
Fill each glass with shaved ice, drizzle generously with evaporated milk, and top with slices of leche flan.
Serve immediately before the ice melts.

intro: Morcon Hubad delivers the familiar sweet-savory flavors of morcon without rolling the beef.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat olive oil over medium heat and brown beef on both sides; transfer it to a plate.
Add more oil if needed, then sauté onion and garlic until the onion is soft and fragrant.
Return beef to the pan. Add soy sauce, calamansi juice, tomato sauce, water, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for about 30 minutes, until beef is tender.
Stir in tomato paste, carrots, capsicum, Vienna sausages, queso de bola, and pickles; simmer 10–15 minutes until carrots soften and sauce thickens.
Fold in quail eggs, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with rice.

intro: Crispy Pata combines tender marinated pork leg with blistered crackling and a sharp vinegar dip.
ingredients: 4 tablespoons brown sugar or preferred sweetener
steps: Combine soy sauce, fish sauce, Sprite, garlic, baking soda, and rock salt in a deep pot. Pierce pork skin repeatedly and submerge the legs.
Marinate for at least 24 hours, turning the pork after 12 hours.
Add quartered onion and bay leaves to the pot. Bring to a boil and cook pork for 1½ hours until tender.
Cool for at least 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until thoroughly cold.
Heat deep oil until nearly smoking. Carefully lower in pork, cover immediately, and fry until the skin is deeply golden and very crisp.
Mix red onion, garlic, pepper, brown sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, water, and chillies for dipping; serve with the crispy pata.

intro: Tuna Sisig is a quick sizzling tuna dish finished with crunchy chicharon and calamansi.
steps: Cook drained tuna in a pan over medium heat until lightly browned.
Stir in soy sauce and ground pepper.
Add onion and red chilies, mix well, and remove from heat.
Heat a sizzling plate over medium-high heat, melt butter, then add tuna and let it sizzle for a few minutes.
Top with chicharon, green chili, and optional calamansi.

intro: Lechon Manok is juicy roast chicken scented with calamansi, lemongrass, and bay leaves.
ingredients: 1/3 cup calamansi juice or lime juice
steps: Pat the chicken dry and rub salt inside and out.
Mix onion, garlic, black pepper, brown sugar, calamansi juice, soy sauce, and fish sauce. Rub over and inside chicken, then marinate overnight in a sealed bag.
Remove chicken from refrigeration 3 hours before cooking. Stuff the cavity with lemongrass and bay leaves, reserving the remaining marinade.
Roast on a rotisserie at 200°C for 1 hour 20 minutes; alternatively, roast on a wire rack over a tray.
Mix reserved marinade with 2 tablespoons oil and basting drippings. Baste every 20 minutes until the chicken is browned and cooked through.
Rest briefly, carve, and serve hot.

intro: Pancit Sisig combines smoky-crisp pork sisig with saucy bihon noodles and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 1 kg whole pork neck and/or jowl, skin on
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub baking soda over pork skin; season with salt and pepper. Roast at 160°C for 2 hours, then 180°C for 45 to 60 minutes until crisp.
Cool pork, chop finely, and toss with 1/4 cup calamansi juice, 3 tbsp soy sauce, diced onion, chillies, and salt.
Heat a wok until smoking with oil. Fry pork with minced garlic, red onion, and ginger until sizzling and crisp; off heat, add remaining juice, pepper, and eggs.
Soak bihon no longer than 10 minutes. Sauté garlic and sliced red onion in oil, then boil chicken broth with cabbage, carrot, Chinese celery, and soy sauce.
Add noodles and stir-fry 5 minutes. Season with fish sauce and pepper, then top with sisig, coriander, and sliced lemon or calamansi.

intro: Pininyahang Manok sa Gata is tender chicken braised in pineapple and coconut milk with colorful vegetables.
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Marinate chicken in the reserved pineapple juice for 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté onion, tomato, and garlic until fragrant, then stir in pepper.
Add chicken and brown lightly on both sides.
Pour in the pineapple marinade and bring it to a boil. Add coconut milk, cover, and simmer 40 minutes or until tender.
Stir in fish sauce and pineapple chunks; cook 5 minutes. Add carrots and cook 5 minutes more.
Add both bell peppers and cook 3 minutes, then serve.

intro: Sweet, tangy Pinoy Style Chicken Barbecue develops a glossy charred crust over charcoal.
steps: Mix catsup, soda, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, lemon juice, pepper, and oil in a deep bowl. Coat chicken thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for at least 24 hours.
Lift chicken from the marinade and reserve the liquid.
Whisk water and cornstarch in a saucepan until smooth; add reserved marinade, bring to a simmer, and cook for 5 minutes.
Prepare a charcoal grill. Grill chicken until the underside looks dry, then turn and baste the cooked side with sauce.
Continue turning and basting until deeply browned and the chicken is cooked through, with clear juices at the thickest part.

intro: Ginataang Bilo-bilo with Langka is a creamy coconut dessert with chewy rice balls and sago.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot.
Stir in coconut cream and return to a boil.
Gradually add sugar, stirring until dissolved.
Add jackfruit, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add bilo-bilo and cook 15 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes so they do not stick.
Stir in cooked sago and cook 3 to 5 minutes; transfer to a serving bowl.

intro: Pinakro is a simple saba banana dessert simmered in sweetened coconut milk and cream.
steps: Slice each saba banana lengthwise into four pieces.
Combine coconut milk, 1/2 cup sugar, and salt in a pot. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat and cook 10 minutes.
Raise heat to high, add coconut cream and remaining sugar, and cook 5 to 8 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve the bananas warm with the coconut sauce.

intro: Dinengdeng with Fried Fish combines fried fish with tender vegetables in a bagoong monamon broth.
ingredients: 2 cups hot pepper leaves (dahon ng sili)
steps: Rub fish with salt and fry in hot oil until golden on both sides; set aside.
Bring water to a boil, then add onion, ginger, and tomato; cover and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Stir in bagoong monamon, okra, ampalaya, and sitaw; cover and cook 7–12 minutes.
Add dahon ng sili and squash flowers; cook 3 minutes.
Lay fried fish over the vegetables, cover for 1 minute, and serve.

intro: No Bake Lasagna Pinoy Style layers pork tomato sauce, creamy cheese sauce, and tender pasta.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Brown pork in a pan, separating it as it cooks. Sauté onion 30 seconds, add garlic until soft, then stir in parsley and basil.
Add tomato sauce, cover, and simmer on low 15 minutes. Stir in tomato paste, cover, and cook 12 minutes until thick; season.
Melt butter in a saucepan, stir in flour until smooth, then gradually whisk in evaporated milk until thick and smooth.
Stir 3/4 cup cheddar into the white sauce until melted.
Boil noodles in salted water for 10 minutes or package-directed time; drain and cool briefly under tap water.
Layer meat sauce, noodles, meat sauce, and white sauce in a baking dish; repeat, finish with remaining cheddar, and microwave 8 to 10 minutes.

intro: Salted duck eggs and juicy tomatoes make a quick, punchy side for grilled or fried dishes.
steps: Place chopped salted duck eggs and tomatoes in a serving bowl.
Drizzle with light soy sauce and toss gently until evenly combined.
Serve at once alongside fried or grilled pork or fish.

intro: Bukayo is a chewy Filipino coconut sweet with deep brown sugar and pandan fragrance.
steps: Halve the young coconuts, reserve their water, and grate the coconut meat into strips.
Heat a small amount of oil in a wok over medium heat. Cook coconut strips until slightly browned, then set aside.
Boil 1 cup reserved coconut water with brown sugar and pandan leaves until reduced to a thick syrup; discard pandan.
Dissolve cornstarch in 1/4 cup coconut water.
Return coconut strips to the wok over medium heat. Stir in syrup and cornstarch mixture until very thick and able to hold its shape.
Lower heat, spoon rounds onto wax paper, and cool completely until firm.

intro: Pork Asado Kapampangan is tender braised pork in a tomato, liver spread, and cheese sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 3–4 large chunks
2 medium onions or 1 large onion, chopped
1/4 cup lemon juice or calamansi juice
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons oil over medium-high heat; fry potato slices until lightly browned and set aside.
Add remaining oil and sear pork until browned; remove from the pot.
Sauté garlic and onion over medium heat until aromatic, then add tomato sauce, citrus juice, and soy sauce.
Return pork with thyme or oregano and peppercorns; turn in the sauce for 1–2 minutes.
Add water, cover, and simmer on low 45–60 minutes until fork-tender.
Stir in liver spread, reduce to a thicker sauce, add cheese, and cook 2–3 minutes. Serve warm with rice.

intro: Pancit Puti is a light, fragrant bihon stir-fry finished with chicharon and crisp garlic.
ingredients: 400 g rice noodles (bihon), soaked 15 minutes and drained
1 large chicken leg-and-thigh section, pre-boiled and flaked
steps: Heat oil in a large wok over medium heat and sauté minced garlic and shallots until the shallots soften.
Increase heat to very high. Add bihon and flaked chicken, stir-frying continuously while adding stock 1/2 cup at a time.
Add spring onions, sesame oil, fish sauce, and white pepper; stir-fry for 1 minute until noodles are tender.
Transfer to a platter, cover generously with crispy garlic and chicharon, and serve with lemon.

intro: Honey Beef Rice combines seared beef with a sweet-savory Filipino-style sauce over rice.
ingredients: 800 g thinly sliced rump steak or sukiyaki-cut beef
2 tablespoons flour dissolved in 1/2 cup water
steps: Heat about 3 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Sear beef in batches until browned on both sides; remove.
Add a little oil and stir-fry onion over medium heat for 1 minute, until its layers separate.
Add water, scrape up browned bits, and bring to a boil.
Mix flour slurry, soy sauce, oyster sauce, hoisin sauce, and honey; add to wok and boil over high heat.
Return beef, coat with sauce, cover, and simmer on low for 15 minutes. Serve over cooked rice.

intro: Sipo Eggs is a creamy Filipino shrimp and quail egg dish with crisp vegetables and cashews.
steps: Boil quail eggs for 2 minutes, cool, peel, and set aside.
Melt butter with oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook shrimp about 1 minute per side; remove.
Sauté garlic for 30 seconds, then add onion until softened. Add ham, carrot, and jicama; cook 1 minute.
Add chicken broth, boil, then simmer 3 minutes. Stir in cream and green peas; simmer 3 minutes.
Return shrimp, season with MAGGI Magic Sarap and pepper, then gently add quail eggs and cook 1–2 minutes.
Transfer to a serving dish, top with roasted cashews, and serve warm.

intro: Lihim ni Lola is a violet cassava sweet filled with bukayo and salted duck egg.
ingredients: 1 salted duck egg, cut into 10 pieces
steps: Mix cassava, coconut milk, sugar, egg, and violet food coloring until even.
Cook in a nonstick pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 30–40 minutes until a very dense dough forms; add butter during the final 5 minutes.
Cook grated coconut and brown sugar over medium heat until caramelized; stir in cornstarch mixed with water until thick.
Divide cassava dough into 10 portions and grease 10 puto molds with coconut oil.
Press dough into molds, fill each with bukayo and one salted duck egg piece, then seal the filling inside.
Set 30 minutes, unmold, top with latik, and serve.

intro: Ensaladang Filipino is a fresh, colorful platter of smoky, salty, sweet, and savory Filipino favorites.
steps: Arrange chopped char-grilled eggplants, diced mangoes, chopped salted duck eggs, and diced tomatoes separately on a serving plate.
Place bagoong alongside the salad for dipping or spooning over individual portions.
Serve immediately as a side dish for grilled meat or seafood.

intro: Lauya de Palanyag is a rich, annatto-tinted meat soup with saba, squash, and sweet potato.
ingredients: 750 grams pork leg and/or pork bones
2 small bunches chives, tied into knots
2 tablespoons annatto seeds, soaked in 1/4 cup water
steps: Combine beef shanks, pork, onions, and enough water to cover in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off scum.
Lower to a simmer and cook 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until meat is tender and broth is flavorful.
Add saba, squash, sweet potatoes, and annatto seeds with their soaking water.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until vegetables are cooked but still firm.
Add cabbage, chives, and palm sugar. Season with salt and pepper, then simmer 5 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls.

intro: Creamy queso de bola pimiento filling makes these ham sandwiches especially festive.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups edam cheese (queso de bola), grated
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Mix mayonnaise, queso de bola, cream cheese, pimento peppers, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper until smooth and evenly combined.
Trim crusts from the bread. Spread a generous layer of pimiento cheese over one side of two bread slices.
Place one slice filling-side up, add ham, then cover with the second slice filling-side down.
Cut each sandwich into triangles and serve.

intro: Bulalugaw is a hearty beef-bone and glutinous-rice soup finished with tender shank and classic toppings.
ingredients: 2 beef leg bones, cut into 3–4 pieces each
2 large corn, each cut into 5 pieces
steps: Cover bones, onions, and peppercorns with water in a deep pot. Boil, then simmer for 2 1/2 hours.
Cool the stock; remove bones, reserve any meat, strain broth, chill until fat hardens, then discard the fat.
Sauté garlic in oil over medium heat until golden; remove for topping. Salt and brown beef shanks on all sides.
Add defatted stock and corn, bring to a boil, then simmer 1 hour until shanks are tender. Remove shanks and corn.
Add glutinous rice to the broth and simmer on low 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding water as needed for a thick soup.
Season with salt or fish sauce and pepper. Serve soup with shank, corn, reserved meat, eggs, spring onions, and fried garlic.

intro: Pastillas de Leche are soft milk candies rolled in sugar for an easy Filipino treat.
steps: Combine powdered milk and condensed milk in a large bowl, folding until a uniform dough forms.
Pinch off small portions and roll between your palms into short cylinders.
Roll every pastillas in white sugar to prevent sticking.
Wrap in cellophane and keep in an airtight container.

intro: Sago at Gulaman is an iced banana-scented drink with chewy tapioca and almond jelly.
steps: Prepare gelatin according to its package, using 1 1/4 cups water, milk, sugar, and almond extract. Chill until firm, then cut into small pieces.
Boil tapioca pearls in water for 10 minutes, strain and rinse, then return them to the boiling water until translucent with no white centers.
Boil brown sugar and 1 cup water over medium heat for 7 to 10 minutes, until dissolved and syrupy. Cool.
Combine chilled water with half the syrup, banana essence, tapioca, gulaman, and ice. Add more syrup to taste.

intro: Nilagang Pasko is a festive mixed-meat broth with corn, vegetables, Chinese ham, and chorizo.
ingredients: 3 ears corn, each cut into 3 sections
steps: Place pork leg, pork belly, chicken, Chinese ham, chorizo, peppercorns, and onions in a pot. Cover with water, boil, then simmer on low for 1 hour.
Remove chicken and set aside. Add corn and simmer on low for 25 minutes.
Add carrots and simmer 15 minutes.
Add Chinese cabbage and simmer 5 minutes.
Return chicken if desired, add spring onions, season with fish sauce, and simmer 2 minutes before serving.

intro: Creamy Pininyahang Manok is tender chicken simmered with pineapple, vegetables, and rich creamer.
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
20 oz canned pineapple chunks, juice reserved
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup cooking oil, for frying and sautéing
steps: Heat oil and fry potatoes and carrots until beginning to brown; remove.
Leave 3 tablespoons oil in the pan. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add chicken and cook until light brown.
Add reserved pineapple juice and pineapple chunks. Cover and simmer 30 minutes, adding water if needed.
Add bell peppers, potatoes, and carrots; simmer 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper, stir in creamer, and simmer 2 minutes. Serve with rice.

intro: Sizzling Teriyaki Squid is charred quickly and finished in a sweet, glossy ginger-garlic sauce.
ingredients: 2 large fresh squid with tentacles, cleaned and scored
1 tablespoon cornstarch dissolved in 1/4 cup water
steps: Combine water, soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, brown sugar, pepper, ginger, garlic, and onion in a saucepan; bring to a boil.
Stir in cornstarch slurry and simmer until thick. Remove ginger and onion.
Heat a sizzling plate over high heat.
Grill squid for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until opaque and lightly charred.
Place squid on the hot plate, pour over sauce, sprinkle sesame seeds, and serve immediately.

intro: Bulalo Mami is a deeply beefy noodle soup with corn, greens, and tender shank.
ingredients: 2 beef leg bones, each cut into 3–4 pieces
2 large corn, each cut into 5 pieces
Leafy vegetables such as bok choy or cabbage
Sea salt and/or fish sauce, to taste
steps: Cover bones, onions, and peppercorns with water; boil, then simmer for 2 1/2 hours.
Strain broth, chill until fat solidifies, then lift off and discard the fat.
Return clear broth, bones, and shanks to a pot; boil, skim, then simmer 30 minutes.
Add corn and simmer 1 hour, until beef is tender; add leafy vegetables for the final 3 minutes.
Season with salt or fish sauce and pepper. Cook noodles separately, then bowl with beef, vegetables, broth, spring onion, and fried shallots.

intro: Cheesy Chicken Afritada is a tomato-braised chicken stew finished with sharp cheddar.
ingredients: 2½ lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
½ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
steps: Heat oil in a pot and pan-fry chicken for 1–2 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.
Sauté onion in the remaining oil for 20 seconds. Add garlic and cook until onion softens.
Return chicken and sauté for 3 minutes. Add tomato sauce and broth, then bring to a boil.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 40–45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add potato and carrot; cook 5–7 minutes. Add bell pepper and cook 3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in cheese for 1 minute, then serve.

intro: Chicken Adobo with Pineapples balances tangy adobo sauce with sweet pineapple and crunchy fried garlic.
ingredients: 1 225-gram can pineapple chunks in syrup, syrup reserved
1 teaspoon cornstarch, diluted in 3 tablespoons water
steps: Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden; remove and reserve. Fry chicken wings until browned all over.
Add water, vinegar, soy sauce, reserved pineapple syrup, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar. Boil, then simmer 25 minutes.
Drain the braising liquid into a heatproof container. Cook chicken until dry and frying in its own oil, about 5 minutes.
Whisk diluted cornstarch into the reserved liquid, then return it to the wok with pineapple chunks.
Simmer 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Top with fried garlic and serve.

intro: Ginataang Manok with Kalabasa is tender chicken and squash in a quick savory gata sauce.
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 packet Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix (40 g)
steps: Heat oil in a pot and pan-fry chicken for 2 minutes per side. Remove the chicken.
Sauté onion and garlic in the remaining oil until onion softens, then return chicken to the pot.
Dissolve Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix in water. Pour into the pot, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low-medium heat for 25 minutes.
Add kalabasa, cover, and cook 7 to 8 minutes until tender. Stir in malunggay and cook 2 minutes before serving.

intro: Ginataang Kuhol braises apple snails in a spicy, creamy coconut broth with spinach.
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Sauté garlic and onion, then add ginger and cook for 1–2 minutes.
Add apple snails and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Stir in shrimp paste and chillies, then pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes. Add black pepper and spinach, then cook uncovered for 5 minutes until spinach wilts.
Serve as pulutan or with warm white rice.

intro: Tocilog is a classic Filipino breakfast plate of tocino, sinangag, egg, and atchara.
steps: Warm the prepared tocino in a skillet over medium heat until heated through and lightly caramelized.
Reheat the prepared sinangag in a pan over medium heat until hot.
Cook the sunny-side-up eggs until the whites are set and yolks remain runny or as preferred.
Mound sinangag on a plate, arrange tocino and atchara alongside, and top the rice with eggs.

intro: Fish Adobo gently simmers galunggong in a bold soy-vinegar broth until richly seasoned.
ingredients: 2 lb round scad (galunggong), gutted and cleaned
steps: Rub sea salt over each fish, including the cavities, and arrange fish in a cooking pot.
Pour in water and dark soy sauce, then bring to a boil.
Add garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves; cook uncovered for 5 minutes.
Pour in vinegar, cover, and let the liquid return to a boil.
Cook over low to medium heat for 10–15 minutes, until the liquid reduces, then serve with steamed rice.

intro: Java Rice with Pork Chop pairs golden annatto-turmeric rice with crisp brined pork chops.
