steps: Dissolve salt and bay leaves in cold water, add pork chops, cover, and refrigerate for 7 hours. Drain before coating.
Boil washed rice and water with the Pork Cube. Cover and cook over low-medium heat until done, then cool completely.
Heat annatto oil and margarine; sauté garlic and onion until soft. Stir-fry cooled rice 2 minutes, then season with turmeric, sugar, and salt.
Mix flour, baking powder, onion powder, and garlic powder in a bag. Coat each chop, dip in egg, then coat again.
Fry pork chops over medium heat until golden brown on both sides and cooked through. Serve each with Java rice.

intro: Pandan Mamon is a light, buttery sponge cake scented with buko pandan flavouring.
ingredients: ⅓ cup butter, melted, plus more for brushing
steps: Beat egg yolks, ½ cup sugar, and water at high speed until combined.
Mix in baking powder, salt, flour, melted butter, and buko pandan flavouring on low speed; set aside.
Beat egg whites with cream of tartar on high until frothy. Gradually add remaining sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Gently fold yolk batter into egg whites. Line muffin pans, place one pandan leaf in each, and fill cups three-quarters full.
Bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, until set and springy. Brush warm mamon generously with melted butter before serving.

intro: These crisp Chicken Lumpia have a seasoned ground-chicken filling and a reliably golden wrapper.
ingredients: 2 sachets Knorr SavorRich Chicken Liquid Seasoning
steps: Mix ground chicken, Knorr SavorRich Chicken Liquid Seasoning, onion, carrot, egg, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Place 1 1/2 tablespoons filling near the lower edge of each wrapper. Fold over, tuck in sides, roll tightly, and seal the tip with water.
Heat oil to about 260°F. Fry lumpia in batches for 8 minutes over low heat until wrappers brown and filling is cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack or paper-lined plate for 5 minutes, then serve.

intro: Tinolang Manok sa Upo is a gingered chicken soup with tender upo and fresh leafy greens.
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces
1 small upo, peeled and cut into large chunks
2 thumbs ginger, cut into thin strips
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add chicken and cook until lightly browned on every side. Add ginger and cook 1 minute.
Pour in rice washing or water, bring to a boil, and stir in the Knorr Chicken Cube.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, adding water if needed.
Add upo and siling pansigang, cover, and cook 5 to 7 minutes until upo is tender.
Stir in hot pepper leaves and malunggay; season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Pork Dinuguan Isaw at Tenga is a deeply savory pork blood stew with tender ears and intestines.
steps: Boil pork ears and intestines with 4 bay leaves, salt, peppercorns, and water for 20 minutes. Cool and slice into serving pieces.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil until soft. Add sliced pork and sauté 15 minutes until fat renders; remove excess fat if needed.
Add fish sauce and vinegar, bring to a boil, and cook 3 minutes. Add water, cover, and simmer 40 minutes until tender.
Stir in pork blood immediately with Serrano peppers. Cook 12 to 15 minutes, adding water if needed, until the sauce thickens.
Season with black pepper; adjust fish sauce or vinegar as desired and serve hot.

intro: Salabat is a soothing Filipino ginger tea brightened with calamansi and sweetened to taste.
steps: Place sliced fresh ginger and water in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then simmer until the tea is fragrant and ginger-forward.
Strain into cups and sweeten with honey or sugar.
Stir in calamansi juice to taste and serve warm.

intro: Killer Crispy Sinigang crowns tangy pork-and-vegetable soup with crisp fried pork belly.
ingredients: 44 g Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc mix, divided
Ground black pepper and fish sauce, to taste
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a pot; sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened. Add pork and brown lightly.
Add water and all but 1 tablespoon sinigang mix. Cover and simmer on low about 45 minutes, until pork is tender.
Remove pork, cool, rub with reserved sinigang mix and Liquid Seasoning, then air-dry at least 3 hours.
Deep-fry pork in remaining hot oil until crisp and golden; double-fry if desired.
Bring soup back to a boil. Add beans, spinach, eggplant, okra, daikon, and peppers; cook 5 minutes.
Season soup with pepper and fish sauce. Bowl the soup and vegetables, then top with crispy pork.

intro: Coconut and Okra Mango Curry balances warm spices, sweet mango, and bright lime.
steps: Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté okra until slightly browned and no longer sticky; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion until soft. Add turmeric, cumin, and paprika, and toast briefly until aromatic.
Add tomato and cook until soft, then add mango and simmer 1–2 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter, then coconut milk. Bring to a gentle boil, lightly mashing the mixture to thicken the sauce.
Return okra, simmer 5 minutes, and season with salt. Remove from heat, add lime juice, garnish with coriander, and serve hot.

intro: Shrimp Monggo with Lechon Kawali pairs savory mung bean stew with crisp pork belly.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil pork belly in 6 cups water over medium heat for 30–40 minutes; remove and cool.
Meanwhile, stir-fry shrimp in 4 tablespoons oil for 3 minutes; remove.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomato in the same pot, then add mung beans, 4–5 cups water, and Shrimp Cube; simmer covered until tender.
Coat cooled pork with Liquid Seasoning and rest 10–20 minutes. Add spinach to tender mung beans for 3 minutes, return shrimp, and season.
Heat 1 1/2 cups oil and fry pork over medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides; cool slightly and slice. Serve with monggo and rice.

intro: Ginataang Monggo with Tofu and Malunggay is a creamy coconut mung bean stew with tender greens.
ingredients: 6 cups water, plus more as needed
1½ cups water, for diluting the mix
steps: Heat oil and sauté garlic, onion, and optional tomato until softened. Add mung beans and sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in 6 cups water and bring to a boil. Add Knorr Pork Cube and cook until mung beans are mushy, adding water if needed.
Dissolve Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix in 1½ cups water, then stir it into the pot.
Add fried tofu and cook for 2 minutes.
Add malunggay, season with salt and pepper, and serve once the leaves wilt.

intro: Sinigang na Bayabas is a guava-soured pork soup with tender taro and fresh vegetables.
steps: Place pork, onion, tomatoes, and guavas in a pot; add water until barely covered.
Bring to a boil, then simmer 45 minutes until pork begins to tenderize.
Add taro and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in sinigang mix and okra; cook 10 minutes.
Add spinach, cover, and turn off heat. Season with fish sauce and pepper before serving.

intro: Bilo-bilo are chewy glutinous rice balls ready for Filipino dessert soups and coconut sweets.
steps: Combine glutinous rice flour and water in a bowl until a soft, sticky dough forms.
With slightly wet hands, scoop 1 1/2 to 2 teaspoons of dough and roll into a smooth ball.
Arrange balls in a single layer on a plate, repeating until all dough is used.
Use immediately in a Filipino dessert recipe, or cover and freeze the uncooked balls for later.

intro: Chopsuey Stir Fry keeps shrimp and colorful vegetables crisp in a lightly thickened sauce.
ingredients: 1 small red bell pepper, cut into small rectangles
1 green bell pepper, cut into small rectangles
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Fry shrimp 30 seconds per side; remove.
Sauté onion in the remaining oil until beginning to soften.
Add bell peppers, cauliflower, broccoli, snow peas, baby corn, and cabbage; stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes.
Return shrimp, season with salt and pepper, and stir-fry 1 minute.
Mix broth and cornstarch, add to wok, and toss 1 to 2 minutes until slightly thickened.

intro: Monay Bread is a soft, dense Filipino milk bread with its characteristic split top.
ingredients: 4 cups bread flour or all-purpose flour
3/4 cup lukewarm water, plus more as needed
1/4 cup unsalted butter or margarine, softened
2 tablespoons milk or evaporated milk, for brushing
steps: Mix flour, milk powder, sugar, and salt. Make a well, add lukewarm water, sprinkle in yeast, and stir to moisten.
Add butter and egg, then mix into a dense dough. Knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, adding water by tablespoons only if dry.
Place dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Deflate gently, divide into 8 balls, rest 5 to 10 minutes, then arrange on a baking tray.
Cut a deep crosswise slit halfway down each ball. Cover and proof 30 minutes, until cuts open slightly.
Bake at 160°C for 15 minutes for light brown or 20 minutes for golden brown. Brush hot rolls with milk.

intro: Kinilaw na Tanigue cures fresh wahoo in calamansi with ginger, chili, and onion.
ingredients: 2 lb tanigue (wahoo), filleted and cut into cubes
8 Thai chillies or siling labuyo, chopped
steps: Squeeze calamansi into a large bowl through a sieve, discarding the seeds.
Stir sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and black pepper into the juice until dissolved.
Add ginger, chili, and onion; stir briefly to combine.
Add fish cubes and toss until coated. Rest for 10 minutes, then taste and adjust salt or calamansi.
Cover securely and refrigerate for at least 3 hours before serving chilled.

intro: Lelot Balatong is a comforting coconut rice porridge enriched with toasted mung beans.
ingredients: 1/2 cup glutinous rice, rinsed and drained
400 milliliters coconut milk, plus extra for topping
1/3 cup sugar, or more to taste
steps: Toast mung beans in a dry pan over medium heat until browned, then cool.
Pulse cooled beans briefly until cracked but not powdered, using a food processor or mortar and pestle.
Bring half the coconut milk and water to a boil in a pot.
Add glutinous rice and mung beans. Cook over very low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding water if needed.
Once thick and mostly absorbed, stir in remaining coconut milk and sugar; simmer 5 minutes.
Serve hot with extra coconut milk on top.

intro: Shingaling is a crunchy seasoned miki noodle snack that is especially good with vinegar.
steps: Mix garlic powder, chili powder, and beef powder in a bowl.
Rub the seasoning over the miki noodles until all sides are coated.
Spread noodles in a single layer on a wide tray and sun-dry for 1 day, covered with a clean screen or cheesecloth.
Heat oil and deep-fry dried noodles until golden brown and crisp.
Drain and serve with vinegar.

intro: Pancit Canton ala Corazon is a hearty noodle stir-fry loaded with pork, chicken, liver, sausage, and vegetables.
steps: Heat oil in a wok and sauté red onion and garlic until fragrant. Stir-fry pork for 1 minute, then chicken liver for 1 minute.
Add shredded chicken and Chinese sausage; stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, water, and bouillon cube. Bring to a boil and stir until the cube dissolves.
Add Pancit Canton and raise heat to high, tossing until noodles absorb the liquid evenly.
Reduce to medium, add snow peas, cabbage, bell peppers, and carrot, then toss every 20 seconds for 3 to 5 minutes. Season and serve.

intro: Chicken Siomai are tender steamed dumplings with shrimp, mushrooms, and aromatic seasonings.
steps: Mix chicken, shrimp, mushrooms, carrots, onion, chicken powder, pepper, garlic powder, salt, sesame oil, and egg until evenly combined.
Place about 1 tablespoon filling in each wonton wrapper; gather the sides around filling, leaving the top open, until all filling is used.
Bring water to a boil in a steamer. Brush steamer racks with olive oil to prevent sticking.
Arrange siomai without touching and steam 15 to 25 minutes, until wrappers are tender and centers are fully cooked.
Serve hot with preferred dipping sauce and chili.

intro: Special Chicken Afritada enriches tomato-braised chicken with liver, hotdogs, vegetables, and cheese.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into serving pieces
Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok and pan-fry potatoes and carrots for 3–4 minutes until lightly browned; set aside.
Leave 3 tablespoons oil. Fry chicken liver 30 seconds per side and set aside, then sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add chicken and sauté until lightly browned. Add soy sauce for 30 seconds, then hotdogs for 1 minute.
Add tomato sauce and 1 cup water; bring to a boil. Add liver and bay leaves, then simmer 30 minutes.
Add peas and bell peppers for 2 minutes, then stir in potatoes and carrots.
Stir in Maggi Magic Chicken Cube for 1 minute, adjust with fish sauce and pepper, top with cheese, and serve.

intro: Hopia Mongo is flaky pastry wrapped around a sweet, thick adzuki bean filling.
steps: Cover beans with water by about 2 inches, boil until soft, adding water as needed, then mash.
Cook over low heat with sugar and butter until dissolved; stir in flour until a very thick paste forms, then cool.
Thaw one pastry roll, halve it, wrap each half around half the filling, and chill the two filled rolls for 1 hour.
Thaw remaining pastry, cut rounds, slice filled rolls into 1-inch pieces, and enclose each slice between pastry rounds, sealing edges.
Brush with egg and bake in a greased pan at 200°C for 8 minutes per side. Cool before serving.

intro: Halaan Bopis gives chopped clam meat a spicy, sour, aromatic sauté treatment.
ingredients: 800 g steamed clam meat, finely chopped
1 tablespoon annatto powder, dissolved in 3 tablespoons stock
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant and translucent.
Add clam meat, chillies, and bay leaves; stir-fry for about 3 minutes.
Add capsicum, 1 cup vinegar, clam stock, bruised lemongrass, and pandan. Bring to a boil over high heat until the sauce thickens.
Add more vinegar to taste, then stir in dissolved annatto powder.
Season with fish sauce, pepper, and salt. Simmer 2 minutes, discard lemongrass and pandan, and serve hot.

intro: Spicy Sotanghon Chicken Soup is a fragrant ginger-lemongrass chicken broth with tender glass noodles.
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Crush garlic, onion, ginger, lemongrass, and Thai chilies with a mortar and pestle or food processor.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the crushed aromatics for 1 minute.
Add chicken and sauté until lightly browned outside.
Add water, bring to a boil, then add the Knorr Chicken Cube. Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 30 minutes.
Add sotanghon and cook 3 minutes until tender.
Stir in green onions, patis, and white pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Mango Cake is a tall chiffon layer cake filled with cream cheese frosting and fresh Philippine mangoes.
ingredients: 3 cups fresh Philippine mango flesh, puréed
7 large eggs, yolks and whites separated
⅓ cup reduced mango purée or mango concentrate
80 g cream cheese, cubed and at room temperature
steps: Simmer mango purée, lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons sugar over low heat until reduced to 1 cup. Reserve ⅓ cup for batter.
Whisk flour, corn flour, baking powder, salt, and ¾ cup sugar. Mix in oil, yolks, mango juice, reserved purée, and vanilla.
Beat whites with cream of tartar until frothy; gradually add remaining sugar to stiff peaks, then gently fold into batter.
Divide between two 9-inch pans and bake at 180°C for 50 minutes, until a tester comes out clean. Cool completely, then split each cake horizontally.
Whip cream, icing sugar, and vanilla until stiff. Fold in cream cheese without overbeating; layer cakes with frosting and sliced mangoes.
Dissolve gelatine in boiling water and mix into remaining mango purée. Frost cake, drizzle with mango topping, decorate with mangoes, and chill.

intro: Fish Kardilyo features cornmeal-crusted tilapia topped with a quick tomato-and-egg sauce.
steps: Rub tilapia with salt and pepper, then let stand for 10 minutes. Heat oil in a frying pan.
Dredge fish in flour, dip in some beaten egg, and coat with cornmeal. Fry until light golden brown on both sides; set aside.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened. Add fish sauce and pepper, then pour in water and bring to a boil.
Simmer 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in the remaining beaten egg for 5 seconds, then spoon sauce over fried fish and garnish with scallions.

intro: Tinuom na Manok steams chicken in fragrant banana-leaf parcels with a warming savory broth.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Lay a ginger slice on each banana leaf, top with chicken, red onion, tomato, and lemongrass, then season with salt and pepper.
Fold leaves into secure parcels and tie with kitchen twine.
Place parcels in a deep pot with chicken stock, water, fish sauce, and white onions; bring slowly to a boil.
Lower to a simmer and cook 1 hour, until chicken is tender and fully cooked.
Place a parcel in each bowl, open carefully, and ladle over hot broth.

intro: Sinigang na Buto-buto with Gabi is a tart pork-bone soup with soft taro and fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 1 pack tamarind-base sinigang mix, for 2 liters
3 cups water spinach (kangkong), stems chopped and leaves separated
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork neck bones and fish sauce; cook briefly, then add water and bring to a boil.
Add tomatoes, lower heat, and simmer 40 minutes or until pork is tender.
Add sinigang mix, radish, chilies, and gabi; simmer 8 minutes.
Add eggplant and okra; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in kangkong, turn off heat, cover 5 minutes, then serve.

intro: Kareng Ingles is a coconut-braised chicken dish with okra, snake beans, bok choy, and chilies.
ingredients: 1 bunch snake beans, cut into 2-inch sections
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add chicken and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes, browning all sides.
Add coconut milk and chicken stock, bring to a boil, then simmer 25 minutes.
Add snake beans and okra and simmer 5 minutes.
Add green chilies and bok choy, cover, and simmer 2 minutes.
Season with fish sauce or sea salt and black pepper before serving.

intro: Ginataang Alimango combines tender mud crab, squash, beans, and chili in thick coconut milk.
ingredients: 1 cup yardlong beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Bring enough water to boil in a large pot. Add crabs head-first, salt, and simmer 10 minutes; halve crabs and reserve 1/2 cup cooking liquid.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil over medium heat until tender and aromatic. Add squash and water or reserved crab stock.
Simmer until squash is tender, then add coconut milk and cook until squash is very soft and the sauce is thickened.
Add crab, yardlong beans, chili, and fish sauce. Simmer 10–15 minutes until beans are tender and sauce thickens.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve with steamed rice.

intro: Sinigang na Baboy with Gabi is a hearty tamarind pork soup with vegetables and soft taro.
ingredients: 2 packets Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix Original, 20 g each
steps: Bring water to a boil; add onion and tomatoes and cook 5–8 minutes.
Add pork and boil 25 minutes, then add gabi, cover, and boil 30 minutes.
Stir in Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix, patis, and pepper.
Add labanos and cook 3–5 minutes.
Add siling pansigang, okra, and sitaw; cook 7 minutes.
Add kangkong, cover, turn off heat, and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

intro: Pinipig Ice Drops are creamy frozen milk treats with crisp pinipig and a crackling chocolate shell.
steps: Whisk cornstarch with 1/4 cup milk. In a saucepan, whisk sugar and 1/2 cup milk powder, then gradually whisk in whole milk.
Heat over medium until simmering. Whisk in slurry and cook until thickened but still pourable; stir in vanilla.
Cool slightly, fill ice-drop molds, insert sticks, and freeze at least 4 hours or overnight.
Mix coconut oil, cocoa powder, powdered sugar, and optional milk powder until smooth. Unmold frozen drops by briefly dipping molds in lukewarm water.
Coat each drop in pinipig, dip in chocolate mixture once or more for a thicker shell, let harden, and serve or refreeze.

intro: This Aloha Yumburger-style burger layers beef, bacon, pineapple, cheese, and honey mustard.
ingredients: 4 burger buns or brioche burger buns
8 slices streaky bacon, each cut in half
4 lettuce leaves, folded to bun size
steps: Divide beef into 4 equal portions, form patties, and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Fry bacon until crisp on both sides, then remove.
Cook patties in the same skillet for 3–4 minutes per side; remove and keep warm.
Build each burger with bottom bun, hot patty, cheese, pineapple, four bacon halves, folded lettuce, honey mustard sauce, and top bun.
Serve immediately.

intro: Chilli Butter Garlic Tilapia is crisp fried fish coated in a sweet, spicy, buttery garlic sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Season tilapia with salt and pepper, then deep-fry in medium-hot oil about 10 minutes until golden and crisp; drain.
Heat a little oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic and shallots for about 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add capsicum and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in butter, chili garlic oil, and oyster sauce until melted and simmering.
Add sugar, salt, and pepper; stir until sugar dissolves, then gently coat fried tilapia in the sauce and serve hot.

intro: Egg Pie is a creamy baked custard pie with its characteristic airy browned top.
steps: Line two 8-inch pie or quiche pans with pastry and refrigerate. Blind-bake first if using silicone or glass molds.
Separate 2 eggs, reserving their whites. Beat the whites to stiff peaks.
Microwave evaporated milk and water for 2½ minutes until hot.
Beat the remaining 3 whole eggs with 2 yolks, gradually adding sugar. Mix in hot milk and vanilla.
Fold in egg whites, leaving some foam intact, then divide filling between pastry-lined pans.
Bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, then 160°C for 30–40 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool before serving.

intro: Copycat Jollibee Garlic Pepper Beef is slow-braised beef ribs in a peppery gravy crowned with fried garlic.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kilograms beef ribs, cut into sections
steps: Season beef ribs generously with salt. Heat oil in a wok and sear ribs in batches until deeply browned on all sides.
Transfer ribs and their drippings to a pot. Add water, 3 tablespoons fried garlic, and 1 tablespoon black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours until tender; add water as needed.
Reduce liquid over higher heat if needed until about 3 cups remain.
Mix flour with 1/2 cup water, stir into the pot, and simmer on low 15 minutes until gravy-thick.
Stir in butter, adjust salt and pepper, then top generously with fried garlic.

intro: This Kimcheese Roast-style chicken is slowly roasted with gochujang, aromatic garlic, and warm nacho cheese sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 to 1 3/4 kg whole chicken thighs with legs
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rinse chicken and pat completely dry. Season with sea salt and pepper; rest 30 minutes.
Mix liquid smoke, gochujang, melted butter, minced garlic, and ginger. Massage into chicken, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Remove chicken from the refrigerator 1 hour before roasting.
Place pounded garlic and spring onions in a baking tray, set chicken on top, and roast at 135°C for 3 hours until cooked through.
Baste with drippings hourly for 2 hours, then every 15 minutes during the final hour.
Brush with combined lemon juice and honey, rest 10 minutes, then serve with warmed nacho cheese sauce.

intro: Beef Pochero is a comforting tomato-based stew with saba bananas, sweet potatoes, and greens.
ingredients: 1 kg stewing beef or 1 1/2 kg beef short ribs
1 can (400 g) chickpeas, drained, or 1 can (400 g) baked beans in tomato sauce
2 bunches bok choy or Chinese cabbage
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion. Add chorizo and cook for 2 minutes.
Add beef and brown the sides. Pour in stock, add enough water to barely cover meat, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 1 hour.
Add saba bananas, tomato paste, and sugar; simmer 15 minutes. Add sweet potatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
If using French beans, add them and simmer 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Stir in chickpeas or baked beans and bok choy, turn off heat, cover 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

intro: Buko Salad is a chilled, creamy fruit dessert packed with young coconut and Filipino pantry sweets.
ingredients: Young coconut meat from 5 coconuts, sliced into strips
1 cup condensed milk, adjusted to taste
1 cup thickened cream or whipped cream
steps: Drain the kaong, nata de coco, fruit cocktail, and pineapple thoroughly.
Combine young coconut, kaong, nata de coco, fruit cocktail, and pineapple in a large bowl.
Gently fold condensed milk into the thickened cream or whipped cream.
Fold cream mixture into the fruit mixture until evenly coated.
Chill for at least 6 hours before serving.

intro: Pinoy Style Baked Macaroni with White Sauce is a comforting meat-sauced pasta finished with creamy cheese sauce.
steps: Cook macaroni according to package directions, drain, and set aside. Heat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft. Brown ground beef and pork, then add red and green bell peppers.
Stir in Beef Cube, tomato sauce, and water. Cover and simmer over low-medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes; season with sugar, salt, and pepper.
Melt butter, stir in flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in milk and half the cheddar. Cook until thickened.
Toss macaroni with meat sauce and remaining cheese. Transfer to a baking dish, spread white sauce over top, and bake 15 to 20 minutes.

intro: Sweet Corn Ice Cream is a silky custard ice cream with the familiar sweetness of creamed corn.
steps: Combine cream, milk, sugar, and creamed corn in a saucepan. Heat slowly, stirring until sugar dissolves and the mixture is nearly boiling.
Whisk about 1 cup of hot cream mixture gradually into egg yolks.
Pour yolks back into the saucepan and cook while stirring until the custard coats the back of a spoon.
Cool in a heatproof container, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Churn in an ice-cream maker according to its instructions, about 30–35 minutes.
Serve soft or freeze at least 6 hours for a firmer texture.

intro: Kinamatisang Baboy is a homey tomato-pork stew finished with tender pechay.
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, cut into bite-sized pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Blanch pork in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Heat oil over medium heat; sauté garlic and onions until fragrant and translucent.
Add diced tomatoes and cook until softened and juicy.
Return pork, add enough water to cover, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low about 1 hour until tender.
Add pechay and simmer 2 minutes until wilted but bright. Season with fish sauce, salt, and pepper.
Serve hot, optionally garnished with cherry tomatoes.

intro: Vigan Empanada is a crisp orange rice-flour turnover filled with longaniza, green papaya, and egg.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Knead rice flour, water, 1/2 tsp salt, and annatto oil until smooth. Divide into six balls.
Sandwich one dough ball between two large squares of wax paper and press into a thin round.
Place one longaniza portion and grated green papaya in the center. Crack in one egg, add spring onion, season with salt and pepper, then fold and seal.
Deep-fry immediately in 160°C oil for about 4 minutes per side, until crisp. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

intro: Cebu-style Ngohiong wraps a fragrant pork, prawn, and vegetable filling in a crisp five-spice shell.
ingredients: 1/2 kg ubod, cut into small strips
1/4 cup singkamas (jicama), cut into small strips
steps: Sauté garlic and onion in a little oil. Add pork and cook until browned, then add prawns, spring onions, ubod, and singkamas.
Season filling with 3 tablespoons five-spice, salt, soy sauce, and black pepper. Drain in a colander, reserving liquid, and cool.
Mix 2 cups cornstarch, white pepper, and 1 1/2 cups water into a shallow batter. Wrap cooled filling in rehydrated rice paper or lumpia wrappers.
Dip rolls in batter and deep-fry at 180°C for 3–4 minutes until golden. Drain on a wire rack.
Combine reserved liquid, 1/3 cup water, 1 teaspoon cornstarch, soy sauce, brown sugar, five-spice, and salt; simmer 2 minutes until thick.
Stir in egg white to form fine strands, remove from heat, and serve sauce with Ngohiong.

intro: Arroz Palabok is creamy shrimp-and-tinapa rice porridge topped with classic palabok-style garnishes.
ingredients: 1/4 cup tinapa flakes, plus extra for topping
1/4 cup annatto oil, plus extra for topping
Patis and ground white pepper, to taste
steps: Boil shrimp in 2 cups water for 30 seconds. Remove shrimp and reserve the cooking water.
Heat annatto oil in a pot. Sauté garlic until starting to brown, then add onion and cook until soft.
Add rice and cook 30 seconds. Pour in shrimp water and remaining water, then bring to a boil.
Stir in the Knorr Shrimp Cube and tinapa flakes. Cook on low, stirring occasionally, until rice is soft and mushy.
Season with patis and white pepper. Serve with annatto oil, chicharon, shrimp, toasted garlic, tinapa flakes, and eggs.

intro: Giniling with Alugbati at Kalabasa is a simple pork and squash stew with tender leafy greens.
ingredients: 500 g buttercup squash, peeled and cubed
1 bunch Malabar spinach (alugbati) or large-leaf spinach
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until aromatic.
Add minced pork and cook until golden brown.
Add squash and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock, bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 10 minutes until squash is tender.
Add alugbati and cook 2 minutes; season with fish sauce and black pepper before serving.

intro: Nilaneg is a savory fish and pork liver stew with squash, eggplant, string beans, and bagoong.
ingredients: 1 kilogram fresh fish, cut into sections
1 bunch string beans, cut into 2-inch lengths
steps: Season fish and pork liver with salt, then broil or pan-fry in oil until lightly browned. Set aside.
Bring water and bagoong to a boil in a large saucepan.
Add buttercup squash, browned fish, and liver; cook about 3 minutes.
Add string beans and eggplant. Simmer 5 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and fish is cooked through.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

intro: Cathy’s Lechon Rice layers crackling pork belly over rice with bok choy in a savory thickened sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 pack baby bok choy, about 10 bunches
steps: Place pork belly, water, fish sauce, pepper, whole garlic, and white onion in a pot; boil, then simmer 1 hour.
Drain, reserving liquid. Pat pork dry skin-side up and refrigerate at least 12 hours until cold.
Deep-fry pork in hot oil over high heat until skin is golden and crisp. Drain, rest 5 minutes, then chop.
Sauté garlic and sliced onion in some frying oil. Add bok choy and carrot; stir-fry 1 minute.
Add 1 cup reserved stock, diluted if salty, and bring to a boil. Mix cornstarch with 1/4 cup stock, add, and simmer until thickened.
Season sauce with pepper. Plate cooked rice with vegetables and sauce, then top with crispy pork.

intro: Pholalo pairs fragrant pho-style broth with tender Bulalo beef and rice noodles.
ingredients: 2 1/2 kg beef shank with marrow bones
1 lemon or lime, cut into wedges
steps: Cover beef shanks with water; boil for 10 minutes. Drain, rinse the bones thoroughly, and return them to a clean large pot.
Char onion and ginger in a dry pan or over a flame until lightly blackened. Add them with spices and 3 to 3.5 litres water.
Bring to a gentle simmer; skim as needed and cook 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until beef is tender and marrow is soft.
Season broth with fish sauce, salt, and optional sugar. Cook noodles according to the package, then briefly rinse with cold water.
Divide noodles, beef, and marrow bones among bowls. Ladle over hot broth and finish with spring onions, herbs, citrus, and chili.

intro: Ginataang Mais at Monggo is a warm coconut dessert porridge with sweet corn and toasted mung beans.
steps: Bring coconut milk to a boil in a pot.
Stir in malagkit and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring every minute.
Add toasted mung beans and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add sweet corn and cook, stirring constantly, for 8–10 minutes.
Stir in sugar, vanilla, and optional salt. Continue cooking until mung beans are soft.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot.

intro: Aligue Pasta is fettuccine dressed in a luxurious taba ng talangka cream sauce with mixed seafood.
ingredients: 1 lb fettuccine, cooked according to package directions
1 lb mixed seafood, cleaned (shrimp, mussels, squid, and crab)
steps: Arrange cooked fettuccine on a serving platter.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add rice wine and cook for 1 minute. Stir in taba ng talangka and simmer for 2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, add cream, and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until lightly thickened.
Add mixed seafood and cook 2 minutes until just done. Pour over fettuccine, garnish with green onions, and serve.

intro: Spicy Sardinas with Patola and Miswa is a quick, comforting tomato-sardine noodle soup.
ingredients: 1 large can (15 oz) spicy sardines in tomato sauce
steps: Heat oil in a cooking pot and sauté onion until soft.
Add sardines with their tomato sauce, chili peppers, and garlic powder; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in water, stir, and bring to a boil.
Add miswa and patola; cook 3–5 minutes until noodles are tender and patola is soft.
Season with patis and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Crispy pork belly is served with a rich, spicy Bicol Express sauce.
ingredients: 1 (45 g) pack Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix
1 thumb-sized ginger, cut into thin strips
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a pot. Add pork belly and simmer for 30 minutes; remove and cool slightly.
Stir Ginataang Gulay Mix into the cooking liquid. Add onion, ginger, garlic, long peppers, Thai chilies, alamang, and pepper.
Boil the sauce, then cook 3 minutes after adding the chilies. Simmer until reduced by half; set aside.
Rub pork with salt and rest 10 minutes. Heat oil to 330°F and deep-fry pork for 8 minutes.
Rest pork 5 minutes, then fry again for 3 to 5 minutes until deeply crisp. Slice and spoon sauce over it.

intro: Soft Filipino cheese bread is coated in a buttery, sweet, cheesy crumble.
ingredients: 1/4 cup butter, room temperature and cubed
steps: Stir yeast, warm water, and 1 tbsp sugar; leave somewhere warm for 10 minutes until foamy.
Whisk melted butter, milk, egg, 3/4 cup sugar, and salt. Mix in the yeast mixture.
Gradually incorporate high-grade flour and potato flakes; knead 10 minutes until smooth. Cover in a greased bowl and let double, about 1 hour.
Combine cheddar, powdered milk, all-purpose flour, powdered sugar, and cubed butter until crumbly.
Divide dough into 3 logs, then cut each into 7 to 10 pieces. Shape into balls and press generously into the cheese coating.
Place on lined trays, rise 30 minutes until about 1 1/2 times larger, then bake at 150°C for 15 minutes until lightly golden.

intro: A light, savory Misua soup with pork, seafood, and tender vegetables.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until browned and crisp at the edges; add squid balls and fry until heated through.
Pour in chicken broth and add patola, if using; boil, then simmer for 4 minutes.
Add misua, shrimp, and cabbage; simmer for 2 minutes, until shrimp are opaque and vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve immediately.

intro: Tender okra and pork jowl simmer in a savory coconut milk sauce.
steps: Season pork jowl generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the pork on all sides.
Push pork aside; sauté garlic and onion until fragrant. Add water, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add coconut milk, bagoong, finger chilies, and okra. Bring to a boil, toss gently, then cover and cook on low for 8 minutes.
Adjust with salt and black pepper, garnish with red chilies, and serve hot.

intro: Chicken Bistek is a tangy, savory soy-citrus braised chicken dish with tender onion rings.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine soy sauce, lemon juice, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and crushed garlic; coat the chicken, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Drain the chicken well, reserving the marinade. Fry in 2 tablespoons oil over medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side; set aside.
Heat remaining oil and sauté minced garlic with half the onions over medium heat until softened.
Return chicken to the wok, cook 30 seconds, then add reserved marinade and water. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 35 minutes, adding water if needed. Add remaining onions and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in sugar; season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with the sauce and onions.

intro: A lighter, tomato-rich Chicken Menudo with tender chicken, vegetables, and hotdogs.
ingredients: 1 tbsp calamansi juice or lemon juice
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Marinate chicken with soy sauce and calamansi juice for 20–30 minutes.
Heat oil over medium heat; fry potato and carrot for 3–4 minutes until lightly browned. Remove, then brown hotdogs for 1–2 minutes; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté garlic until golden and onion until soft. Add chicken and cook 5–6 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in tomato paste for 1–2 minutes. Add water and bay leaves; boil, cover, and simmer 15–18 minutes until chicken is tender.
Blend in liver spread, then return potato, carrot, and hotdogs. Simmer 7–8 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Add bell peppers and cook 2–3 minutes. Adjust with optional sugar, salt, and pepper; serve hot with rice.

intro: This baked cassava cake has macapuno throughout and a golden coconut custard topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a baking tray.
Mix cassava, 1 1/2 cans coconut milk, evaporated milk, 1/2 can condensed milk, eggs, butter, cheese, and brown sugar until uniform.
Spread the mixture in the tray, scatter macapuno over the surface, and bake for 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk remaining coconut milk, condensed milk, flour, sugar, and yolks in a saucepan over low heat until thick.
Pour topping evenly over the cake. Bake at 220°C for 15 minutes, until the top is golden brown.

intro: Chicken Waray is deeply marinated in coconut, citrus, and aromatics before being grilled until browned.
steps: Process coconut milk, lemon juice, soy sauce, fish sauce, turmeric, lemongrass, shallots, garlic, and pepper into a coarse paste.
Coat chicken evenly with the paste in a sealed bag and refrigerate overnight.
Set chicken at room temperature for 1 hour. Reserve the marinade and arrange chicken on a wire rack over a baking tray.
Preheat the oven grill to 180°C. Grill 50–60 minutes, turning and basting with reserved marinade every 10 minutes.
Serve when the chicken is browned and thoroughly cooked through.

intro: This Filipino chicken curry is creamy, gently spiced, and packed with tender vegetables.
ingredients: 1 medium green bell pepper, cut into squares
1 fresh chili pepper, cut into 4-5 pieces, or dried chili flakes
steps: Heat oil and fry potato and carrot until cooked with lightly browned edges; transfer to a plate.
Sauté garlic and onion over medium heat until fragrant. Add chicken and sear both sides for 1 minute.
Add fish sauce, curry powder, optional paprika, and pepper. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to low; add coconut milk and simmer until chicken is fully cooked and sauce thickens.
Stir in potato, carrot, bell pepper, and chili. Cook 1 minute, then serve hot with rice.

intro: Rellenong Alimasag features crab shells filled with a savory crab, pork, and vegetable mixture.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and shallot until fragrant.
Add carrot and minced pork; stir-fry until the pork is lightly browned. Transfer the mixture to a bowl.
Mix crab meat, mashed potato, tomato, pork mixture, parsley, and eggs. Season with salt and black pepper.
Pack the filling firmly into the crab shells.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying to medium-high. Fry the stuffed crabs for 3 to 5 minutes, until browned and cooked through.

intro: Beef Short Rib Kare Kare is a rich peanut stew finished with crisp-tender vegetables and sautéed shrimp paste.
ingredients: 1 tbsp glutinous rice flour mixed with 1/4 cup water
steps: Heat oil in a pressure cooker over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant, then stir in ground peanuts for 3 minutes.
Add short ribs and cook until lightly browned. Pour in annatto water and water, then bring to a boil.
Lock the lid and pressure-cook for 30 minutes. Release pressure safely before opening.
Add banana blossom and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the glutinous rice flour slurry until the sauce thickens.
Add snake beans and baby bok choy; cook 5 minutes until tender. Serve with sautéed shrimp paste.

intro: This quick ginisa pairs sweet kalabasa, sitaw, malunggay, and tender shrimp in a light broth.
ingredients: 1 lb medium shrimp, heads and shells removed
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat and pan-fry shrimp for 1 minute per side. Transfer to a plate.
Sauté garlic and onion in the remaining oil until fragrant.
Stir-fry squash for 3 minutes, then add sitaw and cook 1 minute.
Add malunggay and chicken broth; bring to a boil, cover, and cook 5 to 8 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve the shrimp with the vegetables and broth.

intro: Manyaman Beef Asado is a deeply savory tomato-braised beef dish with potatoes and mushrooms.
ingredients: 1 kg marbled chuck steak, whole or in large pieces
steps: Season steak with salt and pepper. Grill over high heat for 4 minutes per side; rest 5 minutes, then cube, reserving juices.
Heat oil in a wok; sauté garlic and onion. Add tomato paste and cook over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add beef and juices, stock, tomatoes, soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, sugar, and star anise. Simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add mushrooms and cook 45 minutes, adding water if needed. Add potatoes and butter; cook 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Raise heat to reduce sauce until thick. Season, stir in lemon juice, and serve with rice.

intro: This rich Chicken and Pork Embutido is a festive steamed meatloaf with hotdog and egg centers.
ingredients: 3/4 cup breadcrumbs, plus more if needed
steps: Mix ground chicken and pork thoroughly in a large bowl.
Mix in relish, raisins, carrot, onion, and mayonnaise; add raw eggs, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Fold in breadcrumbs gradually, adding a little more only if the mixture remains too wet to shape.
Spread about 3/4 cup mixture over each 12-by-8-inch foil sheet; arrange hotdog and egg along the center, roll tightly, and twist the ends shut.
Steam the wrapped embutido over boiling water for 1 hour, until firm and cooked through.
Cool for 30 minutes, refrigerate for at least 3 hours, then unwrap and slice to serve.

intro: Caldo Puch is a hearty seafood-and-pork rice stew finished with crisp bacon.
steps: Boil clam and chicken stocks with clams until shells open. Strain through muslin, reserving liquid; remove clam meat, keeping a few shells for garnish.
Heat olive oil over low heat; cook bacon until crisp, then remove it. Sauté garlic and onion in the same pot until fragrant.
Raise heat to high and brown pork belly lightly on all sides.
Add reserved stock, rice, and tomatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring often so rice does not stick.
Add clam meat, chicken, squid, prawns, and peas; simmer 5 minutes until seafood is cooked. Season with salt and serve with bacon.

intro: Gule Magalang is a quick vegetable-and-seafood stew brightened with fried fish flakes.
ingredients: 1 bunch pea shoots or chayote tops
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add chayote, squash, fried fish flakes, and chicken stock; bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, until the squash begins to soften.
Add pea shoots or chayote tops, squash flowers, luffa, and prawns; simmer for 3 minutes until prawns are opaque.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve hot.

intro: Tinolang halaan is a light ginger-clam soup finished with spring onions.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion until aromatic.
Add clams and enough water to just cover them. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer.
When the shells open, add spring onions and simmer for 2 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Discard any unopened clams before serving.

intro: Cassava Suman with Macapuno is a softly sweet steamed cassava cake wrapped in banana leaves.
steps: Mix grated cassava, brown sugar, salt, macapuno, and coconut cream in a bowl until evenly combined.
Cut banana leaves into 30 x 15 cm pieces. Place 2 tablespoons filling along each long side, roll tightly, and fold both ends.
Arrange the parcels in a steamer over simmering water. Steam for 30 minutes, until the suman is firm.
Cool before unwrapping and serving.

intro: This quick Pork and Kangkong Guisado balances savory pork with tender water spinach.
ingredients: 1 bunch kangkong, leaves separated and stalks chopped
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook pork until browned on both sides and its fat has rendered.
Add garlic and stir for 20 seconds, then add onion and cook until soft.
Add kangkong stalks and cook 2 minutes. Stir in soy sauce and black pepper; cook 2 minutes.
Add kangkong leaves, cover for 1 minute, then stir in beef broth and bring to a boil.
Cook 1 minute, until the leaves are wilted but bright, then serve.

intro: Binukadkad na Isda is crisp whole fish, butterflied and deep-fried for sharing.
ingredients: 1 whole fish, such as snapper or tilapia
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Butterfly the fish, leaving the center bones intact, then season both sides with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C.
Fry the fish until deeply golden, crisp, and cooked through to the bone.
Drain briefly and serve hot with your preferred dip.

intro: Adobong Puti lets vinegar, garlic, and peppercorns shine in a rich chicken adobo.
steps: Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté onion and minced garlic until soft and aromatic.
Add chicken, optional fish sauce, and peppercorns. Cover and cook, turning once or twice, until edges are lightly browned.
Lower heat; add bay leaves and whole garlic. Pour in vinegar and simmer uncovered without stirring for 5 minutes.
Cover and cook 20 to 25 minutes, until chicken is tender. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Uncover and simmer over low heat 8 to 10 minutes, until reduced to a thick sauce. Serve with steamed rice.

intro: Saba con Yelo combines caramel-scented sweet saba, syrup, crushed ice, and evaporated milk.
steps: Cook 1 tbsp brown sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until melted and lightly caramelized, without burning it.
Add water and bring to a boil. Stir in remaining brown sugar, salt, and vanilla until dissolved, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add saba and cook 10 to 15 minutes until tender but still holding their shape.
Cool completely, preferably overnight. Fill glasses with crushed ice, spoon over saba and syrup, and drizzle with evaporated milk.

intro: Baked Macaroni layers pasta, a hearty Filipino-style meat sauce, creamy béchamel, and melted mozzarella.
ingredients: 2 cans (400 g each) Italian-style chopped tomatoes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan, stir in flour, then gradually whisk in milk; season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper and cook until smooth and thick.
Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a pan; sauté garlic and onion, then cook beef and pork until lightly browned.
Stir in tomatoes, stock, tomato paste, vinegar, sugar, basil, oregano, and cayenne; simmer 20 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Mix macaroni with meat sauce in a baking dish; spread béchamel over it and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes, then at 220°C for 7–10 minutes until bubbly and partly golden; cool briefly before serving.

intro: Pata Ken Pusi is a hearty pork hock stew with black-eyed peas, ampalaya, and greens.
ingredients: 1 1/2 kg pork hock (pata), cut into serving portions
1 cup dried black-eyed peas (pusi), soaked overnight
1 bunch spinach or bitter gourd shoots, trimmed
steps: Drain the overnight-soaked pusi. Soak ampalaya in salted water for 15 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Heat oil in a large pot; sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant. Sear pork hock until lightly browned.
Add fish sauce, soy sauce, and enough water to cover pork. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Add pusi and simmer 45 minutes, until beans are soft and broth thickens.
Add ampalaya for 5 minutes, then spinach or shoots just until wilted. Season with salt and pepper; serve with rice.

intro: Pinakupsan slowly renders pork belly until it fries crisp in its own fat.
steps: Place pork, salt, vinegar, black pepper, and water in a wok. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 20 minutes.
Uncover and cook until the water evaporates and pork fat begins to render, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Continue frying the pork in its rendered fat, stirring occasionally, until crisp and golden brown.
Lift pork out with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve.

intro: Sinabawang Tilapia is a bright, gingery fish soup with calamansi and sweet potato leaves.
ingredients: 1 kg tilapia, scaled, gutted, and cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub tilapia sections with salt and set aside.
Heat oil in a pot; sauté ginger, onion, garlic, and tomatoes for several minutes, gently crushing the tomatoes.
Add water and black pepper, cover, and bring to a boil.
Add green chilies and gently submerge tilapia. Cover and simmer 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Stir in calamansi juice and fish sauce. Add sweet potato leaves and cook 2 minutes before serving hot.

intro: Strawberry Taho pairs warm tofu jelly with ruby sago and a fresh strawberry syrup.
ingredients: White sugar, equal in volume to the sago pearls
2 teaspoons cornstarch, mixed with 1/4 cup water
steps: Combine strawberries, 1/2 cup sugar, lemon juice, and 1/2 cup water in a saucepan; boil over medium heat, then simmer 15 minutes until very soft.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer on low for 5 minutes, until the syrup thickens; set aside.
Cook sago according to the package directions, adding equal parts sugar and sago plus several drops of red food coloring; cool slightly.
Portion tofu jelly into heatproof mugs, cover to keep out condensation, and steam for 15 minutes until hot.
Top warm tofu with strawberry syrup and sago pearls, then serve immediately.

intro: Habichuelas is a hearty pork, chorizo, and white bean stew with a naturally thickened broth.
ingredients: 4 cans (400 g each) white beans, drained
500 g pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until softened. Add pork and brown on all sides.
Add chorizo and cook for 1 minute. Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Pour in water and pork stock. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Mash the beans from one can into the stew and cook for 5 minutes until thickened.
Add remaining beans, bring back to a boil, season with fish sauce and pepper, then simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.

intro: Adobong Manok sa Buko balances classic adobo flavors with lightly sweet buko juice.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Combine chicken, soy sauce, and vinegar; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until the onion softens, then brown the marinated chicken.
Add remaining marinade, peppercorns, bay leaves, and buko juice. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the Chicken Cube, reduce to low-medium heat, and simmer for 30 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Add green onion and cook for 3 minutes. Serve with the braising sauce.

intro: Pancit Sotanghon na May Hipon is a savory shrimp noodle dish with cabbage and Chinese sausage.
steps: Soak sotanghon in water for 5 minutes, no longer than 8 minutes, until manageable; drain.
Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté garlic until light brown, then cook onion until soft.
Add Chinese sausage, parsley, and paprika; sauté for 30–60 seconds. Add water and fish sauce and bring to a boil.
Stir in the Shrimp Cube, cover, and cook 5 minutes. Add pepper, shrimp, carrot, and cabbage; cook 3 minutes.
Add sotanghon, stir gently, cover, and cook 3–5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Toss in scallions and serve.

intro: Ginataang Baka braises beef in spicy coconut milk with crisp green beans and spinach.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups long green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add beef and sauté until lightly browned. Pour in coconut milk and water, then stir well.
Cover and cook over low to medium heat for 1 hour. Add chili peppers and continue cooking 30 to 60 minutes, until beef is tender.
Add green beans, cover, and cook 3 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Add spinach and cook 1 minute, just until wilted. Serve immediately.

intro: Leftover pork roast becomes a comforting, creamy mushroom-gravy dinner.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a heavy pan over medium heat and sauté onion until soft.
Add mushrooms and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in gravy, cream of mushroom soup, and sliced pork. Bring to a boil, then simmer 5 to 10 minutes until hot throughout.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper, then serve.

intro: Pork belly asado is braised until tender in a sweet, savory, star-anise sauce.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine pork, banana ketchup, soy sauce, and garlic. Cover and marinate overnight.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté onion until soft. Add pork with its marinade and brown lightly.
Add water, Pork Cube, and star anise. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until tender.
Stir in brown sugar and butter. Mix cornstarch with 1/4 cup water, add it, and cook until thickened.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve with rice.

intro: Taco Pao fills soft bao with tender five-spice pork, crunchy cabbage, and tangy pickled daikon.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons cornstarch, dissolved in 1/3 cup water
1 cup water, plus more as needed
Taco-shaped steamed buns (bao or gwa pao)
steps: Sauté garlic in oil, add pork, and stir-fry for 3 minutes. Add 1 cup water, soy sauce, brown sugar, and five-spice; simmer gently for 2 hours until pull-apart tender.
Stir occasionally and add water if needed; mix in hoisin and cornstarch slurry, simmer until thick, then season with salt.
Toss daikon with 1 tablespoon salt and rest 1 hour; rinse thoroughly, squeeze dry, and combine with ginger.
Boil vinegar, 1/2 cup water, sugar, and 1 teaspoon salt for 5 minutes without stirring; pour over daikon, cover, and refrigerate for 2 days.
Steam bao according to package directions; fill with pork, cabbage, pickled daikon, chilies, and mayonnaise.

intro: Kaleskes is an annatto-colored offal stew with a bright cane-vinegar broth.
ingredients: 500 g beef or carabao intestines, thoroughly cleaned, parboiled, and cut into bite-sized pieces
500 g beef or carabao tripe, thoroughly cleaned, parboiled, and cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add intestines, tripe, and annatto powder. Stir-fry over high heat for 5 minutes.
Pour in cane vinegar and boil for 2 minutes.
Add beef stock and green finger chilies. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes or until tender.
Season with sea salt and black pepper, stir in spring onions, and serve.

intro: Tapsilog pairs garlicky fried rice with crisp-edged marinated beef tapa.
ingredients: 800 g beef tenderloin, sliced 1/2 cm thick
2 whole garlic bulbs, crushed with skins on
steps: Mix crushed garlic, black pepper, vinegar, bay leaves, and salt. Cut beef into 2 x 3-inch pieces, coat, and marinate for at least 1 day.
Fry minced garlic in oil over medium heat until golden and crisp. Add rice and stir-fry for about 10 minutes; season with salt and pepper.
Drain the beef and pat dry. Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry beef until crisp outside and browned on both sides, then serve alongside the garlic rice.

intro: Garlic Butter Shrimp Pancit Canton combines buttery shrimp with saucy noodles and crisp cabbage.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter with oil in a wok over medium heat. Stir-fry garlic until light brown.
Cook shrimp for 1 minute per side. Squeeze over lemon, cover, and cook 1 minute; season with salt and remove shrimp.
Let the remaining juices evaporate until only butter and oil remain. Sauté onion until soft.
Add soy sauce and water; bring to a boil. Stir in the Shrimp Cube and cabbage, then cook 30 seconds.
Add pancit canton and toss until it absorbs the liquid. Toss in oyster sauce, green onion, and pepper.
Plate noodles and top with shrimp and fried egg.

intro: Tokwa and Tuna combines grilled ahi and crisp tofu in a bright vinegar dressing.
ingredients: 3/4 cup apple cider or cane vinegar
steps: Combine vinegar, soy sauce, and sugar; microwave 15 seconds and stir until dissolved. Set aside.
Season tuna with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon pepper; rest 15 minutes.
Grill tuna for 3 to 5 minutes per side, then cut into cubes.
Heat oil in a deep pot. Fry tofu, two pieces at a time, until golden; drain and cube.
Gently toss tuna, tofu, onion, and chilies with dressing. Transfer to a serving dish.

intro: Masikoy is a chewy coconut rice cake served in a warm pandan coconut sauce.
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour, water, coconut strips, and ground sesame seeds into a workable dough.
Pinch off small portions and flatten each into an oblong disc.
Combine coconut milk, brown sugar, and pandan leaves in a wok; bring slowly to a boil.
Gently add the rice cakes and cook until they float. Spoon cakes and sauce into serving bowls.

intro: Tinapa fried rice turns leftover rice into a smoky breakfast or easy meal.
steps: Toss leftover rice with salt and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook garlic until lightly browned, then add tinapa flakes and cook 3 minutes.
Add rice and stir-fry 2 to 5 minutes until evenly combined and heated through.
Add black pepper and green onions; stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes more.
Plate the rice and top with sliced salted duck eggs and cubed tomatoes.

intro: Tapa frita is a hearty pork, vegetable, and cheese stew in tomato sauce.
ingredients: 800 g pork scotch, cut into long thin strips
1 large potato, cut into long thin strips
1 large carrot, cut into long thin strips
1/2 cup grated processed cheese, plus more for topping
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until softened, then brown pork on all sides.
Add chicken stock and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in potato, carrot, tomatoes, pickle relish, 1/2 cup cheese, basil, and tomato paste. Simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add green peas and simmer 5 minutes more, until vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Top with additional grated cheese and serve.

intro: Ginisang Repolyo with Egg is a savory cabbage stir-fry finished with fluffy scrambled egg.
steps: Toss cabbage with salt and rest 10 minutes. Rinse well and drain.
Beat eggs with a little salt and pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons oil, cook eggs until firm, break into small pieces, and set aside.
Heat remaining oil over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant and the onion softens.
Add optional carrots and sauté 30 seconds. Add cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, optional sesame oil, and optional sugar; cook 1 minute.
Return egg, add green onions, season with pepper, and toss just until combined.

intro: Sarciadong Pechay at Itlog is a comforting tomato-based pechay dish with both poached and boiled eggs.
steps: Boil 12 eggs for 10–12 minutes until firm; peel and set aside. Beat the remaining 3 eggs.
Heat oil over medium heat; sauté onion for 1 minute, then garlic for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft; stir in fish sauce and black pepper.
Add water, bring to a boil, and cook for 1–2 minutes. Slowly stream in beaten eggs, let them set briefly, then stir gently.
Add pechay and cook 1–2 minutes. Season with Maggi Magic Sarap, add boiled eggs, and cook 1 minute more.
Transfer to a bowl and serve with rice.

intro: Pinaputok na Isda is charcoal-grilled fish stuffed with a fresh tomato and ginger filling.
ingredients: 1 medium tilapia, black snapper, or other grilling fish, scaled
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Score the fish 3 to 4 times on each side. Season the cavity, exterior, and cuts with salt and pepper; rest 15 minutes.
Mix tomato, onion, ginger, juice of 1/2 lemon, salt, and pepper. Pack the mixture into the fish cavity.
Rub fish with oil and grill over charcoal, turning as needed, until cooked through and lightly charred on both sides.
Mix soy sauce with remaining lemon juice for dipping. Serve the grilled fish with the dip.

intro: Sinabawang Manok is a clean, ginger-scented chicken soup with chayote, beans, and spinach.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add chicken wings and sauté for 3 minutes, until their exterior begins to brown.
Pour in water, cover, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the Maggi Magic Chicken Cube and chayote; cook 4 minutes.
Add long green beans, fish sauce, and pepper; cook 5 minutes. Stir in spinach and cook 1 minute before serving.

intro: Filipino Fruit Salad is a creamy, chilled mix of fruit, nata de coco, and sweet corn.
ingredients: 2 cans fruit cocktail (800 g each), drained
1 can lychees (560 g), drained and quartered
steps: Drain the fruit cocktail, lychees, and nata de coco thoroughly in a colander.
Whisk condensed milk and thickened cream together until smooth.
Combine drained fruit, quartered lychees, nata de coco, apples, and corn in a large bowl.
Fold in the milk mixture until every piece is coated; garnish with maraschino cherries if using.
Freeze for 2 hours before serving.

intro: Pork Chop Suey is a hearty stir-fry of tender pork and vegetables in a light savory sauce.
ingredients: 1 medium carrot, peeled and sliced crosswise
1 small bell pepper, sliced into strips
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Sauté onion for 1 minute, then garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir-fry pork 5–7 minutes until lightly browned and no longer pink.
Add optional soy sauce and carrot; cook 3 minutes. Add bell pepper and cabbage and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium, cover, and cook 5–8 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Dissolve cornstarch in broth. Stir it into the wok with parsley and cook 1–2 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve warm.

intro: Pinamalhan na bangus is tangy milkfish braised with vinegar, ginger, and aromatics.
ingredients: 2 milkfish, cleaned and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
steps: Layer garlic, shallots, and ginger in a pot. Arrange milkfish over them, then add green chilies.
Pour in cane vinegar and soy sauce. Scatter black peppercorns and season with salt.
Cover and bring to a rapid boil over high heat. Lower to medium-high and cook about 15 minutes, until nearly dry but saucy.
Drizzle olive oil over the fish and serve.

intro: Ginataang Santol, or Sinantolan, is a rich coconut dish balanced by savory shrimp paste and chilies.
ingredients: 2 long green peppers (siling pansigang), sliced crosswise
steps: Finely mince santol in a food processor or by hand. Wrap in cheesecloth and squeeze out the liquid.
Heat oil in a pan; sauté garlic and onion until translucent. Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
Add squeezed santol and cook 3 to 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut cream; bring to a boil, stir, cover, and cook over medium heat until reduced by half.
Stir in shrimp paste, siling pansigang, and siling labuyo. Cook until the liquid evaporates, then serve.

intro: Magic Water is a chilled banana-flavored drink with clear gulaman cubes and plenty of ice.
steps: Sprinkle gelatin over 1/2 cup cold water and let soften for 5 minutes.
Heat 1/2 cup water with 2 tbsp sugar over medium heat. Stir in softened gelatin until dissolved, pour into a container, and chill until set.
Cut the set gulaman into small cubes.
Bring the remaining 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup water to a boil, then reduce heat until dissolved. Cool completely.
Combine mineral water, cooled syrup, and banana extract in a pitcher. Stir in gulaman and lots of ice, then serve.

intro: Lengua Con Setas is tender ox tongue in a glossy mushroom sauce with savory pantry seasonings.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
steps: Boil ox tongue in about 1 quart water for 90 minutes, or until tender. Cool, remove the skin, and slice into serving pieces.
Heat oil over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add tongue and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and Worcestershire sauce; simmer for 1 minute.
Add mushrooms and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the liquid reduces; season with salt and pepper.
Stir in cornstarch slurry and cook until thick. Transfer to a platter and sprinkle with parsley.

intro: Spicy Pork Ribs Adobo reduces pork ribs in a fiery, sweet-sour soy and vinegar sauce.
ingredients: 1 cup water, plus more as needed
steps: Toss pork ribs with salt and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat; stir-fry ribs for about 3 minutes until browned at the edges, then cook garlic for 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, oyster sauce, lemon-lime soda, water, peppercorns, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until ribs are tender, adding a little water if the pan dries out.
Add chili flakes and cook uncovered until the sauce reduces and clings to the ribs.
Toss in Thai chilies until evenly distributed, then serve warm with steamed rice.

intro: Creamy Lengua turns tender pork tongue into a rich, corn-studded skillet dish.
ingredients: 1 can (15.25 oz) whole kernel corn, drained
steps: Pressure-cook pork tongue with 1 tablespoon salt and enough water to cover for 25–30 minutes.
Cool slightly, reserve 1 cup broth, peel away the outer skin, and slice tongue about 1/4 inch thick.
Melt butter over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until tender and fragrant.
Add tongue and soy sauce; cook 2–3 minutes, turning slices once or twice.
Add evaporated milk, reserved broth, corn, salt, and pepper. Simmer 5–7 minutes until beginning to thicken.
Stir in all-purpose cream and simmer 1 minute. Adjust seasoning and serve with rice or mashed potatoes.

intro: Ginataang kalabasa at pechay pairs pork, squash, and greens in coconut milk.
ingredients: 400 g pork belly, cut into small cubes
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Cook pork belly until browned and lightly crisp.
Add garlic, onion, and finger chilies; sauté for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add squash and stir-fry a few minutes, until its edges begin to color.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes until squash is tender.
Stir in bagoong monamon and pechay. Simmer 2 minutes until wilted, season with black pepper, and serve with rice.

intro: Sabo Kamatis is a tomato-rich beef rib soup with daikon and leafy vegetables.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot over high heat. Brown beef ribs on all sides, then transfer them out.
Reduce to medium heat; sauté garlic and onions for 1 minute. Add tomato paste for 30 seconds, then tomatoes until softened, about 3 minutes.
Return beef, add fish sauce and water, and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer on low 1 1/2 hours until ribs are tender.
Add green chilies and daikon; cover and simmer 5 minutes. Add cabbage and bok choy, cover, and cook 3 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Tinolang Manok sa Gata is a comforting chicken soup enriched with coconut milk, papaya, and spinach.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken, cut into serving pieces
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until golden brown. Pour in chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes. Add green papaya and cook until tender.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 to 10 minutes.
Add spinach and cook until wilted. Season with fish sauce, salt, and pepper, then simmer briefly before serving.

intro: Pastimallows are festive marshmallows wrapped in colorful pastillas and rolled in sugar.
steps: Mix powdered milk, condensed milk, and melted butter until smooth. Divide the mixture equally between two bowls.
Mix red coloring into one portion and green coloring into the other.
Scoop 1 tablespoon of colored mixture, roll into a ball, then flatten it into a wrapper.
Enclose one marshmallow, roll in sugar, and place in a small cupcake liner. Repeat with both mixtures and all marshmallows.

intro: Caramelized Patis Wings are sticky, sweet-salty chicken wings with lemon, garlic, and chili.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Raise heat to high, add chicken wings, and stir-fry continuously until browned on all sides.
Add fish sauce, honey, water, lemon juice, and chilies. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and raise heat to high. Reduce the sauce, stirring occasionally, until thick and coating the wings.
Season with black pepper and salt if needed. Garnish with coriander and serve.

intro: This homemade Puto Bumbong uses soaked glutinous rice, coconut, sugar, and margarine for a classic holiday treat.
steps: Combine both rices, cover fully with water, and soak in a cool place for 24 hours.
Drain thoroughly. Pulse in a processor with a little water until gritty and moist like fine wet sand.
Spread loosely in a lightly greased shallow tray no deeper than 2 cm; do not compact. Steam over high heat for 20 minutes until tender.
Slice and shape into small cylinders. Serve on banana leaf with margarine, grated coconut, and muscovado or palm sugar.

intro: Tangigue steaks are pan-fried and gently finished in a lemon-garlic butter sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg Spanish mackerel, cut into thick steaks
steps: Season Spanish mackerel steaks generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 1/4 cup olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry fish until golden and cooked through; remove.
Melt butter with remaining olive oil in another skillet over medium heat. Sauté garlic for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Return fish to the skillet, pour over lemon juice, and arrange lemon slices on top. Adjust seasoning.
Cover and cook 2 minutes. Transfer to a platter, garnish with spring onions, and serve hot.

intro: Chicken Adobo sa Gata combines deeply savory adobo chicken with creamy coconut sauce and chilies.
ingredients: 3/4 cup coconut vinegar or cane vinegar
steps: Sauté garlic in oil over low heat until golden. Remove and reserve for topping.
Fry chicken in the same pot until browned. Add water, vinegar, soy sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves, and sugar.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 25 minutes. Drain the chicken, reserving the cooking liquid.
Fry drained chicken in oil over high heat until browned on the sides.
Mix coconut milk with reserved liquid and pour into the pan. Add chilies, simmer 5 minutes, and top with fried garlic.

intro: Tofu Balls with Miswa and Patola is a satisfying shrimp-seasoned noodle soup with crisp-edged tofu dumplings.
ingredients: Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Press tofu dry and mash it with egg, carrot, minced green onion, minced onion, flour, salt, and pepper; shape into balls.
Heat the oil and fry tofu balls until medium brown outside; drain and set aside.
Heat 3 tablespoons frying oil in a pot; sauté garlic until browning, then cook onion until soft.
Add water and bring to a boil. Add Knorr Shrimp Cube and tofu balls; cook 3–5 minutes.
Add patola and cook 5 minutes until tender. Stir in misua and season with fish sauce and pepper.
Serve topped with chopped green onions.

intro: Pamplina is a comforting pork leg and white bean stew enriched with chorizo and vegetables.
ingredients: 1.5 kg pork leg (pata), cut into sections
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil pork leg in water for 10 minutes. Drain and rinse well.
Heat olive oil in a clean pot. Sauté garlic and onions, then brown pork lightly on all sides.
Add tomatoes and cook 2 minutes. Add soaked white beans and bay leaves, cover with water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer gently over low heat for 1 hour. Meanwhile, pan-fry chorizo in a little olive oil until fragrant.
Add chorizo and its oil, potatoes, fish sauce, and pepper. Simmer 40 minutes until pork, beans, and potatoes are tender.
Add cabbage and simmer 5 minutes. Serve hot.

intro: Pancit Palabok features rice noodles under a richly flavored crab, shrimp, and smoked-fish sauce.
ingredients: 500 g thin rice noodles or bihon
steps: Cook noodles according to package directions; drain and set aside. Boil shrimps in 3 cups water, reserving broth and seafood.
Shell shrimp. Pound shells, strain with the reserved broth, then blend broth with crab meat, crab fat, annatto, and fish sauce.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil. Add pork for 3 minutes, then stir in crab mixture and smoked fish.
Whisk cornstarch with a little water; add to sauce. Boil and simmer until thickened, loosening with water if necessary.
Top noodles with sauce, shrimp, chicharon, spring onions, eggs, and fried garlic. Add lemon before serving.

intro: Gisadong Munggo with Chicharon is a thick, savory mung bean stew with crunchy pork rind.
ingredients: 200 g chicharon, plus more for garnish
steps: Sauté minced garlic in oil over medium heat until golden. Remove and reserve the crisp garlic.
Add mung beans, chicharon, and stock to the pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer 45 to 60 minutes until beans are very soft.
Stir in spinach and reserved garlic. Season with fish sauce and pepper, cooking only until spinach wilts.
Serve hot and garnish with extra chicharon.

intro: Toasted Siopao has soft baked buns filled with savory chicken, Hoisin sauce, and egg.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh fillet, finely diced
3 tbsp oil, plus more for coating
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil over medium heat; brown chicken, then sauté garlic and onion. Add soy sauce, brown sugar, bay leaves, and 2 cups water; simmer 20 to 30 minutes until tender.
When sauce is reduced, stir in Hoisin and pepper. Mix cornstarch with 1/2 cup water, add, and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until thick.
Dissolve sugar in lukewarm milk and water. Stir in yeast and 3 tbsp oil, then mix in flour and baking powder. Knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Oil dough, cover, and rise 30 to 60 minutes until nearly doubled. Divide into 12 balls, rest 3 to 5 minutes, then roll each with thinner edges.
Fill each round with 1 tbsp chicken filling and an egg quarter. Seal, arrange on a baking sheet, cover, and rise 20 to 30 minutes.
Bake at 170°C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden. Cool briefly on a rack and serve warm.

intro: Ginisang Upo with Ground Pork and Shrimp is a quick, clean-tasting squash sauté for everyday rice meals.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic until light brown.
Add onion and tomato; cook until softened.
Add ground pork and cook until lightly browned, then add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes.
Add upo and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in water, cover, and cook over low to medium heat for 7 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, black pepper, and parsley if using; serve hot.

intro: Creamy chicken pastel is a rich, savory chicken stew with chorizo, vegetables, and cream.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine chicken, soy sauce, and lime juice. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until soft, then sauté Chorizo de Bilbao for 1 minute.
Add chicken and sauté until light brown. Add water and Chicken Cube, bring to a boil, cover, and cook 20 minutes.
Add hotdogs and cook over medium heat until the liquid is reduced by half.
Add potato, carrot, and cream. Cover and cook 8 minutes, then add mushrooms and bell peppers for 3 minutes. Season and serve with rice.

intro: Chicken Dynamite Lumpia wraps mild long green peppers in crisp, chicken-filled lumpia.
ingredients: 10 long green peppers (siling pansigang or finger peppers)
steps: Mix chicken, garlic powder, onion powder, 1 egg, bread crumbs, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Place one pepper on each wrapper, cover with 1 to 2 tbsp chicken mixture, and roll tightly, leaving the stem end visible.
Heat oil to about 250°F. Beat the remaining egg, dip each lumpia in it, then coat completely with Panko.
Fry over low-medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden brown and chicken is cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve.

intro: Sayote Guisado with Chicken and Shrimp is a light, brothy sauté with tender chayote.
ingredients: 6 oz boneless chicken breast, thinly sliced
8–10 medium shrimp, deveined, peeled, and heads removed
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until the onion is soft.
Add chicken and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in 1 cup chicken broth, cover, bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes.
When the broth has reduced by more than half, add sayote and cook 2 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook 1 minute. Add remaining broth, boil, and cook 1–2 minutes until shrimp are opaque.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve.

intro: Spicy Monggo with Tinapa is a smoky, chili-laced mung bean stew finished with ampalaya leaves.
steps: Heat oil in a pot. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add tinapa flakes and cook 1 minute. Add Thai chilies and monggo; cook 2 minutes.
Pour in water and bring to a boil. Add the Knorr Shrimp Cube, cover, and cook over medium heat until monggo is soft.
Add water as needed, then stir in ampalaya leaves, fish sauce, and pepper. Cook 3 to 5 minutes and serve with rice.

intro: Ginataang Langka is a creamy coconut braise of young jackfruit, pork belly, and optional shrimp.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat; sauté garlic, onion, finger chilies, and ginger until fragrant.
