Add pork belly and stir-fry until browned on all sides.
Pour in 2 cups coconut milk, bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add young jackfruit and simmer for 20 minutes, until tender and most liquid has reduced.
Add remaining coconut milk and shrimp, if using; simmer 5 minutes until shrimp are opaque.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Pork dinuguan sa gata is a creamy, tangy pork-and-blood stew with green chilies.
ingredients: 1 (40 g) pack Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté garlic and onion until soft, then add pork and cook until light brown.
Stir in black pepper and 1 1/2 cups water. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low-medium heat for 20 minutes.
Add vinegar and let it return to a boil before stirring. Continue cooking until pork is tender.
Gradually stir in pork blood and cook 12 minutes. Season with salt if needed.
Dissolve Ginataang Gulay Mix in 3/4 cup lukewarm water. Add it with long green peppers and cook 8 to 10 minutes, then 2 minutes more.

intro: Crispy Tofu Squares are panko-crusted tofu bites served with a bright, savory creamy sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
4 tbsp liver spread, optional for a vegetarian version
4 tsp liquid seasoning, such as Knorr or Maggi
steps: Cut tofu into bite-sized cubes and pat very dry. Combine flour, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Set out flour mixture, beaten eggs, and panko. Coat each tofu cube in flour, egg, then panko.
Deep-fry in batches until golden, about 4 minutes. Drain briefly, then refry at higher heat for 30 seconds.
Mix mayonnaise, liver spread, liquid seasoning, and lemon juice until smooth.
Drizzle sauce over hot tofu, garnish with spring onion, and serve immediately.

intro: This creamy tuna macaroni salad is an easy chilled Filipino party side.
steps: Bring 10 cups water to a boil in a pot.
Add macaroni and return to a boil. Cook over medium heat for 7 minutes, stirring gently once each minute.
Drain macaroni and let it cool.
Combine macaroni, Lady's Choice Mayonnaise, tuna, onion, celery, relish, cheddar, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Toss until evenly coated, cover, and refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.

intro: Dulong Fishcake makes delicate silver fish into crisp, lemony pan-fried patties.
steps: Mix dulong with 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, egg, mayonnaise, lemon juice, garlic, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
Shape into patties and coat with the remaining 1/4 cup breadcrumbs.
Melt butter in a pan over medium heat and add olive oil.
Pan-fry patties for 5–6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Serve warm with chips or salad and ranch dressing, if desired.

intro: This rich beef adobo pairs melting cheeks and tendons with crisp fried pearl potatoes.
ingredients: 350 g beef tendons, cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Simmer beef tendons in beef stock over low heat for 1 hour. Boil potatoes 15 minutes, drain and cool, then pan-fry until lightly browned.
Heat oil in a large pan and brown beef cheeks. Push aside, sauté garlic over low heat until golden, then remove pan from heat.
Put tendons with their stock, beef cheeks and oil, garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pressure cooker.
Pressure-cook for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is very tender.
Transfer everything to a wok over highest heat and rapidly boil until the sauce reduces.
Mix 1 tsp cornstarch with 2 tbsp water; add with potatoes and cook until sauce thickens. Balance soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar before serving.

intro: Tochong Bangus is fried milkfish and tofu simmered in a savory tahure and tausi tomato sauce.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Rub bangus with salt and rest 10 minutes. Heat oil and fry both sides until light to medium brown; set aside.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a clean pan. Sauté garlic, onion, ginger, and tomatoes until onion softens.
Add vinegar, tahure, and tausi; cook 30 seconds. Add water, bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat for 3 minutes.
Add fried bangus and tofu, cover, and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, adding water if needed.
Season with salt, pepper, and optional sugar. Serve warm with rice.

intro: Sweet Pata Asado is tender pork hock braised with star anise in a lightly sweet, thick sauce.
ingredients: Salt and ground white pepper, to taste
steps: Cover pata with water in a pot, boil for 15 minutes while skimming impurities, then discard water. Cool, rinse, and set aside.
Heat oil over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until softened, then add pata and sauté for 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, water, and star anise; bring to a boil. Stir in the Pork Cube, cover, and simmer on low-medium until tender.
Stir occasionally and add water as needed. Add brown sugar and cook for 3 minutes; season with salt and white pepper.
Mix cornstarch with 3 tablespoons water, stir into the pot, and cook until sauce thickens. Serve hot.

intro: This frozen buko pandan dessert blends young coconut, nata de coco, and pandan jelly.
ingredients: 25 g green pandan gulaman powder, prepared according to package instructions
350 g green nata de coco, drained
steps: Cut prepared pandan gulaman into small cubes and set aside.
Churn young coconut and chilled fresh cream in an ice cream maker until slightly thickened.
Add nata de coco and pandan jelly; continue churning while slowly pouring in condensed milk.
Transfer to a covered container and freeze overnight before serving.

intro: Hotdog and Corned Beef Sopas is a creamy, filling macaroni soup for sharing.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt butter in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add corned beef and hotdogs; cook for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock and bring to a boil. Stir in macaroni and simmer 10 minutes.
Add carrot and simmer 5 minutes until pasta and carrot are tender.
Stir in evaporated milk, simmer 2 minutes, then season with salt and black pepper.

intro: Ginataang Mackerel Okra is a fast coconut-milk stew with tender okra and savory canned fish.
ingredients: 1 can mackerel in oil (425 g), including contents
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat; sauté garlic and onion until soft and fragrant.
Add canned mackerel with all its oil and sauce; gently break into large pieces and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Add okra and cook for 2 minutes, until it starts to soften.
Add coconut milk and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes, until okra is tender and sauce slightly thickens.
Add green chilies, simmer 1 minute, season with salt and pepper, and serve with rice.

intro: Pancit Bato Mami is a simple pork noodle soup with crisp vegetables in a clear broth.
steps: Heat oil in a soup pot over medium-high heat. Sauté pork 3–4 minutes until light to medium brown.
Add chicken broth and water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer 20 minutes until pork is tender.
Add snap peas and carrot; cook 2 minutes.
Add cabbage and Pancit Bato. Stir and cook 3 minutes until noodles soften.
Season with salt and pepper, adding more broth or water if needed, then serve.

intro: Aligue Fried Rice turns leftover rice into a buttery seafood dish with taba ng talangka.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons oil. Cook shrimp and mussels 1 minute; add 1 1/2 tablespoons butter, then squid for 30 seconds. Season and reserve seafood with pan liquid.
Heat remaining oil in the same pan. Sauté garlic until browning, then add onion and cook until soft.
Add remaining butter and rice. Stir-fry 2 minutes, breaking apart clumps.
Fold in taba ng talangka until evenly distributed. Add lemon juice and reserved seafood liquid; stir-fry over high heat 1 to 2 minutes.
Season to taste, plate the rice, and top with the cooked seafood.

intro: Steamed pork siomai is paired with silky Nido Oriental Style Soup.
ingredients: 1 (40 g) pack Knorr Real Chinese Soup, Nido Oriental Style
steps: Mix pork, onion, carrot, scallions, 1 egg, sesame oil, pepper, and crushed Pork Cube until evenly combined.
Place about 2 tablespoons filling in each wrapper, fold up the sides, press the top lightly, and arrange in a steamer.
Bring 6 cups water to a boil and steam siomai for 20 to 25 minutes, until the centers are fully cooked.
Whisk Nido Oriental Style Soup mix with 3 cups water in a soup pot. Cook, stirring every minute, until boiling and thickened.
Stir in the remaining egg and cook 1 to 2 minutes. Serve soup with siomai and chili garlic sauce.

intro: Sarah’s Creamy Chicken Macaroni Soup is a rich sopas with chicken, sausage, vegetables, and cheese.
ingredients: 1 small can Vienna sausage, drained and sliced
1 small carrot, peeled and cut into strips
1 cup green cabbage, sliced or roughly shredded
Salt, pepper, or patis, to taste
steps: Boil chicken breasts in 4 cups water until cooked through. Remove chicken, reserve broth, and add water to make 10 cups; shred the meat.
Cook macaroni in salted water until al dente, then drain.
Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion. Add butter, chicken, Vienna sausage, cheddar, carrot, peas, kosher salt, sugar, pepper, and patis; stir well.
Pour in 10 cups broth and bring to a boil. Add evaporated milk, stirring until the soup returns to a boil.
Add cabbage and macaroni. Adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or patis, then serve hot topped with fried garlic.

intro: Chicken Pakam is a tangy tomato-braised chicken dish with ginger, shallots, and coriander.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
steps: Combine chicken, vinegar, bay leaves, and pepper in a wok. Bring to a boil over high heat, turning chicken once, until vinegar nearly evaporates.
Add oil before the liquid fully dries. Fry chicken until lightly browned on each side, then set aside.
Over medium heat, sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger in the same wok until aromatic. Add tomatoes and cook until shallots soften.
Add water and bring to a boil. Return chicken, cover, and cook over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes.
Cook until chicken is done and liquid reduces by half. Season with fish sauce, garnish with coriander, and serve.

intro: Kadyos, Baboy at Langka is a smoky, sour pork soup packed with pigeon peas and young jackfruit.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups pigeon peas or black beans
1 bunch spinach, water spinach, or sweet potato tops
Fish sauce or sea salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: If using dried pigeon peas or black beans, soak them overnight. Grill pork leg over charcoal until lightly charred on all sides.
Place pork, water, batuan or tamarind, lemongrass, and onion in a pot; bring to a boil and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add pigeon peas or beans and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add young jackfruit and simmer for another 30 minutes, until pork and jackfruit are tender.
Add greens and finger chilies; simmer 5 minutes, then season with fish sauce or salt and black pepper.

intro: Steamed Okra and Bagoong is a clean, crisp vegetable side with salty shrimp paste.
steps: Bring 2 cups water to a boil in a steamer.
Arrange okra in the steaming basket and steam 8–10 minutes until tender but still bright green.
Transfer okra immediately to ice water for 2 minutes to stop cooking and preserve its crisp texture.
Drain well, arrange on a serving plate, and serve with bagoong.

intro: Adobo Rice is a quick garlic fried rice that makes excellent use of leftover pork adobo.
ingredients: 4 cups leftover white rice, preferably day-old
3 stalks green onions, chopped, white and green parts separated
Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil over medium heat. Cook garlic until golden, then remove about three quarters for topping.
Add the white green-onion parts and sauté for 20 seconds.
Add rice and stir-fry 2 minutes, breaking up clumps. Stir in oyster sauce and cook 1 minute.
Add pork adobo and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes, until heated through. Season with salt and pepper.
Toss in green onion tops and reserved garlic. Transfer to a serving plate.

intro: Pancit Batil Patung combines saucy miki noodles, beef, liver, lechon carajay, and eggy broth.
steps: Boil beef bones in water for 5 minutes. Add celery, cubed carrot, and small onion tied in cheesecloth, plus bouillon; simmer low 45 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok. Sauté red onion, minced beef for 3 to 5 minutes, then pork liver for 3 minutes.
Add sprouts, green onions, cabbage, and julienned carrot; sauté 2 to 3 minutes. Add 4 to 5 cups stock and bring to a boil.
Add miki, soy sauce, and pepper; toss 2 to 3 minutes. Poach 1 egg in the broth, remove it, and plate noodles.
Boil remaining pan stock separately, stir in the second egg for 1 to 2 minutes, then serve as batil beside noodles topped with fillings, lechon carajay, and poached egg.

intro: Kimchi Adobo Fried Rice layers savory pork adobo with kimchi, crispy toppings, and a fried egg.
steps: Melt butter in a wok over medium heat and add garlic-infused oil.
When bubbling settles, add pork adobo and cook until the edges are lightly crisp.
Add kimchi and gochujang; cook 2 minutes. Add rice and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add kimchi juice, sesame oil, and sesame seeds; cook 2 minutes.
Stir in bacon bits, chicharon, nori, and green onion for 1 minute. Plate and top with the fried egg.

intro: Chicken Callos is a Spanish-influenced chicken stew with chorizo, chickpeas, tomatoes, and paprika.
ingredients: 4 whole chicken legs, about 1.25 to 1.5 kg
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauté garlic and red onion in olive oil over medium heat until garlic is golden. Brown chicken on all sides, then remove.
Cook tomatoes and tomato paste for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Return chicken to the pot with chorizo and chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Add bay leaves, capsicum, chickpeas, and paprika. Simmer on low for 15 minutes, or until chicken is tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Lechon Macau delivers crackling pork belly skin over fragrant, five-spice-seasoned meat.
ingredients: 2.5 kg whole pork belly or large pork belly slices
steps: Cover pork belly with water in a pot. Add about 2 tablespoons rock salt, sugar, star anise, garlic, and onion; simmer 30–40 minutes until cooked but firm.
Drain and air-dry. Once cool, brush with Shaoxing wine and refrigerate uncovered for 24 hours.
Prick the skin generously. Season skin with salt and meat side with five-spice powder and black pepper; bring to room temperature and pat skin completely dry.
Roast skin-side up at 200°C over a pan holding a little water for 45 minutes.
Increase oven to 220°C and roast 15–20 minutes until the rind is crackled and crisp. Rest briefly before slicing.

intro: Pungko Pungko is a shareable platter of crisp pork, intestines, and Lumpiang Shanghai served with sawsawan.
ingredients: 700 g pork intestines, cleaned and sliced
700 g fatty pork cuts (pork cheeks, belly, neck, or shoulder), sliced
steps: Cover intestines with water, boil, then simmer 30 minutes. Drain and rinse thoroughly under running water.
Place intestines and pork in a clean pot with 4 cups water, whole garlic, vinegar, 2 tablespoons salt, and peppercorns; simmer 30 minutes, then drain and cool.
Mix eggs with minced garlic and 1 teaspoon salt. Put cornstarch on a separate plate.
Coat meats in egg mixture, then cornstarch. Deep-fry at 180°C for 10 to 12 minutes until golden; drain.
Deep-fry Lumpiang Shanghai until cooked and golden. Arrange everything on a platter with sawsawan and rice.

intro: Pork Kare Kare is a rich peanut-and-atsuete stew of tender pata and vegetables, served with bagoong alamang.
ingredients: 2 bunches baby bok choy or pechay
steps: Soak achiote seeds in 1/2 cup warm water for 10 minutes, stir to release color, then strain and reserve the atsuete water.
Boil pata in 2 quarts water over medium heat for 20 minutes; drain and discard the cooking water.
Heat oil, sauté garlic and onion until soft, then sauté pata for 2 minutes.
Add 1 1/2 quarts water, boil, cover, and simmer over low to medium heat for 60 minutes until tender; add water if needed.
Stir in Pork Cube, peanut butter, and atsuete water; cook over medium heat for 5–8 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with 1/2 cup water, add it, and cook 5 minutes until slightly thick. Season, then cook sitaw and eggplant 5 minutes and bok choy 2 minutes.
Serve with cooked bagoong alamang.

intro: Ginataang Pagi is a creamy coconut stingray dish with ginger, chilies, and capsicum.
ingredients: 800 g stingray, skinned, deboned, and cubed
2 large red capsicums, chopped and seeded
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Put stingray in a pot, cover it just barely with water, add 1 tsp salt, and boil 15 minutes.
Drain stingray, cool it, then flake the fish.
Heat olive oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté onion until soft, then stir-fry garlic, ginger, and finger chilies until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and bring to a boil. Fold in flaked stingray until evenly mixed.
Add red capsicums, cover, and simmer 7 minutes. Season with fish sauce and black pepper before serving.

intro: Paksiw na salmon sa gata braises salmon heads in coconut cream, vinegar, and chilies.
steps: Combine salmon heads, ginger, garlic, onion, Thai chilies, coconut vinegar, and water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Add long green peppers, cover, and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut cream and stir. Let it return to a boil, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in ampalaya leaves, if using. Season with salt and black pepper, then serve.

intro: Ensaladang Talong is a smoky grilled eggplant salad sharpened with vinegar, tomatoes, and bagoong.
ingredients: 2 tbsp bagoong (shrimp paste), or sea salt for a vegetarian option
3/4 cup coconut vinegar or white vinegar
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Halve eggplants crosswise and grill until fully soft and cooked through.
Cool slightly, scrape the flesh from the skins, and roughly chop it.
Combine eggplant, tomatoes, onion, bagoong or sea salt, chili, vinegar, and black pepper in a bowl.
Mix well, transfer to a small serving plate, and serve.

intro: Buko pandan drink is a chilled coconut refresher with tapioca, nata de coco, and pandan jelly.
ingredients: 6 pandan leaves, washed and cut into 1-inch pieces
Meat and juice of 2 large coconuts, meat shredded
steps: Boil pandan leaves in water until fragrant and green-tinted. Remove and discard the leaves.
Prepare green gelatin according to its packet, using two-thirds of the pandan water and reduced liquid for a firm set. Cool until solid, then cube.
Drain nata de coco to remove its syrup.
In a large pitcher, combine coconut meat and juice, cooked tapioca pearls, nata de coco, condensed milk, gelatin cubes, water, and remaining pandan water.
Tint with green food coloring if desired. Mix well and refrigerate for 2 hours before serving.

intro: Inihaw na Pork Chop is a smoky grilled pork dish glazed with a sweet-savory citrus soy marinade.
steps: Mix soy sauce, banana ketchup, garlic, salt, sugar, black pepper, and lemon or calamansi juice for the marinade.
Place pork chops and marinade in a sealed bag, remove excess air, and refrigerate for 5 to 8 hours.
Remove chops and mix the remaining marinade with cooking oil for basting.
Grill over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side while basting. Repeat the grilling and basting cycle, cooking longer as needed.
Serve once the pork is cooked through and nicely charred.

intro: Sinarsahang Pork Ribs is a tomato-rich braise finished with butter and crisp-tender vegetables.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Steam string beans and carrot for 3 minutes, then set aside.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until onion softens.
Add pork ribs and sauté until lightly browned.
Add soy sauce, tomato paste, and water; bring to a boil, then add Knorr Pork Cube.
Cover and simmer until ribs are completely tender.
Add butter and simmer uncovered until sauce reduces by half; stir in sugar, salt, and pepper.
Serve ribs with the steamed string beans and carrot.

intro: Asadong Matua is a slow-braised pork roast served in a smooth tomato, liver, and cheese sauce.
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Boil baby potatoes in water until tender; drain and set aside. Season pork and chicken liver generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot and brown pork on all sides; remove. Brown chicken liver in the same pot and remove.
Sauté garlic and onion until soft. Add tomatoes, water, lemon juice, soy sauce, pork, and oregano; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour. Add chicken liver and cook 30 minutes more.
Remove pork. Blend the sauce smooth with an immersion blender, stir in cheese, return pork, and adjust seasoning.
Rest pork for 5 minutes, slice into 1/2-inch steaks, and serve with sauce and boiled baby potatoes.

intro: Beef Pares Lomi is a thick, comforting noodle soup with sweet-savory star anise beef.
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add beef and sauté until lightly browned. Add soy sauce and water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Add star anise, brown sugar, and Knorr Beef Cube. Cover and cook over low heat until beef is tender.
Discard star anise. Add miki noodles, season with salt and pepper, and cook 3 minutes.
Mix potato starch with 3 tablespoons water. Stir it and beaten egg into the soup; cook until thickened to your preferred consistency.

intro: Chicken lollipop is the frenched, fried chicken wing that turns up at nearly every Filipino birthday party, with the meat pushed to one end so the bone becomes a handle.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken wings (about 12), separated at the joints
Sweet chili sauce or banana ketchup, for dipping
steps: Shape the lollipops: on each drumette, cut around the narrow end of the bone to release the skin and tendons, then push the meat down to the thick end to form a ball. For the two-bone wingette, cut around one end, pull out the thinner bone and push the meat down the remaining bone the same way. Save the wing tips for stock.
Mix the soy sauce, calamansi juice, garlic, pepper and half of the salt in a bowl. Add the chicken, turn to coat, cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Beat the egg into the marinated chicken. Combine the flour, cornstarch and remaining salt in a shallow dish, then dredge each piece, pressing the coating onto the meat and leaving the bone clean.

Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Fry the chicken in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and cooked through; the thickest piece should reach 74°C or show no pink at the bone.
Drain on a rack or paper towels. Serve hot with sweet chili sauce or banana ketchup.

intro: Sweet and sour pork is a Chinese-Filipino panciteria classic: crisp fried pork tossed with pineapple and bell peppers in a tangy sauce built on vinegar and banana ketchup.
ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder (kasim), cut into 2.5 cm cubes
1/2 cup cornstarch, plus 1 tablespoon for the sauce
1 small carrot, sliced thinly on the diagonal
1 red bell pepper, cut into squares
1 green bell pepper, cut into squares
1 can (227 g) pineapple chunks, syrup reserved
steps: Season the pork with the soy sauce, salt and pepper and let it stand for 15 minutes. Stir in the beaten egg, then toss the pieces in 1/2 cup cornstarch until evenly coated.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep pan to 175°C. Fry the pork in two batches for 5 to 6 minutes each until golden, crisp and cooked through. Drain on a rack and pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil.
Stir the vinegar, banana ketchup, brown sugar, reserved pineapple syrup, water and the remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch together in a bowl until smooth.

Reheat the wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the garlic and onion for 1 minute, add the carrot and cook for 2 minutes, then add the bell peppers and pineapple and cook for 1 minute more; the vegetables should stay crisp.
Pour in the sauce mixture and stir until it boils and turns glossy and thick, about 2 minutes. Taste and adjust with a little more sugar or vinegar.
Return the pork to the wok, toss just until coated and serve at once with steamed rice so the coating stays crisp.

intro: Yang Chow fried rice is the mixed fried rice ordered at Chinese-Filipino restaurants, studded with shrimp, sweet pork asado, egg and green peas.
ingredients: 4 cups cold cooked rice, preferably a day old
150 g small shrimp, peeled and deveined
150 g pork asado or Chinese-style barbecued pork, diced
3 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
steps: Break up the cold rice with your fingers so no clumps remain.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs, scramble into soft curds, then transfer to a plate.
Add another tablespoon of oil and cook the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes until pink and opaque. Add the diced pork and toss for 30 seconds, then set aside with the eggs.

Add the remaining oil and sauté the garlic for 20 seconds. Add the carrot and cook for 1 minute, then add the rice. Stir-fry over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, pressing and tossing, until the grains are hot and separate.
Season with the soy sauce, salt and white pepper. Return the egg, shrimp and pork to the wok, add the peas and toss for 1 minute until everything is heated through.
Turn off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and spring onion, and serve hot.

intro: Buttered garlic shrimp is a quick Filipino seafood favorite of shell-on shrimp simmered in butter, plenty of garlic and a splash of lemon-lime soda for sweetness.
ingredients: 500 g medium shrimp, shell-on, whiskers trimmed and deveined
1 tablespoon chopped parsley or spring onion
steps: Soak the shrimp in the lemon-lime soda for 10 minutes, then drain and reserve 1/4 cup of the soda.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until light golden and fragrant; do not let it burn.
Raise the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in a single layer. Cook for about 1 minute per side until they turn orange.
Pour in the reserved soda and the calamansi juice. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce reduces and coats the shrimp and the shrimp are opaque all the way through.
Season with the salt and pepper, sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately with steamed rice.

intro: Chili garlic crab is a dampa-style seafood dish of cut crabs wok-tossed in a buttery, spicy-sweet sauce loaded with garlic.
ingredients: 1 kg live mud crabs (alimango) or blue crabs (alimasag), about 2 to 3 pieces
1 thumb-size piece ginger, cut into thin strips
4 red bird's eye chilies (siling labuyo), chopped, or to taste
steps: Chill the crabs in the freezer for 15 minutes so they stop moving. Scrub the shells, lift off the top shell, remove the gills and the apron, and cut each crab in half or in quarters. Crack the claws lightly with the back of a knife so the sauce can get in.
Heat the oil and butter in a large wok over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes until pale golden, then add the ginger, onion and chilies and cook until the onion softens.
Add the crabs and toss for 2 minutes until the shells start to turn orange.

Stir in the banana ketchup, chili garlic sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and water. Cover and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, turning the pieces once, until the shells are bright orange all over and the meat is opaque.
Uncover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more until the sauce thickens and clings to the crab. Season with salt.
Scatter with spring onion and serve hot with rice.

intro: Crispy kangkong is a Filipino restaurant appetizer of water spinach leaves dipped in a light batter, fried until shatteringly crisp and served with a garlic mayonnaise dip.
ingredients: 2 bundles kangkong (water spinach), leaves only, about 4 packed cups
steps: Pick the kangkong leaves from the stems, wash them and dry them thoroughly with a clean towel; wet leaves will make the oil spatter and the batter slide off.
Stir the mayonnaise, garlic and calamansi juice together for the dip and chill until needed.
Whisk the cornstarch, flour, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add the egg and ice-cold water and stir just until combined; a few lumps are fine and the batter should be thin.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C. Dip the leaves in the batter a few at a time, let the excess drip off and slip them into the oil one by one so they do not stick together.
Fry for 1 to 2 minutes, turning once, until pale golden and crisp. Drain on a rack or paper towels and continue with the remaining leaves.
Serve at once with the garlic mayonnaise dip.

intro: Tortang alimasag is a Tagalog crab omelette of flaked blue crab meat, potato and aromatics bound with egg and pan-fried until golden.
ingredients: 1 kg blue crabs (alimasag), or 250 g cooked crab meat
1 small potato, peeled and finely diced
steps: If using whole crabs, steam them for 15 minutes until bright orange. Cool, then pick out the meat, discarding the gills and any bits of shell. Keep the top shells if you want to serve the torta in them.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté the garlic, onion and tomato until soft, add the potato and carrot and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until tender. Stir in the crab meat, season with half of the salt and the pepper, and let the mixture cool for a few minutes.
Beat the eggs with the remaining salt in a bowl. Fold in the cooled crab mixture and the spring onion.

Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Ladle in about 1/2 cup of the mixture and flatten it into a patty, or pack the mixture into the crab shells and fry them filling-side down.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the underside is set and golden, flip and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes until the egg is cooked through. Repeat with the remaining mixture, adding oil as needed.
Serve warm with banana ketchup and steamed rice.

intro: Utan Bisaya, also called law-uy, is the everyday Visayan soup of mixed vegetables simply boiled with lemongrass and tomato and often topped with fried or dried fish.
ingredients: 1 stalk lemongrass (tanglad), pounded and tied in a knot
2 small taro roots (gabi), peeled and cubed
1 medium eggplant, sliced on the diagonal
1 bundle string beans (sitaw), cut into 5 cm lengths
2 pieces fried fish or 4 pieces fried dried fish (buwad), optional
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a pot with the lemongrass, ginger, onion and tomatoes. Simmer for 5 minutes so the broth takes on their flavor.
Add the taro and cook for 8 minutes until it begins to soften.
Add the squash and cook for 4 minutes, then add the okra, eggplant and string beans and simmer for another 4 to 5 minutes until all the vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Season with the salt. If using fried fish, lay it on top now and let it warm through for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat and stir in the alugbati and malunggay leaves; they will wilt in the hot broth. Remove the lemongrass and serve hot with rice.

intro: Adobong itik is a Laguna and Central Luzon specialty of native duck braised slowly in vinegar, soy sauce and garlic until tender, then fried in its own fat.
ingredients: 1 whole duck (itik), about 1.5 kg, cut into serving pieces
steps: Trim excess fat and skin from the duck and rinse the pieces. Rubbing them with a little salt and rinsing again helps remove any gamey smell.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Brown the duck in batches, skin-side down first, for 4 to 5 minutes per side to render the fat. Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat.

Sauté the garlic, ginger and onion in the pot until fragrant. Return the duck and add the vinegar, soy sauce, bay leaves, peppercorns and water. Bring to a boil without stirring and let it boil uncovered for 3 minutes to cook off the sharpness of the vinegar.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, turning the pieces occasionally and adding water if the pot gets dry, until the duck is fork-tender.
Uncover, add the sugar and finger chilies and raise the heat to medium. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce reduces and the duck begins to fry in its own fat.
Taste, season with salt if needed and serve with steamed rice.

intro: Yema is a soft Filipino custard candy of egg yolks and condensed milk cooked until thick, then rolled into balls or pyramids and wrapped in colored cellophane.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon calamansi or lemon zest, optional
steps: Whisk the condensed milk and egg yolks together in a heavy non-stick pan until smooth before turning on the heat.

Add the butter and cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or spatula and scraping the bottom and sides, for 15 to 20 minutes. The mixture is ready when it is very thick, pulls away from the sides of the pan and holds its shape when you drag the spoon through it.
Stir in the vanilla and zest, transfer to a buttered plate and let it cool for about 15 minutes until comfortable to handle.
Butter your hands lightly. Scoop about 2 teaspoons of the mixture at a time and roll into balls or shape into small pyramids.
Roll each piece in the sugar and wrap in cellophane. This makes about 30 pieces; keep them in a covered container at room temperature for up to 3 days or in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

intro: Ginanggang is a Mindanao street snack of saba bananas grilled over charcoal on a stick, then brushed with margarine and sprinkled with sugar.
ingredients: 8 ripe but firm saba bananas, peeled
8 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 15 minutes
steps: Prepare a charcoal grill and let the coals burn down to medium heat, or heat a stovetop grill pan over medium heat.
Thread each banana lengthwise onto a soaked skewer.
Grill the bananas for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until they are soft, heated through and lightly charred in spots.
Brush the hot bananas all over with the margarine so it melts into the surface.
Sprinkle generously with the sugar and serve warm.

intro: Tsokolate batirol is traditional Filipino hot chocolate made by dissolving pure cacao tablea in hot water and frothing it with a wooden batirol until thick.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons brown or muscovado sugar, or to taste
2 tablespoons ground roasted peanuts or smooth peanut butter, optional
steps: Bring the water to a gentle boil in a saucepan or tsokolatera. Add the tablea and lower the heat.
Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring and pressing the tablets against the side of the pot until completely dissolved.
Add the sugar, salt and the ground peanuts if using, and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Pour in the evaporated milk and heat for 1 to 2 minutes without letting it boil over.
Froth the chocolate by spinning a batirol between your palms, or whisk briskly, for about 1 minute until thick and foamy.
Pour into small cups and serve hot with suman, puto or pandesal.
